RECIPE: BBQ Chicken Sliders (bbq-chicken-sliders.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/bbq-chicken-sliders/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken and glaze ---
  - 2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, raw; fresh or fully thawed
  - 1 cup BBQ sauce, divided; keep the glazing share separate from raw chicken
  - 1 tbsp olive oil
  - 1 tsp smoked paprika
  - 1 tsp garlic powder
  - 1 tsp kosher salt
  - 1/2 tsp black pepper
  - 6 sharp cheddar slices, halved to fit sliders
  - --- Rolls and toppings ---
  - 12 Hawaiian rolls, split
  - 2 tbsp butter, melted
  - dill pickle chips, as wanted for the sliders
  - 1/2 cup crispy fried onions
  - additional BBQ sauce, as wanted for serving, separate from the measured marinade and glaze
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

BBQ sauce, smoked paprika and garlic coat the thighs before broiling; reserve a clean share of sauce for the glaze. The cheese and buttered rolls keep these sliders rich, while pickles and fried onions add tang and crunch. Watch the sauce and bread closely under the broiler: their sugars can darken before the chicken is ready.

## Directions

1. **Marinate in the refrigerator:** Toss boneless skinless chicken thighs, 1/3 of the BBQ sauce, olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, kosher salt, and black pepper together, using one-third of the measured BBQ sauce and leaving the other two-thirds in a clean container for glazing. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours. Keep the clean sauce and utensils away from the raw chicken.
2. **Broil the thighs:** Set up a broiler-safe metal sheet pan and use the rack position permitted by the oven, about 6 inches below the broiler where the oven instructions permit. Lift the thighs from the marinade, shake off excess and discard the used marinade. Arrange in a single layer without overlap; cook in additional loads if necessary. Start checking at 6–7 minutes per side, turning as the surface browns. Check the thickest part of each thigh with a thermometer and continue until each reaches 165°F / 74°C. Watch sugary spots closely rather than waiting for heavy blackening. Move cooked chicken with clean utensils.
3. **Glaze and melt the cheese:** Use 2/3 of the BBQ sauce and sharp cheddar slices for the glaze and topping: brush the cooked thighs with the clean reserved sauce, then distribute all the cheese halves evenly over the chicken. The number of thighs need not equal the number of rolls. Broil for about 1–2 minutes, watching until the cheese melts; remove before the sauce burns.
4. **Rest the chicken and toast the rolls:** Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, use Hawaiian rolls and butter for the rolls: brush their cut faces with all the melted butter. Put the rolls cut-side up on a clean broiler-safe sheet pan and watch for 1–2 minutes, removing them as soon as the cut faces are golden.
5. **Slice and assemble:** Divide all the rested chicken and melted cheese into one bun-sized portion for each measured roll. Add dill pickle chips, crispy fried onions, and additional BBQ sauce to the sliders and serve while the rolls and onions are crisp.

RECIPE: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry (beef-and-broccoli-stir-fry.md)
CUISINES: Chinese, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/beef-and-broccoli-stir-fry/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Beef and broccoli ---
  - 680 g trimmed boneless top sirloin steak, weighed after removing tough outer membranes
  - 450 g trimmed broccoli, florets about 1 1/2 inches wide and peeled stems sliced 1/4 inch thick
  - 3 tbsp neutral cooking oil, divided
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) water, for steaming broccoli, divided
  - 2 tbsp water, reserved for correcting dry broccoli or thick sauce
  - --- Sauce ---
  - 4 tbsp regular soy sauce
  - 2 tbsp oyster sauce
  - 1 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) unsalted beef stock or water
  - 2 tsp cornstarch
  - 1/4 tsp ground white pepper
  - 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil, added after sauce thickens
  - --- Aromatics and finish ---
  - 3 cloves garlic, finely minced
  - 1 tbsp finely minced fresh ginger
  - 40 g scallions, white parts thinly sliced and green parts cut into 1-inch lengths
  - 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds, optional garnish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Chinese-American combination pairs broccoli with sliced beef and a soy-oyster sauce. The ginger, garlic, rice vinegar and sesame oil give this version its own balance. Small batches matter more than creating smoke: brown the food without burning the oil or aromatics, and bring the cooked components together only after the sauce is ready. The sirloin is sliced and seared directly, so expect a different texture from beef treated with baking soda and starch.

## Directions

1. **Prepare everything:** Pat the steak dry and cut across the grain into roughly 1/4-inch-thick, 2-inch-long slices. Divide into three batches of about 225 g. Cut the broccoli as listed and divide in half. Whisk soy sauce, oyster sauce, vinegar, stock or sauce water, cornstarch and white pepper together. Keep sesame oil separate. Mince garlic and ginger and separate scallion whites and greens.
2. **Brown and steam broccoli in two batches:** Heat the pan over medium-high heat. Add 1 1/2 tsp cooking oil and half the broccoli. Cook about two minutes, turning occasionally, until some edges brown. Lower the heat slightly, carefully add 2 tbsp of the steaming water and cover for 2–3 minutes. Check a thick stem; use a little reserved water and another short steam if still hard. Uncover and let remaining water evaporate, about 30–60 seconds. Transfer to a bowl. Repeat with the other half, another 1 1/2 tsp oil and the remaining 2 tbsp steaming water.
3. **Sear three beef batches:** Let the empty pan dry and regain medium-high heat. Add 1 1/2 tsp oil; it should shimmer without heavy smoke. Spread one beef batch in one layer. Leave for about one minute until browned underneath, then turn and stir-fry another 1–3 minutes as needed. Check representative thick slices with a fine-tip thermometer inserted from the edge: at least 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean bowl. Repeat twice with 1 1/2 tsp oil per batch. Turn the heat down if residue blackens; remove burned deposits before continuing. Allow the beef at least three minutes after reaching temperature before serving.
4. **Make the sauce:** Reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining 1 1/2 tsp cooking oil, garlic, ginger and scallion whites. Stir about 30 seconds until fragrant, keeping the garlic pale. Re-stir the sauce and pour it in. Bring to a gentle bubble, stirring for about 45–90 seconds until glossy and lightly thickened. Stir in the separate tablespoon sesame oil. Use reserved water in small spoonfuls if the sauce is too thick. Pour half the sauce into a heatproof cup.
5. **Combine in two rounds:** Add half the beef and its collected juices, half the broccoli and half the scallion greens to the sauce remaining in the pan. Fold over medium heat for about 30–60 seconds to coat and rewarm, then transfer to a serving platter. Return the reserved sauce to the pan and fold in the rest of the beef, juices, broccoli and scallion greens. Once hot and coated, add this round to the platter. Do not keep boiling the meat to chase a thicker glaze.
6. **Serve:** Confirm at least three minutes have elapsed since the last beef batch reached 145°F / 63°C. Divide into four portions and scatter the optional teaspoon of sesame seeds over the full dish. Serve with plain rice prepared separately; the stir-fry already includes its vegetable portion.

RECIPE: Beef Chow Fun (beef-chow-fun.md)
CUISINES: Chinese, Cantonese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/beef-chow-fun/
SOURCE: Adapted from thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/beef-chow-fun-noodles/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Beef and coating ---
  - 450 g trimmed flank steak, sliced across the grain about 1/8 inch thick and 2 inches long
  - 1 tbsp regular soy sauce, for the beef
  - 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, for the beef
  - 2 tbsp water, for the beef
  - 2 tsp cornstarch
  - 1/4 tsp baking soda
  - 1 tsp neutral oil, for the beef coating
  - --- Noodles and vegetables ---
  - 680 g fresh wide rice noodles (ho fun), about 3/4–1 inch wide
  - 120 g fresh mung bean sprouts, rinsed and well drained
  - 60 g trimmed scallions, cut into 2-inch lengths, white and green parts separated
  - 1 tbsp finely julienned fresh ginger
  - 4 tbsp neutral oil, for cooking, divided
  - 1 tbsp water, for cooking sprouts
  - 2 tbsp water, reserved for loosening noodles only if needed
  - --- Noodle seasoning ---
  - 2 tbsp regular soy sauce, for the noodles
  - 1 tbsp Chinese dark soy sauce
  - 2 tbsp Shaoxing wine, for the noodles
  - 1 tsp sugar
  - 1/2 tsp toasted sesame oil
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Beef chow fun is a Cantonese dish built around wide rice noodles, beef and a thin soy coating. This version follows the dry style, with no thick gravy. Flexible noodles, enough oil and small portions make the technique workable on a home stove. A few toasted surfaces are welcome; restaurant wok hei is not a promise that every domestic burner can fulfill, and burned oil is not the goal.

## Directions

1. **Coat the beef:** Stir the beef's measured soy, wine, coating water, cornstarch and measured baking soda until dispersed. Add the thinly sliced beef, turn and gently mix until evenly coated, then mix in its measured coating oil. Cover and refrigerate for twenty minutes while preparing everything else. Do not rinse off this small-dose coating or add more baking soda.
2. **Prepare flexible noodles:** Separate supple fresh noodles gently. If they are cold and stiff, follow the package warming directions. Where the package permits microwaving, transfer noodles out of non-microwave-safe packaging to a microwave-safe plate, cover loosely and warm in short 20–30-second intervals, checking and turning between intervals until they separate without force. Work in manageable portions; one fixed thirty-second blast is not enough for every cold block. Cut whole sheets into 3/4–1-inch ribbons if necessary. Divide the prepared noodles into four 170 g portions.
3. **Mix and portion:** Whisk the noodle soy, Chinese dark soy, noodle wine, sugar and sesame oil, then divide the mixture into four equal portions. Prepare ginger, scallions and drained sprouts. Keep scallion whites and greens separate; divide each and the ginger into four portions. Set out clean bowls for the cooked sprouts and beef.
4. **Cook sprouts separately:** Heat 1 tsp of the cooking oil in the pan over medium-high heat. Add the sprouts and stir for about one minute. Add the measured sprout-cooking water, cover for 1–2 minutes, then uncover and let free water evaporate. The sprouts should be steaming hot and softened through their stems, not merely warmed on the surface; extend briefly if needed. Transfer to a clean bowl and divide into four portions.
5. **Cook two beef batches:** Let the pan dry and recover heat. Add 1 1/2 tsp cooking oil and spread half the beef in one layer, leaving excess loose coating in its raw-meat bowl. Cook about one minute until browned below, turn, and cook another 1–3 minutes as needed. Check representative thicker slices with a fine probe inserted sideways from the edge: at least 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean bowl. Repeat with another 1 1/2 tsp oil and the other half. Discard leftover raw-contact coating and wash its bowl and tools. Divide the cooked beef and its juices into four portions; each has time to rest at least three minutes before serving.
6. **Finish one noodle portion:** Reduce heat if the pan is smoking heavily; remove any blackened deposits. Add 2 tsp of the remaining cooking oil over medium-high heat. Stir in one portion of ginger and scallion whites for about 20 seconds until fragrant. Add one noodle portion and lift gently to coat, then let it touch the pan for 15–20 seconds at a time, lifting and turning between contacts. Add one portion of noodle seasoning and fold until evenly coated. Add one portion each of cooked beef, juices, sprouts and scallion greens. Fold just until hot throughout, about 3–4 minutes for this whole finishing step. If firm noodles need moisture, use a little of the reserved water rather than adding extra soy; use no more than the full measured noodle-water reserve across the batch.
7. **Plate and repeat:** Serve the first portion promptly, confirming at least three minutes have passed since its beef reached 145°F / 63°C. Repeat step 6 three more times, letting the empty pan recover heat between portions before adding each fresh 2 tsp oil; add aromatics once that oil shimmers. Use the remaining measured ingredient portions. Serve as four moderate noodle-main portions. A separately prepared vegetable side can accompany them; extra rice is unnecessary because the noodles already supply the starch.

## Source

Adapted from [Bill Leung's Beef Chow Fun at The Woks of Life](https://thewoksoflife.com/beef-chow-fun-noodles/), with small batches for a home stove.

RECIPE: Beef Pad See Ew (beef-pad-see-ew.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/beef-pad-see-ew/

INGREDIENTS:
  - FOR THE STEAK & MARINADE, YOU’LL NEED:
  - 8 ounces flank steak (thinly sliced)
  - 1 teaspoon Thai black soy sauce (or regular light soy sauce)
  - 1 teaspoon vegetable oil
  - 1 teaspoon cornstarch (or tapioca starch)
  - FOR THE REST OF THE DISH, YOU’LL NEED:
  - 1 tablespoon oyster sauce
  - ½ teaspoon sugar
  - 2 teaspoons Thai soy sauce (or regular light soy sauce)
  - 1 tablespoon Thai black soy sauce
  - 1 teaspoon fish sauce
  - Freshly ground white pepper (to taste)
  - 1 pound fresh wide rice noodles (you can also use 8 ounces dried rice noodles)
  - 4 tablespoons vegetable oil
  - 3 cloves garlic (sliced thinly)
  - 3 cups Chinese broccoli (cut into 2-inch/5 cm pieces)

## Chef's Note

This beef version uses Thai black soy sauce, oyster sauce and a little fish sauce. Loosen the noodles before they reach the wok, cook in manageable batches and use a clean plate for the seared beef.

## Directions

1. **Toss:** Toss steak with its marinade soy sauce, one teaspoon oil and cornstarch. Mix oyster sauce, sugar, regular soy sauce, Thai black soy sauce, fish sauce and white pepper separately.

5. **Continue:** Push the mixture aside. Add the remaining cooking oil and eggs. Scramble until set, then fold through the noodles. Continue cooking until everything is hot and the beef reaches 145°F / 63°C; allow the beef three minutes before serving. Cook longer if necessary, using tenderness and doneness rather than the original brief timer.

RECIPE: Beef Hot Dogs with Corn Relish (beef-tenderloin-dogs-with-corn-relish.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/beef-tenderloin-dogs-with-corn-relish/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/beef-tenderloin-34dogs-corn-relish
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Center-cut Beef Tenderloin, cut into 4 long "dogs"
  - 1 tbsp Olive Oil
  - 1 tsp Garlic Powder
  - 1 tsp Paprika
  - 4 6-inch Baguette pieces or High-quality Brioche Buns
  - 1 cup Roasted Corn (charred in a pan or oven)
  - 1/4 cup Red Bell Pepper, finely diced
  - 2 tbsp Red Onion, finely diced
  - 2 tbsp Apple Cider Vinegar
  - 1 tsp Sugar
  - Salt and Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Hot dogs made from beef tenderloin aren't a tradition - they're a luxury. The corn relish is the main event: fresh corn kernels provide sweetness and texture that store-bought relish can't match. The magic is in the quick pickle: fresh corn with vinegar, onion, and mustard seeds transforms an ordinary hot dog stand item into something worth serving at a table.

## Directions

1.  **The Relish:** In a small bowl, whisk the vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper. Toss with the roasted corn, peppers, and onions. Let marinate while you cook the beef.

Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
4.  **The Bread:** Toast the baguette or brioche buns until golden.
5.  **Assemble:** Place a beef strip in each bun. Top generously with the corn relish.

RECIPE: Beef with Snow Peas (beef-with-snow-peas.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/beef-with-snow-peas/
SOURCE: foodnetwork.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/ree-drummond/beef-with-snow-peas-recipe-3381538
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1/2 cup low-sodium soy sauce
  - 3 tablespoons sherry or cooking sherry
  - 2 tablespoons cornstarch
  - 2 tablespoons brown sugar
  - 1 tablespoon peeled and minced fresh ginger
  - 1 1/2 pounds flank steak, trimmed of fat and sliced very thin against the grain
  - 3 tablespoons peanut or olive oil
  - 8 ounces fresh snow peas, trimmed
  - 5 whole scallions, cut into 1/2-inch pieces on the diagonal
  - Crushed red pepper
  - Salt, as needed (use sparingly!)
  - Jasmine or long-grain rice, cooked according to package directions
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Thinly cut flank steak and brief cooking keep this stir-fry tender. Divide the sauce before it touches raw beef and use a clean plate for cooked meat. Cook in batches so the steak sears instead of steaming.

## Directions

1. **Mix:** In a bowl, mix together the soy sauce, sherry, cornstarch, brown sugar and ginger. Add the beef to a separate bowl and pour one-third of the liquid over the top. Save the rest of the liquid. Toss the beef and set aside.

2. **Cook:** Heat the oil in a heavy skillet (iron is best) over high heat. Add the snow peas and stir for 45 seconds, getting as much color on them as possible. Remove to a plate.

3. **Finish:** Allow the skillet to get very hot again. With tongs, add half the meat mixture, leaving most of the marinade still in the bowl. Spread out the meat as you add it to skillet, but do not stir for a good minute. (You want the meat to get as brown as possible as quickly as possible.) Sprinkle half the scallions over the meat. Flip the meat to the other side and cook for another 30 seconds. Remove to a clean plate.

4. **Continue:** Repeat with the other half of the meat, allowing the skillet to get very hot again first. After flipping, add the first plateful of meat, the reserved liquid, the crushed red pepper and snow peas. Stir over high heat for 30 seconds, and then turn off the heat. Check the seasonings and add salt only if it needs it. The mixture will thicken as it sits. Use a clean plate for the first cooked batch. Discard the raw-contact marinade; the reserved sauce must have been kept separate. Check beef for 145°F / 63°C and allow three minutes before serving. Serve immediately over rice.

RECIPE: Cinnamon Rolls (best-cinnamon-roll-recipe-cinnabon-copycat.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/best-cinnamon-roll-recipe-cinnabon-copycat/
SOURCE: Cambrea Gordon, Cambrea Bakes; earlier saved version
SOURCE_URL: https://cambreabakes.com/the-best-cinnamon-rolls/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Tangzhong ---
  - 1/4 cup Bread Flour
  - 3/4 cup Water
  - --- Dough ---
  - 3 2/3 cups Bread Flour
  - 1/3 cup Granulated Sugar
  - 2 tsp Instant Yeast
  - 3/4 tsp Fine Sea Salt
  - 1/3 cup Heavy Cream (room temp)
  - 1/3 cup Whole Milk (room temp)
  - 1 large Egg (room temp)
  - 1 tsp Vanilla Bean Paste
  - 8 tbsp European-style Salted Butter (cool room temp)
  - --- Cinnamon filling ---
  - 12 tbsp Salted Butter (cool room temp)
  - 3/4 cup Light Brown Sugar, packed
  - 2 tbsp Ground Cinnamon
  - 2 tsp Vanilla Powder (optional, for the filling)
  - --- Cream cheese frosting ---
  - 5 oz Cream Cheese (cold)
  - 6 tbsp Unsalted Butter (room temp)
  - 1 cup Powdered Sugar
  - 1/2 tsp Vanilla Bean Paste
  - 1 tbsp Heavy Cream
  - --- For handling ---
  - Butter, for greasing the bowl
  - Bread flour, for dusting
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

These soft, pull-apart rolls have a buttery cinnamon spiral and tangy cream-cheese frosting. Cooking a small portion of the flour with water helps the dough retain moisture; cool the paste until just warm before mixing it into the dough. Keep the filling butter soft but cool enough to hold its shape, so it spreads rather than runs out of the spirals.

Plan about 4 hours through warm serving, with longer if the dough rises slowly. Make the filling during the 30-minute dough rest and the frosting during baking; judge the final rise by the rolls doubling in size.

## Directions

1. **The Tangzhong:** In a small saucepan, whisk the tangzhong flour and water. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until a thick paste forms, about 4–5 minutes. Scrape into a bowl and cool until just warm.

2. **The Mix:** In a stand mixer, combine the dough flour, granulated sugar, yeast and salt. Add the cream, milk, egg, dough vanilla and all the cooled tangzhong. Knead with a dough hook on low speed for about 2 minutes.

3. **The Butter:** On low speed, add the dough butter one tablespoon at a time, letting each addition incorporate. Knead for another 10–12 minutes, until smooth and elastic and a stretched piece forms a thin windowpane.

4. **Rest the Dough:** Shape into a ball, place seam-side down in a butter-greased bowl, cover and rest for 30 minutes.

5. **Make the Filling:** During the rest, mix all the filling butter, brown sugar and cinnamon with the optional vanilla powder into a spreadable paste.

6. **Shape:** On a lightly floured surface, roll to a 15 x 21-inch rectangle with a 21-inch edge facing you. Spread all the filling over the dough, leaving a 1-inch clean border along the far 21-inch edge.

7. **The Cut:** Cut across the 21-inch width into twelve strips, each 1.75 inches wide and 15 inches long. Roll each strip away from you toward its clean edge and place in a parchment-lined metal 9 x 13-inch pan.

8. **Final Rise:** Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1–2 hours. Preheat the oven to 325°F during this rise and wait for it to reach temperature before baking.

9. **Bake:** Bake for about 30–35 minutes, until the tops are lightly golden and the center roll is set rather than wet dough. Check the center as well as the edges; continue baking if the middle is still doughy.

10. **The Frosting:** While the rolls bake, beat all the frosting cream cheese and butter until smooth. Mix in the powdered sugar, frosting vanilla and cream, beating until fluffy.

11. **Finish:** Cool the pan on a rack for 15 minutes. Spread all the frosting over the warm rolls, then let stand another 15 minutes before serving warm.

Refrigerate frosted leftovers in a covered container at 40°F / 4°C or below within 2 hours, or within 1 hour if the room is above 90°F / 32°C. Bring out only the portions you plan to serve.

## Cooking Notes

Fluff flour, spoon it into the measuring cup and level it rather than scooping compacted flour. A pizza wheel makes the long dough strips easy to cut. For an overnight schedule, cover shaped rolls and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below for up to 24 hours, then let them rise until doubled before baking. For a freezer schedule, wrap the shaped pan tightly and freeze for 2–3 weeks for best quality; thaw in the refrigerator overnight, then let the rolls rise until doubled before baking. These schedules add chilling, thawing and the final rise to the listed elapsed time.

RECIPE: Brownies (best-homemade-brownies.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/best-homemade-brownies/
SOURCE: Love and Lemons, adapted from Michelle Lopez’s Weeknight Baking
SOURCE_URL: https://www.loveandlemons.com/brownies-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 1/2 cups Granulated Sugar
  - 3/4 cup All-Purpose Flour
  - 2/3 cup Unsweetened Cocoa Powder, sifted
  - 1/2 cup Powdered Sugar
  - 1/2 cup Dark Chocolate Chips (60% cacao or higher)
  - 3/4 tsp Sea Salt
  - 2 large Eggs
  - 1/2 cup Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 2 tbsp Water
  - 1/2 tsp Vanilla Extract
  - Cooking spray, for the pan and parchment
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

These brownies have dense, fudgy centers, chewy edges, and a noticeable olive-oil flavor. Keep the 8-inch square pan: a wider pan makes a thinner layer that bakes faster. Fold only until no dry flour remains, and cool completely before cutting so the soft center has time to firm up. Budget about 2 hours 55 minutes, including at least 2 hours of cooling; a warm pan may need longer.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 325°F. Spray an 8x8 baking pan and line with parchment paper so it hangs over the edges. Spray the parchment too.
2.  **Dry Mix:** In a medium bowl, whisk together the sugar, flour, cocoa, powdered sugar, chocolate chips, and salt.
3.  **Wet Mix:** In a large bowl, whisk eggs, olive oil, water, and vanilla until well combined and slightly frothy.
4.  **Combine:** Sprinkle the dry ingredients over the wet. Fold gently with a spatula until **just combined**. The batter will be very thick.
5.  **Bake:** Spread evenly in the prepared pan. Bake for 40-45 minutes until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.
6.  **The Finish:** Allow to cool completely in the pan for at least 2 hours before slicing. This is mandatory for the structure to set.

## Variations

Use canola oil in place of the same listed olive-oil amount for a more neutral flavor. For a separate less-sweet version of this fixed batch, use 1 cup granulated sugar instead of 1½ cups; keep every other quantity, the 8-inch square pan and the method unchanged. Keep the moist-crumb cue and complete cooling; texture and baking time may differ.

RECIPE: Bibimbap (bibimbap.md)
CUISINES: Korean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/bibimbap/
SOURCE: Adapted from MyKoreanKitchen.com
SOURCE_URL: https://mykoreankitchen.com/bibimbap-korean-mixed-rice-with-meat-and-assorted-vegetables/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 cups Cooked Rice (See note)
  - 4 Eggs, fried sunny-side up
  - 2 tbsp Gochujang
  - 1 tbsp Toasted Sesame Oil
  - 1 tbsp Sugar
  - 1 tbsp Water
  - 1 tsp Rice Vinegar
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Bibimbap has roots in Korean royal court cuisine but became a peasant dish in the Joseon Dynasty, when farmers would mix leftover vegetables and rice in a bowl. The name means 'mixed rice,' and it reflects the Korean philosophy of balance - multiple flavors and textures coming together in harmony. In Jeonju, the dish is so revered there's an annual Bibimbap Festival. The magic moment is when you break the runny egg yolk and stir everything together, creating a creamy sauce that coats the rice.

## Critical Components

This dish relies on having several prepared sides ("Banchan") ready to assemble. Use these recipes or store-bought alternatives:

- **The Meat:** [Korean Marinated Ribeye](/mise/recipes/marinated-korean-ribeye) (Bulgogi)
- **The Crunch:** [Korean Pickled Cucumbers](/mise/recipes/korean-pickled-cucumbers) (Oi Muchim)
- **The Green:** [Seasoned Spinach](/mise/recipes/simply-seasoned-korean-spinach-salad) (Sigeumchi Namul)
- **The Sprout:** [Seasoned Bean Sprouts](/mise/recipes/seasoned-bean-sprouts) (Kongnamul)
- **The Rice:** [Short Grain Rice](/mise/recipes/steamed-white-rice) (must be hot!)

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Have all your component recipes ready ([Ribeye](/mise/recipes/marinated-korean-ribeye), [Cucumbers](/mise/recipes/korean-pickled-cucumbers), etc.).
2.  **Base:** Scoop 1 cup of hot rice into each bowl. (Tip: For crispy rice, use the "Cast Iron Skillet Hack" mentioned in the [Ribeye](/mise/recipes/marinated-korean-ribeye) recipe).
3.  **The Clock:** Arrange the prepared vegetables and meat in distinct piles around the perimeter of the bowl, moving clockwise.
4.  **The Crown:** Place the fried egg in the center.
5.  **Sauce:** Drizzle the mixed Gochujang sauce over the egg.
6.  **Serve:** Mix vigorously before eating.

RECIPE: Big-Batch Chicken Chili Verde (big-batch-chicken-chili-verde.md)
CUISINES: Mexican-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/big-batch-chicken-chili-verde/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken and aromatics ---
  - 1.35 kg (3 lb) boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
  - 3 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - 200 g yellow onion, finely diced
  - 4 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1 1/2 tsp fine salt, divided and partly added to taste
  - 2 tsp ground cumin
  - 1 tsp ground coriander
  - 1/4 tsp cayenne, optional
  - --- Green sauce ---
  - 1.35 kg (3 lb) tomatillos, weighed after removing husks, rinsed and halved
  - 3 poblano peppers, about 450 g before trimming
  - 2 jalapeños, optional or reduced for milder heat
  - 2 cups (480 ml) low-sodium chicken broth, divided, plus up to 1 cup (240 ml) only if needed to loosen
  - 1 can (15 oz / 425 g) plain white beans, rinsed and drained, about 255 g drained total
  - 2 tbsp fresh lime juice, added gradually only if needed
  - 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro
  - --- Optional toppings, for the whole batch ---
  - 1/2 cup (120 g) sour cream
  - 80 g radishes, thinly sliced
  - 40 g prepared tortilla strips
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Roasted tomatillos and poblanos give this home chili verde its character. Brown the chicken separately, then braise it in the blended sauce; the small white-bean addition gives texture without turning it into white chicken chili. Adjust broth and lime after seeing the actual roasted-vegetable yield. This is a weekend batch intended to divide into eight portions.

## Directions

1. **Roast peppers:** Heat the broiler and position a rimmed tray about 6 inches from the element, following the oven's guidance. Broil whole poblanos and optional jalapeños, turning regularly, about 12–20 minutes until blistered. Put them in a heatproof bowl and cover for 10 minutes. Peel loose charred skin, remove stems and seed cores, and chop; handle hot chiles with care and wash hands before touching eyes.
2. **Roast tomatillos:** Arrange halved tomatillos cut-side down on the tray, retaining their juices. Broil about 10–15 minutes until soft with browned or blistered tops. Use two batches if they cannot fit in one layer. Watch rather than following the clock past burning.
3. **Blend the sauce:** Let vegetables cool enough for your blender's warm-liquid guidance. Blend tomatillos and collected juices with peeled peppers and 1 cup of the measured broth, in batches as needed. Vent as the appliance directs; do not seal steaming liquid in a personal blender. Have this sauce ready before beginning the chicken.
4. **Brown chicken:** Pat chicken dry and season with two-thirds of the listed salt. Heat 2 tsp oil in a roomy Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown one-third of the chicken on two sides, about 5–6 minutes, then transfer to a bowl. Repeat twice with 2 tsp oil per batch. The centers need the following braise; continue directly.
5. **Build aromatics:** Lower heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp oil. Cook onion about 6–8 minutes until softened. Add garlic, cumin, coriander and optional cayenne and stir about 30 seconds. Pour in the remaining initial 1 cup broth and scrape up brown residue, then add the blended green sauce and chicken with its juices.
6. **Braise and check:** Bring to a gentle simmer, partly cover and cook about 25–35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C and are tender. Add a little of the extra broth only if sauce is too thick before the meat is ready. Stir in drained beans for the final 5 minutes to heat through.
7. **Finish:** If sauce needs further reduction, remove finished chicken briefly and simmer the sauce alone, then return it. Turn off heat. Taste and add the remaining salt only if needed. Stir in cilantro and start with just a little lime juice, adding more only if the sauce benefits.
8. **Serve and portion:** Divide into eight servings. Offer the listed sour cream, radishes and tortilla strips as optional full-batch supplies. Omit sour cream for a dairy-free version and check packaged ingredients. Bread or slaw is prepared separately.

## Scaling and make-ahead

A half batch uses half the ingredients, but smaller pans and evaporation can change timing and liquid needs. A double batch requires additional roasting/searing batches and suitable pot capacity; do not double the cooking temperature or assume the same elapsed time. For future meals, portion promptly into shallow containers and follow the storage guidance, including cold transport for lunches.

RECIPE: Soft Black Bean Tacos with Lime Crema (black-bean-tacos-with-lime-crema.md)
CUISINES: Mexican-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/black-bean-tacos-with-lime-crema/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Beans ---
  - 2 cans (15 oz / 425 g each) black beans, rinsed and drained, about 510 g drained total
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil
  - 150 g onion, finely diced
  - 3 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1 tsp ground cumin
  - 1/2 tsp mild chili powder blend
  - 1/4 tsp smoked paprika
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) low-sodium vegetable broth, plus a little only if needed
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, added gradually to taste
  - --- Lime crema ---
  - 1/2 cup (120 g) Mexican crema or plain Greek yogurt
  - 1 tbsp fresh lime juice, plus up to 1 tsp more to taste
  - 1/8 tsp fine salt, only if needed
  - 1 tbsp water, only if needed to loosen yogurt
  - --- To serve ---
  - 8 soft corn or flour tortillas, about 6 inches across
  - 150 g green cabbage, finely shredded
  - 200 g tomatoes, diced and drained of pooled juice
  - 1/4 cup chopped cilantro
  - 1 lime, cut into 8 wedges
  - 30 g cotija cheese, crumbled, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This version makes a soft bean filling rather than a roasted one. Mash only part of the beans so their solids thicken the broth while some beans keep their shape. A measured tablespoon of neutral oil softens the onion and carries the brief spice bloom before the beans and broth enter the pan.

## Directions

1. **Prepare toppings and crema:** Shred cabbage, dice and drain tomatoes, chop cilantro and cut the serving lime. Stir crema or yogurt with the initial measured lime juice. Taste before adding the crema's optional salt and reserved juice; thin thick yogurt with up to the measured water allowance. Refrigerate while cooking.
2. **Soften the aromatics:** Heat oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium. Add onion and cook 6–8 minutes, stirring, until softened and translucent. Add garlic for 30 seconds, then cumin, chili powder and smoked paprika for about 20 seconds. Lower heat if the spices begin to darken.
3. **Build the filling:** Add drained beans, broth and half the bean salt. Simmer gently 5–7 minutes, stirring. Mash about one-third of the beans with a fork or masher, then stir into a soft, thick filling. Add a little broth if stiff; simmer briefly if watery. Taste and add the remaining bean salt only if needed, remembering the optional cheese is salty.
4. **Warm the tortillas:** Cover beans off heat for the short warming period. In a second dry skillet, warm tortillas over medium-high for roughly 10–30 seconds per side until hot and pliable, then wrap in a clean towel. For one skillet, microwave four tortillas at a time between damp paper towels for 30–45 seconds, adding short bursts if needed.
5. **Fill and serve:** Divide beans among eight tortillas. Add cabbage, tomato, cilantro, a little lime crema and optional measured cotija. Serve two tacos per person, with wedges to adjust the lime at the table. Assemble at serving so the cabbage stays crisp and tortillas do not soak through.

## Choose the texture

For browned, drier bean edges and an avocado-based sauce, use [Roasted Black Bean Tacos](/mise/recipes/crispy-black-bean-tacos). These skillet tacos deliberately keep more moisture in the filling.

RECIPE: Blackout Chocolate Cake (blackout-chocolate-cake.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/blackout-chocolate-cake/
SOURCE: Adapted from Pinchofyum.com
SOURCE_URL: http://pinchofyum.com/blackout-chocolate-cake
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chocolate cake ---
  - butter or neutral oil, for greasing the pans and parchment
  - 2 cups boiling water
  - 1 1/2 cups unsweetened cocoa powder
  - 1 tbsp instant espresso powder
  - 1 1/2 cups plain full-fat Greek yogurt
  - 1/2 cup vegetable oil
  - 4 large eggs
  - 1 tbsp vanilla extract
  - 3 cups all-purpose flour
  - 3 cups granulated sugar
  - 1 tbsp baking soda
  - 1 1/2 tsp baking powder
  - 1 1/2 tsp sea salt
  - --- Chocolate cream-cheese frosting ---
  - 1 1/2 cups butter, softened, not melted
  - 8 oz cream cheese, softened
  - 1 1/2 cups unsweetened cocoa powder
  - 1 tbsp vanilla extract
  - salt, a pinch
  - 7 cups powdered sugar
  - 1/4 cup heavy cream
  - --- Chocolate coating and drizzle ---
  - 3–4 cups chocolate chips
  - additional chocolate, for melting and drizzling, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This three-layer chocolate cake combines cocoa and espresso with tangy Greek yogurt, chocolate cream-cheese frosting and a chocolate-chip coating. Whisk the hot cocoa mixture smooth, then let it cool before the eggs enter; cool the baked layers completely so the frosting holds its shape.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the pans:** Preheat the oven to 350°F. Use butter or neutral oil to grease three 9-inch round cake pans, line their bottoms with parchment and grease the parchment. Check that the pans fit in the oven with space for air to circulate; if baking in batches, allow extra time.
2. **Bloom and cool the cocoa:** Whisk the cake’s boiling water, unsweetened cocoa powder, and instant espresso powder together in a heatproof bowl until smooth. Let stand briefly, then cool until lukewarm before adding the eggs.
3. **Mix the liquids:** Whisk the cake’s plain full-fat Greek yogurt, vegetable oil, large eggs, and vanilla extract into the cooled cocoa mixture until evenly combined.
4. **Mix the dry ingredients:** In another large bowl, whisk the cake’s all-purpose flour, granulated sugar, baking soda, baking powder, and sea salt thoroughly, breaking up lumps.
5. **Combine the batter:** Fold the dry mixture into the chocolate mixture just until no dry pockets remain. Divide evenly among the prepared pans.
6. **Bake and cool:** Bake for about 30–35 minutes, until the layers are set, the centers spring back lightly and a tester has no wet batter. Cool on racks for about 10 minutes in the pans, loosen the edges and turn out carefully. Remove the parchment and let cool completely.
7. **Make the frosting:** While the layers cool, beat the frosting’s butter, cream cheese, unsweetened cocoa powder, vanilla extract, salt, powdered sugar, and heavy cream until smooth: cream the softened butter and cream cheese first, mix in cocoa, vanilla and salt, then add powdered sugar gradually on low speed with the heavy cream. Beat until spreadable.
8. **Stack and chill:** Place one completely cooled layer on a cake board or serving plate. Spread frosting between the layers and over the top and sides. Refrigerate for 30 minutes to firm the frosting before applying the chocolate coating.
9. **Coat with chocolate chips:** Gently press the chocolate chips into the chilled cake’s sides over a tray to catch loose chips. Use as much of the listed coating allowance as needed for coverage; the remainder can be served alongside or saved separately.
10. **Finish and serve:** Melt additional chocolate (if using) and drizzle over the top. Let the cake lose its refrigerator chill before slicing; for cleaner cuts, slice before a chocolate drizzle hardens.

## Cooking Notes

A rich chocolate ganache can replace the cream-cheese frosting. Use a complete ganache recipe with enough coverage for three 9-inch layers; its setting time and storage guidance may differ. The optional chocolate drizzle is additional to the chip coating.

RECIPE: Blistered Shishito Peppers (blistered-shishito-peppers.md)
CUISINES: Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/blistered-shishito-peppers/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 8 oz Shishito Peppers, left whole with stems on
  - 1 tbsp Neutral Oil (avocado or grapeseed)
  - 1 tsp flaky sea salt
  - 1 tsp Sesame Seeds
  - 1 lemon wedge, for squeezing
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Dry peppers and a single layer let the skins blister before the flesh becomes soft. Heat varies from pepper to pepper; a mild batch does not guarantee that every pepper is mild. Eat the peppers while hot, holding the stems and leaving them behind.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and heat:** Wash the whole peppers under running water and dry thoroughly. Keep their stems on. Heat a cast-iron skillet over medium-high to high heat until hot, following the pan instructions; visible smoke is not required.

2. **Blister:** Use enough pan space for one loose layer. Divide the listed oil and peppers among batches if necessary. Add each batch’s oil, then the peppers. Leave undisturbed about 60–90 seconds until blistered and dark in spots, then toss and cook another 60–90 seconds. Continue briefly if needed until the skins have several blistered patches; reduce heat if oil smokes or peppers blacken all over.

3. **Season:** Transfer to a serving plate. Squeeze the listed lemon wedge over the peppers and distribute all the measured flaky salt and sesame seeds over the whole batch.

4. **Serve:** Serve promptly, picking peppers up by their stems and leaving the stems behind. Earlier batches soften while later ones cook.

RECIPE: Blueberry Oatmeal (blueberry-baked-oatmeal.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/blueberry-baked-oatmeal/
SOURCE: Adapted from cookieandkate.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cookieandkate.com/baked-oatmeal-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups Old-Fashioned Rolled Oats
  - 12 oz Fresh or Frozen Blueberries
  - 2/3 cup Toasted Sunflower Seeds or Pumpkin Seeds (Nut-Free option)
  - 1 3/4 cups Milk of choice
  - 1/3 cup Maple Syrup
  - 2 large Eggs
  - 3 tbsp Butter, melted
  - 2 tsp Cinnamon
  - 1 tsp Baking Powder
  - 1 tsp Vanilla Extract
  - 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt
  - Butter or oil for greasing the baking dish
  - 2 tsp Raw Sugar (optional, for pre-bake topping)
  - Plain or vanilla yogurt or whipped cream, optional for serving
  - Extra maple syrup or honey, optional for drizzling
  - Additional fresh fruit, optional for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Berries form a juicy layer beneath the oats, with a smaller amount on top. The toasted seeds are mixed through the oats, rather than added only as a topping. Pour the milk mixture through the dry layer and press down any dry oat patches gently so the center cooks evenly. Half the measured butter goes into the mixture and the rest finishes the cooked oatmeal.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and divide berries:** Preheat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9-inch square baking dish for the original batch with the separate pan-fat allowance. Wash and drain fresh blueberries; use frozen berries without thawing. Use all the measured berries: reserve a small portion for the top and spread the rest over the bottom.

2. **Mix the dry ingredients:** Combine all the oats, toasted sunflower or pumpkin seeds, cinnamon, measured kosher salt and baking powder. Spread evenly over the bottom berries.

3. **Mix the wet ingredients:** Whisk the milk, eggs, maple syrup, vanilla and half the measured melted butter until combined. Keep the other half of the butter for finishing.

4. **Hydrate and top:** Pour the wet mixture evenly over the oats. Gently wiggle the dish to let the milk settle through, then press down any dry oats on the surface. Scatter all the reserved berries over the top. If using the optional raw sugar, scatter all its listed amount over the surface before baking.

5. **Bake:** Load only once the oven has reached 375°F. Bake about 40–45 minutes with fresh berries, or start checking around 45–50 minutes with frozen berries. Continue until the top is golden and the center is set without liquid egg mixture; an egg-dish center should reach 160°F. Berry temperature, dish material and deeper filling can extend cooking.

6. **Finish and rest:** Drizzle with all the remaining measured butter. Let stand for a few minutes so it holds together when portioned. Serve warm with optional yogurt or whipped cream, extra maple syrup or honey, and additional fresh fruit as desired. These serving allowances are separate from the measured batter. Refrigerate promptly for cold service.

SOURCE: Adapted from Mykidslickthebowl.com
SOURCE_URL: https://mykidslickthebowl.com/healthy-blueberry-banana-pancake-muffins/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 large Ripe Bananas
  - 1 cup Rolled Oats
  - 1 cup Full-Fat Cottage Cheese
  - 2 large Eggs
  - 1 tbsp Maple Syrup
  - 1 tsp Vanilla Extract
  - 1/2 cup Frozen Blueberries
  - Oil or nonstick spray for the muffin wells
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Blend the bananas, oats, full-fat cottage cheese and eggs until the oats and curds are smooth, then add the blueberries to the individual wells. These muffins have a soft, dense interior, with richness from the full-fat cottage cheese. Give the cooked muffins time to settle in the tin before lifting them.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease enough standard-size muffin wells for the listed planning count with the separate oil or spray allowance; the original batch plans twelve. Use ripe bananas and keep the frozen blueberries separate.

RECIPE: Blueberry Date Oatmeal (blueberry-date-oatmeal.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/blueberry-date-oatmeal/
SOURCE: Adapted from Kids Eat in Color
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup Rolled Oats
  - 2 tbsp Frozen Riced Cauliflower
  - 1 1/2 cups Water (all or part may be milk of choice)
  - 6 Medjool Dates, pitted and finely chopped
  - 2 tbsp Coconut Oil
  - 1/2 cup Frozen Blueberries
  - Pinch of Sea Salt
  - Ground Cinnamon, to taste
  - Additional water or milk, as needed to loosen the oatmeal
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Chop the pitted dates finely so they soften into the oats. Coconut oil adds richness to the porridge. Blueberry juice may color the porridge purple; that is normal. Choose the stove or microwave route, and check the frozen cauliflower and berry packages before deciding whether they can simply be warmed in the oats.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Check the rolled-oat and frozen cauliflower and blueberry packages. If a frozen product requires cooking before eating, follow its cooking directions; do not rely on a brief off-heat thaw to satisfy them. Cook those products separately first if the oatmeal route will not meet their instructions, retaining all the listed amounts. Remove the date pits and finely chop the flesh.

2. **Combine:** Choose the stovetop OR microwave route. Combine oats, cauliflower, water or milk, chopped dates and all the coconut oil in a saucepan, or in a microwave-safe bowl with generous room for foaming. Use the prepared cauliflower if its package required separate cooking. Keep the berries aside until the finish unless they need cooking with the oats under their package directions.

3. **Stovetop option:** Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer. Stir frequently and start checking at 5–7 minutes, following the actual rolled-oat package if it needs longer. Stop when the oats are tender and creamy. If too thick before the oats are tender, add a little of the additional water or milk allowance and continue gently. Skip the microwave step.

4. **Microwave option:** Follow the oatmeal package where it provides microwave directions. Otherwise heat on high for about 3 minutes as a first check, stopping earlier if it rises toward the rim. Carefully stir, then heat in short intervals, checking until the oats are tender and thickened; another 2–3 minutes is a planning range, not a guarantee for every microwave. If too thick before tender, stir in a little of the additional water or milk allowance before continuing. The bowl and steam will be hot. Skip the stovetop step.

5. **Berry finish:** If the measured blueberries already cooked with the oats, leave them in; do not add another amount. Otherwise, off heat, fold in all the measured blueberries if their package allows this use, or fold in the same amount cooked separately as required. Let any berries added frozen thaw and let the oatmeal become comfortable to eat before serving.

6. **Season and serve:** Add the pinch of salt and cinnamon to taste. Divide among the listed portions and serve.

## Cooking Notes

Stove and microwave are alternatives, not sequential cooking steps. Frozen-product directions may add a separate cooking stage.

When scaling, use a larger saucepan or separate batches. For the microwave, use separate roomy bowls or loads rather than multiplying the original timing in one crowded bowl. Recombine or divide the measured ingredients evenly.

Allow about 15–20 minutes for preparation, heating and cooking, plus any separate cooking required by frozen-product directions. Larger batches can take longer.

Refrigerate promptly in a shallow covered container at 40°F / 4°C or below. Limit time out to 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C. Use within 3–4 days. Reheat to 165°F / 74°C; oats become softer and thicker.

RECIPE: Blueberry Oat Breakfast Bars (blueberry-oat-breakfast-bars.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/blueberry-oat-breakfast-bars/
SOURCE: Adapted from myfussyeater.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.myfussyeater.com/blueberry-oat-breakfast-bar-flapjacks/?fbclid=IwAR13JrU7Ex3syixlLB4WnakqHoubzLDS_l6q-jsruiyBjxFBfag6CsigWrc
INGREDIENTS:
  - 5 tbsp Coconut Oil (or Unsalted Butter)
  - 4 tbsp Honey or Maple Syrup
  - 3 tbsp Almond or Peanut Butter
  - 2 cups Rolled Oats
  - 3/4 cup Fresh Blueberries
  - 1 tbsp Greek Yogurt or Coconut Cream
  - 3 tsp Orange Juice
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Press the coated oats firmly into the corners as well as the center of the pan. Baking to lightly golden edges is followed by cooling and a long cold rest; cut the bars only once the slab is firm. The choice of coconut oil or butter and nut butter affects the texture, so chilling helps the bars hold together without guaranteeing that every nut butter sets alike.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 340°F (170°C). Line an 8-inch square baking dish with parchment for the original batch, leaving enough paper to lift the cooled slab. Wash and drain the fresh blueberries.

2. **Melt:** Gently melt all the measured coconut oil or butter, honey or maple syrup, and almond or peanut butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir until smooth and combined, then take off the heat.

3. **Coat and fold:** Stir in all the oats until evenly coated. Gently fold in all the drained blueberries without deliberately crushing them.

4. **Press:** Transfer the whole mixture to the prepared dish. Press firmly with the back of a spoon across the base and into the corners, making an even, compact layer.

5. **Bake:** Load only once the oven has reached 340°F / 170°C. Bake about 15–18 minutes, until the edges are just beginning to turn golden. The hot slab will still be delicate; browning is followed by cooling and chilling.

6. **Cool and chill:** Let the slab cool in the pan until manageable, then refrigerate promptly for at least 1 hour and until firm enough to cut; overnight chilling is an option. Keep the slab in its pan while it sets.

7. **Drizzle:** Whisk all the measured yogurt or coconut cream with all the orange juice until smooth. Drizzle over the cold, firm slab.

8. **Cut and serve:** Lift with the parchment and cut into the listed number of bars; the original batch plans eight. Serve cold, or let individual bars stand briefly for serving. Return the rest to the refrigerator.

RECIPE: Blueberry Pancakes (blueberry-pancakes.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/blueberry-pancakes/
SOURCE: Adapted from Kingarthurflour.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.kingarthurflour.com/recipes/blueberry-pancakes-recipe
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 large Eggs
  - 1 cup Whole Milk
  - 2 tsp Vanilla Extract
  - 3 tbsp Unsalted Butter, melted and cooled
  - 1 1/2 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 3/4 tsp Fine Sea Salt
  - 2 tsp Baking Powder
  - 2 tbsp Honey
  - 3/4 cup Fresh Blueberries
  - Butter for greasing the griddle
  - Salted butter and maple syrup for serving (optional)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Whisk the eggs and milk until foamy, then stir the flour in briefly and let the batter rest for five minutes. Sprinkle berries onto each wet pancake so they stay evenly distributed. The goal is tender golden pancakes with cooked centers and berries in every bite.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Heat a griddle to 350°F, or a large nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Lightly grease with the separate butter allowance; the measured melted butter all goes into the batter.
2. **Whisk the wet ingredients:** In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, and vanilla until light and foamy, about 2–3 minutes. Whisk in the cooled melted butter and honey until evenly combined.
3. **Add the dry ingredients:** Whisk the flour, salt, and baking powder together in another bowl, then add them to the wet mixture. Stir with a spatula just until no dry flour pockets remain. Small lumps are fine; scrape the bottom and sides, then stop rather than beating the batter smooth.
4. **Rest:** Let the batter sit for 5 minutes while the griddle finishes heating. Do not vigorously stir it again.
5. **Portion and add berries:** Drop batter by 1/4 cupfuls, leaving room to turn each pancake. Immediately sprinkle 1 tbsp blueberries onto each wet surface. Distribute the listed berries across the batch; the original 3/4 cup supplies twelve tablespoon portions.
6. **Cook and turn:** Cook until the underside is golden and the edges begin to set, with bubbles forming and popping, about 2 minutes. Flip gently and cook about 2–2 1/2 minutes more, until the center has no wet batter. Lower the heat if the exterior darkens before the center cooks. Repeat with the remaining batter, lightly renewing the griddle butter as needed.
7. **Serve:** Serve immediately, with salted butter and warm maple syrup if desired. If finishing another griddle round, hold the cooked pancakes briefly on a covered oven-safe platter in a 200°F oven. Covered pancakes may soften; serve promptly once the batch is ready.

RECIPE: Peking Ravioli (boston-style-peking-ravioli.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/boston-style-peking-ravioli/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Ground Pork (not too lean)
  - 2 cups Napa Cabbage, finely minced and squeezed dry
  - 3 stalks Green Onion, minced
  - 1 tbsp Ginger, freshly grated
  - 2 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1 tbsp Shaoxing Wine
  - 1 tbsp Soy Sauce
  - 1 tsp Toasted Sesame Oil
  - 1/2 tsp White Pepper
  - 1 tsp Salt
  - 2 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 3/4 cup Boiling Water
  - 1/4 cup Soy Sauce
  - 2 tbsp Chinkiang Black Vinegar (or Balsamic fallback)
  - 1 tbsp Brown Sugar or Molasses
  - 1 tbsp Ginger, finely grated
  - 1 tsp Chili Crisp (optional)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Peking ravioli (also called potstickers) were popularized in Boston by Joyce Chen's restaurant in the 1950s-60s. The Boston style is distinctive for its thick, chewy wrapper - more like pasta than delicate dim sum. The secret is using boiling water to make the dough, which partially cooks the flour and creates a chewier texture that stays soft even after frying. The bottom should be fried until deeply golden and crispy. A ginger-forward dipping sauce with black vinegar and a touch of sweetness is traditional.

## Directions

### The Thick Wrappers

1.  **Mix:** Place flour in a bowl. Slowly pour in the boiling water while stirring with chopsticks until a shaggy dough forms.
2.  **Knead:** Knead for 5-8 minutes until smooth. Cover with a damp cloth and let rest for 30 minutes.
3.  **Roll:** Divide into small balls. Roll each into a circle about 3.5 inches wide. They should be significantly thicker than a standard wonton wrapper (about 1/8 inch).

### The Filling

1.  **Squeeze:** Ensure the minced cabbage is salted and squeezed in a towel to remove ALL moisture. (Watery cabbage = soggy ravioli).
2.  **Mix:** Combine all filling ingredients. Stir vigorously in one direction for 3 minutes until the meat is sticky and emulsified.

### Assembly

1.  **Portion:** Place a large tablespoon of filling in each wrapper.
2.  **Seal:** Fold in half and pleat only 3-4 times (the Boston style is more rustic and "chunky" than delicate). Press hard to seal.

### The "Boston Fry"

1.  **Sear:** Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large flat-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat. Place ravioli in the pan and fry undisturbed for 2-3 minutes until the bottoms are dark golden.
2.  **Steam:** Pour in 1/2 cup of water and immediately cover with a tight lid. Reduce heat to medium and steam for 6-8 minutes until the water is gone.
3.  **Crisp:** Remove lid. Add 1 more tsp of oil. Fry for 1 more minute until the bottoms "crackle" and are perfectly crisp.

RECIPE: Boulevardier (boulevardier.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/boulevardier/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 oz bourbon or rye whiskey
  - 1 oz red Italian bitter aperitif
  - 1 oz sweet vermouth
  - Ice for stirring
  - Orange peel for garnish
CONTENT:

## Directions

1. **Combine:** Add the bourbon, red Italian bitter aperitif and sweet vermouth to a mixing glass filled with ice.

2. **Stir well for 20-30:** seconds until properly chilled.

3. **Strain into a chilled:** coupe glass or over a large ice cube in an Old Fashioned glass.

4. **Express an orange peel:** over the drink and garnish.

5. **Serve immediately.:**

## Chef's Note

Created in 1920s Paris by American expat Erskine Gwynne, editor of a magazine called 'The Boulevardier,' this cocktail embodies the era of Americans living the high life in post-WWI Paris. It's essentially a whiskey Negroni, swapping gin for bourbon or rye, and was popular at Harry's New York Bar, the legendary watering hole of Hemingway and F. Scott Fitzgerald. The equal-parts ratio (1:1:1) is traditional, but many prefer more whiskey (1.5 or 2 oz) for a less bitter, more spirit-forward drink.

RECIPE: Braised French Lentils (braised-french-lentils.md)
CUISINES: French
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/braised-french-lentils/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 cups French Green Lentils (lentilles du Puy), rinsed and picked over
  - 2 tbsp Olive Oil
  - 1 medium Onion, finely diced
  - 2 medium Carrots, finely diced
  - 2 stalks Celery, finely diced
  - 4 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 2 sprigs Fresh Thyme
  - 1 Bay Leaf
  - 1 tbsp Dijon Mustard
  - 3.5 cups Low-Sodium Vegetable or Chicken Broth
  - 1 tbsp Red Wine Vinegar
  - 2 tbsp Fresh Parsley, chopped
  - 1 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1/2 tsp Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

French green lentils (lentilles du Puy) are the only lentils worth braising as a side dish. Unlike their brown or red cousins, they hold their shape beautifully and develop a firm, almost al dente bite. Building the flavor base with a proper mirepoix -- onion, carrot, celery sauteed until softened -- gives these humble legumes a backbone of savory depth. The splash of vinegar and mustard at the end is essential: it lifts the earthiness and prevents the dish from tasting flat.

## Directions

1.  **Build the Base:** Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven or heavy saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 6-7 minutes until the vegetables are softened and the onion is translucent. Add garlic and cook 1 minute more until fragrant.

2.  **Add Lentils and Aromatics:** Stir in the lentils, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Pour in the broth and stir to combine. Bring to a boil over high heat.

3.  **Braise:** Reduce heat to low, partially cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape. They should be creamy inside with a slight bite. Most of the liquid should be absorbed -- if it evaporates too quickly, add a splash of water.

4.  **Finish:** Remove the thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Stir in the Dijon mustard and red wine vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Fold in the fresh parsley just before serving.

RECIPE: Breakfast Burrito (breakfast-burrito.md)
CUISINES: Mexican, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/breakfast-burrito/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6 large Eggs
  - 2 tbsp Whole Milk
  - 1/4 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1 tbsp Unsalted Butter
  - 1/2 cup Red or Green Bell Pepper, diced small
  - 1/4 cup Yellow Onion, diced small
  - 1 cup Shredded Cheddar or Pepper Jack Cheese
  - 4 large (10-inch) Flour Tortillas
  - 4 slices Cooked Bacon or 1/2 cup Cooked Breakfast Sausage, crumbled
  - Optional: salsa, hot sauce, sour cream, avocado slices
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A good breakfast burrito is all about assembly order and restraint -- overfill it and it becomes an unwrappable mess. Cooking the peppers and onions first gives them time to soften and release their moisture before the eggs go in, preventing a soggy tortilla. Warming the tortillas in a dry skillet for 15-20 seconds per side makes them pliable enough to fold tightly without cracking. These freeze beautifully: wrap tightly in foil, freeze for up to a month, and reheat in a 375 degree F oven for 20 minutes straight from frozen.

## Directions

1.  **Cook Vegetables:** Melt butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add bell pepper and onion. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened.
2.  **Scramble Eggs:** Whisk eggs with milk and salt. Pour into the skillet with the vegetables. Stir gently with a spatula, folding from the edges to the center, until the eggs are just set but still slightly glossy, about 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat immediately.
3.  **Warm Tortillas:** In a separate dry skillet over medium-high heat, warm each tortilla for 15-20 seconds per side until pliable and lightly toasted.
4.  **Assemble:** Lay each tortilla flat. Layer in the center: a quarter of the scrambled egg mixture, a quarter of the cheese, and a quarter of the cooked bacon or sausage. Add optional toppings if desired.
5.  **Roll:** Fold the bottom edge of the tortilla up over the filling, fold both sides in, then roll tightly away from you to seal. The cheese should melt from the residual heat of the eggs.
6.  **Serve:** Serve immediately with salsa and hot sauce on the side. For meal prep, wrap each burrito tightly in foil before the cheese is added, let cool, and freeze.

RECIPE: Breakfast Carrot Cake (breakfast-carrot-cake.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/breakfast-carrot-cake/
SOURCE: Adapted from southerneatsandgoodies.com
SOURCE_URL: https://southerneatsandgoodies.com/easy-breakfast-carrot-cake/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Cake ---
  - 250 g carrots, finely grated; about 2 large carrots at the original batch size
  - 1 1/4 cups whole wheat flour
  - 1 large egg
  - 1/4 cup granulated sugar
  - 1/4 cup brown sugar, packed
  - 1/2 cup canola or avocado oil
  - 1/3 cup plain Greek yogurt
  - 1 tsp vanilla extract
  - 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
  - 3/4 tsp baking powder
  - 1/2 tsp baking soda
  - 1/4 tsp sea salt
  - 1/4 cup walnuts or pecans, chopped
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Fine carrot shreds distribute through the whole-wheat crumb, while the full oil and yogurt amounts keep the mixture rich. Whisk the wet ingredients thoroughly, then fold the flour mixture gently until moistened and mix in all the carrots and nuts. Give the baked cake its pan rest before lifting it; cool it completely before adding cream-cheese frosting or wrapping for storage.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment for the original batch.
2. **Grate:** Wash and peel the carrots. Finely grate the carrots using the small holes of a grater. Use the listed weight; the original two-large-carrot description is only a shopping guide.
3. **Wet ingredients:** In a large bowl, whisk large egg, granulated sugar, brown sugar, canola or avocado oil, plain Greek yogurt, and vanilla extract for about 3–5 minutes until thoroughly blended and frothy.
4. **Dry ingredients:** Whisk whole wheat flour, ground cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda, and sea salt together to distribute the leaveners and spice, then fold gently into the wet mixture until moistened without dry flour pockets.
5. **Fold:** Add carrots and walnuts or pecans. Fold gently until evenly distributed, stopping once combined.
6. **Bake:** Spread the batter evenly in the prepared pan and tap lightly. Load only once the oven has reached 375°F / 190°C. Begin checking at about 25–30 minutes: the center should be set, spring back gently and give a tester without wet batter. Continue as needed; pan material, filling depth and oven temperature affect the time. Pan dimensions and baking time do not multiply with ingredient scale; use suitable smaller pans or additional pans to keep similar filling depth.
7. **Cool:** Let stand in the pan for 10 minutes, then lift gently onto a wire rack. Cool completely before frosting or wrapping; warm serving after the pan rest is also an option.

RECIPE: Breakfast Egg Cups (breakfast-egg-cups.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/breakfast-egg-cups/
SOURCE: Adapted from superhealthykids.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.superhealthykids.com/recipes/breakfast-egg-cups-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6 large Eggs
  - 1/4 cup Whole Milk
  - 1/8 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1/8 tsp Black Pepper
  - 1 medium Red Bell Pepper, finely diced
  - 1 cup Fresh Spinach, chiffonade
  - 1 oz Sharp Cheddar Cheese, shredded
  - Cooking spray
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Thin spinach ribbons and finely diced pepper distribute through the egg cups instead of forming large pockets. Whisk until the eggs and milk are blended, then stop; excessive foam is not needed. Let the cups settle for five minutes before loosening them from the well-greased tin.

## Directions

1. **Prep:** Preheat the oven to 375 °F. Generously coat standard muffin cups with the cooking spray, including the sides. The original batch makes about eight cups; keep extra greased cups available if the chopped pepper changes the volume.

2. **The Base:** Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper until no separate streaks of white remain; do not whip to a thick foam.

3. **The Veg:** Wash and dry the pepper and spinach. Finely dice the pepper. Stack the spinach leaves, roll them together and slice thin ribbons.

4. **Combine:** Fold the pepper, spinach and shredded cheddar into the eggs until distributed throughout.

6. **Bake:** Bake for about 20–25 minutes, until the centers are opaque and set, with no liquid egg when gently moved, and reach 160 °F / 71 °C. Measure a center without touching the metal tin. Continue baking if needed rather than relying on surface browning alone.

7. **Cool and store:** Let stand in the tin for 5 minutes, then loosen gently and remove. Refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers and use within 3–4 days. Reheat the center to 165 °F / 74 °C; 30 seconds in a microwave is not a dependable endpoint.

RECIPE: Breakfast Protein Biscuits (breakfast-protein-biscuits.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/breakfast-protein-biscuits/
SOURCE: Adapted from nourishedbynic.com
SOURCE_URL: https://nourishedbynic.com/breakfast-protein-biscuits/#recipe
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 1/2 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 1 3/4 cups Plain 2% Greek Yogurt
  - 4 large Eggs
  - 1/4 cup Ground Flaxseed
  - 1 tbsp Baking Powder
  - 2 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1 1/2 cups Fresh Spinach, finely chopped
  - 1/2 cup Fresh Chives, finely diced
  - 1 1/2 cups Sharp Cheddar, shredded
  - 2 cups Cooked Ham, diced small
  - 1 tsp Garlic Powder
  - 1/2 tsp Red Pepper Flakes
  - A little flour for dusting your hands
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Greek yogurt and eggs make a thick, sticky dough with chopped spinach, chives and cooked ham. Fold the fillings and two thirds of the cheese through it so each biscuit gets a share, then use the remaining cheese on top. Browned cheese is a surface cue; check that the thick centers are cooked before cooling or packing the biscuits.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a large baking sheet, or additional sheets as needed, with parchment. Use cooked ham, diced small. Wash and dry the spinach and chives, then chop them finely.

2. **Wet and dry:** Whisk all the yogurt and eggs in a large bowl. Separately whisk all the measured flour, flaxseed, garlic powder, red pepper flakes, baking powder and sea salt until distributed.

3. **Combine:** Add the dry mixture to the wet mixture gradually, stirring until the flour is moistened and a thick, sticky dough forms without dry pockets.

4. **Fold:** Fold in all the spinach, chives, cooked ham and two thirds of the measured cheddar. Distribute the fillings through the dough, stopping once combined; use your hands gently if needed. Keep the remaining one third of the cheese for the tops.

5. **Shape:** Lightly dust your hands with the separate flour allowance. Divide the whole dough evenly into the listed number of biscuits; the original batch plans twelve. Form disks about 1 inch thick with space between them on the prepared sheets. Use additional sheets or oven loads rather than crowding them or discarding extra dough.

6. **Bake:** Scatter all the remaining measured cheese over the biscuits. Load only once the oven has reached 400°F. Bake at 400°F for 5 minutes, then reduce the oven setting to 350°F without opening the door and bake about 20 minutes more. Keep the same temperature sequence for additional oven loads; do not multiply the heat settings or make thicker disks when scaling.

7. **Check and cool:** The bottoms should be golden and the cheese browned, with set centers and no wet flour or egg mixture. Check the center of a thick biscuit; for this cooked-ham-and-egg bake, use 165°F as the casserole-style endpoint. Continue baking as needed. Let stand briefly until firm enough to move, then serve warm or cool promptly before packing.

RECIPE: Breakfast Quesadilla (breakfast-quesadilla.md)
CUISINES: Mexican, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/breakfast-quesadilla/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 large Eggs
  - 1 tbsp Unsalted Butter
  - 1/4 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 2 large (10-inch) Flour Tortillas
  - 1 cup Shredded Cheddar or Mexican Blend Cheese
  - 2 tbsp Pickled Jalapenos, chopped (optional)
  - Salsa and sour cream for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A breakfast quesadilla should be crispy on the outside, melty on the inside, and ready in under 15 minutes. The key is scrambling the eggs first and slightly undercooking them -- they will continue to cook inside the quesadilla from the residual heat and the time on the griddle. Using a dry skillet over medium heat (no oil) to cook the quesadilla allows the tortilla to crisp without becoming greasy. Press gently with a spatula while cooking to ensure the cheese makes full contact with the eggs and creates a cohesive, sliceable pocket.

## Directions

1.  **Scramble Eggs:** Melt butter in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Whisk eggs with salt and pour into the skillet. Stir gently with a spatula until the eggs are just barely set -- slightly wetter than you would normally eat them. Remove to a plate.
2.  **Build the Quesadilla:** Wipe the skillet clean. Lay one tortilla flat. Spread half the cheese on one half of the tortilla, top with half the scrambled eggs and jalapenos (if using), then add the remaining cheese on top. Fold the tortilla in half. Repeat with the second tortilla.
3.  **Cook:** Place the quesadilla in the dry skillet over medium heat. Cook for 2-3 minutes, pressing gently with a spatula, until the bottom is golden brown and crispy. Flip carefully and cook for 2 minutes more until the other side is golden and the cheese is fully melted.
4.  **Slice and Serve:** Transfer to a cutting board. Let rest for 30 seconds, then cut into thirds. Serve with salsa and sour cream on the side.

RECIPE: Brisket with Carrots and Onions (brisket-with-carrots-and-onions.md)
CUISINES: Jewish
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/brisket-with-carrots-and-onions/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodnetwork.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/ina-garten/brisket-with-carrots-and-onions-recipe-1944457
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6–7 lb beef brisket flat cut
  - 2 tbsp kosher salt
  - 2 tsp black pepper
  - 1 tbsp minced garlic
  - 2 tsp dried oregano
  - 1 lb carrots, cut into 2-inch chunks
  - 8 celery stalks, cut into 2-inch chunks
  - 6 large yellow onions, sliced
  - 6 fresh bay leaves
  - 1 (46 oz) can tomato juice
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This tomato-brisket braise uses flat cut, carrots, celery, onions and six bay
leaves. A tight cover gives the brisket time to become
tender without adding a sear. The final reduction is a separate stage: remove the
meat, discard the bay leaves, and concentrate the vegetables and tomato juice
only until the sauce still generously coats the sliced brisket.

## Directions

1. **Heat the oven and prepare the pan:** Heat the oven to 350°F / 175°C. Choose a heavy roasting pan that holds the brisket in one layer with the vegetables and has room for the full can of tomato juice below its rim.
2. **Season the brisket:** Mix the kosher salt, pepper, garlic and oregano. Rub the mixture over all sides of the brisket.
3. **Layer the braise:** Put the brisket in the pan. Arrange all the carrots, celery, onions and bay leaves on and around it.
4. **Add the tomato juice and seal:** Pour in the entire 46-ounce can of tomato juice. The pan geometry and vegetables determine how high it comes around the meat; it does not need to reach a fixed mark. Lay two sheets of parchment over the pan, then seal tightly with heavy-duty foil.
5. **Braise until tender:** Bake, covered, for about 3 1/2 hours. Check the thickest part with an instant-read thermometer: it must reach at least 145°F / 63°C, followed by a 3-minute rest, and it must also be fork-tender. If the temperature is safe but the fork meets resistance, re-cover and continue in 15-minute intervals until tender.
6. **Rest and reduce:** Transfer the brisket to a cutting board and tent loosely with foil. Remove and discard all bay leaves. If the roasting pan is approved for stovetop use across two burners, use it; otherwise transfer all vegetables and sauce to a wide saucepan. Boil over medium-high heat for 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until glossy and thickened but still saucy.
7. **Slice and serve:** Find the direction of the meat fibers and slice across the grain. Serve the brisket with the reduced sauce, carrots, celery and onions.

RECIPE: Broccoli all'Agro (broccoli-all-agro.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/broccoli-all-agro/
SOURCE: Saved Paprika recipe
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 large heads Broccoli (florets only)
  - 2 tbsp Extra Virgin Olive Oil
  - 1 Lemon (Juice and Zest)
  - 1 small clove Garlic (grated into paste)
  - 1/2 tsp Salt
  - Water, as needed for steaming
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Lemon juice and zest dress the steamed broccoli, with raw grated garlic for a sharp finish. Drain off surface water before gently tossing the hot florets with all the dressing. Keep the broccoli tender-crisp rather than forcing every batch into the same steaming time.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Wash the broccoli and cut the listed florets to similar sizes. Wash the lemon, zest it before juicing, and grate the garlic into a paste. Set up a steamer following its instructions, with cooking water below the basket and enough headroom for the florets; bring the water to a simmer.

2. **Make the dressing:** Whisk all the measured olive oil, lemon juice and zest, garlic and salt in a large serving bowl. This dressing keeps the garlic raw; do not hold a garlic-and-oil mixture at room temperature for later storage.

3. **Steam:** Add the broccoli to the basket, cover and steam. Start checking at 4–5 minutes: a fork should enter the thickest floret stem with slight resistance and the florets should remain intact. Continue as needed for their actual size. Use separate loads if the steamer is crowded.

4. **Drain and toss:** Lift out carefully, keeping clear of steam, and let excess surface water drain briefly. Add the hot broccoli to the dressing and toss gently until coated, scraping the bowl so the measured dressing reaches the whole batch. Serve promptly.

## Cooking Notes

The original batch uses two large heads and makes about six side portions; head size affects yield. When scaling, use the head count in the ingredient list.

Use a larger steamer or separate loads when scaling. Keep florets similarly sized and divide the measured dressing across loads; neither steaming time nor pot dimensions scale proportionally.

About 15–25 min includes preparation, heating and cooking; larger batches and product directions can add time.

Refrigerate promptly in a shallow covered container at 40°F / 4°C or below. Limit time out to 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C. Use within 3–4 days. Refrigerate any extra fresh garlic dressing promptly; lemon is not a validated preservation process. Reheated broccoli softens; reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C.

RECIPE: Broccolini, Chicken Sausage, and Orzo Skillet (broccolini-chicken-sausage-and-orzo-skillet.md)
CUISINES: Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/broccolini-chicken-sausage-and-orzo-skillet/
SOURCE: Adapted from Thekitchn.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.thekitchn.com/recipe-broccolini-chicken-sausage-and-orzo-skillet-234135
INGREDIENTS:
  - 8 oz fully cooked hot Italian chicken sausage, sliced into 1/4-inch rounds
  - 1 cup Orzo pasta
  - 2 bunches broccolini (about 1 lb total), trimmed and coarsely chopped
  - 2 1/2 cups Chicken Broth
  - 2 tbsp Olive Oil
  - 2 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1/2 cup Grated Parmesan
  - Salt and Black Pepper
  - 1 cup frozen peas, optional replacement for the broccolini; do not add both
  - Hot water, as needed for firm or dry orzo
  - Additional grated Parmesan, for serving, optional
  - Chile flakes, for serving, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Use fully cooked chicken sausage, then keep it and the sautéed broccolini aside while the orzo absorbs the broth. Return both only when the pasta is tender, and stir in the full Parmesan off heat. The peas option replaces the broccolini and goes into the simmer near the end.

## Directions

1. **Brown the cooked sausage:** Heat all the olive oil over medium-high heat in a roomy skillet with a lid. Add the fully cooked sausage rounds and brown for about 3–4 minutes, then transfer to a clean plate. Raw chicken sausage needs its own complete cooking method and is not a direct substitute.

2. **Cook the vegetable:** Wash and dry broccolini, trim the woody ends and coarsely chop it. Begin checking around 10 minutes, guided by the orzo package, until the center is tender with a little bite. If tender pasta has pooled broth, uncover and simmer briefly. If the pan is dry while the center is firm, add a little of the hot-water allowance and continue. When using the frozen-peas option, add the full chosen amount near the end and allow enough time to heat it through.

5. **Return and enrich:** Return all the reserved fully cooked sausage and broccolini, if used. Stir over low heat until hot throughout, then remove from heat and incorporate all the measured Parmesan.

6. **Finish:** Use a little hot water only if needed to loosen the pasta. Taste and adjust with the listed salt and black pepper. Serve promptly, with the separate optional extra Parmesan or chile flakes.
