RECIPE: Chicken & Spinach Pasta with Lemon (chicken-and-spinach-skillet-pasta-with-lemon-and-parmesan.md)
CUISINES: Italian, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-and-spinach-skillet-pasta-with-lemon-and-parmesan/
SOURCE: Adapted from eatingwell.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/267768/chicken-spinach-skillet-pasta-with-lemon-parmesan/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 12 oz (340 g) dried penne or rigatoni
  - 1 lb (450 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
  - 10 oz (280 g) baby spinach, washed and thoroughly drained
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - 4 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) dry white wine
  - 1 tsp finely grated lemon zest
  - 1–2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 1/2 cup (30 g) finely grated Parmesan
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, for the chicken
  - 1/4 tsp black pepper, plus more to taste
  - 1 1/2 tsp fine salt, for 3 quarts pasta water
  - 1 cup (240 ml) reserved pasta water, added as needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Spinach, pasta, and cheese all change the water balance of the pan. Start with a little reserved cooking water, let the spinach wilt, then decide whether more is needed. Lemon zest contributes aroma without much acidity; juice is added at the end so you can control the tartness.

## Directions

1. **Boil the pasta:** Bring 3 quarts water and the pasta-water salt to a boil. Add pasta and stir. Cook until about 1 minute short of the package's suggested time, tasting for a slightly firm center. Reserve 1 cup cooking water before draining.
2. **Cook chicken alongside:** Pat chicken dry and season with its measured salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a deep 12-inch skillet over medium-high. Cook in a single layer, turning occasionally, for about 6–9 minutes, until golden in patches and several larger pieces measure 165°F / 74°C. Work in batches if needed. Transfer to a clean plate.
3. **Build the sauce:** Reduce heat to medium and add the remaining oil. Stir in garlic for about 30 seconds, until fragrant but not brown. Add wine and scrape up golden residue. Simmer 2–4 minutes, until reduced by roughly half.
4. **Finish the pasta:** Add drained pasta and 1/3 cup reserved water to the skillet. Toss over medium-low heat for 1–2 minutes, until the pasta is just tender. Add a splash of water if it sticks.
5. **Wilt the greens:** Add spinach in two or three batches, tossing each until it begins to wilt. Return cooked chicken and its juices. Toss just until the chicken is hot and the spinach is fully wilted, about 2–3 minutes. Keep a little liquid in the pan; add reserved water only as needed.
6. **Add cheese and lemon:** Remove the skillet from heat and wait until active bubbling stops. Add Parmesan in two additions while tossing. Add the zest and the lower end of the listed lemon-juice range. Taste a complete bite, then add more juice, pepper, or a pinch of salt if needed. Loosen with water by the tablespoon and serve promptly.

RECIPE: Chicken and White Bean Enchiladas (chicken-and-white-bean-enchiladas-with-creamy-green-chile-sauce.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-and-white-bean-enchiladas-with-creamy-green-chile-sauce/
SOURCE: Adapted from Skinnytaste.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.skinnytaste.com/chicken-and-white-bean-enchiladas-with/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Creamy green sauce ---
  - 12 oz tomatillo salsa or enchilada sauce
  - 1/2 cup light sour cream or Greek yogurt
  - 1 can (4 oz) diced green chiles
  - 1/2 cup fresh cilantro, washed
  - --- Filled rolls ---
  - 1 lb cooked shredded chicken, poached or rotisserie; cooled and stored safely if prepared ahead
  - 1 can (15 oz) navy or cannellini beans, fully cooked canned beans, rinsed and drained
  - 1 tsp ground cumin
  - 8 flour tortillas (8-inch)
  - 1 cup Mexican cheese blend, shredded
  - --- Optional garnish ---
  - additional fresh cilantro, washed and chopped, as wanted for garnish, optional
  - pickled red onions, as wanted for garnish, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The creamy green sauce uses prepared salsa, green chiles and all the listed sour cream or yogurt. Reserve sauce for the filling and dish before topping the rolls, and divide the full chicken-and-bean filling among all tortillas. Bubbling edges and brown cheese are useful cues, but check the center filling temperature as well.

## Directions

1. **Blend sauce:** Preheat the oven to 375°F. Blend tomatillo salsa or enchilada sauce, light sour cream or Greek yogurt, diced green chiles, and fresh cilantro smooth in a blender suited to this cold sauce. The full measured salsa and dairy belong in this mixture; garnish cilantro is separate.

Divide all the filling evenly among all tortillas, roll and place seam-side down. Use additional or suitably smaller dishes for altered batches; preserve roll size and room for sauce rather than multiplying pan dimensions.
4. **Top:** Pour all remaining blended sauce over the rolls, then cover with Mexican cheese blend. The filling, bottom layer and topping together use the whole sauce once.
5. **Bake:** Bake at 375°F, starting to check after 20–25 minutes, until the center of the filling reaches 165°F / 74°C and the sauce is bubbling. Cover loosely with foil if the cheese browns before the center is hot; chilled filling may take longer.
6. **Finish:** Let stand briefly until manageable to portion, then garnish with additional fresh cilantro (if using) and pickled red onions (if using) if wanted. [Quick Pickled Red Onions](/mise/recipes/pickled-red-onions) are a separately prepared recipe. Serve all rolls; the original planning yield is eight enchiladas, one per serving with separately prepared sides.

RECIPE: Chicken and Wild Rice Soup (chicken-and-wild-rice-soup.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-and-wild-rice-soup/
SOURCE: Adapted from Chowhound.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.chowhound.com/recipes/chicken-and-wild-rice-soup-11481
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup (160 g) uncooked wild rice; check the package for processing and cook time
  - 4 cups (960 ml) water, for cooking rice, plus more as needed
  - 2 tbsp olive oil
  - 1 large yellow onion, diced
  - 3 medium carrots, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
  - 3 celery stalks, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
  - 4 cloves garlic, minced
  - 8 cups (1.9 liters) low-sodium chicken broth, plus up to 2 cups to adjust consistency
  - 2 lbs (900 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
  - 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, plus more to taste
  - 1/2 tsp black pepper
  - 1–2 tbsp lemon juice, to taste
  - 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Wild rice is the seed of an aquatic grass. Its processing changes how quickly it cooks, so a dark-finished grain and a quick-cook product should not share a rigid timer. Cooking it separately also lets you keep this soup brothy and finish the chicken on its own schedule.

## Directions

1. **Cook the grain:** Rinse the wild rice. Combine with the measured rice-cooking water in a saucepan and bring to a boil. Reduce to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook according to the package range, checking early for quick-cook grain. Add hot water if the pan dries before the rice is tender. When many grains open and have a tender, chewy center, drain any excess water.
2. **Soften vegetables:** While the rice simmers, heat oil in a 6-quart pot over medium heat. Add onion, carrots, and celery. Cook 8–10 minutes, stirring, until the onion is softened. Add garlic and cook about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
3. **Build the broth:** Add the initial measured chicken broth, thyme, salt, and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook about 8–10 minutes, until carrots are approaching tenderness; they will cook further with the chicken.
4. **Poach the chicken:** Add chicken and return gently to a simmer. Cook about 12–18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until several larger pieces reach 165°F / 74°C and the vegetables are tender. Avoid a rolling boil.
5. **Combine:** Stir in the tender, drained rice and heat through. Add extra broth as needed to keep the soup spoonable and brothy. If the rice is not yet ready, keep the soup gently hot while it finishes; do not keep boiling the chicken.
6. **Finish:** Add parsley and the lower end of the listed lemon-juice range. Taste the broth with some chicken and rice, then add more lemon, salt, or pepper as needed. Ladle into eight bowls. For planned leftovers, keep the remaining rice and soup separate before chilling promptly.

RECIPE: Chicken, Apple, and Butternut Stew (chicken-apple-and-butternut-stew.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-apple-and-butternut-stew/
SOURCE: Adapted from Myrecipes.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.myrecipes.com/recipe/chicken-apple-butternut-stew
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 lbs (900 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, divided, plus more to taste
  - 1/2 tsp black pepper
  - 1 large yellow onion, diced
  - 1 cup (130 g) parsnip, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
  - 1 tbsp chopped fresh sage
  - 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
  - 3 tbsp (25 g) all-purpose flour
  - 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) unsweetened apple cider (cloudy apple juice, not vinegar or hard cider)
  - 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) low-sodium chicken stock, plus more as needed
  - 3 cups (420 g) butternut squash, peeled, seeded, and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
  - 2 cups (250 g) Granny Smith apple, cored and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
  - 1–2 tsp apple cider vinegar, optional, to finish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This stew depends on contrast: savory chicken, sweet squash and cider, aromatic sage, and tart apple. The ingredients do not soften at the same speed. Smaller parsnip pieces get a head start; squash simmers with the chicken; apple goes in only near the end.

## Directions

1. **Brown chicken in batches:** Pat chicken dry and season with half the salt and the pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high. Brown half the chicken for about 3 minutes per side, then transfer to a temporary plate. Repeat with remaining oil and chicken. It need not be cooked through yet.
2. **Soften the base:** Reduce heat to medium. Add onion, parsnip, and remaining salt. Cook about 7–9 minutes, stirring, until onion is softened and lightly golden. Add a small splash of stock if the browned residue threatens to scorch. Add sage and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
3. **Disperse the flour:** Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and stir for 1 minute. Gradually stir in cider, scraping up golden residue and smoothing out flour pockets. Add stock and bring to a simmer.
4. **Simmer chicken and squash:** Return chicken and its accumulated juices. Add squash. Keep at a gentle simmer, partially covered, for about 18–25 minutes, stirring occasionally. Continue until squash and parsnip are tender and several larger chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Add stock if the sauce becomes too thick before the vegetables soften.
5. **Add apple late:** Fold in the apple and simmer 5–8 minutes, until hot and just tender but still holding its shape. Stir gently so the squash stays intact.
6. **Balance and serve:** Taste a spoonful containing sauce and vegetables. Add optional cider vinegar 1 tsp at a time if the stew needs more tartness, and adjust salt or pepper. Serve in six bowls with a green vegetable or salad.

RECIPE: Hyderabadi-style Chicken Biryani (chicken-biryani.md)
CUISINES: Indian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-biryani/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken marinade ---
  - 2.5 lbs (1.13 kg) boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into pieces about 2 inches across and no more than 1 inch thick
  - 1 cup (240 g) full-fat plain yogurt
  - 2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (or 1 tbsp each finely grated ginger and garlic)
  - 2 tsp Kashmiri chile powder
  - 1 tsp ground turmeric
  - 1 tsp garam masala
  - 1 tsp ground cumin
  - 1 tsp ground coriander
  - 1 1/2 tsp fine salt, for the chicken
  - 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 1/2 cup loosely packed chopped cilantro, divided
  - 1/2 cup loosely packed chopped mint, divided
  - --- Rice ---
  - 2 1/2 cups (500 g) aged basmati rice, not parboiled or quick-cooking
  - 10 cups (2.4 liters) water, for boiling the rice
  - 1 tbsp fine salt, for the rice water
  - 4 green cardamom pods, lightly cracked
  - 1 black cardamom pod, optional
  - 1 cinnamon stick, about 2 inches long
  - 4 whole cloves
  - 2 bay leaves
  - 1 tsp cumin seeds
  - --- Onions and layering ---
  - 3 large yellow onions (about 600 g trimmed total), sliced evenly about 1/8 inch thick
  - 1 cup (240 ml) neutral oil, for frying onions
  - 2 tbsp of the drained onion frying oil, reserved for layering
  - 1/4 tsp saffron threads
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) warm whole milk
  - 2 tbsp (28 g) ghee, melted
  - 1 tsp food-grade rose water or kewra water, optional (not concentrated essence or essential oil)
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water, only if needed during cooking
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Hyderabadi-style biryani uses the kacchi approach: raw marinated chicken is layered beneath partially cooked rice, then both finish in a covered pot. The central problem is coordination. The rice must retain enough firmness to finish with the chicken, and the burner must sustain steam without scorching the bottom. Aromas and elapsed time help you follow the process; a thermometer and a tasted grain establish the final endpoints.

## Directions

1. **Marinate 4–24 hours:** Mix yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chile powder, turmeric, garam masala, ground cumin, ground coriander, the chicken salt, lemon juice, half the cilantro, and half the mint. Coat the chicken, cover, and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below. Do not leave raw chicken out while preparing the other components.
2. **Fry onions:** Heat the neutral oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Fry onions in two batches, stirring frequently, until evenly golden brown, about 12–18 minutes per batch. Lower heat as they color; lift them out before dark brown. Drain in a metal strainer over a heatproof bowl, then spread on a tray lined with paper towels. Reserve 2 tbsp drained onion oil for the biryani; the remaining frying oil is not poured into the dish.
3. **Prepare rice and saffron:** While the onions cook, rinse basmati in several changes of cool water, soak for 20–30 minutes, and drain. Steep saffron in the warm milk for at least 15 minutes. Bring the measured rice water to a boil in a large pot with its salt, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaves, and cumin seeds.
4. **Partially cook rice:** Add the drained soaked rice to the boiling water. Stir once gently and return to a boil. Begin tasting at 3 minutes; drain when the outside is soft but the center is distinctly firm, often about 4–6 minutes depending on the rice. Do not wait until fully tender. Retain the whole spices with the rice, or remove large whole spices now if preferred.
5. **Layer promptly:** Spread the reserved 2 tbsp onion oil over the bottom of the heavy cooking pot. Take chicken from the refrigerator and spread it with all its marinade in an even layer. Scatter one-third of the fried onions over it. Spread the hot, drained rice on top without packing it down. Drizzle with saffron milk, melted ghee, and optional rose or kewra water. Scatter the remaining onions, cilantro, and mint over the top. Cover tightly; use a sheet of foil under the lid if needed for a snug fit.
6. **Cook under steam:** Heat over medium until you hear a gentle simmer and see light steam at the lid edge, about 5–8 minutes. Reduce heat enough to maintain that gentle simmer, rather than automatically using the lowest burner setting. Cook covered for 30 minutes, lowering heat if you smell scorching. Keep the lid closed between checks to retain steam.
7. **Verify before resting:** Open carefully away from your face. Probe several of the largest chicken pieces at the center and near the pot edge, avoiding the pot itself; each must reach 165°F / 74°C. Check the rice temperature in several places also reaches 165°F / 74°C, and taste a grain for tenderness without a chalky core. If either temperature or texture is short, re-cover and cook another 5–10 minutes before checking again. If rice is drying, sprinkle 2 tbsp hot water over it, with up to the remaining 2 tbsp as needed. Do not use resting time as a substitute for these endpoints.
8. **Rest and serve:** Once chicken and rice meet the checks, turn off heat and rest covered for 15 minutes. Lift portions from the bottom with a wide spoon so each serving includes chicken and rice, disturbing the grains as little as possible. Remove any visible whole spices and tell diners that some may remain. Serve with raita or kachumber salad; additional rice is unnecessary.

RECIPE: Chicken Chile Enchiladas (chicken-chile-enchiladas.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-chile-enchiladas/
SOURCE: Adapted from Thekitchn.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.thekitchn.com/recipe-chicken-chile-enchiladas-223930
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Enchiladas ---
  - 1 lb cooked shredded chicken, rotisserie or already pressure-cooked
  - 1 can (15 oz) red enchilada sauce, prepared; canned or the same measured amount of homemade sauce
  - 8 corn tortillas, already cooked tortillas; the brief oil stage is for flexibility, not cooking raw masa
  - 1 red bell pepper, finely diced
  - 1 can (4 oz) diced green chiles
  - 12 oz Mexican blend cheese, shredded; some inside each roll, all the remainder on top
  - cooking oil, a splash for briefly softening the corn tortillas
  - --- Garnishes ---
  - sour cream, as wanted for serving
  - fresh cilantro, as wanted for serving
  - sliced jalapeños, as wanted for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

These red-sauce enchiladas use corn tortillas warmed briefly in oil before dipping and rolling. Look for a tortilla that bends easily, then divide the filling among all the rolls and keep the full cheese amount for their centers and topping. The soft-tortilla option below uses the same chicken, pepper, chiles and cheese with a different assembly method.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the filling and dish:** Preheat the oven to 375°F. Choose an oven-safe baking dish that fits all the rolled tortillas in a single layer without stacking, or additional dishes for a larger batch. Keep cooked chicken refrigerated until working with it. Toss cooked shredded chicken, red bell pepper, and diced green chiles together in a bowl. Cooking raw chicken or making homemade sauce is a separate preparation, outside this assembly clock.
2. **Soften the corn tortillas:** Use corn tortillas and cooking oil: heat the splash of oil in a small skillet and briefly warm each tortilla in it, starting at about 5 seconds per side and continuing only until it bends readily. Work one at a time; do not crisp the tortilla so it breaks when rolled. Transfer each warm tortilla for filling.
3. **Dip, fill, roll and cover:** Use red enchilada sauce and Mexican blend cheese for dipping, filling and topping. Dip each warm tortilla into the sauce, divide all the prepared chicken filling among the measured tortillas, add a little of the cheese inside each and roll seam-side down in the dish. Pour all the remaining sauce over the rolls and distribute all the remaining cheese on top. Use up the full measured cheese and sauce between the centers and topping.
4. **Bake and check the center:** Bake at 375°F, starting to check after 15–20 minutes. The cheese should be melted and the sauce bubbling, but also check the filling in the center of the dish with a thermometer: it must reach 165°F / 74°C. If it is still cool inside, continue baking; cover if the surface is browning too much. Cold chicken, dish depth and extra dishes can extend the time.
5. **Serve with the garnishes:** Serve with sour cream, fresh cilantro, and sliced jalapeños. Keep the garnishes cold until serving.

## Soft-tortilla option

Use the same number of taco-size soft tortillas instead of corn tortillas and omit the flash-frying oil. Spread a thin layer from the measured sauce over the bottom of the dish, then divide all the measured chicken, pepper and green chiles among the tortillas. Put about 2 tbsp cheese and 2 tbsp sauce inside each taco-size tortilla, using only the measured totals, then roll seam-side down and put all remaining cheese and sauce on top. For the original eight taco-size soft tortillas, use one 9×13-inch or two 8×8-inch dishes only if the rolls actually fit. Use suitably fitted dishes for a different batch size, with the same single-layer arrangement. Bake at 375°F, starting at 15–20 minutes, and verify the filling reaches 165°F / 74°C. Mexican blend, Monterey Jack, cheddar or a mixture can supply all the measured cheese; the original batch uses 12 oz.

## Cooking Notes

For freezing and reheating, use a baking dish whose manufacturer permits the intended temperature changes. Follow its instructions for moving between freezer, refrigerator and oven.

You can freeze assembled, unbaked enchiladas or freeze them after baking and promptly chilling. Wrap well and freeze for up to 3 months for quality. For frozen unbaked enchiladas, the soft-tortilla recipe starts with 375°F, covered for 30 minutes then uncovered for 15 minutes; for previously baked frozen enchiladas, it starts with 350°F, covered for 10 minutes then uncovered for 10–20 minutes. Treat these as first checks, not guarantees for a different dish, batch size or tortilla: continue until the center is 165°F / 74°C. Cover again if the top is getting too dark. Individual cooked portions may be reheated in a microwave-safe dish following the appliance instructions; cover and rotate for even heating, allow the appliance's specified standing time, then check more than one location for 165°F / 74°C rather than relying on an unspecified microwave's fixed time.

RECIPE: Coq au Vin with Chicken Thighs (chicken-coq-au-vin.md)
CUISINES: French
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-coq-au-vin/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 lbs (900 g) bone-in skin-on chicken thighs
  - 4 oz (113 g) bacon or lardons, diced
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil, only if needed to supplement rendered fat
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, plus more only if needed
  - 1/2 tsp black pepper
  - 1 large yellow onion (about 200 g), chopped
  - 8 oz (225 g) fresh cremini mushrooms, halved or quartered if large
  - 3 medium carrots (about 250 g total), cut into 1-inch pieces
  - 4 cloves garlic, smashed
  - 2 cups (480 ml) dry red wine
  - 1 cup (240 ml) unsalted chicken stock, plus a little more if needed
  - 1 tbsp tomato paste
  - 2 sprigs fresh thyme
  - 2 tbsp (28 g) unsalted butter, cold and cubed
  - 2 tbsp chopped flat-leaf parsley
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This coq au vin uses modern chicken thighs, bacon, and a red-wine braise. Brown the mushrooms separately so they develop color instead of steaming among the carrots and onions. Gentle cooking then softens the chicken; a reduced sauce and an off-heat butter finish supply body and gloss. Wine remains an ingredient after cooking, so this is not an alcohol-free dish.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and render:** Pat chicken dry and season with the measured salt and pepper. Cook bacon in a wide Dutch oven over medium heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until it releases fat and begins to crisp. Transfer bacon to a bowl. Leave about 2 tbsp fat in the pot, adding some of the optional neutral oil if there is too little.
2. **Brown mushrooms:** Add mushrooms and cook over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until moisture evaporates and golden surfaces develop. Transfer to a separate bowl for the end of the braise.
3. **Brown chicken:** Keep about 2 tbsp fat in the pot. Sear chicken in two batches, skin-side down for 6–8 minutes, then 2 minutes on the other side. Transfer to a plate. Adjust heat if the browned residue darkens too far. Spoon out excess rendered fat, leaving about 2 tbsp.
4. **Cook vegetables:** Lower heat to medium. Add onion and carrots and cook 6–8 minutes, stirring, until onion softens. Add garlic and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute. Scrape away any black burned residue rather than incorporating it into the sauce.
5. **Reduce wine:** Take the pot briefly off the burner to add wine. Return to medium-high heat, scrape up golden browned residue, and simmer uncovered until the wine reduces by roughly half, about 10–15 minutes.
6. **Braise gently:** Return chicken, accumulated plate juices, and bacon. Add stock and thyme. Liquid should come about halfway to two-thirds up the thighs, not cover them; add a little stock only if needed. Bring to a simmer, cover, and lower heat to maintain gentle bubbles. Cook about 45–60 minutes, adding the reserved mushrooms for the last 10 minutes. Check meat away from the bone reaches at least 165°F / 74°C and feels tender near the joint; continue in 10-minute increments if still firm.
7. **Concentrate and finish:** Transfer tender chicken to a clean platter. Remove thyme stems and skim excess surface fat. Simmer the uncovered sauce about 5–10 minutes until it lightly coats a spoon. Turn off heat, let vigorous bubbling stop, and swirl in cold butter. Taste before adding any extra salt.
8. **Serve:** Return chicken to the warm sauce, spoon sauce over it, and finish with parsley. Serve with one starch such as mashed potatoes and a green vegetable.

RECIPE: Chicken Fingers (chicken-fingers.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-fingers/
SOURCE: Adapted from Lisa Gwock
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken ---
  - 1 lb chicken tenderloins or boneless skinless chicken breasts, breasts cut into even strips
  - cooking spray, as needed to coat the rack
  - 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
  - 2 large eggs
  - 1 tbsp water
  - 1 1/2 cups panko breadcrumbs
  - 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese
  - 1 tsp garlic powder
  - 1 tsp dried oregano
  - salt, to taste
  - black pepper, to taste
  - cooking spray, as needed to lightly coat the breaded chicken
  - --- Optional serving accompaniments ---
  - lemon wedges, for serving, optional
  - dipping sauce, for serving, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This panko-Parmesan adaptation of Lisa Gwock’s chicken fingers uses three shallow dishes to build an even coating. Shake off excess flour and egg before pressing on the crumbs, then leave space around the strips on an oven-safe rack. The cheese seasons the crust; use the thermometer to judge the chicken inside.

## Directions

1. **Prepare chicken and rack:** Set out chicken tenderloins or boneless skinless chicken breasts and cooking spray. Preheat the oven to 425°F. Set an oven-safe wire rack over a large rimmed sheet pan and spray the rack. If using breasts, cut even strips similar in thickness to tenderloins. Pat the chicken dry; do not rinse it.
2. **Bread:** Set out all-purpose flour, large eggs, water, panko breadcrumbs, grated Parmesan cheese, garlic powder, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper in three shallow dishes: flour with salt and pepper in the first; eggs beaten with the measured water in the second; panko, Parmesan, garlic powder and oregano in the third. Dip each strip in flour, shake off excess, dip in egg and let excess drip off, then press into crumbs on all sides. Arrange on the rack with gaps. Discard coating ingredients left after raw-chicken contact and wash hands and utensils.
3. **Bake and check:** Apply cooking spray lightly to the tops. Bake about 15–20 minutes, checking earlier for thin strips. The coating should be golden and the thickest part of every strip must reach 165°F / 74°C, measured from the side. Continue baking as needed. If the underside remains pale, turn the pieces carefully during cooking; a rack does not guarantee equal browning on every side.
4. **Serve promptly:** Serve hot with lemon wedges (if using) and dipping sauce (if using) alongside. Keep pieces unstacked so steam does not soften the bottoms.

RECIPE: Korean-inspired Chicken Glass-Noodle Salad (chicken-galbi-noodle-salad.md)
CUISINES: Korean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-galbi-noodle-salad/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024250-chicken-galbi-noodle-salad?smid=ck-recipe-iOS-share
INGREDIENTS:
  - 10 oz (280 g) dangmyeon (Korean sweet-potato glass noodles)
  - 1 lb (450 g) ground chicken
  - 4 tbsp soy sauce, divided
  - 2 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar
  - 2 tbsp brown sugar, divided
  - 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil
  - 1 tbsp minced garlic
  - 1 tbsp grated ginger
  - 2 tbsp water, plus more for loosening noodles
  - 1 bell pepper, seeded and thinly sliced
  - 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
  - 1/2 cup loosely packed cilantro leaves, roughly chopped
  - 1/2 cup prepared [Oi Muchim](/mise/recipes/korean-pickled-cucumbers), optional topping
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This is a Korean-inspired noodle salad with soy, sesame, ginger, and garlic. The old name, “galbi,” suggested a rib dish that this ground-chicken recipe does not make. A cooked glaze seasons the chicken; a separate clean dressing seasons the noodles. Keeping those jobs separate lets you control moisture and salt without using raw-meat marinade as a finishing sauce.

## Directions

1. **Mix two sauces:** In a large serving bowl, dissolve 1 tbsp brown sugar in the vinegar and 2 tbsp soy sauce, then whisk in the sesame oil. In a small bowl, mix the remaining 2 tbsp soy sauce, remaining 1 tbsp sugar, and 2 tbsp water for the chicken.
2. **Cook the noodles:** Boil dangmyeon according to its package, tasting for a chewy texture without a hard center. Drain, rinse briefly under cool running water, and drain thoroughly. Cut long strands with clean kitchen shears. Toss promptly with the dressing in the serving bowl.
3. **Cook the chicken:** Heat the neutral oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and break it into small pieces. Cook about 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until most visible moisture has evaporated and some edges are golden.
4. **Glaze:** Lower heat to medium. Add garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds. Add the small bowl of cooking sauce and simmer 2–3 minutes, stirring. Check several thick clusters of chicken reach 165°F / 74°C, keeping the thermometer tip off the pan. Continue cooking if needed. Leave a thin glaze rather than cooking the meat dry.
5. **Toss and finish:** Add the cooked chicken to the noodles. Fold in pepper, cilantro, and sesame seeds. If the noodles stick, loosen with water a tablespoon at a time. Divide among four bowls and top each with 2 tbsp prepared oi muchim if using. Serve promptly, warm or cool.

RECIPE: Chicken Katsu Curry (chicken-katsu-curry.md)
CUISINES: Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-katsu-curry/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Vegetable curry sauce ---
  - 30 g unsalted butter
  - 150 g yellow onion, finely diced
  - 2 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1 tbsp minced fresh ginger
  - 30 g all-purpose flour, reserved only for the sauce
  - 2 tbsp Japanese curry powder
  - 1 tbsp tomato paste
  - 2 cups (480 ml) unsalted chicken stock, plus a little water if needed
  - 1 tbsp soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp mirin
  - 100 g carrot, cut into 1/4-inch dice
  - 150 g potato, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch dice
  - 75 g frozen peas
  - --- Chicken cutlets ---
  - 4 boneless skinless chicken breast portions, about 6 oz (170 g) each
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
  - 60 g all-purpose flour, for coating chicken
  - 2 large eggs, beaten
  - 100 g panko breadcrumbs
  - 500–750 ml neutral frying oil, or enough for 1/2-inch depth in your skillet
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Katsu curry depends on contrast: a crisp cutlet, soft vegetables, and a smooth sauce. Cook the sauce first, then fry the chicken close to serving and ladle gravy beside the breading. This sauce uses its own measured flour; the original ingredient list supplied only dredging flour and could not reliably make the promised gravy.

## Directions

1. **Start the sauce:** Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add onion and cook about 6–8 minutes until soft and lightly golden. Stir in garlic and ginger for 30 seconds. Add the 30 g sauce flour and stir for 2 minutes. Lower the heat, stir in curry powder and tomato paste, and cook about 30 seconds without scorching.
2. **Simmer vegetables:** Gradually whisk in stock, then soy sauce and mirin. Add carrot and potato. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 18–22 minutes, stirring the bottom regularly, until both vegetables are tender and sauce coats a spoon. Add peas and simmer 2 minutes more. Add a small splash of water if the sauce is too thick. Cover and take off heat while frying; rewarm before serving.
3. **Prepare cutlets:** While the sauce simmers, put each chicken portion between sheets of food-safe wrap and pound with a meat mallet to an even 1/2-inch thickness. Pat dry and season with the measured salt and pepper. Keep raw chicken and its tools away from the sauce and cooked food.
4. **Bread:** Set out separate shallow dishes of the 60 g coating flour, beaten eggs, and panko. Coat each cutlet lightly in flour and shake off excess. Dip in egg, let excess drip away, then press both sides into panko. Place on a clean tray and refrigerate until the oil is ready. Discard leftover coating ingredients that touched raw chicken.
5. **Heat oil:** Set a wire rack over a rimmed tray. For holding the first batch briefly, heat the oven to 225°F / 110°C. Add oil to a deep skillet to reach about 1/2 inch, keeping the pan less than half full. Heat to about 350°F / 175°C. Use the pan depth as the guide; the required oil volume varies with its shape.
6. **Fry in batches:** Lower in two cutlets without overlapping. Fry about 3–4 minutes per side, adjusting heat to keep oil around 325–350°F / 165–175°C. Check each cutlet from the side for 165°F / 74°C in its thickest center; cook longer if needed. Transfer to the rack and hold the first batch in the low oven while the second fries. Skim loose crumbs and let the oil return to temperature between batches.
7. **Finish and serve:** Rest the last cutlets on the rack for about 3 minutes. Rewarm the sauce, adding a little water if needed. Slice chicken into strips and divide sauce among four plates, pouring it alongside rather than over the whole crust. Serve with rice prepared separately.

RECIPE: Chicken Lettuce Wraps (chicken-lettuce-wraps.md)
CUISINES: Chinese, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-lettuce-wraps/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb (450 g) ground chicken or ground turkey
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil
  - 1 cup (100 g) finely diced celery
  - 1/2 cup sliced scallions, whites and greens separated
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) hoisin sauce
  - 1 tbsp soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar
  - 2 tbsp water, plus more if needed
  - 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
  - 2 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1 large head butter lettuce, leaves separated (about 12 usable leaves)
  - 1/2 cup purchased ready-to-eat crispy rice noodles, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

These Chinese-American-inspired wraps depend on contrast: warm, savory chicken against cool, crisp lettuce. Celery gives the filling a fresh crunch; water chestnuts are another good option with a different texture. Hoisin provides sweetness and salt, so the sauce needs only a modest amount of additional soy.

## Directions

1. **Prepare leaves and sauce:** Wash and dry the lettuce leaves and chill them. Mix hoisin, soy sauce, vinegar, and water in a small bowl. Separate scallion whites from greens.
2. **Start the chicken:** Heat neutral oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and break into small pieces. Cook 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until released liquid mostly evaporates and some edges begin to brown.
3. **Add crunch and aromatics:** Add celery and scallion whites and cook 2 minutes. Lower heat to medium, add ginger and garlic, and stir for 30 seconds, keeping the garlic from scorching.
4. **Glaze and check:** Add the hoisin mixture. Simmer, stirring, for 2–3 minutes until it coats the filling. Check several thick clusters reach 165°F / 74°C, keeping the thermometer tip off the hot pan. Continue cooking if necessary; add a spoonful of water if the glaze becomes sticky.
5. **Finish and serve:** Turn off heat and stir in sesame oil and scallion greens. Transfer to a serving bowl and let stand briefly until no longer fiercely steaming. Spoon small portions into the lettuce at the table, adding ready-to-eat crispy noodles if desired. Keep the rest of the leaves unfilled until needed.

RECIPE: Chicken Marsala (chicken-marsala.md)
CUISINES: Italian, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-marsala/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodnetwork.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/tyler-florence/chicken-marsala-recipe-1951778
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, opened flat
  - 1/2 cup (60 g) all-purpose flour, for dredging
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, divided
  - 1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - 2 oz (57 g) prosciutto, chopped
  - 8 oz (225 g) fresh cremini mushrooms, wiped clean and thickly sliced
  - 3/4 cup (180 ml) dry Marsala wine
  - 3/4 cup (180 ml) unsalted chicken stock, plus more for loosening
  - 2 tbsp (28 g) unsalted butter, cold and cubed
  - 2 tbsp chopped flat-leaf parsley
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This version pairs chicken thighs with fresh mushrooms and dry Marsala. A light flour coating helps the chicken brown and gives the sauce some body. Prosciutto is a seasoning here, so the stock is unsalted and final salt comes only after reduction. Cooking with wine does not make a dish reliably alcohol-free; use the stock-and-lemon alternative when needed.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the cutlets:** Open thighs flat, trim loose fat, and gently pound only the thick sections to about 1/2 inch between sheets of plastic wrap. Season with half the measured salt and the pepper. Spread flour in a shallow dish, dredge lightly, and shake off excess. Discard leftover flour after raw chicken contact.
2. **Brown in batches:** Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Cook half the chicken about 3–4 minutes on the first side and 2–3 minutes on the second, until golden; it can finish cooking later in the sauce. Transfer to a plate. Repeat with the remaining oil and chicken. Reduce heat if the flour browns too quickly; discard any black, burned bits.
3. **Brown mushrooms:** Lower heat to medium. Add prosciutto and stir for 1 minute. Add mushrooms and cook 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until their liquid has evaporated and they begin to brown. If the pan becomes dry and sticks before the mushrooms release moisture, add a tablespoon of stock and scrape gently.
4. **Make the sauce:** Take the pan briefly off the burner to pour in the Marsala. Return to medium heat and scrape up the golden pan residue. Simmer until the wine reduces by about half, roughly 4–6 minutes. Add stock and simmer 2–3 minutes; the sauce should still be pourable.
5. **Finish cooking the chicken:** Return the chicken and its plate juices to the pan. Simmer gently for about 3–5 minutes, turning once, until the thickest parts reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue if needed, adding stock if the sauce gets too thick. Transfer the cooked chicken to a clean serving platter.
6. **Finish with butter:** Turn off heat and let vigorous bubbling subside. Swirl in the cold butter a few pieces at a time. Add parsley, taste, and use the reserved salt only if needed. Spoon sauce and mushrooms over the chicken and serve. Choose mashed potatoes or pasta, with a green vegetable alongside.

RECIPE: Chicken Milanese (chicken-milanese.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-milanese/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breasts, for thin cutlets
  - 1/2 cup (60 g) all-purpose flour
  - 2 large eggs, beaten
  - 1 1/2 cups (90 g) panko breadcrumbs
  - 1/2 cup (30 g) finely grated Parmesan
  - 1 tsp dried oregano
  - 1/2 tsp garlic powder
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt
  - 1/4 tsp black pepper
  - 1 cup (240 ml) neutral oil, approximately, for a 1/8-inch layer in the skillet
  - 1 batch [Everyday Arugula Salad](/mise/recipes/everyday-arugula-salad), using the linked recipe’s original yield; keep undressed until serving
  - 1 lemon, cut into wedges
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This chicken version of a Milanese-style cutlet uses panko and Parmesan for an open, crisp coating. Thin, even meat is essential: the crumbs should turn golden at about the same time the center finishes cooking. The lemon-arugula salad provides acidity and freshness; keep it beside the chicken if you want the crust to stay crisp longer.

## Directions

1. **Prepare chicken and salad:** Slice the breasts horizontally into four cutlets, then pound between sheets of plastic wrap to an even 1/4 inch. Season both sides with the measured salt and pepper. Prepare one four-portion batch of [Everyday Arugula Salad](/mise/recipes/everyday-arugula-salad), keeping its dressing and cheese separate from the dry leaves. Set a rack over a sheet pan. Heat the oven to 200°F / 95°C if holding the first batch briefly.
2. **Set the coating station:** Place flour in one shallow dish, eggs in a second, and panko mixed with Parmesan, oregano, and garlic powder in a third.
3. **Coat:** Dredge each cutlet lightly in flour, dip in egg and let excess drip off, then press into crumbs on both sides. Keep coated cutlets in one layer. Discard coating ingredients left after raw chicken contact and wash hands and utensils.
4. **Heat and fry:** Pour enough neutral oil into a large skillet to reach about 1/8 inch deep; the amount depends on its flat base. Heat over medium to medium-high to about 350°F / 175°C. Lower two cutlets carefully into the oil, away from you. Fry about 2–3 minutes per side, adjusting the heat so the coating turns golden without burning. Do not crowd or stack them.
5. **Check and drain:** Insert a thermometer horizontally from the side of each cutlet; the meat must reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue cooking as needed. Move cooked cutlets to the rack and hold briefly in a 200°F / 95°C oven while frying the next batch. Skim burned crumbs, replenish oil if needed, and let it reheat before adding more chicken.
6. **Serve promptly:** Toss and finish the arugula salad according to its recipe. Divide among four plates with the hot cutlets and lemon wedges. Add salad on top only just before eating, or serve it alongside to preserve the crust.

RECIPE: Phở Gà (Chicken Pho) (chicken-pho.md)
CUISINES: Vietnamese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-pho/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/chicken-pho
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Broth ---
  - 1 chicken (about 3.5 lbs / 1.6 kg each), cut into quarters, giblets removed
  - 2 lbs (900 g) chicken wings or backs
  - 450 g yellow onions, halved with skin on
  - 80 g fresh ginger, halved lengthwise
  - 2 whole star anise
  - 1 cinnamon stick, about 3 inches long
  - 1 tsp coriander seeds
  - 5 quarts (4.7 liters) water, plus more to adjust the strained broth
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) fish sauce, added gradually to taste
  - 1 tbsp sugar
  - 1 1/2 tsp fine salt, added gradually to taste
  - --- Bowls ---
  - 1 lb (450 g) dried flat rice noodles (bánh phở)
  - 3 scallions, thinly sliced
  - 1/3 cup chopped cilantro
  - 200 g bean sprouts, optional, cooked thoroughly before serving
  - 1 cup loosely packed Thai basil leaves, optional
  - 2 limes, cut into wedges
  - 1 jalapeño, thinly sliced, optional
  - 3 tbsp hoisin sauce, optional at the table
  - 3 tbsp sriracha, optional at the table
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The serving meat and broth have different cooking needs. Remove the chicken quarters when cooked, then let the bones continue simmering for body and flavor. Aromatics vary between phở gà recipes; this version retains a modest amount of star anise, cinnamon, and coriander. Hoisin, chile sauce, and fresh herbs are optional at the table so the broth can be tasted on its own first.

## Directions

1. **Toast aromatics:** Put onion halves and ginger cut-side up on a rimmed sheet pan under the broiler, watching closely and turning as needed, for about 10–15 minutes until softened with charred patches. Cool enough to handle, remove loose blackened onion skin, and scrape off any burned debris. Toast star anise, cinnamon, and coriander in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 1 minute until fragrant.
2. **Start broth:** Put chicken quarters, wings or backs, aromatics, and spices in a 12-quart stockpot with the measured water. Bring just to a boil, skim surface foam, and reduce to a gentle simmer with only occasional bubbles. Do not wash raw chicken in the sink.
3. **Remove serving meat when cooked:** Begin checking quarters after about 30 minutes of simmering. Probe the thickest breast and thigh meat away from bone; remove each quarter only after it reaches 165°F / 74°C. Pieces may need 40 minutes or longer. Transfer to a clean tray and let stand about 10 minutes until safe to handle. Remove meat from bones, put the meat in a shallow covered container, and refrigerate promptly. Return the bones to the stockpot.
4. **Continue the broth:** Simmer bones and aromatics gently for about 2 more hours, skimming occasionally. Add a little water if needed to keep bones submerged. Avoid vigorously stirring the pot.
5. **Strain and balance:** Strain carefully through a fine-mesh sieve into another large pot and discard solids. Skim excess fat, leaving some for flavor. Aim for roughly 3.5–4 liters broth; reduce if weak or add water if overly concentrated. Stir in sugar and start with half the fish sauce and half the salt. Taste and add the remainder gradually only as needed.
6. **Prepare noodles and toppings:** Cook bánh phở according to its package until tender but not falling apart; different widths require different soaking or boiling methods. Drain and divide among six large bowls. Prepare scallion, cilantro, lime, and optional basil, chile, and cooked sprouts.
7. **Warm meat and assemble:** Slice the refrigerated chicken. Add it to simmering broth and heat through to 165°F / 74°C. Distribute meat among the noodle bowls, then ladle in about 500–600 ml broth per bowl. Finish with scallion and cilantro and offer the remaining toppings and sauces at the table. Refrigerate any unused broth promptly.

RECIPE: Chicken Piccata (chicken-piccata-unfried.md)
CUISINES: Italian, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-piccata-unfried/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breasts, for thin cutlets
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt
  - 1/4 tsp black pepper
  - 2 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) unsalted chicken broth, plus more if needed
  - 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 2 tbsp (28 g) unsalted butter, cold and cubed
  - 2 tbsp brined capers, drained and briefly rinsed
  - 2 tbsp chopped flat-leaf parsley
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Piccata pairs a thin cutlet with lemon, capers, and butter. This version omits a flour coating, leaving a light pan sauce. The goal is a thin, bright coating, not a thick gravy. Save the lemon for the finish and keep enough broth in the pan to carry the butter.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Slice the breasts horizontally into four cutlets and pound between sheets of plastic wrap to an even 1/4 inch. Pat dry and season with the measured salt and pepper.
2. **Sear in batches:** Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Cook half the cutlets about 2–3 minutes per side, until lightly golden. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining oil and chicken. Lower heat if the pan residue darkens too quickly.
3. **Deglaze:** Reduce heat to medium. Stir garlic and capers in the pan for 30 seconds, then add broth. Scrape up golden residue and simmer for about 1 minute. Discard blackened residue rather than incorporating it into the sauce.
4. **Check chicken:** Check each cutlet by inserting a thermometer from its side into the center. If any are below 165°F / 74°C, return them and their plate juices to the broth and simmer gently until they reach that temperature. If all are already cooked, add only their plate juices to the broth and bring it back to a simmer. Transfer cooked chicken to a clean platter. Add a little broth if the pan is becoming dry.
5. **Finish off heat:** Turn off heat and let vigorous bubbling stop. Add lemon juice and swirl in cold butter a few pieces at a time until glossy. Stir in parsley. Taste before adding any additional seasoning, then spoon the sauce over the chicken and serve immediately.

RECIPE: Chicken Pot Pie (chicken-pot-pie-ix.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-pot-pie-ix/
SOURCE: Adapted from Allrecipes.com
SOURCE_URL: http://allrecipes.com/recipe/26317/chicken-pot-pie-ix/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Double crust ---
  - 300 g all-purpose flour, plus a little for rolling
  - 225 g cold unsalted butter, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt
  - 100–120 ml ice-cold water, added only as needed
  - --- Filling ---
  - 450 g cooked boneless chicken, chilled and cut into bite-size pieces (weight after cooking)
  - 100 g carrots, cut into 1/4-inch dice
  - 100 g yellow onion, finely diced
  - 50 g celery, cut into 1/4-inch dice
  - 100 g frozen peas
  - 56 g unsalted butter
  - 45 g all-purpose flour
  - 1 3/4 cups (420 ml) low-sodium chicken broth
  - 2/3 cup (160 ml) whole milk
  - 1/2 tsp garlic powder
  - 1/4 tsp celery seed
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, plus more only if needed
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
  - --- Finish ---
  - 1 large egg, beaten, for brushing
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A pot pie asks the pastry and filling to do different jobs. The filling should already contain tender vegetables and a thickened gravy; the oven then bakes the crust and reheats the center. Keep the filling cool enough that it cannot melt the butter in the raw pastry. This version includes its own savory dough rather than sending you through a dessert recipe.

## Directions

1. **Make pastry:** Mix the 300 g flour and pastry salt in a bowl. Work in cold butter with fingertips or a pastry cutter, leaving a mixture of crumbs and flattened pea-size butter pieces. Toss with 100 ml ice water. Squeeze a handful: if it falls apart, add the remaining water a teaspoon at a time just until it holds. Bring together without kneading smooth. Divide into two discs, one slightly larger for the bottom, wrap, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Do not taste raw dough.
2. **Prepare filling ingredients:** While the dough chills, cut carrots and celery into small, even dice. Keep the cooked chicken refrigerated until needed. Measure the filling flour separately from any flour used for pastry or rolling.
3. **Soften vegetables:** Melt filling butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add onion, carrots, and celery; cook, stirring, about 10–12 minutes until onion is soft and carrot is almost tender. Lower the heat if vegetables begin to brown rapidly.
4. **Thicken gravy:** Stir in the 45 g flour, garlic powder, celery seed, salt, and pepper. Cook and stir for 1 minute. Gradually stir in broth, then milk, scraping the bottom and dispersing the flour mixture. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 3 minutes, stirring, until thick enough to coat a spoon. Fold in chicken and frozen peas. Taste for seasoning, then spread the filling in a shallow heatproof dish to release heat. Refrigerate promptly until cool, about 30–45 minutes in a shallow layer; do not leave it out for the whole dough chill.
5. **Heat oven and roll:** Put a sturdy rimmed metal baking sheet on the lower rack and preheat to 425°F / 220°C. On a lightly floured surface, roll the larger dough disc to about a 13-inch circle, roughly 1/8 inch thick. Ease into a deep 9-inch metal pie pan without stretching. Roll the second disc to about 12 inches. If either becomes soft, refrigerate briefly before continuing.
6. **Fill and seal:** Spoon cool filling into the lined pan, keeping it below the rim. If your pan cannot hold it, bake excess separately in a small ovenproof dish to 165°F / 74°C. Lay on the top crust, trim to about 1/2 inch beyond the rim, fold the edges together, and crimp. Cut four generous vents in the lid. Brush lightly with beaten egg; discard the remainder. Refrigerate the assembled pie for 10 minutes if the pastry has softened.
7. **Bake through:** Place the metal pie pan on the hot baking sheet. Bake 20 minutes at 425°F / 220°C, then reduce to 375°F / 190°C and bake about 30–45 minutes longer. Shield darkening edges with foil as needed. The pastry should be deeply golden and filling should bubble through the vents; also insert a thermometer through a central vent to verify 165°F / 74°C in the middle. Continue baking, loosely covered if necessary, until that endpoint is reached.
8. **Rest and serve:** Rest on a rack for 20 minutes, then cut into eight slices. The gravy will settle but remain soft rather than forming a firm slab. A lightly dressed green salad complements the rich pastry.

RECIPE: Chicken Quesadillas with Quick Pico (chicken-quesadillas-with-quick-pico.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-quesadillas-with-quick-pico/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Quesadillas ---
  - 1 lb cooked shredded rotisserie chicken or other cooked chicken
  - 8 8-inch flour tortillas, ready-to-eat, for warming; cook raw tortillas separately according to their package before this recipe
  - 2 cups shredded Oaxaca or mozzarella cheese, choose one; freshly shredded if possible
  - 1 jalapeño, minced; seeds removed for a milder filling
  - 1/2 cup diced onion
  - --- Pico de gallo ---
  - 2 ripe tomatoes, diced
  - 1/4 onion, finely minced
  - 1 jalapeño, minced
  - 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
  - 1 lime, juice only
  - 1/2 tsp kosher salt
  - --- Cooking and serving ---
  - 2 tbsp vegetable oil
  - Mexican crema or sour cream, as wanted; choose one for serving
  - lime wedges, as wanted for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Warm tortillas fold more easily around the chicken, onion, jalapeño and melting cheese. The folded version uses one tortilla per quesadilla; a two-tortilla stacked version is another option. Both use the full chicken and cheese amounts. Keep the pico cold and add it at serving so its fresh crunch contrasts with the warm filling.

## Directions

1. **Make and chill the pico:** Combine ripe tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, fresh cilantro, lime, and kosher salt using the lime juice. Taste, then refrigerate until serving. Count preparation and serving time together: discard cut-tomato salsa left out longer than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C.
2. **Warm the tortillas:** Heat a dry skillet over medium-low heat. Warm 8-inch flour tortillas individually until pliable, then keep them wrapped in a clean kitchen towel while assembling. Start with the original 3–4-minute warming range; use pliability as the cue, and allow longer for more tortillas.
3. **Fill and fold:** Divide cooked shredded rotisserie chicken or other cooked chicken, shredded Oaxaca or mozzarella cheese, jalapeño, and diced onion evenly among all the measured tortillas, covering half of each and leaving a little border. Fold each tortilla over its filling. Each tortilla makes one folded quesadilla: the original eight tortillas make eight folded quesadillas for four planned portions. For some milder quesadillas, put only chicken and cheese in those and distribute the filling onion and jalapeño among the others; keep the pico separate.
4. **Choose the skillet or griddle:** Choose one of these methods and use the full measured vegetable oil across its cooking loads. For a skillet, heat over medium-high, spread a share of the oil in it and add only as many folded quesadillas as fit flat without overlap. Start with 2–3 minutes on the first side and 1–2 minutes on the second. For a griddle, spread the same total oil over its cooking area and start checking at 2–3 minutes per side, cooking in loads if they do not all fit. Use the remaining measured oil between loads. In either method, cook until both faces are golden and the chicken filling reaches 165°F / 74°C throughout; check the center of the filling with a thermometer. If the surface browns first, lower the heat and continue, covering briefly if needed to heat the filling.
5. **Serve with the cold pico:** Cut the quesadillas into triangles and divide among the planned portions. Serve promptly with the refrigerated pico and Mexican crema or sour cream and lime wedges on the side.

## Stacked quesadillas

For the two-tortilla version, use the same full chicken, cheese, onion and jalapeño quantities and the same total cooking oil. Pair the measured tortillas, dividing all the filling among the bottom tortillas and covering each with its partner. The original eight tortillas make four stacked quesadillas. Use the skillet or griddle route above with enough room for the whole 8-inch rounds; turn carefully and check the filling reaches 165°F / 74°C. A stacked round may need longer than a folded one. Serve with the same full pico and garnishes.

RECIPE: Chicken Sausage Pasta (chicken-sausage-pasta.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-sausage-pasta/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb dry linguine or fettuccine
  - 1 lb Italian-style chicken sausage, raw or fully cooked; prepare according to the label and method
  - 1 large bell pepper, stem and seeds removed, sliced into thin strips
  - 9 oz fresh spinach, washed and drained
  - 1 (28 oz) can petite diced San Marzano-style tomatoes, with their juices
  - 1/2 cup dry red wine
  - 3 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1 tsp dried basil
  - 1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan
  - 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  - 1/2 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Brown the sausage, soften the pepper and reduce the tomatoes before adding the pasta. Wilt the spinach in the sauce first so the noodles do not wait for it to collapse. Chicken sausages vary: slice fully cooked links, or remove raw sausage from its casings and cook it as crumbles.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and heat water:** Read the sausage label: slice fully cooked links into rounds about 1/2 inch thick, or remove casings from raw links. Slice pepper, mince garlic and grate Parmesan. Bring a large pot of water to a boil and season moderately with salt.
2. **Brown sausage:** Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium to medium-high. For fully cooked links, add the slices and cook about **5–7 minutes**, turning, until browned in patches. For raw sausage, add the meat and break it into small crumbles; cook about **8–12 minutes**, stirring, until representative thick pieces reach **165°F / 74°C**. If crowded, brown in rounds with the oil divided between them. Transfer to a clean plate.
3. **Build sauce:** Add pepper to the same pan and cook about **4–6 minutes** until starting to soften. Stir in garlic and dried basil for **30–45 seconds**. Add wine, scrape up browned bits and simmer about **2 minutes**. Add all the listed tomatoes and their juices. Simmer uncovered about **10–15 minutes**, stirring, until lightly thickened and pepper is tender.
4. **Time the pasta:** During the tomato simmer, cook pasta according to its package, tasting near the end. Aim for tender with a little bite; a brief sauce toss follows. Reserve **the listed cooking water** before draining without rinsing.
5. **Wilt and combine:** Return sausage to the sauce and add spinach in handfuls, folding until wilted, about **2–3 minutes**. Heat the sausage throughout to **165°F / 74°C**, then add pasta. Toss over low heat for about **1 minute**, adding reserved water in small splashes only if needed for a coating sauce. Use the pasta pot for this stage if the skillet is too full.
6. **Finish:** Remove from heat and fold in Parmesan. Add black pepper and taste before adding salt; sausage and cheese already contribute plenty. Divide into the intended portions and serve promptly.

RECIPE: Chicken Scaloppine with Tomato & White Wine (chicken-scaloppine-with-tomato-and-white-wine.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-scaloppine-with-tomato-and-white-wine/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 lbs (900 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, opened flat
  - 1/2 cup (60 g) all-purpose flour, for dredging
  - 3 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - 3/4 tsp fine salt
  - 1/2 tsp black pepper
  - 5 cloves garlic, minced
  - 2 tbsp tomato paste
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) dry white wine
  - 3/4 cup (180 ml) unsalted chicken broth, plus more if needed
  - 9 oz (255 g) fresh baby spinach, washed if needed and well dried
  - 1 tbsp (14 g) unsalted butter, cold and cubed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Scaloppine are thin slices of meat cooked quickly. Here, a light flour coating and a small quantity of tomato paste give body to a white-wine pan sauce. The spinach must wilt before the off-heat butter finish; otherwise it can cool the sauce and release water after the sauce has been balanced.

## Directions

1. **Prepare chicken:** Open thighs flat and pound thicker sections gently to about 1/2 inch between sheets of plastic wrap. Season with salt and pepper, dredge lightly in flour, and shake off excess. Discard leftover flour after raw chicken contact.
2. **Brown in batches:** Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken in uncrowded batches, about 3–4 minutes on the first side and 2–3 on the second, distributing the remaining oil among later batches. Transfer to a plate; the chicken will finish in the sauce. Adjust heat to avoid burning the flour residue.
3. **Cook paste and garlic:** Lower heat to medium. Stir tomato paste in the pan for 1–2 minutes until slightly darker and fragrant. Add garlic and stir for 30 seconds. If the pan is dry enough to scorch, loosen with a tablespoon of the measured broth.
4. **Deglaze:** Take the pan briefly off the burner to add wine. Return to medium heat, scrape up golden residue, and simmer 2–3 minutes. Add the remaining broth and bring to a gentle simmer.
5. **Finish the chicken:** Return chicken and plate juices. Simmer gently about 3–5 minutes, turning pieces, until the thickest centers reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue as needed, adding broth if the sauce becomes too thick. Transfer cooked chicken to a clean platter.
6. **Wilt spinach and finish:** Add spinach to the simmering sauce in handfuls, turning until wilted, about 2–3 minutes. Simmer briefly if it releases excess water. Turn off heat, let vigorous bubbling stop, and swirl in the butter. Taste and adjust only if needed. Spoon spinach and sauce over the chicken and serve.

RECIPE: Shawarma-style Roast Chicken (chicken-shawarma.md)
CUISINES: Middle Eastern
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-shawarma/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 2 cloves garlic, finely grated
  - 1 tsp ground cumin
  - 1 tsp ground coriander
  - 1 tsp ground turmeric
  - 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
  - 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
  - 3/4 tsp fine salt
  - 1/4 tsp black pepper
  - 1/2 cup prepared [Tahini Sauce](/mise/recipes/tahini-sauce)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Shawarma is cooked on a rotating spit. This home adaptation uses a hot oven and a short skillet finish to create its own tender-meat and browned-edge contrast. Cumin, coriander, turmeric, and a restrained amount of cinnamon provide warm seasoning. It is a practical shawarma-style roast, with a different cooking process from spit-roasted meat.

## Directions

1. **Marinate:** Reserve 2 tsp olive oil for finishing. Mix the remaining oil with lemon juice, garlic, ground spices, salt, and pepper. Coat chicken, cover, and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below for 4–24 hours.
2. **Roast and check:** Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Arrange chicken opened flat with gaps on a foil-lined rimmed sheet pan. Roast about 20–25 minutes, checking every thigh at its thickest part for 165°F / 74°C. Continue as needed. Meanwhile, prepare the tahini sauce and measure out 1/2 cup for this meal.
3. **Rest and slice:** Transfer cooked chicken to a clean board, rest for 5 minutes, and slice across the meat into strips about 1/2 inch wide.
4. **Brown briefly:** Heat half the reserved oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add half the sliced chicken in one layer and leave briefly until some edges brown, about 1–2 minutes, then toss and remove. Repeat with remaining oil and chicken. Stop at browned edges; do not blacken the spices or dry all the strips.
5. **Serve:** Divide chicken among four plates and drizzle each with 2 tbsp tahini sauce, or offer the sauce separately. Add pita and a fresh salad if desired; these are additional components.

RECIPE: Chicken Souvlaki (chicken-souvlaki.md)
CUISINES: Greek
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-souvlaki/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into even 1-inch pieces
  - 2 tbsp olive oil
  - 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 1 tbsp dried oregano
  - 3 cloves garlic, finely grated
  - 3/4 tsp fine salt
  - 1/2 tsp black pepper
  - 1 tsp neutral oil, for brushing the grill grates
  - 1/2 lemon, cut into wedges
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Souvlaki is built around small pieces of meat cooked on skewers. This chicken version uses lemon, garlic, and plenty of oregano. The marinade seasons the surface; even cutting and careful heat control matter more than an extended acidic soak for a juicy center.

## Directions

1. **Marinate:** Mix olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, garlic, salt, and pepper. Toss with chicken, cover, and refrigerate for 30 minutes to 4 hours at 40°F / 4°C or below.
2. **Prepare grill and skewers:** Preheat the grill to medium-high, with a cooler area available. Thread chicken onto about eight skewers without tightly bunching the pieces. Let excess marinade drip off and discard it. Brush clean grates lightly with the measured neutral oil.
3. **Grill:** Cook skewers with the lid closed between turns, turning every 2–3 minutes, until browned on several sides, usually about 10–15 minutes. Move them to the cooler area if garlic or oregano darkens too quickly or dripping marinade causes flare-ups.
4. **Verify:** Insert a thermometer into several of the largest chicken pieces, keeping its sensing tip in the meat and away from the skewer. Cook until each checked piece reaches 165°F / 74°C; continue as needed rather than relying on carryover from 160°F.
5. **Rest and finish:** Move to a clean platter and rest for 5 minutes. Serve with the lemon wedges for a fresh squeeze. A Greek village salad and pita make a fuller meal.

RECIPE: Paprika Chicken Kebabs with Chile-Yogurt Sauce (chicken-thigh-kebabs-with-chile-yogurt-sauce.md)
CUISINES: Mediterranean-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-thigh-kebabs-with-chile-yogurt-sauce/
SOURCE: Adapted from Jimmy Bannos Jr.'s Chicken Thigh Kebabs with Chile-Yogurt Sauce, published by Food & Wine
SOURCE_URL: https://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/chicken-thigh-kebabs-chile-yogurt-sauce
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 3/4 lbs (790 g) boneless skin-on chicken thighs, trimmed of loose excess fat; net weight after deboning
  - 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the chicken
  - 2 tbsp sweet paprika
  - 6 g fine salt, for the chicken
  - 1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper, divided
  - 1 cup (240 g) plain whole-milk Greek yogurt, for the sauce
  - 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the sauce
  - 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 1/4 tsp cayenne, plus up to 1/4 tsp more to taste
  - 1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, for the sauce
  - 1 tsp neutral oil, for the grill grates or skillet
  - 1/2 lemon, cut into wedges
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This paprika-coated chicken is adapted from Jimmy Bannos Jr.'s recipe published by Food & Wine. Its yogurt and dried chiles make a separate serving sauce; the chicken itself receives paprika, oil and seasoning. This adaptation uses two tablespoons coating oil instead of the original half cup, while keeping the sauce's tablespoon; the lighter coating aims to reduce excess dripping, but skin still renders fat. Expose the skin to steady heat and keep a cooler part of the grill available, because rendering fat can flare up before the centers finish.

## Directions

1. **Start the grill:** For gas, preheat with the lid closed, then set a cooking zone to medium and leave another burner low or off. For charcoal, light the coals and let them establish before arranging them on one side for a direct-heat zone and a cooler side. Follow the grill's lighting instructions. Begin the chicken and sauce while it heats.
2. **Cut and season the chicken:** Pat the boneless thighs dry without rinsing. Trim loose excess fat, keeping the attached skin. Cut about twenty-four pieces roughly 1 1/2 inches across, with similar thickness and no thick rolled bundles. Toss with the chicken's two tablespoons olive oil, paprika, six grams fine salt and half the pepper. Cover and refrigerate for fifteen minutes while making the sauce.
3. **Mix a separate sauce:** With clean hands and utensils, whisk yogurt, its tablespoon olive oil, lemon juice, the first quarter-teaspoon cayenne, red pepper flakes, sauce salt and remaining pepper in a clean bowl. Taste and add the extra cayenne only if wanted. Cover and refrigerate. Do not dip raw-chicken tools into this bowl or use its serving spoon for the skewers.
4. **Thread and oil the grate:** Divide chicken among eight skewers, about three pieces each, keeping pieces unfolded and skin facing outward rather than tucked between meat. Do not compress pieces tightly; leave exposed surfaces available for browning. Let excess oily coating drip back into its bowl and discard the residue. Brush clean grill grates lightly with the measured teaspoon cooking oil, using a folded paper towel held in long tongs. Put out a clean serving platter and clean cooked-food utensils.
5. **Grill and measure:** Lay the skewers over moderate direct heat with space between them, starting with the exposed skin toward the grate where possible. Grill about ten to fifteen minutes, turning every two to three minutes after the first surface releases. Move to the cooler zone if skin fat flares or paprika darkens sharply. Close the lid between turns. Begin checking around ten minutes: probe the thickest pieces on every skewer from the side, away from the metal, and continue until they reach at least 165°F / 74°C. Check any unusually large pieces separately. Remove finished skewers rather than waiting for all to reach the endpoint together.
6. **Rest and serve:** Transfer to the clean platter and rest five minutes. Serve two skewers per person with the sauce and lemon wedges. The sauce yields roughly one cup plus the oil and lemon additions; offer about a quarter-cup per diner, with any extra on the side. For four plates, add one full four-side batch of either couscous recipe and a vegetable or salad. Those are additional components and preparation time; the two couscous recipes are alternative starches.

RECIPE: Chicken Tikka Masala (chicken-tikka-masala.md)
CUISINES: Indian, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-tikka-masala/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken and Marinade ---
  - 900 g (about 2 lb) boneless skinless chicken thighs, weighed after trimming large pieces of fat, cut into 1 1/2-inch / 4 cm chunks
  - 3/4 cup plain full-fat Greek yogurt, unsweetened
  - 1 tbsp finely grated garlic, for the marinade
  - 1 tbsp finely grated ginger, for the marinade
  - 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, for the marinade
  - 1 tsp fine salt, for the marinade
  - 1 tbsp Kashmiri red chile powder, pure ground chile rather than a seasoning blend
  - 1 tsp garam masala, a salt-free ground spice blend, for the marinade
  - 1 tsp neutral oil, for lightly brushing the two cooking racks
  - --- Sauce ---
  - 2 tbsp unsalted butter, for the onion
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil, for the onion
  - 250 g white or yellow onion, peeled and finely diced
  - 1 tbsp minced garlic, for the sauce
  - 1 tbsp minced ginger, for the sauce
  - 3 tbsp tomato paste
  - 1 1/2 tbsp ground coriander
  - 1 tbsp ground cumin
  - 1 tsp ground turmeric
  - 1 tbsp sweet paprika, not smoked
  - 3 cups (720 ml) plain unseasoned tomato passata
  - 1 tbsp white sugar, for the sauce
  - 1 tsp fine salt, for the onion and tomato base
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, reserved for final seasoning; use only as needed
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) water, reserved only to loosen the sauce as needed
  - 1 cup (240 ml) heavy cream, at least 35% milk fat
  - --- Finish ---
  - 1 tbsp unsalted butter
  - 1 tbsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), measured loosely before crushing
  - 1 tsp garam masala, for finishing
  - 1 tsp white sugar, optional for the final adjustment
  - 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, optional for the final adjustment
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This restaurant-style tikka masala combines browned chicken with a generous tomato-and-cream sauce. A little char adds flavor, but the chicken should not be black all over. Have the sauce ready first, cook the chicken in manageable batches, and crush the dried fenugreek leaves into the finished curry for their distinctive aroma.

## Directions

1. **Marinate:** Trim and cut the chicken into pieces about **1 1/2 inches / 4 cm** across. Whisk the yogurt, marinade garlic and ginger, marinade lemon juice, marinade salt, Kashmiri chile and marinade garam masala in a bowl. Fold in chicken, cover and refrigerate for **at least 4 hours**, or overnight up to 24 hours. Wash hands, board and tools after handling the raw chicken. Keep the separate rack oil out of the marinade.
2. **Prepare the sauce and pans:** Begin about **75 minutes before the chicken's four-hour marinade ends**. Dice the onion, measure all sauce ingredients and set aside the finishing ingredients. Prepare the number of foil-lined metal pans and broiler-safe racks needed for your batch: two for the full recipe, one for half or quarter. Lightly brush the racks in use with the listed rack oil, dividing it between them. Keep the chicken refrigerated while making the sauce. Set out a clean covered platter and clean tongs for cooked chicken.
3. **Cook the onion, paste and spices:** Heat the onion butter and oil in the heavy pot over medium heat. Add onion and **half the initial sauce salt**. Cook for **15–20 minutes**, stirring regularly, until soft and golden. Add tomato paste and stir for **2 minutes**, until a shade darker. Lower the heat; stir in the sauce garlic and ginger for **30–60 seconds**, then coriander, cumin, turmeric and paprika for **15–20 seconds**. Promptly add passata before the ground spices scorch.
4. **Finish the sauce base:** Stir in the measured sauce sugar and the remaining initial sauce salt. Bring to a gentle simmer, allowing a few minutes to heat, then cook **uncovered for 15–20 minutes**, stirring the bottom regularly. Use the water reserve a little at a time only if it becomes too thick to stir easily. The base should be thick and aromatic but still flow from a spoon. Turn off the heat and let bubbling stop. If blending, keep the immersion-blender head submerged and blend carefully until smooth, following the appliance's hot-food instructions; stop the motor before lifting it. Cover the pot off the heat while broiling. During the last ten minutes of the sauce simmer, preheat the broiler to HIGH according to the oven's instructions; do not load chicken until the sauce base is finished and the chicken has marinated four hours.
5. **Load the first batch:** Arrange **up to about 450 g chicken** on the first rack (half the full recipe; all the chicken for a half or quarter recipe) in one layer with spaces between the pieces. Lift it from the marinade, letting excess drip back into the bowl; retain a thin coating rather than wiping it clean. Keep the remaining raw chicken and marinade refrigerated. Place the top of the food about **5–6 inches below the broiler element**. Broil only one tray at a time.
6. **Broil through, then repeat:** Broil the thighs for about **12–18 minutes total**, turning after **6–8 minutes** and rotating the tray if the element browns unevenly. Watch throughout. Start temperature checks early: insert a clean instant-read probe from the side into the center of several large pieces, avoiding the rack. Every checked center must reach **165°F / 74°C** before removal; take ready pieces out as needed while thicker ones finish. If the surface darkens first, move the tray lower or use the oven finish in troubleshooting. Transfer with clean tongs to the clean platter and cover loosely. If raw chicken remains, load the second prepared rack and broil the same way. Discard any raw marinade once the last batch is loaded. Keep raw utensils away from the cooked platter. Allow a few minutes for loading and temperature checks between the two rounds; do not leave the broiler to prepare another dish. Discard the scorched tray drippings, keeping only the juices that collect on the clean cooked-chicken platter.
7. **Combine and finish:** Turn off the broiler. Reheat the sauce base, stirring, until bubbling throughout. Stir in the cream and bring back to a gentle simmer, using any remaining measured water only if necessary. Add all the cooked chicken and its clean-platter juices; stir gently for about **2–4 minutes**, until the whole curry is hot and chicken centers reach **165°F / 74°C**. Turn off the heat. Taste with a piece of chicken, then add the reserved salt only as needed. Use small amounts of the optional finishing sugar or lemon only if the sauce needs them. Stir in the finishing butter, crush the measured fenugreek leaves between your palms into the pot, and add the finishing garam masala. Rest **5 minutes** before serving.
8. **Serve:** Divide the chicken evenly among the servings and spoon over the sauce, roughly **1 1/4–1 1/2 cups curry per person**. Serve with plain basmati or naan, and small spoonfuls of cucumber raita if wanted. The full basmati recipe provides six rice sides; if also serving naan, start with smaller rice portions and one bread each.
