RECIPE: Chicken Tinga (chicken-tinga.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-tinga/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken and sauce ---
  - 1 1/2 lb cooked shredded chicken, already poached or rotisserie; cooking raw chicken is a separate preparation
  - 2 large tomatoes, halved
  - 3 garlic cloves, unpeeled for charring; peel before blending
  - 1–2 chipotles in adobo
  - 1 tsp adobo sauce
  - 1 small onion, sliced into half-moons
  - 1/2 tsp dried oregano
  - 1/2 cup chicken broth
  - 1 tsp salt
  - cooking oil, a splash for sautéing the onion
  - fresh lime juice, a squeeze to finish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Tinga is associated with Puebla; this version uses cooked shredded chicken in a chipotle-tomato sauce. Char the tomatoes and garlic on the dry skillet (tatemar) for a smoky edge, soften the onion, then bloom the oregano briefly before adding liquid. The chicken warms in the finished sauce, and the small lime squeeze at serving complements its smoky richness.

## Directions

1. **Char the tomatoes and garlic:** Heat a heavy dry skillet over medium-high heat. Add large tomatoes and garlic cloves, tomatoes cut-side down. Start checking at 5–7 minutes, turning as needed, until the tomatoes soften with charred patches and the garlic softens inside its skin. Remove individual garlic cloves if ready before the tomatoes; avoid burning them while waiting for the tomatoes.
2. **Cool and peel:** Transfer the charred vegetables to a clean plate and let them cool to room temperature before using a countertop blender. Peel the garlic and discard the skins. Blend as soon as the vegetables have cooled; refrigerate them promptly if preparing ahead. Cooling takes additional elapsed time.
3. **Blend the sauce:** Blend chipotles in adobo and adobo sauce with all the cooled charred tomatoes and peeled garlic until smooth. Use the lower end of the listed chipotle range for a milder sauce; the adobo sauce remains its separately measured amount. Keep below the blender's marked working capacity and blend in batches if necessary.
4. **Soften the onion:** Wipe out the skillet. Add small onion and cooking oil and sauté until the onion is translucent and softened.
5. **Bloom the oregano:** Stir in dried oregano and toast for 30 seconds, just until fragrant, before it burns.
6. **Simmer the sauce:** Pour the blended sauce into the onion pan. Stir in chicken broth and salt and simmer for about 5 minutes until slightly thickened, stirring to keep the base from catching.
7. **Heat the cooked chicken:** Fold cooked shredded chicken through all the sauce. Start checking after about 5 minutes and continue, stirring, until the chicken and sauce reach 165°F / 74°C throughout. Check more than one part of the pan, especially thick clusters of chicken.
8. **Finish and serve:** Stir in fresh lime juice and serve the saucy chicken among the planned portions.

RECIPE: Chicken Tortilla Soup III (chicken-tortilla-soup-iii.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-tortilla-soup-iii/
SOURCE: Allrecipes.com
SOURCE_URL: http://allrecipes.com/recipe/15553/chicken-tortilla-soup-iii/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Soup ---
  - 3 garlic cloves, minced
  - 1 onion, peeled and chopped
  - 3 tbsp margarine
  - 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
  - 3 cans (14 oz) chicken broth
  - 4 cups half-and-half
  - 1 can (10 3/4 oz) condensed cream of chicken soup
  - 1 cup fresh salsa
  - 1 can (15 oz) creamed corn
  - 6 boneless chicken breast halves, fully cooked, skinned and shredded or cut into spoon-sized pieces
  - 2 tsp ground cumin
  - 1 package (1.27 oz) dry fajita seasoning
  - 3 tbsp fresh cilantro, washed and chopped
  - --- Bowls ---
  - 16 oz tortilla chips
  - 8 oz Monterey Jack cheese, shredded
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This creamy tortilla soup starts with fully cooked chicken and keeps all the half-and-half, condensed soup and creamed corn. Stir along the pot bottom as it heats. Divide the chips and cheese between the bottom and top of each bowl so they keep some crunch rather than soaking in the whole batch.

## Directions

1. **Soften aromatics:** In a large pot over medium heat, sauté garlic cloves, onion, and margarine for about 5 minutes, until the onion softens. Choose a pot with room for all the liquid, chicken and corn, plus stirring headroom.
2. **Cook flour:** Stir in all-purpose flour and cook, stirring, for 1 minute.
3. **Add liquid:** Gradually stir in chicken broth and half-and-half until the flour disperses. Bring to a boil while stirring along the bottom, then reduce heat to low.
4. **Heat soup:** Add condensed cream of chicken soup, fresh salsa, creamed corn, boneless chicken breast halves, ground cumin, dry fajita seasoning, and 2/3 of the fresh cilantro. Heat gently for about 15 minutes, stirring regularly, until the finished soup reaches 165°F / 74°C throughout. Check after stirring so a hot edge does not stand in for the whole pot; cold cooked chicken may take longer.
5. **Build bowls:** Divide all 1/3 of the fresh cilantro, tortilla chips, and Monterey Jack cheese among the listed portions. Crumble some of the chips into the bowls and add half the cheese; ladle in the hot soup. Finish with the remaining chips and cheese and all the reserved cilantro. At the original eight-portion batch, each bowl gets 1 oz cheese total, half below and half above; use proportional shares for other batches.

RECIPE: Chicken with Snow Peas Stir-Fry (chicken-with-snow-peas-stir-fry.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chicken-with-snow-peas-stir-fry/
SOURCE: Adapted from thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/chicken-snow-peas-stir-fry/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken coating ---
  - 12 oz (340 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, sliced across the grain about 1/4 inch thick
  - 1 tsp cornstarch
  - 1 tsp light soy sauce
  - 1 tsp peanut or neutral oil
  - --- Sauce ---
  - 1/3 cup (80 ml) unsalted chicken stock
  - 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
  - 1 tbsp light soy sauce
  - 1 tsp oyster sauce
  - 1 1/2 tsp cornstarch
  - 1/8 tsp sugar
  - 1/8 tsp white pepper
  - --- Stir-fry ---
  - 1 lb (450 g) snow peas, ends and tough strings removed
  - 1 tbsp peanut or neutral oil, divided
  - 1 clove garlic, minced
  - 2 tbsp water, for briefly steaming the peas if needed
  - 1/2 tsp toasted sesame oil
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A thin cornstarch coating gives the chicken a smooth surface; it cannot protect lean meat from unlimited high heat. Cook the chicken and snow peas separately so each reaches the right texture, then combine them briefly in sauce. This is a light main for four with rice, or one dish in a shared meal.

## Directions

1. **Coat chicken:** Mix the coating teaspoon of cornstarch, teaspoon of soy, and teaspoon of oil. Toss with chicken and refrigerate for 10 minutes while preparing the remaining ingredients.
2. **Mix sauce and trim peas:** Whisk all sauce ingredients together in a bowl. Trim snow peas and dry them well. Keep the finishing sesame oil separate.
3. **Cook chicken:** Heat 2 tsp of the stir-frying oil in a wide skillet or wok over medium-high heat until shimmering. Spread chicken in one layer, cooking in batches if needed. Leave for about 1 minute, then turn and stir for another 1–2 minutes. Transfer to a plate; it will finish in the sauce.
4. **Cook peas:** Add the remaining teaspoon of stir-frying oil. Stir garlic for 15 seconds, then add snow peas and stir-fry 1–2 minutes. If the pods remain hard, add the measured water and cover for 30–60 seconds. Uncover and let excess water evaporate; taste a pea for a crisp-tender bite.
5. **Glaze and verify:** Return chicken and any plate juices. Re-stir the sauce so settled starch is suspended, then pour it in. Bring to a simmer, tossing, until glossy, about 1–2 minutes. Check several thick chicken slices from the side with a thermometer, avoiding the pan; they must reach 165°F / 74°C. Cook longer if necessary, removing peas temporarily if they are already tender.
6. **Finish:** Turn off heat, stir in sesame oil, and serve promptly with plain rice.

RECIPE: Turkey and Sweet Potato Chili (chili.md)
CUISINES: Tex-Mex
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chili/
SOURCE: Adapted from Chowhound.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.chowhound.com/recipes/spicy-slow-cooker-beef-chili-30669
INGREDIENTS:
  - 900 g ground turkey, preferably 93% lean
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - 180 g yellow onion, finely diced
  - 500 g peeled sweet potato, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
  - 3 cloves garlic, minced
  - 2 tbsp mild chili powder blend, not pure hot chile powder
  - 2 tsp ground cumin
  - 1 tsp smoked paprika
  - 1 can (28 oz / 794 g) crushed tomatoes
  - 2 cups (480 ml) low-sodium chicken broth, plus up to 1 cup (240 ml) only if needed to loosen
  - 2 cans (15 oz / 425 g each) black beans, rinsed and drained, about 510 g total drained
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, added gradually only if needed
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
  - 1 tbsp fresh lime juice, added gradually to taste
  - --- Optional toppings, for the whole batch ---
  - 60 g grated Cheddar
  - 1/4 cup (60 g) sour cream
  - 1 medium avocado, about 150 g edible flesh, diced just before serving
  - 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Brown the turkey before adding the wet ingredients, then simmer only until the sweet potato is tender. Some softened potato thickens the chili, but the goal is still recognizable cubes and beans. Broth, tomatoes and toppings all contribute salt, so the recipe leaves final seasoning until the consistency is right. This is a Tex-Mex-inspired turkey chili with six substantial portions.

## Directions

1. **Brown turkey in two batches:** Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add half the turkey in loose clumps and leave briefly to brown before breaking it into coarse pieces, about 5–6 minutes total. Transfer to a bowl. Repeat with the remaining oil and turkey. Continue directly with cooking; browning is not the final safety check.
2. **Cook aromatics:** With turkey set aside, add onion and sweet-potato cubes to the pot. Cook about 5–7 minutes over medium heat, stirring, until onion softens. If the pan catches, add a small splash from the measured broth. Stir in garlic, chili blend, cumin, paprika and pepper for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. **Add liquid:** Return turkey and its juices. Add tomatoes and the initial 480 ml broth, scraping up browned residue. Bring to a gentle simmer. Keep the additional broth for consistency adjustments.
4. **Simmer and check:** Partly cover and simmer gently about 30–40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until a potato cube yields easily to a knife. Check several substantial turkey pieces for 165°F / 74°C. Add a little reserved broth if the pot becomes thick before potatoes soften.
5. **Finish beans and consistency:** Add drained beans and simmer about 5 minutes until hot. If too thin, uncover briefly to reduce; if too thick, add reserved broth gradually. Avoid cooking until all the potato dissolves.
6. **Season and serve:** Turn off heat. Taste and add salt only if needed. Start with half the lime juice, then add the rest to taste. Divide into six bowls. Offer the listed optional topping quantities separately, divided across the whole batch; any bread or slaw is prepared separately.

RECIPE: Chimichurri (chimichurri.md)
CUISINES: Argentine
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chimichurri/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup Fresh Flat-Leaf Parsley (packed, stems removed)
  - 1/4 cup Fresh Oregano Leaves (or 1 tbsp dried)
  - 4 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1/2 cup Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 2 tbsp Red Wine Vinegar
  - 1/2 tsp Red Pepper Flakes (adjust to taste)
  - 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1/4 tsp Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Keep parsley and oregano finely chopped but still visible in this Argentine-style herb sauce. Stir the garlic, oil and vinegar through the herbs rather than blending everything to a paste. Allow thirty minutes for the flavors to mix, then refrigerate if serving later; stir again before spooning it over food.

## Directions

1. **Chop:** Finely chop parsley and fresh oregano by hand until they are fine, separate pieces. If using the listed dried oregano alternative, add it with the seasonings instead. Mince garlic separately.

2. **Combine:** Stir the herbs, garlic, oil, red wine vinegar, red pepper flakes, measured salt and pepper together in a bowl.

3. **Rest:** Allow 30 minutes before serving. Rest covered in the refrigerator if preparing ahead; a short room-temperature rest counts toward the total 2 hour limit (1 hour above 90°F /32°C).

4. **Taste:** Stir thoroughly and taste; adjust the seasoning only if needed.

5. **Serve and store:** Spoon out only what will be served and keep the remainder covered in the refrigerator. Use a clean spoon and keep the stored batch away from raw-meat utensils. Stir before serving.

RECIPE: Chicken and Broccoli Stir-Fry (chinese-chicken-broccoli.md)
CUISINES: Chinese, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chinese-chicken-broccoli/
SOURCE: Adapted from omnivorescookbook.com
SOURCE_URL: https://omnivorescookbook.com/chicken-and-broccoli/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken coating ---
  - 1 lb (450 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, sliced across the grain about 1/4 inch thick
  - 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
  - 2 tsp cornstarch
  - 1 tsp light soy sauce
  - --- Sauce ---
  - 2 tbsp oyster sauce
  - 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
  - 1 tsp dark soy sauce
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) unsalted chicken stock
  - 1 tsp sugar
  - 2 tsp cornstarch
  - --- Stir-fry ---
  - 1 lb (450 g) broccoli, cut into small florets with peeled stems sliced thinly
  - 1/3 cup (80 ml) water, for steaming broccoli
  - 2 tbsp peanut or neutral oil, divided
  - 4 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1 tsp minced fresh ginger
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Chinese-American-style stir-fry depends on cooking order. Broccoli needs a brief steam before the final toss, while thin chicken cooks quickly in oil. The sauce should leave a glossy coating with a little fluidity. It is seasoned with oyster sauce and soy, so there is no extra salt in the chicken coating.

## Directions

1. **Coat chicken:** Combine the coating wine, cornstarch, and light soy. Toss with chicken and refrigerate for 10 minutes while preparing broccoli and aromatics.
2. **Mix sauce:** Whisk oyster sauce, the sauce wine, dark soy, stock, sugar, and sauce cornstarch in a bowl. Set beside the stove.
3. **Steam broccoli:** Put broccoli and the measured steaming water in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Cover and steam about 2–3 minutes, until stems are nearly tender with a little resistance. Add another splash of water and more time if needed. Transfer broccoli to a plate, drain excess water, and carefully wipe the pan dry with a towel held in tongs.
4. **Cook chicken:** Heat 1 tbsp oil over medium-high heat. Spread half the chicken in one layer; cook about 1 minute before turning and tossing another 1–2 minutes. Transfer to a plate and repeat with 2 tsp oil and remaining chicken. Add the last teaspoon of oil, garlic, and ginger to the pan and stir for 20–30 seconds, reducing heat if needed to prevent scorching.
5. **Finish together:** Return chicken, its plate juices, and broccoli. Re-stir sauce thoroughly and pour it in. Bring to a simmer and toss 1–2 minutes until glossy. Check several of the thickest chicken slices reach 165°F / 74°C, probing from the side and keeping off the pan. Continue cooking if necessary, adding a tablespoon of water if the sauce thickens too far; lift broccoli out temporarily if already tender.
6. **Serve:** Transfer to a platter immediately. Serve with plain rice, with cucumber salad optional alongside.

RECIPE: Chicken & Broccoli with Lap Cheong Rice (chinese-chicken.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chinese-chicken/
SOURCE: Adapted from Gwock Family
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Rice and sausage ---
  - 2 cups (400 g) jasmine rice
  - 2 1/2 cups (600 ml) water, for the rice
  - 3 oz (85 g) Chinese pork sausage (lap cheong), requiring cooking
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) water, for cooking the sausage, plus more if needed
  - --- Chicken and vegetables ---
  - 2 lbs (900 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
  - 600 g broccoli, cut into small florets with peeled stems thinly sliced
  - 2 medium yellow onions (about 300 g total), sliced
  - 3 cloves garlic, minced
  - 2 tbsp neutral oil, divided
  - 1/3 cup (80 ml) water, for steaming broccoli
  - 1/2 tsp black pepper
  - --- Sauce ---
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) dry sherry or Shaoxing wine
  - 3 tbsp light soy sauce
  - 2 tbsp oyster sauce
  - 1 cup (240 ml) unsalted chicken stock
  - 2 tbsp cornstarch
  - 2 tbsp cold water, for the slurry
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Lap cheong contributes sweet, savory pork flavor in a small quantity, folded through jasmine rice. Cooking it separately gives you a clear endpoint and avoids guessing how much time remains in an unfamiliar rice-cooker cycle. The chicken and broccoli are a separate skillet preparation. Together they make a complete meal; no additional rice side is needed.

## Directions

1. **Start rice:** Rinse rice in several changes of cool water and drain well. Combine with the measured rice water in a saucepan with a tight lid. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, stir once, cover, and reduce to low. Cook about 12–15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Turn off heat and rest covered for 10 minutes, then check a grain is tender. Follow the troubleshooting note if it needs more water or time.
2. **Cook sausage separately:** Meanwhile, place whole lap cheong links in a small lidded skillet with the measured sausage water. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently, turning occasionally, about 15–20 minutes or longer if the package requires it. Keep a little water in the pan. Verify the sausage centers reach 160°F / 71°C by probing from an end toward the center. Once cooked, transfer to a clean board, slice into thin coins, and fold into the finished rice. Keep covered briefly until the chicken is ready.
3. **Prepare sauce and slurry:** Mix soy, oyster sauce, and stock in a bowl. Keep the wine separate. In another small bowl, mix cornstarch with its cold water. Cut chicken and vegetables, using separate clean utensils and surfaces for ready-to-eat components.
4. **Steam broccoli:** Add broccoli and its measured steaming water to a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Cover for 2–3 minutes until almost tender through the stems, extending as needed for larger pieces. Remove broccoli, drain excess water, and dry the pan carefully.
5. **Brown chicken and onions:** Season chicken with pepper. Heat 2 tsp oil over medium-high heat and cook half the chicken for about 4–5 minutes. Transfer to a plate and repeat with another 2 tsp oil and the remaining chicken. Add the final 2 tsp oil and onions; cook 4–5 minutes until softened. Add garlic and stir 30 seconds. Take the pan briefly off heat to add wine, then return to heat and simmer 1–2 minutes, scraping up golden residue.
6. **Finish chicken:** Add stock-sauce mixture, chicken, and plate juices. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 5–8 minutes, stirring, until several of the largest chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue as needed before adding broccoli.
7. **Glaze:** Return broccoli. Re-stir slurry and add about half while stirring the simmering sauce. Simmer for 1 minute, then add more slurry only if needed for a light coating, simmering again after each addition. Taste before deciding whether additional seasoning is needed; soy, oyster sauce, and sausage already supply salt.
8. **Serve:** Divide the sausage rice among six bowls and top with chicken, broccoli, and sauce. Serve promptly. The wine is an ingredient in the sauce; a short simmer does not make it reliably alcohol-free.

RECIPE: Chili-Bean Eggplant with Pork (chinese-eggplant-with-garlic-sauce.md)
CUISINES: Sichuan-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chinese-eggplant-with-garlic-sauce/
SOURCE: Adapted from thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/chinese-eggplant-garlic-sauce/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 600 g Chinese or Japanese eggplant, ends trimmed, cut into 1/2-inch-thick bite-sized pieces
  - 150 g ground pork
  - 3 tbsp neutral oil, divided
  - 4 tbsp water, for covered eggplant cooking, divided, plus more by the tablespoon if needed
  - 1 tbsp (15 g) la doubanjiang, fermented broad-bean chili paste, chopped if coarse
  - 2 tbsp finely minced garlic
  - 2 tsp finely minced fresh ginger
  - 30 g scallions, sliced, white and green parts separated
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) unsalted vegetable stock or water
  - 1 tsp reduced-sodium soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
  - 2 tsp granulated sugar
  - 1 tsp cornstarch, mixed with the separately measured cold slurry water
  - 2 tsp cold water, for the cornstarch slurry
  - 2 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar, divided and partly added to taste
  - 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Fermented chili-bean paste gives this dish a different character from a plain garlic sauce. A small amount of ground pork seasons the eggplant rather than making four large meat portions. Vinegar goes in toward the end, and its amount is adjusted against the salt and heat of the paste.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Cut the eggplant evenly and divide into two batches. Mix stock, soy sauce, wine and sugar in a bowl. Mix cornstarch with its separate cold water. Keep doubanjiang, garlic, ginger and scallion whites ready; reserve greens for finishing.
2. **Cook the eggplant:** Heat 1 tbsp oil over medium-high in a lidded skillet. Brown half the eggplant for 3–4 minutes, turning occasionally. Lower to medium, add 2 tbsp water and cover for another 3–5 minutes, until the center yields readily to a fork. Add a tablespoon more water if needed. Uncover to evaporate excess, then transfer to a plate. Repeat with another tablespoon oil, the second half of the eggplant and remaining 2 tbsp water.
3. **Cook pork:** Add the final tablespoon oil and pork. Cook over medium-high about 4–6 minutes, breaking it into small pieces, until cooked through and reaching 160°F / 71°C. For a reading, gather a small mound and insert the probe without touching the pan.
4. **Flavor the base:** Lower heat to medium-low. Stir in doubanjiang and ginger for about 30 seconds, then garlic and scallion whites for another 20–30 seconds. Pour in the stock mixture before the garlic burns. Simmer about 1 minute.
5. **Coat:** Stir the slurry again and add half. Simmer 20–30 seconds, then fold in eggplant. Add the remaining slurry only if needed for a light coating and discard any unused portion. Cook gently another minute, adding a tablespoon water if the sauce becomes tight.
6. **Finish and serve:** Stir in 1 tbsp vinegar and the sesame oil, then fold in scallion greens off heat. Taste and add remaining vinegar only if wanted. Serve as four shared sides with plain rice and other vegetables; use the pork-free variation for a vegetable-only table.

RECIPE: Garlic-Ginger Stir-Fry Sauce (chinese-garlic-sauce-base.md)
CUISINES: Chinese-American-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chinese-garlic-sauce-base/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 tsp neutral oil
  - 2 tbsp finely minced garlic
  - 1 tbsp finely minced fresh ginger
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) unsalted vegetable broth or water
  - 2 tbsp reduced-sodium soy sauce
  - 1 tsp dark soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp oyster sauce or vegetarian mushroom stir-fry sauce
  - 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
  - 2 tsp granulated sugar
  - 1/8 tsp ground white pepper
  - 1 tsp cornstarch
  - 2 tsp cold water, for the slurry
  - 1 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar
  - 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - Hot water, only as needed to bring the finished sauce to 240 ml
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Garlic and ginger are cooked gently before the sauce thickens. The starch gives a light coating, while soy and oyster or mushroom sauce supply most of the salt. Vinegar and sesame oil go in near the end for a clearer aroma.

## Directions

1. **Measure:** Mix broth, both soy sauces, oyster or mushroom sauce, wine, sugar and white pepper. In a separate cup, stir the cornstarch into the 2 tsp cold slurry water.
2. **Cook aromatics:** Warm neutral oil in a small saucepan over medium-low. Add garlic and ginger and stir for 30–45 seconds, until fragrant but still pale. Lower heat if the edges start coloring.
3. **Simmer and thicken:** Add the broth mixture and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook about 1 minute. Stir the slurry again and pour it in while stirring. Simmer 30–60 seconds, until lightly thickened with no chalky starch taste. Do not reduce to a sticky syrup.
4. **Finish and measure:** Take off heat; stir in vinegar and sesame oil. Carefully pour into a heatproof measuring jug. Add a little hot water, if needed, to reach 240 ml. If the sauce exceeds 240 ml, return it to the saucepan and simmer briefly to the stated yield, then measure again.
5. **Use or chill:** Use 120 ml as the starting portion for the linked 600 g garlic-eggplant recipe. For other cooked vegetables or protein, begin with a little sauce and add only enough to coat; their moisture and seasoning differ. Half this recipe makes the 120 ml needed for one eggplant batch. Chill unused sauce promptly in a shallow container.

RECIPE: Chinese Sausage Fried Rice (chinese-sausage-fried-rice.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chinese-sausage-fried-rice/
SOURCE: Adapted from Taste.com.au
SOURCE_URL: http://www.taste.com.au/recipes/chinese-fried-rice-2/5f3be212-27bf-45a8-abae-7c2e3581f5ab
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Recipe ---
  - 4 cups cooked jasmine rice, cold, properly refrigerated
  - 5 Chinese sausages (lap cheong), thinly sliced after any package-required preparation
  - 3 large eggs, beaten
  - 3 green onions, thinly sliced
  - 2 garlic cloves, minced
  - 1 red chili, finely chopped
  - 1/2 cup frozen peas, thawed
  - 2 tbsp light soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp oyster sauce
  - 2 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - 3 tsp peanut oil
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Cold, separated rice is easier to toss without crushing it. Cook the eggs into ribbons before combining them with the sausage and rice. Lap cheong products differ: the cured appearance does not establish that a sausage is ready to eat; its label determines the preparation needed.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the rice:** Break up cooked jasmine rice gently. Keep it cold until ready to add it to the pan. The listed amount is cooked rice, not dry rice.
2. **Make the egg ribbons:** Use large eggs, 1/2 of the toasted sesame oil, and 1/3 of the peanut oil for this stage. Whisk the eggs with their half of the sesame oil. Use the egg-stage peanut oil across the omelet batches. In a hot wok, cook thin omelets with roughly one-third of the original three-egg mixture at a time, adjusting the number of omelets for the listed quantity. Cook until fully set without liquid egg; an egg-dish center is 160°F / 71°C. Move to a clean board, roll and slice into ribbons. Set aside.
3. **Cook the sausage:** Use Chinese sausages (lap cheong), green onions, and 2/3 of the peanut oil for this stage. Add this stage’s peanut oil to the wok. Add the prepared sausage and all the green onions. Stir-fry over medium-high heat until browned and the labeled cooking requirements are met; 2–3 minutes is a browning check, not proof raw sausage is cooked. Reduce the heat if sugars scorch.
4. **Add the aromatics:** Add garlic cloves and red chili and stir-fry for about a minute until fragrant, lowering the heat if the garlic catches. Omit the chili or serve it separately for milder portions.
5. **Fry the rice:** Add the separated rice and turn it over high heat in an uncrowded pan, pressing out remaining clumps gently. Work in batches rather than packing the wok; 2–3 minutes is a first check.
6. **Season and heat through:** Add frozen peas, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, and 1/2 of the toasted sesame oil, including the remaining half of the sesame oil. Toss until peas and rice are hot throughout, checking the cold-rice mixture at 165°F / 74°C in several places. Do not stop at a fixed two-minute clock if cold clumps remain.
7. **Fold and serve:** Fold in all the fully cooked egg ribbons and serve promptly among the listed portions. More omelets, sausage preparation or rice batches lengthen the schedule.

RECIPE: Steamed Fish (chinese-steamed-fish.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chinese-steamed-fish/
SOURCE: Adapted from rasamalaysia.com
SOURCE_URL: https://rasamalaysia.com/steamed-fish-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Fish and sauce ---
  - 1 (1 1/2 lb) Whole fish (snapper or sea bass), scaled, gutted, gills removed; original-size fish
  - 1 Fresh ginger piece, original 2-inch piece, peeled and julienned
  - 2 Scallions, cut into fine threads
  - Fresh cilantro leaves, as desired
  - 2 tbsp Peanut or other high-heat oil
  - 4 tbsp Light soy sauce
  - 3 tbsp Shaoxing or Chinese rice wine
  - 2 tbsp Water for sauce
  - 1/4 tsp Toasted sesame oil
  - 1 tbsp Rock sugar, powdered
  - 3 White-pepper dashes
  - Water for steaming, as needed with the plate above the water
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Whole steamed fish has a short, thickness-dependent cooking window. Ginger and wine season the fish before steaming; a separate clean soy mixture and hot oil finish it. Keep the steaming wine and sauce wine separate so both reach their intended stages.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the fish:** Prepare Whole fish (snapper or sea bass), 1/2 of the Fresh ginger piece, and 1/3 of the Shaoxing or Chinese rice wine. Keep fish cold until the steamer is ready and thaw frozen fish in the refrigerator, following any vacuum-package opening instructions. Rinse the ginger, scallions and cilantro under running water before cutting and drain well, keeping garnish tools separate from raw fish. Pat the cleaned fish dry. Place the ginger portion assigned here over the fish; retain its other half for the finish. Drizzle the wine portion assigned here over the fish; the remaining wine belongs to the sauce.
2. **Mix the sauce:** Combine Light soy sauce, 2/3 of the Shaoxing or Chinese rice wine, Water for sauce, Toasted sesame oil, Rock sugar, and White-pepper dashes in a clean bowl until the powdered sugar dissolves. This sauce is separate from the raw-fish plate; do not dip raw-contact utensils into it.
3. **Steam:** Use Water for steaming under a stable rack and heatproof fish plate, with a lid that closes. Bring the water to a boil before inserting the cold fish. Cover and begin checking around 8–10 minutes; continue until thick flesh reaches 145°F /63°C away from bone, is no longer translucent and separates easily. Fish thickness and plate loads change the time; use additional uncrowded plates or batches rather than piling fish.
4. **Drain:** Turn off the steam, lift the plate carefully with heat protection and discard the collected steaming liquid. Keep the cooked fish on a clean heatproof plate; do not return it to raw-contact dishes.
5. **Add aromatics:** Rinse and drain 1/2 of the Fresh ginger piece and Scallions well, then arrange over the hot fish. Use all the scallion threads and the retained half of the ginger.
6. **Hot oil:** Heat Peanut or other high-heat oil in a small dry pan over controlled heat until hot and shimmering, without keeping it smoking. Carefully pour over the well-drained aromatics, keeping face and hands clear of splashes.
7. **Heat the sauce:** Reduce the pan heat and carefully add the entire clean prepared sauce to the oil pan, allowing for splatter. Bring the sauce to a bubble and stir until the sugar is fully dissolved, then pour all of it over the cooked fish. Do not add another dose of oil or wine.
8. **Serve:** Garnish with Fresh cilantro leaves and serve promptly. Four portions are the original whole-fish planning yield, including bones. For larger batches use additional original-size fish with adequate plate capacity; smaller batches need appropriate fish portions and earlier center checks. Ingredient arithmetic does not multiply the steaming clock.

RECIPE: Chinese-Style Snapper (chinese-style-snapper.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chinese-style-snapper/
SOURCE: Adapted from taste.com.au
SOURCE_URL: https://www.taste.com.au/recipes/chinese-style-snapper/fd791197-4ba2-4cc8-9a88-560eeaa101d3
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.8 kg Whole Snapper, scaled and gutted
  - 3 cloves Garlic, finely chopped
  - 1 (3-inch) piece Fresh Ginger, finely shredded
  - 1/4 cup Soy Sauce
  - 1/4 cup Chicken Broth
  - 2 tbsp Chinese Rice Wine (Shaoxing)
  - 3 tsp Toasted Sesame Oil
  - 2 tbsp Peanut Oil
  - 6 Scallions, shredded into 4-inch threads
  - 1/2 cup Fresh Cilantro
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This covered whole-snapper preparation uses ginger, garlic and a soy-wine dressing, followed by a hot peanut-oil finish. Slashes expose thicker flesh to the seasoning; they do not guarantee that every fish cooks in the same time. Keep the whole fish supported on a large heatproof platter when transferring it.

## Directions

1. **Prep:** Preheat the oven to 425°F /220°C. Choose a roasting pan that holds the original-size whole snapper without bending it; for multiples use additional pans. Line it with foil and nonstick baking parchment rated for the temperature, keeping the paper inside the covered pan.

2. **Slash:** Use a scaled, gutted fish with the gills removed. Pat the inside and outside dry, keeping raw-contact tools separate from the serving platter. Cut three approximately 1-cm-deep slashes into the thick flesh on each side. Put it in the pan. Rinse fresh ginger, scallions and cilantro under running water as appropriate and drain thoroughly.

3. **Season:** Spread all the garlic and half the listed ginger into and over the slits. Mix all the soy sauce, broth, rice wine and sesame oil and pour over the fish.

4. **Bake:** Cover the pan tightly with foil. Begin checking before the original 45–50-minute planning range is complete and continue as needed until thick flesh on both sides reaches 145°F /63°C without touching bone, and is no longer translucent and separates easily. Fish thickness, starting temperature and pan load change the time.

5. **Transfer:** With broad spatulas, carefully move the cooked fish to a warmed heatproof platter. Reserve all the cooking juices in the roasting pan, taking care with steam. Put all the scallions and the remaining ginger on the fish.

6. **Oil:** Heat all the peanut oil in a small dry saucepan over controlled heat until hot and shimmering; do not maintain smoking oil. Carefully pour it over the well-drained scallions and ginger, keeping hands and face clear of splashes.

7. **Finish:** Check the reserved raw-contact pan juices at 145°F /63°C before pouring them over the cooked fish. If needed, return the pan to the oven or transfer juices to a saucepan to finish heating. Add all the cilantro and serve promptly. When scaling, use additional original-size fish and roomy pans; do not multiply the oven clock or assume a fractional fish has the same geometry.

RECIPE: Chipotle Pork Bowls (chipotle-pork-and-sweet-corn-tamale-bowls.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chipotle-pork-and-sweet-corn-tamale-bowls/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Polenta base ---
  - 1 cup Dry polenta or cornmeal
  - 4 cups Chicken broth
  - 1/2 tsp Ground cumin
  - 2 tbsp Unsalted butter
  - 1/4 cup Cotija cheese, crumbled
  - --- Separate charred corn ---
  - 1 cup Frozen sweet corn
  - --- Smoky pork sauce ---
  - 1 1/2 lb Ground pork
  - 1 Red bell pepper, washed, stemmed, seeded and diced
  - Cooking oil, as needed for the pork skillet
  - Salt, to taste in the cooked pork sauce
  - Black pepper, to taste in the cooked pork sauce
  - 3 Garlic cloves, minced
  - 1 tsp Dried oregano
  - 2–3 Chipotle peppers in adobo, minced
  - 1 tbsp Adobo sauce
  - 1 can (14 1/2 oz) Fire-roasted crushed tomatoes
  - --- Current toppings ---
  - 1 Avocado, cubed just before serving
  - 1 Lime, washed and cut into wedges
  - 1 cup Green cabbage, washed and shredded
  - 2 tbsp Pepitas, toasted
  - Sour cream, for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This bowl pairs broth-cooked polenta with smoky ground pork, separately charred corn, cotija, cabbage and pepitas. Cook the frozen corn according to its package before the brief browning stage; char alone is not proof that a ready-to-cook product is cooked. Break up the pork and check 160°F, keeping the garlic and chipotle adobo sauce in the pork sauce. [Carnitas Bowl](/mise/recipes/carnitas-bowl) has its own braised-shoulder ingredients and cooking schedule; follow that full recipe separately.

## Directions

1. **Cook and enrich polenta:** Have Dry polenta or cornmeal, Chicken broth, Ground cumin, Unsalted butter, and Cotija cheese ready. Bring the measured broth to a boil, gradually whisk in the polenta and cumin, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook, whisking frequently to prevent sticking, until the grains are tender and no longer gritty. Begin checks after 15 minutes, using the actual polenta’s package cooking guidance; coarse grinds can take substantially longer. Once tender, stir in all the butter and cotija. Cover and keep gently hot while the pork finishes.
2. **Cook then char corn:** Cook Frozen sweet corn according to its package’s required instructions, then drain well if wet. Use a heavy skillet suitable for dry browning and spread the cooked kernels in a manageable single layer. Brown over medium-high heat, beginning checks after about 2 minutes, then stir to color another face. Stop before kernels turn black or dry out. Transfer the whole cooked corn amount to a clean dish; keep it separate from the polenta for this version.
3. **Cook pork and pepper:** Have Ground pork, Red bell pepper, and Cooking oil ready. Add the cooking-oil allowance to the skillet only as needed, then cook the pork and pepper over medium-high heat, breaking the meat into crumbles and turning to cook it evenly. Use manageable loads if crowded. Continue until the pork reaches 160°F /71°C, measured in several thicker clusters; browning or a 3-minute crust clock alone does not establish the endpoint.
4. **Add aromatics and adobo:** Lower the heat if needed and push the cooked meat aside enough to add Garlic cloves, Dried oregano, Chipotle peppers in adobo, and Adobo sauce to the skillet. Stir briefly until fragrant, starting checks after about 45 seconds; stop before the garlic darkens. Include the full measured adobo sauce as well as the minced peppers.
5. **Simmer and season:** Add Salt, Black pepper, and Fire-roasted crushed tomatoes, using the salt and pepper allowances after tasting the fully cooked sauce. Scrape the browned bits into the tomatoes and simmer gently, beginning checks after about 5 minutes, until the sauce coats the pork. Keep the pork hot while the polenta finishes; extend cooking as needed instead of serving gritty grains to meet the header time.
6. **Assemble bowls:** Divide the hot polenta and pork across the listed portions, add the separate charred corn and finish with Avocado, Lime, Green cabbage, Pepitas, and Sour cream. Offer the lime wedges at the table; Serve promptly.

RECIPE: Chocolate Blended Oats with Raspberry Chia Jam (chocolate-blended-oats-with-raspberry-chia-jam.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chocolate-blended-oats-with-raspberry-chia-jam/
SOURCE: Adapted from glow-diaries.com
SOURCE_URL: https://glow-diaries.com/choc-blended-oats/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup Frozen Raspberries
  - 1 tbsp Chia Seeds
  - 1 3/4 cups Rolled Oats
  - 1 3/4 cups Soy or Almond Milk
  - 1/2 cup Greek Yogurt
  - 1/4 cup Cacao Powder
  - 1/4 cup Maple Syrup
  - 2 tbsp Chia Seeds
  - 1 tsp Vanilla Extract
  - 1/8 tsp Sea Salt
  - 2 oz Dark Chocolate, melted
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This is ideal for meal-prep breakfasts. Blending standard rolled oats transforms them into a smooth, cake-like batter. The tart, seed-studded raspberry jam provides essential brightness that cuts through the dense, earthy cacao. By letting this set overnight, the chia seeds fully hydrate, giving the oats a pudding-like texture that keeps you full until lunch.

## Directions

1.  **The Jam:** Place raspberries in a microwave-safe bowl. Heat until they break down into a compote. Stir in 1 tbsp chia seeds and let sit for 5 minutes to thicken.
2.  **The Base:** Combine all blended oats ingredients in a high-powered blender. Blend for 60 seconds until perfectly smooth.
3.  **Layer:** Divide the raspberry jam among 4 jars. Pour the blended oat mixture over the jam.
4.  **The Cap:** Drizzle the melted dark chocolate over the top of each jar to create a Crunch layer.
5.  **The Finish:** Seal the jars and refrigerate for at least 90 minutes (or ideally overnight). The mixture will firm up significantly as the oats and chia seeds absorb the liquid.
6.  **Serve:** These keep for up to 5 days. Eat cold straight from the jar.

RECIPE: Chocolate Bread Pudding (chocolate-bread-pudding-with-vanilla-ice-cream.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chocolate-bread-pudding-with-vanilla-ice-cream/
SOURCE: Adapted from The Ritz-Carlton, Cancun
INGREDIENTS:
  - 13 cups Brioche bread, 3/4-inch cubes (stale preferred)
  - 6 oz Bittersweet Chocolate (70% cacao), chopped
  - 6 oz White Chocolate Chips
  - 4 large Eggs
  - 1/2 cup + 4 tbsp Granulated Sugar
  - 2 tsp Vanilla Extract
  - 1 1/2 cups Heavy Cream
  - 1/2 cup Whole Milk
  - 2 cups Vanilla Bean Ice Cream
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Bread pudding is a way to honor stale bread - brioche is rich and tender, so it soaks up custard without becoming mushy. The double chocolate (bittersweet and white) creates complexity: dark chocolate for depth, white chocolate for sweetness. The 15-minute soak before baking is mandatory - it lets the bread fully hydrate so the custard distributes evenly and the whole thing sets together.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 350°F. Spray eight 6-oz ramekins (or a 9x13 baking dish) with non-stick spray.
2.  **The Mix:** In a large bowl, toss the brioche cubes with the chopped bittersweet chocolate and white chocolate chips.
3.  **The Custard:** In a mixer, beat eggs, 1/2 cup sugar, and vanilla until pale. Gradually whisk in the heavy cream and milk until smooth.
4.  **The Soak:** Pour the custard over the bread mixture. Toss gently to coat. **Let stand for 15 minutes** to allow the brioche to hydrate.
5.  **Assemble:** Transfer the mixture to the prepared ramekins, spreading evenly. Drizzle the remaining 4 tbsp of sugar over the tops.
6.  **Bake:** Bake for 15-20 minutes until the edges are golden and the custard is set in the center but still has a slight wobble.
7.  **Serve:** Serve warm with a generous scoop of vanilla bean ice cream.

RECIPE: Chocolate Chia Pudding (chocolate-chia-pudding.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chocolate-chia-pudding/
SOURCE: Adapted from eatingbirdfood.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.eatingbirdfood.com/chocolate-chia-pudding/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup Unsweetened Vanilla Almond Milk
  - 6 tbsp Chia Seeds
  - 1/4 cup Maple Syrup
  - 2 tbsp Unsweetened Cocoa Powder
  - 1 tsp Vanilla Extract
  - 1/8 tsp Sea Salt
  - Fresh Berries, Chocolate Chips, or Chopped Nuts
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The secret to smooth chia pudding is the blender method. Many recipes leave the seeds whole, which can result in a gritty, uneven texture. By blending the seeds on high speed, we break them down until they are undetectable, creating a silky, mousse-like consistency that feels like a comforting dessert but provides superfood nutrition. Always let it chill for at least 3 hours to allow the fibers to fully set.

## Directions

1.  **Blend:** Combine almond milk, chia seeds, maple syrup, cocoa powder, vanilla, and salt in a high-powered blender.
2.  **Pulverize:** Start on low and gradually increase to high. Blend for 60 seconds until the mixture is completely smooth and the seeds have disappeared.
3.  **The Finish:** Transfer the mixture to individual jars or a large bowl. Cover and refrigerate for **at least 3 hours** (or overnight) until thick and set.
4.  **Serve:** Stir once before serving. Top with fresh berries and nuts for **Textural Balance**.

RECIPE: Chocolate Chip Beet Muffins (chocolate-chip-beet-muffins.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chocolate-chip-beet-muffins/
SOURCE: Adapted from minimalistbaker.com
SOURCE_URL: https://minimalistbaker.com/fudgy-vegan-double-chocolate-beet-muffins/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup Beet Puree (Roasted or canned)
  - 2 large Eggs
  - 1/4 cup Unsalted Butter, melted
  - 1/4 cup Honey
  - 1/3 cup Brown Sugar, packed
  - 1/4 cup Whole Milk
  - 1 1/3 cups Whole-Wheat Flour
  - 1/2 cup Unsweetened Cocoa Powder
  - 1 1/2 tsp Baking Soda
  - 1/4 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1/3 cup Semisweet Chocolate Chips
  - Whole milk, a little more only if needed for a scoopable batter
  - Additional chocolate chips, optional, for topping
  - Butter or baking spray, as needed for greasing if not using liners
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Beet puree, cocoa and chocolate chips make a thick, scoopable batter. Fold only until the flour disappears, and check the center rather than judging doneness by the dark color.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 375°F. Line a standard 12-cup muffin tin, or grease it with the listed pan allowance. Use smooth prepared beet puree: blend drained plain canned beets, or blend already roasted beets once cool enough for your blender according to its instructions. Let any warm puree and melted butter cool before adding the eggs. Beet roasting and its cooling are separate advance preparation.

2. **Wet mix:** Whisk beet puree, eggs, melted butter, honey and brown sugar together, then whisk in the listed whole milk.

3. **Dry mix:** Whisk flour, cocoa, baking soda and salt together, then fold into the wet mixture just until no dry flour remains. The batter should be thick and scoopable. If it is too stiff to scoop, fold in a little of the separate extra-milk allowance at a time; stop before it becomes pourable.

4. **Fold:** Fold all the listed semisweet chocolate chips into the batter.

5. **Fill:** Divide among the muffin cups, filling no more than ¾ full. Sprinkle on the separate optional topping chips. Bake any excess batter in additional cups or a later batch.

6. **Bake:** Bake for 18–22 minutes, until a center tester comes out without wet batter; melted chocolate on the tester is different from raw batter.

7. **Cool:** Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack. Cool completely before sealing for storage.

RECIPE: Chocolate Chip Cookie Cake (chocolate-chip-cookie-cake.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chocolate-chip-cookie-cake/
SOURCE: Adapted from thatskinnychickcanbake.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.thatskinnychickcanbake.com/chocolate-chip-cookie-cake/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Cookie dough ---
  - 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature
  - 1 cup light brown sugar, packed
  - 1/2 cup granulated sugar
  - 2 large eggs
  - 2 tsp vanilla extract
  - 2 1/8 cups all-purpose flour
  - 1 tsp baking soda
  - 1/2 tsp sea salt
  - 2 cups semisweet chocolate discs
  - 1/2 cup candy-coated milk chocolate candies
  - --- Topping ---
  - 3/4 cup candy-coated milk chocolate candies
  - --- Pan preparation ---
  - butter or baking spray, enough to grease the pan and parchment
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Chocolate discs make larger pockets of chocolate; the same listed amount of chips is also an option. The candy-coated chocolates add sweetness and color, with separate amounts inside and on top. Use a deep pan so the dough has room to spread, and let the whole cookie cake cool before slicing.

## Directions

1. **Prep:** Preheat the oven to 375°F. For the original batch, line a 14-inch deep round pizza pan with parchment and use butter or baking spray to grease the entire pan including the paper. Have enough appropriate pans for the full dough before mixing; keep similar dough thickness and expansion room when scaling.
2. **Cream:** In a large bowl, cream unsalted butter, light brown sugar, and granulated sugar until light and fluffy, about 3–5 minutes.
3. **Add eggs:** Add large eggs and vanilla extract and beat until combined.
4. **Dry mix:** Whisk all-purpose flour, baking soda, and sea salt together, then stir into the butter mixture until just combined.
5. **Fold:** Fold in semisweet chocolate discs and candy-coated milk chocolate candies.
6. **Shape:** Spread all the dough evenly onto the prepared pan, leaving the original 1/2-inch border for expansion. Sprinkle all candy-coated milk chocolate candies over the top, pressing them in lightly. At other scales divide all dough and its topping proportionally among enough appropriate pans; do not force every batch into the same 14-inch pan.
7. **Bake:** Bake for 20–25 minutes until the edges are deep golden brown and the center is set but still soft. Keep the same dough thickness when scaling; use additional pans, rather than multiplying pan dimensions or baking time.
8. **Cool:** Let cool completely in the pan before slicing so the structure can firm up.

RECIPE: Chocolate Chip Walnut Cookies (chocolate-chip-walnut-cookies.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chocolate-chip-walnut-cookies/
SOURCE: allrecipes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/10813/best-chocolate-chip-cookies/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup butter, softened
  - 1 cup white sugar
  - 1 cup packed brown sugar
  - 2 eggs
  - 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
  - 1 teaspoon baking soda
  - 2 teaspoons hot water
  - 1/2 teaspoon salt
  - 3 cups all-purpose flour
  - 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips
  - 1 cup chopped walnuts
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Dissolve the baking soda in the listed hot water before adding it to this walnut-and-chocolate dough. Keep the portions similar in size and leave room for them to spread; browned edges and a center that has set are more useful than a timer alone.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 350°F / 175°C. Set out ungreased baking sheets and a cooling rack.

2. **Cream:** Beat the softened butter with the white sugar and packed brown sugar until smooth and creamy, scraping the bowl. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then mix in the vanilla.

3. **Dissolve:** In a small cup, dissolve the baking soda in the listed hot water. Stir this mixture and the salt into the butter mixture.

4. **Mix and portion:** Stir in the flour just until no dry pockets remain, then distribute the chocolate chips and chopped walnuts throughout. Drop similarly sized large spoonfuls onto the ungreased sheets, leaving about 2 inches between portions. Keep dough waiting for later trays covered and refrigerated.

5. **Bake:** Load the oven only once it has reached temperature. Bake for about 10 minutes per tray, until the edges are browned and the centers have set but remain soft. Check the first tray closely; scoop size and your pan affect the time. Bake the remaining dough in further loads as needed.

6. **Cool:** Let the cookies firm on the sheet until they can be lifted intact, then transfer them to a rack. Let the sheets cool before loading more dough. Cool the cookies completely before packing them.

RECIPE: Chocolate Crinkle Cookies (chocolate-crinkle-cookies.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chocolate-crinkle-cookies/
SOURCE: Adapted from thepioneerwoman.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.thepioneerwoman.com/food-cooking/recipes/a37810333/chocolate-crinkle-cookies-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6 oz Semisweet Chocolate, chopped
  - 1/2 cup Salted Butter, cubed
  - 1/2 cup Light Brown Sugar, packed
  - 1 1/2 cups Granulated Sugar (divided)
  - 3 large Eggs
  - 2 tsp Vanilla Extract
  - 1 1/2 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 1/2 cup Unsweetened Cocoa Powder
  - 1 tsp Baking Powder
  - 1/4 tsp Baking Soda
  - 1/4 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1 cup Powdered Sugar
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A firm, chilled dough is easier to portion and coat. Roll each ball in granulated sugar first and powdered sugar second, then bake until the coating cracks and the edges feel firm. Keep the centers soft after baking rather than drying them out to make the tops look done.

## Directions

1. **Melt:** Set a heatproof bowl above gently simmering water, with its bottom clear of the water. Melt the chopped chocolate and salted butter together, stirring until smooth. Remove the bowl from the pan and let the mixture cool slightly before adding it to the eggs.

2. **Dry mix:** Whisk the flour, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda and kosher salt until evenly mixed and free of lumps.

3. **Beat:** Beat the brown sugar, eggs, vanilla and one-third of the listed granulated sugar on medium-high until light and smooth, about 2–3 minutes. For the original batch, that sugar portion is 1/2 cup; reserve the other two-thirds for rolling.

4. **Combine:** Mix the slightly cooled chocolate-butter mixture into the egg mixture. On low speed, add the dry ingredients only until the dough is evenly combined. Cover and refrigerate for 2–4 hours, until firm enough to scoop and roll.

5. **Prepare and coat:** Near the end of chilling, preheat the oven to 350°F. Line baking sheets with parchment. Put the reserved two-thirds of the granulated sugar in one shallow bowl and all the powdered sugar in another. Scoop about 1 tablespoon of dough per cookie, form balls, and coat first with granulated sugar and then generously with powdered sugar. Leave about 2 inches between balls. Keep unportioned dough refrigerated while later trays wait.

6. **Bake:** Once the oven reaches 350°F, bake for 10–12 minutes per tray, until the tops have cracked and the edges feel firm. Use further loads as needed; do not crowd the sheets to force a particular count.

7. **Cool:** Leave the cookies on the sheet for 5 minutes, then move them to racks to cool completely. Let a hot sheet cool before loading another batch. Discard coating sugar that has contacted raw dough.

RECIPE: Chocolate Pie (chocolate-pie.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chocolate-pie/
SOURCE: Adapted from thepioneerwoman.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thepioneerwoman.com/cooking/chocolate-pie/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 Pie Crust, baked and cooled (Use the [Apple Pie](/mise/recipes/apple-pie) Vodka Hack dough!)
  - 6 1/2 oz Bittersweet Chocolate, finely chopped
  - 1 1/2 cups Granulated Sugar
  - 1/4 cup Cornstarch
  - 1/4 tsp Sea Salt
  - 3 cups Whole Milk
  - 4 large Egg Yolks
  - 2 tbsp Unsalted Butter
  - 2 tsp Vanilla Extract
  - Whipped Cream
  - Shaved Dark Chocolate
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This chocolate cream pie uses a cooked pudding filling. Stir until it bubbles and thickens, then take it off the heat before melting in the chopped chocolate. Keep the surface covered during chilling for a smooth top; the center must be cold before slicing.

## Directions

1.  **The Base:** Have the baked, cooled crust and chopped chocolate ready before heating the filling. In a medium saucepan, whisk together sugar, cornstarch, and salt.
2.  **Emulsify:** Slowly whisk in the milk and egg yolks until the mixture is perfectly smooth.
3.  **The Cook:** Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture begins bubbling and becomes thick and glossy like pudding. Start checking around 6-8 minutes, but continue if still thin; the texture, not the clock, determines when to stop.
4.  **The Melt:** Remove from heat immediately. Stir in the chopped bittersweet chocolate, butter, and vanilla. Whisk until the chocolate is completely melted and the filling is uniform.
5.  **The Finish:** Pour the hot filling into the cooled pie crust without overfilling; refrigerate any extra pudding separately in small dishes. Press a piece of plastic wrap directly onto the surface of the pudding to prevent a "skin" from forming.
6.  **Chill:** Refrigerate for **at least 4 hours**, keeping the wrap against the surface, until the filling is cold and set.
7.  **Serve:** Top with billowy whipped cream and shaved chocolate for contrast.

## Cooking Notes

The linked Apple Pie supplies dough, not a blind-baking method: use its dough only, not its apple filling, egg wash or filled-pie baking schedule. For a homemade shell using the linked two-crust Apple Pie dough, use one half of that dough for a single 9-inch pie shell; reserve the other half for another use. Fit and crimp the shell, line with parchment and fill about two-thirds with pie weights. Chill 30 minutes, bake at 375°F for about 20 minutes, remove parchment and weights, prick the bottom and bake another 15–20 minutes until golden across the base. Shield edges if needed and cool completely before filling. Follow package directions instead for a purchased crust, and use a pan rated for the baking temperature.

RECIPE: Chocolate Protein Zucchini Muffins (chocolate-protein-zucchini-muffins.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chocolate-protein-zucchini-muffins/
SOURCE: yummytoddlerfood.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.yummytoddlerfood.com/chocolate-zucchini-muffins-with-blueberries/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup whole wheat flour
  - 1/4 cup chocolate protein powder
  - ¼ cup unsweetened cocoa powder
  - 1 teaspoon cinnamon (optional)
  - 1 teaspoon baking powder
  - ½ teaspoon baking soda
  - ½ teaspoon salt
  - 1 cup grated zucchini, squeezed very dry and packed tightly (measure after grating and squeezing)
  - 1 cup milk
  - ¼ cup honey or maple syrup
  - 2 eggs (lightly beaten)
  - ¼ cup unsalted butter (melted, or use canola or avocado oil)
  - 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
  - ½ cup chocolate chips (or 1 cup blueberries or up to 1 cup chocolate chips)
  - Nonstick spray or butter, for greasing the muffin pan
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Measure the listed zucchini amount after grating, squeezing very dry and packing it tightly. This cocoa-and-protein-powder batter is different from the buckwheat zucchini muffins; fold briefly and check the center rather than relying on dark color.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 375°F. Grease a standard 12-cup muffin pan with the listed spray or butter. Grate zucchini, squeeze very dry in a clean towel, then measure the listed amount packed tightly.

2. **Dry mix:** Whisk flour, chocolate protein powder, cocoa, optional cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda and salt together.

3. **Wet mix:** Whisk squeezed zucchini, milk, the chosen honey or maple syrup, eggs, the chosen melted and slightly cooled butter or canola or avocado oil, and vanilla together.

4. **Fold:** Fold the dry mixture into the wet just until no dry flour remains. Fold in the chosen chocolate chips or blueberries. The original 12-muffin batch uses ½ cup chips, or 1 cup blueberries, or up to 1 cup chips; follow the corresponding listed scaled choice and use only one.

5. **Bake and cool:** Fill muffin cups no more than ¾ full, using extra cups or a later batch for excess batter. Bake about 16–18 minutes, until a center tester comes out without wet batter. Cool briefly in the pan, then transfer to a rack to cool to room temperature before storage.

RECIPE: Chocolate Soufflé (chocolate-souffle.md)
CUISINES: French
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chocolate-souffle/
SOURCE: Adapted from Epicurious.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/chocolate-souffle-106173
INGREDIENTS:
  - 5 oz Bittersweet Chocolate (not unsweetened), chopped
  - 3 large Egg Yolks (room temp)
  - 6 large Egg Whites (room temp)
  - 1/3 cup + 1 tbsp Granulated Sugar
  - Pinch of Sea Salt
  - Unsalted Butter (for the dish)
  - Powdered sugar, as desired for serving
  - Lightly sweetened whipped cream, as desired for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Fold the chocolate and egg foam gently but thoroughly so no streaks remain. The thumb-run clears a shallow channel at the rim; it helps an even rise but does not replace a correctly prepared dish and properly beaten whites. Have bowls and accompaniments ready before baking so the soufflé can be served immediately.

## Directions

1. **Prepare dish:** Preheat the oven to 375°F. Butter an original-batch 6-cup soufflé dish generously. Reserve 3/19 of the full listed granulated sugar for coating and 16/19 for the egg whites; for the original batch these are 1 tablespoon and ⅓ cup respectively. Coat the buttered dish with its allocated sugar and knock out the excess.
2. **Melt chocolate:** Melt all the chocolate in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water, stirring until smooth. Remove the bowl from the heat and let it cool enough that it will not cook yolks on contact, while staying fluid. Stir in all the yolks; the mixture stiffens.
3. **Beat whites:** In a clean bowl, beat all the whites with the pinch of salt until they just hold soft peaks. Gradually add all the reserved batter sugar, then beat until just-stiff glossy peaks hold. Avoid dry, clumpy whites. Keep egg preparation brief rather than leaving eggs out for an indefinite warming period.
4. **Lighten:** Stir some meringue into the chocolate to make it easier to fold; the source uses about 1 cup for its original batch. At other scales, start with a proportionately smaller or larger spoonful and stop once the base is loosened, reserving most foam for folding.
5. **Fold:** Fold in all the remaining meringue gently but thoroughly, lifting from the bottom until no white streaks remain.
6. **Fill:** Spoon all the batter into the prepared dish without overflowing it, then run the end of your thumb around the inside rim to make a shallow groove. For scaled batches, divide the full batter and coating among appropriately sized dishes before baking.
7. **Bake:** Bake in the middle of the oven, starting checks around 24–26 minutes for the original dish. Look for a puffed, crusted top and a center that moves slightly; check the egg-containing center reaches 160°F /71°C. Continue if it has not, checking each dish rather than using jiggle alone as the endpoint.
8. **Serve:** Dust with optional powdered sugar and serve immediately with the optional lightly sweetened whipped cream.

RECIPE: Chocolate Vanilla Swirl Layer Cake (chocolate-vanilla-swirl-layer-cake.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/chocolate-vanilla-swirl-layer-cake/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodiewithfamily.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.foodiewithfamily.com/chocolate-vanilla-swirl-layer-cake-with-ganache/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Shared batter ---
  - 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  - 1 1/2 cups cake flour
  - 1 tbsp baking powder
  - 1/2 tsp sea salt
  - 2 sticks unsalted butter, softened
  - 1 3/4 cups superfine sugar
  - 4 large eggs, room temperature
  - 1 tbsp vanilla extract
  - 1 1/4 cups whole milk, room temperature
  - butter, as needed for pans
  - all-purpose flour, as needed for dusting pans
  - --- White batter additions ---
  - 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
  - 2 tbsp whole milk
  - --- Chocolate batter additions ---
  - 2 tbsp dark cocoa powder, level measures
  - 2 tbsp whole milk
  - --- Ganache and optional finish ---
  - 16 oz bittersweet chocolate, finely chopped
  - 2 cups heavy cream
  - white chocolate, as desired for drizzling, melted, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The white batter gets its own flour and milk additions, while the chocolate half gets cocoa and a separate milk addition. Equal alternating pours in the center create the swirls. Cool the cakes fully before cutting four thin layers and spreading the dark ganache.

## Directions

1. **Prepare pans:** Use butter and all-purpose flour to grease and lightly flour two 8- or 9-inch round pans for the original batch. Heat the oven to 325°F.
2. **Mix dry batter ingredients:** Whisk all-purpose flour, cake flour, baking powder, and sea salt together. Keep the separate white-batter flour aside.
3. **Cream and add eggs:** Using unsalted butter, superfine sugar, large eggs, and vanilla extract, cream the softened butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, scraping the bowl. Beat in the eggs one at a time until incorporated, then the vanilla.
4. **Combine and divide:** Alternate the shared dry mixture and whole milk in several additions, beginning and ending with the dry mixture, just until smooth. Divide the batter equally between two bowls.
5. **Finish white batter:** Whisk all-purpose flour and whole milk into one half of the batter until smooth.
6. **Finish chocolate batter:** Whisk dark cocoa powder and whole milk into the other half until smooth.
7. **Build swirls and bake:** Alternate small equal scoops of white and chocolate batter directly into the center of each pan until both batches of batter have been used. About 1/3 cup per pour is an original-batch patterning guide, not a dose multiplied by the ingredient scaler. Bake at 325°F, starting checks around 35 minutes for the original pans; rotate partway through if the oven browns unevenly. Centers should be set and a tester should have no wet batter. Cool in pans on racks 5 minutes, then turn out and cool completely.
8. **Make ganache:** For bittersweet chocolate and heavy cream, heat the cream in a heavy saucepan just until about to boil. Pour over all the chopped bittersweet chocolate in a heatproof bowl and wait 5 minutes. Stir gently in one direction until smooth and glossy. Cool until spreadable; refrigerate if needed and while waiting for the cakes, stirring occasionally. Do not hold the cream ganache on the counter throughout a long cooling schedule.
9. **Layer, frost and chill:** Level the fully cool cakes, then cut each into two even layers for four layers altogether. Spread some ganache between each layer and all the remaining ganache over the top and sides. Drizzle white chocolate (if using) over the finished cake if desired. Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour before slicing.

RECIPE: Cilantro-Lime Rice (cilantro-lime-rice.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/cilantro-lime-rice/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 180 g jasmine rice (about 1 cup), rinsed and well drained
  - 1 1/4 cups (300 ml) water, plus water for rinsing
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt
  - 1 tbsp olive oil
  - 15 g fresh cilantro leaves and tender stems, finely chopped
  - 1 tsp finely grated lime zest
  - 1 tbsp fresh lime juice, plus up to 1 tbsp more to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Mexican-inspired bowl rice uses jasmine for its fragrance and tender texture. It is a different preparation from toasted tomato rice or rice cooked with a blended green sauce. The fresh finish belongs after the covered rest here: taste the rice with its main dish before deciding how much lime it needs.

## Directions

1. **Rinse and drain:** Rinse the rice in several changes of cool water until noticeably less cloudy, then drain well in a fine-mesh strainer. A little cloudiness is fine; do not soak it while preparing the other ingredients.
2. **Heat and cover:** Put drained rice, the measured water and salt in a heavy 2-quart saucepan. Stir once, bring to a gentle boil, then cover snugly and reduce to low. Cook at a gentle simmer for about fifteen minutes without repeatedly lifting the lid.
3. **Check the grains:** Briefly lift the lid and part the rice near the edge. There should be no pooled water, and a tasted grain should be tender through the center. If hard and dry, add a little hot water as described in troubleshooting. If firm with water still present, cover and cook a few minutes longer.
4. **Rest covered:** Once the rice is tender and the free water is absorbed, move the pan off the hot burner. Leave covered for ten minutes. Prepare cilantro, zest and juice during the cooking or resting time.
5. **Fluff and season:** Uncover, fluff gently, and fold in oil, cilantro, zest and the first tablespoon of lime juice. Taste with the food it will accompany. Add the optional juice a teaspoon at a time only if it needs more acidity. Divide into four side portions.

## With a rice cooker

Use the appliance's instructions for this quantity of white jasmine rice and its measuring cup. Do not assume its marked water line is calibrated for every rice variety. Keep the cilantro, oil and lime for the finish after the machine's rest; the stovetop time above does not describe every cooker.

RECIPE: Sweet Potatoes with Cinnamon (cinnamon-sweet-potatoes.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/cinnamon-sweet-potatoes/
SOURCE: Adapted from Craig Plummer
INGREDIENTS:
  - 900 g peeled and trimmed orange-fleshed sweet potatoes, cut into even 1/3-inch rounds
  - 2 tbsp (28 g) unsalted butter, melted
  - 2 tbsp (42 g) honey
  - 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
  - 1 tbsp (15 ml) fresh lime juice
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt
  - 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Honey, cinnamon and butter give these orange sweet-potato rounds a sweet American-style side-dish character, with lime for a tart finish. Add the honey after the first roast so the glaze has less time to darken before the centers soften. Expect tender rounds with browned patches, rather than a dry, brittle fry.

## Directions

1. **Heat and prepare pans:** Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C, with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Line two roughly 18-by-13-inch rimmed sheets with oven-safe parchment. Melt the butter and let it remain warm and fluid.
2. **Slice and season:** Peel and trim sweet potatoes to the listed weight. Slice crosswise into even one-third-inch rounds; halve unusually broad rounds if needed to handle them comfortably. Pat away surface water. Toss with all the melted butter, salt and pepper, then divide between the sheets in one layer with small gaps and no overlap.
3. **Begin roasting:** Roast for 15 minutes. Near the end of this first roast, warm the honey briefly in a microwave-safe bowl until fluid and stir in the cinnamon. Check the potatoes: bottoms should have some golden patches and centers should be beginning to soften. If still very firm and pale, give them another five minutes before glazing.
4. **Turn, glaze and finish:** Turn the rounds carefully with a thin spatula. Brush the upward-facing surfaces with all the honey-cinnamon mixture in a thin layer. Swap the sheets between shelves and rotate them front to back. Roast another 10–15 minutes, checking early, until several tested centers yield easily to a knife and the glaze bubbles lightly with brown edges. Remove ready pieces if some finish before thicker ones; do not wait for blackened sugar.
5. **Add lime and serve:** Drizzle the measured tablespoon of lime juice evenly over both pans. Transfer gently to a warm serving dish and serve promptly. Divide into four generous side portions, or six smaller holiday portions if the meal includes another starch. Avoid covering tightly while serving, which traps steam and softens the edges.

RECIPE: Beef Stew (classic-beef-stew.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/classic-beef-stew/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 lbs (900 g) boneless beef chuck, cut into 1.5-inch cubes
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, plus more to taste
  - 1/2 tsp black pepper
  - 1/4 cup (30 g) all-purpose flour
  - 3 tbsp neutral oil, divided
  - 2 oz (55 g) pancetta or bacon, diced
  - 1 large yellow onion, diced
  - 3 carrots, cut into 1-inch chunks
  - 2 celery stalks, diced
  - 3 garlic cloves, minced
  - 2 tbsp tomato paste
  - 2 cups (480 ml) dry red wine
  - 3 cups (720 ml) low-sodium beef stock, plus more as needed
  - 2 sprigs fresh thyme
  - 1 lb (450 g) Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1-inch chunks
  - 1 cup frozen peas
  - 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar, added to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A beef stew uses two kinds of heat for two different jobs: a hot, relatively dry pan for browning, then gentle moist heat to soften the chuck's connective tissue. The meat can be safely cooked yet still tough, so the braise ends when a fork enters easily. Add the carrots and potatoes later to keep them from dissolving while the beef becomes tender.

## Directions

1. **Dry and coat:** Pat the beef dry, season with salt and pepper, and toss with flour. Shake off loose excess.
2. **Brown in batches:** Heat 2 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef in three uncrowded batches, about 6–8 minutes each, turning to develop deep brown patches. Add the remaining oil as needed. Transfer each batch to a plate; reduce heat if the fond starts to blacken.
3. **Cook the base:** Reduce heat to medium. Add pancetta and cook 3–4 minutes until fat begins to render. Add onion and celery and cook 6–8 minutes until softened. Stir in tomato paste for 1 minute, then garlic for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. **Deglaze:** Add wine and scrape up brown fond with a wooden spoon. Simmer 5 minutes. This reduces wine but does not guarantee removal of all alcohol.
5. **Braise gently:** Return beef and accumulated juices. Add thyme and enough stock to nearly cover the meat. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and reduce heat to low. Cook about 2 hours, checking occasionally for slow bubbles and sufficient liquid.
6. **Add vegetables when ready:** Test several beef pieces. When they are beginning to soften but not yet fully tender, add carrots and potatoes. Simmer, covered, another 35–50 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the beef yields easily to a fork. If the beef is still quite firm at 2 hours, give it more time before adding vegetables.
7. **Finish the sauce:** Remove thyme stems. If the sauce is too thin, lift out meat and vegetables and reduce the sauce uncovered before returning them. Add peas and simmer 2–3 minutes until hot. Add balsamic vinegar gradually, taste, and adjust salt and pepper.

RECIPE: Classic Carrot Cake (classic-carrot-cake.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/classic-carrot-cake/
SOURCE: Adapted from ajc.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.ajc.com/things-to-do/food-and-recipes/recipe-apple-syrup-is-key-to-moist-carrot-cake/NFOH5GZCPFHDXPD3WU2ZD6TDNU/?fbclid=IwAR0mPjiVsWlmKp6Q16-0zVkVk6g_oK8Iys0zLMuRUF7HMtIBsTJhs6pq_sc
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Pans ---
  - 1 tbsp unsalted butter, for greasing pans
  - 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, for dusting pans
  - --- Cake batter ---
  - 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  - 1 cup granulated sugar
  - 1 1/2 tsp baking soda
  - 1 tsp baking powder
  - 1 tsp ground cinnamon
  - 1/2 tsp ground allspice
  - 1/2 tsp ground cloves
  - 1/2 tsp freshly grated nutmeg
  - 1/2 tsp salt
  - 2/3 cup vegetable oil
  - 3 large eggs
  - 1 1/2 lb carrot, peeled and finely grated
  - --- Apple syrup ---
  - 1 Granny Smith apple, washed, peeled and grated
  - 1/2 cup granulated sugar
  - 1/2 cup water
  - --- Cream cheese frosting ---
  - 1 lb brick-style cream cheese, cold, not softened
  - 1 stick unsalted butter, softened
  - 8 cups powdered sugar
  - 2 tsp vanilla extract
  - 1/2 tsp salt
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Mercer Street Meals’ carrot cake uses a light brush of strained apple syrup on completely cooled layers. Keep the remaining syrup separate rather than soaking the cakes with the full batch. The cream cheese frosting is mixed from cold brick-style cream cheese and softened butter; chill it while the cakes cool.

## Directions

1. **Prepare pans:** Heat the oven to 350°F. For the original batch, use unsalted butter and all-purpose flour to grease two 8-inch round cake pans with all the pan butter, then divide the dusting flour between them, coating and shaking out excess. Dusting flour is separate from batter flour.
2. **Mix batter:** Combine all-purpose flour, granulated sugar, baking soda, baking powder, ground cinnamon, ground allspice, ground cloves, freshly grated nutmeg, salt, vegetable oil, large eggs, and carrot until the batter is smooth and all the carrot is distributed. Divide between the prepared pans, keeping similar depth and room to rise.
3. **Bake and cool:** Bake at 350°F, starting checks around 25–30 minutes for the original pans. Layers should begin pulling slightly from the sides, centers should be set and a tester should have no wet batter. Cool in the pans, then remove carefully once cool. Wait until fully cool before leveling and frosting.
4. **Make and strain syrup:** Bring Granny Smith apple, granulated sugar, and water to a rolling boil in a small saucepan, then remove from heat. Strain through a sieve and discard the apple solids. Keep the strained syrup for a light brush and reserve the excess separately; the cake does not absorb the whole syrup batch.
5. **Mix frosting:** Beat brick-style cream cheese, unsalted butter, powdered sugar, vanilla extract, and salt with a stand mixer or electric beaters until smooth, beginning slowly so powdered sugar does not scatter. Keep refrigerated while waiting for the cakes.
6. **Glaze and assemble:** Level the completely cool cakes with a serrated knife. Brush each cut surface lightly with apple syrup: about 1 tbsp per layer is the original-batch guide, not all the syrup. Reserve unused syrup separately in the refrigerator. Spread about one-third of the frosting on the first layer, stack the second and use all the rest over the top and sides. Refrigerate the finished cake.
