RECIPE: Crispy Gold Potatoes with Smoked Salt and Paprika (crispy-gold-potatoes-with-lemon-garlic-butter.md)
CUISINES: None
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/crispy-gold-potatoes-with-lemon-garlic-butter/
SOURCE: Mise variation on Garlic Roasted Potatoes, adapted from Ina Garten
SOURCE_URL: https://barefootcontessa.com/recipes/garlic-roasted-potatoes
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 lb petite gold potatoes, scrubbed and thoroughly dried
  - 1/4 cup olive oil
  - 2 tsp finely minced garlic
  - 1 1/4 tsp fine smoked sea salt, plus more to taste
  - 1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
  - 1 1/2 tsp sweet paprika (not smoked)
  - 3 tbsp unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Smoked sea salt provides the smoke while sweet paprika adds warmth. Gold potatoes roast with creamy centers and browned cut faces; a final toss with butter rounds out the seasoning. Dry them well, leave room around each piece and watch the garlic. Use fine smoked salt for the measured amount; coarse or flaky salt needs adjustment because its volume varies.

## Directions

1. **Heat and cut:** Heat the oven to **400°F convection**, with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Set out two bare metal rimmed half-sheet pans. Halve the dry potatoes lengthwise; quarter larger ones so pieces are roughly **1–1 1/2 inches** across.
2. **Season and arrange:** Toss potatoes with the olive oil, garlic, smoked sea salt, black pepper and sweet paprika. Divide between pans with space around each piece, setting a cut face flat against the metal. Scrape the coating from the bowl onto the potatoes; avoid piles of loose garlic on the pans.
3. **Roast:** Check after **20 minutes**, rotating pans front to back and swapping racks. Turn potatoes once their undersides are golden and release with a thin spatula; leave pale or stuck pieces a little longer. Start checking tenderness at **30 minutes**. They are ready when browned and a thin knife slides easily into the largest centers, usually **35–45 minutes total**. If garlic darkens quickly, lower to **375°F convection** and continue until tender.
4. **Butter and serve:** Add butter in small pieces to the hot potatoes and toss gently on the pans until melted. **No extra roasting is needed.** Taste before adding more salt. Serve promptly; avoid covering tightly or piling into a deep bowl, which traps steam.

RECIPE: Crispy Oven Zucchini Fries (crispy-oven-zucchini-fries.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/crispy-oven-zucchini-fries/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 lbs Fresh Zucchini (about 4 medium)
  - 1/2 cup All-Purpose Flour
  - 1/4 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1/4 tsp Black Pepper
  - 2 Large Eggs, beaten
  - 1.5 cups Panko Breadcrumbs
  - 1/2 cup Freshly Grated Parmigiano-Reggiano
  - 1 tsp Garlic Powder
  - 1/2 tsp Dried Italian Seasoning
  - 2 tbsp Olive Oil for brushing
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Zucchini fries are the gateway vegetable for kids who resist anything green - they look like legitimate fries but deliver actual nutrition. The trick is removing excess moisture (zucchini is 95% water) by salting the cut pieces and letting them sit. The panko coating must be toasted golden in the oven while brushed with oil, not baked from wet flour. This creates the crispy exterior that keeps kids coming back.

## Directions

1. **Remove Moisture:** Cut zucchini lengthwise into quarters, then cut each quarter into fry-sized sticks (about 1/2-inch thick). Place on a paper towel-lined plate. Sprinkle generously with 1/4 tsp salt. Let sit for 5 minutes while the zucchini weeps water. Pat completely dry.
2. **Set Up Stations:** Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Set up three shallow bowls: one with flour mixed with salt and pepper; one with beaten egg; one with panko mixed with Parmigiano, garlic powder, and Italian seasoning.
3. **Coat:** Working with a few zucchini sticks at a time, coat in the flour mixture (shake off excess), dip in egg, then roll in the panko mixture, pressing gently so the coating sticks.
4. **Arrange:** Place breaded zucchini on the prepared baking sheet in a single layer, not touching.
5. **Brush:** Lightly brush or spray each stick with olive oil on all sides. This is crucial for crisping.
6. **Bake:** Bake for 18-22 minutes until golden brown and crispy, flipping halfway through.
7. **Serve:** Serve hot with marinara sauce, ranch dressing, or a squeeze of fresh lemon for dipping.

RECIPE: Crispy Pancetta, Sweet Pea & Lemon Ricotta Pasta (crispy-pancetta-sweet-pea-lemon-ricotta-pasta.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/crispy-pancetta-sweet-pea-lemon-ricotta-pasta/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 12 oz dry orecchiette or similar short pasta
  - 4 oz diced pancetta
  - 1 medium shallot, finely minced
  - 2 cloves garlic, finely minced
  - 1 cup sweet peas, fresh or frozen
  - 1/4 cup dry white wine or unsalted chicken stock
  - 1/2 cup whole-milk ricotta
  - 1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan
  - 1 lemon, finely grated zest
  - 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, taken from the zested fruit if possible
  - Water, a small splash if needed for sticking shallot
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  - 1 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Render pancetta before building the sauce, and keep the crisp pieces aside for serving. Cook the peas fully, then let the pan stop sizzling before adding ricotta and Parmesan. Warm cooking water loosens the sauce; it need not become perfectly smooth to coat the orecchiette well.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and heat water:** Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Mince shallot and garlic, zest the lemon and measure its listed juice amount, and grate Parmesan. Season pasta water moderately, remembering the pancetta and cheese.
2. **Render pancetta:** Put pancetta in a cold skillet and set over medium heat. Cook, stirring, about **8–12 minutes**, or as its package directs, until cooked through and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon to a clean plate. Pour off excess fat into a heatproof container, retaining about **1 1/2–2 tablespoons of fat for each 4 ounces of pancetta cooked**, or what it releases if less. This is a ratio: retain proportionally less for a smaller batch and more for a larger one.
3. **Build the base:** Over medium-low, soften shallot in the retained fat for about **3–5 minutes**. If there is very little fat and it sticks, add a small splash of water. Add garlic for **30–45 seconds**, then wine or stock. Simmer about **2 minutes**, scraping browned bits, until reduced by roughly half. Turn off heat while pasta finishes.
4. **Cook pasta and peas:** Meanwhile boil pasta according to package directions until tender with a little bite; do not drain early for an unheated finish. Cook frozen peas according to their package, or simmer fresh peas separately until tender, then drain. Reserve **the listed pasta-water amount** before draining pasta. Combine cooked hot pasta and peas with the aromatic base.
5. **Finish away from heat:** Move the skillet completely off the burner and wait until it no longer sizzles; transfer to a large bowl if the pan stays very hot. Stir in ricotta, Parmesan, lemon zest, **half the measured lemon juice** and **half the reserved pasta water**. Toss gently until creamy, adding more water in small amounts only if needed.
6. **Taste and plate:** Add black pepper, then taste before adding salt and the remaining lemon juice. Divide into the intended portions and top with the crisp pancetta. Serve immediately.

RECIPE: Crispy Parmesan Roasted Broccoli (crispy-parmesan-roasted-broccoli.md)
CUISINES: Italian, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/crispy-parmesan-roasted-broccoli/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 lbs (680 g) fresh broccoli, cut into 1.5-inch florets with flat stem sides
  - 3 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - 1/2 cup (30 g) finely grated Parmesan
  - 3 cloves garlic, finely minced
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, plus more to taste
  - 1/4 tsp black pepper
  - 1–2 tsp fresh lemon juice, to finish
  - Pinch of red pepper flakes, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The important temperature is at the broccoli surface, not just on the oven dial. Dry florets and space on the tray let moisture escape so browning can develop. Garlic and cheese go in near the end: both need far less time than the broccoli stems.

## Directions

1. **Heat and dry:** Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C with a rack in the upper middle. Wash broccoli, drain, and towel-dry thoroughly. Cut thick stems to a similar size so they finish with the florets.
2. **Season and arrange:** Toss broccoli with 2 tbsp oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a rimmed half-sheet pan, placing flat cut sides down with space between pieces. Use a second pan if necessary.
3. **Roast:** Roast undisturbed for 15 minutes. Check the undersides: they should have golden patches. Turn the pieces and roast another 3–5 minutes if the stems still feel very firm.
4. **Add the delicate ingredients:** Mix garlic with the remaining 1 tbsp oil. Toss it through the broccoli, then sprinkle with Parmesan. Roast 3–5 minutes more, until the cheese is golden and a knife pierces the stems easily. Check early; do not wait for black garlic.
5. **Finish:** Taste a floret. Add lemon juice a little at a time and adjust salt only if needed. Add optional pepper flakes and serve immediately, uncovered, to preserve the edges.

RECIPE: Crispy Shallots (crispy-shallots.md)
CUISINES: Vietnamese, Thai, Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/crispy-shallots/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 large Shallots, peeled and sliced into thin, uniform rings
  - 1 cup Neutral Cooking Oil (Canola or Vegetable)
  - 1 pinch Kosher Salt
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Crispy shallots (hành phi in Vietnamese, hom jiao in Thai) are a cornerstone condiment across Southeast Asia, adding texture, sweetness, and aroma to soups, salads, and stir-fries. The secret to perfect shallots is the **cold-oil start**. Starting shallots in cold oil allows their moisture to gently evaporate as the oil heats up, resulting in a shatteringly crisp texture. Hot-oil starts burn the outer layers while leaving the interiors soggy. Save the strained shallot oil; it is an incredibly flavorful base for searing proteins or frying eggs.

## Directions

1. **Slicing:** Peel the shallots. Slice them into thin, uniform rings (about 1/16-inch thick) using a mandoline or a very sharp chef's knife. Uniformity is crucial for even browning.
2. **Cold Start:** Place the sliced shallots in a cold, small saucepan. Pour in the neutral oil until the shallots are just submerged.
3. **Slow Fry:** Turn the heat to medium. Once the oil begins to gently bubble around the shallots, reduce the heat to medium-low. Cook for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally to ensure they do not clump or burn.
4. **The Pull:** Watch the shallots closely towards the end. The moment they turn a pale, light golden brown, immediately pour the contents of the pan through a fine-mesh strainer set over a heat-proof bowl. Do not wait for them to look dark brown in the oil, as carryover heat will continue to cook and darken them as they cool.
5. **Drain and Salt:** Spread the hot shallots in a single layer on a paper towel-lined plate. Immediately sprinkle with a pinch of kosher salt while they are still wet with oil. This helps them dry crisp and seasons them.
6. **Store:** Allow them to cool completely. Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. Use the leftover shallot-infused oil in the fridge for cooking.

RECIPE: Sheet Pan Gnocchi & Veggies (crispy-sheet-pan-gnocchi-and-veggies.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/crispy-sheet-pan-gnocchi-and-veggies/
SOURCE: Adapted from Thekitchn.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.thekitchn.com/recipe-crispy-sheet-pan-gnocchi-and-veggies-247360
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Fresh or Shelf-stable Potato Gnocchi
  - 12 oz Mini Bell Peppers, cut into 1-inch chunks
  - 1 pint Cherry Tomatoes
  - 1 small Red Onion, cut into chunks
  - 4 cloves Garlic, smashed
  - 2 tbsp Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 1 tsp Fresh Rosemary, chopped
  - 1/4 cup Fresh Basil, chopped
  - 1/2 cup Freshly Grated Parmesan
  - Salt and Black Pepper
  - 1/4 tsp kosher salt, optional alternative to salt to taste; choose one salt route
  - 1/2 lb shrimp or fully cooked chicken sausage, optional; choose one
  - Water, for separately cooking raw shrimp, if using

## Chef's Note

Roast the gnocchi and vegetables with room between the pieces. The tomatoes provide some pan juices while the gnocchi edges color; check the centers for tenderness as well. Add all the basil and measured Parmesan at the end. Optional shrimp or fully cooked sausage has its own cooking or heating step before joining the tray.

## Directions

1. **Heat and prepare:** Heat the oven to 450°F. Use rimmed metal sheets with room for one uncrowded layer. Leave them bare or line with suitable foil; use parchment only if its actual label permits this temperature. Wash the peppers, tomatoes, onion and herbs before cutting, and dry the produce.

2. **Toss:** In a roomy bowl combine the full gnocchi, peppers, tomatoes, onion and smashed garlic. Add all the olive oil and rosemary, plus the salt from your chosen seasoning route and black pepper to taste. Toss to distribute the oil. 4. **Roast:** Roast, stirring halfway through and exchanging tray positions if using more than one shelf. Actual gnocchi product, oven and tray load may need longer.

Drain and use clean utensils to add it to the finished vegetables. If choosing chicken sausage instead, use fully cooked product and heat it separately according to its package before adding; refrigerated cooked leftovers must reach 165°F throughout. Raw chicken sausage needs a complete separate method to 165°F and is not a direct substitute. Cooked shrimp may instead be reheated to 165°F before adding. Do not add both proteins.

6. **Finish and serve:** Toss the finished gnocchi and vegetables with all the chopped basil and all the measured Parmesan, then fold in the chosen cooked or heated protein if used. Serve promptly.

RECIPE: Smashed Potatoes (crispy-smashed-potatoes.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/crispy-smashed-potatoes/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 lbs Baby Potatoes (Red or Yukon Gold)
  - 1/4 cup Olive Oil
  - 1 tsp Garlic Powder
  - 1 tsp Dried Rosemary or Thyme
  - Kosher Salt and Black Pepper
  - Flaky Sea Salt for finishing
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Boil the skin-on baby potatoes until soft, then flatten them gently to expose uneven edges. Let surface steam escape before coating with all the measured oil. Space the potatoes so those edges can brown, and use tenderness and color rather than expecting every tray to finish on the same clock.

## Directions

1. **Boil:** Scrub whole baby potatoes and keep the skins on. Place in cold water and salt it with the listed allowance. Bring to a boil and cook about 15–20 minutes after boiling, until the centers yield easily to a fork. Drain. Start preheating to 425 °F while they boil.

2. **Smash:** Line a baking sheet with oven-suitable parchment. Arrange with space between potatoes; use additional sheets if needed. Gently press each with a heavy glass bottom or masher to about 1/2 inch thick, keeping the skin-on pieces together.

3. **Dry:** Let the smashed potatoes stand about 5 minutes so surface steam can escape.

4. **Season:** Distribute all the measured olive oil across the total batch, including any extra sheets. Add all the garlic powder and chosen dried rosemary or thyme; salt and pepper to taste. Do not repeat the full measured oil/seasoning amount on each tray.

5. **Roast:** Roast at 425 °F for about 25–30 minutes as a first window, flipping carefully halfway through. Continue until edges are deep golden and crisp and centers remain tender. Extra trays may need rotation and longer; judge the edges by color and crispness as well as the tenderness of the centers.

6. **Finish:** Add the flaky sea salt finish to taste and serve hot. Refrigerate leftovers promptly; reheat to 165 °F and use the oven to help restore edges rather than expecting microwave crispness.

## Timing

Allow about 75 minutes including preparation and bringing water to a boil. The 15–20-minute tenderizing window starts after boiling; 5-minute steam dry and 25–30-minute roast follow. Preheat during boiling. More trays and larger potatoes can extend time.

RECIPE: Hot Chocolate (crock-pot-hot-chocolate.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/crock-pot-hot-chocolate/
SOURCE: Adapted from thepioneerwoman.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.thepioneerwoman.com/food-cooking/recipes/a42027300/crock-pot-hot-chocolate-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6 cups Whole Milk
  - 2 cups Heavy Cream
  - 1/2 cup Granulated Sugar
  - 1/3 cup High-Quality Unsweetened Cocoa Powder
  - 8 oz Bittersweet Chocolate (60% cacao), finely chopped
  - 2 teaspoons Vanilla Extract
  - 1 teaspoon Instant Espresso Powder (Brings out the chocolate depth)
  - 1/4 teaspoon Fine Sea Salt
  - Marshmallows and Shaved Chocolate for garnish
  - 8 oz Irish Cream Liqueur (Optional, for adults)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

While serious chocolatiers prefer the stovetop, the slow cooker is an excellent tool for **gentle tempering**. The low, consistent heat prevents the chocolate from seizing and allows the espresso and vanilla to infuse deeply into the dairy. By using real bittersweet chocolate bars instead of just powder, we transform this from "cocoa" into a rich "drinking chocolate" with a luxurious mouthfeel. A pinch of salt is non-negotiable - it cuts the sweetness and makes the cacao sing.

## Directions

1.  **Whisk:** In a 6-quart slow cooker, whisk together the sugar, cocoa powder, espresso powder, and salt.
2.  **Incorporate:** Gradually pour in the milk and heavy cream, whisking constantly until the powder is mostly dissolved.
3.  **Melt:** Stir in the chopped bittersweet chocolate and vanilla extract.
4.  **Slow Cook:** Cover and cook on **LOW** for 2 hours. Whisk vigorously every 30-45 minutes to ensure the chocolate emulsifies with the dairy.
5.  **Finish:** Just before serving, stir in the liqueur (if using).
6.  **Serve:** Ladle into mugs. Top with fresh marshmallows and shaved chocolate.

RECIPE: Slow-Cooker Mac and Cheese (crockpot-mac-and-cheese.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/crockpot-mac-and-cheese/
SOURCE: Adapted from amandascookin.com
SOURCE_URL: https://amandascookin.com/crockpot-macaroni-and-cheese/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 pound elbow pasta (uncooked, regular - not quick-cook)
  - 2½ cups whole milk
  - 12 ounces evaporated milk (from a 12-ounce can)
  - 12 ounces extra-sharp cheddar, freshly shredded (about 3 cups)
  - 4 ounces American cheese, shredded (about 1 cup - from the deli, not slices)
  - 1 teaspoon kosher salt
  - ½ teaspoon black pepper
  - ½ teaspoon dry mustard
  - ¼ teaspoon garlic powder
  - Pinch of cayenne pepper
  - 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, cubed
  - Non-stick cooking spray, for the cooker
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Regular uncooked elbow pasta cooks in the full milk-and-cheese mixture on LOW. Check and stir after the first hour rather than leaving it unattended for a fixed two hours. Freshly shredded cheese and stopping at tender pasta help the texture, but neither ingredient choice guarantees a smooth sauce in every cooker.

## Directions

1. **Set up:** For the original batch, use the source’s 6-quart slow cooker only if its actual instructions permit the load. Aim for a suitable fill between half and two-thirds full, with a lid that closes; scaling may require smaller, larger or separate cookers, not the same vessel at every amount. Keep milk and cheese refrigerated until preparation. Spray the insert with the listed cooking-spray allowance. Rinse regular uncooked elbow pasta in cold water and drain well.

2. **Build:** Add all the drained uncooked pasta, whole milk, evaporated milk, both cheeses, salt, pepper, dry mustard, garlic powder and cayenne. Stir thoroughly so the pasta is submerged as much as possible. Dot with all the cubed butter. Start cooking immediately; do not use a delayed-start timer.

3. **Cook on LOW:** Cover and cook on LOW for 1 hour, then quickly uncover and stir, reaching the bottom and edges. Check a cooled pasta sample: it should be tender without a hard center. Return the lid promptly if it needs longer. Keep LOW for this method; HIGH is not an equivalent shortcut.

4. **Check and finish:** Continue on LOW as needed, checking and stirring about every 30 minutes as in the saved method, or sooner as it approaches tenderness. Total cooking may take about 1–3 hours depending on the actual cooker and pasta. Stop when the pasta is tender and sauce creamy; check several central locations reach 165°F before serving. That casserole-temperature check and pasta tenderness are separate endpoints, not a claim that a timer alone makes it safe.

5. **Rest and serve:** Let stand 5–10 minutes before serving; it thickens as it cools. If holding for service, use a suitable hot setting and verify at least 140°F rather than assuming WARM is sufficient. Refrigerate leftovers promptly rather than leaving the switched-off cooker to cool.

RECIPE: Slow-Cooker Three-Bean Vegetable Chili (crockpot-vegetarian-chili.md)
CUISINES: Tex-Mex
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/crockpot-vegetarian-chili/
SOURCE: Adapted from showmetheyummy.com
SOURCE_URL: https://showmetheyummy.com/crockpot-vegetarian-chili-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 180 g red onion, cut into 1/4-inch dice
  - 100 g celery, cut into 1/4-inch pieces
  - 100 g carrot, cut into 1/4-inch pieces
  - 300 g mixed red and green bell peppers, seeded and diced
  - 300 g peeled sweet potato, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
  - 1 can (15 oz / 425 g) kidney beans, rinsed and drained, about 255 g drained total
  - 1 can (15 oz / 425 g) chickpeas, rinsed and drained, about 255 g drained total
  - 1 can (15 oz / 425 g) black beans, rinsed and drained, about 255 g drained total
  - 2 cans (4 oz / 113 g each) mild diced green chiles, with juices
  - 1 can (15 oz / 425 g) diced tomatoes, with juices
  - 1 can (8 oz / 227 g) plain tomato sauce
  - 1 tbsp olive oil
  - 2 tbsp mild chili powder blend, not pure hot chile powder
  - 2 tsp ground cumin
  - 2 tsp garlic powder
  - 1 tsp dried oregano
  - 1 cup (240 ml) low-sodium vegetable broth, plus a little only if needed to loosen
  - 1 tsp fine salt, added gradually only if needed
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
  - 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar, added gradually to taste
  - --- Optional toppings, for the whole batch ---
  - 1/2 cup (120 g) plain yogurt or unsweetened plant-based yogurt
  - 1 medium avocado, about 150 g edible flesh, diced just before serving
  - 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Three cooked beans provide different textures while small sweet-potato pieces soften in the tomato base. If more body is needed, mash a small portion near the end rather than assuming all the potato should dissolve. The vegetables supply sweetness, so finish with cider vinegar only after tasting the cooked pot. This is a six-serving Tex-Mex-inspired vegetable chili.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the cooker:** Put diced onion, celery, carrot, peppers and sweet potato in a 6-quart slow cooker. Add all drained beans, green chiles and juices, tomatoes and juices, and tomato sauce.
2. **Bloom measured spices:** Warm olive oil in a small skillet over medium-low heat. Add chili blend, cumin, garlic powder and oregano and stir about 20–30 seconds until fragrant, without darkening. Add a few tablespoons from the measured broth to loosen the paste, then scrape it into the cooker.
3. **Add liquid:** Add the rest of the initial 240 ml broth and the pepper. Stir thoroughly, cover and start cooking immediately. Keep salt, vinegar and fresh toppings for later.
4. **Cook and test vegetables:** Cook on HIGH about 4–5 hours or LOW about 7–8 hours, until carrot and sweet potato are fork-tender. Keep the lid closed between checks. Extend if needed; add a little extra broth only if the mixture becomes too dry before the vegetables soften.
5. **Set body and season:** If thin, mash roughly half a cup of cooked beans and sweet potato against the side and stir in. Taste and add measured salt gradually only if needed. Turn off heat and start with half the vinegar, then add more to taste.
6. **Serve:** Divide into six bowls. Offer the listed yogurt, avocado and cilantro as optional supplies for the whole batch; use plain plant-based yogurt or omit it for a vegan version. Bread or slaw is prepared separately.

RECIPE: Crustless Sausage & Spinach Quiche (crustless-sausage-and-spinach-quiche.md)
CUISINES: French
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/crustless-sausage-and-spinach-quiche/
SOURCE: Adapted from skinnytaste.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.skinnytaste.com/crustless-sausage-and-spinach-quiche/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 8.5 oz raw Italian chicken sausage, casings removed (3 links in the original batch)
  - 12 oz Fresh Baby Spinach
  - 5 large Eggs
  - 2/3 cup 2% Milk
  - 1/4 cup Half & Half
  - 1 cup Sharp Cheddar (or Havarti), freshly grated
  - 1/4 cup Freshly Grated Parmesan
  - 3/4 tsp kosher salt
  - 1/8 tsp Black Pepper
  - Pinch of Freshly Grated Nutmeg
  - Cooking spray
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Wilt spinach with the cooked sausage, then drain the released water before adding the custard. Nutmeg seasons the milk and eggs without turning the filling sweet. Use the listed total sausage weight; links vary in size between packages.

## Directions

1. **Prep:** Preheat the oven to 350 °F and generously spray the 9-inch pie dish. Use the listed total sausage weight. Link sizes vary; the three-link note describes the original 8.5 oz batch. Have a sieve ready for the cooked spinach.

2. **Cook the sausage:** Cook the raw chicken sausage in a large skillet over medium heat, breaking it into small crumbles, until cooked through and reaching 165 °F / 74 °C. About 5 minutes is a first estimate, not a guarantee; browning alone does not establish the endpoint.

3. **Wilt and drain:** Add the spinach in manageable handfuls, reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until fully wilted, about 7 minutes. Drain the sausage-spinach mixture in a sieve and press gently to release excess water; do not treat this as a requirement to strip away every bit of fat.

4. **The Custard:** Whisk the eggs, milk, half-and-half, measured kosher salt, pepper and nutmeg until smoothly blended without separate egg-white streaks. Do not whip to a thick foam.

5. **Assemble:** Spread the drained sausage and spinach in the prepared dish and distribute all the cheddar or Havarti and Parmesan over it.

6. **Pour:** Pour the custard over the filling, leaving space below the rim. Nine-inch dishes vary in depth; do not force an enlarged batch into this dish. For multiples, use separate original-size dishes; reduced batches need an appropriately smaller dish and earlier center checks.

7. **Bake:** Bake about 35–40 minutes as a first range, until the center is set with no liquid egg and measures 165 °F / 74 °C, checking without touching the dish. Edges may be lightly golden and puffed. Continue if the center has not reached the endpoint rather than relying on color.

8. **Rest:** Rest 5 minutes before slicing. The full original batch makes six wedges; apportion a different batch size accordingly. Refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers, use within 3–4 days and reheat centers to 165 °F / 74 °C.

RECIPE: Crustless Spinach & Gruyère Quiche (crustless-spinach-quiche.md)
CUISINES: French
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/crustless-spinach-quiche/
SOURCE: Adapted from Rebecca Cybulsky
INGREDIENTS:
  - 10 oz Fresh Baby Spinach
  - 1 large Yellow Onion, thinly sliced
  - 6 large Eggs
  - 1 cup Gruyère Cheese, freshly grated
  - 1/2 cup Plain Greek Yogurt for richness
  - 1/2 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1/4 tsp Black Pepper
  - 1 tbsp Olive Oil
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This French-style quiche sautés onions over high heat until edges char and caramelize, adding smokiness that balances earthy spinach. Greek yogurt replaces heavy cream for a firmer, protein-rich custard that doesn't turn watery. Gruyère's nutty flavor is more complex than standard Swiss cheese.

## Directions

1.  **The Blacken:** In a large skillet, heat oil over high heat. Add the sliced onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply browned and slightly charred at the edges.
2.  **The Wilt:** Add the spinach to the onions. Toss for 1 minute until just wilted. **Discard any excess liquid** from the pan.
3.  **The Custard:** In a medium bowl, whisk together the eggs, Greek yogurt, salt, and pepper until perfectly smooth.
4.  **Fold:** Stir the onion-spinach mixture and 3/4 of the Gruyère into the egg custard.
5.  **Bake:** Preheat oven to 350°F. Spray a 9-inch pie plate with oil. Pour the mixture into the plate and sprinkle the remaining cheese over the top.
6.  **Finish:** Bake for 25-30 minutes until the top is golden brown and the center is set.
7.  **Serve:** Serve warm or at room temperature with a side of greens.

RECIPE: Cu Chao Mian (Shanghai Fried Noodles) (cu-chao-mian.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/cu-chao-mian/
SOURCE: Adapted from thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/shanghai-fried-noodles/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Japanese-style Udon or thick Egg Noodles
  - 6 oz Pork Tenderloin, sliced into thin strips
  - 3/4 tsp Cornstarch
  - 1 tsp Shaoxing Wine
  - 1/2 tsp Light Soy Sauce
  - 2 1/2 tsp Dark Soy Sauce (for the iconic "Gold" color)
  - 2 1/2 tsp Light Soy Sauce
  - 1/4 tsp Sugar
  - 8 Fresh Shiitake Mushrooms, sliced
  - 1 bunch Baby Bok Choy, trimmed
  - Neutral Oil
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Cu chao mian is a Shanghai classic characterized by its dark, glossy noodles coated in generous dark soy sauce for a deep mahogany color and subtle sweetness. Velveting the pork in cornstarch and Shaoxing wine keeps it tender during high-heat cooking, while thick udon noodles provide a satisfying chew against wilted bok choy.

## Directions

1.  **Velvet:** Toss pork strips with cornstarch, wine, and soy sauce. Let stand for 10 minutes.
2.  **The Sear:** Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok until smoking. Sear the pork for 2 minutes until browned. Remove.
3.  **The Crunch:** Add 1 tbsp oil. Sauté shiitakes for 2 minutes. Separate the prepared noodles before they enter the wok. Add them to the hot pan and loosen or toss with cooking chopsticks or tongs; keep hands out of the hot oil.
4.  **Glaze:** Add both soy sauces and sugar. Stir-fry for 3 minutes over high heat until the noodles are evenly dark and glossy.
5.  **Finish:** Add the bok choy and the cooked pork. Toss for 1 minute until the greens are just wilted but the stems stay crunchy.
6.  **Serve:** Serve immediately. Add a dash of Chinese black vinegar at the table for the mandatory **Acid Balance**.

RECIPE: Cucumber Raita (cucumber-raita.md)
CUISINES: Indian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/cucumber-raita/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 480 g plain whole-milk yogurt, chilled, unsweetened and unstrained
  - 300 g Persian or English cucumber, washed, ends trimmed
  - 1 tsp cumin seeds
  - 1/4 cup chopped cilantro or mint
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt
  - 1/4 tsp sugar, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Raita can be a small condiment or a more generous yogurt side. Here, lightly squeezed grated cucumber keeps it spoonable without making it dry and dense. Toasted cumin supplies its main spice aroma. It remains distinct from tzatziki: this version has cumin and unstrained yogurt, with no added garlic, oil, or vinegar.

## Directions

1. **Toast cumin:** Put cumin seeds in a small dry skillet over medium-low heat. Shake or stir for about 1–2 minutes until fragrant and slightly darker. Transfer to a plate to cool, then crush finely with a mortar or the back of a spoon.
2. **Prepare cucumber:** Grate cucumber coarsely, peeling a tough skin and removing large seed cores first if needed. Let drain in a sieve for about 5 minutes. Gently squeeze out freely dripping liquid with clean hands or a clean towel; keep the shreds moist. No extra draining salt is needed.
3. **Mix:** Whisk chilled yogurt until smooth. Fold in cucumber, crushed cooled cumin, herbs, measured salt, and optional sugar. Taste; the result should be lightly seasoned and spoonable rather than a thick spread.
4. **Chill and serve:** Refrigerate about 10 minutes, then stir gently and serve. For a small curry-bowl garnish, offer roughly two tablespoons per person; for biryani, a larger three-to-four-tablespoon serving works well. Keep the bowl cold until needed.

RECIPE: Curried Carrot and Apple Soup (curried-carrot-and-apple-soup.md)
CUISINES: Indian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/curried-carrot-and-apple-soup/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/curried-carrot-and-apple-soup
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 lbs Carrots, cut into 1/4-inch rounds
  - 1 1/4 lbs Celery Root, peeled and chopped
  - 1 Granny Smith apple, peeled, cored and chopped
  - 4 tbsp Unsalted Butter
  - 1 medium Onion, chopped
  - 1 leek, halved lengthwise, washed between layers and sliced
  - 1 fennel bulb, cored and chopped
  - 1 tbsp Madras Curry Powder
  - 7 gingersnap cookies
  - 2 cloves Garlic, crushed
  - 1 tsp Fresh Ginger, grated
  - 2 thyme sprigs
  - Salt and black pepper, to taste
  - 2 quarts Chicken Stock
  - 1 cup Sour Cream
  - 1 tsp Apple Cider Vinegar
  - Toasted pumpkin seeds, for garnish
  - Fresh mint, chopped, for garnish
  - Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Carrots, celery root and tart apple make the base, while gingersnaps add ginger-spice flavor and body alongside the Madras curry powder. Cook both roots until very soft before blending with all the sour cream and the measured vinegar. Pumpkin seeds, mint and cilantro finish the bowls with texture and fresh aroma.

## Directions

1. **Aromatics:** Melt all the measured butter in a pot large enough for the roots, aromatics and stock with stirring room. Add onion, washed sliced leek and cored fennel with salt and pepper from the listed allowance. Cook over medium-high heat, stirring, about 9 minutes as a first check, until softened and just starting to brown; lower heat if butter or edges scorch.

2. **Build the base:** Add carrots, peeled chopped celery root, prepared apple, all the gingersnaps, curry powder, garlic, ginger and thyme sprigs. Cook while stirring for about 10 minutes, until the roots begin to soften and the cookies break down. Keep the bottom from catching rather than insisting every vegetable is already tender.

3. **Simmer:** Add all the chicken stock, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Stir occasionally and cook about 25 minutes as a first check, continuing until both carrots and celery root crush easily with a fork. Remove the thyme stems before blending.

4. **Blend:** Take the pot off the heat. Check the actual blender and vessel manual before starting. Never put hot soup in a sealed personal cup. For countertop blending, use a vessel approved for the mixture’s temperature and follow its fill, lid, venting and speed limits; cool first as the manual requires. Cooling and subsequent reheating add time. Purée in permitted loads with all the measured sour cream and vinegar divided among those loads. The entire listed dairy/vinegar amount is for the total batch, not each blender fill. Recombine all the purée; check for firm root pieces and blend further within the machine’s limits if needed.

5. **Finish:** Return to the pot and warm gently while stirring. Taste and adjust with the listed salt and pepper. Avoid prolonged hard boiling after the sour cream is included.

6. **Serve:** Ladle into bowls and add the toasted pumpkin seeds, chopped fresh mint and chopped fresh cilantro to taste. These are garnish allowances, not measured additions to each blender batch.

RECIPE: Custard Macaroni and Pimento Cheese (custard-mac-and-pimento-cheese.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/custard-mac-and-pimento-cheese/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Elbow Macaroni or Cavatappi pasta
  - 4 tablespoons Unsalted Butter (melted)
  - 3 large Eggs, beaten
  - 2 cups Whole Milk
  - 12 oz Sharp White Cheddar, shredded
  - 4 oz Sharp Yellow Cheddar, shredded
  - 4 oz Pimentos (from a jar), drained and chopped
  - 1/2 tsp Dry Mustard Powder
  - 1/2 tsp Garlic Powder
  - 1/4 tsp Smoked Paprika
  - 1 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1/2 tsp Black Pepper
  - Water and salt, for cooking the pasta
  - Butter or cooking spray, for greasing the baking dish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Eggs and milk set around the pasta while the two cheddars and pimentos remain distinct ingredients. Toss in all the melted butter, then let the pasta stop steaming before adding the egg mixture so it does not scramble on contact. Bubbling edges and a browned top are useful cues, but check the center before resting and serving.

## Directions

1. **Heat and boil:** Heat the oven to 375°F. Bring a roomy pot of water to a boil and salt it with the listed cooking allowance. Cook all the pasta about 2 minutes short of its package’s al-dente time, until firm but hydrated, then drain.

2. **Butter and cool slightly:** Return pasta to the pot and coat it with all the melted butter. Let it stop steaming hot, stirring occasionally, while preparing the egg mixture. This brief cooling helps avoid scrambling the eggs; butter coating does not guarantee that pasta cannot soften further.

3. **Mix the custard:** In a separate bowl whisk all the beaten eggs, whole milk, measured kosher salt, black pepper, garlic powder, dry mustard and smoked paprika until evenly combined. Keep raw-egg utensils separate from ready-to-eat food.

4. **Combine:** Mix three-quarters of EACH cheddar with all the pimentos into the buttered pasta. Stir in all the egg-milk mixture so there are no isolated pockets of custard. Reserve the remaining quarter of each cheese for the top.

5. **Load the dish:** Grease the baking dish with the separate allowance. The original batch uses a 9-by-13-inch dish, but actualdepth/capacity matters. Use additional or appropriately smaller oven-safe dishes if needed to keep a similar shallow layer with headroom. Distribute the full mixture and all remaining cheese across the dishes; do not overfill or discard custard to make it fit.

6. **Bake and check:** Bake, starting checks around 25–30 minutes for the original-size load, until the top is golden, edges bubble and the center is set without flowing egg mixture. Measure several central locations in every dish: each must reach 165°F. Continue baking if needed, shielding an already-browned top with suitable foil. For an optional crisp finish, use a broiler-rated vessel and the appliance’s clearance, watching continuously for up to about 60 seconds and stopping before scorching; a broil does not replace the center check.

7. **Rest and serve:** Rest 5 minutes before serving. The original batch is planned for six portions; use the listed portion count when scaling and portion according to appetite.

RECIPE: Custard Peach Ice Cream (custard-peach-ice-cream.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/custard-peach-ice-cream/
SOURCE: Adapted from houseofnasheats.com
SOURCE_URL: https://houseofnasheats.com/old-fashioned-fresh-peach-ice-cream/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 medium Ripe Peaches, peeled and mashed
  - 1 1/4 cups Granulated Sugar (divided)
  - 1/2 tsp Fresh Lemon Juice (The Acid Balance)
  - 1/4 tsp Sea Salt
  - 5 large Egg Yolks
  - 1 1/2 cups Heavy Cream
  - 1 1/2 cups Whole Milk
  - 1 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Macerate peaches with their share of sugar, then mash them finely so large pieces do not freeze into hard chunks. Keep both the drained syrup and fruit: syrup flavors the custard, while fruit goes into the final moments of churning. Cook the yolk custard gently and chill it fully before using the machine.

## Directions

1.  **Macerate:** Toss peeled peaches with two-fifths of the sugar and the lemon juice (1/2 cup sugar at the original batch size). Let stand for 30-60 minutes, until juicy. Mash until only very small pieces remain, then strain, reserving both the liquid and fruit. Refrigerate both until needed.
2.  **Custard:** In a saucepan, heat cream, milk, salt, and another two-fifths of the sugar (1/2 cup at the original batch size) until steaming but not boiling. This can overlap the peach maceration.
3.  **Emulsify:** Whisk yolks with the remaining one-fifth of the sugar (1/4 cup at the original batch size). Slowly whisk in a little of the hot dairy at a time until the yolks are warmed; at the original batch size, about 1 cup in total is used to temper. Return everything to the pan.
4.  **Cook:** Stir over medium-low heat until the custard reaches 170-175°F and coats a spoon; do not boil. Remove from the heat and stir in vanilla.
5.  **Chill:** Strain into a clean, shallow bowl. Whisk in the peach syrup. Refrigerate promptly for **at least 4 hours** until thoroughly cold, at 40°F / 4°C or below. Prepare the ice cream maker, freezing its bowl in advance if required by the manufacturer.
6.  **Churn:** Pour into the prepared ice cream maker, respecting its fill limit; churn in batches if necessary. Churn according to its instructions until soft-serve consistency. Additional batches add time. Divide the mashed peaches in proportion to the custard portions, keep waiting custard and fruit refrigerated, and add each fruit portion during that batch’s last 30 seconds.
7.  **Set:** Freeze for 4-6 hours to ripen the texture.

RECIPE: Dal Tadka (dal-tadka.md)
CUISINES: Indian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/dal-tadka/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup (200 g) split, hulled yellow mung dal, picked over and rinsed
  - 3 cups (720 ml) water, plus hot water as needed
  - 1/2 tsp ground turmeric
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, plus more to taste
  - 1 medium tomato, finely diced
  - 1 green serrano chile, slit, optional
  - 3 tbsp ghee or neutral oil
  - 1 medium yellow onion, finely diced
  - 1 tsp cumin seeds
  - 1 tsp black mustard seeds
  - 8 fresh curry leaves, washed and dried, optional
  - 2 dried red chiles, broken in half
  - 4 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
  - 1/4 tsp asafoetida (hing), optional; check for wheat if avoiding gluten
  - 1 tsp Kashmiri red chile powder or paprika
  - 2 tbsp chopped cilantro
  - 1 tbsp lemon juice, added to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Dal tadka brings together tender pulses and spices cooked in fat; the exact pulses and tempering vary across Indian homes and regions. This version specifies split hulled mung dal to make the timing useful. Cook the onion before the short garlic-and-spice stage, and add ground chile off heat so the aromatics stay fragrant rather than bitter.

## Directions

1. **Soften the dal:** Combine rinsed mung dal, water, turmeric, and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding hot water if needed, until a lentil crushes easily without a firm center. Skim excessive foam; there is no need to remove all starch.
2. **Build the base:** Stir in tomato and optional green chile. Simmer 5–8 minutes until tomato softens. Mash a little dal with the back of a spoon to thicken, and adjust with hot water until spoonable rather than stiff.
3. **Cook the onion:** While dal simmers, heat 2 tbsp ghee or oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook 7–10 minutes, stirring, until soft and light gold. Move onion to one side and lower the heat if the pan is very hot.
4. **Temper the spices:** Add the remaining 1 tbsp fat to the clear space. Add mustard and cumin seeds; when they begin to sizzle and pop, add dried red chiles and dried-off curry leaves carefully, as they can splatter. Add garlic and cook 30–60 seconds, stirring until pale gold. Mix with the onion. Turn off heat and stir in asafoetida and ground chile for a few seconds.
5. **Combine and balance:** Pour the fragrant onion and spice mixture over the hot dal. Stir, then taste. Add lemon juice gradually and adjust salt and consistency. Scatter with cilantro and serve with rice or bread.

RECIPE: Dan Dan Noodles (dan-dan-noodles.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/dan-dan-noodles/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 12 oz Dried Chinese Wheat Noodles (or fresh if available)
  - 8 oz Ground Pork
  - 2 tbsp Yacai (Sichuan preserved mustard greens), rinsed and minced
  - 1 tbsp Neutral Oil
  - 1 tbsp Shaoxing Wine
  - 2 tbsp Chinese Sesame Paste (or tahini)
  - 1 tbsp Soy Sauce
  - 1 tbsp Chinkiang Black Vinegar
  - 2 tsp Chili Oil with Sediment
  - 1/2 tsp Ground Sichuan Peppercorn
  - 1 clove Garlic, finely grated
  - 1 tsp Sugar
  - 3-4 tbsp Noodle Cooking Water
  - 2 Green Onions, thinly sliced
  - 1/4 cup Roasted Peanuts, roughly chopped
  - 4 small heads Baby Bok Choy, halved (optional)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Dan dan noodles are about the sauce that coats every strand, not a soupy broth. The sauce is assembled raw in the bottom of each bowl -- the hot noodle cooking water emulsifies it into a silky, clinging paste. Chinese sesame paste (made from toasted sesame) has a deeper, nuttier flavor than tahini, but tahini works if you toast it briefly in a dry pan first. Yacai (preserved mustard greens) provides a funky, salty crunch in the pork topping that is difficult to substitute, but it can be found in most Asian grocery stores.

## Directions

1.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** Divide the following among four serving bowls: sesame paste, soy sauce, Chinkiang vinegar, chili oil, ground Sichuan peppercorn, grated garlic, and sugar. Do not stir yet -- the hot noodle water will bring it together.

2.  **Cook the Pork Topping:** Heat the neutral oil in a wok or skillet over high heat. Add the ground pork and cook for 3-4 minutes, breaking it into very small, crispy crumbles. When browned, add the Shaoxing wine and minced yacai. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until the pork is deeply savory and slightly caramelized. Set aside.

3.  **Cook the Noodles:** Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. If using bok choy, blanch it for 60 seconds, remove with a spider, and divide among the bowls. Cook the noodles according to package directions until just al dente. Before draining, ladle 3-4 tbsp of the starchy cooking water into each bowl.

4.  **Emulsify the Sauce:** Using chopsticks, vigorously stir the cooking water into the sauce base in each bowl until the sesame paste dissolves and the sauce becomes creamy and emulsified.

5.  **Assemble:** Drain the noodles and divide among the bowls. Toss with the sauce until every strand is coated. Top with the crispy pork and yacai mixture.

6.  **Garnish:** Scatter with sliced green onions and chopped peanuts. Drizzle with additional chili oil to taste. Serve immediately -- these do not wait well.

RECIPE: Dashi (dashi-japanese-sea-stock.md)
CUISINES: Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/dashi-japanese-sea-stock/
SOURCE: Adapted from Epicurious.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/dashi-japanese-sea-stock-103413
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6 cups Cold Water
  - 1 oz (about 30g) kombu (dried kelp), approx 20 sq inches in the original batch
  - 2 packs (5g each) Katsuo Bushi (Dried Bonito Flakes), approx 1 cup total
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Kombu and dried bonito flakes make a combined, seafood-based dashi for Japanese soups and simmered dishes. Remove the kombu before the stock boils strongly, then give the bonito a brief hot extraction and strain gently. The measured water is the starting amount; absorption and evaporation change the finished volume.

## Directions

1. **Soak:** Put all the measured cold water and kombu in a saucepan with room for the flakes. Let stand about 10 minutes. Set a strainer over a clean vessel large enough for the finished liquid.

2. **Heat and remove kombu:** Heat over medium-high until bubbles begin forming and the liquid is close to boiling. Remove the kombu before a sustained boil. This is a short extraction, not a prolonged kombu simmer.

3. **Add bonito:** Open the measured packages of plain dried bonito flakes and sprinkle all the flakes over the liquid. Let the liquid just reach a boil, then immediately take the pan off the heat.

4. **Steep:** Let stand about 3 minutes. Flakes may settle, but complete sinking is not a required endpoint or a reason to keep boiling.

5. **Strain:** Pour carefully through a fine-mesh sieve, or a coffee-filter-lined sieve, into the waiting vessel. Let it drain without squeezing the flakes. Discard spent kombu/flakes, or cool and refrigerate them promptly and separately if saving them for another recipe. Possible separate uses are kombu for pickled Napa cabbage and bonito flakes for rice with soy-glazed bonito flakes and sesame seeds; this stock method does not supply their pickling or seasoning instructions.

6. **Use or cool:** Use the strained dashi promptly in the dish being prepared. If saving it, divide into shallow containers and refrigerate promptly; do not leave a large bowl of warm stock out until completely cold. Measure the strained amount before using it in a dish that calls for a fixed stock volume.

## Quick Off-Heat Variation

For a version without the initial soak, put the measured cold water and kombu in a saucepan and heat just until the water begins to boil. Take the pan off the heat and remove the kombu. Add all the measured bonito flakes and steep off heat for about 3 minutes; if necessary, stir gently to wet floating flakes. Strain as in step 5. This route omits the later bonito boil as well as the soak, and uses the same ingredient amounts. Actual heating time still depends on the pot and starting water.

RECIPE: Doc Chey’s Chicken Lo Mein (doc-cheys-chicken-lo-mein.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/doc-cheys-chicken-lo-mein/
SOURCE: ajc.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.ajc.com/lifestyles/food--cooking/lomein-dish-can-made-from-ingredients-hand/nm6EiZJQkRfSmBI9T8PUUK/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 pound boneless chicken breast
  - Salt and pepper
  - 1 tablespoon vegetable oil
  - 2 teaspoons minced garlic
  - 1 teaspoon minced ginger
  - 1 cups sliced onions
  - 1 cup sliced carrots
  - 1 cup sliced bok choy
  - 1 cup edamame
  - 4 cups cooked egg noodles
  - Cantonese Sauce (see recipe)
  - 2 tablespoons sliced scallions
  - Cantonese Sauce
  - 1/4 cup soy sauce
  - 1/4 cup Shaoxing cooking wine
  - 1/4 cup oyster sauce
  - 2 tablespoons granulated sugar
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Doc Chey’s lo mein uses a soy, wine and oyster-sauce mixture with chicken and several vegetables. Have the cooked noodles and sauce ready before heating the wok, and return the cooked chicken only near the end.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Cut chicken into thin strips and season with salt and pepper. Whisk soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, oyster sauce and sugar together until sugar dissolves. Prepare the cooked noodles and vegetables before heating the pan.

2. **Cook:** Heat oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken in uncrowded batches, about 3 minutes or as needed, until the thickest pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Transfer to a clean plate.

3. **Continue:** Add garlic and ginger to the pan and stir about 30 seconds. Add onions, carrots, bok choy and edamame. Stir-fry about 4 minutes, until vegetables are tender-crisp; use fully cooked edamame prepared according to its package.

4. **Continue:** Add noodles and the prepared Cantonese sauce. Return chicken and toss about 3 minutes, until hot and coated and the sauce has reduced. Divide between bowls and garnish with scallions.

RECIPE: Double Chocolate Cookies (double-chocolate-cookies.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/double-chocolate-cookies/
SOURCE: Adapted from Samantha Seneviratne
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1018459-double-chocolate-cookies
INGREDIENTS:
  - 10 tbsp (141 g) Unsalted Butter, room temp
  - 3/4 cup (150 g) Dark Brown Sugar, packed
  - 2/3 cup (133 g) Granulated Sugar
  - 1 large Egg
  - 2 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - 1 cup (145 g) All-Purpose Flour
  - 3/4 cup (75 g) Dutch-process Cocoa Powder
  - 3/4 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1/2 tsp Baking Powder
  - 1/2 tsp Baking Soda
  - 2 cups (305 g) Semisweet Chocolate Discs (preferred)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Dutch-process cocoa and a generous disc filling make these large cookies deeply chocolatey. Plan for the full 24–36-hour dough chill, then bake a few well-spaced portions at a time. Stop when the edges are set and the centers are still soft.

## Directions

1. **Dry mix:** Whisk the flour, Dutch-process cocoa, kosher salt, baking powder and baking soda until evenly mixed and free of lumps.

2. **Cream:** With a paddle attachment, beat the softened butter and both sugars until very light, about 5 minutes, scraping the bowl. Beat in the egg and vanilla until combined.

3. **Combine and chill:** On low speed, mix in the dry ingredients just until no dry pockets remain, then briefly mix in the chocolate discs. Press plastic wrap against the dough and refrigerate for 24–36 hours.

4. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment. Keep the remaining dough covered and refrigerated between loads.

5. **Portion:** Make balls slightly larger than golf balls, about 3 1/2 oz each. The original batch makes roughly 9–10 cookies. Put no more than 5 of these large portions on the original-size sheet, with ample room to spread; use fewer if the actual sheet cannot provide that space. Scaling changes the amount of dough and number of loads, not the portion size or pan capacity.

6. **Bake:** Once the oven reaches 350°F, bake for about 18 minutes, until the edges are set and the centers remain slightly soft. Bake the rest in further loads as needed.

7. **Cool:** Let the cookies firm on the sheet for about 10 minutes, then carefully transfer them to a rack. Let the sheet cool before loading more dough. Serve warm once firm enough to lift, or cool completely before packing.

## Cooking Notes

For the same listed chocolate volume, choose semisweet or bittersweet discs. For the original batch, the discs are 2 cups / 305 g. Alternatively, replace the discs with chocolate chips: the original batch uses 2 cups / 340 g. When scaling, scale that chosen alternative’s volume and weight together; buy and use one option. Chips and discs will distribute differently.

For rack cooling straight from the oven, move the whole parchment sheet with the baked cookies onto a rack instead of leaving them on the pan for 10 minutes. Let them firm there before lifting individual cookies.

RECIPE: Double Chocolate Layer Cake (double-chocolate-layer-cake.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/double-chocolate-layer-cake/
SOURCE: Ed Kasky, Gourmet (March 1999), via Epicurious
SOURCE_URL: https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/double-chocolate-layer-cake-101275
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Cake layers ---
  - butter or neutral oil, for greasing the pans and parchment
  - 3 oz semisweet chocolate, finely chopped
  - 1 1/2 cups hot brewed coffee
  - 3 cups granulated sugar
  - 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  - 1 1/2 cups unsweetened natural cocoa powder (not Dutch-process)
  - 2 tsp baking soda
  - 3/4 tsp baking powder
  - 1 1/4 tsp sea salt
  - 3 large eggs
  - 3/4 cup vegetable oil
  - 1 1/2 cups buttermilk, well-shaken
  - 3/4 tsp vanilla extract
  - --- Ganache frosting ---
  - 1 lb semisweet chocolate, finely chopped
  - 1 cup heavy cream
  - 2 tbsp granulated sugar
  - 2 tbsp light corn syrup
  - 1/4 cup unsalted butter, cubed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This dark chocolate cake combines natural cocoa with semisweet chocolate melted into hot coffee, then adds a smooth ganache coating. Keep the specified cocoa and leaveners, and use two 10-inch round pans that are 2 inches deep. Let the layers cool completely and the ganache thicken until spreadable before assembly; corn syrup helps the frosting stay smooth and flexible.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the pans:** Preheat the oven to 300°F. Use butter or neutral oil to grease two 10-inch round cake pans, each 2 inches deep; line the bottoms with parchment and grease the parchment.
2. **Melt the cake chocolate:** Combine the cake's semisweet chocolate and hot brewed coffee. Let stand, stirring occasionally, until smooth, then let cool while preparing the other ingredients.
3. **Dry mixture:** Sift the cake's granulated sugar, all-purpose flour, unsweetened natural cocoa powder (not Dutch-process), baking soda, baking powder, and sea salt together into a large bowl.
4. **Beat the eggs:** In another large bowl, beat the large eggs until slightly thickened and pale yellow, about 3 minutes with a stand mixer or 5 minutes with a hand mixer.
5. **Add the liquids:** Slowly add the cake's vegetable oil, buttermilk, and vanilla extract and the cooled coffee-chocolate mixture to the eggs, beating until combined.
6. **Combine:** Add the dry mixture and beat on medium speed only until combined. Scrape the bowl so no pockets of dry ingredients remain. The batter will be thin.
7. **Bake and cool:** Divide the batter evenly between the prepared pans and bake in the middle of the oven for 60–70 minutes, until a tester inserted in the center comes out clean. Cool the layers completely in their pans on racks. Run a thin knife around the edges, carefully invert, and remove the parchment. Do not frost warm layers.
8. **Heat the ganache cream:** While the layers cool, put the ganache's heavy cream, granulated sugar, and light corn syrup in a 1 1/2- to 2-quart saucepan. Heat over moderately low heat, whisking until the sugar dissolves and the mixture reaches a boil. Remove from the heat.
9. **Melt the ganache chocolate:** Add the ganache's semisweet chocolate to the hot cream mixture and whisk until melted.
10. **Finish and cool the ganache:** Add the ganache's unsalted butter and whisk until smooth. Transfer to a shallow bowl and cool, stirring occasionally, until spreadable. Refrigerate as needed to thicken it, and keep it refrigerated if the layers are not yet ready; do not leave the ganache on the counter throughout a long cake-cooling period.
11. **Assemble:** Once the layers are completely cool and the ganache holds a soft, spreadable consistency, frost between the layers and over the top and sides. If refrigerated ganache has become too firm, let it soften briefly just until it spreads without tearing the cake. Refrigerate the assembled cake until serving.

## Timing and storage

Allow about 4 hours for preparation, baking, complete layer cooling, ganache cooling, and assembly; cooling can take longer in a warm kitchen. Make the ganache during the layers' cooling period and refrigerate it while waiting. The planning estimate does not mean leaving the ganache or frosted cake at room temperature for four hours.

Keep the frosted cake covered at 40°F or below for up to 3 days. Let only the slices you plan to serve soften briefly at room temperature, keeping the rest refrigerated. Count ganache cooling, frosting, and service toward a combined 2-hour limit out of refrigeration, or 1 hour above 90°F; refrigerate sooner if needed. The plain, unfrosted layers may be made one day ahead and kept at room temperature, wrapped well once completely cool.

RECIPE: Pad Kee Mao (Drunken Noodles) (drunken-noodles-pad-kee-mao.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/drunken-noodles-pad-kee-mao/
SOURCE: Adapted from thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/drunken-noodles-pad-kee-mao/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken ---
  - 450 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced about 1/4 inch thick
  - 2 tbsp water, for the chicken
  - 2 tsp cornstarch
  - 1 tsp light soy sauce, for the chicken
  - --- Noodles and vegetables ---
  - 800 g fresh wide rice noodles (sen yai); see the dried-noodle substitution
  - 3 tbsp neutral oil, divided
  - 4 cloves garlic, finely chopped
  - 1 to 4 Thai chiles, finely chopped, to suit your heat preference
  - 100 g shallots, thinly sliced
  - 150 g canned baby corn, drained and halved lengthwise
  - 30 g holy basil leaves; see substitution if unavailable
  - --- Sauce ---
  - 2 tbsp oyster sauce
  - 1 tbsp fish sauce
  - 1 tbsp light soy sauce
  - 1 tsp dark soy sauce
  - 2 tsp brown sugar
  - 2 tbsp water, for the sauce, plus small splashes if noodles need loosening
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Pad kee mao combines bold chile-and-basil flavor with wide rice noodles, shallots and baby corn. Use holy basil when available; Thai basil gives a different aroma. Prepare everything before heating the pan and finish one serving at a time so the noodles have room to toast without tearing. Lift gently rather than scraping vigorously.

## Directions

1. **Marinate and prepare noodles:** Mix chicken with its water, cornstarch, and marinade soy; refrigerate while preparing the rest, about 15 minutes. Gently separate flexible fresh noodles and divide into four equal portions. For dried noodles, follow the substitution instructions before portioning.
2. **Mix sauce and prep vegetables:** Dissolve sugar in the sauce water, then stir in oyster sauce, fish sauce, light soy, and dark soy. Chop garlic and chiles, slice shallots, drain and halve corn, and pick basil leaves. Keep basil separate from the vegetables.
3. **Cook chicken in two batches:** Heat 1 tsp oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add half the chicken in a single layer; leave about 1–2 minutes, then turn and cook until several thick slices reach 165°F / 74°C, usually about 4–5 minutes total. Transfer to a clean bowl. Repeat with another teaspoon oil and the remaining chicken.
4. **Cook the vegetables:** Add 1 tbsp oil and lower heat to medium. Stir garlic and chiles about 30 seconds until fragrant. Add shallots and baby corn; stir-fry about 3–4 minutes until shallots soften and corn is hot. Transfer out. Divide chicken, vegetables, basil, and well-stirred sauce into four portions.
5. **Finish the first portion:** Heat 1 tsp oil over medium-high heat. Add one noodle portion and its sauce, then gently lift and fold until coated. Add its cooked chicken and vegetables, including their portion of any cooking juices. Keep folding until hot and the sauce is absorbed, about 1–2 minutes. If noodles are sticking and still firm, add a small splash of water; do not flood the pan.
6. **Toast briefly and add basil:** Spread loosely and leave about 15–20 seconds, then lift and turn. Repeat once if needed for a few browned patches, lowering heat if sauce begins to burn. Turn off heat and fold in one portion of basil until just wilted. Taste and plate immediately.
7. **Repeat and serve:** Repeat steps 5–6 with the remaining three portions, using 1 tsp oil for each. If the first portion needs a seasoning adjustment, adjust the remaining sauce before continuing. Serve each plate as it is ready; no additional rice is needed.

RECIPE: Dutch Baby Pancake (dutch-baby-pancake.md)
CUISINES: German, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/dutch-baby-pancake/
SOURCE: Adapted from prettyprovidence.com
SOURCE_URL: https://prettyprovidence.com/german-pancakes/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6 large Eggs
  - 1 cup Whole Milk
  - 1 cup All-Purpose Flour
  - 4 tbsp Unsalted Butter
  - 1 tsp Vanilla Extract
  - Pinch of Sea Salt
  - Fresh Lemon Juice and Powdered Sugar
  - Warm Maple Syrup
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The egg batter expands as it heats and settles after leaving the oven. Keep all the butter and choose the pan route before mixing. The baking-dish and skillet versions have different shapes and batter depths; use the center, not the height of the rim, to judge readiness.

## Directions

1. **Choose and heat:** For the original-batch baking-dish version, use a 9×13-inch vessel suitable for 425°F and for the hot-pan/batter temperature change. Follow the vessel’s manufacturer instructions; do not assume a glass or ceramic dish permits preheating empty or adding cooler batter. Use a metal pan rated for this oven temperature if the glass or ceramic vessel’s instructions do not allow the required temperature change. Heat the oven to 425°F. For one pan, put all the listed butter in that pan; when using several pans, divide all the listed butter proportionally among them, keeping the same butter-to-batter ratio. Let the butter melt during preheating; remove each pan promptly once it has melted if the oven is not ready, so it does not burn.

2. **Mix:** Blend all the eggs, milk, flour, vanilla and salt until smooth, starting with 30–45 seconds, or stop once no flour lumps remain. This is unheated batter; follow the blender’s ordinary capacity limit and work in batches if needed, recombining them before filling the pan. Keep raw batter away from serving utensils.

3. **Fill:** Once the oven is ready and the butter has melted, carefully place each hot vessel on a heat-safe surface. Pour all the batter into the single appropriately sized pan, or divide it proportionally among the prepared pans, keeping similar batter depth and headroom. Keep oven gloves on for the pans. Do not pour a scaled larger batch into the same original pan.

4. **Bake:** Bake until puffed and golden with a set center, beginning checks around 20 minutes for the original baking-dish batch. Check 160°F in the egg-batter center; continue if it remains wet or below the endpoint, even if the rim is already tall and brown. Avoid unnecessary early opening, but open the oven when a needed center check is due.

5. **Serve:** Remove with oven gloves. Some settling is normal as the pancake cools; immediate service keeps the edges crispest. Divide into the listed portions and add the separate unmeasured lemon juice and powdered sugar, or warm maple syrup and powdered sugar, as wanted. Wash the lemon before cutting.

RECIPE: Turkey Meatballs (easy-baked-turkey-meatballs.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/easy-baked-turkey-meatballs/
SOURCE: Adapted from Blog.myfitnesspal.com
SOURCE_URL: http://blog.myfitnesspal.com/easy-baked-turkey-meatballs/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 lbs Ground Turkey (93/7 fat ratio preferred)
  - 1/2 cup Unseasoned Breadcrumbs
  - 1/2 cup Carrots, finely minced
  - 1/4 cup Yellow Onion, finely minced
  - 2 large Eggs
  - 1 tbsp Italian Seasoning
  - 1 tsp Garlic Powder
  - 1 tsp Sea Salt
  - Pinch of red pepper flakes, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Finely minced carrots and onion disperse through the turkey and breadcrumb mixture. Mix just until combined and keep the two-tablespoon portions uniform; use their center temperature to judge when baking is complete.

## Directions

1. **Prep:** Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line enough baking sheets with parchment paper to leave space between meatballs.
2. **Mince:** Finely mince all the measured carrots and onion by hand or in a food processor.
3. **Combine:** In a large bowl, gently combine all the turkey, breadcrumbs, minced vegetables, eggs, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, sea salt and red pepper flakes if using. Stop when the ingredients are evenly distributed.
4. **Shape:** Form all the mixture into two-tablespoon portions and gently roll each into a ball. Keep that size at every batch amount and arrange with space between them on the prepared sheets.
5. **Bake:** Start checking at 25–30 minutes and continue baking until meatball centers reach 165°F / 74°C. Insert a thermometer into the center, checking large meatballs and different pan positions; use additional oven loads if needed. A lack of pink is not a substitute for the temperature check.
6. **Serve:** Serve the cooked meatballs with separately prepared tomato sauce, pasta or spaghetti squash if wanted. For a vegetable serving option, add separately sautéed onion, zucchini, red pepper and grape tomatoes; these are additional serving supplies, with no amounts included in the meatball mixture.

RECIPE: Yogurt Popsicles (easy-breakfast-yogurt-popsicles.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/easy-breakfast-yogurt-popsicles/
SOURCE: Adapted from Iheartnaptime.net
SOURCE_URL: https://www.iheartnaptime.net/breakfast-popsicles/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Popsicles ---
  - 1 cup plain Greek yogurt, full-fat preferred
  - 1/2 cup whole milk
  - 2 tsp honey
  - 1/2 cup [granola](/mise/recipes/granola), prepared and cooled
  - 1 cup fresh berries or chopped fruit, washed and drained; large pieces cut to fit the molds
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Adapted from the I Heart Naptime recipe contributed by Jane at Baking-Ginger, these pops can be prepared ahead for summer breakfasts or snacks. These fruit-and-yogurt pops keep the full-fat yogurt, whole milk and granola. Half the honey sweetens the dairy mixture and half coats the granola. A frozen granola base may soften where it touches yogurt; honey does not guarantee lasting crunch. Freeze until firm before trying to release a pop.

## Directions

1. **Mix the base:** Whisk all plain Greek yogurt, whole milk, and 1/2 of the honey until smooth. Keep the other half of the honey for the granola.
2. **Add fruit:** Divide all fresh berries or chopped fruit among the molds. The original eight-pop count is a planning yield; actual mold capacity can require more or fewer molds.
3. **Fill:** Divide the entire dairy mixture among the fruit-filled molds, leaving enough room for the granola layer and expansion as directed by the mold maker. The original half-inch gap is a starting context only when suitable for that mold.
4. **Add granola:** Mix 1/2 of the honey and [granola](/mise/recipes/granola) and divide all of it over the molds, gently pressing into contact with the dairy mixture. If honey is too stiff to mix, warm it briefly in a microwave-safe vessel, checking frequently, then mix it with the granola.
5. **Freeze:** Insert sticks according to the mold instructions and freeze at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, until firm throughout. Keep dairy cold while working; more or larger molds can take longer.
6. **Release:** Run warm water briefly over the outside of each mold until the pop releases, without immersing the open top. Do not force a stick from an incompletely frozen pop. Serve promptly; keep remaining pops frozen.

RECIPE: Chia Pudding (easy-chia-pudding.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/easy-chia-pudding/
SOURCE: Adapted from eatingbirdfood.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.eatingbirdfood.com/basic-chia-seed-pudding/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3-4 tbsp Chia Seeds
  - 1 cup Milk of choice (Coconut or Almond preferred)
  - 1/2 tbsp Maple Syrup or Honey
  - 1/4 tsp Vanilla Extract
  - Fresh Berries
  - Almond Butter
  - [Granola](/mise/recipes/granola)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Stir the seeds into the full listed milk, wait five minutes, then stir again before refrigerating. The second stir breaks up early clumps. Three to four tablespoons seeds per cup of milk gives a range of thickness, and milk composition changes the result. For the separate blended chocolate recipe, see [Chocolate Chia Pudding](/mise/recipes/chocolate-chia-pudding); its ingredients and yield are different.

## Directions

1. **Combine:** In a bowl or jar with room to stir, whisk all the listed chia seeds, milk, chosen maple syrup or honey, and vanilla. The original batch uses 3–4 tbsp seeds per 1 cup milk; use the listed scaled quantities.

2. **First set:** Let stand for 5 minutes before the second stir.

3. **Stir again:** Stir thoroughly or close the jar securely and shake, then inspect the bottom and sides for clumps and break them up.

4. **Chill:** Cover and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight, until the pudding is thick and spoonable.

5. **Adjust:** If too thick, stir in a little additional milk. If still thin after sufficient chilling, add about 1 tbsp additional seeds at the original one-cup batch; adjust proportionally for another batch, stir and refrigerate for another 30 minutes or longer until thick. These adjustments are additions beyond the base formula, not a promise that every product sets at one exact time.

6. **Serve:** Wash and drain fresh berries, then top the pudding with the listed berries, almond butter and prepared granola as wanted. These toppings are unmeasured allowances; keep granola separate until serving for crunch.

RECIPE: Cinnamon French Toast Sticks (easy-cinnamon-french-toast-sticks.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/easy-cinnamon-french-toast-sticks/
SOURCE: Adapted from justataste.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.justataste.com/easy-cinnamon-french-toast-sticks-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 8 slices Thick-cut Texas Toast (Day-old preferred)
  - 4 large Eggs
  - 1 cup Whole Milk
  - 2 1/2 tsp Ground Cinnamon
  - 1 tbsp Honey
  - 1 tbsp Vanilla Extract
  - Unsalted Butter (for the pan)
  - Warm Maple Syrup
  - Fresh Berries
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Use thick bread with sturdy crusts so the sticks survive dipping and turning. Keep the full milk, honey and cinnamon formula. Coat all sides, let excess drip away, then cook in uncrowded rounds; the color of one face does not establish that the center is cooked.

## Directions

1. **Cut:** Cut each listed Texas-toast slice into four similar sticks. Keep the original bread thickness and stick size when scaling; increase or decrease the number of slices and cooking rounds rather than making larger sticks.

2. **Mix:** Whisk all the eggs, whole milk, cinnamon, honey and vanilla together until the honey is dispersed and no egg-white streaks remain.

3. **Coat:** Dip a cooking-sized batch, turning each stick to coat all sides and lifting while it still holds its shape. Let excess custard drip back into the bowl. Coat the surfaces without leaving the sticks so saturated that they collapse. Keep raw-coated sticks and their utensils separate from cooked sticks.

4. **Heat pan:** Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Melt some of the unmeasured pan butter, starting with 2–3 tablespoons for an original large-skillet round, enough to coat it. Use more of the separate pan supply as needed for later rounds; add enough for a thin coating in each round.

5. **Cook and repeat:** Add only as many sticks as fit in a single uncrowded layer. Begin checking a broad side after about 2 minutes; turn as each face becomes golden and cook the remaining faces as needed. Check that the center is set, without liquid custard, and reaches 160°F using a thermometer inserted along a thick stick. Lower heat if the butter or coating browns too quickly. Repeat coating and cooking with all the remaining sticks, adding pan butter as needed. Refrigerate custard during pauses and discard unused bread-contact custard after the last round.

6. **Serve:** Divide the cooked sticks among the listed portions and serve promptly with warm maple syrup and washed berries as wanted. Let a child’s serving cool enough to handle comfortably.

RECIPE: Pumpkin Pancakes (easy-homemade-pumpkin-pancakes.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/easy-homemade-pumpkin-pancakes/
SOURCE: Adapted from inspiredtaste.net
SOURCE_URL: https://www.inspiredtaste.net/8896/pumpkin-pancakes/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 1 cup Pure Pumpkin Puree (Not pumpkin pie filling)
  - 1 3/4 cups Whole Milk
  - 1 large Egg
  - 2 tbsp Vegetable or Avocado Oil
  - 3 tbsp Light Brown Sugar, packed
  - 2 tsp Baking Powder
  - 1 tsp Baking Soda
  - 2 tsp Pumpkin Pie Spice
  - 1/2 tsp Sea Salt
  - Butter or oil spray for the skillet
  - Salted butter and maple syrup for serving (optional)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Pumpkin puree gives the batter moisture and body. Whisk the pumpkin mixture smooth before flour enters, then stir the dry ingredients in only until fully moistened. Small hydrated lumps are fine; cook modest portions until their middles are set as well as their surfaces browned.

## Directions

1. **Dry mix:** Whisk together the flour, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, pumpkin pie spice, and salt in a medium bowl. Break up any brown-sugar lumps so the sugar and leaveners are evenly distributed.
2. **Wet mix:** In a large bowl, whisk the milk, pumpkin puree, egg, and the measured vegetable or avocado oil until evenly blended and smooth.
3. **Combine:** Add the dry mixture gradually to the pumpkin mixture, stirring with a spatula until no dry flour pockets remain on the bottom or sides. Stop once combined; small hydrated lumps may remain. Do not beat the flour batter smooth.
4. **Rest:** Let the batter sit for 5 minutes while the griddle heats.
5. **Prepare the pan:** Heat a skillet or griddle over medium heat. Lightly grease with the separate butter or oil-spray allowance; the measured oil all belongs in the batter.
6. **Portion:** Drop batter by 1/4 cupfuls, leaving space to turn the pancakes. If it mounds, spread each portion gently with the back of the scoop so its center is not much thicker than the edges.
7. **Cook and turn:** Cook until the edges look set and the underside is lightly browned, with small bubbles on top, about 2 minutes. Flip gently and cook about 1–2 minutes more, until the middle is cooked through with no wet batter. If the outside browns too quickly, lower the heat and keep cooking the center. Repeat with the remaining batter, renewing the light pan coating as needed.
8. **Serve:** Serve immediately with salted butter and warm maple syrup if desired.
