RECIPE: Chocolate Sandwich Cookie Truffles (easy-oreo-truffles.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/easy-oreo-truffles/
SOURCE: Adapted from allrecipes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/127491/easy-oreo-truffles/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 16 oz cream-filled chocolate sandwich cookies
  - 1 pkg (8 oz) Cream Cheese, softened
  - 16 oz Semi-Sweet Baking Chocolate, melted
  - Flaky Sea Salt (Optional)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Use the full measured cookie mass, including the cream filling, and reserve part of those same cookies for garnish. Firm cold balls are easier to coat than soft ones. Let the melted chocolate cool enough not to soften them on contact, then keep the finished cream-cheese truffles refrigerated until serving.

## Directions

1. **Crush and reserve:** Weigh the full listed cookie amount, including its cream filling. Finely crush one-fifth and reserve these crumbs for garnish; crush the remaining four-fifths for the filling. The source’s original 16-ounce package was roughly 45 cookies, with 9 reserved and 36 inside; do not force those literal counts on a different package or scale. A sealed bag and rolling pin is the source alternative to a processor.
2. **Mix:** Beat all the softened cream cheese with all the four-fifths filling crumbs until evenly combined. The reserved garnish crumbs are not an additional cookie supply.
3. **Shape:** Roll into roughly 1-inch balls, aiming for about the listed count as a planning yield. Use more or fewer same-sized balls when scaling and enough lined trays to hold them.
4. **Chill:** Refrigerate the balls about 30–60 minutes until firm enough to dip. Keep cream-cheese preparation and service within the cold-handling limits below.
5. **Melt:** Melt all the baking chocolate in a dry heatproof bowl over barely simmering water, or in short microwave bursts with stirring between them. Start with the existing 30-second bursts and shorten as it melts. Keep water out; allow the chocolate to cool a little if it softens the cold balls on contact.
6. **Dip:** Coat each cold ball using a fork or dipping tool, tap off excess and place on a lined tray. Work in batches, keeping waiting balls refrigerated. Use the full chocolate supply for coating, recognizing that a dipping bowl may retain a little excess.
7. **Garnish:** While the coating is wet, distribute all the reserved cookie crumbs among the balls. Add the optional flaky salt if desired.
8. **Set:** Refrigerate at least 1 hour until the coating is firm. Store covered in the refrigerator until just before serving. Dipping chocolate that has touched cream-cheese crumbs belongs in refrigerated handling; the source’s room-temperature leftover-chocolate note applies only to a clean separate supply.

RECIPE: Pan-Seared Chicken Breasts (easy-pan-seared-chicken-breasts.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/easy-pan-seared-chicken-breasts/
SOURCE: Adapted from whatsinthepan.com
SOURCE_URL: https://whatsinthepan.com/easy-pan-seared-chicken/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breasts, butterflied into 4–6 cutlets about 1/2 inch thick
  - 1/2 cup (60 g) all-purpose flour, for dredging; excess will be discarded
  - 3 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt
  - 1/4 tsp black pepper
  - 1/2 tsp garlic powder
  - 1/2 tsp onion powder
  - 1 tsp dried Italian herbs
  - Lemon wedges, for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A chicken cutlet cooks quickly because its center is close to the hot surface. Even thickness is more useful than a promise of an exact cooking time. A light flour coating gives browning a head start; a thermometer tells you when to stop.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Butterfly thick breasts into 4–6 cutlets about 1/2 inch thick, evening them gently if necessary. Pat dry with paper towels. Wash hands and clean surfaces after handling raw chicken.
2. **Dredge lightly:** Mix flour, salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and herbs in a shallow dish. Coat each cutlet and shake off excess. Discard flour that contacted raw chicken.
3. **Sear in batches:** Heat 1.5 tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add only enough cutlets to fit without touching. Cook about 3–4 minutes until the bottom is golden; lower heat if flour specks darken rapidly.
4. **Finish by temperature:** Turn and cook about 2–4 minutes more, adjusting heat as needed. Insert a thermometer from the side into the thickest part and remove each cutlet when it reaches 165°F / 74°C. Thick pieces may take longer. Set on a clean plate. Carefully remove scorched residue, add remaining oil, and repeat with the second batch.
5. **Rest and serve:** Rest the cooked chicken for 5 minutes, loosely covered. Serve with lemon wedges. The rest is for serving quality; do not remove under-temperature chicken in the hope that resting will make it safe.

RECIPE: Spinach Gnocchi (easy-spinach-gnocchi.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/easy-spinach-gnocchi/
SOURCE: Adapted from 100daysofrealfood.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.100daysofrealfood.com/gnocchi-recipe-easy-spinach/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 10 oz Frozen Spinach, defrosted
  - 1 1/2 cups Whole-Milk Ricotta
  - 3/4 cup Parmesan, freshly grated
  - 1 1/4 cups Whole-Wheat Flour (plus extra for dusting)
  - 1 large Egg
  - Salt and Black Pepper
  - Pinch of Nutmeg (The "High Note")
  - Tomato sauce or brown butter and sage, as desired for serving; choose one route
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Squeeze the thawed spinach firmly before mixing it with the full ricotta, Parmesan, egg and whole-wheat flour. Add only the dusting flour needed to handle the dough. Floating is a useful first cue; cut a representative piece open and check that its center is cooked through.

## Directions

1. **Prepare spinach:** Thaw the spinach in the refrigerator. If its package requires cooking before use, follow that instruction, cool enough to handle and squeeze it firmly in a clean towel. Do not assume every frozen product is ready to eat.

Check representative egg-containing centers for 160°F; allow longer when needed.

RECIPE: Egg Fried Rice (egg-fried-rice.md)
CUISINES: Chinese, Cantonese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/egg-fried-rice/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 cups (about 450 g) cooked rice, safely chilled and gently separated
  - 4 large eggs, beaten
  - 2 cloves garlic, minced
  - 3 scallions, whites and greens separated and sliced
  - 1/2 cup frozen peas and diced carrots, thawed and drained
  - 1.5 tbsp soy sauce, plus more to taste
  - 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - 2 tbsp neutral oil, divided
  - 1/4 tsp ground white pepper
  - 1 tsp sesame seeds, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Fried rice is a flexible way to turn cooked rice into a new meal. What matters is the rice's texture and surface moisture, not its birthday: chilled rice is often easier to separate, while freshly cooked rice needs excess steam released and careful cooling first. A home burner also rewards smaller batches more than an overloaded, smoking-hot wok.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Gently separate the cold rice with clean fingers or a fork. Beat eggs. Drain thawed vegetables. Measure soy sauce and sesame oil separately; set out garlic, scallion whites, greens, and pepper.
2. **Cook the eggs:** Heat a large wok or skillet over medium-high, then add 1 tbsp neutral oil. When shimmering, add eggs and stir until set with no liquid egg remaining. Transfer to a clean plate. Do not intentionally smoke oil or overheat empty nonstick cookware.
3. **Fry the rice:** Add remaining oil and rice. Spread briefly, then toss and gently break remaining clumps. Cook 4–6 minutes, adjusting heat to maintain a sizzle. If liquid collects or the pan is crowded, work in two batches.
4. **Add vegetables and aromatics:** Make space in the pan. Add garlic and scallion whites; stir for about 15 seconds until fragrant, then add drained vegetables. Toss for 1–2 minutes until vegetables are hot.
5. **Season and heat through:** Return eggs. Add soy sauce around the rice and toss thoroughly. Continue until the rice is steaming throughout and reaches 165°F / 74°C in several spots. Add sesame oil and white pepper. Taste before adding more soy sauce.
6. **Finish:** Fold in scallion greens and transfer to bowls. Add optional sesame seeds. Serve promptly.

RECIPE: Egg in a Hole (egg-in-a-hole.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/egg-in-a-hole/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 slices Thick-Cut Bread (sourdough, white, or whole wheat)
  - 2 large Eggs
  - 2 tbsp Unsalted Butter
  - Kosher Salt
  - Freshly Ground Black Pepper
  - Optional: shredded cheese, hot sauce, everything bagel seasoning
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Egg in a hole (also called toad in the hole, egg in a basket, or one-eyed jack) is one of the simplest and most satisfying breakfast preparations. The trick is using enough butter to get the bread golden and crispy while the egg cooks within the cutout. A 2.5 to 3-inch circle cut from the center is the ideal size -- too small and the egg overflows, too large and there is not enough bread left. Do not forget to toast the cutout rounds alongside the bread -- they are the best part for dipping into the runny yolk.

## Directions

1.  **Cut the Holes:** Using a round cookie cutter, biscuit cutter, or the rim of a drinking glass (2.5-3 inches), press and twist to cut a circle from the center of each bread slice. Reserve the cutout rounds.
2.  **Heat the Pan:** Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Swirl to coat the entire surface evenly.
3.  **Toast and Fry:** Place the bread slices and the cutout rounds in the skillet. Cook the bread for about 1 minute until the bottom is golden. Crack one egg into each hole. Season with salt and pepper.
4.  **Cook:** Cook undisturbed for 2-3 minutes until the egg white is mostly set on the bottom and the bread is deeply golden. Flip the bread carefully with a spatula. Cook for another 30-60 seconds for a runny yolk, or 1-2 minutes for a more set yolk. Flip the cutout rounds when golden.
5.  **Serve:** Transfer to plates. Serve the toasted rounds alongside for dipping into the yolk. Add shredded cheese, hot sauce, or everything bagel seasoning if desired.

RECIPE: Pork and Cabbage Skillet (Egg Roll in a Bowl) (egg-roll-in-a-bowl.md)
CUISINES: Chinese-American-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/egg-roll-in-a-bowl/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 450 g (1 lb) ground pork
  - 1 tsp neutral oil
  - 500 g green cabbage, shredded into thin ribbons
  - 100 g carrot, cut into fine matchsticks
  - 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
  - 2 cloves garlic, minced
  - 3 scallions, whites and greens sliced separately
  - 2 tbsp reduced-sodium soy sauce
  - 2 tbsp water, plus 1 tbsp only if needed
  - 2 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1 tsp unseasoned rice vinegar, plus 1 tsp more only to taste
  - 2 tsp toasted sesame seeds
  - 2 tsp chili crisp or sriracha, optional and served separately
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This is a Chinese-American-inspired pork-and-cabbage skillet, built around an egg-roll filling idea. It is useful because the meat and vegetables cook in sequence in one pan. A few browned pork surfaces add depth; the cabbage supplies moisture and a lighter texture. Serve promptly once the meat is cooked and the cabbage reaches the texture you want.

## Directions

1. **Prepare everything:** Shred cabbage, cut carrot into fine matchsticks, grate ginger and mince garlic. Slice scallions, keeping whites separate from greens. Mix soy sauce with 2 tbsp water. Measure the sesame oil, vinegar and garnishes.
2. **Brown and cook the pork:** Heat neutral oil in a deep 12-inch skillet over medium-high. Add pork in flattened clumps, leave about 2 minutes to color, then turn and break into crumbles. Cook another 4–5 minutes, or until several substantial clumps reach 160°F / 71°C. Spoon off excess rendered fat if it pools, leaving about 1 tbsp in the pan.
3. **Add the aromatics:** Lower to medium. Stir ginger, garlic and scallion whites into the pork for about 30 seconds, until fragrant but not scorched.
4. **Cook the vegetables:** Add carrot and half the cabbage and toss for about 1 minute. Add the remaining cabbage and soy-water mixture. Cook uncovered 3–5 minutes, stirring, until cabbage is hot and tender with a little bite. Add the extra tablespoon water only if the pan dries while vegetables are firm; if watery, let the excess evaporate briefly.
5. **Finish and portion:** Turn off heat, stir in toasted sesame oil, scallion greens and 1 tsp vinegar. Taste before the optional second teaspoon. Divide among four bowls and sprinkle with measured sesame seeds; offer chili crisp or sriracha separately. Serve promptly. If serving with [Steamed White Rice](/mise/recipes/steamed-white-rice), allow that recipe's full preparation and cooking time separately.

RECIPE: Eggless Spinach and Ricotta Stuffed Shells (eggless-spinach-and-ricotta-stuffed-shells.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/eggless-spinach-and-ricotta-stuffed-shells/
SOURCE: loveandlemons.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.loveandlemons.com/stuffed-shells-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 18 to 20 jumbo pasta shells
  - Extra-virgin olive oil, for drizzling
  - 5 ounces fresh spinach
  - 2 cups ricotta cheese, 16 ounces
  - ¼ cup grated pecorino cheese, plus more for sprinkling
  - 2 garlic cloves, grated
  - 1 teaspoon dried oregano
  - 1 teaspoon lemon zest
  - ¼ teaspoon red pepper flakes
  - ¾ teaspoon sea salt, plus more for the pasta water
  - Freshly ground black pepper
  - 2 cups Marinara Sauce*, plus more for serving
  - Chopped fresh parsley, for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Ricotta and pecorino bind this filling without eggs or mozzarella. Squeeze the steamed spinach dry and drain the ricotta if liquid pools around it so the shells do not sit in watery sauce.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 425°F. For the original batch, have a 9×13-inch oven-safe dish ready. At other scales use enough dishes for similar shell spacing and sauce depth; divide all the marinara and filling among them before assembly.
2. **Steam spinach:** Wash and drain the fresh spinach. Set a steamer over a pot with 1 inch of water and bring to a simmer. Cover and steam the spinach about 1 minute, until wilted. Transfer to a strainer, let cool enough to handle, squeeze dry and chop.

Cover with foil and bake about 20 minutes as a first check. Continue until the filling centers reach 165°F /74°C, checking each dish and allowing extra time for chilled shells.
6. **Serve:** Sprinkle with the additional pecorino and chopped parsley as desired. Serve with the additional marinara on the side.

## Cooking Notes

Assembled shells can be covered and frozen. Thaw completely in the refrigerator before baking, allow extra oven time for a chilled dish and check that the filling centers reach 165°F /74°C. Follow the baking dish manufacturer's instructions for temperature changes. The source’s roughly 10-hour thaw and 30-minute chilled bake are planning references, not guaranteed thawing or doneness clocks.

RECIPE: Eggless Strawberry Ice Cream (eggless-strawberry-ice-cream.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/eggless-strawberry-ice-cream/
SOURCE: Allrecipes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/140877/easy-eggless-strawberry-ice-cream/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups whole milk
  - 2 cups heavy cream
  - 3/4 cup white sugar
  - 1/4 teaspoon salt
  - 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
  - 2 cups pureed fresh strawberries
  - 4 tablespoons lemon juice
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This eggless formula keeps the full milk and cream, the listed sugar amount and all the lemon juice. Dissolve the sugar and chill the mixture thoroughly before churning. Prepare the machine’s freezing bowl in advance when required; a cold mixture does not compensate for an unfrozen bowl.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Prepare and freeze the ice-cream maker bowl in advance if its actual instructions require it. Use pasteurized milk and cream. Wash and hull the fresh strawberries, puree them and then measure the full listed puree amount; no whole-fruit weight is implied. Wash lemons before juicing if using fresh juice.
2. **Mix:** Whisk all the milk, cream, sugar, salt and vanilla until sugar dissolves, then stir in all the measured strawberry puree and lemon juice.
3. **Chill:** Cover and refrigerate until thoroughly cold, about 1–2 hours as a planning reference if the ingredients were already chilled.
4. **Churn:** Follow the actual ice-cream maker’s instructions and maximum liquid fill. Split the fully mixed cold base among batches if it exceeds that limit, keeping unused base refrigerated and preparing the bowl again if required. Churn to the machine’s soft-ice-cream consistency.
5. **Serve or firm:** Serve soft, or transfer to covered freezer-safe containers with expansion room for about 2–3 hours or longer until firm. Keep frozen between servings.

RECIPE: Garlic-Ginger Eggplant (eggplant-with-garlic-sauce.md)
CUISINES: Chinese-American-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/eggplant-with-garlic-sauce/
SOURCE: Adapted from christieathome.com
SOURCE_URL: https://christieathome.com/blog/chinese-spicy-garlic-eggplant/#recipe
INGREDIENTS:
  - 600 g Chinese or Japanese eggplant, ends trimmed, cut into 2-inch-long batons about 1/2 inch thick
  - 2 tbsp neutral oil, divided
  - 4 tbsp water, for covered cooking, divided, plus up to 2 tbsp more if needed
  - 120 ml [Garlic-Ginger Stir-Fry Sauce](/mise/recipes/chinese-garlic-sauce-base), made with vegetarian mushroom sauce; half its recipe
  - 1 tsp sambal oelek chili paste, optional, plus up to 1 tsp more to taste
  - 30 g scallions, thinly sliced
  - 1 tsp unseasoned rice vinegar, optional, only if needed after tasting
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Eggplant browns on the outside before its center becomes silky. Two manageable batches and a little covered steam let you finish the texture without chasing color or continually adding oil. The measured garlic-ginger sauce goes in only after the eggplant is tender.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the sauce:** Make half the linked Garlic-Ginger Stir-Fry Sauce recipe, using vegetarian mushroom sauce, for a finished 120 ml. Alternatively, measure 120 ml from a previously prepared batch and keep its original storage date in mind.
2. **Cut the vegetables:** Trim eggplant and cut into roughly 2-inch batons about 1/2 inch thick. Slice scallions. Divide eggplant into two equal batches.
3. **Brown and soften in two batches:** Heat 1 tbsp oil in a lidded skillet over medium-high. Add half the eggplant in one layer and cook 3–4 minutes, turning to color several surfaces. Reduce to medium, add 2 tbsp water, cover and cook another 3–5 minutes until a fork enters the center easily. Add a little more water only if the pan dries while centers are firm. Uncover to evaporate remaining water, then transfer to a plate. Repeat with the remaining tablespoon oil, eggplant and 2 tbsp water.
4. **Coat gently:** Return all eggplant to the pan with the 120 ml sauce and optional initial amount of chili paste. Fold gently over medium heat for about 1–2 minutes until bubbling and evenly coated. If using refrigerated sauce, check the finished dish reaches 165°F / 74°C. Thin a very tight coating with a tablespoon of hot water if needed.
5. **Finish:** Take off heat, fold in scallions and taste. Add optional vinegar or the additional chili-paste allowance only if wanted. Divide into four vegetable sides with rice and a separate main or protein component.

RECIPE: Elderberry Syrup (elderberry-syrup.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/elderberry-syrup/
SOURCE: Adapted from Wellnessmama.com
SOURCE_URL: https://wellnessmama.com/1888/elderberry-syrup/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2/3 cup Dried Black Elderberries
  - 3 1/2 cups Water
  - 2 tbsp Fresh Ginger, minced
  - 1 tsp Ground Cinnamon
  - 1/2 tsp Whole Cloves
  - 1 cup Raw Honey (Local preferred)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This spiced elderberry-and-honey syrup is a culinary preparation. Use food-grade dried ripe elderberries and follow their cooking instructions; raw or unripe berries and other plant parts can cause illness. Do not treat it as a medicine or a shelf-stable preserve. Freeze the finished syrup in small portions for storage, and do not serve honey-containing syrup to children under 12 months.

## Directions

1.  **Concentrate:** In a medium saucepan, combine water, elderberries, ginger, cinnamon, and cloves.
2.  **Simmer:** Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover. Simmer for 45-60 minutes until the liquid has reduced by half.
3.  **Mash:** Remove from heat. Use a flat utensil or potato masher to crush the berries, releasing any remaining juice.
4.  **Strain:** Pour the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth into a clean glass jar. Press firmly on the solids. Discard the berries.
5.  **Sweeten:** Let the liquid cool until it is lukewarm (below 110°F). Stir in the raw honey until completely dissolved and integrated.
6.  **Freeze for storage:** Cool promptly in small, clean containers and freeze in portions suitable for later use, leaving freezer-safe headspace. Thaw only the portion needed in the refrigerator. Do not can this syrup or try to make it shelf-stable by adding alcohol or citric acid.
7.  **Serve as a food:** Use a little for flavor in a drink or with food if desired. This homemade syrup has no established standard medicinal dose for children or adults.

RECIPE: Elote-Style Corn on the Cob (elote-style-corn-on-the-cob.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/elote-style-corn-on-the-cob/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Corn ---
  - 4 ears of fresh corn, husked and silk removed
  - --- Cream coating ---
  - 3 tbsp Mexican crema or sour cream
  - 1 tbsp milk, only for the sour-cream alternative, optional
  - 1/4 tsp kosher salt
  - black pepper, a pinch, to taste
  - --- Topping and wedges ---
  - 1/2 cup queso fresco, crumbled
  - 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, washed, dried and chopped
  - 1/2 tsp chili powder or chile-lime seasoning
  - 1 lime, washed and cut into wedges
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This elote-style version uses crema, queso fresco, cilantro and chile seasoning. Coat the cooked ears while warm so the cheese adheres. Check for tender kernels as well as charred spots; the heat source and ear size determine the actual time.

## Directions

1. **Cook the corn:** Pat ears of fresh corn dry after husking. Preheat the actual grill or broiler according to its instructions. For the broiler route, arrange ears in one layer on a foil-lined broiler-safe sheet, about 4–6 inches from the heat if the appliance permits, then broil, turning every 2–3 minutes. For the grill route, put ears directly on clean hot grates and turn every 2–3 minutes. Start checking around 8–10 minutes: kernels should be tender with browned spots. Continue or move away from intense heat if color develops before tenderness; more ears need uncrowded batches.
2. **Mix the coating:** Mix Mexican crema or sour cream, milk (if using), kosher salt, and black pepper in a clean bowl: use either the listed crema alone, or the same listed sour-cream amount with all the optional milk. Add all the measured salt and the pepper allowance. Refrigerate this coating while the corn cooks.
3. **Coat and top:** Let the cooked ears cool just enough to handle with tongs or corn holders. Brush all the coating across the ears over a shallow dish to catch drips. Distribute the full listed amounts of queso fresco, fresh cilantro, and chili powder or chile-lime seasoning over the cooked ears, turning to coat the sides. The cheese and coating remain separate from raw-food-contact utensils.
4. **Serve:** Serve warm with lime wedges for diners to squeeze as desired. Keep any unused coating and topped leftovers refrigerated promptly.

RECIPE: Enchiladas Suizas (enchiladas-suizas.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/enchiladas-suizas/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Shredded Chicken (Poached or Rotisserie)
  - 12 Corn Tortillas
  - 1 lb Tomatillos, husked and rinsed
  - 2 Jalapeños or Serranos
  - 1 white Onion, quartered
  - 3 cloves Garlic
  - 1/2 cup Heavy Cream (The "Suiza" secret)
  - 1/2 cup Fresh Cilantro
  - 8 oz Monterey Jack or Chihuahua Cheese, shredded
  - Pickled Red Onions (for garnish)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Enchiladas Suizas (Swiss-style) refers to the generous use of cream and cheese, a style that originated in Mexico City in the 1950s. The dish balances tart, roasted tomatillos with rich heavy cream. Briefly frying tortillas in oil for 10 seconds before filling creates a protective layer that prevents them from dissolving under the wet sauce.
For kids, serve the heat on the side or reduce/omit the spicy elements.

## Directions

1.  **Roast:** Place tomatillos, jalapeños, onion, and garlic on a baking sheet. Broil for 5-7 minutes until charred and softened.
2.  **Blend:** Place the roasted veg in a blender with the cilantro and heavy cream. Blend until smooth. Season with salt.
3.  **Prep Tortillas:** Heat 1/4 inch of oil in a small skillet. Dip each tortilla in the oil for 5-10 seconds per side (until pliable but not crisp). Drain on paper towels.
4.  **Assemble:** Dip a tortilla in the green sauce, fill with shredded chicken and a sprinkle of cheese, and roll tightly. Place in a baking dish.
5.  **Bake:** Pour the remaining sauce over the top and cover with the rest of the cheese. Bake at 375°F for 15-20 minutes until the cheese is bubbling.
6.  **Finish:** Top with pickled red onions and fresh cilantro.

RECIPE: Everyday Arugula Salad (everyday-arugula-salad.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/everyday-arugula-salad/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 5 oz (142 g) baby arugula
  - 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 20 g Parmesan, shaved (about 1/3 cup loose shavings)
  - 1/8 tsp fine salt, plus more only if needed
  - 1/8 tsp freshly ground black pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Lemon and peppery arugula provide a lively counterpoint to a breaded cutlet, buttery pasta, or pan sauce. The dressing is deliberately sharp, at two parts oil to one part lemon juice. Start with most of it and judge the coated leaves before adding the rest; leaf size and dryness affect how much is needed.

RECIPE: Extraordinary Chocolate Chip Cookie (extraordinary-chocolate-chip-cookie.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/extraordinary-chocolate-chip-cookie/
SOURCE: Adapted from pbs.org
SOURCE_URL: https://www.pbs.org/food/features/martha-bakes-north-american-cookies/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 1/4 cups (2 1/2 sticks) Unsalted Butter, room temp
  - 1 1/4 cups Dark Brown Sugar, packed
  - 3/4 cup Granulated Sugar
  - 2 large Eggs, room temp
  - 1 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - 2 3/4 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 1 1/4 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1 tsp Baking Powder
  - 1 tsp Baking Soda
  - 4 1/2 cups Semisweet Chocolate Chips
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This dough has a large chocolate-chip filling and can be baked as soon as it is mixed. A refrigerated rest is optional. Cream the softened butter and sugars until pale and fluffy, then finish mixing as soon as the flour and chips are evenly incorporated.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and dry mix:** For immediate baking, start preheating the oven to 350°F before mixing. Whisk the flour, kosher salt, baking powder and baking soda together. For the refrigerated route, preheat near baking time instead.

2. **Cream:** With a paddle attachment, beat the softened butter and both sugars on medium speed until pale and fluffy, about 4 minutes. Scrape the bowl, then beat in the eggs one at a time and mix in the vanilla.

3. **Combine:** On low speed, add the dry ingredients just until no flour pockets remain. Fold in all the chocolate chips until evenly distributed.

4. **Choose the rest:** Bake the dough now, or cover and refrigerate it overnight. A longer 24–36-hour refrigerated rest is another option, not a requirement. Keep any rested dough covered at 40°F / 4°C or below.

5. **Portion:** Preheat the oven to 350°F if it is not already heating, and line sheets with parchment. Use a 2 1/4-inch scoop and leave 3 inches between portions. Keep waiting dough covered and refrigerated and use additional sheets or loads rather than crowding.

6. **Bake:** Load only when the oven reaches 350°F. Bake for 15–17 minutes per tray, until the edges are golden brown and the centers are set but still soft. For chilled dough, begin checking in the same window and continue as the actual cookies need.

7. **Cool:** Let the cookies sit on the sheet for 5 minutes, then carefully transfer them to a rack to cool completely. Allow the sheet to cool before loading more dough.

RECIPE: Falafel (falafel.md)
CUISINES: Middle Eastern
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/falafel/
SOURCE: Adapted from Einat Admony
SOURCE_URL: https://www.kcet.org/food/falafel-by-einat-admony
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups (400 g) dried chickpeas, sorted and rinsed; weigh before soaking
  - 10 cups (2.4 L) cold water for soaking, plus more if needed to keep the chickpeas covered
  - 1 cup (30 g) fresh parsley leaves and tender stems, washed and thoroughly dried
  - 1 cup (30 g) fresh cilantro leaves and tender stems, washed and thoroughly dried
  - 1 small yellow onion (120 g peeled), roughly chopped
  - 4 medium garlic cloves, peeled and roughly chopped
  - 1 tbsp cumin seeds
  - 1 tbsp coriander seeds
  - 1 tsp double-acting baking powder
  - 6 g salt, weighed (about 1 tsp fine salt), plus up to 3 g more only after tasting a fried test piece
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
  - Refined canola or sunflower oil for frying: about 8 cups (1.9 L), with the actual amount set by pot width and required depth
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This herb-heavy chickpea falafel is served with bread, sesame sauce, and fresh vegetables in many Middle Eastern meals. Soaking supplies water to the chickpeas; frying supplies heat to cook their moist centers while the surface dries into a crust. Grind finely enough for the mixture to hold a small portion, then fry one test piece to check both crust and center.

## Directions

1. **Soak ahead:** Put the sorted and rinsed dried chickpeas in a large bowl with the soaking water. Cover and refrigerate for 12–24 hours, allowing plenty of room for expansion and adding water if needed to keep them covered. Drain and rinse. The beans should be plump and hydrated but still firm; do not boil them. Cut open a few: the inside should be evenly hydrated rather than showing a hard, dry core. If needed, continue the refrigerated soak within the stated twenty-four-hour window. Spread on a clean towel and blot away surface water.
2. **Prepare herbs and spices:** Wash and thoroughly dry the herbs, then roughly chop them. Put cumin and coriander seeds in a small dry skillet over medium-low heat. Stir for about 1–2 minutes, until fragrant but not smoking or blackened. Tip out promptly, cool, and grind finely. Peel and roughly chop onion and garlic.
3. **Grind in batches:** Put chickpeas, herbs, onion, and garlic in the processor. Divide the chickpeas, herbs, onion and garlic evenly between processor batches if needed, so the bottom does not become paste while the top stays coarse. Pulse, stopping to scrape, until finely and evenly chopped with no large chickpea fragments. A spoonful pressed between your palms should hold a rough mound. Combine all processor batches in a large bowl.
4. **Season and chill:** Mix in the ground toasted spices, baking powder, measured salt, and pepper evenly. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes. The rest makes the mixture easier to handle; it does not cook the chickpeas. Season by tasting a cooked test piece in step 6, rather than the raw mixture.
5. **Prepare one test portion:** After chilling, weigh one 25 g portion and press gently into a small ball, closing large cracks without compressing it into a hard lump. About 1 1/2 inches across is a guide; weight governs if the two differ. Keep the remaining mixture covered and refrigerated while the oil heats.
6. **Heat, test and adjust:** Set a wire rack over a rimmed sheet. Add oil to the deep pot to a two-inch depth with at least three inches of clear space above it. Heat to 350°F / 175°C under supervision, with the thermometer sensing in the oil rather than against the pot bottom. Lower the test with a dry metal slotted spoon. Fry about four to five minutes, turning as needed, until evenly brown. Drain on the rack, turn off the burner and leave the stable pot in place. Stay nearby while the test cools enough to split and taste: its center should be tender and finely crumbed, without hard fragments or dense wet paste. Add some of the reserved salt to the remaining mixture only if the test needs it. Correct any breakup or undercooked center and fry another test before shaping the rest; do not carry the hot oil pot to another work area.
7. **Shape the remaining batch:** With the burner off and the pot undisturbed, shape 25 g portions at an adjacent clear work surface away from the oil. Stay in the kitchen with the pot in view and keep splashing water away. Expect about forty to forty-five pieces in total, depending on hydration; close cracks gently. Refrigerate the shaped portions while bringing the oil back to 350°F / 175°C, allowing another five to ten minutes.
8. **Fry in small batches:** Cook five or six pieces at a time for about four to five minutes, turning for even color. Monitor the oil and reduce the next load if its temperature drops sharply or recovers slowly. Let it return to 350°F between rounds and skim loose crumbs. Check another center when batch size or browning changes. Keep waiting portions refrigerated, drain cooked pieces in one layer, and serve successive batches promptly. After the final round, turn off the burner and let the oil cool in place before handling or disposal.
9. **Serve with accompaniments:** Divide the actual batch among six diners, usually six or seven small falafel each, sharing extras; an eaten test piece reduces the number for the table. Offer about two tablespoons tahini sauce each, or three-quarters of a cup total, plus warm pita and vegetables. Six pocket breads require more warming rounds than the linked four-bread recipe. For six generous fattoush sides, make one and a half batches of that recipe, including its separately counted crisp pita; account for that bread alongside the pocket breads. Hummus can be a small optional dip. These accompaniments are additional recipes and time.

## Serving successive batches

This home-pot method produces hot falafel in successive rounds. Set out the cold sauce and prepared vegetables first; a second cook can warm pita as rounds arrive, or serve the bread at room temperature. Pita warmed before the first fry will not stay freshly warm through the whole batch. A simultaneous plated dinner needs a separate holding plan and the early falafel will lose some fresh-fried texture; all forty-plus pieces do not finish together.

RECIPE: Farfel Muffins (farfel-muffins.md)
CUISINES: Jewish
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/farfel-muffins/
SOURCE: Adapted from Jodi Silton
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 cups Matzo Farfel
  - 2 cups Boiling Water
  - 5 tbsp Unsalted Butter, melted
  - 4 large Eggs
  - 1 tsp Kosher Salt (or to taste)
  - Butter or baking spray, as needed to grease muffin cups
  - Salted butter, as desired for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Jodi Silton’s farfel muffins start by hydrating the matzo pieces, then cooling them before adding butter and eggs one at a time. Keep the full butter amount and serve warm. Matzo farfel is broken matzo, not toasted egg barley.

## Directions

1. **Hydrate and cool:** Preheat the oven to 400°F. Pour all the boiling water over all the matzo farfel in a heatproof bowl and stir to moisten evenly. Let hydrate and cool until the mixture is only mildly warm, so it will not cook eggs on contact. Grease enough muffin cups with the separate pan allowance while it cools.
2. **Mix:** Stir in all the measured melted butter, cooled if still very hot. Add all the eggs one at a time, mixing thoroughly after each, then mix in the listed kosher salt. Do not taste raw egg batter.
3. **Fill:** Divide all batter among the greased cups about three-quarters full, using enough cups to preserve similar fill depth. The source plans 8 muffins for its original batch but does not name the cup size; use actual capacity rather than forcing overflow or a fixed count at every scale.
4. **Bake:** Bake about 20 minutes as a first check, until golden and the centers are set without wet egg mixture. Check representative center muffins reach 160°F /71°C with a thin probe, keeping it away from the pan. Additional tins or different cup sizes can change the clock.
5. **Serve:** Let stand briefly until they can be lifted without breaking, and serve warm with optional salted butter.

## Cooking Notes

The batch doubles well. Divide among enough muffin tins to keep the same fill depth, and serve warm.

RECIPE: Fattoush Salad (fattoush-salad.md)
CUISINES: Middle Eastern
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/fattoush-salad/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 120 g pita bread, split into thin layers and torn into bite-sized pieces
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, for the pita
  - 1 tsp ground sumac, for the pita
  - 400 g ripe tomatoes, cut into bite-sized pieces
  - 200 g Persian or English cucumber, sliced
  - 100 g radishes, thinly sliced
  - 4 scallions, thinly sliced
  - 1 cup loosely packed parsley leaves, roughly chopped
  - 1/2 cup loosely packed mint leaves, torn
  - 150 g romaine or Little Gem lettuce, washed and dried, then torn
  - 3 tbsp olive oil, for the dressing
  - 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus up to 1 tbsp more to taste
  - 1 tbsp pomegranate molasses
  - 1 small clove garlic, finely grated
  - 1 tsp ground sumac, for the dressing
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt
  - 1/4 tsp black pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Fattoush combines vegetables and herbs with pieces of bread and a tangy dressing. This version toasts the pita and adds it at the last moment for contrast. Sumac and pomegranate molasses already bring tartness, so the lemon is measured and adjusted after tasting. Softer bread is inevitable as it absorbs dressing; serving some pita separately extends the contrast.

## Directions

1. **Toast pita:** Heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Toss pita with its 2 tbsp oil and teaspoon of sumac. Spread in one layer on a rimmed sheet pan. Bake about 8–10 minutes, turning once, until golden and dry. Cool uncovered; thick pieces may need a little longer.
2. **Mix dressing:** Whisk the dressing oil, initial 2 tbsp lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, garlic, dressing sumac, salt, and pepper. Set aside the optional extra lemon.
3. **Prepare vegetables:** Combine tomatoes, cucumber, radishes, scallions, dry lettuce, parsley, and mint in a large bowl. Keep refrigerated if the meal is not ready.
4. **Dress and taste:** Just before serving, add about three-quarters of the dressing and toss gently. Taste a bite and add the rest only as needed. Add some of the reserved lemon if it needs more brightness.
5. **Add bread:** Fold in cooled pita just before dividing among four plates, or offer it separately for diners to add themselves. Serve promptly.

RECIPE: Cream Cheese Frosting (favorite-cream-cheese-frosting.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/favorite-cream-cheese-frosting/
SOURCE: Adapted from sallysbakingaddiction.com
SOURCE_URL: https://sallysbakingaddiction.com/favorite-cream-cheese-frosting/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 8 oz Full-fat Block Cream Cheese, softened
  - 1/2 cup (1 stick) Unsalted Butter, softened
  - 3 cups Confectioners’ Sugar
  - 1 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - 1/8 tsp Sea Salt (The Finishing Touch)
  - 1/4 cup additional Confectioners’ Sugar, optional for a thicker frosting
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Use full-fat block cream cheese rather than tub spread. Softened butter and cream cheese should blend smoothly, but neither needs an exact matching temperature. Start the sugar on low speed, then beat until creamy; cream cheese frosting is softer than buttercream and does not promise stiff, intricate piping.

## Directions

1. **Blend:** In a large bowl, beat all the softened cream cheese and butter until smooth and creamy. Use a stand mixer with paddle or whisk, or a handheld mixer. Scrape the bowl and use smoothness rather than an exact two-minute promise.
2. **Add sugar:** On low speed, add all the main confectioners’ sugar, vanilla and salt. Beat about 30 seconds until the sugar is incorporated, then increase speed and beat about 2 minutes or until creamy, scraping as needed.
3. **Adjust:** If a thicker frosting is desired, beat in the separate listed optional extra sugar, not a second main sugar supply. If piping, the publisher suggests chilling the filled piping bag about 20–30 minutes; keep to simple shapes rather than expecting buttercream stiffness.
4. **Use or store:** Frost only completely cooled baked goods. Cover and refrigerate unused frosting promptly. After chilling or refrigerator thawing, allow only brief softening as needed and beat for a few seconds to restore a creamy consistency; keep this time within the cumulative cold-handling limits below.

## Cooking Notes

For taller carrot or red velvet cakes, use the complete frosting formula in that cake recipe. Sally McKenney’s chocolate cream cheese frosting is a separate recipe with its own ingredient amounts and method.

RECIPE: Pumpkin Oatmeal Muffins (favorite-pumpkin-oatmeal-muffins.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/favorite-pumpkin-oatmeal-muffins/
SOURCE: Adapted from yummytoddlerfood.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.yummytoddlerfood.com/pumpkin-oatmeal-muffins/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups Rolled Oats
  - 1 cup Pure Pumpkin Puree
  - 1 cup Milk of choice (Soy or Almond preferred)
  - 1/3 cup Maple Syrup
  - 2 large Eggs
  - 1 tsp Pumpkin Pie Spice
  - 1 tsp Baking Soda
  - 1/4 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1 tsp Vanilla Extract
  - 1/4 cup Dark Chocolate Chips
  - Butter or baking spray, as needed for greasing if not using silicone liners
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Blend rolled oats with the pumpkin and wet ingredients until the oats are finely broken down. These are moist oat muffins: check that the center is set, and move them from the pan to a rack before storing.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 375°F. Grease a standard 12-cup muffin tin with the pan allowance, or use silicone liners. Use plain pumpkin puree, not sweetened pie filling; homemade puree should be cooled before mixing with eggs or loading a blender.

2. **Blend:** Combine rolled oats, pumpkin puree, milk, maple syrup, eggs, pumpkin pie spice, baking soda, vanilla and salt in a blender or food processor. Keep the chocolate chips out for topping. Follow the appliance’s actual capacity and loading instructions; divide a larger batch into proportionate loads if needed.

3. **Continue blending:** Blend until the oats are finely broken down and the batter is smooth, stopping and scraping with the appliance off as needed. Stop when no coarse oat flakes remain; blending time varies with the appliance and load.

4. **Fill:** Fill the prepared cups no more than ¾ full and distribute all the listed chocolate chips over the tops. Bake excess batter in additional cups or a later batch.

5. **Bake:** Bake for 20–22 minutes, until the tops are firm, the edges lightly golden and a center tester comes out without wet batter.

6. **Cool:** Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack. Serve warm, at room temperature or chilled; cool completely before sealing for storage.

7. **Store:** Refrigerate cooled muffins promptly at 40°F / 4°C or below, within 2 hours of baking or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C; use within 3–4 days. Freeze cooled muffins airtight for up to 3 months for quality, and thaw portions in the refrigerator.

## Cooking Notes

For a honey variation, replace the listed maple syrup with the same volume of honey; do not serve honey-containing muffins to children under one year. For stronger spice, double the listed pumpkin pie spice (2 tsp in the original 12-muffin batch). Chocolate chips may be omitted for the separate plain version. For the dairy-free option, use plain unsweetened nondairy milk and dairy-free chocolate chips if including the topping; choose silicone liners or a dairy-free baking spray rather than butter for the pan. Use certified gluten-free oats when needed.

For mini muffins, start checking around 12–14 minutes and use the same center-doneness cues; the written 12 count refers to standard muffins, not mini yield. A store-bought egg replacer can be used according to its own instructions for the listed egg count, with a different crumb and checking time. Serve smaller pieces to younger children.

RECIPE: Fennel and Carrot Soup (fennel-and-carrot-soup.md)
CUISINES: Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/fennel-and-carrot-soup/
SOURCE: Adapted from Bonappetit.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/fennel-and-carrot-soup
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 Carrots, peeled and chopped
  - 1 large Fennel Bulb, thinly sliced
  - 1 small Yellow Onion, thinly sliced
  - 1 small Yukon Gold Potato, peeled and halved
  - 6 tbsp Unsalted Butter (divided)
  - 4 cups Low-sodium Vegetable Broth
  - 2 sprigs Fresh Thyme
  - 1 Fresh Bay Leaf
  - 1/4 cup Roasted Chestnuts, chopped
  - 1/4 cup Crème Fraîche
  - 1 tbsp Pure Maple Syrup
  - Salt and Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Cook the covered vegetables gently until soft without browning, then simmer until the potato falls apart. The potato gives the purée body. Two-thirds of the butter cook the vegetables; the remaining third browns with the roasted chestnuts. Keep the maple crème fraîche separate until serving.

## Directions

1. **Sweat:** Wash the fennel, carrots, potato and thyme before trimming or peeling. In a large heavy pot, melt two-thirds of the butter over medium heat. Add sliced fennel and onion, chopped carrots, halved potato, thyme and bay leaf. Season with the listed salt and pepper. Use a pot with room for the vegetables, broth and stirring.
2. **Soften:** Reduce heat to medium-low, cover and cook for 45–60 minutes, stirring occasionally and reducing heat if needed. The vegetables should become very soft without browning; the clock is a guide to that texture.
3. **Simmer:** Add all the broth. Bring to a boil, season with salt and pepper as needed, then reduce heat and simmer about 8–10 minutes, until the potato is falling apart. Remove the thyme stems and bay leaf.
4. **Purée:** Take the pot off the heat. Use an immersion blender approved for this load, keeping its head submerged and switching it off before lifting it. For a countertop blender, use only a model approved for hot liquids and follow its temperature, fill, lid and venting instructions; work in batches. If your model requires cold ingredients, cool promptly in shallow containers before blending, then reheat the soup. Never seal hot soup in a personal blending cup. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot if desired, then taste with the listed salt and pepper.
5. **Brown chestnuts:** In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt the remaining one-third of the butter. Add all the chopped roasted chestnuts and cook, stirring often, for about 4 minutes until the butter smells nutty and the chestnuts toast. Remove from the heat before the butter blackens.
6. **Mix maple cream:** Whisk all the crème fraîche and maple syrup together.
7. **Serve:** Ladle the soup into bowls. Distribute all the maple cream and brown-butter chestnuts over the soup.

RECIPE: Flourless Chocolate Cake (flourless-chocolate-cake.md)
CUISINES: French
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/flourless-chocolate-cake/
SOURCE: Adapted from kingarthurbaking.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2008/04/10/flour-takes-a-passover-break-and-chocolate-steps-into-the-breach
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup Semisweet or Bittersweet Chocolate Chips (for the batter)
  - 1/2 cup (1 stick) Unsalted Butter
  - 3/4 cup Granulated Sugar
  - 1/2 cup Cocoa Powder, sifted
  - 3 large Eggs
  - 2 tsp Espresso Powder (The complex flavor)
  - 1 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - 1/4 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1 cup Semisweet Chocolate Chips (for the glaze)
  - 1/2 cup Heavy Cream
  - Butter, as needed to grease the pan and parchment
  - Whipped cream or ice cream, as desired for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This flourless cake is dense and fudgy beneath the full chocolate-and-cream glaze. Espresso at the listed dose can lend a hint of mocha. Let the cake cool completely before glazing, and let the ganache set before slicing. Its Passover context comes from the source; choose ingredients suitable for the dietary requirements of the people you are serving.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 375°F. For the original batch, grease an 8-inch round pan, line its bottom with parchment and grease the parchment with the separate pan-butter allowance.
2. **Melt:** Melt all the cake chocolate and the full measured butter in a microwave-safe bowl in short bursts, stirring between them, until smooth. Start with the existing 30-second bursts and shorten as it melts; do not scorch the chocolate. A very-low-heat burner is the source alternative.
3. **Mix:** Stir in all the sugar, salt, espresso powder and vanilla. When the mixture is warm rather than hot enough to cook eggs on contact, add all the eggs one at a time, beating briefly until smooth. Mix in all the sifted cocoa only until combined; do not taste raw batter.
4. **Bake:** Spoon all the batter into the prepared pan. Bake about 25 minutes as a first check. Look for the thin crust, moist crumbs on a tester and at least 200°F in the center, as the source specifies. A dark pan may reach these cues earlier. At other scales, divide the whole batter among appropriate pans before baking; no fixed-pan or linear-time claim is made.
5. **Cool:** Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, loosen the edges and invert onto a plate. A little edge crumbling can happen. Cool completely before glazing.
6. **Glaze:** Heat all the cream until steaming, then pour it over all the separate glaze chocolate. Let stand about 5 minutes and stir gently until smooth. If needed, warm briefly and stir rather than adding unlisted cream. Keep water out of the chocolate bowl.
7. **Finish:** Pour all the glaze over the cool cake and spread to the edges, letting it drip down the sides. Allow it to set before slicing. Use a knife dipped in hot water and wiped dry between slices. Serve plain or with the optional whipped cream or ice cream.

RECIPE: Soft Scrambled Eggs (fluffy-scrambled-eggs.md)
CUISINES: French
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/fluffy-scrambled-eggs/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6 large eggs
  - 2 tbsp (28 g) unsalted butter
  - 1 tbsp crème fraîche or sour cream
  - 1/8 tsp fine salt, plus more to taste
  - Freshly ground black pepper
  - 1 tbsp finely snipped chives
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

French-style soft scrambled eggs use gentle heat and frequent stirring to make small curds. Heat unfolds proteins and helps them join into a network; too much heat tightens that network and makes the eggs dry. Butter and crème fraîche add richness, but neither instantly stops the cooking, so transfer the finished eggs out of the hot pan.

## Directions

1. **Whisk:** Beat the eggs and salt in a bowl until the whites and yolks are fully combined. Melt butter in a nonstick skillet over low to medium-low heat; it should foam gently without browning.
2. **Stir gently:** Add eggs and continuously sweep a flexible spatula across the bottom and sides. As small curds form, keep folding them through the liquid. If the eggs set rapidly or stick in a dry layer, lift the pan off the heat briefly and lower the burner. Expect about 5–7 minutes, depending on the pan.
3. **Finish cooking:** Stir in the crème fraîche when most of the eggs have formed curds. Continue gently until the eggs are set with no liquid egg pooling and reach 160°F / 71°C. Measure in the eggs without touching the pan. The curds can remain moist without being runny.
4. **Serve promptly:** Transfer to plates immediately. Taste and adjust salt and pepper, then add chives. The hot pan would continue to firm the eggs if you left them in it.

RECIPE: Freezer Banana Bread (freezer-banana-bread.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/freezer-banana-bread/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 medium Ripe Bananas, mashed
  - 1 3/4 cups Whole-Wheat Flour
  - 1/4 cup Maple Syrup
  - 1 large Egg
  - 1/2 cup Plain Greek Yogurt
  - 1/3 cup Milk of choice
  - 1 tsp Ground Cinnamon
  - 1 tsp Baking Powder
  - 1/2 tsp Baking Soda
  - 1 tsp Vanilla Extract
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This banana bread is designed for freezer storage. The key to a perfect slice every morning is using Greek yogurt instead of butter to create a dense, moist texture that survives the freezing process without becoming crumbly. We blend the bananas and wet ingredients in a blender to create a smooth mixture before folding in the flour - this ensures even distribution of sweetness and prevents mushy pockets.

## Directions

1.  **The Emulsion:** Preheat oven to 350°F. In a blender, combine bananas, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, egg, yogurt, and milk. Blend on high for 30 seconds until perfectly smooth.
2.  **Dry Mix:** In a large bowl, whisk together the whole-wheat flour, baking soda, and baking powder.
3.  **Combine:** Pour the wet ingredients into the dry. Stir with a spatula until **just combined** (do not over-mix, or the whole-wheat will turn tough).
4.  **Bake:** Pour into a greased loaf pan. Bake for 50-55 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
5.  **Cool:** Let cool in the pan for 15 minutes before slicing.
6.  **The Freeze:** To store, slice the loaf into 1/2-inch rounds. Place parchment between slices and freeze in a zip-top bag. Reheat individual slices in the toaster for a Crunch finish.

RECIPE: Freezer Date Cookies (freezer-date-cookies.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/freezer-date-cookies/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Date cookie dough ---
  - 1 cup Medjool dates, pitted
  - 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted, then cooled until only mildly warm
  - 1 large egg
  - 1/4 cup plain Greek yogurt
  - 1 tsp vanilla extract
  - 1/3 cup buckwheat flour
  - 2/3 cup white whole wheat flour
  - 1 cup quick oats
  - 1/2 tsp baking soda
  - 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
  - sea salt, a pinch
  - --- Pan preparation ---
  - butter or baking spray, enough to lightly grease cookie sheets
  - --- Other-date option only ---
  - hot water, enough to soak other types of dates if that option is chosen, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The dates supply the sweetness, with the full butter, egg and Greek yogurt forming the wet mixture. Blend that mixture evenly, then stir it into the two flours and quick oats. Freezing is a make-ahead route; the actual cold texture depends on the dates and how the cookies were baked.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 350°F. Have butter or baking spray and hot water (if using) ready: lightly grease cookie sheets with the fat or spray. The optional hot water is only for the other-date option; pit and measure the full listed date volume first, soak those dates until soft, then drain before making the paste. Follow the food processor’s actual loading and temperature instructions, and let the melted butter become only mildly warm before it will meet the egg.
2. **Make date paste:** Process Medjool dates and unsalted butter until a smooth, thick paste forms, stopping and scraping as needed. Work within the processor’s capacity; split a larger batch proportionally into complete dough batches rather than overfilling it.
3. **Mix wet ingredients:** Add large egg, plain Greek yogurt, and vanilla extract and process until evenly mixed, stopping to scrape as needed. Stop when the mixture is uniform, without unmixed egg or yogurt.
4. **Mix dry ingredients:** Whisk buckwheat flour, white whole wheat flour, quick oats, baking soda, ground cinnamon, and sea salt together in a mixing bowl, including the pinch of salt.
5. **Combine:** Stir the date mixture into the dry ingredients until a thick, sticky dough forms and no dry flour remains.
6. **Shape:** Use all the dough in small balls, about 1 tbsp each, and press them into ½-inch-thick disks on the prepared sheets, leaving room between them. The listed cookie count is a planning value; tablespoon portions may give a different number. Keep portion size and thickness consistent and use more sheets and oven loads when scaling.
7. **Bake:** Wait for the oven to reach 350°F, then bake for 12–15 minutes per load until the edges are lightly browned and the centers are set, not wet dough. Keep remaining raw dough refrigerated at 40°F / 4°C or below between loads.
8. **Cool and freeze:** Cool the baked cookies completely on a rack, then pack airtight in a freezer bag or container and label the date. Freeze at 0°F / −18°C or below; avoid trapping steam in the package. If staging cooled cookies before freezing, keep them refrigerated at 40°F / 4°C or below rather than leaving them out. They can be eaten cold from the freezer if comfortably chewable, or thawed covered in the refrigerator; cold texture varies with the dates and bake.

## Cooking Options

### Other dates

Other types of dates may replace the same listed volume of Medjool dates. Pit and measure the full listed date amount, then soak in hot water until soft and drain before processing; the soaking water is separate from the dough. Date size and moisture can change paste consistency and cookie texture, so use the same disk thickness and check that the baked centers are set. No soaking time or additional dough liquid is specified.

RECIPE: Slow Cooker French Dip Sandwiches (french-dip-sandwiches.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/french-dip-sandwiches/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 lb Beef Chuck Roast
  - 1 large Yellow Onion, sliced
  - 4 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 2 cups Beef Stock (Low sodium)
  - 1/2 cup Soy Sauce (The umami secret)
  - 1 tbsp Worcestershire Sauce
  - 1 tsp Dried Rosemary
  - 6 Hoagie Rolls or Baguette pieces
  - 6 slices Provolone Cheese
  - Oil, as needed for optional searing
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Chuck needs time to become easy to pull apart. The broth, soy sauce, Worcestershire and rosemary make the dipping liquid; keep all their measured quantities. Searing is optional and adds browned flavor when there is time. Assemble and broil close to serving so the bread stays firm enough for dipping.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and optionally sear:** Start with fully thawed beef, kept refrigerated until preparation. Check the cooker’s capacity and meat-size instructions. If searing, brown the roast on all sides in a hot skillet with the optional oil allowance, then transfer immediately to the cooker to continue cooking. Otherwise place the roast directly in the cooker.

2. **Combine:** Add all the sliced onion, garlic, measured stock, soy sauce, Worcestershire and rosemary. Cover and start cooking promptly; do not use a delayed start.

3. **Cook until tender:** Cook on LOW for about 8 hours or HIGH for about 4–5 hours as planning ranges, until the beef pulls apart with a fork. Check that the roast has reached at least 145°F / 63°C with a three-minute rest before serving; shreddable chuck usually needs substantially more cooking than that minimum. Continue if it remains tough.

4. **Shred and strain:** Remove the cooked beef to a clean board and shred into large chunks, or slice thinly if preferred. Strain the cooking liquid into a heatproof vessel and keep it hot for dipping. The softened onions can be served with the beef if wanted rather than discarded automatically.

5. **Assemble and broil:** Split the listed rolls or baguette pieces and distribute the beef and measured provolone among them. Put them on a broiler-safe pan, keeping within the actual oven instructions. Broil about 1–2 minutes as a first check, watching continuously until the cheese bubbles and the bread toasts; remove individual sandwiches if ready sooner.

6. **Serve:** Divide the hot jus among individual dipping bowls and serve promptly.

## Cooking Notes

Check the actual cooker’s instructions for its permitted food load, liquid requirements and meat size. Follow your cooker’s stated minimum and maximum fill limits. When scaling, choose suitable cooker capacity or separate appropriately filled cookers, and divide all measured ingredients across them. Cooking times do not multiply with portions. Keep the lid closed except for necessary additions and doneness checks; cook on LOW or HIGH, not WARM.

Refrigerate promptly in shallow covered containers at 40°F / 4°C or below, within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C). Use within 3–4 days. Reheat on the stove, in the microwave or oven outside the slow cooker, stirring or turning as appropriate for even heating and checking 165°F / 74°C throughout; do not use the slow cooker to reheat cold leftovers. For leftover jus, USDA additionally recommends bringing it to a rolling boil; stir and keep the boil brief, since prolonged boiling concentrates the jus. If holding cooked food in the cooker, maintain at least 140°F / 60°C and follow its holding instructions.

RECIPE: French Toast (french-toast.md)
CUISINES: French
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/french-toast/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodnetwork.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/robert-irvine/french-toast-recipe-1951408
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- French toast ---
  - 8 slices of challah or brioche, day-old preferred; slice size stays fixed when count scales
  - 4 large eggs
  - 1/4 cup whole milk
  - 2 tbsp honey, warmed gently until fluid
  - 4 tbsp unsalted butter
  - 1 tsp ground cinnamon
  - 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
  - 1/2 tsp pure vanilla extract
  - 1/2 cup maple syrup, warmed
  - fresh berries, as wanted for serving, washed and drained, optional
  - additional maple syrup, as wanted for serving, warmed, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Keep the full honey custard and all the pan butter. A brief dip suits this low-milk formula, but bread texture controls absorption; lift a slice while it still holds its shape. Browning should accompany a cooked center. Serve with all the listed warm syrup, adding the separate optional berries or extra syrup if wanted.

## Directions

1. **Mix spices:** Stir honey, ground cinnamon, and ground nutmeg together until the spices are dispersed.
2. **Make custard:** Whisk large eggs, whole milk, and pure vanilla extract with all the honey-spice mixture in a shallow dish until no egg-white streaks remain.
3. **Dip:** Working in cooking-sized batches, dip slices of challah or brioche in the custard on both sides, starting with a few seconds per side. Check 160°F in the center of a thick slice with a food thermometer inserted from its edge; reduce the heat and continue gently if the outside browns first. Keep later bread-contact utensils away from finished toast. Discard unused bread-contact custard after cooking.
5. **Serve:** Divide maple syrup, fresh berries (if using), and additional maple syrup (if using) among the cooked slices and serve promptly. The measured syrup is separate from the honey in the custard; additional syrup and berries are optional finishes.

RECIPE: Fresh Cabbage, Cucumber and Radish Kimchi (fresh-cabbage-cucumber-and-radish-kimchi.md)
CUISINES: Korean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/fresh-cabbage-cucumber-and-radish-kimchi/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/fresh-cabbage-cucumber-and-radish-kimchi
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 lbs Napa Cabbage, halved and cut into 2-inch pieces
  - 3 English Cucumbers, sliced 1/3-inch thick
  - 1 1/4 lbs Daikon Radish, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
  - 20 Radishes, quartered
  - 1/2 cup Kosher Salt (for the cure)
  - 4 oz Fresh Ginger, coarsely chopped
  - 1/2 cup Gochugaru (Korean Red Chile Flakes)
  - 6 cloves Garlic, chopped
  - 1/4 cup + 2 tbsp Rice Vinegar (The Finishing Touch)
  - 3 tbsp Toasted Sesame Oil
  - 3 tbsp Fish Sauce
  - 2 Scallions, chopped
  - 3/4 tsp Sugar
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This is fresh kimchi ready to eat immediately. The key to crisp, non-watery kimchi is salting the vegetables heavily for an hour to draw out excess moisture that would otherwise dilute the spice paste. Using three vegetables - cabbage, cucumber, and daikon - ensures a complex texture in every bite. Always use gochugaru; the specific smoky heat is essential to authentic kimchi.

## Directions

1.  **The Cure:** In four separate large bowls, divide the cabbage, cucumbers, daikon, and radishes. Sprinkle 2 tbsp of salt into each bowl and toss well. **Let stand for 1 hour** at room temperature.
2.  **The Paste:** In a high-powered blender, combine ginger, garlic, gochugaru, rice vinegar, sesame oil, fish sauce, scallions, and sugar. Puree until almost smooth.
3.  **The Rinse:** Drain the vegetables thoroughly. Gently squeeze each handful to remove all remaining water.
4.  **The Bind:** In one massive bowl, toss all the vegetables with the kimchi paste until every piece is uniformly coated in the deep red glaze.
5.  **The Finish:** Transfer to glass jars. Cover and refrigerate for **at least 4 hours** (ideally 24) to allow the flavors to meld and the fermentation to begin.
6.  **Serve:** This fresh kimchi (Geotjeori style) is at its best within the first week.

RECIPE: Fresh Egg Pasta (fresh-egg-pasta.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/fresh-egg-pasta/
SOURCE: Adapted from Cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1017391-fresh-egg-pasta
INGREDIENTS:
  - 290 g all-purpose flour, plus a little for dusting
  - 2 large eggs
  - 3 large egg yolks
  - 1 tbsp olive oil
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, for the dough
  - 2 tbsp cool water, only as needed for the dough
  - 2 tbsp fine semolina or all-purpose flour, for dusting cut pasta
  - 4 quarts (3.8 liters) water, for cooking pasta
  - 1 tbsp fine salt, for the pasta water
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This dough keeps the original combination of whole eggs and extra yolks for a rich, flexible pasta. Flour weight establishes the starting ratio; a squeeze test and small water adjustments account for egg size and flour absorption. The dough should be firm, not wet like bread dough. Resting and gradual rolling make it easier to handle without excessive dusting flour.

## Directions

1. **Mix:** Pulse the measured flour and dough salt in a food processor. Beat eggs, yolks, and oil together, add, and pulse until evenly crumbly. Squeeze a small handful: if it holds together, stop. If it falls into dry crumbs, add the measured water a teaspoon at a time, pulsing briefly and checking again. You may not need all of it. Do not taste the raw mixture.
2. **Knead:** Tip onto a clean work surface and press together. Knead for about 5–8 minutes until firm and reasonably smooth. Use very little dusting flour. If still dry and cracked, knead with lightly damp hands; if tacky, dust sparingly.
3. **Rest covered:** Wrap tightly or place in a covered container so the surface cannot dry out. Rest for 1 hour at ordinary room temperature. Refrigerate instead if the kitchen is very hot or preparation will be delayed.
4. **Roll gradually:** Divide into four pieces and keep three covered. Flatten one piece, dust lightly, and pass through the roller's widest setting. Fold in thirds and repeat once or twice to form an even strip. Progress through narrower settings without skipping several at once, stopping at about 1 mm for fettuccine. Rest a resistant piece covered for 5–10 minutes rather than forcing it.
5. **Cut:** Let a tacky sheet sit just briefly until its surface no longer sticks, then cut into ribbons. Dust with the measured semolina or flour, shake off excess, and arrange in loose nests on a lined tray. Repeat with the remaining dough. Cook promptly, or refrigerate/freeze as described below.
6. **Boil and finish:** Bring the cooking water and its salt to a full boil. Add noodles, separating them gently, and cook until no floury center remains, generally 2–5 minutes depending on thickness and drying. Taste only after cooking. Reserve a little cooking water before draining, then combine promptly with the chosen sauce.

RECIPE: Pasta Dough (fresh-pasta-dough.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/fresh-pasta-dough/
SOURCE: Adapted from Bonappetit.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/fresh-pasta-dough
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups All-Purpose or "00" Flour
  - 3 large Eggs, lightly beaten
  - 1 tbsp Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 1 tsp Kosher Salt
  - Flour or semolina, as needed for dusting the work surface and roller
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This three-egg dough includes the full olive oil and kosher salt. Knead until smooth and elastic, then keep it covered during the rest and rolling. A piece that springs back benefits from another short covered rest; do not force it through a narrow roller gap.

## Directions

1. **Mix:** Place all the measured dough flour and salt in the stand-mixer bowl. Make a well and add all the beaten eggs and olive oil. Mix by hand until a shaggy dough forms; keep hands clear before starting the mixer.
2. **Knead:** Fit the dough hook and use the actual mixer’s recommended speed and dough capacity. Knead about 10 minutes, checking for a smooth, elastic dough. If kneading by hand, work until the same texture develops rather than treating the clock as a guarantee.
3. **Rest:** Wrap tightly and rest at least 30 minutes at ordinary room temperature. For advance preparation, wrap and refrigerate for up to 1 day; refrigerate sooner in a hot kitchen or if rolling is delayed. Do not taste raw dough.
4. **Roll:** Divide into manageable pieces and keep the others wrapped. Start at the roller’s widest setting, fold and pass through to form an even sheet, then narrow gradually, dusting only as needed. Machine numbers differ; stop at the thickness required for the chosen shape. See [Fresh Egg Pasta](/mise/recipes/fresh-egg-pasta) for rolling technique, using this recipe’s full formula rather than its different yolk-enriched formula.
5. **Shape and cook:** Cut or fill for the chosen pasta dish. Follow that dish’s cooking method and check for a cooked center without raw floury dough; filled pasta also needs its filling’s endpoint. This recipe’s zero cook time describes making the dough, not serving it raw.

RECIPE: Strawberry Vinaigrette (fresh-strawberry-vinaigrette-salad-dressing.md)
CUISINES: American

SOURCE: Adapted from Rachel at Grow a Good Life
SOURCE_URL: https://growagoodlife.com/strawberry-vinaigrette/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced
  - 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar
  - 1 tbsp honey
  - Salt and black pepper, to taste

## Chef's Note

Blended fruit gives this dressing body, while balsamic vinegar and honey balance its flavor. Give the sliced berries their rest before blending, then taste on the greens you intend to serve. RECIPE: Wonton Wrappers (fresh-wonton-wrappers.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/fresh-wonton-wrappers/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1 Egg, beaten
  - 1/3 cup Water (Adjust as needed)
  - Cornstarch (for dusting - Do not use flour for dusting!)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Homemade wonton wrappers have a delicate, silky texture that's hard to match with store-bought. The dough should be quite firm after kneading, then rested for 30-60 minutes to relax the gluten so you can roll it paper-thin. The key: use cornstarch for dusting between sheets, never flour. Flour will absorb into the dough and make it gummy, while cornstarch keeps them separate and provides a smooth finish when boiled.

## Directions

1.  **Mix:** In a large bowl, whisk the flour and salt. Make a well in the center. Add the egg and water. Mix until a shaggy dough forms.
2.  **Knead:** Turn out onto a clean surface and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. The dough should be quite firm.
3.  **Rest:** Wrap in plastic and let rest at room temperature for at least 30-60 minutes. This relaxes the gluten so you can roll it paper-thin.
4.  **Roll:** Divide dough into 4 pieces. Use a pasta machine (recommended) or a heavy rolling pin. Roll until the dough is thin enough to see your hand through it (Setting 6 or 7 on most pasta machines).
5.  **Cut:** Dust generously with cornstarch. Cut into 3.5-inch squares.
6.  **Store:** Stack with plenty of cornstarch between layers. Wrap tightly in plastic. (Can be refrigerated for 2 days or frozen for 3 months).

RECIPE: Fried Sweet Plantains (Maduros) (fried-plantains.md)
CUISINES: Caribbean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/fried-plantains/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 very ripe Plantains (skins should be mostly black with yellow patches)
  - 3 tbsp Neutral Oil (vegetable, canola, or coconut)
  - Pinch of Kosher Salt
  - Optional: Pinch of Cinnamon
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Maduros use very ripe sweet plantains rather than the firm green fruit used for tostones. Mostly black skins and yielding flesh are useful cues; ripening time varies with the starting fruit and room. Fry the half-inch slices gently until golden and soft through the center, lowering heat if the sugar darkens too quickly.

## Directions

1. Choose the listed very ripe plantains: mostly black skins with some yellow and flesh that yields to gentle pressure. If firm and yellow, allow more room-temperature ripening and check daily; there is no guaranteed one- or two-day finish. Reject fruit with visible mold or spoiled flesh rather than treating every black mark as proof of readiness.
2. Wash the skins under running water and dry before cutting. Score lengthwise, peel and slice diagonally into roughly 1/2-inch pieces.
3. Heat all the listed oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering without smoking. Add only enough slices for one uncrowded layer, keeping space to turn; the oil is the total pan-frying supply, not a fresh 3 tbsp dose for each round.
4. Start checking around 3–4 minutes per side, and flip gently with a thin spatula once the underside is golden. Continue until the centers are soft; lower heat if the surface darkens before the center softens. Remove finished pieces while thicker ones continue.
5. Transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate and divide the listed salt pinch and optional cinnamon pinch over all the cooked slices as each batch finishes. Repeat with the remaining slices using the oil left in the pan; adjust heat between rounds so sugary residue does not scorch.
6. Serve promptly for the clearest contrast between browned edges and soft centers. More plantains require more rounds or separate pans, dividing the same full oil supply among them.

RECIPE: Frozen Blueberry Muffins (frozen-blueberry-muffins.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/frozen-blueberry-muffins/
SOURCE: Adapted from tasteofhome.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/frozen-blueberry-muffins/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Blueberry muffin batter ---
  - butter or neutral oil, for greasing the muffin cups if not using liners
  - 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, softened
  - 2 cups granulated sugar
  - 4 large eggs, at room temperature
  - 1 cup 2% milk
  - 2 tsp vanilla extract
  - 4 cups all-purpose flour
  - 4 tsp baking powder
  - 1/2 tsp sea salt
  - 2 cups frozen unsweetened blueberries, keep frozen until folding
  - --- Nutmeg-sugar topping ---
  - 2 tbsp granulated sugar
  - 1/2 tsp ground nutmeg
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Frozen blueberries make these buttery muffins practical year-round, with a nutmeg-sugar finish. Fold in the fruit without thawing and keep mixing brief so berry juice does not spread through the batter; look for cooked crumb around the fruit rather than a perfectly dry berry stain on the tester.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the oven and pans:** Heat the oven to 375°F. For the original batch, line two standard 12-cup muffin tins or use butter or neutral oil to grease the cups. For a different quantity, prepare more or fewer standard cups, keeping the same cup size and about two-thirds fill. Plan oven space with air circulation; additional oven batches add baking and pan-cooling time.
2. **Mix the dry ingredients:** Whisk the batter’s all-purpose flour, baking powder, and sea salt together in a bowl.
3. **Cream the butter and sugar:** In another large bowl beat the batter’s unsalted butter and granulated sugar for about 3–5 minutes, until light and fluffy. The topping sugar is separate; none is subtracted from the batter sugar.
4. **Add the eggs:** Beat in the large eggs one at a time, scraping the bowl between additions.
5. **Add the milk and vanilla:** Mix in the 2% milk and vanilla extract until incorporated.
6. **Fold in the flour mixture:** Fold the dry mixture into the butter mixture just until moistened. Scrape the bottom of the bowl so no dry flour pockets remain; do not keep beating to remove every small lump.
7. **Fold in the frozen berries:** Gently fold in the frozen unsweetened blueberries with as few strokes as needed to distribute them. Portion into standard muffin cups about two-thirds full, using the listed muffin yield as a guide rather than forcing every batch into 24 cups. The original batch uses about 24 cups; use more or fewer cups and additional pans or oven batches for different quantities.
8. **Add the topping:** Combine the topping’s granulated sugar and ground nutmeg and sprinkle it evenly over the muffins.
9. **Bake and cool:** Bake for 20–25 minutes, until a tester through the crumb has no wet batter; berry juice on the tester is different from uncooked batter. Check muffins from both tins. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then remove to racks. Let cool completely before packing for storage.
