RECIPE: Funfetti Cake (funfetti-cake-from-scratch-and-an-unbirthday.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/funfetti-cake-from-scratch-and-an-unbirthday/
SOURCE: Adapted from sugarspunrun.com
SOURCE_URL: https://sugarspunrun.com/funfetti-cake-scratch/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Cake batter ---
  - 9 tbsp unsalted butter, softened
  - 3 cups (600 g) granulated sugar
  - 1 cup (236 ml) vegetable oil
  - 4 tsp vanilla extract
  - 4 1/8 cups (516 g) all-purpose flour, all into batter; separate pan flour below
  - 4 1/2 tsp baking powder
  - 1 1/2 tsp sea salt
  - 1 1/2 cups (355 ml) whole milk
  - 9 large egg whites, room temperature
  - 1/2 cup (80 g) jimmies or flat confetti sprinkles
  - butter, as needed for greasing pans
  - all-purpose flour, as needed for dusting pans
  - --- Buttercream ---
  - 1 lb (453 g) unsalted butter, softened
  - 1/4 tsp salt
  - 6 cups (750 g) powdered sugar
  - 6 tbsp heavy cream
  - 2 tsp vanilla extract
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Whip the egg whites in a clean, grease-free bowl, then fold them and the sprinkles into the batter gently. Jimmies or flat confetti sprinkles retain their colors better than nonpareils. Cool all three layers before the crumb coat and brief freezer firming stage.

## Directions

1. **Prepare pans:** Heat the oven to 350°F. Use butter and all-purpose flour to grease and flour three 8-inch round pans for the original batch, shaking out excess flour. All the listed batter flour goes into the cake; pan dusting uses a separate supply.
2. **Cream cake ingredients:** Using unsalted butter, granulated sugar, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract, beat the softened cake butter until creamy, then add all the sugar and oil and beat until combined. Scrape the bowl and mix in all the cake vanilla.
3. **Mix dry ingredients:** Whisk all-purpose flour, baking powder, and sea salt together in a separate bowl.
4. **Combine batter:** Alternate the dry mixture and whole milk into the butter mixture, beginning and ending with dry. Stir until each addition is nearly combined and scrape the bowl; stop once no flour pockets remain.
5. **Whip whites:** In a clean, dry, grease-free bowl, beat large egg whites to stiff peaks. Peaks should stand when the beaters lift; avoid continuing until the foam looks dry or broken.
6. **Fold whites and sprinkles:** Fold all the whipped whites and jimmies or flat confetti sprinkles into the batter gently with a spatula, reaching the sides and bottom without beating out the foam.
7. **Bake and cool:** Divide all the batter among the prepared pans. Bake at 350°F, starting checks around 35–40 minutes for the original three 8-inch pans. Rotate partway through if browning is uneven. Each center should be set, with a clean tester or a few dry crumbs rather than wet batter. Cool in pans 15 minutes, loosen edges and turn onto racks; cool completely.
8. **Make buttercream:** Using unsalted butter, salt, powdered sugar, heavy cream, and vanilla extract, beat the softened frosting butter until smooth, then mix in all the frosting salt. Gradually beat in all the powdered sugar, then add all the heavy cream a little at a time and all the frosting vanilla. Scrape the bowl and beat until smooth and spreadable.
9. **Layer and finish:** Frost between all three completely cool layers, then apply a thin crumb coat. Freeze about 10–15 minutes until that coat is firm, then use all the remaining buttercream for the final top and sides. Refrigerate while waiting to serve.

## Cooking Notes

Use jimmies or flat confetti sprinkles rather than nonpareils, which can bleed into the batter. For the original full batch in three nine-inch pans, start checking around 25 minutes; shallower layers bake sooner.

RECIPE: Gambas al Ajillo (gambas-al-ajillo.md)
CUISINES: Spanish
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/gambas-al-ajillo/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Large Shrimp (16-20 count), peeled and deveined, tails on
  - 1/3 cup Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 8 cloves Garlic, thinly sliced
  - 2 Dried Guindilla Peppers (or 1 tsp red pepper flakes)
  - 1/4 cup Dry Sherry (fino or amontillado)
  - 1 tsp Smoked Paprika (pimenton de la Vera)
  - 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 2 tbsp Fresh Flat-Leaf Parsley, roughly chopped
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice
  - Crusty Bread, for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Gambas al ajillo puts garlic and chile into the olive oil that becomes the sauce. Have everything ready before heating the pan: pale golden garlic can turn bitter quickly, and shrimp need to come off the heat as soon as their centers are cooked. Serve with crusty bread for the full garlicky oil and sherry sauce.

## Directions

1. **Prep Everything First:** Thaw frozen shrimp in the refrigerator, then pat dry with paper towels. Season with the measured salt and smoked paprika. Have sliced garlic, your chosen dried peppers or pepper flakes, sherry, parsley and measured lemon juice beside the stove. Keep the shrimp refrigerated until the pan is ready.

2. **Heat the Oil:** Pour the full measured olive oil into a cast-iron skillet or a cazuela suitable for your hob over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the garlic and dried guindilla peppers, or the alternative pepper flakes. Cook for 30–45 seconds, swirling, until the garlic is pale golden; lower the heat if it colors too quickly.

3. **Add the Shrimp:** Increase to medium-high. Add the shrimp in a single layer, cook for about 1 minute, then turn and begin checking after another 30 seconds. These are first checks, not a required stopping point. For a larger batch, use additional suitable pans or cook separate proportionate batches, dividing all measured oil, seasonings and liquids among them.

4. **Add the Sherry:** Pour in the measured sherry carefully and let it bubble, about 30 seconds as a first check. Continue only as needed for the thickest shrimp to reach 145°F, with firm, pearly, opaque flesh through the center. Lower the heat if the garlic darkens before the shrimp finish. A brief simmer does not remove all the alcohol.

5. **Finish:** Take the pan off the heat as soon as the shrimp are cooked. Add all the measured lemon juice and parsley. Curl and outside color alone do not establish that the centers are done.

6. **Serve:** Serve promptly with crusty bread and all the garlicky oil and sherry sauce. Set a hot skillet on a heatproof trivet and keep its handle out of reach.

RECIPE: Garlic Bread (garlic-bread.md)
CUISINES: Italian-American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/garlic-bread/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 400 g crusty Italian-style bread or baguette
  - 6 tbsp (85 g) unsalted butter, softened
  - 4 cloves garlic, finely grated or minced
  - 2 tbsp finely chopped fresh parsley
  - 25 g finely grated Parmesan
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, or less if bread and cheese are salty
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Italian-American home version combines garlic butter, parsley and Parmesan. Weigh the bread so the topping has a useful ratio: a vague large loaf could be twice the size of a baguette. Baking warms the center; an optional brief broil adds top color. The finished bread should taste of garlic and butter without scorched garlic or an oil-soaked crumb.

## Directions

1. **Prepare oven and bread:** Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Halve the loaf lengthwise and put both pieces cut-side up on a rimmed baking sheet. Use already softened butter; allow extra time if starting with a cold block.
2. **Mix spread:** Stir butter, garlic, parsley, Parmesan and the measured salt until uniform. Use less salt if the bread and cheese are already strongly seasoned.
3. **Spread evenly:** Divide all the butter mixture across the two cut surfaces, reaching the edges in a thin, even layer. Avoid large isolated clumps of garlic.
4. **Bake:** Bake about 12–15 minutes until the edges are golden and the center is hot with melted butter. Thick loaves may need a few more minutes; cover loosely with foil if the edges brown too soon.
5. **Optional top color:** If wanted, broil briefly for about 20–60 seconds, watching continuously and stopping as soon as the top colors. Keep the pan at least 6 inches from the element and follow the oven's broiler guidance. Do not put parchment close to a broiler.
6. **Portion:** Cut each half into six pieces, making twelve pieces total, or two pieces per side portion. Serve hot. For a small accompaniment to a pasta-containing soup, make half a batch and share its six pieces among six diners.

RECIPE: Garlic Butter Pearl Couscous (garlic-butter-couscous.md)
CUISINES: Mediterranean-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/garlic-butter-couscous/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 225 g (about 1 1/2 cups) dry pearl couscous, not fine instant couscous
  - 2 tbsp (28 g) unsalted butter, divided
  - 3 cloves garlic, minced
  - 2 1/4 cups (540 ml) low-sodium vegetable or chicken broth, with package-specific adjustment if needed
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, added only as needed
  - 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
  - 2 tbsp chopped parsley
  - 1 tsp finely grated lemon zest, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Pearl couscous needs time in simmering liquid, while fine instant couscous generally hydrates off the heat. A short butter toast gives this version a little color before the garlic goes in. Finish with parsley and optional zest after cooking so their flavor remains clear beside a saucy main.

## Directions

1. **Toast gently:** Melt 1 tbsp butter in a 2-quart saucepan over medium. Add pearl couscous and stir 2–3 minutes until a few pearls turn golden. Reduce heat if the butter darkens quickly.
2. **Add garlic and broth:** Stir garlic for about 30 seconds, then carefully pour in the measured broth. Add black pepper. Bring to a simmer; hold the salt until you know how salty the broth tastes after cooking.
3. **Cover and cook:** Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer about 10–15 minutes, or according to the package’s absorption method, until tender with slight chew. Check near the end. If dry and firm, add hot water 2 tbsp at a time; if tender with excess liquid, uncover briefly to reduce it without overcooking.
4. **Rest and finish:** Take off heat and leave covered 5 minutes. Fluff gently, fold in the remaining tablespoon butter, parsley and optional zest. Taste and add the measured salt only if needed.
5. **Portion:** Divide into four normal sides or use the smaller portion specified by a composed meal. This recipe already contains its finishing butter; add no extra oil automatically at the table.

RECIPE: Garlic Butter Green Beans (garlic-butter-green-beans.md)
CUISINES: French, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/garlic-butter-green-beans/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 lbs Fresh Green Beans, trimmed
  - 3 tbsp Unsalted Butter
  - 4 cloves Garlic, sliced thin
  - 1/3 cup Sliced Almonds, toasted
  - 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1/4 tsp Black Pepper
  - Flaky Sea Salt for finishing
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Cook the beans to the texture you want before the short garlic-butter finish. The blanched route keeps the garlic cooking brief; the direct route adds garlic only after the raw beans have softened. All the butter and toasted almonds stay in either route.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and blanch:** Wash and trim the beans. For the blanched route, bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it to taste separately from the measured finishing salt. Cook beans about 3–4 minutes until barely tender-crisp, checking a thick bean; drain well. To prepare ahead, cool and refrigerate promptly as described below. For the direct route, skip the boiling water and continue with raw trimmed beans.

2. **Prepare almonds:** Set aside the already-toasted sliced almonds. If starting with untoasted sliced almonds in the same listed amount, toast in the dry skillet over medium-low heat for about 2–3 minutes, stirring until fragrant and lightly golden; transfer to a plate.

3. **Cook the chosen route:** For blanched beans, melt all the cold butter with the sliced garlic over medium heat, stirring about 60–90 seconds until fragrant without deep browning. Add drained beans and toss about 1–2 minutes until hot. For raw beans, melt all the butter over medium heat, add the beans first and cook, tossing, about 7–8 minutes or longer until a thick bean is tender enough to eat. Reduce heat if the butter darkens; then add all the garlic and toss about 60–90 seconds until fragrant. Use more skillets or rounds rather than crowding; divide the same butter and garlic among them.

4. **Season:** Season the whole batch with all the measured kosher salt and black pepper. The separate blanching-water salt is an unmeasured preparation allowance, not part of this finishing amount.

5. **Finish:** Toss in all the toasted almonds and transfer to a serving dish. Add the listed unmeasured flaky finishing salt to taste and serve promptly.

RECIPE: Garlic Butter Salmon with Potatoes and Asparagus (garlic-butter-roasted-salmon-with-potatoes-and-asparagus.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/garlic-butter-roasted-salmon-with-potatoes-and-asparagus/
SOURCE: Adapted from Carolyn Casner, EatingWell
SOURCE_URL: https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/280316/garlic-butter-roasted-salmon-with-potatoes-asparagus/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 1/4 lb skinless salmon fillet, cut into 4 similar portions
  - 1 lb baby Yukon Gold potatoes, halved; quarter larger ones into pieces about 1 inch across
  - 12 oz asparagus, woody ends trimmed
  - 2 tbsp unsalted butter, melted
  - 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 2 cloves garlic, minced
  - 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided equally between potatoes and asparagus
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  - Fresh parsley, chopped, for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Potatoes need a head start, but their tenderness matters more than a fixed fifteen-minute timer. Add salmon once a knife nearly slides through a potato, then check fish and asparagus separately. The lemon-garlic butter adds richness without requiring a separate sauce.

## Directions

1. **Heat and cut:** Heat the oven to **400°F / 205°C**. Halve baby potatoes; quarter larger ones so the pieces are about **1 inch across**. Pat salmon dry and check for pin bones. Keep it refrigerated while the potatoes start.
2. **Start potatoes:** Toss potatoes with **half the olive oil**, salt and pepper. Spread cut-side down on the rimmed tray. Roast for about **20–25 minutes**, checking at 15, until nearly tender with some browning. If the knife still meets a hard center, continue before adding fish.
3. **Prepare asparagus and butter:** While potatoes roast, toss trimmed asparagus with **the remaining olive oil**, salt and pepper. Stir melted butter, lemon juice and garlic together. Season the salmon lightly with salt and pepper.
4. **Arrange:** Move potatoes to one side without piling them deeply. Put salmon in the center and asparagus alongside, using a second tray if needed to prevent overlap. Spoon garlic butter over salmon and asparagus. For very thin asparagus, add it about 5 minutes after the salmon instead.
5. **Finish independently:** Roast about **10–15 minutes**, checking fish at 10 minutes. Measure the thickest center of each salmon portion from the side for **145°F / 63°C**. Check that potatoes are fully tender and asparagus has the bite you like. Lift each finished component to a clean plate while the rest continues; do not leave fish baking solely for the potatoes.
6. **Serve:** Divide salmon, potatoes and asparagus among the plates. Spoon over pan butter and scatter with parsley. This includes its own starch and green vegetable; an additional salad is optional.

Adapted from [Carolyn Casner’s recipe at EatingWell](https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/280316/garlic-butter-roasted-salmon-with-potatoes-asparagus/).

RECIPE: Garlic Butter Shrimp (garlic-butter-shrimp.md)
CUISINES: Italian, Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/garlic-butter-shrimp/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 1/2 lb raw large shrimp (20–24 per pound), peeled and deveined, tails removed
  - 4 tbsp unsalted butter, divided
  - 6 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes
  - 1/2 cup dry white wine or unsalted chicken stock
  - 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
  - 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided to taste
  - 1/4 tsp black pepper
  - 1 lemon, finely zested before juicing
  - Extra unsalted butter, optional, a small piece for finishing
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Lift the cooked shrimp out before reducing the wine. That gives the sauce time to concentrate while the shrimp stay tender. Add lemon and parsley at the end, then bring everything together only long enough to coat.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Zest the lemon before juicing it and measure the listed juice. Mince garlic and chop parsley. Pat shrimp dry, then season with half the salt and all the pepper. Keep the remaining salt for tasting the sauce.

2. **Cook the shrimp:** Melt half the butter over medium to medium-high heat, dividing this allocation between batches if needed. Add shrimp in a single layer without crowding. Cook about 1–2 minutes on the first side, turn, then cook another 1–2 minutes or as needed until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Move cooked shrimp to a clean plate; repeat with the remaining shrimp.

3. **Cook the garlic:** Reduce heat to medium-low and let the pan cool briefly if very hot. Add the remaining butter and garlic. Stir about 30 seconds until fragrant, then add pepper flakes for another 15 seconds. Do not let the garlic darken.

4. **Reduce:** Pour in wine or stock and scrape up the pale brown pan juices. Bring to a gentle simmer and reduce the liquid by roughly half, about 2–4 minutes, leaving the shrimp on their plate.

5. **Finish:** Turn off the heat and stir in lemon juice, parsley and zest. Add the shrimp and their juices and toss to coat; warm briefly over low heat only if needed. Taste and add remaining salt as needed. Swirl in a small piece of optional extra butter if you want a rounder finish.

6. **Serve promptly:** Divide shrimp and sauce evenly and serve with separately cooked noodles, rice or bread. Do not hold the finished shrimp in a simmering sauce.

RECIPE: Garlic Honey Lime Shrimp (garlic-honey-lime-shrimp.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/garlic-honey-lime-shrimp/
SOURCE: Adapted from Bee Yinn Low, Rasa Malaysia, Garlic Honey Lime Shrimp
SOURCE_URL: https://rasamalaysia.com/garlic-honey-lime-shrimp/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb raw jumbo shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails removed
  - 1 tbsp unsalted butter
  - 1 tbsp olive oil
  - 4 cloves garlic, minced
  - 3 tbsp honey
  - 1 1/2 tbsp fresh lime juice, divided
  - 1/4 tsp salt
  - Cayenne pepper, a pinch or to taste
  - Fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped, for finishing
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Honey makes this a deliberately sweet glaze, balanced by lime and a little cayenne. Cook over moderate heat and stop when the shrimp are ready; reduce a watery sauce separately if necessary. Adapted from [Bee Yinn Low’s Garlic Honey Lime Shrimp](https://rasamalaysia.com/garlic-honey-lime-shrimp/).

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Pat thawed shrimp dry. Mince garlic, chop the finishing herbs and measure honey and lime juice. Divide lime juice into two equal portions. Have separately prepared rice and vegetables ready for service.

2. **Warm the garlic:** Heat olive oil and butter in the skillet over medium heat. When the butter foams, add garlic and stir about 20–30 seconds until fragrant without browning it deeply.

3. **Start the shrimp:** Add shrimp in a single layer. Cook about 1–2 minutes until the underside changes color, then turn. Keep the garlic moving around the shrimp so it does not burn.

4. **Glaze and finish cooking:** Add honey, half the lime juice, salt and cayenne. Stir gently and cook about 1–3 minutes more, checking the thicker pieces early, until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. If the sauce remains watery, transfer cooked shrimp to a clean plate and simmer the sauce briefly on its own. If too thick, loosen with a small splash of water.

5. **Brighten and serve:** Turn off the heat. Stir in the remaining lime juice and return any removed shrimp, tossing to coat. Scatter with parsley or cilantro and serve immediately. Divide the batch among rice-and-vegetable bowls for modest portions, or serve as two larger portions.

RECIPE: Garlic Mashed "Mock" Potatoes (garlic-mashed-mock-potatoes.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/garlic-mashed-mock-potatoes/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodnetwork.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/mock-garlic-mashed-potatoes-recipe-1942447
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 medium head Cauliflower, cut into small florets
  - 1 tbsp Cream Cheese, softened
  - 1/4 cup Freshly Grated Parmesan
  - 1/2 tsp Garlic, minced
  - 3 tbsp unsalted butter
  - 1/2 tsp concentrated chicken or vegetable bouillon paste, using a paste labeled 1 tsp per cup of prepared broth
  - Salt, for boiling water and to taste; black pepper, to taste
  - Fresh Chives, chopped
  - Additional unsalted butter, a pat for serving, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Drain the cooked cauliflower well and let surface steam escape before puréeing. Removing free water helps the mash hold its shape, while cream cheese, Parmesan and all the measured butter keep it rich. The concentrated bouillon is a paste with the stated broth strength, not an interchangeable cube.

## Directions

1. **Boil:** Bring a pot of water to a boil and salt it with the listed allowance. Add small cauliflower florets and cook about 6–8 minutes, until very soft and easily crushed.

2. **Drain and dry:** Drain thoroughly in a colander and let surface steam escape briefly. Spread on a heatproof tray if needed. If free water remains, use tongs or a utensil to blot with clean absorbent towels once manageable; do not press scalding florets between paper towels with bare hands. Keep the cauliflower warm where the chosen equipment permits.

3. **Purée:** Use a food processor or immersion blender only as its actual manual permits for this food temperature and quantity. Never put hot cauliflower in a sealed personal cup. If cooling is required, allow it and rewarm after puréeing; it adds time. Combine cauliflower with all the cream cheese, Parmesan, minced garlic, specified concentrated bouillon paste and black pepper.

4. **Check texture:** Process until smooth, checking safely rather than assuming 1 minute works for every machine. Use batches if needed and recombine; do not add water to compensate for undercooked florets.

5. **Finish:** Stir in all the measured butter until melted. Taste after the cheese and bouillon are mixed through, and use any additional salt only if needed. Add the chopped chives.

6. **Serve:** Serve warm with the separate optional extra butter pat. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and reheat gently, stirring for even warmth.

RECIPE: Garlic Mashed Red Potatoes (garlic-mashed-red-potatoes.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/garlic-mashed-red-potatoes/
SOURCE: Adapted from tasteofhome.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/garlic-mashed-red-potatoes/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 8 medium Red Potatoes, quartered (Skin-on)
  - 3 large Garlic Cloves, peeled
  - 2 tbsp Unsalted Butter
  - 1/2 cup Whole Milk, warmed
  - 1/4 cup Freshly Grated Parmesan
  - Salt and Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Keep the red skins on and cook the potato quarters with whole garlic cloves until both crush easily. Drain well, then mash by hand with butter, warmed milk and Parmesan. A brief return to the warm pot removes surface water without needing a blender or perfectly smooth texture.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Scrub the potatoes and leave the skins on. Quarter them into similar-size pieces. Put potatoes and peeled whole garlic in a large pot, cover with cold water and add salt from the listed allowance.

2. **Simmer:** Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer about 15–20 minutes after boiling, until potato quarters and garlic crush easily. Larger quarters may need longer; check the thickest pieces.

3. **Drain:** Drain potatoes and garlic thoroughly. Return to the warm pot briefly, about 1 minute, letting surface steam escape without scorching the bottom.

4. **Mash:** Add all the butter and mash potatoes and garlic together by hand. Season with the listed salt and pepper to taste. Keep skin pieces and some rustic texture rather than beating vigorously.

5. **Finish the mash:** Gradually add all the warmed milk and Parmesan, mashing just enough to combine. Avoid a blender or food processor for the potatoes; stop at the desired rustic texture.

6. **Serve:** Serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers in shallow containers and reheat gently to the measured leftover endpoint, stirring for even heating.

RECIPE: Chicken and Potatoes with Garlic Parmesan Cream (garlic-parmesan-chicken-potatoes.md)
CUISINES: American, Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/garlic-parmesan-chicken-potatoes/
SOURCE: Adapted from Damndelicious.net
SOURCE_URL: http://damndelicious.net/2016/05/08/chicken-potatoes-garlic-parmesan-cream-sauce/print/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken and vegetables ---
  - cooking spray, as needed for the baking-dish variation, optional
  - olive oil, as needed to coat the potatoes for roasting
  - 6 bone-in skin-on chicken thighs
  - 1 tbsp Italian seasoning
  - salt, to taste
  - black pepper, to taste
  - 2 tbsp unsalted butter, for searing
  - 1 tbsp unsalted butter, for the spinach
  - 3 cups baby spinach, roughly chopped
  - 1 lb baby potatoes, quartered
  - salt, to taste for roasted potatoes
  - --- Garlic-Parmesan cream sauce ---
  - 4 tbsp unsalted butter, for the sauce
  - 4 garlic cloves, minced
  - 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
  - 1 1/2 cups chicken broth
  - 1 tsp dried thyme
  - 1/2 tsp dried basil
  - 1/2 cup heavy cream or half-and-half
  - 1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan
  - salt, to taste after the completed bake
  - black pepper, to taste after the completed bake
  - --- Finish ---
  - 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

These chicken thighs finish in a garlic-Parmesan cream sauce with spinach, while the potatoes roast separately. Keep the potatoes beside the sauce at serving if you want their browned edges to remain crisp; sauce contact softens them. Brown the chicken first, then use temperature rather than skin color to judge the oven finish.

## Directions

1. **Start the potatoes:** Preheat the oven to 425°F. Set out cooking spray (if using), olive oil, baby potatoes, and salt. Quarter the baby potatoes into similar pieces, toss with enough olive oil to coat and salt to taste, and spread in one layer on a rimmed sheet pan. Roast about 20–25 minutes, checking for browned edges and a center that yields easily to a knife; continue as needed. Check that all the measured thighs fit without overlap in your oven-safe skillet; use a baking dish for the chicken finish if needed. Prepare the chicken and sauce while the potatoes roast. The optional cooking spray is for the baking-dish variation below, which uses a different oven temperature and omits the separate potato roast.
2. **Brown the chicken:** Use bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, Italian seasoning, salt, black pepper, and unsalted butter: pat chicken dry with paper towels, then season with Italian seasoning, salt and pepper. Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden, about 5–7 minutes, then brown the other side for about 2 minutes. Work in batches if needed, reducing heat if the butter or fond begins to burn. Transfer to a plate reserved for partly cooked chicken; continue directly with the recipe.
3. **Wilt the spinach:** Use unsalted butter and baby spinach: melt the butter for this step in the skillet, add spinach and stir until it begins to wilt, about 2 minutes. Transfer spinach to a bowl. Pour off excessive rendered chicken fat, keeping the browned fond and leaving no burned bits.
4. **Make the roux:** Use unsalted butter, garlic cloves, and all-purpose flour: melt the sauce butter over medium heat. Add garlic and stir until fragrant, about 1–2 minutes, without browning it. Whisk in flour and cook about 1 minute, stirring until smooth and lightly colored.
5. **Finish the sauce:** Use chicken broth, dried thyme, dried basil, heavy cream or half-and-half, and freshly grated Parmesan: gradually whisk broth into the roux with thyme and basil, loosening the browned fond. Simmer gently, whisking, until smooth and lightly thickened, about 1–2 minutes. Lower the heat and stir in cream and Parmesan, about 1–2 minutes, until the cheese melts. Do not boil hard after adding cheese. The sauce has contacted partly cooked chicken fond; wait until the final bake is complete before tasting it.
6. **Finish the chicken in sauce:** Stir the wilted spinach into the sauce and return the seared chicken skin-side up. Keep as much skin above the sauce as possible. If your oven-safe skillet cannot hold the thighs in one layer, transfer chicken, spinach and sauce to a baking dish large enough to fit them without overlap. Keep the roasted potatoes separate for crispness; adding them to the sauce will soften their surface.
7. **Bake and measure:** Transfer the skillet or chicken baking dish to the 425°F oven. Begin checking after about 10 minutes; the thickest part of every thigh, away from bone, and the sauce at the center must reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue baking as needed; ten minutes is a first check, not a guarantee of completion. If the skin darkens early, shield it loosely with foil while the meat finishes. Check the separately roasted potatoes for tenderness as well. Rest safely cooked chicken 5 minutes before serving.
8. **Serve:** After the bake meets the temperature checks, taste the sauce with a clean spoon. Use salt, black pepper, and fresh parsley (if using): adjust salt and pepper, then add parsley if using. Serve one thigh per portion with potatoes, spinach and sauce.

## Potatoes Baked in the Sauce

For the baking-dish variation, omit the separate potato roast and its oil. Preheat to 400°F and lightly coat a 9-by-13-inch baking dish with the optional cooking spray. Sear the chicken and make the spinach and sauce as directed. Put chicken skin-side up in the dish, arrange the raw quartered potatoes and spinach around it and pour in the sauce. Bake about 25–30 minutes as a first check, then continue until every thigh and the sauce center reach 165°F / 74°C and potatoes are easily pierced. If safely cooked chicken finishes first, move it to a clean plate while the potatoes finish. Rest cooked chicken five minutes, then taste and season the safe sauce. Potatoes baked this way are soft and sauced. Add dishes as needed to keep the scaled chicken in one layer.

RECIPE: Toum (garlic-paste-toum-the-washington-post.md)
CUISINES: Lebanese, Middle Eastern
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/garlic-paste-toum-the-washington-post/
SOURCE: Adapted from Washingtonpost.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.washingtonpost.com/recipes/garlic-paste-toum/14095/?utm_term=.4ad477758d1a
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Garlic paste ---
  - 2 cups fresh garlic cloves, peeled
  - 1/2 tsp kosher salt
  - 3 cups neutral oil (grapeseed or canola)
  - 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice
  - 1/3 cup cold water
  - --- Optional source finish ---
  - neutral oil, a little more as needed for the source finishing option, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Toum is a Lebanese garlic emulsion. Start with a smooth garlic paste and introduce oil in a very thin stream, pausing to scrape as needed. A separated oily mixture needs attention before more liquid goes in. The oil stages below follow the Washington Post method.

## Directions

1. **Puree garlic:** Use fresh garlic cloves and kosher salt in a food processor with sufficient usable liquid capacity for the entire mixture. Puree until smooth, stopping and scraping as needed. Follow its motor-duty and minimum-load instructions; make separate proportionally divided batches if necessary.
2. **Begin the emulsion:** With the motor running as permitted by the appliance, add 1/2 of the neutral oil (grapeseed or canola) in the thinnest stream. Stop to scrape. Do not speed up the pour if the mixture looks oily rather than cohesive.
3. **Build the paste:** Gradually add 1/6 of the neutral oil (grapeseed or canola) in the same thin stream, checking for a thick, cohesive paste.
4. **Add lemon:** Gradually add all fresh lemon juice; the mixture should lighten.
5. **Add oil and water:** Gradually add the assigned neutral oil, then slowly add all the cold water. These are 1/6 of the neutral oil (grapeseed or canola) and cold water. The paste should loosen without becoming runny.
6. **Finish the emulsion:** Gradually add all the remaining measured neutral oil. For the optional source finish, add only a little of the separate extra-oil allowance at a time if needed for a creamy, white, fluffy paste; stop if the mixture separates. The measured remainder and optional allowance are 1/6 of the neutral oil (grapeseed or canola) and neutral oil (if using).
7. **Refrigerate:** Transfer to clean covered containers and refrigerate at least 4 hours before serving. Refrigerate promptly at 40°F or below and use within 4 days, or freeze small portions promptly. Thaw in the refrigerator; the emulsion may separate. Do not rely on lemon juice alone to establish a longer storage life.

RECIPE: Garlic Roasted Potatoes (garlic-roasted-potatoes.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/garlic-roasted-potatoes/
SOURCE: Adapted from Ina Garten, Garlic Roasted Potatoes
SOURCE_URL: https://barefootcontessa.com/recipes/garlic-roasted-potatoes
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 lb small red or Yukon Gold potatoes, scrubbed, dried and cut into roughly 1 1/2-inch pieces
  - 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, divided
  - 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt
  - 1 tsp ground black pepper
  - 2 tbsp minced garlic
  - 2 tbsp minced fresh parsley
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Dry the potatoes after washing and leave space between pieces. Their cut faces need time against the hot pan to brown. Minced garlic enters only once the centers are nearly tender, so it has time to become fragrant without spending the whole roast on a hot surface.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Heat the oven to **400°F / 205°C**. Scrub and dry the potatoes, then halve or quarter them into roughly **1 1/2-inch pieces**. Set out one or two rimmed half-sheet pans according to the space needed.
2. **Coat and spread:** Reserve **one-quarter of the measured oil** for the garlic. Toss potatoes with the remaining oil, salt and pepper. Spread in one layer with a cut face against the pan and a little space between pieces.
3. **Roast until nearly ready:** Roast for about **40–55 minutes**, turning with a wide spatula after about 25 minutes and again if another face needs browning. Start checking at 40 minutes: a thin knife should slide into a thick center easily and the cut faces should have golden patches. If still firm, continue before adding garlic. Rotate pans and swap racks if using two.
4. **Add garlic:** Mix the garlic with the reserved oil. Once the potatoes are nearly tender, toss this mixture through them and return to the oven for about **5 minutes**, watching for fragrant, pale-golden garlic. Extend briefly if needed for tenderness; stop before garlic turns dark. Total roasting is usually **45–60 minutes**, but doneness governs.
5. **Finish:** Transfer to a serving bowl and toss with the parsley. Serve promptly, dividing into side portions. Avoid covering tightly during a short wait, which traps steam and softens the crust.

RECIPE: Garlic Sauteed Green Beans (garlic-sauteed-green-beans.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/garlic-sauteed-green-beans/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb fresh green beans, stem ends trimmed
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, divided between the beans and garlic
  - 4 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
  - 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes, optional
  - Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  - 1 tsp fresh lemon juice
  - Water, a small splash only if needed to finish firm beans
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Brown the beans first, then check a bite before adding garlic. If the center is still firm, a small splash of water and a brief covered steam can finish it without burning the surface. Lower the heat for the sliced garlic and add the measured lemon off heat.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Trim, wash and thoroughly dry the beans. Slice garlic and measure lemon juice. Set aside **one-quarter of the oil for garlic**; the remainder is for cooking the beans.
2. **Brown:** Heat **the bean oil** in a broad skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add beans in a shallow layer with room to toss, splitting beans and this oil between rounds if crowded. Leave undisturbed about **2 minutes**, then toss and cook another **3–5 minutes** until browned in patches. Reduce heat if they scorch.
3. **Check the center:** Taste a cooled bean. If still firm, lower heat to medium, add a **small splash of water carefully** and cover for **2–4 minutes**, then check again. Add another small splash only if the pan dries before the beans become tender. Uncover and let excess water evaporate. Skip steaming if already tender. If browning in rounds, finish their tenderness separately before combining.
4. **Add garlic gently:** Return all beans to the pan if using rounds. Reduce heat to medium-low and move the skillet off the burner briefly if still very hot. Push beans aside, add **the reserved oil**, garlic and optional pepper flakes. Stir for about **30–60 seconds** until fragrant and lightly golden, then toss through the beans.
5. **Season and serve:** Remove from heat. Add salt, black pepper and **the measured lemon juice**. Toss and taste, then divide into side portions and serve promptly.

RECIPE: Sigeumchi Namul (Sesame Spinach) (garlic-sesame-spinach.md)
CUISINES: Korean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/garlic-sesame-spinach/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 450 g fresh baby spinach, washed, tough stems removed
  - 2 liters water, for blanching
  - Cold water and ice, for cooling
  - 2 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1 tsp finely minced fresh garlic, added gradually to taste
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, added gradually to taste
  - 2 tsp toasted sesame seeds
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Sigeumchi namul is a Korean spinach banchan. Brief blanching softens the leaves; cooling and gentle pressing keep the final seasoning from becoming watery. Loosen the greens after pressing so sesame and garlic reach the individual strands. This version uses salt rather than soy sauce and keeps the seasoning light enough to accompany a saucy main.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Wash spinach and remove tough stems. Bring 2 liters water to a boil in a large pot. Fill a large bowl with cold water and ice and set a colander nearby.
2. **Blanch in two batches:** Submerge half the spinach, stir it under the water and cook about 30–60 seconds, until leaves wilt and stems bend. Lift directly into the cold water. Let the pot return to a boil and repeat with the remaining spinach.
3. **Cool, drain and press:** Once spinach is cool, drain. Take small handfuls and squeeze gently to remove excess water, stopping while the leaves remain moist. Do not twist into a hard, dry mass. Cut long strands into bite-sized lengths and loosen with your fingers in a bowl.
4. **Season:** Add sesame oil, seeds, half the garlic and half the salt. Toss gently, taste a small portion, then add remaining garlic and salt only as needed. Avoid crushing the greens into a paste.
5. **Serve or chill:** Divide into four small side portions. Serve promptly at cool room temperature or refrigerate until wanted. The spinach is blanched and dressed, not sautéed in garlic oil.

RECIPE: Garlicky Lemon Kale with Carrots (garlicky-lemon-kale-with-carrots.md)
CUISINES: American, Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/garlicky-lemon-kale-with-carrots/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 large bunch Kale (stems removed; about 8 cups chopped for the original batch)
  - 3 medium Carrots, sliced into thin coins
  - 4 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 2 tbsp Olive Oil (or vegetable oil)
  - 1/4 cup Water or Vegetable Broth
  - 1/2 Lemon, juiced (about 2 tbsp juice for the original batch)
  - 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt (plus more to taste)
  - 1/4 tsp Black Pepper
  - 1/4 tsp Red Pepper Flakes (optional, for heat)
  - 1 tsp Sesame Oil (optional, for Asian-style preparation)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Thin carrot coins get a head start before the kale. Add the leaves in manageable handfuls, then use the measured water or broth for a short covered steam. The lemon and optional sesame-oil finish go in off heat; different hearty greens can need different cooking times.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Wash kale and carrots under running water. Remove the tough kale stems and chop leaves into roughly 2-inch pieces. Slice the carrots into thin coins. About 8 cups kale and about 2 tbsp juice from half a lemon describe the original batch, not exact scaled equivalents.

2. **Cook carrots:** Heat all the measured olive or vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add all carrots and sauté about 3–4 minutes, tossing until starting to soften with some color on the edges. Use enough vessels for the full batch, dividing all the cooking oil and later ingredients among them.

3. **Add garlic:** Add all minced garlic and cook about 30 seconds until fragrant, reducing heat if it browns quickly.

4. **Wilt:** Add kale in handfuls, tossing each until it settles enough for the next. Do not pile more than the vessel can toss and cover.

5. **Steam:** Add all the measured water or broth, cover and steam about 2–3 minutes, then check a leaf and carrot. Continue as needed until tender to your liking; a bright green color alone is not a tenderness test.

6. **Finish:** Uncover and toss about 30–60 seconds to evaporate excess liquid without drying the pan. Remove from heat. Add juice from all the listed lemon, all measured salt and black pepper, and optional red-pepper flakes. Add the optional measured sesame oil now if wanted. Toss through.

7. **Serve:** Taste and use the listed additional-salt allowance if needed. Additional lemon juice or pepper is optional seasoning beyond the measured base; serve warm.

## Variations

**Mediterranean style:** At the original batch, add 1/4 cup toasted pine nuts or slivered almonds and 2 tbsp golden raisins in step 6; scale these additions proportionally and use all in the finish.

**Sesame-soy variation:** Replace the full listed cooking-oil amount with sesame oil in step 2; keep the separate listed optional finishing sesame-oil amount if wanted. Use heat suitable for the actual oil and reduce it if the oil smokes. At the original batch, add 1 tbsp soy sauce in step 6 and sesame seeds as an unmeasured garnish; scale the soy sauce proportionally. Keep all other base ingredients. Soy sauce adds salt, so taste before any additional salt; use a gluten-free soy sauce if required.

**Spicy variation:** Use twice the listed red-pepper flakes, or add 1 tsp sriracha in step 6 at the original batch, scaled proportionally. These are separate options, not an instruction to add both.

RECIPE: Gefilte Fish Terrine (gefilte-fish-terrine.md)
CUISINES: Jewish
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/gefilte-fish-terrine/
SOURCE: Adapted from Saveur.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.saveur.com/article/recipes/jewish-gefilte-fish-terrine-recipe
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Terrine and salad ---
  - 12 oz Boneless skinless carp or pike fillet, chopped
  - 12 oz Boneless skinless salmon fillet, chopped
  - 3 tbsp Olive oil
  - 1 cup Heavy cream
  - 2 tbsp Matzo meal
  - 2 Large eggs, beaten
  - 1 Medium onion, minced
  - 1 Carrot, shredded
  - 1 tbsp Fresh dill, minced
  - 2 Lemons for zest, zest only; measured juice separate
  - 3 tbsp Lemon juice
  - 3/4 cup Cold water
  - 1 tsp Black pepper
  - 2 tsp Kosher salt
  - 2 cups Baby arugula, rinsed unless labeled prewashed or ready-to-eat; drained
  - 4 Radishes, washed and sliced
  - 1 tbsp Fresh horseradish, peeled and grated
  - 1 Shallot, thinly sliced
  - Dill sprigs, for garnish
  - Salt for salad, to taste
  - Black pepper for salad, to taste
  - Lemon wedges, for serving
  - Matzos, for serving
  - Boiling water for water bath, as needed to reach halfway up the loaf pan
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Eli and Max Sussman’s baked gefilte-fish terrine combines salmon with carp or pike and sets in a water bath. Coarsely ground fish gives a different texture from a smooth paste. Keep the full cream and egg binder, allow the loaf to chill throughout, and toss its fresh horseradish salad shortly before slicing.

## Directions

1. **Sweat onion:** Rinse fresh produce under running water before peeling, cutting or zesting, including the lemons, dill, shallot and horseradish; follow any prewashed or ready-to-eat arugula label. Heat the assigned oil from 1/3 of the Olive oil and Medium onion in a skillet. Cook the onion about 8–10 minutes until soft and translucent without browning; transfer all the onion and cooking oil to a mixing bowl.
2. **Grind fish:** Keep Boneless skinless carp or pike fillet and Boneless skinless salmon fillet cold during preparation; check for bones. Pulse in a food processor until coarsely ground, then add to the onion bowl. Do not grind to a smooth paste.
3. **Bind:** Stir Heavy cream, Matzo meal, Large eggs, Carrot, Fresh dill, Lemons for zest, 1/9 of the Lemon juice, Cold water, Black pepper, and Kosher salt into the fish and onion until evenly combined. Add one ninth of the measured lemon juice here and reserve the remaining eight ninths for the salad. The original batch uses 1 tsp juice here; scale that share with the listed juice total. All the measured cream, matzo meal, eggs, carrot, dill, lemon zest, water, salt and pepper belong in this mixture.
4. **Prepare pan:** Preheat the oven to 325°F. For the original batch, line the bottom and sides of a 9-by-5-inch loaf pan with nonstick baking parchment rated for at least 325°F, leaving overhang to fold over the surface. Spread all the mixture into the pan, fold the parchment over it and cover with foil. Keep the paper inside the covered pan; do not use wax paper or ordinary plastic wrap. Multiples need separate original-size loaves and baths; smaller amounts need appropriate smaller pans and earlier center checks. Keep comparable mixture depth and headroom rather than forcing every scale into this pan.
5. **Water bath:** Place the loaf pan in an original-batch 9-by-13-inch baking dish, or a suitable larger outer vessel, and carefully add Boiling water for water bath. Support the hot vessels securely and keep bath water out of the fish mixture.
6. **Bake:** Bake at 325°F, checking near the original 1 hour 15 minute planning time. Continue until a thin-tip thermometer in the center reaches 160°F /71°C and the center is firm. Check the center of every separately baked loaf; a firm surface or clean knife alone does not replace the measured endpoint.
7. **Cool and chill:** Remove the loaf pan carefully from the hot bath and cool briefly on a rack, then refrigerate promptly at 40°F /4°C or below, within 2 hours of cooking (1 hour above 90°F /32°C). Chill at least 4 hours until cold throughout before inverting and peeling away the parchment. Making it the day before allows cooling and chilling without rushing.
8. **Finish salad:** Toss 2/3 of the Olive oil, 8/9 of the Lemon juice, Baby arugula, Radishes, Fresh horseradish, Shallot, Dill sprigs, Salt for salad, and Black pepper for salad together just before serving. Use all the remaining two thirds of the measured olive oil and eight ninths of the measured lemon juice, with the separate salad salt and pepper allowances. The original batch uses 2 tbsp oil and 2 tbsp plus 2 tsp juice here; scale those shares with the listed totals. Keep washed vegetables and raw-fish tools separate.
9. **Serve:** Slice the chilled terrine and serve with all the salad, Lemon wedges and Matzos. Ten portions are the planning yield for the original batch; slicing that original loaf into 8–10 portions is another serving option. Refrigerate unused terrine promptly, keeping the fresh salad separate.

RECIPE: General Tso's Cauliflower (general-tsos-cauliflower.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/general-tsos-cauliflower/
SOURCE: Adapted from purewow.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.purewow.com/recipes/General-Tsos-Cauliflower
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Cauliflower and batter ---
  - 1 cauliflower head, washed, well drained and cut into bite-sized florets
  - 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
  - 1/3 cup cornstarch
  - 3/4 tsp baking powder
  - 1 tsp salt
  - 2 large eggs
  - 3 tbsp soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp rice vinegar
  - water, as needed to thin overly stiff batter
  - 1/2 cup peanut or vegetable oil, for shallow frying
  - --- Sauce ---
  - 2 tsp sesame oil
  - 6 scallions, washed; whites finely sliced and greens cut into 1-inch pieces, reserved
  - 3 garlic cloves, minced
  - 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
  - 5 small dried red chilies, optional
  - 1/4 cup vegetable broth
  - 1/4 cup soy sauce
  - 3 tbsp rice vinegar
  - 2 tbsp mirin
  - 3 tbsp granulated sugar
  - 1 tbsp cornstarch
  - sesame seeds, for garnish, if wanted, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This vegetarian General Tso adaptation brings a Chinese-American takeout sauce to cauliflower. The cauliflower gets an egg-and-starch coating and a separate soy, vinegar and mirin glaze. Fry uncrowded florets until the coating is set and their centers are tender, then coat them only when the sauce is ready. The coating softens in sauce; serving promptly matters more than promising lasting crunch.
For kids, serve the heat on the side or reduce or omit the spicy elements.

## Directions

1. **Mix the batter:** For the batter, use all-purpose flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, large eggs, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and water. Whisk the flour, coating cornstarch, baking powder and salt. Separately whisk the eggs, batter soy sauce and batter vinegar, then pour into the dry mixture while whisking. If too stiff to coat a floret, stir in a little of the thinning-water allowance until thick but dip-able. Do not taste raw egg/flour batter.
2. **Fry the cauliflower:** Use cauliflower head and peanut or vegetable oil for this stage. For the measured-oil route, heat the full listed frying oil in a skillet suitable for shallow frying. The separate oil-to-depth option uses a different, unmeasured frying supply. A small drop of batter should sizzle and float promptly without burning. Dip florets and fry in uncrowded rounds, turning until golden on all sides, starting checks around 4–5 minutes per original-size round. Cut a large sample: the coating should be set without wet batter and the center tender. Check 160°F in large coated pieces with a thin probe from the side; color alone is not an egg-batter endpoint. Lift onto absorbent paper towels; do not pour unused raw batter into the sauce.
3. **Start the sauce:** Have sesame oil, scallions, garlic cloves, fresh ginger, and small dried red chilies (if using) ready. Heat the sesame oil over medium heat in a saucepan with room for the finished dish. Stir scallion whites, garlic, ginger and optional chilies about 30 seconds until fragrant, lowering heat if garlic browns. Keep all the scallion greens aside for the thickened sauce.
4. **Simmer the sauce liquids:** Add vegetable broth, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and mirin, bring to a simmer and cook about 5 minutes over medium heat. The distinct batter and sauce soy/vinegar measures are both used.
5. **Disperse the sauce starch:** Whisk granulated sugar and cornstarch together in a small bowl. For the original batch, gradually whisk about 1/4 cup of hot sauce from the saucepan into this mixture until smooth; for a scaled batch take the corresponding proportional amount from that same sauce supply. Return all this mixture to the pot, bring to a simmer and add all the reserved scallion greens. This is recirculated sauce, not extra broth.
6. **Finish thickening:** Cook, stirring occasionally, about 7–9 minutes more, checking for a glossy sauce that clings to a spoon without scorching. Lower heat as needed; do not treat the clock as a requirement to boil a nearly dry pot.
7. **Glaze the cauliflower:** Add all the fried cauliflower and fold gently until coated and rewarmed, starting checks around 4–5 minutes for the original batch. Use enough uncrowded vessels for larger batches, dividing the entire batter, frying oil and sauce quantities proportionally. Serve promptly; extended holding softens the coating.
8. **Serve:** Garnish with sesame seeds (if using) and serve with separately prepared steamed rice.

RECIPE: General Tso's Tofu (general-tsos-tofu.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/general-tsos-tofu/
SOURCE: Adapted from thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/general-tsos-tofu/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Tofu and coating ---
  - 1 lb extra-firm tofu, pressed dry and cut into 1-inch squares
  - 1 1/2 tbsp honey
  - 2 tsp thin vinegar-based red-pepper hot sauce
  - 1 1/2 tbsp sesame seeds
  - 3 tbsp cornstarch
  - 1/3 cup peanut oil, for shallow frying; part is reused for aromatics
  - --- Sauce and vegetables ---
  - 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
  - 2 garlic cloves, minced
  - 7 dried Chinese red chilies
  - 1/2 red bell pepper, sliced
  - 1/2 tbsp Shaoxing wine, optional
  - 1 cup vegetable stock
  - 2 cups broccoli florets
  - 1 1/2 tbsp light soy sauce
  - 1 tsp dark soy sauce
  - 2 tsp rice vinegar
  - 1/4 tsp salt
  - 1 tbsp granulated sugar
  - 1/2 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - --- Separate slurry ---
  - 1 1/2 tbsp cornstarch
  - 1 tbsp cold water
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This tofu adaptation brings a Chinese-American takeout sauce to plant-based protein. Coat the dry tofu gently with honey, thin red-pepper hot sauce, sesame seeds and cornstarch, then fry uncrowded pieces before making the glaze. The coating softens once it meets sauce, so finish the broccoli first and return the tofu only when ready to eat. Keep the frying oil separate from the finished dish except for the portion reused for the aromatics.
For kids, serve the heat on the side or reduce or omit the spicy elements.

## Directions

1. **Mix the slurry:** Mix cornstarch and cold water in a small bowl. Keep this separate from the tofu coating; re-stir just before adding it to the sauce.
2. **Coat the tofu:** For the coating, use extra-firm tofu, honey, thin vinegar-based red-pepper hot sauce, sesame seeds, and cornstarch. Wash and drain the vegetables before cutting. Mix the honey and hot sauce, gently toss in the dry tofu, then add all the sesame seeds and coating cornstarch. Lift and turn rather than crushing the pieces; aim for a light coating, not a pool of wet batter.
3. **Fry in batches:** Heat peanut oil in a shallow-frying skillet to about 350°F. Carefully add coated tofu in a single layer with space between pieces. Fry about 4–5 minutes per original-size round, turning once, until golden with a formed crust; lower heat if the coating darkens too quickly. Lift to a sheet pan with a slotted spoon. Repeat without crowding, allowing the oil to recover its heat.
4. **Cook the aromatics:** Have fresh ginger, garlic cloves, dried Chinese red chilies, red bell pepper, and Shaoxing wine (if using) ready. Transfer a portion of the used frying oil to a wok or saucepan: 3/16 of the listed frying-oil amount, which is 1 tbsp for the original batch. This comes from the frying supply, not an additional dose; do not add the remaining frying oil to the sauce. Heat over medium and stir the ginger, garlic and chilies about 30 seconds until fragrant, without scorching. Add all the bell pepper and optional wine.
5. **Cook the broccoli:** Use vegetable stock and broccoli florets in sequence: bring all the stock to a boil first, then add all the broccoli. Keep enough room to turn the vegetables; use additional vessels with the complete ingredients divided proportionally for larger batches.
6. **Season and thicken:** Add light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rice vinegar, salt, granulated sugar, and toasted sesame oil and return the sauce to a boil. Re-stir the separate slurry, then pour it in gradually while stirring. Simmer 30–60 seconds after each addition before deciding whether more is needed; stop when it coats a spoon and leave any unused slurry out of the dish. Continue until a broccoli stem yields with slight resistance.
7. **Glaze and serve:** Return all the fried tofu to the ready sauce and fold gently about 30 seconds to coat without breaking the pieces. Serve promptly over separately prepared rice. Holding glazed tofu softens its coating.

RECIPE: Glazed Carrots (glazed-carrots.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/glazed-carrots/
SOURCE: Adapted from Allrecipes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/229669/glazed-carrots/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 lbs carrots, peeled and cut into matchsticks
  - 1/4 cup unsalted butter
  - 1/4 cup light brown sugar, packed
  - 1/4 tsp sea salt, for glaze
  - 1/8 tsp ground white pepper
  - 1 tsp fresh thyme, chopped, optional
  - Water, for a 1-inch depth in the saucepan
  - Salt as needed, optional for the boiling water
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Simmer the carrot sticks until tender, drain well and return them to the full butter-and-brown-sugar glaze. Keep the glaze salt separate from any optional salt in the boiling water. Stir gently so tender sticks stay intact.

## Directions

1. Wash and peel the carrots, then cut even matchsticks. Put them in a large saucepan and add water to a 1-inch depth. Use plain water, or add the separate optional boiling-salt allowance if you prefer salted water. The measured glaze salt stays reserved.
2. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low and cover. Start checking around 8–10 minutes, sooner for very thin sticks. A fork should enter a center readily without raw hardness; stop before the sticks fall apart. Boiling and actual cut thickness determine the clock.
3. Drain and transfer the carrots to a bowl without rinsing. Melt all the butter in the same saucepan over low heat, then stir in all the brown sugar, glaze salt and white pepper until dissolved and glossy.
4. Return all the drained carrots and toss gently over medium-low heat until hot and coated. Start checking at 2–3 minutes; the carrots may need up to about 5 minutes to heat through and take on the glaze. Follow the clinging glaze rather than driving the sugar to a burnt crust.
5. Stir in all the optional listed thyme if using and serve promptly.

RECIPE: Glazed Chicken & Broccoli Sheet Pan Dinner (glazed-chicken-and-broccoli-sheet-pan-dinner.md)
CUISINES: American, Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/glazed-chicken-and-broccoli-sheet-pan-dinner/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodnetwork.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/food-network-kitchen/glazed-chicken-and-broccoli-sheet-pan-dinner-3543898
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken and vegetables ---
  - 4 skin-on chicken drumsticks
  - 3/4 lb fingerling potatoes, halved lengthwise
  - 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - salt, to taste for potatoes
  - black pepper, to taste for potatoes
  - 1 broccoli head, cut into small florets
  - salt, to taste for broccoli
  - black pepper, to taste for broccoli
  - --- Glaze ---
  - 2 tbsp teriyaki glaze, thick purchased glaze or prepared homemade glaze
  - 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The chicken and potatoes get a head start before the broccoli and ginger-teriyaki glaze go onto the pan. Leave enough room for the broccoli to spread out so it roasts at the edges instead of sitting in a crowded mound. A thin layer of glaze gives flavor without leaving a large sugary puddle to scorch.

## Directions

1. **Start chicken and potatoes:** Preheat the oven to 450°F. Line a large rimmed sheet pan with foil, or parchment rated by its manufacturer for this temperature. Use skin-on chicken drumsticks, fingerling potatoes, 1/3 of the extra-virgin olive oil, salt, and black pepper: pat the drumsticks dry with paper towels and space them on one side. Put potatoes on the other side, leaving room in the center for broccoli. Toss potatoes with their one-third share of the oil, salt and pepper. Roast about 20 minutes, until potatoes begin to soften and chicken begins to brown.
2. **Add broccoli:** Use 2/3 of the extra-virgin olive oil, broccoli head, salt, and black pepper: add broccoli to the center space, tossing it with the remaining two-thirds of the oil, salt and pepper. Spread into one layer. If the vegetables crowd the chicken or pile up, use a second rimmed pan rather than compressing everything.
3. **Brush on glaze:** Mix teriyaki glaze and fresh ginger in a small bowl and brush a thin, even layer over the chicken. Keep this brush and bowl separate from serving utensils. Discard any glaze left in the bowl after the brush touches partly cooked chicken.
4. **Finish roasting:** Return to the 450°F oven and roast about 20–25 minutes more. The potatoes should be tender and the broccoli browned in spots; check the thickest part of every drumstick, away from bone, for 165°F / 74°C. Continue cooking as needed. If the glaze darkens too quickly, loosely shield the chicken with foil while it reaches its endpoint. If vegetables sharing the chicken pan finish first, check that they have reached 165°F / 74°C after contact with chicken juices before transferring them with clean utensils to a clean dish. Vegetables cooked on a separate pan without chicken contact can be removed when tender. Continue cooking the chicken to its endpoint.
5. **Rest and serve:** Rest the safely cooked chicken for 5 minutes, then divide chicken and vegetables among the portions. Leave behind any scorched glaze on the pan rather than scraping it over the potatoes.

RECIPE: Gluten-Free Lemon Cupcakes (gluten-free-lemon-cupcakes.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/gluten-free-lemon-cupcakes/
SOURCE: Adapted from glutenfreepalate.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.glutenfreepalate.com/gluten-free-lemon-cupcakes/#mv-creation-79-jtr
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 1/4 cups gluten-free measure-for-measure baking flour blend containing xanthan gum
  - 1 1/2 tsp Gluten-free Baking Powder
  - 1/4 tsp Sea Salt
  - 3/4 cup Granulated Sugar
  - 1/2 cup Avocado or Canola Oil
  - 2 large Eggs
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Lemon Zest
  - 1/4 cup Fresh Lemon Juice (for the batter)
  - 1/2 cup Whole Milk
  - 1 tbsp Vanilla Extract
  - 1/2 cup (1 stick) Unsalted Butter, softened
  - 4 cups Confectioners’ Sugar
  - 2 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice (for the frosting)
  - 2 tbsp Milk (as needed)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Lemon juice and zest go into the batter, with a separate lemon supply for the buttercream. Use a measure-for-measure blend containing xanthan gum and mix just until incorporated. Cool the cupcakes completely before spreading the full buttercream.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line enough standard cupcake cups with paper liners; the original batch uses 12 cups. Wash lemons before zesting and juicing, and measure the batter and frosting juice separately.
2. **Dry:** Whisk all the flour blend, baking powder and salt together.
3. **Wet:** Beat all the oil and granulated sugar together about 1 minute. Add all the eggs one at a time, beating after each, then stir in all the vanilla, batter lemon juice and zest.
4. **Combine:** Add all the dry mixture and the full batter milk supply, mixing only until incorporated without dry flour pockets. Do not taste raw batter.
5. **Bake:** Divide all batter among the liners, about two-thirds full, using more or fewer same-sized cups when scaling. Bake about 18–20 minutes as the original-batch first check, until the center is set and a toothpick comes out clean; continue if wet batter remains.
6. **Cool:** Cool completely on a rack before frosting. Extra pans or batches add elapsed time; do not frost warm cakes.
7. **Buttercream:** Beat all the softened butter until creamy. Beat in all the separate frosting lemon juice, then add the full confectioners’ sugar in several portions, starting on low speed. Gradually add the listed frosting milk as needed for a spreadable consistency; it is separate from the full batter milk. Scrape and beat until smooth, without promising a stiff peak.
8. **Finish:** Divide all frosting among the cooled cupcakes. Store covered in the refrigerator as described below.

RECIPE: Gnocchi with Zucchini Ribbons & Brown Butter (gnocchi-with-zucchini-ribbons-and-parsley-brown-butter.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/gnocchi-with-zucchini-ribbons-and-parsley-brown-butter/
SOURCE: Adapted from Eatingwell.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/251860/gnocchi-with-zucchini-ribbons-parsley-brown-butter/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Fresh or Frozen Potato Gnocchi
  - 1 lb Zucchini (about 3 small), shaved into ribbons
  - 1 pint Cherry Tomatoes, halved
  - 2 tbsp Unsalted Butter
  - 2 medium Shallots, minced
  - 1/2 cup Fresh Parsley, chopped
  - 1/2 cup Freshly Grated Parmesan
  - 1/4 tsp Ground Nutmeg (The "High Note")
  - Salt and Black Pepper
  - 1/2 tsp salt, optional alternative to salt to taste; choose one salt route
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Watch the butter’s milk solids rather than waiting for all foaming to stop: they should begin turning golden and smell nutty before the shallots and thin zucchini ribbons go in. Toss the gnocchi gently so the full Parmesan and parsley coat it without crushing the pieces.

## Directions

1. **Cook gnocchi:** Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the fresh or frozen gnocchi according to its package, generally 3–5 minutes as a starting point, until floating and cooked through. Drain; do not automatically thaw a product whose package says to cook from frozen.
2. **Brown butter:** Meanwhile, melt all the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook until the milk solids begin turning golden and smell nutty, around 2 minutes as a guide. Lower the heat if they darken rapidly; do not wait for a fixed clock or complete cessation of foam.
3. **Cook vegetables:** Add all the minced shallots and washed, ribbon-thin zucchini. Cook, stirring often, about 2–3 minutes until softened. Use enough skillet batches for the full scaled vegetables, dividing the full butter and seasonings among them.
4. **Add tomatoes:** Add all the washed halved tomatoes, the salt from your chosen seasoning route, all the nutmeg and pepper to taste. Cook about 1–2 minutes until the tomatoes begin to release juices and break down.
5. **Combine:** Add all the drained gnocchi, Parmesan and parsley and toss gently until coated and the cheese melts. Combine all cooked batches for serving if a bowl gives more room than the skillet.
6. **Serve:** Serve promptly, keeping the gnocchi intact rather than tossing vigorously against a crowded pan.

## Cooking Notes

Cut ribbon-thin zucchini lengthwise with a vegetable peeler or mandoline. Use a guard with the mandoline.

RECIPE: Golden Veil (golden-veil.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/golden-veil/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 oz soft, juniper-forward dry gin
  - 1.5 oz unaged mezcal
  - 2 oz cognac
  - 2.5 oz Fresh Lemon Juice (The Acid Balance)
  - 1 oz French honeyed herbal liqueur (40% ABV)
  - 0.5 oz Agave Syrup
  - 3 dashes Orange Bitters
  - 6 oz Prosecco, chilled
  - Lemon Peel Twist
  - Fresh Thyme Sprig
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Slap the thyme sprig sharply in your palm before garnishing - this ruptures oil glands and releases the herb's essence without the bitterness of muddling. Add Prosecco only after shaking and straining the base so bubbles stay effervescent, cutting through smoky mezcal and rich cognac. Express lemon peel over the rim for aromatic oils.

## Directions

1.  **Thermal Prep:** Chill a large coupe or wine glass in the freezer for 10 minutes.
2.  **The Base:** Combine gin, mezcal, cognac, lemon juice, French honeyed herbal liqueur, agave, and orange bitters in a shaker filled with large ice cubes.
3.  **Aeration:** Shake vigorously for 15 seconds until the shaker is frosted and the mixture is perfectly emulsified.
4.  **Strain:** Double strain into the chilled glass to ensure a silky mouthfeel.
5.  **The Crown:** Top with the chilled Prosecco. Do not stir - let the bubbles naturally integrate the layers.
6.  **The Slap:** Take the thyme sprig, slap it between your palms, and place it in the glass. Express the lemon peel over the rim and drop it in for the mandatory **High Note**.

RECIPE: Brined Roast Turkey, Inspired by Good Eats (good-eats-roast-turkey.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/good-eats-roast-turkey/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodnetwork.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/alton-brown/good-eats-roast-turkey-recipe-1950271
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Turkey and brine ---
  - 1 whole young turkey, 14–16 lb (6.4–7.3 kg), fully refrigerator-thawed, not kosher, pre-brined or enhanced with a salt solution
  - 225 g salt, weighed regardless of crystal size
  - 100 g light brown sugar
  - 3.8 L unsalted vegetable stock, divided
  - 3.8 L cold water, for the brine
  - 1 tbsp whole black peppercorns
  - 1 1/2 tsp whole allspice berries
  - 10 g candied ginger, chopped
  - --- Roasting ---
  - 2 tbsp canola or other neutral oil
  - 150 g red apple, cored and sliced
  - 100 g peeled onion, sliced
  - 1 cinnamon stick
  - 4 small rosemary sprigs
  - 6 sage leaves
  - 1 cup (240 ml) water, for the roasting pan, plus up to 2 cups (480 ml) hot water if needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Adapted from Alton Brown’s Good Eats turkey, this roast starts with an aromatic wet brine. Weigh the salt, use unsalted stock and keep the turkey refrigerated throughout brining. Roast at a steady 325°F and check the required internal temperatures before removing it from the oven.

Salt changes how meat proteins interact with water and seasons the bird; brining is not simply water being driven inward by osmosis, and it cannot prevent all moisture loss from overcooking. The spices mainly flavor the brine and surface. Dry the skin after brining, and give the meat enough time without using skin color as a thermometer.

## Directions

1. **Make and chill the brine concentrate:** Put 1 L of the measured stock in a saucepan with all the weighed salt, sugar, peppercorns, allspice and ginger. Bring to a simmer and stir until dissolved, then remove from heat. Cool the saucepan in an ice-water bath, stirring the brine without getting bath water into it, then refrigerate until 40°F / 4°C or below. Keep the remaining 2.8 L stock and 3.8 L water cold. Budget up to two hours for cooling and use a thermometer rather than a clock to confirm readiness.
2. **Brine for twelve hours:** Remove packaging, neck and giblet bags from the fully thawed turkey. Reserve neck/giblets separately under appropriate refrigerated storage or discard. Combine the cold concentrate, remaining cold stock and measured water in a food-grade brining container. Submerge the turkey breast-side down, cover, and refrigerate for twelve hours at 40°F / 4°C or below. If necessary use a close-fitting food-grade brining bag supported in a deep leak-catching container; do not top up with plain water or leave the setup outside the refrigerator. The turkey’s original raw-storage limit still applies.
3. **Drain and dry:** Lift the bird carefully, letting cavity liquid drain into the container. Discard all used brine. Do not rinse the turkey in the sink. Pat dry with disposable towels, remove clinging spice pieces, and set on a rack over a rimmed tray, uncovered in the refrigerator, for four hours. Keep it below and separate from ready-to-eat foods. Clean raw-poultry contact surfaces.
4. **Prepare for roasting:** Heat the oven to 325°F / 163°C. Put the apple, onion, cinnamon, rosemary, sage and initial cup of pan water below a rack in a shallow roasting pan. Set turkey breast-side up on the rack, leaving its cavity empty; cook any dressing separately. Tuck wing tips underneath and brush the skin with the measured oil. Place a probe in the thickest breast meat without touching bone if using a leave-in thermometer.
5. **Roast and check the whole bird:** Roast for roughly 3 3/4–4 1/4 hours, beginning checks around three hours. Keep a shallow film of liquid in the pan, adding the listed hot water in small amounts if it dries; do not pour water over the skin. Shield areas that brown early loosely with foil. Before removing the bird, use an instant-read thermometer to verify at least 165°F / 74°C in both thick breast sections, the innermost part of each thigh and the innermost wing areas, away from bone. Continue cooking if any site is below that endpoint. The time is a planning range, not a finish guarantee.
6. **Rest and carve:** Transfer to a clean carving board, cover loosely and rest thirty minutes. Remove breast meat from the breastbone and slice across its grain; separate leg and thigh joints for serving. Offer about twelve portions with sides, distributing light and dark meat as desired. Pan aromatics are for flavoring drippings rather than a required side; discard them after straining drippings if used.

## Planning notes

This is an unstuffed, conventionally raised whole turkey of the stated size. A different size, a pre-brined bird, a breast-only roast or a tightly stuffed cavity requires a different plan. It remains distinct from the smaller dry-brined [Roast Turkey](/mise/recipes/simple-roast-turkey) and [Herb-Roasted Turkey Breast](/mise/recipes/roast-turkey-breast). Brined drippings can be salty; gravy is a separate preparation and should not receive automatic extra salt.

RECIPE: Grandmommy’s Pecan Pie (grandmommys-pecan-pie.md)
CUISINES: Southern
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/grandmommys-pecan-pie/
SOURCE: Adapted from Miriam Hamilton
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 Pie Shells (unbaked)
  - 2 cups Whole Pecans (halved)
  - 1 1/4 cups Granulated Sugar
  - 1/2 cup White Karo Syrup
  - 4 large Eggs, slightly beaten
  - 1/2 stick (4 tbsp) Unsalted Butter, melted
  - 1 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - Pinch of Sea Salt
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Southern pecan pie is built on a simple syrup custard that's meant to barely set - you're aiming for that wobbling center that firms up completely as it cools. Karo syrup is traditional for a reason: it creates the right balance of sweetness and texture without crystallizing. Don't skip the cooling step; this pie needs at least two hours to develop its proper structure.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 350°F. Place the unbaked pie shells on a baking sheet.
2.  **The Mix:** In a large bowl, whisk together the sugar, Karo syrup, and slightly beaten eggs until well combined.
3.  **The Emulsion:** Slowly whisk in the melted butter, vanilla, and salt until the filling is glossy and uniform.
4.  **Layer:** Divide the pecans evenly between the two pie shells. Pour the syrup mixture over the pecans - they will naturally float to the top to create the Crunch layer.
5.  **Bake:** Bake for 40-45 minutes until the edges are set and the center has a slight, stable wobble (the Texture).
6.  **Cool:** Let cool completely (at least 2 hours) before slicing. This is mandatory for the structure to set.

RECIPE: Grandmommy’s Pound Cake (grandmommys-pound-cake.md)
CUISINES: Southern
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/grandmommys-pound-cake/
SOURCE: Adapted from Miriam Hamilton
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3/4 lb (3 sticks) Unsalted Butter, softened
  - 6 large Eggs, room temperature
  - 2 cups Granulated Sugar
  - 3 cups All-Purpose Flour, pre-sifted
  - 1 tsp Lemon Extract
  - 1 tsp Almond Extract
  - 1 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Grandmommy’s pound cake has a rich, buttery crumb. The key is baking at 275°F for a full 90 minutes; this ensures the cake rises evenly without a tough outer crust, resulting in a dense, velvety texture that defines a true pound cake. Room temperature eggs are mandatory for a perfect emulsion.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 275°F. Generously grease and flour a large Bundt pan or three 9x5 loaf pans.
2.  **Cream:** In a stand mixer, cream the butter and sugar on medium-high for 5-7 minutes until the mixture is pale, light, and doubled in volume.
3.  **Emulsify:** Add the eggs one at a time, beating for 30 seconds after each addition to ensure a stable structure.
4.  **Incorporate:** Reduce speed to low. Gradually add the pre-sifted flour in three parts, mixing until **just combined**.
5.  **Flavor:** Fold in the lemon, almond, and vanilla extracts by hand.
6.  **Bake:** Pour the thick batter into the prepared pan. Bake at 275°F for 1.5 hours (or at 300°F for 1 hour if using loaf pans) until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
7.  **Cool:** Let cool in the pan for 20 minutes before inverting onto a rack.
