RECIPE: Grandmommy’s Turkey Dressing (grandmommys-turkey-dressing.md)
CUISINES: Southern, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/grandmommys-turkey-dressing/
SOURCE: Grandmommy
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Cornbread ---
  - 1 cup self-rising cornmeal mix, spooned into the cup and leveled; use an unsweetened mix containing leavening and salt
  - 1 cup (120 g) all-purpose flour
  - 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk
  - 8 tbsp (113 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled until just warm
  - 3 large eggs
  - --- Dressing ---
  - 180 g plain white sandwich bread, about 6–7 ordinary slices, weighed before drying
  - 150 g celery, finely diced, about 3 medium stalks
  - 200 g yellow onion, finely diced, about 1 large onion
  - 4 1/2 cups (1080 ml) unsalted chicken or turkey stock, measured as a reserve; add only as needed, including the portion used for the vegetables
  - 2–3 tsp salt-free poultry seasoning, to taste
  - 1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, plus up to 1/2 tsp more after tasting
  - 2 tsp softened unsalted butter, divided, for greasing both pans
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Grandmommy's dressing combines unsweetened cornbread, white bread and poultry seasoning for a soft, spoonable center and browned edges. Cook the vegetables until tender before mixing, then add stock gradually until the bread is moist without a pool of liquid.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the cornbread:** Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Grease an 8-inch square metal pan with one teaspoon of the pan butter. Whisk the self-rising cornmeal mix and flour in one bowl. In another, whisk the milk, eggs and just-warm melted butter. Fold wet into dry only until no dry flour remains. Do not taste the raw batter. Spread in the pan and bake promptly.
2. **Bake and cool:** Bake about 30–40 minutes, checking at 30 minutes, until golden and a tester inserted in the center comes out with crumbs but no wet batter. Cool in the pan on a rack for 15 minutes, then turn out carefully and cool another 30–45 minutes, until no warmth remains in the middle. A compact crumb is acceptable for this dressing; a gummy, underbaked center is not.
3. **Dry the white bread during cooling:** Reduce the oven to 300°F / 150°C. Tear the white bread into small pieces and spread in one layer on a rimmed sheet. Dry about 15–25 minutes, turning once, until a cooled piece feels dry through the center, with little browning. Already dry bread may need less time. Cool on the sheet while the vegetables cook; this cooling overlaps the cornbread cooling period.
4. **Tenderize the vegetables:** Put onion, celery and half a cup of the measured stock in a covered skillet. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook about 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the celery is tender and the onion has no raw bite. If the pan dries before the vegetables soften, add a spoonful of stock from the measured supply. Keep any remaining pan liquid; it counts toward the dressing's total stock.
5. **Crumble, season and hydrate:** Heat the oven to 350°F / 177°C and grease a roughly 3-quart, 9-by-13-inch dish with the remaining teaspoon of butter. Crumble the entire cooled cornbread into coarse crumbs in a very large bowl; add the dried white bread, cooked vegetables and their liquid. Fold in two teaspoons of poultry seasoning, the pepper and half a teaspoon of salt. Fold in further stock in half-cup additions, allowing each addition to absorb before deciding on the next. Once evenly damp, wait five minutes, then add more stock a quarter-cup at a time only if dry centers remain. Stop when a spoonful forms a loose, moist mound without liquid collecting beneath it; the full reserve is not compulsory. Stock used for the vegetables comes from this same measured supply. Taste a cooled spoonful now that the eggs and flour are cooked; add the remaining seasoning or salt only if needed.
6. **Bake immediately:** Spread loosely in the prepared dish without pressing it dense. Bake uncovered about 50–60 minutes, until the center reaches at least 165°F / 74°C and the surface and edges are golden. Check around 40 minutes; if the top browns too quickly, cover loosely with foil and finish to the measured center temperature.
7. **Rest and serve:** Rest 10 minutes and spoon into twelve side portions. Serve with turkey and tart cranberry sauce; the cranberry supplies brightness without changing the family dressing's flavor.

RECIPE: Executive Granola (granola.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/granola/
SOURCE: Adapted from Gwock Family
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups Old-fashioned Rolled Oats (not quick)
  - 1/2 cup Mixed Nuts (Almonds, Walnuts, Pecans), chopped
  - 1/4 cup Seeds (Sunflower or Sesame)
  - 1/2 cup Canola or Avocado Oil
  - 1/3 cup Pure Maple Syrup
  - 2 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - 1 tsp Ground Cinnamon
  - 1/2 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1/2 cup Dried Fruit (Raisins or Cranberries)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This is the go-to granola recipe for batch breakfast prep. The secret to getting those perfect clusters is creating a stable emulsion: whisk the oil and maple syrup together before pouring over the oats. This ensures every grain is coated in a thin layer that caramelizes beautifully in the oven. Roast at 350°F and stir twice to ensure even browning, but only add the dried fruit after the granola has cooled to prevent it from turning into rock-hard pieces.

## Directions

1.  **Dry Mix:** Preheat oven to 350°F. In a large bowl, toss together oats, nuts, and seeds.
2.  **The Emulsion:** In a separate jar or bowl, whisk together the oil, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt until smooth and uniform.
3.  **Combine:** Pour the liquid emulsion over the dry mix. Toss with a spatula until the oats look dark and saturated.
4.  **The Roast:** Spread the mixture in a thin, even layer on a large rimmed baking sheet.
5.  **Stir:** Bake for 20-25 minutes. **Stir the granola every 8 minutes** to ensure the edges don't burn and the center gets crispy.
6.  **The Finish:** Remove from the oven when deep golden brown. The granola will still feel soft; it will Crunch only after cooling.
7.  **Finish:** Once stone-cold, stir in the dried fruit. Store in an airtight glass jar for up to 3 weeks.

RECIPE: Grapefruit-Basil Gin Fizz (grapefruit-basil-gin-fizz.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/grapefruit-basil-gin-fizz/
SOURCE: Adapted from rachaelraymag.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.rachaelraymag.com/recipe/grapefruit-basil-gin-fiz
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 oz London dry gin
  - 3/4 cup Fresh Pink Grapefruit Juice
  - 1/4 cup Tonic Water or Seltzer
  - 1/2 tsp Fresh Basil, finely chopped
  - 3 dashes aromatic bitters (The Finishing Touch)
  - 1 Fresh Basil sprig
  - Large Ice Cubes
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Muddling the basil before adding liquids releases its chlorophyll and essential oils, creating the botanical foundation of this cocktail. Fresh pink grapefruit provides bright acidity, amplified with aromatic bitters to bridge the gap between bitter tonic and sweet citrus. The result is a refreshing, herbaceous drink perfect for warm weather.

## Directions

1.  **Muddle:** Place the chopped basil in the bottom of a tall Collins glass or highball glass. Use a muddler or the back of a spoon to press firmly for 10 seconds.
2.  **Thermal Prep:** Fill the glass to the brim with large ice cubes.
3.  **Combine:** Pour in the gin and the fresh grapefruit juice. Stir twice to integrate.
4.  **Effervescence:** Top with the tonic water or seltzer. Do not stir again - let the bubbles carry the basil essence to the top.
5.  **The Finishing Touch:** Add 3 dashes of bitters directly onto the surface.
6.  **The Slap:** Take the basil sprig, slap it between your palms to release the scent, and tuck it into the ice as a garnish.

RECIPE: Greek-Style Lamb Burgers with Mint Yogurt (greek-style-lamb-burgers-with-yogurt-cucumber-sauce.md)
CUISINES: Greek-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/greek-style-lamb-burgers-with-yogurt-cucumber-sauce/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/greek-style-lamb-burgers-with-yogurt-cucumber-sauce
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Lamb patties ---
  - 680 g ground lamb, preferably about 80–85% lean
  - 60 g yellow onion, very finely minced
  - 1 clove garlic, finely grated, for the patties
  - 3 tbsp finely chopped fresh mint, for the patties
  - 3 tbsp finely chopped fresh parsley
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, for the patties
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper, for the patties
  - 2 tsp olive oil, for the skillet, divided
  - --- Mint tzatziki ---
  - 1 1/2 cups prepared [Mint Tzatziki with Honey](/mise/recipes/mint-tzatziki), approximately
  - --- To serve ---
  - 4 pita breads, about 6–7 inches across; warm using [Warm, Soft Pita Bread](/recipes/warm-pita-bread)
  - 40 g crumbled feta, optional
  - 200 g ripe tomato, sliced, optional
  - 40 g mixed greens, washed and dried, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Mint and parsley lighten the impression of rich lamb, while thick yogurt adds a cool tang. Fine onion disperses through the patty; large wet pieces create weak spots. Fold the mixture only until it holds together. Shape affects how the burger fits the pita, but an oval is not a special guarantee of rendered fat or crispness.

## Directions

1. **Make the sauce and prepare toppings:** Make one full batch of [Mint Tzatziki with Honey](/mise/recipes/mint-tzatziki), approximately 1 1/2 cups, or measure the same amount already prepared. This is the sauce counted in the ingredients; make it once. Refrigerate while preparing the meat. Slice any optional tomato and wash/dry greens before handling raw lamb. Heat the oven to 350°F / 175°C for the bread.
2. **Mix and shape:** Combine cold lamb with onion, patty garlic, the three tablespoons each of mint and parsley, patty salt and patty pepper. Fold gently just until evenly mixed and cohesive. Divide into four equal patties, each using about 170 g meat plus its share of aromatics. Shape into broad rounds or ovals about 3/4 inch thick. Keep the second pair refrigerated while the first cooks.
3. **Cook the first pair:** Heat a 12-inch heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tsp of the skillet oil and two patties with space between them. Cook about 4–5 minutes on the first side until well browned, then turn with a broad spatula. Reduce to medium as needed and cook another 4–5 minutes, then check from the side into each center. Continue cooking and turning as needed until each reaches 160°F / 71°C; allow roughly 10–14 minutes per batch. Do not press out the juices. Transfer to a clean plate and cover loosely.
4. **Cook the second pair and warm bread:** Carefully spoon excessive rendered fat into a heatproof container, leaving a thin film in the pan; add the remaining 1 tsp skillet oil. Cook the second pair with the same temperature check. During this batch, warm the four pitas as a foil-wrapped stack using the [oven method](/mise/recipes/warm-pita-bread#oven-alternative), without the optional finishing oil or salt. Check the center bread and keep the stack wrapped. The first patties soften and cool slightly during this brief wait; a large griddle avoids the wait if available.
5. **Balance and assemble:** Stir and taste the chilled mint tzatziki. Start with 2–3 tbsp inside each pita and offer the remaining sauce alongside. Add one cooked patty to each and divide any optional feta, tomato and greens among them. Fold or serve open-faced if the bread is small. Serve promptly.

## Grill option

Use clean grates and a medium-high cooking zone with a cooler area available. Use the same two teaspoons of cooking oil to lightly brush the patties instead of adding it to a skillet. Turn when a crust forms; move away from flare-ups caused by dripping fat. Cook every patty to 160°F / 71°C measured at its center. Warm the bread separately and assemble as above.

## Sauce alternative

If [Dill Tzatziki](/mise/recipes/tzatziki-sauce) is already prepared, use about 1 1/4 cups in place of the entire batch of Mint Tzatziki with Honey. Do not make both. Keep its original preparation date when planning storage.

RECIPE: Greek-Style Turkey Meatball Pitas (greek-turkey-meatball-gyro-with-tzatziki.md)
CUISINES: Greek-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/greek-turkey-meatball-gyro-with-tzatziki/
SOURCE: Adapted from Joyfulhealthyeats.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.joyfulhealthyeats.com/greek-turkey-meatball-gyro-with-tzatziki/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Turkey meatballs ---
  - 450 g ground turkey, 93% lean
  - 30 g baby spinach, washed, thoroughly dried and finely chopped
  - 40 g red onion, very finely minced, for the meatballs
  - 2 cloves garlic, finely grated
  - 1 tsp dried oregano
  - 3/8 tsp fine salt, for the meatballs
  - 1/4 tsp ground black pepper, for the meatballs
  - 1 tbsp olive oil, for the tray and meatball surfaces, divided
  - --- Cucumber-yogurt sauce ---
  - 3/4 cup (180 g) plain full-fat Greek yogurt
  - 75 g English cucumber, coarsely grated then squeezed, for the sauce
  - 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus 1 tsp more only if needed
  - 1/2 tsp dried dill
  - 1/4 tsp garlic powder
  - 1/8 tsp fine salt, for the sauce
  - --- To serve ---
  - 4 pita breads, about 6–7 inches across; warm using [Warm, Soft Pita Bread](/recipes/warm-pita-bread)
  - 200 g ripe tomato, diced
  - 100 g English cucumber, diced, for serving
  - 30 g red onion, thinly sliced, for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This is a Greek-inspired meatball sandwich, not shaved spit-roasted gyro meat. A little finely chopped spinach adds moisture and color, but turkey still needs careful cooking. Roasting all twelve meatballs together avoids repeatedly rolling a fragile mixture around a crowded skillet. The resulting crust is lighter than a hard pan sear.

## Directions

1. **Heat and prepare:** Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Brush a rimmed half-sheet pan with 1 tsp of the oil. Wash, dry and cut the vegetables as listed, keeping the sauce cucumber separate from the serving cucumber. Reserve the remaining 2 tsp oil for the meatball surfaces.
2. **Make the sauce:** Squeeze the grated 75 g sauce cucumber in a clean towel until dripping slows, then stir into yogurt with the initial tablespoon of lemon juice, dill, garlic powder and sauce salt. Refrigerate. Keep the serving tomato, cucumber and sliced onion separate; do not stir them into the meat.
3. **Mix and portion:** Fold turkey with dried chopped spinach, the 40 g minced onion, fresh garlic, oregano, meatball salt and pepper. Mix just until evenly distributed and cohesive. Divide into twelve equal balls, roughly 45 g each and about 1 1/2 inches across. Set apart on the prepared tray and dab their surfaces with the remaining 2 tsp oil. Wash hands and raw-meat utensils before touching bread or sauce.
4. **Roast and measure:** Roast for about 15–20 minutes. Start checking at fifteen minutes by inserting a thermometer into the center of several of the largest balls; all checked centers must reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue cooking those that need it and check again. Do not wait for a dark crust if the centers are already done.
5. **Warm the bread:** During the roast, use a separate skillet and the [pita warming method](/mise/recipes/warm-pita-bread), omitting its optional oil and salt. Keep the four breads wrapped. Stir and taste the sauce, adding the reserved teaspoon of lemon only if needed.
6. **Fill and serve:** Divide sauce among the pitas, then put three cooked meatballs in each. Divide tomato, serving cucumber and sliced onion across the four. Fold loosely or serve open-faced. Serve promptly; the meatballs do not need a ten-minute rest before assembly.

## Sauce alternative

Use about 1 cup [prepared Dill Tzatziki](/mise/recipes/tzatziki-sauce) instead of the whole inline sauce if it is already available. This is a substitution, not an extra component.

RECIPE: Greek Village Salad (Horiatiki) (greek-village-salad.md)
CUISINES: Greek, Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/greek-village-salad/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 600 g ripe tomatoes, cut into large bite-sized pieces
  - 300 g English cucumber, cut into thick half-moons
  - 120 g green bell pepper, seeded and sliced
  - 50 g red onion, thinly sliced
  - 1/3 cup (60 g) drained Kalamata olives, pitted
  - 150 g feta, in thick slices
  - 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, plus 1 tsp more only if needed
  - 1 tsp dried oregano
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, only as needed
  - 1/8 tsp black pepper, optional
  - 1 tbsp drained capers, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This horiatiki-style salad centers on tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, olives, and feta. Keep the pieces substantial enough to retain their individual texture. Tomato juice becomes part of the dressing, so a modest amount of oil and vinegar is enough. Taste the vegetables with the brined cheese and olives before adding salt.

## Directions

1. **Prepare vegetables:** Wash and dry the produce, cut as listed, and place tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, and onion in a wide serving bowl. If the onion tastes particularly sharp, rinse its slices briefly, then drain and dry them first.
2. **Dress lightly:** Add olive oil, the initial tablespoon of vinegar, and oregano. Toss gently. Fold in olives and optional capers.
3. **Add feta and taste:** Lay feta slices on top. Taste a complete bite with a little cheese and olive. Add some of the measured salt only if needed, optional pepper, and the extra teaspoon of vinegar only if the vegetables need more brightness.
4. **Serve:** Divide among four plates, distributing vegetables, olives, and feta. Serve promptly. Keep any prepared-ahead components refrigerated and combine them shortly before eating.

RECIPE: Greek Yogurt Bowl (greek-yogurt-bowl.md)
CUISINES: Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/greek-yogurt-bowl/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup Plain Full-Fat Greek Yogurt

RECIPE: Green Beans with Shallots and Lemon (green-beans-with-shallots-and-lemon.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/green-beans-with-shallots-and-lemon/
SOURCE: Adapted from downshiftology.com
SOURCE_URL: https://downshiftology.com/recipes/green-beans-with-shallots/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 450 g green beans, trimmed
  - 60 g peeled shallots, finely diced
  - 1 tbsp unsalted butter
  - 1 tsp honey, optional
  - 1 tsp finely grated lemon zest
  - 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus up to 1 tsp more to taste
  - 2 L water, for boiling
  - 10 g salt, for the boiling water
  - 1/8 tsp fine salt, for finishing, optional after tasting
  - 1/8 tsp freshly ground black pepper
  - 2 tbsp water, for warming the beans if needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Cook the beans to a texture you enjoy, then dress them. Shallots bring a gentle sweetness; a teaspoon of optional honey is enough to soften the lemon edge without turning this into candied vegetables. Lemon goes in at the end because prolonged heating with acid dulls green color. An ice bath slows further cooking when holding beans ahead, but does not permanently protect their color or texture.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the vegetables and water:** Trim the beans, rinse and drain. Dice the shallots, zest the lemon and measure its juice. Bring two liters of water with ten grams salt to a boil in a 4-quart pot. Begin the shallots in step three while the water heats if you can watch both pans.
2. **Cook to tenderness:** Add beans and return to a gentle boil. Begin tasting after three minutes; many beans need four to six minutes, and very thick ones can need longer. A cooled piece should bite cleanly with a little resistance. Drain thoroughly. For immediate serving, keep them warm and move straight to the skillet finish; do not chill them first.
3. **Soften shallots:** Melt butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-low heat. Add shallots and cook five to seven minutes, stirring, until softened and translucent. Lower heat if they begin browning sharply. Use a small splash from the listed finishing water if needed to help them soften.
4. **Warm and coat:** Add the drained beans and optional teaspoon of honey. Toss gently over medium heat for two to three minutes until hot and lightly coated. If the pan is dry, add a little of the remaining finishing water. For refrigerated prepared-ahead beans, allow about four to six minutes, cover briefly with the water as needed, and check they reach 165°F / 74°C before proceeding; then uncover so excess water evaporates.
5. **Finish off heat:** Remove from heat. Add lemon zest, the first tablespoon of juice and pepper. Toss, taste a bean and add the optional finishing salt or extra teaspoon of juice only if needed. Divide among four plates and serve promptly.

## Preparing ahead

After step two, chill beans in a bowl of ice water until cold, then drain thoroughly and refrigerate as described above. This makes the final shallot-and-bean step easier to coordinate with a roast, at the cost of another heating cycle. Use fresh lemon at service. Do not leave a bowl of cooked beans at room temperature for the afternoon.

RECIPE: Thai Green Curry with Chicken (green-curry-chicken.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/green-curry-chicken/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 680 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
  - 400 ml full-fat unsweetened coconut milk, divided
  - 3 to 4 tbsp Thai green curry paste, according to its strength
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil, only if needed when frying the paste
  - 1 cup (240 ml) unsalted chicken stock, plus a little hot water only if needed to loosen
  - 250 g Japanese or Chinese eggplant, trimmed, halved lengthwise and sliced 1/2 inch thick
  - 150 g red bell pepper, sliced
  - 75 g canned bamboo shoots, drained and rinsed
  - 4 makrut lime leaves, torn into large pieces
  - 20 g Thai basil leaves
  - 1 tbsp fish sauce, added gradually only as needed
  - 1 tsp palm sugar or brown sugar, plus a little more only if needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Chicken, Asian eggplant, red pepper and bamboo shoots sit in a fragrant coconut sauce with Thai basil. Leave enough sauce to spoon around the solids and over rice. Cook the paste until fragrant without scorching it; some canned coconut milks will not visibly split into oil.

## Directions

1. **Prepare ingredients:** Cut vegetables and pick basil before handling raw chicken, then clean the board and tools. Measure 120 ml of the coconut milk for the paste; use the thick top portion if it has separated, or stir the can and measure if uniform. Reserve the rest.
2. **Cook coconut and paste:** In a wide saucepan, simmer the 120 ml coconut milk over medium heat about 3–5 minutes until thickened, stirring. Add green curry paste and cook about 2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant. If it sticks and has not released oil, add the measured tablespoon of neutral oil; a small splash of the reserved coconut milk can also loosen the pan. Do not require darkening or oil pooling before continuing.
3. **Start chicken:** Stir in chicken, remaining coconut milk, stock and torn lime leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer, separating the chicken pieces, and cook about 5 minutes. Do not taste the curry while chicken is still undercooked.
4. **Cook vegetables and check:** Add eggplant, pepper and bamboo shoots. Simmer gently about 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally so pieces are exposed to the hot liquid, until eggplant is tender and several thick chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Extend as needed; if chicken finishes well before eggplant, follow troubleshooting.
5. **Season and finish:** Add the sugar and start with about 1 tsp fish sauce. Taste and add more fish sauce only as needed; some pastes need very little. If too thick, add a small splash of hot water. Remove the large lime-leaf pieces, turn off heat, and fold in basil. Serve four main portions with separately prepared plain rice.

RECIPE: Green Smoothie (green-smoothie-for-kids-with-2-hidden-veggies.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/green-smoothie-for-kids-with-2-hidden-veggies/
SOURCE: Adapted from theconsciousplantkitchen.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.theconsciousplantkitchen.com/green-smoothie-for-kids/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3/4 cup Almond Milk (or milk of choice)
  - 1 medium Banana
  - 1/4 Fresh Avocado (for richness)
  - 1/2 cup Frozen Mango Chunks
  - 1 tbsp Rolled Oats (for sustained nutritious)
  - 1 cup Fresh Baby Spinach (Hidden Veggie #1)
  - 2 tsp Nut Butter (Almond or Sunflower)
  - 1/2 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - 1-2 tsp Maple Syrup (Optional)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Frozen mango and fresh avocado blend together into a thick, creamy smoothie that masks spinach's leafy texture. The avocado provides healthy fats and silkiness, while oats add complex carbohydrates for sustained energy. Vanilla extract creates milkshake-like aroma that makes this green smoothie appealing to young palates.

## Directions

1.  **The Stack:** In a high-speed blender, add ingredients in this exact order: milk, oats, spinach, banana, avocado, and finally the frozen mango. Placing the greens at the bottom ensures they are completely pulverized first.
2.  **Process:** Blend on low, then quickly increase to high speed. Process for 60 seconds until the mixture is a vibrant, uniform green with no visible leaf flecks.
3.  **Adjust:** If the smoothie is too thick, add a splash more milk. If you need more "High Note" sweetness, add 1 tsp of maple syrup and pulse again.
4.  **Serve:** Serve immediately in a chilled glass with a wide straw.

## Cooking Notes

For a gluten-free version, use certified gluten-free oats or millet flakes in place of the rolled oats.

RECIPE: Grilled Cheese and Tomato Soup (grilled-cheese-and-tomato-soup.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/grilled-cheese-and-tomato-soup/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 (28 oz) can whole peeled San Marzano-style tomatoes, with their juices
  - 1 small onion, diced
  - 2 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1 tbsp unsalted butter, for the soup
  - 1/2 cup heavy cream
  - 1 cup chicken broth
  - 1 tsp dried basil
  - 4 slices sourdough or brioche, of similar size and moderate thickness
  - 4 thin slices sharp Cheddar or Gruyère, sized to fit the bread
  - 1/2 avocado, thinly sliced
  - 2 tbsp mayonnaise, for the outside of the bread
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Make the soup first and keep it gently hot while the sandwiches cook. A thin mayonnaise layer helps the bread brown evenly, but heat control still matters: lower the heat if the crust darkens before the cheese melts. Avocado belongs inside, where it contrasts with the crisp exterior.

## Directions

1. **Soften aromatics:** Melt the measured butter in a saucepan over medium-low. Cook onion about **6–8 minutes** until soft, then add garlic for **30–45 seconds** until fragrant.
2. **Simmer soup:** Add all listed tomatoes and juices, broth and dried basil. Break up tomatoes with a spoon, bring to a gentle simmer and cook about **15 minutes**, stirring, until soft. Prepare sandwich ingredients while it simmers.
3. **Blend and add cream:** Remove from heat and let active bubbling stop. Blend with an immersion blender, keeping its guard submerged and stopping before lifting it. Alternatively, cool to your countertop blender’s permitted temperature and blend in as many small batches as its hot-liquid fill limit requires, with the lid and steam vent arranged exactly as its instructions specify. Start low; do not use a sealed personal cup for hot soup. Stir in cream and season with salt and pepper. Warm gently and keep hot at **140°F / 60°C or above** for the brief sandwich cooking period, without a hard boil.
4. **Assemble sandwiches:** Spread a thin layer of mayonnaise on one face of each bread slice, using only what is needed from the measured allowance. Place **half the bread slices**, mayonnaise-side down, in a cool skillet. Divide all the cheese and avocado evenly over these bases. Top with the remaining bread, mayonnaise-side up.
5. **Toast gently:** Set over medium-low to medium heat. Cook about **4–6 minutes per side**, turning carefully, until golden and cheese has melted in the center. Lower heat if bread colors too quickly; cover briefly if the center needs help warming, then uncover. Use additional rounds if the skillet is crowded.
6. **Serve together:** Cut sandwiches as desired and divide the soup among the intended portions. Serve immediately for dipping; do not leave the sandwiches sitting in the soup.

RECIPE: Chicken with Herbed Corn Salsa (grilled-chicken-with-herbed-corn-salsa.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/grilled-chicken-with-herbed-corn-salsa/
SOURCE: Adapted from Goodhousekeeping.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.goodhousekeeping.com/food-recipes/a40851/grilled-chicken-with-herbed-corn-salsa-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 1/4 lbs Skin-on, Bone-in Chicken Thighs
  - 2 large ears Fresh Corn, shucked
  - 1 cup Fresh Basil, packed
  - 1/2 cup Fresh Mint, packed
  - 1/4 cup Freshly Grated Parmesan
  - 1 clove Garlic
  - 1/4 cup Fresh Lemon Juice
  - 2 tbsp Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - Salt and Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Mexican-inspired grilled chicken showcases summer corn charred directly on the grill until the kernels develop smoky, caramelized spots. The herb salsa combines fresh basil and mint with lemon and Parmesan, creating a bright, aromatic topping. The lemon's acidity cuts through the rich fat of chicken thighs.

## Directions

1. **Grill chicken:** Preheat the grill to medium-high. Season all the thighs with the listed salt and pepper allowance. Grill skin-side down first, turning as the surface browns; start checking at 15–20 minutes total and continue until the thickest part of each thigh reaches 165°F / 74°C, away from the bone. Move away from flare-ups or excessive direct heat. Transfer cooked chicken with clean utensils to a clean platter.
2. **Grill corn:** Grill all the shucked corn, rotating occasionally, for about 10 minutes, until the kernels are tender and charred in spots. Keep ready-to-eat corn away from raw chicken and its utensils.

4. **Combine:** When the corn is safe to handle, cut all its kernels off the cobs into a bowl and mix them with all the herb sauce.
5. **Serve:** Divide the chicken and complete corn-herb topping among the listed portions and serve promptly.

RECIPE: Pork and Peaches (grilled-pork-and-peaches.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/grilled-pork-and-peaches/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/12690-grilled-pork-and-peaches
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Pork and seasoning ---
  - 2 lb Boneless pork butt or shoulder, butterflied and trimmed
  - Salt, to taste for pork
  - Black pepper, to taste for pork
  - --- Garlic–rosemary paste and pan oil ---
  - 8–10 Garlic cloves, peeled and minced
  - 2 tbsp Fresh rosemary, minced
  - 8 tbsp Extra-virgin olive oil
  - --- Buttered peaches ---
  - 6 Fresh peaches, washed, skin on, halved and pitted
  - 4 tbsp Unsalted butter, diced
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Butterflied pork shoulder is pounded to an even thickness so its centers cook more evenly. Cook it and the skin-on peach halves on a solid cast-iron pan or griddle over the grill, where the full butter and pan oil can stay with the food. Pounding does not turn this into a slow-braised cut, and buttered peaches need not finish at the same time as the pork. Keep a clean resting board and check the pork before its 5-minute rest.

## Directions

1. **Pound and season:** Prepare Boneless pork butt or shoulder, Salt, and Black pepper on a raw-meat board. Pound the butterflied pork with a meat mallet to an even approximately ¾ inch thickness and season with the salt and pepper allowances. Keep it refrigerated if waiting while preparing the grill.
2. **Coat both sides:** Mix Garlic cloves, Fresh rosemary, and 3/4 of the Extra-virgin olive oil into a paste in a small bowl and spread over both sides of the prepared pork, dividing evenly. This is three-quarters of the total olive oil; the remaining quarter is reserved for the cooking surface.
3. **Heat solid cooking surface:** Heat a large cast-iron pan or griddle over the grill. Once hot, reduce a gas grill to medium or move away from an intense fire as needed. Brush the solid surface with 1/4 of the Extra-virgin olive oil, shared across the chosen pan area. For two pans, divide this allocation across both. Use shimmering oil as the cue and manage heat rather than insisting on prolonged smoking.
4. **Brown the pork:** Place the coated pork on the hot solid surface. Leave it long enough to form a golden crust, beginning checks before the original approximately 8–10 minute first-side interval if the heat is strong. Lower or move away from intense heat if garlic is blackening before the pork center cooks. Turn with raw-pork tongs, then keep those tools separate from serving tools.
5. **Cook buttered peaches:** While the pork cooks, arrange Fresh peaches and Unsalted butter in a separate solid pan brushed with part of the reserved pan oil. The separate pan keeps ready fruit apart from raw pork juices. Put peaches cut-side down and dot with all the diced butter. Begin checking after about 5 minutes for softened fruit and browned faces; remove ready peaches with clean utensils to a clean platter. If the pan cannot hold a single layer, cook fruit in additional loads, sharing the full butter across them. Keep the fruit pan and its utensils separate from the raw-pork paste and cooking tools.
6. **Finish and rest:** Continue cooking pork on its second side, beginning checks during the original 5–7 minute interval and allowing longer if needed. Check several thick centers for at least 145°F /63°C before removal. Transfer with clean utensils to a clean board and rest 5 minutes, meeting the minimum 3-minute rest. Do not infer doneness from color or assume it finishes with the peaches.
7. **Slice and serve:** Slice the rested pork across the grain and serve with the buttered peaches. If serving pooled aqueous juices from the pork-cooking pan, bring those juices to a rapid boil before serving and use clean utensils. This means the watery juices, not the oil; do not add liquid to create a boil. Juices from the clean resting board may be served with the rested pork. Never add liquid from the raw-pork board or paste bowl.

RECIPE: Banh Mi (grilled-pork-banh-mi.md)
CUISINES: Vietnamese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/grilled-pork-banh-mi/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/grilled-pork-banh-mi
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Pork and marinade ---
  - 1 1/2 lb pork tenderloin or pork butt, raw, fresh or fully thawed; thinly sliced
  - 1/4 cup fish sauce
  - 2 tbsp sugar
  - 1 tbsp honey
  - 3 garlic cloves, peeled and minced
  - 2 lemongrass stalks, tough outer layers removed; white parts finely minced
  - suitable grilling oil, as needed for the grates or grill basket
  - --- Bread and cold toppings ---
  - 2 crusty baguettes, soft crumb and crisp crust; cut into serving lengths
  - [Pickled Carrots and Daikon](/mise/recipes/quick-pickled-carrots-and-daikon), as wanted for the sandwiches; prepared ahead, chilled and drained
  - fresh cilantro, as wanted for the sandwiches, washed
  - jalapeños, as wanted for heat, washed and sliced
  - cucumber spears, as wanted for the sandwiches, washed and cut
  - mayonnaise, a generous layer as wanted
  - liquid seasoning or soy sauce, a few drops as wanted per sandwich
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Bánh mì sandwiches bring grilled pork, crisp bread, cool pickled vegetables, cilantro and creamy mayonnaise together. This lemongrass version uses the listed sugar and honey with fish sauce and garlic; a medium grill helps keep the sweet coating from blackening. Drain the pickles for assembly so they brighten the filling without soaking the bread.

## Directions

1. **Marinate the pork cold:** Have pork tenderloin or pork butt, fish sauce, sugar, honey, garlic cloves, and lemongrass stalks ready. Whisk the full fish sauce, sugar, honey, garlic and lemongrass supply together, then toss with all the thinly sliced pork. Cover and refrigerate at 40°F or below for at least 2 hours, or overnight. Keep the entire batch coated and use enough covered food-safe vessels for larger batches.
2. **Prepare the pickles:** If not prepared ahead, make the linked [Pickled Carrots and Daikon](/mise/recipes/quick-pickled-carrots-and-daikon) while the pork marinates: allow about 20 minutes cutting and packing, then at least 1 hour in the refrigerator. Keep them refrigerated until assembly; choose the serving amount separately rather than assuming the full pickle recipe is used.
3. **Grill the thin pork:** Thread the pork onto suitable skewers or use a grill basket, following the equipment’s preparation instructions. Use suitable grilling oil as needed for the cooking surface. Lift the pork from the marinade and wipe away excess; discard the raw-contact marinade. Grill uncrowded slices over medium heat, starting checks around 3–4 minutes per side, until browned without blackening and at least 145°F in the thickest part, measured from the side with a thermometer suitable for thin food. Pork butt and tenderloin can differ in chewing texture; neither is guaranteed finished by the clock. Keep waiting raw pork refrigerated and add grill loads as needed.
4. **Rest cooked pork:** Transfer fully cooked pork to a clean platter and rest at least 3 minutes before assembly. Use clean utensils and remove any skewers before eating.
5. **Assemble and serve:** Use crusty baguettes, [Pickled Carrots and Daikon](/mise/recipes/quick-pickled-carrots-and-daikon), fresh cilantro, jalapeños, cucumber spears, mayonnaise, and liquid seasoning or soy sauce. Split the measured bread, spread generously with mayonnaise and add a few drops of liquid seasoning or soy sauce. Divide all the cooked pork among the serving lengths; layer cucumber, drained chilled pickles and cilantro, then jalapeños if wanted. Serve promptly. Four portions is the current original-batch plan, not a measured baguette-size yield.

RECIPE: Grilled Zucchini with Mint and Lemon (grilled-zucchini-with-mint.md)
CUISINES: Mediterranean-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/grilled-zucchini-with-mint/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 680 g small-to-medium zucchini, trimmed and sliced lengthwise into 3/8-inch planks
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, divided between cooking and finishing
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt
  - 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
  - 2 tbsp fresh mint leaves, torn
  - 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus 1 tsp more only if needed
  - 1 tsp finely grated lemon zest
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Zucchini needs enough heat to brown, but an extremely hot grill can blacken the contact lines before a thick center softens. Even planks and a fork check make the method repeatable. Finish with lemon and mint after cooking, then serve with their aroma still fresh.

## Directions

1. **Heat and slice:** Preheat a clean grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. Trim zucchini and slice into even 3/8-inch lengthwise planks. Pat the surfaces dry. For a stovetop pan, plan several uncrowded rounds.
2. **Oil and season:** Reserve 1/2 tbsp of the oil for finishing. Brush the remaining 1 1/2 tbsp over both sides of all the planks and distribute the measured salt and pepper. Oil coats the vegetables; do not add another unmeasured pour to the pan.
3. **Cook in batches:** Lay planks across the grill bars with space, using tongs. Cook about 3–4 minutes per side, turning once they release and have browned patches. Reduce heat if they blacken quickly. Check a thick center with a fork: it should be tender with light resistance, and the plank should lift intact. Transfer to a broad platter and repeat with remaining planks; do not pile and tightly cover the finished ones.
4. **Dress and taste:** Drizzle the cooked zucchini with the reserved 1/2 tbsp oil and initial tablespoon of lemon juice. Add mint and zest, then turn gently. Taste before adding any of the optional extra teaspoon of lemon.
5. **Serve:** Divide into four sides and serve warm, or after a brief hold while the main finishes. The planks will soften somewhat as they stand; this is not a promise that holding always improves them.

RECIPE: Guacamole (guacamole.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/guacamole/
SOURCE: Adapted from Alton Brown's Guacamole
SOURCE_URL: https://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/alton-brown/guacamole-recipe-1940609
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 ripe Hass avocados
  - 1 large lime, juiced, divided
  - 1/2 medium red onion, finely diced
  - 1/2 jalapeño, seeded and finely minced
  - 2 Roma tomatoes, cored, seeded and finely diced
  - 1 clove garlic, finely minced
  - 1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
  - 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided
  - 1/2 tsp ground cumin
  - 1/2 tsp ground cayenne pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Adapted from Alton Brown's guacamole, this version combines avocado with tomato, garlic, cumin and cayenne. Keep the tomatoes well drained and fold them in after mashing. Add lime and salt in stages, and cover the surface closely during a refrigerated rest to limit exposure to air.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Rinse produce before cutting. Dice the onion and tomatoes, removing tomato cores and loose seed pulp; drain excess tomato juice. Mince jalapeño and garlic, chop cilantro, and juice the lime.
2. **Mash:** Halve and pit the avocados and scoop the flesh into a bowl. Toss with half the lime juice. Add half the measured salt, the cumin and cayenne, then mash with a fork or potato masher until creamy with small soft chunks.
3. **Fold:** Gently fold in the onion, tomatoes, jalapeño, garlic and cilantro until distributed. Keep the vegetables in distinct pieces rather than puréeing them into the mash.
4. **Rest and season:** Smooth the surface, press food wrap against it and refrigerate for about one hour. Stir gently and taste with a tortilla or other accompaniment. Add remaining lime and salt gradually only as needed. For immediate service, skip the rest and make the same seasoning check.
5. **Serve:** Share as four generous dip portions or use smaller spoonfuls as a taco or fajita topping. Finished volume varies with avocado size. Keep covered and refrigerated until needed.

RECIPE: Gwock Family Macaroni and Cheese (gwock-family-macaroni-and-cheese.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/gwock-family-macaroni-and-cheese/
SOURCE: Gwock Family
INGREDIENTS:
  - 8 oz. macaroni
  - 1 lb Cheese (medium) cut in chunks
  - 4 eggs
  - 1/2 stick margarine
  - milk
  - 1/2-3/4 tsp salt
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The Gwock family recipe uses eggs and chunks of medium cheese rather than a flour-thickened sauce. Add milk until the macaroni is almost covered, as the original specifies; the exact milk volume and cheese type were not recorded. Beat the eggs before combining and use the center temperature to decide when the casserole is ready.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 475°F. For the original batch, use a 9 × 9-inch baking dish rated for that temperature, with enough depth and headroom for the milk-filled pasta. Cut all the cheese into chunks and thinly slice all the margarine. Beat all the eggs with the listed salt in a separate bowl.
2. **Boil:** Boil all the macaroni in salted water, beginning the original recipe's check at 10 minutes and checking the actual package and pasta texture. Drain well and let the pasta cool from steaming-hot to warm before adding beaten eggs.
3. **Combine:** Mix the full cheese and margarine supplies through the drained pasta, then fold in all the beaten eggs and salt evenly. Transfer to the baking dish. Add milk until the macaroni is almost covered; stir gently so the egg mixture is distributed throughout. Do not overfill the vessel.
4. **Bake:** Bake at 475°F, checking before the end of the original 20–25-minute window. Continue until the center reaches 165°F / 74°C and the custard is set, without a pool of liquid egg. Check each dish if the batch is divided.
5. **Stand:** Stand 5 minutes before serving.

RECIPE: Ham & Cheese Green Bean Casserole (ham-and-cheese-green-bean-casserole.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/ham-and-cheese-green-bean-casserole/
SOURCE: Adapted from Gwock Family
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Beans and pan ---
  - unsalted butter, as needed for greasing the dish
  - 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth or water
  - 1 lb fresh green beans, washed, trimmed and cut into 2-inch lengths
  - --- Full casserole filling ---
  - 2 cans (10 3/4 oz) condensed cream of mushroom soup
  - 3/4 cup half-and-half
  - 1 tsp garlic powder
  - 1/2 tsp kosher salt
  - 1/2 tsp black pepper
  - 1/2 lb cooked ham, diced; ready-to-eat product
  - 1/2 cup yellow onion, diced
  - 2 1/2 cups sharp cheddar cheese, freshly grated
  - 1 cup canned French fried onions
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Adapted from the Gwock Family recipe. Parboil the beans until they begin yielding, then drain before mixing so the condensed soup stays concentrated. Most of the cheddar and half the fried onions go inside; the reserved amounts finish on top near the end of baking.

## Directions

1. **Prepare dish:** Heat oven to 350°F. For the original batch, use unsalted butter to butter a 9×13-inch oven-safe baking dish. Use enough dishes for similar filling depth with room below the rim when scaling.
2. **Parboil beans:** Set out low-sodium chicken broth or water and fresh green beans. Bring the blanching liquid to a boil in a saucepan, then add the beans. Begin checking around 5–6 minutes after adding beans: they should yield with slight resistance rather than remain hard or fall apart. Drain immediately without rinsing. Keep blanching liquid separate from casserole filling; discard it, or cool promptly and refrigerate separately if saving for another use.
3. **Combine filling:** Set out condensed cream of mushroom soup, half-and-half, garlic powder, kosher salt, black pepper, cooked ham, yellow onion, 4/5 of the sharp cheddar cheese, and 1/2 of the canned French fried onions. Whisk all the soup, half-and-half, garlic powder, salt and pepper together. Fold in all the drained beans, cooked ham, diced onion and the allocated cheese/fried onions. Four-fifths of the full cheddar and half the fried onions go inside; reserve the rest for the finishing stage. Do not dilute the condensed soup with the blanching broth.
4. **Heat the full casserole:** Transfer all filling to the buttered dishes. Bake at 350°F, starting checks around 30 minutes for the original pan, until bubbling toward the center. This begins the final check rather than certifying the center by color alone.
5. **Add reserved topping:** Scatter 1/5 of the sharp cheddar cheese and 1/2 of the canned French fried onions over the full filling, dividing the topping among dishes. Continue baking, starting checks around 10 minutes later, until the center reaches 165°F /74°C and the onions are golden. Check every dish; tent lightly if toppings brown before its center is ready.
6. **Rest and serve:** Rest 5 minutes before dividing the full casserole into the listed portions. The short rest thickens the hot sauce; keep leftovers chilled promptly.

RECIPE: Ham & Cheese Quiche (ham-and-cheese-quiche.md)
CUISINES: French
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/ham-and-cheese-quiche/
SOURCE: Adapted from iheartnaptime.net
SOURCE_URL: https://www.iheartnaptime.net/ham-and-cheese-quiche/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 9-inch Deep-dish Pie Crust (unbaked)
  - 1 cup Cooked Ham, cubed
  - 1 cup Sharp Cheddar, shredded
  - 1/2 cup Mozzarella, shredded
  - 1/2 cup Fresh Spinach, chopped
  - 1/2 cup Yellow Onion, minced
  - 1 tbsp Unsalted Butter
  - 5 large Eggs
  - 1/2 cup Half-and-Half (for texture)
  - 1/2 tsp Dried Parsley
  - 1/4 tsp Black Pepper
  - Pinch of Nutmeg
  - 1/4 cup cooked bacon, chopped, optional
  - Butter or oil, as needed to grease a separate dish for excess filling
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Sauté the onion in butter before adding the cooked ham, then whisk parsley, pepper and nutmeg into the custard so they season every slice. This version uses a deep-dish shell and a relatively egg-heavy filling. A brief parbake starts the crust cooking but does not guarantee a dry bottom; the shell instructions and its actual depth matter.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the shell:** Preheat the oven to 400 °F. Place the 9-inch deep-dish shell on a baking sheet. Follow its own instructions for partial baking, including any weights or docking they require. For a shell whose instructions permit this brief parbake, prick the bottom and bake 5–7 minutes to begin cooking it, then set aside. This short parbake is not a guarantee against sogginess; other shell instructions can take longer.

2. **The Sauté:** Melt the butter in a small skillet over medium heat. Sauté the minced onion for about 2–3 minutes, until softened and translucent, then add the cooked ham and optional cooked bacon. Cook about 2 minutes more, until warmed through and lightly browned in places. Set aside to cool slightly.

3. **The Custard:** Whisk the eggs and half-and-half with all the dried parsley, black pepper and pinch of nutmeg until smoothly blended. Do not whip to a thick foam.

4. **Assemble:** Scatter the ham-onion mixture, chopped spinach, cheddar and mozzarella into the partly baked shell. Slowly pour the custard over the fillings. Leave room below the rim; deep-dish shells vary. If it will not fit, bake the excess in a separate suitable greased oven-safe dish rather than overflowing the crust.

5. **Bake:** Reduce the oven to 375 °F. Bake for about 25–35 minutes as a first range, until the center is set with no liquid egg and measures 165 °F / 74 °C, checking without touching the crust or pan. The top may be golden; shield the crust edge with foil if it colors before the center is ready, and continue baking as needed.

6. **Rest:** Rest 10 minutes before slicing. The full original batch makes eight portions; apportion a different batch size accordingly. Refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers and use within 3 days. Reheat centers to 165 °F / 74 °C; cover the crust to limit further browning.

RECIPE: Hamantaschen (hamantaschen.md)
CUISINES: Jewish
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/hamantaschen/
SOURCE: Adapted from ToriAvey.com
SOURCE_URL: https://toriavey.com/toris-kitchen/buttery-hamantaschen/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Butter dough ---
  - 3/4 cup unsalted butter, room temperature
  - 2/3 cup granulated sugar
  - 1 large egg, room temperature
  - 1 tsp pure vanilla extract
  - 1 tsp orange zest, grated
  - 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
  - 1/4 tsp sea salt
  - 1–5 tsp water, cold; only as needed, optional
  - all-purpose flour, a little only if the dough is too sticky, optional
  - --- Rolling and pan supplies ---
  - all-purpose flour, enough to dust the surface and rolling pin lightly
  - butter or baking spray, enough to lightly grease baking sheets
  - --- Filling — choose one ---
  - apricot jam, poppy seed paste, or chocolate-hazelnut spread, enough for up to 1 tsp per 3-inch cookie; choose one filling
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Hamantaschen are triangular Jewish cookies for Purim. Keep the butter dough cool enough to handle, and give each flap one over-and-one-under corner. The 3-inch circle has room for no more than a teaspoon of filling. Pinching and repairing cracks improve the fold, but filling consistency and dough thickness still affect leakage.

## Directions

1. **Cream:** Beat unsalted butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
2. **Add egg and flavorings:** Beat in large egg, pure vanilla extract, and orange zest until evenly combined, scraping the bowl.
3. **Mix the dough:** Sift in all-purpose flour and sea salt and mix on low until a crumbly dough forms.
4. **Bring the dough together:** Have water (if using) and all-purpose flour (if using) available only if needed. Knead the crumbles gently into a smooth, slightly tacky ball. Add the listed water slowly, a little at a time, only if the dough is too dry to join; in the original batch use 1–5 tsp total as needed, adding about 1 tsp at a time. Scale that total range with the dough, but continue adding small increments by feel. If it becomes sticky, knead in a little of the optional flour. Stop once the dough holds together and can be rolled; avoid overworking it.
5. **Chill:** Flatten into a disk, wrap and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below for at least 3 hours or overnight.
6. **Prepare to assemble:** Choose and prepare the filling before rolling; follow its own recipe or product instructions. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Use all-purpose flour and butter or baking spray for handling: lightly flour the work surface and rolling pin, then lightly grease the sheets with the butter or spray.
7. **Roll and cut:** Roll to the main ⅛-inch thickness. If needed, begin around ¼ inch, lift the dough with a pastry scraper, lightly re-flour and flip it, then finish rolling. Repair cracks with your fingers. Cut 3-inch circles and gather and re-roll scraps gently until all usable dough is portioned; avoid adding unnecessary flour. Keep unused circles covered with a lightly damp towel while filling. The listed cookie count is a planning value; thickness changes yield. Larger batches need more sheets and oven loads, with the same circle size and thickness.
8. **Fill and fold:** Use apricot jam, poppy seed paste, or chocolate-hazelnut spread, placing no more than 1 tsp in each 3-inch circle. Fold the left side toward the center; fold the right side so its upper part overlaps the left flap. Fold the bottom up with its left corner under the left flap and its right corner over the right flap. Each flap then has one corner over and one under, leaving a small center of filling visible. Pinch the corners gently but firmly and repair cracks; Keep the filling away from the seams and make each fold secure.
9. **Bake:** Space the cookies on the prepared sheets and wait for the oven to reach 350°F. The main route is 20–25 minutes per oven load, until cooked through and lightly golden. Begin checking at 10 minutes when cookies are thin: thickness and filling can make them finish sooner. Keep unbaked dough refrigerated between loads.
10. **Cool and store:** Cool completely on a wire rack before storing airtight. Follow the selected filling’s storage requirements; refrigerate cookies with perishable filling at 40°F / 4°C or below promptly, within 2 hours or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C.

## Cooking Options

### Rolling thickness

The main route uses ⅛-inch dough. Tori Avey’s thinner, more delicate option rolls just under ⅛ inch while keeping the dough strong enough to hold the filling. Her thicker, more doughy option stays closer to ¼ inch and makes fewer cookies from the same dough. Keep the 3-inch cutter and the one-teaspoon maximum filling per circle for either option; do not force the listed count by changing thickness. Check thin cookies from 10 minutes and continue only until cooked through and lightly golden.

Apricot jam, poppy seed paste and chocolate-hazelnut spread are separate filling choices, not three additions to each cookie. Their preparation, total quantity and storage requirements depend on the selected filling; a homemade filling needs its own complete recipe.

RECIPE: Har Gow (Shrimp Dumplings) (har-gow-dim-sum-shrimp-dumplings.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/har-gow-dim-sum-shrimp-dumplings/
SOURCE: Adapted from thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/har-gow/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1/2 lb Raw Shrimp, peeled, deveined, and patted dry
  - 1/4 cup Bamboo Shoots, finely minced
  - 1 tsp Oyster Sauce
  - 1 tbsp Vegetable Oil
  - 1/4 tsp White Pepper
  - 1 tsp Toasted Sesame Oil
  - 1/4 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1 tsp Granulated Sugar
  - 1/2 tsp Fresh Ginger, minced
  - 1 cup Wheat Starch (Tin Mein Fun)
  - 1/2 cup Cornstarch or Tapioca Starch
  - 1 1/4 cups Boiling Water
  - 3 tsp Lard or Neutral Oil
  - 1 to 2 tsp boiling water, optional only if the dough cracks in dry conditions
  - Neutral oil, as needed for the flat-blade shaping option
  - Chili oil and soy sauce, as desired for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Har gow are Cantonese dim sum shrimp dumplings with translucent wrappers. They use a boiling-water starch dough, distinct from egg-and-flour wonton wrappers. Keep the dough covered as you work. Stir the shrimp filling in one direction until sticky, then fold in the bamboo shoots; fill lightly enough that the wrappers close without tearing.

## Directions

1. **Mix filling:** Thaw frozen shrimp in the refrigerator if needed and pat dry. Mash and coarsely chop large shrimp; for small shrimp, the source also permits leaving them whole or halving them. Combine with all the oyster sauce, measured vegetable oil, white pepper, sesame oil, sea salt, sugar and minced ginger. Stir vigorously in one direction for about 3 minutes until sticky, then fold in all the minced bamboo shoots. Cover and refrigerate for a 30-minute chill while preparing the dough; keep the filling cold between assembly batches.
2. **Mix dough:** Whisk all the wheat starch and your chosen cornstarch or tapioca starch in a heatproof bowl. Slowly pour in the full measured boiling water while stirring rapidly, then add all the measured lard or neutral oil. Wheat starch is not interchangeable with wheat flour.
3. **Knead and divide:** When cool enough to handle without burning, knead about 2 minutes until smooth. If a test piece cracks when gently rolled, the source permits the listed optional extra boiling-water allowance in dry conditions; work it in cautiously, let it cool enough to handle and check again rather than automatically adding it. Divide into roughly the listed dumpling count, keeping each piece the original size, and cover with a damp towel. More or fewer same-sized pieces are needed at other scales.
4. **Roll:** Roll each piece into a thin circle about 3 inches across, keeping the remaining pieces covered. If using the flat-blade shaping option, lightly oil the blade with the separate tooling allowance; the measured dough and filling fats remain in their own mixtures.
5. **Fill:** Divide all the filling among the wrappers, starting with a modest spoonful rather than a fixed tablespoon in every piece. Fold and pleat to close, keeping the rim clean. Do not taste raw filling, and wash raw-contact hands and utensils before handling cooked dumplings.
6. **Steam:** Line a steamer with perforated parchment and bring its water to a boil. Leave about 1½ inches around dumplings for expansion and work in batches, replenishing the steamer according to its instructions. Cover and steam on high heat; begin checking around the source’s 6-minute mark rather than stopping at an exact clock. Check representative fillings, including a larger dumpling in each batch, for 165°F /74°C, continuing when needed. Use a thin probe without touching the steamer and check the center. Serve on a clean plate.
7. **Serve:** Serve hot with the optional chili oil and soy sauce. These are separate serving allowances, not required additions to the filling.

RECIPE: Harvest Sheet Pan Gnocchi with Kale (harvest-sheet-pan-gnocchi-with-crispy-kale.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/harvest-sheet-pan-gnocchi-with-crispy-kale/
SOURCE: Adapted from jenneatsgoood.com
SOURCE_URL: https://jenneatsgoood.com/harvest-sheet-pan-gnocchi-crispy-kale/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 12 oz Frozen Cauliflower Gnocchi
  - 12 oz Apple Chicken Sausage, sliced into rounds
  - 2 cups Butternut Squash, diced into 1/2-inch cubes
  - 2 cups Fresh Kale, shredded
  - 3 tbsp Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 2 tsp Dried Rosemary
  - 1 tsp Dried Thyme
  - 1/2 tsp Smoked Paprika
  - 1 tsp Garlic Powder
  - 1/3 cup Freshly Grated Parmesan or Nutritional Yeast
  - Salt and Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Sheet-pan gnocchi is a weeknight trick that turns frozen cauliflower gnocchi into something crispy and caramelized without a pot of boiling water. The key is a single layer - crowding the pan steams everything into mush instead of roasting it. The kale should emerge dark green and shatteringly crisp, which only happens if it gets coated in oil and given space.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
2.  **Toss:** In a massive bowl, combine gnocchi, sliced sausage, squash, and kale. Drizzle with 3 tbsp olive oil. Add rosemary, thyme, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper. Toss until every leaf and cube is coated.
3.  **Spread:** Spread the mixture in a **single layer** on the pan. (Crucial for the kale to crisp!)
4.  **Roast:** Bake for 24-26 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the squash is tender and the gnocchi are golden.
5.  **The Crunch:** The kale should be dark green and shatteringly crisp.
6.  **Finish:** Sprinkle with Parmesan or nutritional yeast while still piping hot. Serve immediately.

RECIPE: Apple Muffins (healthy-apple-muffins.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/healthy-apple-muffins/
SOURCE: Adapted from cookieandkate.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cookieandkate.com/healthy-apple-muffins-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 3/4 cups Whole Wheat Flour
  - 1 cup Grated Apple, squeezed dry
  - 1 cup Apple, diced into 1/4-inch cubes
  - 1/2 cup Applesauce (unsweetened)
  - 1/2 cup Maple Syrup
  - 1/3 cup Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 2 large Eggs
  - 1/2 cup Plain Greek Yogurt
  - 1 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - 1 1/2 tsp Baking Powder
  - 1/2 tsp Baking Soda
  - 1 tsp Ground Cinnamon
  - 1/2 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1 tbsp Turbinado Sugar (for the Crunch)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Grated apple spreads through the batter while the small diced pieces remain distinct. Applesauce and Greek yogurt stay alongside the full oil and maple syrup amounts. Mix until the dry ingredients are incorporated without extended beating, and distribute the whole turbinado sugar supply over the tops.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and dry:** Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line enough standard muffin cups; the original batch plans 12. Wash apples before grating or dicing and measure the prepared amounts. Whisk all the flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and salt together.
2. **Apples:** Add all the listed grated and diced apples to the dry mixture and stir to distribute them evenly.
3. **Wet:** Whisk all the oil and maple syrup together, then whisk in all the eggs, yogurt, applesauce and vanilla until evenly mixed.
4. **Combine:** Stir the complete wet mixture into the complete dry mixture only until incorporated. Small lumps are fine, but scrape the bottom and remove dry flour pockets; flour streaks are not required. Do not taste raw batter.
5. **Bake:** Divide all thick batter evenly among enough lined cups, leaving expansion room and maintaining the original cup size and similar fill depth. Sprinkle all the turbinado sugar over the tops. Bake about 13–16 minutes as the original-batch first check, until golden with set centers and a toothpick coming out clean. Extra tins or batches add time.
6. **Cool:** Cool in the pan about 5 minutes before carefully transferring to a rack to finish cooling; do not package warm muffins.

RECIPE: Banana Bread (healthy-banana-bread.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/healthy-banana-bread/
SOURCE: Adapted from cookieandkate.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cookieandkate.com/healthy-banana-bread-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Batter ---
  - butter or neutral oil, for greasing the pan
  - 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil
  - 1/2 cup honey or maple syrup
  - 2 large eggs
  - 1 cup (225 g) ripe banana, mashed
  - 1/4 cup milk of choice
  - 1 tsp baking soda
  - 1 tsp vanilla extract
  - 1/2 tsp sea salt
  - 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
  - 1 3/4 cups white whole-wheat flour
  - 1/2 cup dark chocolate chips or walnuts, chop walnuts if using, optional
  - ground cinnamon, a pinch for the top, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Whole-wheat flour, measured mashed banana and olive oil make a moist loaf sweetened with honey or maple syrup. Whisk the wet ingredients first, then fold the flour briefly and cool the loaf completely before slicing. Chocolate chips or walnuts are optional additions.

## Directions

1. **Preheat and grease the pan:** Preheat the oven to 325°F. Grease a 9-by-5-inch loaf pan for the original batch with butter or neutral oil. Measure the mashed banana before mixing.
2. **Whisk the wet ingredients:** In a large bowl whisk the extra-virgin olive oil, honey or maple syrup, large eggs, ripe banana, and milk of choice, combining the oil and honey or syrup first, beating in the eggs, then whisking in the banana and milk. Whisk until evenly combined; small banana lumps may remain.
3. **Distribute the soda and seasonings:** Whisk in the baking soda, vanilla extract, sea salt, and ground cinnamon until evenly distributed; break up any baking-soda lumps.
4. **Fold in the flour:** Switch to a large spoon or spatula and fold in the white whole-wheat flour until no dry pockets remain. Stop once combined; small banana lumps are fine.
5. **Add the optional mix-ins:** Gently fold in the dark chocolate chips or walnuts (if using).
6. **Fill and finish the loaf:** Scrape the batter into the prepared pan and level it gently. Sprinkle with ground cinnamon (if using); run a knife tip in a shallow zigzag to swirl the topping.
7. **Bake and cool:** Bake for about 55–60 minutes, checking the center at 55 minutes. A tester through the crumb should have no wet batter; try another spot if it hits melted chocolate. Continue baking if necessary and tent loosely with foil if the top darkens first. Cool in the pan on a rack for at least 10 minutes, loosen the edges and turn out carefully. Cool completely on the rack before slicing; allow about an hour, longer if still warm.

RECIPE: Carrot Cake Muffins (healthy-carrot-cake-muffins-with-cream-cheese-glaze.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/healthy-carrot-cake-muffins-with-cream-cheese-glaze/
SOURCE: Adapted from ambitiouskitchen.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.ambitiouskitchen.com/healthy-carrot-cake-muffins-cream-cheese-glaze/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Muffin batter ---
  - 1 1/2 cups whole-wheat pastry flour
  - 1 cup carrots, wash and finely shred before measuring
  - 1/2 cup pure maple syrup
  - 1/3 cup unsweetened applesauce
  - 1/2 cup unsweetened milk of choice
  - 1 large egg
  - 2 tbsp avocado or olive oil
  - 1 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
  - 1 tsp baking soda
  - 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
  - 1/4 tsp sea salt
  - 1 tsp pure vanilla extract
  - --- Optional mix-ins ---
  - 1/2 cup unsweetened shredded coconut, optional
  - 1/2 cup raisins, optional
  - 1/4 cup chopped walnuts or pecans, optional
  - --- Pan preparation ---
  - nonstick cooking spray, enough for the inside of the liners or the unlined wells
  - --- Cream-cheese glaze ---
  - 4 oz light cream cheese, softened
  - 1/4 cup powdered sugar
  - 1 tbsp milk
  - 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
  - --- Optional glaze thinning ---
  - 1 tbsp milk, optional
  - --- Optional finish ---
  - shredded coconut, a sprinkle after glazing, if desired, optional
  - chopped walnuts or pecans, a sprinkle after glazing, if desired, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Monique Volz’s carrot muffins use finely shredded carrots with maple syrup and applesauce, then a cream-cheese glaze. Fine shreds distribute through the batter without leaving large pieces. Stop stirring when the flour disappears, and let the muffins cool completely so the glaze stays on their tops.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 350°F. For the original batch, line a 12-cup muffin tin and coat the insides of the liners with nonstick cooking spray, or grease the unlined wells. Finely shred the carrots before measuring their listed volume. For a scaled batch use enough similar wells; mix-ins can change the amount of batter, so use another well or load rather than overflowing a cup.
2. **Mix dry ingredients:** Whisk whole-wheat pastry flour, ground cinnamon, baking soda, ground nutmeg, and sea salt in a medium bowl until evenly distributed.
3. **Mix the wet base:** In a large bowl, whisk carrots, pure maple syrup, unsweetened applesauce, large egg, avocado or olive oil, and pure vanilla extract until combined. The carrots remain finely shredded, not pureed.
4. **Combine:** Stir unsweetened milk of choice and the prepared flour mixture into the wet base just until no dry flour pockets remain. Stop mixing then; do not beat the batter smooth.
5. **Fold in optional mix-ins:** Fold any chosen unsweetened shredded coconut (if using), raisins (if using), and chopped walnuts or pecans (if using) through the batter. Each is optional; keep all the batter quantities whether using one, several or none.
6. **Fill and bake:** Divide the batter among the prepared wells without overflowing. Wait until the oven reaches 350°F, then bake for 18–20 minutes per load, until a center toothpick comes out clean. Check the center again if wet batter remains.
7. **Cool:** Rest the muffins in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack and cool completely before glazing. Extra oven loads and rack cooling take additional time.
8. **Mix the glaze:** Once the muffins are cool, whisk light cream cheese, powdered sugar, milk, and vanilla extract until smooth. Use the full glaze milk here, separate from the batter milk.
9. **Adjust the glaze:** If the glaze is too thick, gradually stir in milk (if using) as needed, stopping when it will coat a muffin top without running straight off. This additional milk is optional; do not add it automatically.
10. **Glaze and finish:** Dip the cooled muffin tops into the glaze, then return them to the rack. Add shredded coconut (if using) and chopped walnuts or pecans (if using) only if desired. Refrigerate the glazed muffins promptly.

## Cooking Notes

### Batter and glaze choices

White whole-wheat flour or all-purpose flour may replace the listed pastry flour at the same listed volume. Replace all the applesauce with one mashed ripe banana for the original twelve-muffin batch; scale that banana count with the batch. Use the same listed oil amount of melted, cooled coconut oil, walnut oil or butter instead of the avocado or olive oil, and any milk of choice at the listed batter volume. Nuts and nut oils affect allergen suitability.

The optional coconut, raisins and chopped nuts have independent listed amounts; do not take them out of the measured batter ingredients. Keep any extra coconut or nuts for the glazed tops separate from those mix-ins. If softened cream cheese will not mix smoothly, the original glaze method warms the cheese alone in a microwave-safe bowl for a reference 10–20 seconds, just until somewhat warm and soft, before adding the other glaze ingredients. Follow the appliance instructions and texture rather than multiplying that clock.

### Plant-based option

For the original one-egg batch, the publisher describes replacing the egg with 1 tbsp ground flaxseed mixed with 3 tbsp water; let it gel before adding to the wet base. Scale both amounts with the listed egg count. Use nondairy milk, the oil choice rather than butter, and omit the entire cream-cheese glaze, its additional milk and the optional glaze finishes. A little cinnamon and coarse sugar may be sprinkled on top instead. The egg-free batter can bind and bake differently; use the center check rather than assuming the same clock. The main recipe keeps its full egg and glaze.

### Make ahead

Freeze cooled unglazed muffins airtight for up to three months, then thaw and add the glaze when serving. For plain unglazed muffins, the publisher’s plan is an airtight day at room temperature followed by refrigeration for up to 4–5 days. Glazed muffins need prompt refrigeration; keep them at 40°F / 4°C or below and use within 3–4 days. Get the glaze and glazed muffins refrigerated within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C. Do not treat the plain-muffin room-temperature plan as a glazed-muffin allowance.

RECIPE: Heirloom Tomato & Pesto Galette (heirloom-tomato-pesto-and-ricotta-galette.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/heirloom-tomato-pesto-and-ricotta-galette/
SOURCE: Adapted from abrightmoment.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.abrightmoment.com/recipes/heirloom-tomato-pesto-ricotta-galette
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Dough ---
  - 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  - 3/4 cup cold butter, cubed
  - 4 tbsp ice-cold water
  - 1 tbsp granulated sugar
  - 1/2 tsp sea salt
  - all-purpose flour, for rolling
  - --- Filling and crust finish ---
  - 1 cup whole-milk ricotta
  - 1/2 cup sharp cheddar or Gruyère, shredded; choose one
  - 1/3 cup basil pesto, prepared homemade or store-bought
  - 3 medium heirloom tomatoes, washed before slicing thinly
  - 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - fresh chives and basil, chopped, for garnish
  - flaky sea salt and chile flakes, for finishing
  - extra-virgin olive oil, additional optional finishing drizzle, optional
  - whole-milk ricotta, additional optional finishing dollops, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Pesto and ricotta sit beneath the tomatoes, while the cheese and full measured olive oil finish the folded pastry. Pat the tomatoes dry before layering, but expect some juice as they bake. Keep the butter cold and check the pastry base as well as the golden folded edge.

## Directions

1. **Make and chill dough:** Pulse all-purpose flour, cold butter, ice-cold water, granulated sugar, and sea salt as follows: combine flour, sugar and salt, then add all cold butter and pulse until crumbly with visible pieces. Add the listed ice water and pulse briefly until the dough holds when pressed. Form a disk, wrap tightly and chill for 30 minutes. Do not work the pastry until the butter disappears into a warm paste.
2. **Heat oven and dry tomatoes:** Heat the oven to 425°F. Slice medium heirloom tomatoes thinly, lay them on clean absorbent towels and pat the tops dry. Remove surface moisture without pressing the slices into pulp; the tomatoes will still release some juice during baking. Use a rimmed baking sheet and parchment rated for the oven temperature.
3. **Roll and fill:** Use all-purpose flour, whole-milk ricotta, and basil pesto for assembly. Before rolling or filling, decide the pan load and divide the full measured dough, pesto, ricotta and dried tomatoes proportionally among the galettes being made. For the original batch, roll one 12-inch circle with a 2-inch border; a circle up to 14 inches may have a border up to 3 inches. Leave enough pastry to fold and check that its allocated filling can fit before spreading pesto or ricotta. Transfer each circle to the lined sheet, spread its allocated pesto within the border, distribute its allocated ricotta and lay its allocated tomatoes on top. Keep every measured portion in the planned galettes; do not wait until all the dough is filled to decide on additional galettes.
4. **Fold and finish crust:** Fold the dough border over the tomato edges, pleating without stretching. Use sharp cheddar or Gruyère and extra-virgin olive oil to finish the border: brush all the measured oil onto the folded pastry, then sprinkle all the shredded chosen cheese over it. The optional serving drizzle is a separate allowance.
5. **Bake:** Bake at 425°F, beginning checks around 25–30 minutes for the original galette, until the pastry edges are golden and baked through and the tomatoes are hot and juicy. Lift an edge carefully to inspect the base; continue if pastry underneath is still pale and doughy, shielding an already-browned edge if needed. Keep additional galettes uncrowded and allow extra oven rounds as needed.
6. **Serve:** Serve warm with fresh chives and basil, flaky sea salt and chile flakes, extra-virgin olive oil (if using), and whole-milk ricotta (if using). Distribute the herbs and finishing seasoning; add the separate extra oil drizzle or ricotta dollops only if wanted. Keep the full measured oil and ricotta already used in the galette distinct from these optional extras.

RECIPE: Herb Pork Tenderloin (herb-marinated-pork-tenderloins.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/herb-marinated-pork-tenderloins/
SOURCE: Adapted from foodnetwork.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/ina-garten/herb-marinated-pork-tenderloins-recipe-1948375
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Lemon–herb marinade ---
  - 3/4 cup Fresh lemon juice
  - 1 tbsp Lemon zest
  - 1/2 cup Extra-virgin olive oil for marinade
  - 2 tbsp Garlic, minced
  - 1 1/2 tbsp Fresh rosemary, minced
  - 1 tbsp Fresh thyme, chopped
  - 2 tsp Dijon mustard
  - 2 tsp Kosher salt for marinade
  - 3 Pork tenderloins, about 1 lb each in the original batch; keep individual diameter similar when scaling
  - --- Separate searing oil and seasoning ---
  - 3 tbsp Extra-virgin olive oil for searing
  - Kosher salt for meat seasoning, as needed before searing
  - Black pepper, to taste before searing
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Lemon juice, zest, rosemary and thyme flavor the refrigerated marinade. Its olive oil is separate from the oil used for searing. Discard the raw-contact liquid while leaving the herbs that cling to the pork, then cook each tenderloin to 145°F before removing it from the oven and rest 10 minutes. The marinade’s acidity does not justify an enzyme claim or a lower cooking endpoint.

## Directions

1. **Mix the coating or marinade:** Mix Fresh lemon juice, Lemon zest, Extra-virgin olive oil for marinade, Garlic, Fresh rosemary, Fresh thyme, Dijon mustard, and Kosher salt for marinade in a clean bowl or raw-meat container before adding the pork.
2. **Coat and refrigerate:** Add Pork tenderloins to the prepared lemon–herb marinade in a sealable raw-meat container or sturdy bag and turn to coat. Seal and refrigerate for at least 3 hours, preferably overnight. Keep the container separate from ready-to-eat ingredients.
3. **Discard marinade and sear:** Heat the oven to 400°F. Lift the tenderloins out, discard the raw-contact liquid and leave the herbs that cling to the meat. Have Extra-virgin olive oil for searing, Kosher salt for meat seasoning, and Black pepper ready. Season the pork with the separate salt and pepper allowances. Heat the measured pan oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering and sear the tenderloins on all sides until golden. Use manageable loads and divide that pan oil over the loads as needed; it is the whole batch amount, not 3 tbsp per skillet.
4. **Roast and check every piece:** Transfer the oven-safe skillet to the oven; if the batch needs more room, use an oven-safe roasting pan with space between the pieces. Begin checking after about 10 minutes and continue until the thickest center of every tenderloin reaches at least 145°F /63°C before removal. Do not assume that rest will supply a missing cooking temperature.
5. **Rest on a clean platter:** Transfer ready tenderloins to a clean platter, cover with foil. **Rest for 10 minutes** before carving each tenderloin. This exceeds the minimum 3-minute rest after the measured 145°F endpoint. Keep hot handles protected and avoid the raw marinade vessel.
6. **Slice and serve:** Carve across the grain into roughly ½-inch diagonal slices. Serve warm with the juices collected on the clean resting platter.
