RECIPE: Lemon Ricotta Pasta (lemon-ricotta-pasta.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/lemon-ricotta-pasta/
SOURCE: Adapted from Delish, Lemon Ricotta Pasta
SOURCE_URL: https://www.delish.com/cooking/recipe-ideas/a26830130/ricotta-pasta-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb dry bucatini or spaghetti
  - 1 cup fresh whole-milk ricotta
  - 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, including any finishing drizzle
  - 1/2 cup freshly grated Pecorino Romano
  - 1 lemon, zested before juicing
  - 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes
  - 1/2 cup fresh basil, torn
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  - 1 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Ricotta, Pecorino and a generous measure of olive oil make this a rich sauce. Whisk it while the pasta boils, then loosen with hot cooking water and toss in a bowl. Cook the pasta to the texture you want before draining: the off-heat finish will coat it, not replace another minute of boiling.

## Directions

1. **Start water and sauce:** Bring a large pot of water to a boil and season moderately with salt; the Pecorino will also season the dish. Zest then juice the lemon. If you want a finishing drizzle, set aside a little of the measured oil first. In a large heatproof bowl, whisk ricotta, the remaining oil, Pecorino, zest, **half the lemon juice** and pepper flakes.
2. **Cook to tenderness:** Add pasta and stir as it softens. Follow package timing, tasting a strand near the end. Cook until tender with a little bite and no hard center. Before draining, scoop out **the listed cooking-water reserve**. Drain without rinsing.
3. **Loosen the sauce:** Whisk about **one-quarter of the reserved water** into the ricotta mixture. Add more a little at a time only if it is still too stiff to fold through the pasta.
4. **Toss and finish:** Add hot pasta to the bowl and toss thoroughly, adding further warm cooking water in small splashes until coated and slightly loose. Fold in basil and black pepper. Taste a complete bite, then add remaining lemon juice and salt only as needed. Use any oil deliberately reserved for finishing and serve promptly.

Adapted from [Delish’s Lemon Ricotta Pasta](https://www.delish.com/cooking/recipe-ideas/a26830130/ricotta-pasta-recipe/).

RECIPE: Lemony Broccoli Pasta (lemony-broccoli-pasta.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/lemony-broccoli-pasta/
SOURCE: Adapted from The Kitchn, Lemony Broccoli Pasta
SOURCE_URL: https://www.thekitchn.com/recipe-lemony-broccoli-pasta-253244
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb dry spaghetti
  - 5 cups fresh broccoli florets, cut into small bite-sized pieces, thick stems sliced thinner
  - 1 cup frozen peas
  - 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil
  - 3/4 cup freshly grated Parmesan
  - 1 lemon, zested before juicing
  - 1 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Broccoli and pasta can share a pot when their timing lines up. Cut the florets small and check both before draining; cook the peas by their package directions alongside. Finish away from direct heat, adding Parmesan and warm cooking water gradually for a light coating.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cut broccoli into small bite-sized florets and slice thick stems thinner. Zest and juice the lemon, grate Parmesan and measure the oil. Season the boiling water moderately with salt.
2. **Cook pasta and broccoli:** Add spaghetti and stir as it softens. Follow package timing. Add broccoli when about **3–5 minutes** remain, return to a gentle boil and check both for tenderness. RECIPE: Lime & Honey Glazed Salmon (lime-and-honey-glazed-salmon-with-warm-black-bean-and-corn-salad.md)
CUISINES: Mexican, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/lime-and-honey-glazed-salmon-with-warm-black-bean-and-corn-salad/
SOURCE: Adapted from Lori Lange at RecipeGirl
SOURCE_URL: https://www.recipegirl.com/lime-and-honey-glazed-salmon-with-black-bean-and-corn-salad/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Salmon and glaze ---
  - 2.25 lb (about 1,020 g) skinless, boneless salmon, cut into seven similar portions
  - 1 1/2 tsp mild chili powder blend, without added salt
  - 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
  - 1 1/2 tsp ground cumin, divided
  - 1 tsp fine salt, divided, plus up to 1/4 tsp more for the salad after tasting
  - 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
  - 4 tbsp honey
  - 2 tbsp fresh lime juice, for the glaze
  - 1 tsp olive oil, for the foil
  - --- Warm salad and fresh finish ---
  - 5 medium ears fresh sweet corn, husked and kernels cut off; about 600 g kernels
  - 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the skillet
  - 1 medium red onion, finely diced
  - 1 medium red bell pepper, cored, seeded and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
  - 3 garlic cloves, minced
  - 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes, optional, for the salad
  - 2 cans (15 oz each) black beans, rinsed and well drained; about 500 g drained
  - 1 tbsp fresh lime juice, for the salad, plus up to 1 tbsp more after tasting
  - 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro
  - 8 loosely packed cups baby spinach, washed and dried; about 240 g
  - 1/4 cup toasted unsalted pepitas
  - 1 avocado, diced just before serving, optional
  - 1 lime, cut into eight wedges for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Mexican-inspired salmon dinner pairs sweet lime-honey glaze with cumin-scented beans and corn, fresh spinach and toasted pepitas. Bake the fish most of the way before glazing, then give the broiler your full attention. The warm salad softens the leaves slightly at serving while the seeds keep their crunch.

## Directions

1. **Prepare everything and heat the oven:** Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C with a middle rack and a second rack positioned so the fish surface will sit 7–9 inches below the broiler. Cut corn from the cobs, chop onion, pepper, garlic and cilantro, and rinse and drain beans. Prepare the spinach and measure the pepitas. Line the metal half-sheet pan with foil and spread its teaspoon of oil where the fish will sit. Pat salmon dry, check for pin bones and divide into seven similar portions. Season with chili powder, smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp salt and all the black pepper. Keep chilled while charring corn. Whisk honey with the 2 tbsp glaze lime juice in a clean bowl; set aside the separate salad juice and serving wedges. Wash raw-fish tools and hands before returning to vegetables.
2. **Char corn in two batches:** Heat the deep, well-seasoned skillet over medium-high heat for about 2–3 minutes. Add half the dry corn without oil and spread into a shallow layer. Let it sit briefly, then stir occasionally for about 5–7 minutes, until juicy and tender with scattered browned patches. Lower heat if it starts blackening. Transfer to a large bowl. Let the pan recover its heat and repeat with the remaining corn; remove any burnt loose residue afterward.
3. **Start baking the fish:** Arrange salmon on the prepared pan with about an inch between portions. Bake on the middle rack while making the salad in the next two steps. Start checking the fish after 8 minutes; allow roughly 10–15 minutes for the specified thickness, aiming for about 135–140°F / 57–60°C before the glaze finish. This is an intermediate temperature, not the serving endpoint. If ready before the salad, remove the pan briefly to a heatproof surface.
4. **Soften the aromatics:** Reduce skillet heat to medium and add the tablespoon of olive oil, onion, bell pepper and remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Cook, stirring, about 6–8 minutes until the onion softens and pepper is tender with a little bite. Add garlic, the remaining 1 tsp cumin and optional red pepper flakes; stir 30–45 seconds until fragrant.
5. **Warm and finish the salad:** Fold the beans and all the corn into the skillet. Cook over medium heat for about 4–6 minutes, turning gently, until hot throughout. Remove from heat and fold in cilantro and the first tablespoon of salad lime juice. Taste and add some or all of the reserved lime and extra salt if wanted. Cover loosely and turn off the skillet before broiling.
6. **Glaze and watch the broiler:** Remove salmon from the oven if it is still inside and switch to high broil, allowing the element to heat according to the oven's instructions. Spread all the honey-lime mixture over the seven fillets in an even coating, without deliberately pooling it on the foil. Broil with the fish surface 7–9 inches below the heat for about 1–3 minutes, watching continuously; rotate the pan if needed. The glaze should bubble and develop golden patches without turning black. Check each fillet sideways in its thickest center and finish to 145°F / 63°C, with flesh that flakes under gentle pressure. If the glaze colors first, use the gentler oven finish in troubleshooting. Use clean utensils for serving and discard glaze left in the brushing bowl; it is not a cold sauce.
7. **Serve seven complete portions:** Divide all the spinach among seven wide bowls, then divide the warm bean-and-corn salad over it. Add one fillet per bowl. Dice the optional avocado and divide it among the bowls, then scatter the pepitas. Offer lime wedges for squeezing to taste. The spinach remains a fresh bed, lightly softened by the warm toppings.

## With rice

For a more substantial dinner, one full batch of [Aromatic Purple Rice](/mise/recipes/purple-rice) supplies seven small side portions, roughly 3/4 cup each. Begin its 80-minute preparation before this recipe and allow time for the rice's transition and grain checks; leave the final fish broiling until the rice is resting or ready. The beans and corn are already included in every salmon portion.

## Smaller oven

Use the same bake-then-glaze method only with the appliance's approved broiler pan, foil placement and rack clearance. If seven portions do not fit with space between them, cook in separate batches and allow roughly 20–25 extra minutes. Divide the foil oil and glaze between pans and keep the waiting raw fish chilled. The first batch will rest longer and lose heat; a full-size oven is the simpler way to serve all seven portions together.

## Cooking Notes

A ten-ounce package of frozen corn can replace fresh corn. For a gluten-free preparation, check the broth and canned-bean labels as well as the other ingredients.

RECIPE: Chicken Lo Mein with Shiitake and Bok Choy (lo-mein.md)
CUISINES: Chinese-American, Cantonese-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/lo-mein/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Noodles and chicken ---
  - 450 g (1 lb) fresh raw lo mein egg noodles, not dried noodles or pre-cooked noodles
  - 450 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced across the grain about 1/4 inch thick
  - 2 tsp cornstarch
  - 1 tsp neutral oil, for the chicken
  - 1 tsp light soy sauce, for the chicken
  - 1/8 tsp ground white pepper, for the chicken
  - --- Sauce, divided between two finishing batches ---
  - 2 tbsp light soy sauce
  - 2 tsp dark soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp oyster sauce
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) low-sodium chicken broth or water
  - 1 tsp sugar
  - 1/8 tsp ground white pepper
  - --- Pan ingredients ---
  - 3 tbsp (45 ml) prepared strained scallion-shallot oil, divided (preferred; or shallot oil or neutral oil)
  - 3 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1 tbsp minced fresh ginger
  - 4 scallions, whites thinly sliced and greens cut into 1-inch lengths
  - 225 g fresh shiitake caps, tough stems removed, sliced 1/4 inch thick
  - 340 g baby bok choy, washed and thoroughly dried, stems and leaves separated
  - 150 g mung bean sprouts, rinsed and drained
  - 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
  - 2 tsp toasted sesame oil, divided between finishing batches
  - 1 tsp Chinkiang black vinegar or unseasoned rice vinegar, optional, divided between finishing batches
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water, only as needed to loosen noodles
  - 15 g crisp fried shallots and scallions from the oil recipe, or prepared fried shallots, optional garnish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Scallion-shallot oil gives this home-pan lo mein its fragrant allium base. Use **3 tbsp (45 ml) strained [Scallion-Shallot Oil](/mise/recipes/scallion-shallot-oil)** for the full five-serving recipe, made ahead; the chicken coating uses a separate teaspoon of neutral oil. Strained shallot oil works too, and neutral oil is the shortcut for a milder dish. Reserve the crisp fried alliums for serving. Dark soy contributes flavor and salt as well as color. Toasted sesame oil goes in at the finish for a clear aroma.

## Directions

1. **Coat the chicken and prepare the sauce:** Toss chicken with its cornstarch, 1 tsp oil, 1 tsp light soy and white pepper; refrigerate while preparing everything else. Whisk the six sauce ingredients together and divide into two equal portions.
2. **Set up the vegetables:** Keep mushroom slices, bok choy stems, leaves, sprouts and scallion greens separate. Cut stems into 1/2-inch pieces and large leaves into manageable pieces. Mix garlic, ginger and scallion whites. Divide every vegetable and aromatic group, the Shaoxing wine, sesame oil and optional vinegar into two portions for the final rounds.
3. **Prepare noodles for this product:** Bring a large pot of unsalted water to a full boil. Add fresh raw noodles, separate gently and cook according to their package range, tasting early until cooked through but springy. Rinse briefly with cold water, drain thoroughly and toss with 1 tsp of the measured pan oil. Divide into two loose piles and proceed promptly; start the pan work as soon as the noodles are ready.
4. **Cook the chicken fully in two batches:** Heat the wok or deep skillet over medium-high to high as appropriate for the pan, then add 2 tsp pan oil. Spread half the chicken in a layer. Leave about 1 minute for color, then turn and stir for another 2–3 minutes or until the thickest slices reach 165°F / 74°C. Transfer to a clean plate. Repeat with another 2 tsp oil and the remaining chicken. Keep the cooked chicken divided for the two finishing rounds.
5. **Cook the first vegetable portion:** Add 2 tsp of the remaining oil. Cook half the mushrooms 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until some surfaces brown. Add half the aromatics for 20–30 seconds, then half the wine and bok choy stems. Stir-fry about 2 minutes, adding a little measured hot water if needed for the stems to soften. Add half the leaves, sprouts and scallion greens and cook another 2–3 minutes, stirring, until thoroughly hot and cooked rather than raw-crisp.
6. **Finish the first noodle batch:** Add half the noodles and one portion of sauce. Fold from the bottom for about 1–2 minutes, using a little measured hot water only if needed to separate strands. Add half the cooked chicken and toss over the heat until everything is hot and evenly coated. Turn off the heat and fold in half the sesame oil and optional vinegar. Transfer to a warm serving platter and cover loosely for the short second round.
7. **Repeat and serve:** Use the last 2 tsp pan oil and the remaining vegetables, aromatics, wine, noodles, sauce and chicken to repeat steps 5–6. Finish with the remaining sesame oil and optional vinegar. Divide both batches among five bowls and add the optional 15 g crisp fried alliums from the oil recipe or prepared fried shallots. Serve promptly.

## Scaling and variations

The pan oil is fully allocated: 1 tsp on noodles, 2 tsp for each chicken batch and 2 tsp for each vegetable round, totaling 3 tbsp. The chicken coating has its own separate teaspoon. If scaling up, add complete cooking rounds; multiplying ingredients does not make the pan larger. At half batch, a single finishing round is appropriate for the same pan, while the noodle type still determines boiling time.

The preferred oil is [Scallion-Shallot Oil](/mise/recipes/scallion-shallot-oil), already made and stored as directed. Use 3 tbsp (45 ml) of strained oil, not the whole batch; its separate recipe also includes an all-shallot option. Substitute the same amount of neutral oil for a shortcut. Making the oil from scratch adds its own 50 minutes to the stated lo mein time. For a cool accompaniment, see [Smashed Cucumber Salad](/mise/recipes/smashed-cucumber-salad).

RECIPE: Omelet Muffins (loaded-baked-omelet-muffins.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/loaded-baked-omelet-muffins/
SOURCE: Adapted from skinnytaste.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.skinnytaste.com/loaded-baked-omelet-muffins/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 9 large Eggs
  - 3 slices Bacon, cooked and chopped
  - 2 oz Sharp Cheddar, shredded
  - 3 tbsp Frozen Spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
  - 3 tbsp Roma Tomato, finely diced
  - 3 tbsp Onion, finely diced
  - 3 tbsp Bell Pepper, finely diced
  - 1/4 tsp Kosher Salt
  - Black Pepper
  - Cooking spray
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Use cooked bacon and thawed spinach squeezed free of excess water. Divide the finely diced vegetables among the cups, then add the eggs and cheese. The filling supplies savory flavor; a crisp bottom is not guaranteed once it is surrounded by moist egg.

## Directions

1. **Prep:** Preheat the oven to 350 °F. Generously spray standard muffin cups, including the sides, and set the tin on a baking sheet. Start with cooked, chopped bacon. Prepare the frozen spinach according to its package if cooking is required, cool enough to handle, squeeze dry and measure the listed spinach amount after draining. These preparations add time if they are not already done.

2. **The Base:** Divide the cooked bacon, squeezed spinach, finely diced tomato, onion and pepper among the cups. The original batch uses about 12 standard cups; different quantities need more or fewer cups at the same size and fill depth.

3. **The Eggs:** Whisk the eggs, measured kosher salt and black pepper until the whites and yolks are blended. Do not whip to a thick foam.

4. **Assemble:** Divide the eggs evenly among the filled cups, leaving about one-quarter headroom. Sprinkle all the cheddar over the tops. Use additional cups if needed rather than pouring over the rim.

5. **Bake:** Bake for about 20–25 minutes, until the centers are set and opaque with no liquid egg, and reach 165 °F / 74 °C. Check a center without touching the metal tin; surface color does not replace the temperature check.

6. **Cool and store:** Let stand 5 minutes before loosening and removing. Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers and use within 3–4 days, or freeze individually for up to 3 months for quality. Reheat the center to 165 °F / 74 °C; a fixed 45-second microwave time cannot cover chilled and frozen portions.

RECIPE: Made-In-The-Pan Chocolate Cake (made-in-the-pan-chocolate-cake.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/made-in-the-pan-chocolate-cake/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020063-made-in-the-pan-chocolate-cake
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Cake ---
  - 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
  - 1 cup granulated sugar
  - 1/3 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
  - 3/4 tsp baking soda
  - 1/2 tsp sea salt
  - 1/3 cup canola or avocado oil
  - 1 tsp pure vanilla extract
  - 1 tsp apple cider vinegar
  - 1 cup water, cold
  - 2 tbsp semisweet chocolate chips
  - --- Optional finish ---
  - confectioners’ sugar, a light dusting after cooling, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Mixing directly in the pan works only if the corners and bottom are scraped thoroughly. The vinegar and baking soda provide leavening in this egg-free batter; cold water is retained here, but it is not required to “bloom” the cocoa. Use the full listed oil and sugar, and judge the center with a toothpick rather than the color of the chocolate surface.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and mix dry ingredients:** Preheat the oven to 325°F. For the original batch use an 8×8-inch square glass or metal baking dish. Whisk all-purpose flour, granulated sugar, unsweetened cocoa powder, baking soda, and sea salt directly in the dish until evenly combined, breaking up cocoa lumps. When scaling, use enough proportional pan area to keep a similar batter depth; do not put extra full batches into this one pan.
2. **Add the oil and flavorings:** Make three wells in the dry mixture and divide canola or avocado oil, pure vanilla extract, and apple cider vinegar between them: oil in one, vanilla in another and vinegar in the third.
3. **Mix the batter:** Pour water over everything. Stir slowly with a fork or small whisk, mashing lumps and scraping the bottom, sides and corners until the batter is smooth and uniform. Spread evenly.
4. **Add the chocolate:** Sprinkle semisweet chocolate chips over the batter. Wipe batter off the pan rim with a damp paper towel.
5. **Bake:** Wait until the oven reaches 325°F, then bake for 28–33 minutes. A toothpick inserted into the center should come out mostly clean with a few cake crumbs, rather than coated in wet batter. Pan material, depth and oven loads can change the time.
6. **Cool and finish:** Let the cake cool before cutting into portions. Dust with confectioners’ sugar (if using) if desired; it is optional.

## Cooking Notes

### Vinegar and chocolate options

Use the same listed amount of white vinegar instead of apple cider vinegar if desired. Keep the full water, oil, flour and leavening amounts. The chocolate topping may be omitted, or the same listed amount of vegan chocolate chips may replace the semisweet chips. A vegan version requires checking the selected chips; the powdered-sugar finish is optional.

For the original batch, the source uses ½ tsp kosher salt rather than the listed ½ tsp sea salt, but it does not identify a salt density or a fine-salt equivalent. Those spoon volumes are not a demonstrated conversion; keep the listed sea salt for this version.

RECIPE: Mandarin/Pineapple Orange Salad (mandarinpineapple-organge-salad.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mandarinpineapple-organge-salad/
SOURCE: Adapted from Gwock Family
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 small box Orange Jello
  - 1 small can Crushed Pineapple (with juice)
  - 1 small can Mandarin Oranges, drained
  - 3/4 cup Sour Cream (for richness)
  - 1/2 cup Granulated Sugar
  - 1 cup Boiling Water
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Citrus salads are a Southern and Caribbean tradition - canned or fresh fruit with a bright dressing and sometimes nuts for crunch. The trick is draining fruit well so the salad doesn't turn watery. If you're using canned fruit, rinse it under cold water to remove the heavy syrup, then dress it right before serving.

## Directions

1.  **Dissolve:** In a large bowl, whisk the Orange Jello and sugar into the boiling water until no crystals remain.
2.  **Emulsify:** Add the sour cream to the hot liquid. Whisk vigorously until the mixture is completely smooth and pale orange.
3.  **Texture:** Fold in the crushed pineapple (with its juice) and the drained mandarin oranges.
4.  **The Finish:** Pour the mixture into a glass bowl or a decorative mold.
5.  **Chill:** Refrigerate for **at least 4 hours** (ideally overnight) until perfectly congealed and firm.
6.  **Serve:** Serve chilled as a bright side dish or a light dessert.

RECIPE: Mango Cabbage Slaw (mango-cabbage-slaw.md)
CUISINES: Caribbean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mango-cabbage-slaw/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 cups green cabbage, cored and very thinly shredded
  - 2 cups red cabbage, cored and very thinly shredded
  - 1 large ripe but firm mango, peeled and cut into matchsticks
  - 1 red bell pepper, stemmed, seeded and thinly sliced
  - 1/2 small red onion, thinly sliced
  - 1/2 cup fresh cilantro, roughly chopped
  - 2 scallions, thinly sliced
  - --- Dressing ---
  - 3 tbsp fresh lime juice, plus more to taste
  - 2 tbsp neutral oil
  - 1 tbsp honey or agave syrup
  - 1 tsp Dijon mustard
  - 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more only if needed
  - 1/4 tsp black pepper
  - 1 pinch ground allspice
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Mango brings sweetness to a lime-dressed mix of cabbage, pepper and herbs. Slice the cabbage finely and give the dressed slaw a short chilled rest so the shreds bend without losing their crunch. It makes a cool, bright side for spiced pork or rice and peas.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Core and thinly shred the cabbages, then measure them into a large bowl. Peel the mango and cut the flesh away from the pit into thin matchsticks. Prepare the bell pepper, onion, cilantro and scallions.
2. **Whisk the dressing:** Whisk the measured lime juice, oil, honey or agave, mustard, measured salt, pepper and allspice in a small bowl until well combined. Whisk again if it separates before use.
3. **Toss gently:** Add the mango, pepper, onion, cilantro and scallions to the cabbage. Pour over the dressing and lift gently from the bottom to coat everything without crushing the mango.
4. **Rest and taste:** Cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes, or up to 30 minutes for softer cabbage. Toss gently and taste a forkful, adding a little extra lime or salt only if needed. Serve as six generous side portions, lifting out of any pooled liquid.

RECIPE: Mango-Rita Green Smoothie (mango-rita-green-smoothie.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mango-rita-green-smoothie/
SOURCE: Adapted from Cookieandkate.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cookieandkate.com/2017/mango-pineapple-green-smoothie/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups Fresh Baby Spinach
  - 2 cups Frozen Mango chunks
  - 1 cup Frozen Pineapple chunks
  - 1 cup Unsweetened Coconut Water
  - 1 fresh Orange, peeled and halved
  - 1 Lime, juiced (The Acid Balance)
  - Tiny pinch of Sea Salt (The "Trust Me" Note)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A green smoothie with mango and lime is tropical and tart - the acid cuts through the sweet fruit and mild greens. The trick is using ripe mango (it should yield slightly to pressure) so the smoothie is thick and creamy without needing yogurt or ice cream. Blend greens first with liquid, then add the fruit so it breaks down evenly.

## Directions

1.  **The Base:** In a high-powered blender, combine the spinach, coconut water, and orange. Blend on high for 30 seconds until the greens are completely pulverized.
2.  **The Bulk:** Add the frozen mango, frozen pineapple, lime juice, and the pinch of sea salt.
3.  **Process:** Blend on high for 60 seconds until perfectly velvety.
4.  **Adjust:** If the smoothie is too thick, add a splash more coconut water. If you want more "Snap," add extra lime juice.
5.  **Serve:** Pour into two chilled glasses. Garnish with a lime slice and serve immediately.

RECIPE: Maple-Roasted Sweet Potato Wedges (maple-roasted-sweet-potato-wedges.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/maple-roasted-sweet-potato-wedges/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Sweet potato wedges ---
  - 2 lb sweet potatoes, scrubbed, skin left on and cut lengthwise into wedges about ½ inch thick
  - 3 tbsp olive oil
  - 1/2 tsp kosher salt
  - 1/4 tsp black pepper
  - --- Maple glaze ---
  - 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
  - 1/2 tsp smoked paprika, optional
  - --- Finish ---
  - flaky sea salt, a pinch, to taste at serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Brown the sweet potato wedges on their cut faces before brushing on the maple syrup. The late glaze gives a sticky, sweet finish with less time to scorch; it still needs close attention during the final 8–10 minutes. Check a thick center before glazing and at the end so browned sugar is not mistaken for a cooked potato.

## Directions

1. **Heat and cut:** Heat the oven to 425°F. Use a large rimmed baking sheet or enough sheets for the measured wedges; if lining, use parchment rated for this heat or suitable foil. Scrub the sweet potatoes under running water, leave the skins on and cut lengthwise into wedges about ½ inch thick, with a skin edge and flat cut faces. Dry the cut surfaces. Make wedges rather than parallel planks.
2. **Coat and arrange:** Toss sweet potatoes, olive oil, kosher salt, and black pepper in a large bowl until the wedges are evenly coated. Arrange in one layer on a flat cut face, with space between wedges. The measured oil and seasonings coat the full batch, not each sheet.
3. **Brown the first face:** Roast for 18–20 minutes. Lift a wedge to check the underside for golden browning; test a thick center for softening. If still hard, continue the unglazed roast before adding maple. The final stage should finish nearly tender wedges, rather than leave syrup to scorch while a raw center cooks.
4. **Turn and brush:** Turn the wedges onto another cut face and set out pure maple syrup and smoked paprika (if using). Brush the syrup across all the wedges, using the whole measured maple amount for the full batch. Sprinkle the optional paprika over them if using. Keep the thin glaze on the wedges rather than pouring a pool onto the empty pan.
5. **Finish and watch the maple:** Return to the oven for 8–10 minutes, checking the maple closely. Centers should be easily pierced and the glaze bubbling and browned, without blackened sugar. Remove ready wedges sooner if they darken quickly. The two stages normally total 26–30 minutes, but thicker pieces or extra sheets may need longer before glazing.
6. **Taste and serve:** Transfer to a serving dish and use flaky sea salt if needed after tasting. Serve warm; expect tender centers and browned, sticky edges rather than guaranteed fry-like crispness.

RECIPE: Mapo Tofu (mapo-tofu.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mapo-tofu/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 block (14 oz) Medium-Firm Tofu, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
  - 6 oz Ground Pork
  - 2 tbsp Doubanjiang (Pixian chili bean paste)
  - 1 tbsp Fermented Black Beans, rinsed and roughly chopped
  - 1 tbsp Sichuan Peppercorns, toasted and ground
  - 4 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Ginger, minced
  - 2 Green Onions, white and green parts separated, thinly sliced
  - 2 tbsp Neutral Oil
  - 1 tbsp Soy Sauce
  - 1 tsp Sugar
  - 3/4 cup Low-Sodium Chicken Broth
  - 1 tbsp cornstarch, mixed with the separately measured slurry water
  - 2 tbsp water, for the cornstarch slurry
  - 1 tsp Toasted Sesame Oil
  - 1 tsp Chili Oil, for drizzling
  - Water, enough for the tofu bath; drained and discarded
  - Salt, to taste, for the tofu bath; drained and discarded
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Sichuan peppercorns and doubanjiang give mapo tofu its numbing, spicy character. This version uses medium-firm tofu, briefly warmed in salted water and then handled gently in the pork sauce. Softer tofu can also be used for mapo tofu, but needs more careful handling; it is not inherently a mistake. Cook the bean paste in the existing oil and pork fat until fragrant without scorching, and keep the tofu intact with gentle spooning rather than vigorous stirring.

## Directions

1. **Parcook the tofu:** Wash the scallions before slicing. Mix the separately measured slurry cornstarch and cold water in a small bowl and set aside. Bring enough tofu-bath water to cover the cubes to a gentle boil and season it with the bath salt allowance to taste. Slide in all the tofu and simmer 2–3 minutes, then lift and drain gently; discard this bath water.
2. **Cook the pork:** Heat all the neutral oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Add all ground pork and break into small crumbles, beginning checks around 3–4 minutes. Retain all rendered fat. Brown color is a cooking cue, not proof of 160°F; continue cooking the pork with the sauce.
3. **Fry the bean paste:** Push pork aside and add all doubanjiang and rinsed, chopped fermented black beans to the existing oil and fat. Stir 1–2 minutes until fragrant and the oil takes on red color, reducing heat before the paste scorches.
4. **Build the sauce:** Stir in all garlic, ginger and scallion whites about 30 seconds, then add all measured broth, soy sauce and sugar and bring to a simmer.
5. **Warm the tofu:** Gently slide in all drained tofu. Spoon sauce over the cubes or nudge with the back of a ladle rather than stirring hard. Simmer about 5 minutes; check representative pork-containing sauce areas for at least 160°F before tasting or finishing. Use enough vessels for the complete scaled formula, divided proportionally, without crowding the cubes.
6. **Thicken:** Re-stir the entire separate slurry and drizzle it in two additions, gently swirling between them. Let the sauce simmer after each addition until thickening is visible; use the full listed mixture for this route and cook until the sauce clings without raw-starch taste.
7. **Finish:** Add all measured sesame oil and chili oil, then all the toasted, ground Sichuan peppercorns and scallion greens. Fold gently and serve promptly over separately prepared white rice.

RECIPE: Marinated Flank Steak Salad (marinated-flank-steak-salad.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/marinated-flank-steak-salad/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Steak and Marinade ---
  - 1 1/4 lb flank steak
  - 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, for the marinade
  - 3 tbsp soy sauce, or gluten-free tamari
  - 1 tbsp Dijon mustard
  - 2 garlic cloves, minced
  - 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 1 tbsp neutral cooking oil, or shallot oil, for searing
  - --- Salad and Toppings ---
  - 1 large head romaine lettuce, washed and torn
  - 1 head butter lettuce, washed and torn
  - 1 English cucumber, washed and sliced
  - 1 avocado, washed before cutting, then diced
  - 4 radishes, washed and shaved thinly
  - 1/4 cup toasted pepitas
  - [Crispy Shallots](/mise/recipes/crispy-shallots), for topping
  - --- Lemon Vinaigrette ---
  - 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil
  - 3 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 1 tsp Dijon mustard
  - 1 small shallot, finely minced
  - 1/2 tsp kosher salt
  - 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Flank steak’s long grain makes the direction of slicing especially important. This soy-Dijon and lemon version keeps a rich vinaigrette, pepitas and crisp shallots around the sliced beef. Dry the marinated surface before searing, keep the salad away from raw meat and marinade, and dress the leaves just before serving.

## Directions

1. **Score the Steak:** Lightly score both sides of flank steak in a shallow diagonal diamond pattern, about 1/8 inch deep. Keep the cuts superficial; do not cut through the steak. Use separate equipment for the raw meat and ready-to-eat salad.
2. **Marinate:** Whisk extra-virgin olive oil, soy sauce, Dijon mustard, garlic cloves, and fresh lemon juice in a nonreactive dish or food-storage bag and add the steak. Seal and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or up to 12 hours.
3. **Dry the Surface:** Take the steak from the refrigerator when ready to cook. Lift it from the marinade and pat the surface dry. Discard the used marinade; keep it away from the dressing and salad.
4. **Make the Vinaigrette:** Shake or whisk extra-virgin olive oil, fresh lemon juice, Dijon mustard, small shallot, kosher salt, and freshly ground black pepper together. Keep the washed salad and toppings cold while the meat cooks.
5. **Sear the Steak:** Use flank steak and neutral cooking oil: heat the oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high to high heat until shimmering. Lay the steak flat without crowding. Begin checking around 4–5 minutes per side for the original cut, adjusting heat if the surface is burning; continue until the thickest part reaches at least 145°F before removing it. For more steaks, use additional suitable pans or complete cooking batches, dividing all the measured searing oil among them. Cut thickness and starting temperature change the clock.
6. **Rest:** Transfer to a clean cutting board and let the steak rest for 10 minutes, exceeding the minimum 3-minute rest after the 145°F endpoint. Keep the meat and cooked juices separate from the raw-meat equipment.
7. **Slice:** Slice as thinly as possible across the grain with the carving knife angled about 45 degrees. Keep the salad cold until assembly.
8. **Assemble:** Bring large head romaine lettuce, head butter lettuce, English cucumber, avocado, and radishes to the serving bowl. Toss both lettuces with half of the prepared vinaigrette. Arrange the cucumber, avocado and radishes over the greens, add all the sliced steak, and drizzle with all the remaining vinaigrette.
9. **Finish:** Scatter toasted pepitas and [Crispy Shallots](/mise/recipes/crispy-shallots) over the top just before serving so the toppings stay crisp.

RECIPE: Bulgogi (marinated-korean-ribeye.md)
CUISINES: Korean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/marinated-korean-ribeye/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Beef and marinade ---
  - 1 lb ribeye beef, raw, fresh or fully thawed; very thinly sliced, unseasoned for the homemade marinade
  - 3 tbsp soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1 tbsp brown sugar
  - 1/2 Bosc or Asian pear, washed, cored and grated
  - 2 garlic cloves, peeled and minced
  - 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
  - 2 green onions, washed and minced
  - 1/4 tsp black pepper
  - suitable high-heat cooking oil, a small splash as needed for the pan
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Bulgogi uses very thin slices so the beef can cook quickly in uncrowded pan loads. This marinade keeps its soy, sesame oil, brown sugar and grated pear; the pear contributes fruit and sweetness without a promise of enzyme-driven tenderness. If slicing a whole ribeye, partial freezer firming can make thin cuts easier, but the meat should remain sliceable.

## Directions

1. **Prepare thin slices:** Keep the beef cold. If starting with a whole ribeye, use about 45 minutes in the freezer as a first check until firm enough to slice thinly, still yielding to the knife; this adds preparation time. Pat unseasoned sliced beef dry with paper towels before marinating.
2. **Mix and marinate:** For the homemade route, use ribeye beef, soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, brown sugar, Bosc or Asian pear, garlic cloves, fresh ginger, green onions, and black pepper. Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, grated pear, garlic, ginger, green onions and pepper together. Toss with all the sliced beef, cover and refrigerate at 40°F or below for at least 30 minutes or overnight. The pre-marinated option below replaces the complete homemade marinade.
3. **Cook in uncrowded loads:** Heat a heavy skillet or wok over high heat until hot, adjusting if the coating scorches rather than browns. Use suitable high-heat cooking oil as needed. Lift the marinated beef from excess pooled marinade, leaving a coating on the slices, and spread one uncrowded layer in the pan. Begin checking after 1–2 minutes for browned edges, then flip and begin checking after about 30 seconds. Continue until the pieces reach at least 145°F in the center with a thermometer suitable for thin food, inserted from the side; follow any higher endpoint on a product label. These are first checks, not guaranteed finishing times.
4. **Rest and serve:** Move fully cooked beef to a clean serving dish and rest at least 3 minutes before eating. Continue with the remaining pan loads, keeping waiting raw beef cold and using separate clean utensils for cooked beef. Discard pooled raw-contact marinade; do not add it at the end. More loads extend elapsed time.

RECIPE: Massaman Curry (massaman-curry.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/massaman-curry/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 1/2 lb boneless beef chuck, cut into 1-inch / 2.5 cm cubes; trim tough outer silverskin but retain marbled fat
  - 2 tbsp neutral cooking oil, divided between browning and the curry paste
  - 3 tbsp prepared massaman curry paste; start with less if particularly hot or salty
  - 1 tsp whole green cardamom pods, measured before lightly cracking, optional
  - 3–4 whole dried red chiles, optional for extra heat
  - 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped
  - 1 tbsp finely chopped fresh ginger
  - 1 (14 oz) can full-fat unsweetened coconut milk, stirred together
  - 1 cup (240 ml) unsalted beef stock
  - Hot water, only as needed to maintain the braising liquid
  - 2 medium waxy or all-purpose potatoes, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch / 2 cm cubes
  - 1 large yellow onion, peeled and cut into 1-inch / 2.5 cm chunks
  - 1/2 cup unsalted or lightly salted roasted peanuts
  - 2 tbsp fish sauce, divided and added to taste
  - 1 tbsp finely chopped palm sugar or packed brown sugar
  - 1 tbsp unsweetened Thai-style tamarind purée made from pulp and water, plus more only if needed after tasting
  - Additional palm or brown sugar, only if needed after tasting
  - Fresh cilantro, chopped, for serving
  - Lime wedges, for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The beef needs time before the potatoes join it. Keep the covered curry at a gentle simmer until the meat is nearly tender, then add the vegetables so they hold their shape. Full-fat coconut milk, the cooking oil and whole peanuts give the sauce its richness; finish with tamarind and sugar after the sauce reaches the consistency you want.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the beef and aromatics:** Cut the trimmed chuck into **1-inch / 2.5 cm cubes** and pat dry. Chop garlic and ginger and measure the paste, milk and stock. Reserve **one-third of the oil for the paste**; use the remaining two-thirds for browning. Keep raw-meat tools separate from serving utensils and wash them after preparing the beef.
2. **Brown in batches:** Heat the browning oil in portions over medium-high in the heavy pot. Brown the beef in an uncrowded layer, about **two batches for the full recipe**, using an equal share of that oil for each batch. Leave two broad faces against the pot for about **2–3 minutes per face**, turning once browned. Transfer to a plate; it is still raw inside. Allow the pot to regain heat between batches and lower the heat if the coating starts to blacken.
3. **Build the curry:** Lower to medium-low. Add the reserved oil, optional cracked cardamom pods and whole dried chiles; stir for about **20 seconds**. Add massaman paste and cook **1–2 minutes**, stirring, until fragrant but not scorched. Stir in garlic and ginger for about **30 seconds**. Gradually stir in the coconut milk, then stock and **half the fish sauce**, scraping up brown residue. There is no need to wait for coconut oil to separate. Return the beef and all its plate juices to the pot.
4. **Braise the beef:** Bring to a gentle simmer. Liquid should come just about to the top of the beef in the pot; add a little hot water if needed. Cover, lower the heat and braise gently for about **1 1/2–2 1/2 hours**, beginning tenderness checks after **75 minutes**. Every 20–30 minutes, stir along the bottom and check the liquid, adding hot water as needed to keep the beef mostly surrounded by sauce. A fork should enter the meat with only slight resistance before you continue. Toward the end of this stage, peel and cut the potatoes and onion.
5. **Add potatoes and onion:** Stir in the vegetables, cover and simmer about **20–30 minutes**, stirring gently once or twice. The potatoes should be tender through the center and the beef should yield easily to a fork. Check a thick beef cube reaches at least **145°F / 63°C**; tenderness usually requires cooking beyond that minimum. The off-heat rest comes before serving. If either needs longer, keep cooking gently and maintain enough liquid to prevent sticking. Lift out any potatoes that finish before the beef and return them at the finish.
6. **Finish the sauce:** Stir in peanuts, the starting amount of sugar and the starting amount of tamarind purée. Simmer **3–5 minutes**. If the sauce is watery, simmer uncovered for another **5–10 minutes** before final seasoning; it should coat a spoon but still flow around the meat. Taste with a piece of potato, then add the remaining fish sauce and optional extra sugar or tamarind in small amounts as needed. If using lime instead of tamarind, add it only after turning off the heat. Remove the cardamom pods and whole chiles before serving.
7. **Rest and serve:** Rest off heat for **5 minutes**. Serve with a modest portion of separately prepared [Basmati Rice](/mise/recipes/basmati-rice). The potatoes already supply some starch. [Coconut Jasmine Rice](/mise/recipes/coconut-jasmine-rice) is a richer accompaniment. Add cilantro and lime wedges at the table.

RECIPE: Sushi Rice (Shari) (master-sushi-rice.md)
CUISINES: Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/master-sushi-rice/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 400 g Japanese short-grain white rice, not glutinous rice
  - 480 ml cold water, plus water for rinsing
  - 1 piece dried kombu, about 5 cm square
  - 5 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar
  - 1 1/2 tbsp granulated sugar
  - 1 1/2 tsp fine sea salt, divided
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Shari is seasoned rice used for sushi; a bowl of plain short-grain rice has a different flavor. Add the vinegar seasoning while the cooked grains are hot and lift them gently with a paddle. Fan briefly to release steam, then use the rice soon rather than keeping it warm on the counter for hours.

## Directions

1. **Rinse and soak:** Rinse the rice several times, gently swishing and draining until the water is less cloudy. Drain well, transfer to a heavy 3-quart saucepan and add the measured cooking water. Wipe away visible grit from the kombu with a barely damp cloth and add it. Soak for 30 minutes.
2. **Heat and cook:** Bring toward a boil over medium heat with the lid slightly ajar. Remove the kombu when the water starts bubbling. Close the lid, reduce to low and simmer gently for 12–15 minutes.
3. **Rest and check:** Move off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes. Check a grain for a tender center. If grains are still firm and water remains, cover and cook on low for 3–5 minutes, then rest off heat for 5 minutes and check again. If the pot is dry but the center is hard, use the measured-water correction in troubleshooting. Already mushy rice will not become firm through extra stirring or cooking.
4. **Mix the seasoning:** While the rice cooks, stir four fifths of the measured vinegar, the sugar and two thirds of the measured salt in a small bowl. Warm briefly if needed to dissolve, without boiling. Reserve the remaining vinegar and salt.
5. **Season and cool briefly:** Transfer hot rice to a wide nonreactive bowl. Distribute the seasoning over it and gently lift and fold with a rice paddle. Fan as steam escapes, about 5–10 minutes; judge by the rice rather than expecting a fixed temperature after two minutes. Taste, dissolve any reserved salt needed in the reserved vinegar, then fold in that vinegar whether or not extra salt is used. For poke, let the portion being used become only barely warm before topping with cold fish and serving immediately.
6. **Use or refrigerate:** Cover loosely with a clean damp towel only during brief assembly. Measure the amount required by the main recipe; this batch makes approximately 5 1/2–6 cups. Refrigerate extra rice promptly rather than leaving the whole batch out while eating.

## Rice-cooker alternative

Use the cooker's matched cup and sushi-rice water line, or its weight-based instructions for 400 g rice. Choose its sushi-rice cycle and follow its soaking/resting guidance. The 480 ml pot quantity and 80-minute schedule are not universal cooker settings. Remove the kombu after cooking if the appliance remains closed throughout the cycle, then season as above.

RECIPE: Mediterranean Chicken Bowls (mediterranean-chicken-bowls.md)
CUISINES: Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mediterranean-chicken-bowls/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 lbs Chicken Thighs, boneless and skinless
  - 3 tbsp Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 2 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice
  - 1 tbsp Dried Oregano
  - 2 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1 cup Hummus (The "Silk" Base)
  - 2 cups Cooked Yellow Rice or Quinoa
  - 1 English Cucumber, diced
  - 1 pint Cherry Tomatoes, halved
  - 1/2 cup Feta Cheese, crumbled
  - [Pickled Red Onions](/mise/recipes/pickled-red-onions)
  - Fresh Lemon wedges
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This modular grain bowl treats each component as an independent element. Marinating chicken thighs in oregano and lemon, then searing over high heat develops a charred, crispy crust characteristic of Greek souvlaki. Layering creamy hummus at the bowl's base prevents fresh cucumbers and tomatoes from becoming soggy. Pickled red onions provide bright acidity.

## Directions

1.  **Marinate:** In a large bowl, toss chicken thighs with olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, and garlic. **Let sit for at least 15 minutes** (ideally 2 hours).
2.  **The Sear:** Heat a large skillet or grill to medium-high. Cook chicken for 5-6 minutes per side until deeply charred and the internal temp is 165°F.
3.  **Rest:** Transfer to a board and let rest for 5 minutes. Slice into thin strips.
4.  **Assemble:** In four deep bowls, spread a generous base of hummus. Top with a scoop of warm rice or quinoa.
5.  **Layer:** Arrange the sliced chicken, cucumbers, and tomatoes in distinct "stacks" around the bowl.
6.  **Finish:** Top with crumbled feta and a massive pile of [Pickled Red Onions](/mise/recipes/pickled-red-onions). Serve with a lemon wedge for the final **High Note**.

RECIPE: Lemon-Oregano Chicken with Roasted Peppers (mediterranean-chicken-thighs.md)
CUISINES: Greek-inspired, Mediterranean-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mediterranean-chicken-thighs/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken and marinade ---
  - 900 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, excess loose fat trimmed
  - 3 tbsp olive oil, for the marinade
  - 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 2 cloves garlic, finely grated
  - 2 tsp dried oregano
  - 3/4 tsp fine salt, for the chicken
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper, for the chicken
  - --- Roasted vegetables ---
  - 400 g bell peppers, cored and cut into 3/4-inch strips
  - 200 g red onion, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch wedges
  - 1 tbsp olive oil, for the vegetables
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, for the vegetables
  - 1/4 tsp ground black pepper, for the vegetables
  - 1 tbsp chopped parsley, optional finishing herb
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A measured marinade lets you control lemon, oil and salt instead of assuming every bottled dressing has the same balance. Give the chicken a coating and a refrigerated rest, then roast it opened flat. A second tray lets the peppers and onions lose moisture and brown without forcing the chicken to wait for them.

## Directions

1. **Marinate cold:** Whisk marinade oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, chicken salt and chicken pepper. Toss with chicken, cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours for a longer preparation window. Keep the chicken’s original storage/use-by limit in mind; marinating does not reset it.
2. **Prepare trays and vegetables:** During the marinade, heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Toss peppers and onion with their separate oil, salt and pepper and spread on one rimmed half-sheet pan. Lift the thighs from the marinade, allow excess to drip off, open them flat and space them on a second pan. Discard the raw-contact marinade; do not use it as a serving sauce. Wash raw-meat utensils and hands.
3. **Roast and check separately:** Put chicken below the vegetable tray. Roast for about 25–35 minutes, turning the vegetable pieces and rotating each tray front to back after fifteen minutes. Start checking chicken at twenty-five minutes: insert a thermometer into the thickest part of every thigh and continue until each reaches at least 165°F / 74°C. Remove finished pieces to a clean board. Vegetables should be soft through the thick onion wedges with browned edges; let them continue separately if needed.
4. **Rest and portion:** Rest the cooked chicken for five minutes, then slice across the meat. Divide the full chicken and vegetable batches among four plates. Scatter the optional measured parsley over the vegetables. This recipe supplies the protein and roasted vegetables; bread, grains and sauces are additional components.

## Build the platter

The [Lemon-Oregano Chicken Pita Platter](/mise/meals/mediterranean-chicken-night) gives exact quantities and a preparation schedule for pita, tzatziki and fresh vegetables. The old recipe’s serving spread is preserved there so it is counted once. For a plate, choose a grain instead of adding it on top of a full bread portion.

## About variations

This method is written for boneless thighs with a measured center temperature. Bone-in pieces and breasts need different preparation and timing; do not assume adding ten minutes makes them equivalent. For a spice-led home shawarma adaptation, use the separate [Chicken Shawarma](/mise/recipes/chicken-shawarma) recipe rather than renaming this lemon-oregano roast after adding two spices.

RECIPE: Mediterranean Grain Salad (mediterranean-grain-salad.md)
CUISINES: Greek, Mediterranean, Middle Eastern
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mediterranean-grain-salad/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup Pearled Farro (or Wheat Berries)
  - 2 1/2 cups Vegetable or Chicken Broth
  - 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt, for cooking the grain
  - --- Salad ---
  - 1 large Cucumber, diced
  - 2 large Ripe Tomatoes, diced
  - 1 Red Bell Pepper, diced
  - 1/2 Red Onion, finely diced
  - 1 cup Kalamata Olives, pitted and halved
  - 1 cup Crumbled Feta Cheese
  - 1/4 cup Fresh Flat-Leaf Parsley, chopped
  - 2 tbsp Fresh Mint, chopped
  - 2 tbsp Fresh Dill, chopped
  - --- Dressing ---
  - 1/4 cup Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 3 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice
  - 1 tsp Dried Oregano
  - 1 clove Garlic, finely grated
  - 1/4 tsp Black Pepper
  - Additional kosher salt, to taste after mixing
  - Additional fresh lemon juice, to taste after mixing
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Chewy farro carries the full olive-oil dressing, olives and feta, while diced vegetables and fresh herbs keep the salad varied. Pearled farro and whole wheat berries do not share a guaranteed cooking clock. Prepare the grain first, cool it promptly, then fold in feta and herbs close to serving.

## Directions

1. **Cook the farro:** Rinse all the dry pearled farro. Bring all the listed broth and measured kosher salt to a boil in a pot with room for the grain to expand. Add the farro, reduce to a gentle simmer and cover. Begin checking around 25–30 minutes, following the actual product instructions if they differ; the center should be tender with a pleasant chew, without a hard core. Drain excess cooking liquid.

2. **Cool and prepare:** Spread the drained grain in a shallow layer and refrigerate promptly to cool; do not leave a large warm batch on the counter waiting for room temperature. While it cools, wash the cucumber, tomatoes, pepper, onion and herbs under running water, then prepare as listed. Put all diced vegetables and halved olives in a large clean bowl.

3. **Make the dressing:** Whisk all the measured olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, grated garlic and black pepper together. These full quantities belong to the dressing; keep any additional salt and lemon juice separate for the finished salad.

4. **Combine:** Add the cooled grain to the vegetables and olives. Fold in all the dressing until the full salad is coated. Use enough bowl space, or divide all components proportionally among more bowls, rather than crowding and crushing the grains.

5. **Finish:** Just before serving, fold in all the feta, parsley, mint and dill. Taste and use the separate additional salt or lemon juice allowances only if wanted. Serve chilled, or briefly out of refrigeration for immediate service.

6. **Make ahead:** Refrigerate the grain, dressed vegetables and herbs/feta separately if preparing ahead. Combine and add the full herb/feta supplies close to serving. Keep at 40°F or below; count storage from the oldest prepared component.

## Wheat Berry Variation

Replace the listed dry pearled farro with the same listed dry volume of wheat berries. Use the full listed broth and cooking salt; follow the wheat berry product’s stovetop directions and tender-center cue rather than the farro clock. Bob’s Red Mill’s hard-red wheat berry route uses the same original one-cup grain and two-and-a-half-cup liquid starting amounts, covered for about an hour or until tender, then drained. Other products can differ: establish their required liquid before starting rather than assuming this ratio fits every wheat berry. Cool promptly and use the complete same salad, dressing, feta and herb quantities. Allow the longer grain cook and cooling; no identical cooked yield is claimed.

RECIPE: Mediterranean Pinwheels (mediterranean-pinwheels-vegetarian-appetizer-vegan-and-low-carb-options.md)
CUISINES: Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mediterranean-pinwheels-vegetarian-appetizer-vegan-and-low-carb-options/
SOURCE: Adapted from domesticsuperhero.com
SOURCE_URL: https://domesticsuperhero.com/mediterranean-pinwheels-vegetarian-appetizer/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6 large Spinach or Sun-dried Tomato Tortillas
  - 8 oz Cream Cheese, softened
  - 2 tbsp Oil (reserved from sun-dried tomato jar)
  - 2 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 6 oz Sun-dried Tomatoes in oil, chopped
  - 10 oz Frozen Spinach, thawed and squeezed bone-dry
  - 1/4 cup Grated Parmesan
  - 1/3 cup Feta Cheese, crumbled
  - 1 cup Fresh Basil leaves
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

These quick appetizers or lunch components require proper technique to avoid falling apart. Blending cream cheese with flavored oil from sun-dried tomatoes creates a tacky, flavor-rich spread that binds the fillings to the tortilla. Squeeze spinach until bone-dry - wet spinach makes tortillas soggy and causes rolls to unravel.

## Directions

1.  **The Bind:** In a food processor, blend cream cheese, garlic, a few sun-dried tomatoes, and 2 tbsp of the tomato oil until completely smooth.
2.  **Prep:** Lay out the 6 tortillas. Spread a thick, even layer of the cream cheese mixture over each, leaving a 1/2-inch border at the top.
3.  **Layer:** Scatter the chopped spinach, remaining sun-dried tomatoes, Parmesan, and feta over the cream cheese. Place a single line of fresh basil leaves across the center of each tortilla.
4.  **The Roll:** Starting from the edge parallel to the basil, roll the tortilla **very tightly**, squeezing gently as you go to ensure the "Emulsion" binds the layers.
5.  **The Finish:** Wrap each log tightly in plastic wrap and **refrigerate for at least 30 minutes** (mandatory for clean slicing).
6.  **Cut:** Using a sharp serrated knife, slice into 1-inch pinwheels.

RECIPE: Mediterranean Salmon with Lemon-Herb Emulsion (mediterranean-salmon-with-lemon-herb-emulsion.md)
CUISINES: Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mediterranean-salmon-with-lemon-herb-emulsion/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 skin-on salmon fillets, 6–8 oz each, of similar thickness
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, for searing salmon
  - 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the dressing
  - 1 tbsp olive oil, for chickpeas
  - 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the orzo
  - 1 large lemon, zested before juicing
  - 1 clove garlic, grated
  - 1 tsp honey
  - 1 tsp fresh oregano, chopped
  - 1 tsp smoked paprika, divided equally between salmon and chickpeas
  - 1 cup dry orzo
  - 1 cup canned chickpeas, measured after draining and rinsing, then thoroughly dried
  - 8 oz cherry tomatoes, halved
  - 4 oz feta cheese, crumbled
  - Fresh parsley and mint, chopped, to taste
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This lemon-herb emulsion is a shaken olive-oil dressing: it turns cloudy as oil disperses into lemon juice, then separates again as it stands. Shake just before serving. Add roasted chickpeas at the last moment so the moist orzo does not immediately soften their crisp edges.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Heat the oven to **400°F / 205°C**. Drain, rinse and thoroughly dry the chickpeas. Zest the lemon, then juice it. Halve tomatoes, chop herbs and measure the separate oil amounts. Pat salmon skin dry, remove pin bones and refrigerate while starting the sides.
2. **Roast chickpeas:** Toss chickpeas with **their allotted oil, half the smoked paprika**, salt and pepper. Spread in one layer on a rimmed tray. Roast about **25–35 minutes**, shaking at about 15 minutes, until lightly crisp and beginning to brown. Begin checking at 20 minutes; do not insist that the centers turn hard.
3. **Mix dressing and cook orzo:** Shake **the dressing oil**, garlic, honey, oregano and **half the lemon juice** in a closed jar. Taste, then add more of the remaining lemon juice, salt and pepper as needed. Meanwhile cook orzo in boiling salted water according to its package until tender with a little bite. Drain, then toss with **the orzo oil**, tomatoes, feta, parsley and mint. Cover briefly to keep warm while the fish cooks.
4. **Heat the skillet:** When chickpeas are about 10 minutes from ready, season salmon with lemon zest, **the remaining smoked paprika**, salt and pepper. Heat **the salmon oil** in a broad skillet over medium-high until shimmering, not smoking heavily. If portions cannot fit with space between them, use two skillets with the oil divided between them, or cook in batches, reserving a proportional share of the searing oil for each batch.
5. **Sear and finish:** Lay salmon skin-side down, away from you. Press gently with a spatula for the first few seconds to keep skin in contact. Cook about **4–6 minutes** until the skin browns and releases; reduce heat if spices darken rapidly. Turn carefully and cook about **2–6 minutes** more, depending on thickness. Check the thickest center from the side for **145°F / 63°C**. If the outside is done before the center, lower the heat and continue gently. Remove each portion when ready.
6. **Assemble:** Divide the herbed orzo among plates, scatter over roasted chickpeas and add salmon with its skin facing up. Shake the dressing again and spoon around the fish and over the orzo, keeping the skin exposed. Serve immediately. The pasta, legumes and tomatoes are already part of this dish; a separate grain is unnecessary.

RECIPE: Melon Daiquiri (melon-daiquiri.md)
CUISINES: Caribbean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/melon-daiquiri/
SOURCE: Adapted from The Ritz-Carlton, Cancun
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6 cups Honeydew Melon, peeled, deseeded and cubed
  - 1 cup Light Rum
  - 1/2 cup Fresh Lime Juice (The Acid Balance)
  - 1/2 cup green melon liqueur
  - 12 Cantaloupe cubes (1/2-inch)
  - 4 Sugar Cane Skewers
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The daiquiri is a Cuban drink named after a beach near Santiago - born from American occupation and the sugar trade. A good daiquiri is balanced: rum, lime juice, and sugar in equal parts, with the lime juice providing the backbone. Using fresh melon brings fruit sweetness without needing extra sugar, which keeps the drink bright instead of cloying.

## Directions

1.  **Thermal Prep:** Freeze your melon cubes for 30 minutes prior to starting for the best texture.
2.  **Blend:** Combine the honeydew, light rum, lime juice, and melon liqueur in a high-powered blender.
3.  **Process:** Pulse on low, then increase to high until perfectly smooth. Add a handful of ice only if needed to reach a "thick-shake" consistency.
4.  **Skew:** Thread 3 cantaloupe cubes onto each sugar cane skewer.
5.  **Serve:** Pour into chilled coupes or martini glasses. Garnish with the skewers and serve immediately for the maximum "Bounce."

RECIPE: Arroz Rojo (mexican-red-rice.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mexican-red-rice/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup dry long-grain white rice
  - 2 tbsp neutral oil
  - 1 cup plain tomato puree, or 1 cup freshly blended Roma tomatoes
  - 1 cup chicken broth, plus hot water as needed if the rice remains firm
  - 1/4 cup yellow onion, finely diced
  - 2 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1 tsp salt
  - 1 sprig cilantro
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Toasting brings a lightly nutty flavor to this tomato rice. It does not seal the grains against water: the rice still needs enough liquid and gentle cooking to soften. Measure the tomato, drain the rinsed rice well, and leave time for the covered rest before serving.

## Directions

1. **Rinse and drain:** Rinse the dry rice in several changes of cool water until less cloudy. Drain thoroughly in a fine-mesh strainer, shaking out excess water while you dice the onion and mince the garlic.
2. **Toast:** Warm the oil in a heavy saucepan over medium heat. Carefully add the drained rice; residual water can spatter. Stir constantly for about 3–5 minutes, until the grains look opaque and lightly golden and smell nutty. Lower the heat if individual grains darken quickly.
3. **Add aromatics:** Stir in the onion and garlic. Cook for about 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant without browning the garlic.
4. **Add liquid:** Carefully stir in the measured tomato puree, broth and salt. Bring to a gentle boil, stirring once to distribute the rice and release any grains stuck to the base.
5. **Simmer and check:** Place the cilantro sprig on top. Cover tightly and reduce to a low simmer. Cook about 15–18 minutes without repeatedly opening the lid. Taste a grain: it should have no hard center, and free liquid should be absorbed. If firm and dry, add a little hot water and continue covered; if firm with liquid remaining, continue gently without adding more.
6. **Rest:** Remove from heat once tender and leave covered for 10 minutes.
7. **Finish:** Remove the cilantro sprig. Fluff gently with a fork and divide into four side portions.

RECIPE: Skillet Esquites (Mexican Corn Salad) (mexican-street-corn-salad.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mexican-street-corn-salad/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 cups (600 g) fresh sweet-corn kernels or thawed frozen corn, thoroughly drained
  - 2 tbsp neutral oil, divided
  - 2 tbsp mayonnaise
  - 2 tbsp Mexican crema or sour cream
  - 2 tbsp fresh lime juice, divided, plus more to taste
  - 1/4 cup (30 g) crumbled cotija cheese
  - 1/2 tsp pure ground ancho chile (not a salted seasoning blend)
  - 1 small garlic clove, finely grated
  - 2 scallions, thinly sliced
  - 1/4 cup chopped cilantro
  - 1/2 jalapeño, finely diced, optional
  - Fine salt, to taste after adding the cotija
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Esquites takes several forms, including brothy cups and fried preparations. This skillet salad uses sweet corn. Brown some surfaces for flavor, then finish with chile, lime, cheese, and a modest creamy dressing. Blackening every kernel would hide the corn's sweetness.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and mix the dressing:** Drain corn thoroughly and blot away surface water. Whisk mayonnaise, crema, 1 tbsp lime juice, ground ancho chile, and garlic in a large bowl. Set aside the remaining lime, cheese, scallions, cilantro, and optional jalapeño.
2. **Brown the first batch:** Heat 1 tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add half the corn and spread it out. Leave for about 2 minutes, then stir and continue cooking for 3–5 minutes, until tender with golden-brown patches. Reduce heat if it spits violently or scorches. Transfer to a wide plate.
3. **Repeat:** Add the remaining oil and corn. Cook the second batch in the same way, adjusting the heat as needed. If dark residue is burning, remove it carefully before adding the second batch.
4. **Dress while warm:** Let the corn stop steaming vigorously for 2–3 minutes. Add both batches to the dressing and toss. Fold in cotija, scallions, cilantro, and optional jalapeño.
5. **Balance and serve:** Taste, add the remaining lime by the teaspoon as needed, and add salt only if the cheese has not supplied enough. Divide into six side portions and serve warm or cool. Chill promptly if making ahead.

RECIPE: Yogurt-Marinated Chicken and Onion Kabobs (middle-eastern-style-grilled-chicken-kabobs.md)
CUISINES: Middle Eastern-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/middle-eastern-style-grilled-chicken-kabobs/
SOURCE: Adapted from Jennifer Segal's Middle Eastern-Style Grilled Chicken Kabobs, Once Upon a Chef
SOURCE_URL: https://www.onceuponachef.com/recipes/middle-eastern-chicken-kabobs.html
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 1/2 lbs (1130 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, trimmed and cut into about thirty-six 1 1/2-inch pieces
  - 250 g peeled red onion, cut into 1-inch squares and separated into single or thin paired layers
  - 1 cup (240 g) plain whole-milk Greek yogurt
  - 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 1 tbsp finely grated lemon zest
  - 5 medium garlic cloves, finely grated
  - 2 tsp sweet paprika
  - 1/2 tsp ground cumin
  - 1/8 tsp ground cinnamon
  - 1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, plus up to 1/2 tsp more for extra heat
  - 10 g fine salt
  - 1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
  - 1 tsp neutral oil, for grill grates (or 1 tbsp for the three-batch skillet option)
  - 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
  - 1/2 lemon, cut into wedges
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This home-style version is adapted from Jennifer Segal's Middle Eastern-inspired chicken kabobs, with garlic, lemon, yogurt and a restrained pinch of cinnamon. The yogurt is a marinade rather than a serving sauce. Thin onion layers and evenly cut chicken help the skewers finish together; a thin coating develops browned patches while excess marinade can stick and scorch.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and coat:** Cut the peeled onion into one-inch squares and separate into single or thin paired layers. Cut chicken into about thirty-six pieces roughly 1 1/2 inches across, keeping thickness similar. In a bowl large enough to hold everything, whisk yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice and zest, garlic, paprika, cumin, cinnamon, the desired red pepper flakes, salt and black pepper. Add chicken and onion and turn to coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for eight to twenty-four hours.
2. **Prepare the grill:** Near the end of marinating, heat a gas grill with the lid closed, then keep a medium-high cooking zone and a low or unlit zone. For charcoal, allow coals to establish and arrange them on one side, leaving the other side cooler. Follow the grill's lighting instructions. Set out a clean serving platter and utensils; the raw-marinated tray is not the serving platter.
3. **Thread and drain:** Divide chicken among twelve 10–12-inch skewers, about three pieces each. Distribute onion in thin layers between the chicken and at both ends, keeping the whole food-bearing length over the cooking zone. Do not thicken the onion stacks to use it up; use an additional onion-only skewer if needed and count it in the grill capacity. All this onion has contacted raw chicken and must be cooked; it cannot become a raw garnish. Thread without tightly compressing or wrapping pieces into thick bundles. Let excess marinade drain back into its bowl so a thin film remains, then discard the residue. Keep six skewers refrigerated while the first six cook, unless the grill is large enough for the whole batch with a clear cooler zone. Lightly oil clean grates with the measured teaspoon neutral oil using a folded paper towel held in long tongs.
4. **Grill the first round:** Lay six skewers over the cooking zone without touching. Close the lid between turns and turn about every three minutes once the first surface releases, using a broad spatula to help if needed. Cook for about twelve to fifteen minutes, moving skewers to the cooler zone if the coating browns too quickly. Cook any extra onion skewer alongside until the layers soften and reach 165°F / 74°C because of their raw-chicken contact. Onion edges should soften with some browned spots; the chicken coating need not become uniformly crisp.
5. **Check and repeat:** Begin checking around twelve minutes. Probe the largest pieces on each skewer from the side, avoiding the hot metal, and continue until each reaches at least 165°F / 74°C. Check any unusually thick pieces separately. Transfer fully cooked skewers to the clean platter and cover loosely during the short second round. Cook the remaining six the same way, keeping the same thermometer endpoint. A tight cover softens the coating, and the first round will not retain the same surface texture as chicken served straight from the grill.
6. **Rest and finish:** Rest the final round for five minutes, then serve two skewers per person with the chopped parsley and lemon wedges. For six plates, add one-and-a-half four-side batches of Lemon and Herb Instant Couscous, starting with 375 g dry couscous, plus vegetables or salad. Alternatively, warm six pita breads and add a vegetable side. These are extra components and preparation time. The onion in each portion is a seasoning vegetable, about 40 g raw weight, not a full vegetable side.

RECIPE: Mini-Shell Pasta with Bacon and Peas (mini-shell-pasta-with-creamy-smoked-bacon-and-peas.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mini-shell-pasta-with-creamy-smoked-bacon-and-peas/
SOURCE: Adapted from The New York Times, Mini-Shell Pasta with Creamy Smoked Bacon and Peas
SOURCE_URL: https://mobile.nytimes.com/2009/10/11/magazine/11food-rex002.html?referer=https://www.google.com/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb dry mini-shell pasta
  - 10 slices smoked bacon, cut crosswise into thin slivers
  - 2 cups frozen peas
  - 2 tbsp crème fraîche or heavy cream
  - 1 lemon, juiced, added gradually to taste
  - 6 oz Parmesan, finely grated
  - 2 tbsp fresh mint, finely chopped, divided between sauce and garnish
  - 1 tbsp unsalted butter
  - 1 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Mini shells catch the peas while smoked bacon and a generous amount of Parmesan make a rich sauce. Cook the peas fully, then combine the hot ingredients and move away from direct heat before adding cheese. Keep some of the measured mint for serving so its aroma stays fresh.

## Directions

1. **Start water and prepare:** Bring pasta water to a boil. Cut bacon into thin slivers, finely grate Parmesan, chop mint and juice the lemon. Season the water moderately; bacon and cheese bring much of the salt.
2. **Cook bacon:** Melt butter in a large deep skillet over medium-low to medium. Add bacon and cook, stirring, about **10–15 minutes** or as its package directs, until cooked through and golden with crisp edges. Lower heat if butter darkens quickly. Keep the rendered fat for the sauce; do not add more oil.
3. **Cook pasta and peas:** Meanwhile cook pasta according to package directions until tender with a little bite. Cook peas fully according to their package in a separate saucepan or microwave-safe bowl and drain. Reserve **the listed pasta water** before draining pasta without rinsing.
4. **Combine:** Stir cooked peas, crème fraîche or cream and **half the mint** into the bacon pan over low heat. Add hot pasta and about **one-quarter of the reserved water**. Toss gently until hot and coated, using the pasta pot instead if the skillet is too full.
5. **Add cheese off heat:** Remove from the burner and wait until bubbling subsides. Fold in Parmesan a handful at a time, adding warm water in small amounts as needed for a creamy coating. Add **half the lemon juice**, taste, then add more of the remaining juice only as needed. The sauce should remain slightly loose for plating.
6. **Serve:** Add black pepper and taste before salt. Divide into the intended portions and scatter **the remaining measured mint** over the top. Serve promptly.

Adapted from [The New York Times’ Mini-Shell Pasta with Creamy Smoked Bacon and Peas](https://www.nytimes.com/2009/10/11/magazine/11food-rex002.html).

RECIPE: Mint Tzatziki with Honey (mint-tzatziki.md)

URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mint-tzatziki/

INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup (240 g) plain full-fat Greek yogurt

## Chef's Note

Fine cucumber dice keeps a little crunch, while thick Greek yogurt and olive oil give the sauce a cool, spoonable texture. Fresh mint should stay clear, with garlic and a little honey in the background. The honey softens the tartness without making the sauce taste sweet.

## Directions

RECIPE: Miriam’s Melt-In-Your-Mouth Rosh Hashanah Brisket (miriams-melt-in-your-mouth-rosh-hashanah-brisket.md)
CUISINES: Jewish
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/miriams-melt-in-your-mouth-rosh-hashanah-brisket/
SOURCE: Adapted from Miriam Szokovski, Chabad.org
SOURCE_URL: https://www.chabad.org/recipes/recipe_cdo/aid/2635033/jewish/Miriams-Melt-in-Your-Mouth-Rosh-Hashanah-Brisket.htm
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Brisket and Onions ---
  - 3 lb first-cut brisket, well-marbled
  - 2 large Spanish onions, sliced into thick rounds
  - --- Spice Rub ---
  - 2 tbsp paprika
  - 2 tbsp garlic powder
  - 1 tbsp kosher salt
  - 2 tbsp dried chives, optional
  - --- Braising Sauce ---
  - 1/2 cup balsamic vinegar
  - 1/3 cup honey
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Miriam Szokovski’s honey-and-balsamic brisket is a Rosh Hashanah centerpiece with onions cooked underneath the meat. Its uncovered 400°F start is followed by a tightly covered 250°F braise; check for tenderness with a fork rather than treating four hours as a guarantee. Chilling makes thin slices easier, and all the onions, sauce and rendered fat can return to the serving dish.

## Directions

1. **Foundation:** Preheat the oven to 400°F. Lay large Spanish onions across the bottom of a heavy baking dish or Dutch oven. Choose a vessel in which the meat can lie without folding or crowding, with room for its juices and a tight lid or foil cover. For a larger batch, use enough vessels and divide all the onions, rub and liquids in proportion to the meat in each; a smaller batch needs an appropriately smaller vessel.
2. **Rub:** Mix paprika, garlic powder, kosher salt, and dried chives (if using) in a small bowl, omitting the chives if not using them. Pat the full measured rub over both sides of first-cut brisket.
3. **Uncovered Roast:** Place first-cut brisket on the onions. Roast uncovered for 1 hour for the original 3 lb batch. Watch for browning rather than blackened spices or onions; smaller or thinner cuts need earlier browning checks, and pan shape affects the result.
4. **Cover:** Remove the dish from the oven. Pour balsamic vinegar and honey over the meat, retaining all its juices. Cover tightly with a heavy lid or double layer of foil, and reduce the oven to 250°F. The onions and meat release liquid during the covered cook.
5. **Low and Slow:** Return the covered dish to the oven and begin checking around 4 more hours for the original batch. Turn the meat about once an hour, or at least once halfway through, spooning the liquid back over it and promptly replacing the cover. Begin checking tenderness earlier for smaller or thinner cuts, and allow longer for thicker cuts. Continue until a fork enters with almost no resistance; size, thickness, pan and oven can change the clock. Check that the center has reached at least 145°F, then let it rest at least 3 minutes before handling.
6. **Chill for Slicing:** Divide the cooked brisket into smaller sections that can lie in shallow containers, and divide all the onions, juices and rendered fat among them. Refrigerate promptly at 40°F or below, within 2 hours of cooking, or within 1 hour above 90°F. Do not leave a deep pan on the counter until completely cold. Chill until the meat is cold throughout, preferably overnight.
7. **Slice and Reheat:** Remove the cold meat and slice thinly against the grain. Reheat the full onions, sauce and fat in a saucepan, stirring to bring the sauce to a rolling boil briefly. Return all of it to the sliced meat and reheat covered in the oven or on the stovetop until the meat and sauce reach 165°F throughout, checking several places. Serve with all the onions and sauce; prolonged boiling will concentrate the sweet sauce, so avoid unnecessary continued reduction.
