RECIPE: Misir Wot (Ethiopian Red Lentil Stew) (misir-wot.md)
CUISINES: Ethiopian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/misir-wot/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 cups Red Lentils, rinsed until water runs clear
  - 3 cups Water
  - 3 tbsp Niter Kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced butter) or Extra-Virgin Olive Oil for vegan
  - 2 large Red Onions, finely diced (about 3 cups for the original batch)
  - 4 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1 (1-inch) piece Fresh Ginger, grated
  - 3 tbsp Berbere Spice Blend
  - 2 tbsp Tomato Paste
  - 1 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1/2 tsp Ground Cardamom
  - 1/4 tsp Ground Fenugreek
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice, for finishing
  - Additional water, as needed to adjust the stew consistency
  - Additional kosher salt, to taste after cooking
  - Additional berbere, to taste after cooking
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Berbere and niter kibbeh give this Ethiopian lentil stew its spiced, buttery character; the same-volume olive-oil option gives a different, dairy-free base. Start the finely diced onions without fat until softened and concentrated, then add the full listed fat before the aromatics. This stage is not a promise of deep caramelization in ten minutes. Cook the lentils until they lose their firm centers, then adjust the stew to a thick, scoopable consistency.

## Directions

1. **Soften the onions:** Put all diced onions in a heavy pot over medium heat without oil. Stir frequently for 8–10 minutes as a first check, until their released moisture has reduced and the onions soften. Lower heat if they catch; stop at softened onions with reduced moisture rather than waiting for deep caramelization.
2. **Add fat and spices:** Add all the listed niter kibbeh or olive oil and cook 3–4 minutes until onions begin to turn golden. Add all garlic and grated ginger and stir 30–45 seconds. Add all the measured berbere, tomato paste, cardamom and fenugreek and stir 2 minutes without scorching.
3. **Cook the lentils:** Add all rinsed red lentils, all the listed cooking water and measured kosher salt. Bring to a boil, lower to a gentle simmer and cover. Cook 25–30 minutes as a first check, stirring every 5–7 minutes and reaching the bottom to prevent sticking, until the lentils have broken down with no firm centers. For scaled batches follow the listed water and salt amounts.
4. **Adjust consistency:** If too thick before the lentils are tender, use the separate water allowance a few tablespoons at a time and continue the gentle simmer. If tender but too thin, simmer uncovered briefly until thick and scoopable. Use a vessel with room to stir the full batch; divide the complete formula proportionally among more pots if needed.
5. **Finish:** Stir in all the measured lemon juice. Taste the fully cooked stew and use the separate additional salt and berbere allowances only if wanted; simmer briefly after an extra spice addition to incorporate it. Keep the full listed berbere and fat in the main formula.
6. **Serve:** Serve thick and scoopable with injera, or over separately prepared basmati rice. The starch accompaniment has its own preparation and clock.

RECIPE: Miso-Glazed Roasted Cauliflower (miso-glazed-roasted-cauliflower.md)
CUISINES: Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/miso-glazed-roasted-cauliflower/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Mirin glaze ---
  - 3 tbsp white miso paste
  - 2 tbsp mirin
  - 1 tbsp soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp sesame oil
  - 1 tbsp rice vinegar
  - 1 tsp fresh ginger, minced
  - --- Honey variation — replaces mirin ---
  - 1 1/2 tbsp honey, optional
  - 1/2 tbsp additional soy sauce, optional
  - --- Cauliflower ---
  - 1 1/2 lb fresh cauliflower florets, similar-sized; washed and dried, very large florets split
  - --- Garnish ---
  - sesame seeds, for garnishing
  - scallions, for garnishing, washed and thinly sliced
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

White miso, mirin, soy sauce, sesame oil and rice vinegar make a concentrated glaze for the cauliflower. This sauce coats the florets before roasting, so check it when turning: miso and sweeteners can darken before a thick center is tender. Split unusually large florets, keep the sheet uncrowded and stop at browned coating and tender centers rather than forcing a black char.

## Directions

1. **Heat and prepare:** Heat the oven to 425°F. Set out a large rimmed sheet or enough sheets for one layer of the measured florets. If lining, use parchment rated for this heat or suitable foil. Wash the cauliflower under running water, divide into similar-sized florets, split very large ones and dry them.
2. **Choose one glaze route:** Set out white miso paste, mirin, soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, fresh ginger, honey (if using), and additional soy sauce (if using) and choose one sweetening route before combining. For the mirin version, use the mirin and omit the optional honey and additional soy sauce. For the honey variation, omit mirin and use the measured honey plus additional soy sauce, while retaining the separately listed soy sauce. Do not combine both routes. Whisk the chosen ingredients until the miso is evenly dispersed; taste a small sample to understand the salty, sweet and acidic balance.
3. **Coat and spread:** Toss fresh cauliflower florets with all the chosen glaze in the large bowl. Spread in a single layer, with flat cut faces against the sheet where possible. Keep room between pieces; if the scaled batch piles up, use additional sheets or batches rather than a deeper layer.
4. **Watch the coating and centers:** Roast for 25–30 minutes, gently turning around halfway through and checking the coating then. Test a thick floret with a knife: its center should be tender and the coating browned without blackened bitterness. If the glaze darkens before the centers soften, move pieces away from hot spots, turn the dark faces upward and finish under loose foil while checking the centers; covered pieces will have softer edges. Remove ready pieces promptly rather than requiring every edge to char. More sheet area or larger florets may change the time.
5. **Garnish and serve:** Scatter sesame seeds and scallions over the hot cauliflower and serve. The sesame seeds and scallions are both included finishes; wash the scallions before slicing and keep them away from raw-meat tools.

## Honey–Soy Variation

Replace the measured mirin with the measured honey and additional soy sauce from the variation list, keeping the separately listed soy sauce as well. In the original 1½-pound cauliflower batch this is 1½ tablespoons honey plus ½ tablespoon additional soy sauce, giving 1½ tablespoons soy sauce total. Increase or decrease all these amounts with the cauliflower batch; do not add this variation to the mirin route. This honey version is non-vegan. Use mirin and ingredients suitable for a vegan diet for the vegan version.

RECIPE: Miso-Mashed Potatoes (miso-mashed-potatoes.md)
CUISINES: American, Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/miso-mashed-potatoes/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 900 g peeled and trimmed Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into even 1-inch pieces
  - 2 L cold water, or enough to cover the potatoes by about 1 inch
  - 8 g salt, for the cooking water
  - 4 tbsp (57 g) unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
  - 2 tbsp (36 g) plain white rice miso, without added dashi; choose certified gluten-free miso if needed
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) whole milk, plus up to 1/4 cup (60 ml) more if needed
  - 1/2 tsp garlic powder
  - 1/8 tsp fine salt, optional after tasting
  - 2 tbsp thinly sliced washed scallion greens, optional garnish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

White miso gives a familiar butter-and-milk mash a savory fermented seasoning. This Japanese-inspired variation uses miso as both flavor and seasoning, so taste before adding finishing salt. Whisk the miso into warm dairy first, then fold gently into fully tender potatoes; warmth helps keep dinner hot, while limited mixing protects the texture.

## Directions

1. **Cut and cover:** Peel and trim the potatoes to the listed net weight, then cut into even one-inch pieces. Rinse briefly, put in a 5-quart pot and cover with about two liters cold water, adding enough to sit an inch above the potatoes. Add the eight grams of cooking-water salt.
2. **Simmer to tenderness:** Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook about 18–22 minutes after the water begins simmering, until several tested pieces yield easily to a knife and a cooled bite is completely soft in the center. Keep cooking if needed; larger pieces take longer.
3. **Warm the miso dairy during cooking:** In a small saucepan over low heat, whisk the initial half-cup milk with the miso and garlic powder until the miso has no large clumps. Add the butter and warm gently until melted. Do not boil or reduce the mixture. Wash and slice the optional scallions while the potatoes finish.
4. **Drain and briefly dry:** Drain well in a colander. Return potatoes to the pot over low heat for one to two minutes, shaking gently, until surface water evaporates and the pieces look matte. Remove from heat before they stick or brown.
5. **Mash and fold:** Pass the hot potatoes through a ricer or mash gently by hand. Fold in the warm miso dairy in two additions with a spatula, stopping as soon as it is incorporated. If stiff, warm and add the reserved milk one tablespoon at a time until the mash forms a soft mound. Do not beat it smooth in a blender.
6. **Taste and serve:** Taste before adding the optional one-eighth teaspoon of salt; the miso may supply all the finishing seasoning needed. Scatter with the optional scallions and divide into four generous side portions, or six smaller portions on a plate with another starch. Pair with a simply seasoned roast and a crisp or lemony vegetable.

RECIPE: Miso Salmon with Bok Choy (miso-salmon-with-bok-choy.md)
CUISINES: Japanese, Chinese, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/miso-salmon-with-bok-choy/
SOURCE: Jordan Silton
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Rice ---
  - 270 g dry jasmine white rice
  - 540 ml water, for rice, plus water for rinsing
  - --- Salmon and marinade ---
  - 900 g skinless, boneless salmon, divided into four similar fillets
  - 3 tbsp white miso
  - 3 tbsp honey
  - 2 tbsp Japanese soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp mirin
  - 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 2 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar
  - 3 garlic cloves, finely minced, divided
  - 6 scallions, finely sliced, divided
  - 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper, divided
  - 1 tsp neutral oil, for the foil
  - --- Bok choy ---
  - 600 g trimmed baby bok choy, washed and dried
  - 4 tsp neutral oil, for the skillet, divided
  - 2 tbsp water, for the bok choy, divided
  - 2 tbsp oyster sauce, divided
  - 1 tsp toasted sesame oil, divided
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Jordan Silton's miso salmon pairs a honey-miso marinade with lemon, rice vinegar, garlic and scallions. Oyster-seasoned bok choy and jasmine rice complete the plate. Drain the fish well before roasting and watch closely during the brief broiler finish.

## Directions

1. **Start rice and heat the oven:** Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C with a rack in the middle and another positioned for the later broil. Rinse the jasmine rice and drain well. Put it in a heavy 2-quart saucepan with 540 ml water, bring to a boil, cover and reduce to low. Simmer about 15 minutes until water is absorbed, then move off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Fluff before serving. This is a starting method for regular jasmine white rice; follow the package if its ratio differs.
2. **Mix and divide the marinade:** While the rice cooks, whisk miso, honey, soy sauce, mirin, lemon juice, rice vinegar, half the minced garlic, half the scallions and half the pepper. Reserve 2 tbsp in a clean bowl for finishing. Check fish for pin bones and pat dry; place it in a shallow dish with the remaining marinade, turn to coat, cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes. Do not leave this acidic marinade on overnight.
3. **Prepare the vegetables and pans:** During the marinade, split small bok choy heads lengthwise; quarter larger heads so thick stem sections are about 1 inch across. Wash between the stalks, drain and dry thoroughly, then divide into two equal batches. Divide the remaining garlic, scallions and pepper between those batches. Line a metal half-sheet pan with foil and spread its teaspoon of oil where the fish will sit.
4. **Roast the salmon:** Lift fish from the marinade, letting excess drip off. Gently scrape off thick clumps, leaving a thin coating. Arrange on the prepared pan with space between portions and discard the raw-contact marinade. Roast about 12–16 minutes, until the fish is nearly cooked; check its center toward the end. If it reaches 145°F / 63°C before the final broil, it is already cooked and needs at most a very brief coloring step.
5. **Cook bok choy in two batches:** While fish roasts, heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat with 2 tsp neutral oil. Add half the bok choy cut-side down and cook 2–3 minutes until lightly browned. Turn, add half the reserved vegetable garlic and scallions, and stir 30 seconds until fragrant. Add 1 tbsp water, cover and steam 1–2 minutes until stems are crisp-tender. Uncover, evaporate any pooled water, then toss with 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1/2 tsp sesame oil and half the remaining pepper. Transfer to a serving dish and loosely cover. Repeat with the second batch and the remaining vegetable ingredients. Turn off the skillet before broiling; if the fish is waiting for its finish, set its pan briefly on a heatproof surface.
6. **Glaze and briefly broil:** Spread the clean reserved 2 tbsp marinade over the four fillets, using a clean utensil. Switch to high broil and place the fish surface 7–9 inches below the element. Watch continuously for 1–3 minutes, until the coating bubbles and browns. Check each fillet sideways in its thickest center and cook to 145°F / 63°C. If color arrives first, finish gently in the oven as described above. Let the fish stand briefly while fluffing and serving the rice.
7. **Serve the complete dinner:** Divide all the rice and bok choy among four bowls or plates and add one fillet to each. The original batch supplies about 225 g raw salmon and 150 g trimmed bok choy per diner, with roughly a cup of cooked rice. A small cucumber salad is an optional cool contrast, rather than a second required vegetable batch.

RECIPE: Miso Sesame Dense Bean Salad (miso-sesame-dense-bean-salad.md)
CUISINES: Asian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/miso-sesame-dense-bean-salad/
SOURCE: bakerita.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.bakerita.com/miso-sesame-dense-bean-salad/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
  - 1 cup shelled edamame
  - 1 cup snap peas, optional, when in season
  - 2 cups shredded cabbage
  - 1 cup shredded carrots
  - 4 green onions, thinly sliced
  - Roasted peanuts or almonds, chopped, optional
  - MISO SESAME DRESSING
  - 3 tablespoons white or chickpea miso
  - 2 tablespoons tamari
  - 2 tablespoons rice vinegar
  - 2 tablespoons roasted sesame seeds
  - 1 tablespoon lime juice
  - 1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil
  - 1 teaspoon sweetener, like honey, maple syrup, or coconut sugar

## Chef's Note

Cook and cool edamame as its package directs before it joins the chickpeas and crunchy vegetables. Whisk the thick miso with tamari and the measured acids until smooth, then toss thoroughly so the seasoning does not remain in isolated clumps. Add the optional nuts at serving for crunch.

RECIPE: Miso Soup (miso-soup.md)
CUISINES: Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/miso-soup/
SOURCE: Adapted from Epicurious.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/miso-soup-103391
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 cups prepared dashi, homemade or made with instant dashi granules according to package instructions
  - 3 tbsp Shiro Miso (White Miso)
  - 4 oz Silken Tofu, cut into small cubes
  - 1 tbsp Dried Wakame Seaweed
  - 2 Green Onions, thinly sliced
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Whisk miso smooth with some of the prepared dashi before returning it to the pot off the heat. This disperses the paste through the broth without crushing the silken tofu. Dashi can contain bonito; choose a clearly vegetarian stock if you need a vegetarian version, and measure its finished liquid rather than assuming starting water equals strained yield.

## Directions

1. **Prepare wakame:** Follow the dried wakame package's preparation instructions, using all the listed wakame. If it requires a separate soak and drain, complete that before adding it to the soup; use enough soaking water as instructed and discard it. Wash and thinly slice the green onions.
2. **Heat dashi:** Measure all the prepared dashi into a saucepan with room for tofu and seaweed. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce heat to low. Homemade [Dashi](/mise/recipes/dashi-japanese-sea-stock) is a separately prepared component; measure its strained output for this soup. Instant granules must be prepared according to their package.
3. **Warm tofu and seaweed:** Gently add all the tofu cubes and prepared wakame. Simmer gently, starting with about 2 minutes, until tofu is heated through and the seaweed is tender; product preparation and starting temperature affect the clock. Avoid rough stirring that breaks the tofu.
4. **Disperse miso:** Put all the miso in a small bowl. Ladle enough broth from this same pot to whisk it smooth, about 1/2 cup at the original batch. This is part of the measured dashi, not additional water or stock.
5. **Finish:** Turn off the heat. Gently stir all the miso mixture back into the pot. Add all the green onions and serve promptly in the listed planning number of small bowls.

## Six-serving variation

For a separate six-serving batch, use 6 cups prepared dashi, 1/2 cup dried wakame, 1/4 cup shiro miso, 1/2 lb soft tofu drained and cut into 1/2-inch cubes, and 1/4 cup washed, thinly sliced scallion greens. Do not combine these amounts with the four-serving ingredient list. Soak this wakame in warm water covering it by 1 inch for 15 minutes or until reconstituted, following its package if preparation differs; drain in a sieve and discard the soaking water. Whisk all the miso with 1/2 cup taken from the measured dashi. Heat the remaining dashi until hot, gently stir in tofu and wakame, simmer about 1 minute until heated through, then remove from heat and immediately stir in all the miso mixture and scallion greens. If scaling this separate version, scale all its measured ingredients together; package preparation and saucepan heating time do not multiply. The listed ingredient controls apply to the four-serving main version.

RECIPE: Candy-Coated Chocolate Cookies (mm-cookies.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mm-cookies/
SOURCE: Adapted from allrecipes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/10785/robbis-mms-cookies/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Candy cookie dough ---
  - 1 cup shortening or unsalted butter, choose one; butter softened if used
  - 1 cup light brown sugar, packed
  - 1/2 cup granulated sugar
  - 2 large eggs
  - 1 1/2 tsp pure vanilla extract
  - 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  - 1 tsp baking soda
  - 1 tsp sea salt
  - 1 1/2 cups candy-coated milk chocolate candies
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Some candies are folded through the dough and the remaining portion is pressed onto the tops. Keep that reserved portion separate before scooping; distributing it by the actual number of cookies avoids running short while decorating.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 350°F and have ungreased baking sheets and a cooling rack ready.
2. **Cream:** Beat shortening or unsalted butter, light brown sugar, and granulated sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes, scraping the bowl.
3. **Add eggs:** Beat in large eggs and pure vanilla extract until evenly combined.
4. **Mix the dry ingredients:** Whisk all-purpose flour, baking soda, and sea salt in a separate bowl, then gradually stir into the wet mixture just until no dry flour remains.
5. **Fold in candies:** Fold 2/3 of the candy-coated milk chocolate candies into the dough, reserving the rest cleanly for the tops. This is 1 cup folded and ½ cup reserved in the original 72-cookie planning batch; both allocations follow the listed batch proportionally.
6. **Shape:** Drop teaspoonfuls onto the ungreased sheets, leaving space for spreading. Keep the portions consistent; the listed yield is a planning count for these small cookies. A larger batch needs more sheets and oven loads, not larger dough balls.
7. **Decorate:** Distribute 1/3 of the candy-coated milk chocolate candies across the dough portions, pressing them in slightly. Use all of this reserved amount; the number of candies on each cookie depends on candy size and the actual cookie count.
8. **Bake:** Wait for the oven to reach 350°F, then bake for 9–11 minutes per load, until the edges are lightly golden and the centers are set but soft. Keep remaining dough refrigerated at 40°F / 4°C or below between loads.
9. **Cool:** Leave the cookies on their sheets for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely before packing.

## Cooking Options

### Original candy allocation

For Robbi’s shortening route, fold half of the listed total candies into the dough and reserve half for decoration: ¾ cup for each destination in the original 72-cookie planning batch. Keep every other listed ingredient amount and the 350°F, 9–11-minute bake. This replaces the main two-thirds/one-third allocation; do not add another candy portion. Use a few of the reserved candies on each cookie and distribute the whole remainder across the actual batch.

The listed same-volume unsalted-butter option is a separate fat choice. Use softened butter in place of all the shortening, not both; its spread and texture can differ.

RECIPE: Momma’s Turkey and Vegetable Meatloaf (mommas-healthy-meatloaf.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mommas-healthy-meatloaf/
SOURCE: Adapted from Allrecipes.com
SOURCE_URL: http://allrecipes.com/recipe/240747/mommas-healthy-meatloaf/?internalSource=amp&referringContentType=amp%20recipe&clickId=amp_directions
INGREDIENTS:
  - 680 g ground turkey, preferably 93% lean
  - 40 g fine dry unseasoned whole-wheat breadcrumbs
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) milk
  - 1 tbsp olive oil
  - 100 g green bell pepper, cut into small dice
  - 75 g onion, finely diced
  - 75 g carrot, finely grated
  - 150 g zucchini, coarsely grated, then gently squeezed to about two thirds of its starting weight
  - 1 large egg
  - 1 tsp garlic powder
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
  - 1/4 cup (60 g) ketchup
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This keeps Momma’s vegetable-rich family loaf while making its proportions and turkey endpoint explicit. Soften the vegetables and evaporate loose water before they enter the mixture. Hydrate the crumbs separately and fold everything together gently. A consistent loaf shape and ten-minute rest make portioning more reliable.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment. Mix breadcrumbs and milk and let hydrate at least 5 minutes. Grate and gently squeeze the zucchini to about two-thirds of its starting weight; prepare the other small-cut vegetables.
2. **Soften and cool vegetables:** Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook onion and pepper about 5 minutes, stirring. Add carrot and zucchini and cook another 4–5 minutes until softened and no liquid pools in the pan. Spread on a plate to cool about 5–10 minutes while preparing the remaining ingredients; they should no longer feel hot.
3. **Mix:** Beat egg into the hydrated crumbs with garlic powder, salt and pepper. Stir in cooled vegetables. Add cold turkey and fold gently until evenly combined, without prolonged kneading.
4. **Shape and begin baking:** Shape a free-form loaf roughly 9 by 4 inches and 2–2 1/2 inches high on the prepared tray, smoothing large cracks without packing hard. Bake about 35 minutes.
5. **Glaze and check:** Spread all the ketchup over the top in a thin layer. Continue baking about 15–25 minutes, checking until the center reaches 165°F / 74°C in several positions. Extend as needed. If the top darkens early, tent loosely with foil; a browned glaze is not the doneness test.
6. **Rest and portion:** Let rest for 10 minutes before cutting six portions. Each can be one thick slice or two thinner slices. Serve with separately prepared sides; the base recipe includes the loaf and its ketchup finish only.

RECIPE: Chocolate Cake (moms-famous-chocolate-cake.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/moms-famous-chocolate-cake/
SOURCE: Adapted from Maryls McConnell
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Cake batter ---
  - 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter
  - 4 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder
  - 1 cup water, boiling
  - 2 cups granulated sugar
  - 1/2 cup buttermilk
  - 2 large eggs, room temperature
  - 2 cups all-purpose flour
  - 1 tsp baking soda
  - 1/4 tsp kosher salt
  - 1 tsp vanilla extract
  - --- Warm chocolate frosting ---
  - 1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter
  - 4 tbsp cocoa powder
  - 6 tbsp whole milk
  - 1 lb confectioners’ sugar
  - --- Pan preparation ---
  - butter or baking spray, enough to grease the selected pan or pans
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Maryls McConnell’s family cake is mixed in a saucepan and frosted while warm. Keep the full batter and frosting quantities separate. Let the heated cocoa mixture cool before the eggs go in so they blend into batter rather than cook into strands; the cake still receives its warm frosting straight after baking.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the pans:** Preheat the oven to 350°F. Use butter or baking spray to grease a 9×13-inch rectangular pan or two 8-inch square pans for the original batch. These are alternative pan layouts; divide the full batter and frosting between both squares if selected. When scaling, keep a similar batter depth with proportional pan area and additional pans as needed.
2. **Heat the cocoa mixture:** In a large saucepan over medium heat, bring unsalted butter, unsweetened cocoa powder, and water to a gentle boil. Remove the pan from the heat.
3. **Begin mixing and cool:** Whisk granulated sugar and buttermilk into the cocoa mixture off the heat. Let it cool until lukewarm and no longer steaming before adding eggs; stir occasionally. This cooling pause has no fixed duration.
4. **Add the eggs:** Whisk in large eggs, baking soda, and kosher salt until combined. Keep the pan off the stove; the egg mixture should blend in rather than form cooked strands.
5. **Finish the batter:** Fold in all-purpose flour and vanilla extract until no dry flour pockets remain. The batter can be mixed in the saucepan with a portable egg beater if the tool’s instructions permit its use in that pan.
6. **Bake:** Pour into the prepared pan or divide evenly between the two squares. Wait for the oven to reach 350°F. Bake for 25–30 minutes, until a tester inserted in the center comes out clean. Check each pan separately; different depths and oven loads can change the time.
7. **Make the full frosting:** While the cake bakes, use unsalted butter, cocoa powder, whole milk, and confectioners’ sugar for the frosting. Melt its butter in a clean saucepan over low to medium heat, then whisk in its cocoa and milk. Remove from heat and stir in the full confectioners’ sugar until smooth. These are the frosting quantities, separate from the batter butter and cocoa.
8. **Frost warm and cool:** Pour the warm frosting over the hot cake after removing it from the oven. For two cakes, divide the entire frosting between them. Let cool completely before slicing or wrapping. Refrigerate promptly according to the storage guidance, even if cooling is not yet complete.

## Cooking Notes

### Margarine option

The butter version is written above. For the original batch, two sticks of margarine in the batter and one stick in the frosting may replace the corresponding butter amounts. Scale both full fat amounts with the batch, and use the full listed confectioners’ sugar weight; boxes can differ in size.

### Family make-ahead note

The family note describes one saucepan and a portable egg beater for easy cleanup. With two square cakes, one can be frozen frosted and ready for later: let it cool before wrapping, then freeze. No freezer duration is supplied. Thaw the frosted cake in the refrigerator; bring only the portion being served out when needed.

RECIPE: Mongolian Beef with Ginger and Scallions (mongolian-beef.md)
CUISINES: Chinese-American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mongolian-beef/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 680 g flank steak, sliced across the grain into 1/4-inch-thick strips about 2 inches long
  - 3 tbsp (24 g) cornstarch, for the beef coating
  - 3 tbsp neutral oil, for three beef batches
  - 1 tsp neutral oil, for aromatics
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) reduced-sodium soy sauce
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) water, plus 1 tbsp for the slurry
  - 3 tbsp (40 g) packed light brown sugar
  - 1 tsp cornstarch, for the slurry
  - 1 tbsp finely minced fresh ginger
  - 3 cloves garlic, finely minced
  - 80 g scallions, cut into 2-inch lengths, white and green parts separated
  - 2 small dried red chilies, optional, left whole for mild heat or broken for more
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Chinese-American restaurant-style dish brings ginger, scallions and a sweet-savory glaze to thinly sliced beef. A light starch coating browns in the pan, then softens somewhat as it catches the sauce. Cooking the glaze separately lets you control its thickness without repeatedly boiling the beef.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the beef:** Pat the steak dry and slice across the grain into 1/4-inch-thick, roughly 2-inch-long strips. Toss with the 3 tbsp coating cornstarch, separating slices and shaking off loose excess. Divide into three roughly equal batches.
2. **Mix the sauce and slurry:** Stir soy sauce, 120 ml water and brown sugar together until the sugar mostly dissolves. In a separate cup, mix the 1 tsp slurry cornstarch with 1 tbsp cold water. Keep ginger, garlic, chilies and the two scallion portions beside the stove.
3. **Sear three batches:** Heat a heavy skillet over medium-high. Add 1 tbsp frying oil; it should shimmer without smoking heavily. Add one batch in a single layer and sear about 1–2 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through. Probe thicker strips from the edge to check at least 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean plate. Repeat twice with 1 tbsp oil for each batch, letting the pan regain heat. Reduce heat if the coating burns before the meat cooks.
4. **Cook aromatics:** Reduce heat to medium. Carefully discard excess oil and any blackened starch, leaving browned but unburned bits. Add the separate teaspoon oil, ginger and optional chilies; stir about 20 seconds. Add garlic and scallion whites and stir another 20–30 seconds without browning the garlic deeply.
5. **Thicken gently:** Pour in the mixed sauce and simmer about 1 minute. Stir the slurry again, add half, and simmer 20–30 seconds. Add the rest only if needed for a light spoon-coating consistency; discard unused slurry. Loosen with a tablespoon of water if it becomes sticky or pasty.
6. **Coat and check:** Return beef and its juices with the scallion greens. Toss over medium heat about 30–60 seconds, just until evenly coated and greens wilt. Verify sliced beef reaches at least 145°F / 63°C; give it at least 3 minutes before serving. Transfer off the hot pan for this wait. For the chicken variation, verify 165°F / 74°C in several thick strips instead.
7. **Serve:** Remove whole chilies or tell diners they are present. Divide among four portions with plain rice and vegetables prepared separately. Serve promptly; the coating will continue softening in the glaze.

RECIPE: Mongolian Chicken (mongolian-chicken.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/mongolian-chicken/
SOURCE: thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/mongolian-chicken/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken and frying ---
  - 12 oz boneless skinless chicken breast or thighs, raw, fully thawed if frozen; pat dry and slice ¼ inch / 6 mm thick
  - 1 tbsp vegetable oil for coating the chicken
  - 1/4 cup cornstarch for dredging, use this supply for any second dredge; discard the unused raw-contact starch
  - 1/3 cup (80 ml) vegetable oil for frying, retain part for aromatics after frying; drain the excess
  - 3 scallions, cut diagonally into 1–2-inch lengths (about 5 cm at the long end); keep white and green parts separate
  - --- Sauce and slurry ---
  - 1 tsp ginger, julienned or minced
  - 5 dried red chili peppers, optional
  - 2 garlic cloves, chopped
  - 2 1/2 tbsp soy sauce
  - 2 tbsp brown sugar
  - 1/4 cup hot water or low-sodium chicken stock
  - 2 tbsp cornstarch for the slurry, prepare the full slurry; use only as much as the sauce needs
  - 2 tbsp water for the slurry
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Chinese American takeout-style chicken uses a light cornstarch coat and a sweet soy glaze. Fry the thin pieces until cooked, then add slurry gradually so the sauce clings without becoming a heavy gel.

## Directions

1. **Separate the scallions:** Prepare scallions, keeping all white parts in one bowl and all green parts in another. Both portions will be used; their natural size varies.
2. **Prepare the slurry:** Mix cornstarch for the slurry and water for the slurry in a bowl and set beside the stove. Stir again immediately before using it; settled starch will otherwise thicken unevenly.
3. **Lightly coat the chicken:** Have boneless skinless chicken breast or thighs, vegetable oil for coating the chicken, and cornstarch for dredging ready. Mix the chicken with the coating oil, then dredge in the listed cornstarch, shaking off excess so each piece is lightly coated. If the coating becomes damp before frying, use the same measured dredging supply for a second light coating. Discard unused dredging starch after the chicken has gone into the pan; it has touched raw chicken.
4. **Fry in manageable loads:** Heat vegetable oil for frying in a wok over high heat until hot, without letting it smoke. Add the coated chicken in a single layer; fry in loads if necessary. Start checking the first side at about 1 minute and the second at about 30 seconds, turning as needed until the coating is browned and crisp and the thickest pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Use a thin-tip thermometer from the side. Transfer fully cooked chicken to a clean paper-towel-lined plate. Reuse the frying oil for subsequent loads; the times are first checks, not doneness guarantees.
5. **Use the retained frying oil:** Drain excess frying oil, retaining the corresponding scaled share for the aromatics: the original batch leaves 1 tablespoon from its measured ⅓ cup. This is retained frying oil, not another oil addition. Set the wok over medium-high heat, add ginger and stir about 20 seconds until fragrant.
6. **Add garlic, chilies and scallion whites:** Add dried red chili peppers (if using) and garlic cloves and all the reserved scallion whites. Stir-fry for about 15 seconds, keeping the garlic moving.
7. **Dissolve the sugar:** Add soy sauce, brown sugar, and hot water or low-sodium chicken stock, bring to a simmer and stir until the sugar dissolves. Simmer for about 2 minutes, watching that the small amount of liquid does not reduce to a scorched film.
8. **Thicken and coat:** Stir the prepared slurry again and add it slowly, letting each addition thicken before adding more. Stop when the sauce coats the back of a spoon; the full prepared slurry may not be needed. Add all the cooked chicken and reserved scallion greens, then toss for about 10 seconds until the sauce clings. If there is still excess thin sauce, add a little more of the remaining prepared slurry and stir until thickened. Check chicken for 165°F / 74°C before serving. Discard unused slurry and serve immediately.

RECIPE: Moroccan-Inspired Carrot Salad with Orange and Mint (moroccan-carrot-salad.md)
CUISINES: Moroccan-inspired, North African
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/moroccan-carrot-salad/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 680 g peeled carrots, coarsely grated
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) fresh orange juice
  - 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 1 tsp sugar, optional and only if needed
  - 1/4 tsp orange blossom water, optional, plus up to 1/4 tsp more to taste
  - 1/2 tsp ground cumin
  - 1/4 tsp sweet paprika
  - 1/8 tsp ground cinnamon
  - 1/8 tsp cayenne, optional
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, divided and partly added to taste
  - 1/4 cup fresh mint, thinly sliced just before serving
  - 2 tbsp chopped parsley
  - 20 g golden raisins, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Carrot, orange and orange-blossom water appear together in Moroccan salads. This version adds a light savory spice background and fresh herbs. Beside an apricot braise, start without sugar or raisins so the salad provides a cool citrus contrast rather than a second sweet course. It is a raw grated salad, not a cooked carrot chermoula preparation.

## Directions

1. **Grate carrots:** Use the coarse holes of a box grater or a food-processor shredding disc. Transfer to a bowl. If loose liquid has already collected, pour it away without squeezing the shreds dry.
2. **Mix and taste the dressing:** Whisk orange juice, lemon juice, olive oil, cumin, paprika, cinnamon, optional cayenne and half the salt. Add the optional quarter-teaspoon orange-blossom water and taste a small amount with a carrot shred. Add sugar or more blossom water only if the balance needs it.
3. **Dress and chill:** Toss dressing through carrots, adding the optional raisins if chosen. Cover and refrigerate for about 20 minutes to let the shreds soften lightly. There is no need for a long warm countertop rest.
4. **Finish freshly:** Slice mint and chop parsley just before serving, fold them through and taste. Add remaining salt only if needed. Toss up any dressing from the bottom and divide into six side portions. If excess water has accumulated, drain a little before the final seasoning check.

RECIPE: Moroccan-Inspired Chicken with Apricots, Chickpeas and Almonds (moroccan-chicken-tagine-apricot-chickpea.md)
CUISINES: Moroccan-inspired, North African
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/moroccan-chicken-tagine-apricot-chickpea/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken and aromatics ---
  - 6 bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, about 1.5 kg total, fully thawed
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - 1 tsp fine salt, divided and partly added to taste
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
  - 400 g yellow onion, thinly sliced
  - 5 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1 tbsp tomato paste
  - --- Spices and braise ---
  - 1 1/2 tsp ground cumin
  - 1 1/2 tsp ground ginger
  - 1 tsp sweet paprika
  - 1 tsp ground turmeric
  - 1 tsp ground coriander
  - 1/4 tsp cayenne, optional
  - 1 cinnamon stick, about 3 inches long
  - 1 small pinch saffron threads, about 0.05 g, optional, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water
  - 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) low-sodium chicken stock, plus up to 1/2 cup (120 ml) only if needed
  - 120 g dried apricots, halved
  - 1 can (15 oz / 425 g) chickpeas, rinsed and drained, about 255 g drained total
  - 20 g preserved-lemon rind, pulp removed, rinsed if very salty and finely chopped
  - 1 tsp honey, optional and only if needed after tasting
  - --- Finish ---
  - 40 g slivered almonds
  - 2 tbsp chopped cilantro
  - 2 tbsp chopped parsley
  - 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, added gradually only if needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Dutch-oven braise draws on Moroccan sweet-savory combinations, with chickpeas and a restrained preserved-lemon addition. Apricots provide most of the sweetness; optional honey is a final adjustment. The chicken skin softens during covered cooking, while toasted almonds provide the crisp finish. A specific city or historical lineage is not needed to explain how this version works.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and season:** Pat thighs dry. Season with half the salt and all the pepper. Measure ground spices together, slice onions, chop garlic and preserved rind, and halve apricots. If using saffron, steep it in the listed warm water while preparing the pan.
2. **Sear in two batches:** Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide Dutch oven over medium-high. Sear three thighs skin-side down about 6–8 minutes until golden, then turn for 2 minutes. Transfer to a plate. Add the second tablespoon oil if the pan needs it and repeat with the remaining thighs, lowering heat if drippings scorch. If enough chicken fat rendered, reserve unused oil rather than forcing it into the pan.
3. **Build the onion base:** Pour off excess fat, leaving about 1 tbsp. Cook onions over medium 10–12 minutes until soft and lightly golden, stirring. Add garlic for 30 seconds, ground spices for another 20–30 seconds and tomato paste for 1 minute. Add stock and scrape up the browned residue.
4. **Begin the covered braise:** Add apricots, cinnamon stick and optional saffron water. Return chicken skin-side up with any collected juices. The liquid should reach partway up the meat; add a little of the extra stock only if the base is too dry. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and reduce heat to maintain quiet bubbling.
5. **Finish meat and beans:** After about 30 minutes, add chickpeas and preserved-lemon rind around the chicken. Cover and continue another 10–25 minutes, checking the thickest thighs clear of bone reach 165°F / 74°C and the meat yields readily to a fork. Add a little stock if the pan is drying. Remove the cinnamon stick.
6. **Toast almonds:** During the braise, toast almonds in a dry skillet over medium-low about 3–5 minutes, stirring, until golden and fragrant. Transfer promptly to a cool plate rather than leaving them in the hot pan.
7. **Set sauce and seasoning:** If sauce is thin, lift chicken to a clean plate and simmer the sauce uncovered briefly until spoonable. Taste before adding the remaining salt, optional honey and fresh lemon juice in small amounts. Return chicken, fold half the herbs into the sauce and let stand off heat about 5 minutes.
8. **Serve:** Give each diner one thigh with sauce, chickpeas and apricots. Scatter almonds and remaining herbs at the table. A small portion of [Garlic Butter Pearl Couscous](/mise/recipes/garlic-butter-couscous) is one possible accompaniment; it has its own cooking method and portion size.

RECIPE: Challah (my-favorite-challah.md)
CUISINES: Israeli
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/my-favorite-challah/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/7199-my-favorite-challah
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 1/2 tbsp Active Dry Yeast
  - 8 to 8 1/2 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 5 large Eggs
  - 1/2 cup Vegetable Oil
  - 1/2 cup + 1 tbsp Granulated Sugar
  - 1 tbsp Kosher Salt
  - 1 egg (for wash)
  - Poppy or Sesame Seeds
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Challah is traditional Jewish bread for Shabbat and holidays. Using five eggs creates rich, brioche-like crumb. Braiding strands tightly creates internal tension that forces the bread to rise vertically, producing tall, majestic loaves with crispy golden crust. Let dough rise in a warm, draft-free spot to ensure yeast fully activates.

## Directions

1.  **Activate:** In a massive bowl, whisk yeast and 1 tbsp sugar into 1 3/4 cups lukewarm water. Let stand for 10 minutes until foamy.
2.  **The Emulsion:** Whisk in the oil, 4 eggs, and the remaining sugar and salt.
3.  **Incorporate:** Gradually add the flour, 1 cup at a time, until a shaggy dough forms.
4.  **Knead:** Transfer to a floured surface. Knead by hand for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic (or use a stand mixer with a dough hook).
5.  **First Rise:** Place in a greased bowl, cover with plastic, and let rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled.
6.  **Shape:** Punch down the dough. Divide into two halves. Divide each half into 6 balls. Roll each ball into a 12-inch strand.
7.  **The Braid:** Braid into two 6-strand loaves (see notes for braiding pattern). Place on a greased sheet.
8.  **Second Rise:** Brush with beaten egg. Let rise for another 45-60 minutes.
9.  **Bake:** Preheat oven to 375°F. Brush once more with egg and sprinkle with seeds. Bake for 35-40 minutes until deep mahogany brown.
10. **Cool:** Let cool completely on a rack before slicing.

RECIPE: Meera Sodha's Naan (naan.md)
CUISINES: Indian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/naan/
SOURCE: Meera Sodha, "Made in India" (adapted by Sam Sifton, NYT Cooking)
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1017747-meera-sodhas-naan
INGREDIENTS:
  - 500 g all-purpose flour
  - 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, reserved for kneading and rolling; use only as needed
  - 2 tbsp neutral oil, for the dough
  - 1 tsp neutral oil, for coating the dough
  - 4 tbsp plain whole-milk yogurt, unstrained
  - 2 1/4 tsp (7 g) active dry yeast
  - 2 tsp sugar
  - 1 1/4 tsp (7.5 g) fine salt
  - 1 level tsp double-acting baking powder
  - 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk, warmed to 110–115°F / 43–46°C
  - 2 tbsp (30 ml) whole milk, reserved only if the dough feels dry
  - --- Optional Garlic Butter ---
  - 3 tbsp unsalted butter
  - 2 cloves garlic, finely minced
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Meera Sodha learned this naan from her aunt Harsha. Milk, yogurt and a little oil give the breads a tender crumb. Keep the dough soft, let it rise fully, and adjust the pan after the first bread: brown bubbles should develop while the center cooks through. A towel keeps the early breads supple as the rest finish.

## Directions

1. **Hydrate the yeast:** Warm the measured cup of milk to 110–115°F / 43–46°C. Stir in the sugar and active dry yeast and leave for 5–10 minutes, until the granules have hydrated and activity appears at the surface. Do not use hot milk. Meanwhile, whisk the 500 g flour, fine salt and baking powder together in a large bowl.
2. **Mix and knead:** Add the yogurt, 2 tbsp oil and all the yeast-milk mixture to the flour. Mix until no loose pockets of flour remain, then knead on the work surface for about 5–8 minutes until smoother and elastic. Use the dusting flour sparingly. If the dough is stiff or cracks, knead in the correction milk a teaspoon at a time, only as needed for a soft, slightly tacky dough.
3. **Let rise:** Coat the dough with the separate teaspoon of oil and put it in a bowl with room to double. Cover and leave in a comfortably warm place for 60–90 minutes, until roughly doubled. Allow longer in a cool room; do not speed it up in a hot oven.
4. **Divide and relax:** Gently deflate and divide into 12 equal pieces, about 70 g each before any correction milk or dusting flour. Round into balls, cover and rest for 10 minutes. During this rest, melt the optional butter with the minced garlic in a small saucepan over low heat. Stir for about 1 minute after melting, until fragrant but not browned, then take off heat. Set out the towel-lined platter. During the final 5 minutes of the dough rest, begin heating the dry skillet over medium-high.
5. **Heat the pan and roll:** After the dry 12-inch cast-iron skillet has heated for about 5 minutes, roll two balls on a lightly dusted surface into ovals about 5 by 8 inches and roughly 1/8 inch / 3 mm thick. Keep the remaining balls covered. If a piece springs back, cover it for another 5–10 minutes and work on another. Do not stack uncooked ovals directly together.
6. **Cook one bread:** Brush loose flour off the oval and lay it flat in the hot pan. Cook about 30–45 seconds, until bubbles form and the underside has brown patches. Flip and cook about 30–45 seconds more. Flip again for about 10–20 seconds, pressing an undercooked edge lightly against the pan if needed. Check the first bread by tearing through a thick section near its center: there should be no sticky, raw dough inside. Adjust heat and time for the next round; a few dark freckles are enough, and blackening the whole surface is not the aim. Do not taste raw dough.
7. **Wrap and repeat:** Brush the hot bread with a little of the optional garlic butter, sharing the full amount across twelve, then enclose in the towel. Cook the second rolled bread. Between rounds, take the pan briefly off the burner while rolling the next pair; return it to the heat and let it recover before cooking. Wipe away scorched flour with a dry folded paper towel held in tongs. Allow about 30–40 minutes for rolling, pan adjustments and all twelve cooking rounds.
8. **Serve:** Bring the wrapped stack to the table promptly. Twelve breads make six portions of two, or twelve smaller one-bread accompaniments. If serving rice as well, start with one naan per person and offer the rest as wanted.

RECIPE: Nana Ruth’s Applesauce (nana-ruths-applesauce.md)
CUISINES: Jewish
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/nana-ruths-applesauce/
SOURCE: Adapted from Ruth Shankman
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6 lbs McIntosh Apples
  - 1/2 cup Granulated Sugar
  - 1/4 cup Honey
  - 1 Lemon, juiced (The Acid Balance)
  - 3 shakes Ground Cinnamon
  - 1 shake Ground Nutmeg
  - Filtered Water
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This traditional applesauce appears on Jewish holiday tables for Rosh Hashanah, Thanksgiving, and Hanukkah. McIntosh apples have thin skin and high water content, allowing them to break down into naturally velvety texture without needing a blender. Simmering apples in their own juices with just a splash of water produces concentrated apple intensity that commercial brands can't match. Lemon provides acidity.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Core and peel the apples. Cut into large chunks.
2.  **The Rinse:** Place apple chunks in a heavy nonstick pot. Fill with water, rinse, and repeat, leaving about 1/4 inch of water at the bottom of the pot.
3.  **Season:** Squeeze the lemon over the apples. Add the honey, sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
4.  **Boil:** Bring to a boil over high heat. Immediately cover and reduce heat to **very low**.
5.  **Simmer:** Cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally. The apples should be very soft and falling apart.
6.  **The Crush:** Use a potato masher or the side of a heavy spoon to crush the apples against the side of the pot into a chunky, uniform sauce.
7.  **Serve:** Best served warm with a dusting of extra cinnamon.

RECIPE: Nana’s Biscuits (nanas-biscuits.md)
CUISINES: Southern
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/nanas-biscuits/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups Self-Rising Flour (sifted)
  - 1/4 cup Unsalted Butter, cold and cubed
  - 3/4 cup Buttermilk
  - Pinch of Baking Soda
  - --- For handling ---
  - Butter, for greasing the baking sheet
  - Self-rising flour, for dusting as needed
  - Buttermilk, extra only as needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Nana’s biscuits are mixed by hand, rolled into small balls and flattened with the palm. Keep the butter version’s fat cold and handle the dough gently. The self-rising flour supplies the main leavening; retain the listed pinch of baking soda without adding a second measured baking-powder dose.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 425°F. Lightly grease a metal baking sheet with butter. If you plan to broil the tops, use a broiler-rated pan without parchment and follow your oven’s rack-clearance instructions.

2. **Cut the fat:** Put the sifted self-rising flour in a large bowl. Rub in all the cold cubed butter with your fingertips until coarse crumbs and some pea-sized butter pieces remain.

3. **Mix gently:** Add the listed buttermilk and pinch of baking soda. Mix gently by hand just until the dough comes together. If dry flour remains, add extra buttermilk a little at a time; if too sticky to handle, use a light dusting of self-rising flour.

4. **Shape:** Roll into similarly sized small balls and flatten slightly with your palm on the greased sheet. The original-size butter batch plans about 12; follow the listed scaled count without enlarging the biscuits or crowding the sheet.

5. **Bake and serve:** Bake for about 10–12 minutes until the centers have set. If baked through but still pale on top, broil briefly, watching continuously and removing the pan as soon as the color develops, about 1 minute. Broiling colors the top; it does not replace baking the middle. Let the biscuits stand briefly before serving.

## Shortening Variation

For the original batch, replace the ¼ cup dough butter with about ¼ cup solid vegetable shortening; scale that replacement with the listed dough butter amount. Keep the full self-rising flour, buttermilk and pinch of baking soda. Work the shortening into the sifted flour by hand, adding the listed buttermilk and soda a little at a time until the dough comes together. Use extra flour only as needed, then roll and flatten as in step 4 and bake at 425°F, with the same optional brief broil for color after the centers are baked. This is a separate fat and mixing route; keep the butter version’s cold-cutting method for the main recipe.

RECIPE: New York Crunch Roll (new-york-crunch-roll.md)
CUISINES: Japanese, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/new-york-crunch-roll/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 230 g trimmed boneless, skinless yellowfin tuna, weighed after removing tough connective tissue; see raw-service sourcing note
  - 150 g ripe avocado flesh, from about 1 medium avocado
  - 100 g English cucumber, weighed after removing the watery seed core
  - 1/3 cup ready-to-eat tempura flakes (tenkasu or agedama), not uncooked batter mix
  - 320 g (about 2 cups) prepared [Sushi Rice (Shari)](/mise/recipes/master-sushi-rice)
  - 4 full sheets unseasoned roasted nori, about 19 x 20 cm each; trim as directed
  - 120 ml water, for dampening hands and the knife
  - 1 tsp unseasoned rice vinegar, for the hand-dipping water
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Tuna, avocado, cucumber and tempura flakes fill this nori-wrapped roll. Prepared tenkasu adds a delicate crunch that softens against the filling, so roll and eat promptly.

## Before buying raw tuna

Tell the supplier the tuna is for raw service and confirm species, handling and applicable parasite controls; “sushi-grade” alone is insufficient. Yellowfin has a specific FDA parasite-freezing exemption, not a guarantee against other hazards. Neither domestic freezing nor the vinegar used for dampening fingers makes raw tuna safe. Thaw frozen fish in the refrigerator as directed, removing vacuum packaging before refrigerator thawing.

FDA advises children, pregnant people, older adults and people with weakened immune systems to avoid raw seafood. Choose a fully cooked preparation for those diners. Check tenkasu ingredients for wheat, egg, fish or shellfish; the roll itself contains tuna, and packaged ingredients vary by brand.

## Directions

1. **Prepare rice and equipment:** Make [Sushi Rice (Shari)](/mise/recipes/master-sushi-rice), weigh out 320 g and refrigerate surplus rice promptly. Let the rolling portion become barely warm during final preparation. Wrap a clean mat in food-safe film. Mix water and vinegar for lightly dampening fingers and the knife; it is not a sanitizer. Do not dip a raw-filling-coated hand or blade into this clean water. Wash hands and clean the blade before returning to it, use a separate damp cloth for wiping the cutting blade, and replace the water if contaminated.
2. **Prepare vegetables:** Wash the cucumber, remove the watery core and weigh 100 g; cut into slender matchsticks and pat dry. Near rolling time, halve the avocado, lift its pit out with a spoon, scoop out the flesh and weigh 150 g. Slice about 5–6 mm thick. Divide cucumber into four 25 g portions and avocado into four equal portions, about 38 g each. Refrigerate briefly until needed. Keep tempura flakes sealed and dry.
3. **Cut tuna and portion rice:** With separate clean equipment, remove tough visible connective tissue, weigh the listed usable amount of cold tuna and cut across its muscle grain where visible into strips about 6–10 mm thick. Short strips can be laid end to end. Divide into four equal portions of about 58 g and refrigerate. Clean the work area and hands. Divide rice into four 80 g portions using a clean utensil.
4. **Lay out the first roll:** Trim the first full nori sheet to about 19 x 15 cm and save its dry offcut airtight for another use. Leave the other sheets untrimmed until the first closure check. Place one rectangle shiny side down with its 19 cm edge nearest you. Lightly dampen fingers and shake off extra water, then spread one rice portion evenly, leaving a 1 cm bare strip along the far edge. Take out one portion each of tuna, avocado and cucumber and arrange in a compact horizontal line about 4 cm from the near edge.
5. **Add crunch and roll:** Sprinkle one quarter of the tempura flakes, about 1 tbsp plus 1 tsp, along the filling immediately before rolling. Lift the mat's near edge and tuck nori and rice over the filling. Lift the mat clear as you continue forward so it stays outside the roll. Seal on the bare nori edge, barely moistening it if necessary, then press gently through the mat without crushing the avocado. Check the first roll's closure, then cut and serve it following the next step. Trim the remaining sheets to match and continue one roll at a time, cutting and serving each as it is completed for the clearest crunch. Do not build a rice ridge.
6. **Cut and serve:** Set seam-side down briefly while preparing a sharp knife. Wipe and lightly dampen the blade, cut each roll in half, then halve each section twice for eight pieces per roll. Wipe and dampen between cuts as needed. Serve promptly as 32 pieces, about two main portions or four appetizer portions. Keep unused fish portions cold while working.

RECIPE: No-Cook Playdough (no-cook-playdough.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/no-cook-playdough/
SOURCE: Adapted from tinkerlab.com
SOURCE_URL: https://tinkerlab.com/no-cook-play-dough/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2.5 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 1 1/4 cups Fine Salt
  - 1 1/2 tbsp Cream of Tartar
  - 2.5 cups Boiling Water
  - 5 tbsp Vegetable Oil
  - Liquid Watercolors or Wilton Icing Colors
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

While not edible, this no-cook playdough stays soft and pliable for months. Cream of tartar acts as preservative and stiffener, preventing stickiness. Boiling water instantly gelatinizes flour starch, eliminating the need for stovetop cooking.

## Directions

1.  **Dry Mix:** In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, salt, and cream of tartar until perfectly combined.
2.  **The Emulsion:** In a separate heatproof jug, mix the boiling water and vegetable oil. If using one color for the whole batch, add the coloring to the liquid now.
3.  **Combine:** Slowly pour the liquid into the dry ingredients. Stir with a large spoon until a shaggy dough forms.
4.  **Knead:** Once cool enough to handle, dump the dough onto a clean surface. Knead vigorously for 2-3 minutes until it becomes completely smooth, elastic, and non-sticky.
5.  **Finish:** If you want multiple colors, divide the white dough and knead the colors into each portion separately.
6.  **Store:** Keep in an airtight container or a zip-top bag to maintain the "Bounce."

RECIPE: Noodle Pudding (noodle-pudding.md)
CUISINES: Jewish
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/noodle-pudding/
SOURCE: Adapted from Mary Later
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Pan and noodle cooking ---
  - unsalted butter, as needed for greasing dishes
  - 16 oz medium-width egg noodles, dry
  - water, enough to boil the noodles
  - salt, as desired for the noodle water
  - --- Custard and topping ---
  - 16 oz sour cream
  - 16 oz large-curd cottage cheese
  - 8 oz block-style cream cheese, softened
  - 8 oz unsalted butter, melted and cooled until lukewarm
  - 8 large eggs, beaten
  - 3/4 cup granulated sugar
  - 1 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
  - 2 cups corn flakes, coarsely crushed; measure after crushing
  - 1/2 cup light brown sugar, packed
  - 1/4 cup golden raisins, for half the pudding only, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Adapted from Mary Later’s recipe. Coarsely crushed corn flakes hold more texture than powder on the rich noodle custard. Warm noodles and lukewarm melted butter mix into the eggs without setting them early; check the center before the fifteen-minute rest.

## Directions

1. **Prepare dishes:** Heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the center. For the original batch, use unsalted butter to grease a room-temperature 9×13-inch glass dish, preferably the existing deep 4-quart plan, and have a smaller greased oven-safe overflow dish ready. Follow the actual dish’s temperature and thermal-shock instructions.
2. **Cook noodles:** Set out medium-width egg noodles, water, and salt. Bring the salted water to a boil, then add the full dry noodle amount and cook just to al dente, following its package as a guide. Drain well and let the noodles cool until warm, not steaming hot, before adding to the custard.
3. **Mix custard:** Set out sour cream, large-curd cottage cheese, block-style cream cheese, 3/4 of the unsalted butter, large eggs, granulated sugar, and ground cinnamon. Beat the softened cream cheese with a little sour cream until smooth, then mix in the remaining sour cream and all the cottage cheese, eggs, granulated sugar, cinnamon and allocated butter, keeping the cottage-cheese curds if desired. The butter allocation here is three-quarters of the full butter amount; reserve the other quarter for the topping. Use lukewarm butter and warm noodles so they do not cook the eggs on contact.
4. **Combine and divide:** Fold all the warm noodles into all the custard. Set out golden raisins (if using). For a half-raisin pudding, divide the noodle mixture in half and add all the optional raisins to only one half. Spoon the two mixtures into opposite sides of the greased dish; omit raisins for an entirely plain pudding. Leave at least 1/2 inch below the rim for topping and slight puffing. Put excess mixture in the overflow dish rather than filling to the brim.
5. **Coat topping:** Toss 1/4 of the unsalted butter, corn flakes, and light brown sugar until all the coarse corn flakes are coated with the remaining one-quarter butter and packed brown sugar. Scatter across the full noodle mixture without pressing down. With an overflow dish, divide topping in proportion to surface area.
6. **Bake and check the center:** Bake at 325°F, beginning checks around 60 minutes for the original deep dish; 65–80 minutes is the existing planning range. The edges should be set, the center should have only a slight wobble with no liquid custard, and its center must reach 165°F /74°C. Check every dish; smaller overflow portions may finish earlier. Loosely tent if the topping colors before the center is ready.
7. **Rest and serve:** Set hot glass on a dry trivet following the vessel’s instructions. Rest 15 minutes before dividing into the listed portions. Keep the raisin and plain halves distinct when serving.

RECIPE: Oatmeal Risotto (oatmeal-risotto.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/oatmeal-risotto/
SOURCE: Adapted from Richard Blaise
SOURCE_URL: https://smile.amazon.com/Try-This-Home-Recipes-Plate-ebook/dp/B009JU6UPQ
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup Steel-cut Oats
  - 3 cups Chicken Broth or Filtered Water
  - 1 Overripe Banana, mashed
  - 1/4 cup Golden Raisins
  - 2 tbsp Sherry Vinegar (The Finishing Touch)
  - 1 tbsp Light Brown Sugar
  - Parmesan Cheese, for shaving
  - Pinch of Kosher Salt
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Oatmeal risotto treats steel-cut oats with the same respect Italians give Arborio rice - an overnight soak followed by a slow simmer until each grain is creamy outside and slightly chewy at the center. The mashed banana folded in at the end acts like the butter-and-cheese mantecatura in real risotto, creating body without dairy. The sherry-vinegar raisins and Parmesan shavings provide the finishing acid and umami.

## Directions

1.  **The Hydration:** In a medium bowl, combine the oats and water/broth. Cover and refrigerate overnight at 40°F or below. Keep the oats and all soaking liquid cold until ready to cook.
2.  **The Acid Balance:** In a small bowl, pour the sherry vinegar over the golden raisins. Let soak while the oats cook.
3.  **Simmer:** Pour the oats and their soaking liquid into a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Add brown sugar and salt.
4.  **Cook:** Cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the oats are "squeaky" to the bite (al dente).
5.  **The Emulsion:** Fold in the mashed banana. Cook for 2 more minutes until the banana has melted into the oats, creating a creamy "Bounce."
6.  **Serve:** Divide into bowls. Top with the vinegar-soaked raisins and a few generous shavings of Parmesan cheese for the final savory **High Note**.

RECIPE: Soft Pumpkin Cookies (old-fashioned-soft-pumpkin-cookies.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/old-fashioned-soft-pumpkin-cookies/
SOURCE: Adapted from Verybestbaking.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.verybestbaking.com/recipes/32364/Old-Fashioned-Soft-Pumpkin-Cookies
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Pumpkin cookie dough ---
  - 1 cup pure pumpkin puree
  - 1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, softened
  - 1 1/2 cups granulated sugar
  - 1 large egg
  - 1 tsp pure vanilla extract
  - 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  - 1 tsp baking soda
  - 1 tsp baking powder
  - 1 tsp ground cinnamon
  - 1/2 tsp ground nutmeg
  - 1/2 tsp sea salt
  - --- Vanilla glaze ---
  - 2 cups confectioners’ sugar, sifted
  - 3 tbsp milk
  - 1 tbsp unsalted butter, melted
  - 1 tsp pure vanilla extract
  - --- Pan preparation ---
  - butter or baking spray, enough to lightly grease baking sheets
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Use pure pumpkin puree rather than sweetened pumpkin pie filling. The pumpkin dough and the vanilla glaze each have their own vanilla amount. Cool the cookies completely before drizzling so the glaze stays on the surface rather than running off warm cookies.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 350°F. Use butter or baking spray to lightly grease baking sheets, and have a cooling rack ready.
2. **Mix dry ingredients:** Whisk all-purpose flour, baking soda, baking powder, ground cinnamon, ground nutmeg, and sea salt in a medium bowl so the spices, salt and leaveners are distributed.
3. **Cream:** Beat unsalted butter and granulated sugar in a large bowl until fluffy, scraping the bowl.
4. **Add pumpkin:** Beat in pure pumpkin puree, large egg, and pure vanilla extract until evenly mixed.
5. **Combine:** Gradually stir the dry mixture into the pumpkin mixture just until no dry flour remains. The dough is soft and scoopable.
6. **Shape:** Drop rounded tablespoonfuls onto the greased sheets, leaving room between cookies. Use all the dough; the listed count is a planning value. Keep scoop size consistent and use extra sheets or loads as the batch grows.
7. **Bake:** Wait for the oven to reach 350°F, then bake for 15–18 minutes per load until the edges are firm and the tops are slightly golden. Keep unbaked dough refrigerated at 40°F / 4°C or below between loads.
8. **Cool before glazing:** Cool on the sheets for 2 minutes, then transfer to a rack and cool completely before adding the glaze.
9. **Glaze:** Whisk confectioners’ sugar, milk, unsalted butter, and pure vanilla extract until smooth. Drizzle the full glaze over the cooled cookies, distributing it over the actual batch. Let the glaze settle before packing; these are soft glazed cookies.

## Cooking Options

### Glaze butter option

The melted-butter glaze is written above. The current LIBBY’S publisher version instead uses the same listed amount of softened butter in the glaze. Choose one butter state for that glaze, whisking it smooth; keep all the milk, confectioners’ sugar and vanilla amounts. The dough’s softened butter is a separate allocation.

RECIPE: Old-Fashioned Strawberry Ice Cream (old-fashioned-strawberry-ice-cream.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/old-fashioned-strawberry-ice-cream/
SOURCE: Adapted from selfproclaimedfoodie.com
SOURCE_URL: https://selfproclaimedfoodie.com/old-fashioned-strawberry-ice-cream/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 cups Fresh Strawberries, sliced
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice (The Acid Balance)
  - 3/4 cup Granulated Sugar (divided)
  - 1/4 cup Light Brown Sugar
  - 4 large Egg Yolks
  - 1 1/2 cups Heavy Cream
  - 1 1/2 cups Whole Milk
  - 1 Vanilla Bean, seeds scraped
  - 1/4 tsp Kosher Salt
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Sliced strawberries macerated in lemon juice and sugar for several hours draw out natural syrup and soften the fruit, preventing them from freezing into icy chunks. Tempering yolks with hot milk and vanilla bean ensures dense, custardy texture that showcases bright strawberries perfectly.

## Directions

1.  **Macerate:** Toss strawberries with lemon juice and 1/4 cup sugar. **Refrigerate for at least 3 hours** until syrupy.
2.  **Custard Base:** In a saucepan, heat milk, cream, and vanilla bean seeds until simmering.
3.  **Emulsify:** In a large bowl, whisk yolks, salt, and remaining sugars until pale. Slowly whisk in the hot cream to temper.
4.  **Thicken:** Return mixture to the pan. Cook over medium-low, stirring constantly, until the custard coats a spoon. **Do not boil.**
5.  **Chill:** Remove vanilla pod. Let cool for 30 minutes, then refrigerate for **at least 4 hours** until ice-cold.
6.  **Churn:** Stir the macerated strawberries (including all juice) into the custard. Pour into ice cream maker and process for 25-35 minutes.
7.  **Set:** Freeze for 2 hours to harden into the Kitchen Standard texture.

RECIPE: Old-Fashioned Vanilla Ice Cream (old-fashioned-vanilla-ice-cream.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/old-fashioned-vanilla-ice-cream/
SOURCE: Adapted from Addapinch.com
SOURCE_URL: https://addapinch.com/old-fashioned-vanilla-ice-cream-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 large Egg Yolks
  - 1/2 cup Granulated Sugar
  - 1 cup Whole Milk
  - 1 cup Heavy Cream
  - 2 tsp Pure Vanilla Bean Paste
  - Pinch of Sea Salt
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Gradually whisk hot milk into yolks and sugar, then stir the custard over gentle heat to 165°F. Stop before it boils. Chill the base fully before adding cold cream and vanilla; churning produces soft serve, and the freezer firms it further.

## Directions

1.  **The Base:** In a small saucepan, heat milk and the pinch of salt over medium-low until just simmering.
2.  **Emulsify:** In a medium bowl, whisk egg yolks and sugar until pale yellow. Slowly stream in the hot milk while whisking constantly.
3.  **Thicken:** Return the mixture to the pan. Stir constantly over gentle heat until it reaches 165°F and coats the back of a spoon. Remove from the heat immediately. **Do not boil.**
4.  **The Chill:** Transfer to a shallow container and refrigerate promptly for **at least 4 hours**, until thoroughly cold, at 40°F / 4°C or below. Prepare the ice cream maker, including freezing its bowl if required, according to its instructions.
5.  **Churn:** Stir in the chilled heavy cream and vanilla bean paste. Pour into your prepared ice cream maker, respecting its liquid-fill limit. Churn in batches if needed and keep waiting base refrigerated.
6.  **Set:** Churn according to instructions (usually 20 mins). Transfer to a freezer-safe container and freeze for 2 hours before serving.

RECIPE: Old Fashioned (old-fashioned.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/old-fashioned/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 oz bourbon or rye whiskey
  - 1 sugar cube (or 1/4 oz simple syrup)
  - 2-3 dashes aromatic bitters
  - Orange peel
  - Maraschino cherry (optional)
  - Large ice cube
CONTENT:

## Directions

1. **Place the sugar cube:** in an Old Fashioned glass and saturate with bitters. Add a splash of water.

2. **Muddle the sugar until:** dissolved (or simply add simple syrup instead).

3. **Add the whiskey and:** fill the glass with one large ice cube.

4. **Stir gently for 10-15:** seconds.

5. **Express an orange peel:** over the drink by holding it over the glass and giving it a good twist to release the oils. Rub the peel around the rim of the glass and drop it in.

6. **Optionally add a maraschino:** cherry. Serve immediately.

## Chef's Note

The Old Fashioned dates to the 1880s, when bartenders started getting fancy with cocktails, adding fruit and elaborate garnishes. Patrons who wanted their drinks made the 'old fashioned way' - just whiskey, sugar, water, and bitters - gave the drink its name. It represents the original cocktail formula before mixology got complicated, and experienced a massive revival in the 21st century craft cocktail movement. Use a large single ice cube instead of small cubes to minimize dilution while keeping the drink properly chilled.

RECIPE: Orange-Rosemary Chicken with Beets and Fennel (one-pan-citrus-beets-roasted-chicken.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/one-pan-citrus-beets-roasted-chicken/
SOURCE: Adapted from recipestonourish.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.recipestonourish.com/one-pan-citrus-beets-roasted-chicken/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, about 1 kg total, fully thawed
  - 600 g peeled beets, cut into 1/4-inch-thick half-moons
  - 300 g peeled carrots, cut into pieces no thicker than 1/2 inch
  - 300 g trimmed fennel bulb, cut into 1/2-inch wedges with a little core holding each together
  - 3 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - 1 tsp fine salt, divided
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper, divided
  - 1/2 tsp mild chili powder blend
  - 1 tbsp (14 g) unsalted butter, melted
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) fresh orange juice
  - 1 tsp finely grated orange zest
  - 2 tsp finely chopped fresh rosemary leaves
  - 4 cloves garlic, minced
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The dish gets its contrast from browned chicken skin, earthy roots and a fresh orange finish. Dense beets and carrots start first, while fennel joins the chicken on a separate tray. The orange mixture goes on the vegetables near the end, preserving more aroma and keeping juice off the skin.

## Directions

1. **Heat and prepare:** Heat oven to 425°F / 220°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Cut vegetables evenly and pat chicken skin dry. Mix orange juice, zest, melted butter, rosemary and all the garlic in a small bowl; keep aside for the final stage.
2. **Start roots first:** Toss beets and carrots with 2 tbsp oil, half the salt and half the pepper on one rimmed sheet. Spread into one layer and roast for 15 minutes. If your sheet cannot hold that layer, use a larger pan or accept an additional cooking batch rather than piling the roots.
3. **Add the chicken tray:** On the second sheet, toss fennel with the remaining tablespoon oil and arrange it around the thighs, keeping the skin exposed. Divide remaining salt and pepper over chicken and fennel; sprinkle chili powder over the chicken. Put this tray in the oven, leaving the root tray cooking too.
4. **Roast to separate endpoints:** Roast another 40–50 minutes, swapping the trays' rack positions halfway through and turning vegetables. Begin checking thighs around 35 minutes after they enter: the thickest meat, clear of bone, must reach 165°F / 74°C, and the joint should move easily. Check roots with a fork. Remove any component that finishes early instead of letting it overcook.
5. **Finish the vegetables:** During the final 8–10 minutes of vegetable cooking, spoon the orange-garlic mixture over the roots and fennel, keeping it off chicken skin. Stir the vegetables and return them to the oven so the garlic cooks and the juice reduces a little. If chicken finishes first, transfer it to a clean plate and continue finishing vegetables separately.
6. **Rest briefly and serve:** Let cooked thighs rest about 5 minutes. Divide vegetables among four plates and serve one thigh with each. Spoon a little vegetable-pan liquid around the meat rather than over the skin. Add no extra orange until you taste the finish.

RECIPE: One-Pan Lemon Herb Chicken Thighs (one-pan-lemon-herb-chicken-thighs.md)
CUISINES: Mediterranean, Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/one-pan-lemon-herb-chicken-thighs/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken and lemon-herb pan ---
  - 8 bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, raw, fresh or fully thawed; original eight-thigh batch is about 2.5–3 lb total
  - 3 tbsp olive oil
  - 4 garlic cloves, peeled and sliced
  - 2 tbsp fresh oregano, washed
  - 2 tbsp fresh thyme, washed
  - 2 lemons, washed, zested and juiced; reserve all juice and zest from these same lemons
  - 1/2 cup chicken stock or water
  - 1 tsp kosher salt
  - 1/2 tsp black pepper
  - 1 lb potatoes or root vegetables, washed, peeled if wanted and cut into 1-inch pieces, optional
  - fresh parsley, as wanted for garnish, washed and chopped
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Lemon, oregano and thyme give this skillet chicken its Mediterranean-style flavor. Brown the skin first, keep it above the sauce while roasting where possible, and judge thigh temperature and optional vegetable tenderness separately.

## Directions

1. **Preheat and season:** Preheat the oven to 425°F. Use an oven-safe skillet with room for all the measured thighs in one layer and, if using them, the vegetables; use additional oven-safe vessels if necessary. Pat all the measured thighs dry and season both sides with all kosher salt and black pepper. Divide every measured ingredient proportionally among any extra vessels; do not add extra oil or stock.
2. **Sear the chicken:** Heat the assigned two-thirds of olive oil over medium-high heat and use bone-in skin-on chicken thighs and 2/3 of the olive oil for searing. Put chicken skin-side down without crowding; work in loads if needed, using this same measured oil supply across the loads. Cook about 5–6 minutes until deeply golden and releasing from the pan, then turn and cook about 2 minutes. Transfer to a plate; keep all rendered fat in the cooking pan.
3. **Cook aromatics:** Use 1/3 of the olive oil, garlic cloves, fresh oregano, and fresh thyme for this stage. Reduce heat to medium, add the remaining one-third of the measured oil and all the garlic, and sauté for 30–45 seconds until fragrant. Then stir in all the oregano and thyme for about 15 seconds; do not let the garlic blacken.
4. **Add lemon and stock:** Use lemons and chicken stock or water to deglaze: pour in all the juice from the measured lemons and the stock or water, scrape the browned bits, then stir in all the reserved zest. Keep the whole sauce and rendered fat.
5. **Return chicken and optional vegetables:** Return all the partly cooked chicken and its plate juices to the pan, skin-side up, keeping skin above the liquid where possible. Nestle potatoes or root vegetables (if using) around the thighs. Transfer the oven-safe vessel or vessels to the preheated oven; do not crowd or stack the thighs.
6. **Finish to temperature and tenderness:** Start checking after 12–15 minutes without vegetables, or 15–18 minutes with them. These are first checks, not guaranteed finishing times. Every thigh must reach 165°F / 74°C in its thickest part away from the bone. Vegetables must be fork-tender; if chicken finishes first, remove it with clean utensils to a clean platter and continue cooking the vegetables and full sauce. Check raw-contact sauce and vegetables reach 165°F / 74°C before tasting or serving them, stirring liquid for a representative reading. Larger loads or different roots can need longer.
7. **Rest and garnish:** Rest cooked chicken for 5 minutes. Once chicken and the raw-contact sauce/vegetables have reached their endpoints, taste the sauce and scatter fresh parsley over the finished dish. Serve all the sauce and rendered fat with the chicken.
