RECIPE: One-Pot Chicken Meatballs with Greens (one-pot-chicken-meatballs-with-greens.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/one-pot-chicken-meatballs-with-greens/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1025342-one-pot-chicken-meatballs-with-greens?smid=ck-recipe-iOS-share
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Meatballs ---
  - 1 lb ground chicken, raw; fresh or fully thawed
  - 1/3 cup plain Greek yogurt, thick
  - 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs
  - 2 garlic cloves, peeled and minced
  - 2 scallions, washed and thinly sliced
  - 2 tsp dried oregano
  - 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes
  - 1 tsp salt
  - olive oil, as needed to coat palms
  - additional olive oil, as needed if the pan dries during browning
  - --- Greens and lemon ---
  - 1 lb Swiss chard, washed; tender stalks sliced and leaves cut into 1-inch ribbons
  - 1 lemon, washed; half thinly sliced and half reserved for finishing juice
  - 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
  - 1 tsp ground cumin
  - salt, to taste for the greens
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Yogurt and panko bind these Italian-American-style garlic-and-oregano chicken meatballs. Brown them gently, then cover them with chard and lemon slices to finish cooking in the greens’ moisture. Spoon the cooking juices over the meatballs and greens, and keep the lemon half for the finish.

## Directions

1. **Mix gently:** Combine all ground chicken, plain Greek yogurt, panko breadcrumbs, garlic cloves, scallions, dried oregano, red pepper flakes, and salt in a bowl, mixing just until evenly combined. The oregano and red pepper belong to this mixture; reserve cumin for the greens. Keep the raw chicken mixture cold if preparation pauses and do not taste it raw.
2. **Shape meatballs:** Use olive oil to lightly coat your palms, refreshing the coating as needed, and form all the mixture into uniform balls about 2 inches across. The original batch plans about 14 meatballs; at other batch sizes keep the size similar and use the entire mixture rather than holding the count fixed.
3. **Brown meatballs:** Use a heavy pot with a tight lid and a broad base; the original route uses a 12-inch Dutch oven. Heat over medium, then use additional olive oil and 1/2 of the extra-virgin olive oil, starting with half of the measured oil supply and adding the separate unmeasured browning allowance only if needed. Add the meatballs without crowding and turn gently when they release, about 7 minutes for initial browning. This is not their final temperature check. Use additional cooking vessels when the complete batch and greens cannot fit; divide the whole measured formula proportionally.
4. **Dress greens:** Meanwhile, in a clean bowl toss all Swiss chard, 1/2 of the lemon, 1/2 of the extra-virgin olive oil, ground cumin, and salt, using the remaining half of the measured oil and half the measured lemons as thin slices. Scrunch the leaves to coat; reserve the other lemon half for serving.
5. **Cover with greens:** Pile all the dressed greens and lemon slices directly over all the browned meatballs. Cover tightly and cook over medium for about 12–15 minutes as an initial estimate. The covered greens release moisture to finish cooking the meatballs.
6. **Check centers:** Continue covered cooking until meatball centers reach 165°F / 74°C and the greens and tender stalks have softened. Check large meatballs and different pot positions with a thermometer; browning alone does not establish the endpoint. Extra loads or a deeper mound of greens can take longer.
7. **Scoop and finish:** Scoop the meatballs and greens onto plates, spooning all the cooking juices over them. Use all 1/2 of the lemon for the finish: squeeze the reserved lemon juice over the portions. Use clean serving utensils.

RECIPE: One-Pot Chicken, Quinoa & Mushrooms (one-pot-chicken-quinoa-mushrooms-and-spinach.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/one-pot-chicken-quinoa-mushrooms-and-spinach/
SOURCE: Adapted from Cookincanuck.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.cookincanuck.com/one-pot-chicken-quinoa-mushrooms-spinach-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6 boneless skinless chicken thighs, about 150 g each
  - 255 g dry white quinoa, rinsed and well drained
  - 300 g cremini mushrooms, sliced
  - 150 g yellow onion, finely chopped
  - 2 1/2 cups (600 ml) low-sodium chicken broth, plus a little hot water if needed
  - 150 g fresh spinach, washed and roughly chopped
  - 3/4 tsp dried rosemary, finely crushed
  - 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
  - 1 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, divided
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
  - 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, added to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Mushrooms need a chance to lose water and brown before the grains and broth arrive. Quinoa then cooks in the broth and chicken juices. This is a complete grain-and-protein dish; lemon and spinach finish it with freshness. Quinoa is a seed used like a grain, and its small cooked germ ring is a useful visual cue alongside tasting for tenderness.

## Directions

1. **Sear in batches:** Pat chicken dry and season with half the salt, pepper, rosemary, and paprika. Heat two teaspoons oil in a wide deep sauté pan over medium-high heat. Sear three thighs at a time for about 2–3 minutes per side, lowering heat if spices darken too quickly. Transfer to a plate; the centers are not yet cooked.
2. **Brown mushrooms:** Add remaining oil, mushrooms, onion, and remaining salt. Cook about 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until mushroom liquid has mostly evaporated and golden patches appear. Scrape up browned material without burning it.
3. **Add grains and broth:** Stir in drained quinoa and broth. Bring to a gentle simmer, then nestle chicken and its juices into the quinoa in one layer. Cover tightly and reduce to a gentle simmer.
4. **Check both components:** Cook about 18–22 minutes. Probe each thigh for 165°F / 74°C and check quinoa in several places for the same temperature before tasting it. The seeds should be tender with a little bite and most free liquid absorbed. Extend gently if needed, using the component-specific fixes in troubleshooting rather than overcooking everything together.
5. **Wilt and rest:** When chicken and quinoa meet their checks, scatter spinach over the pan. Cover and heat gently for about 2 minutes until wilted. Remove from heat and rest covered for 5 minutes.
6. **Finish with lemon:** Lift chicken briefly to a clean plate, fold spinach through quinoa, and stir in half the lemon juice. Taste and add the remainder as needed. Divide quinoa and vegetables into six portions and add one thigh to each.

RECIPE: Spicy Thai Noodles (one-pot-spicy-thai-noodles.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/one-pot-spicy-thai-noodles/
SOURCE: Adapted from Domesticsuperhero.com
SOURCE_URL: https://domesticsuperhero.com/one-pot-spicy-thai-noodles/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Penne or Linguine
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - Red pepper flakes, a pinch, optional
  - 1/3 cup Low-sodium Soy Sauce
  - 2 tbsp Dark Brown Sugar
  - 1.5 tbsp Sriracha (adjust for heat)
  - 2 inches Fresh Ginger, grated
  - 2 large Eggs, beaten
  - 1 Zucchini, cut into half-moons
  - 8 oz Mushrooms, chopped
  - 1/2 cup Carrots, shredded
  - 4 Green Onions, chopped
  - 1/2 cup Fresh Cilantro, chopped
  - 1/2 cup Peanuts, crushed
  - Fully cooked chicken or shrimp, optional addition, to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Thai-inspired pasta uses the same pot for boiling noodles, scrambling eggs, and sautéing vegetables. Divide the oil between the eggs and vegetables, then toss everything with the soy-ginger sauce. Cilantro and green onions go in at the end.
For kids, serve the heat on the side or reduce/omit the spicy elements.

## Directions

1.  **Boil:** Cook pasta in a large pot of salted water according to package directions. Drain and set aside.
2.  **The Sauce:** In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, brown sugar, Sriracha, and grated ginger until smooth.
3.  **The Eggs:** In the same large pot, heat 1 tbsp oil. Scramble the eggs with the optional red pepper flakes until fully set, with no liquid egg remaining. Remove and set aside with the pasta.

7.  **Serve:** Remove from heat. Stir in the green onions, cilantro, and crushed peanuts. Serve immediately, or refrigerate promptly for chilled servings.

## Cooking Notes

Allow about 35 minutes for the base recipe, including water heating, with sauce preparation overlapping the pasta cooking. Cooking an optional protein separately adds time. If starting with raw chicken, cook it separately to 165°F / 74°C; cook raw shrimp until pearly and opaque through the center before adding. For chilled servings, refrigerate in shallow containers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C. Keep at 40°F / 4°C or below.

RECIPE: Onigiri (Japanese Rice Balls) (onigiri-japanese-rice-balls.md)
CUISINES: Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/onigiri-japanese-rice-balls/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups Cooked Japanese Short-Grain Rice (warm or room temperature)
  - 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt
  - --- Filling Options (choose one or make variety) ---
  - Filling A: 4 oz Canned Tuna, drained and mixed with 1 tbsp Mayo + 1 tsp Soy Sauce
  - Filling B: 4 Umeboshi (pickled plums), pitted
  - Filling C: 1/4 cup Salmon Flakes (fresh cooked or canned) mixed with 1/2 tsp Soy Sauce
  - Filling D: 2 tbsp Sesame Seeds mixed with 1/2 tsp Sea Salt
  - --- For Assembling ---
  - 4-8 Sheets Nori (seaweed), cut into strips
  - Sesame Seeds for garnish (optional)
  - Water in a small bowl (for wet hands)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Onigiri are Japanese rice balls - simple, transportable, and a staple of bentos and home cooking for centuries. What makes them special is the ritual: the rice is still warm when shaped, and the small amount of salt on your hands seasons the outside just enough. You can fill them with whatever you like (pickled plume, tuna mayo, salmon, sesame), wrap nori around the outside, and pack them for school, work, or a picnic. They're best when still warm, but keep perishable rice balls cold when preparing them ahead or packing them for later. A squeeze of warm rice in your palm wrapped by a sheet of nori is one of the most comforting things to eat.

## Directions

1. **Cook the Rice:** If starting from scratch, prepare 1 cup Japanese short-grain rice according to package directions (usually 1:1 ratio with water). Let rest for 10 minutes after cooking. Use warm rice for the best texture when shaping.

2. **Prepare the Work Surface:** Have a small bowl of water nearby. Wet your hands slightly and sprinkle a pinch of salt into your palm. This is crucial - it prevents sticking and adds a subtle salty flavor to the outer rice.

3. **Form the Triangle (Basic Shape):** Take about 1/2 cup cooked rice in your palm. Make a small indent in the center with your thumb, creating a pocket about the size of a marble. Place 1 tbsp of your chosen filling into the pocket.

4. **Encase the Filling:** Cup your hand to gently bring rice up and around the filling, enclosing it completely. You should have a ball of rice with filling inside. Squeeze gently but firmly - you want it compact enough to hold together but not so tight that it becomes dense.

5. **Shape into Triangle:** Place the rice ball on your work surface. Using both hands (re-wet and re-salt if needed), gently shape it into a triangle by applying even pressure on three sides. The shape comes from your hands, not from pressing into a mold. A triangular onigiri is iconic and practical - it sits flat and is easy to wrap.

6. **Wrap with Nori:** Cut nori into strips about 1 inch wide and 3-4 inches long. Wrap one strip around the middle of the onigiri, like a belt. The nori will stick to the rice from its slight moisture. If wrapping right before serving, the nori stays crispy; if you wrap earlier, it softens slightly from the rice moisture.

7. **Garnish and Store:** Sprinkle with sesame seeds if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature. For make-ahead service, refrigerate promptly at 40°F or below and transport with an ice pack. Count preparation and service together: discard perishable onigiri left out over 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. If frozen, thaw in the refrigerator rather than on the counter. Keep nori separate until serving for crispness.

**Filling Ideas:** Keep fillings minimal - a single flavor is more traditional. Tuna mayo, umeboshi (pickled plum), grilled salmon, kombu (kelp), or just sesame salt all work beautifully.

**Hand Temperature:** Warm hands make shaping easier and prevent the rice from cooling too much. If your hands get cold, re-wet with warm water and re-salt.

**Nori Texture:** For maximum crispness, wrap nori just before serving. For softer nori, wrap 30 minutes ahead and let the moisture from the rice soften it slightly.

RECIPE: Orange and Paprika Pulled Pork (orange-and-paprika-pulled-pork.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/orange-and-paprika-pulled-pork/
SOURCE: downshiftology.com
SOURCE_URL: https://downshiftology.com/recipes/slow-cooker-pulled-pork/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 1/2 pounds pork shoulder
  - 2 tablespoons paprika
  - 1 teaspoon oregano
  - 1 teaspoon salt
  - 1 teaspoon pepper
  - 1/2 teaspoon cumin
  - 1 yellow onion, diced
  - 4 garlic cloves, chopped
  - 1 orange, juiced
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Orange and paprika season this shoulder, distinct from the smoked-salt pulled pork. Cook until it pulls apart with little resistance, then spoon back cooking juices as needed. Shoulder tenderness takes longer than simply meeting the pork safety minimum.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Start with fully thawed pork kept refrigerated until preparation. Check the actual cooker’s load and whole-roast size requirements. Place the diced onion, chopped garlic and all the orange juice in the cooker.

2. **Season:** Mix all the paprika, oregano, salt, pepper and cumin. Trim excess external fat, keeping the shoulder’s internal marbling; rub all the measured spice mixture over the shoulder and put it in the cooker.

3. **Cook:** Cover and cook on LOW for about 8 hours. Start with fully thawed pork. The shoulder should be fork-tender, commonly around 195–205°F; the food-safety minimum is 145°F / 63°C with three minutes rest. Continue cooking if it does not pull apart easily. Keep the cooker covered except for necessary checks.

4. **Shred:** Move the fully cooked shoulder to a clean board or plate and pull apart with two forks. If it resists, return it to covered cooking rather than force it into dry chunks. Remove any bone when present.

5. **Moisten and serve:** Spoon some of the hot cooking juices over the shredded pork until it is moist without flooding it; retain the rest for serving if wanted. Divide among the listed portions and serve.

## Cooking Notes

Check the actual cooker’s instructions for its permitted food load, liquid requirements and meat size. Follow your cooker’s stated minimum and maximum fill limits. When scaling, choose suitable cooker capacity or separate appropriately filled cookers, and divide all measured ingredients across them. Cooking times do not multiply with portions. Keep the lid closed except for necessary additions and doneness checks. Use LOW for this recipe’s cooking route; WARM does not replace cooking.

Refrigerate promptly in shallow covered containers at 40°F / 4°C or below, within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C). Use within 3–4 days. Reheat on the stove, in the microwave or oven outside the slow cooker, stirring or turning as appropriate for even heating and checking 165°F / 74°C throughout; do not use the slow cooker to reheat cold leftovers. If holding cooked food in the cooker, maintain at least 140°F / 60°C and follow its holding instructions.

RECIPE: Chocolate Sandwich Cookie Cheesecake (oreo-chocolate-cream-cheesecake.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/oreo-chocolate-cream-cheesecake/
SOURCE: Adapted from Kraft Recipes, now at Snackworks
SOURCE_URL: https://www.snackworks.com/recipes/oreo-chocolate-cream-cheesecake-55897/index.html
INGREDIENTS:
  - 32 regular-size chocolate sandwich cookies with chocolate-flavored creme, about 14–15 g each, divided; keep the creme filling
  - 32 oz (907 g) full-fat block cream cheese, softened as directed
  - 1 cup (200 g) granulated sugar
  - 1 tsp vanilla extract
  - 4 large eggs
  - 8 oz (227 g) semisweet baking chocolate, chopped
  - 1 tsp neutral oil, for greasing the pan
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Melted semisweet chocolate gives this cheesecake its dense chocolate filling, with chocolate-creme cookies in the base, middle and top. Smooth the softened cream cheese before adding the eggs, then mix slowly. Chill the cake thoroughly before cutting so the filling supports the cookie pieces.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the pan and cookies:** Once the cheese is softened as described above, heat the oven to 325°F / 163°C with a rack in the middle. Grease the bottom and sides of the springform pan with the measured oil. Finely crush twelve whole cookies, creme included. Quarter the other twenty cookies and keep all their crumbs. Measure a level 1 1/2 cups of these pieces and crumbs without packing for the filling; set all the remaining pieces aside for the top.
2. **Bake the crust and melt the chocolate:** Press the fine crumbs evenly and firmly across the bottom of the pan, with no bare patches. Set the pan on a rimmed baking sheet and bake for 10 minutes. Cool on a rack while mixing the filling. Put the chopped chocolate in a dry microwave-safe bowl and heat at half power in 20–30-second bursts, stirring between each, until just melted. Let it become lukewarm but still fluid; avoid getting water in it.
3. **Smooth the cheese:** Beat the softened cream cheese, sugar and vanilla at low to medium-low speed until smooth, about 2–3 minutes, stopping to scrape the bottom and sides of the bowl. Mix in the lukewarm chocolate until the color is even. Scrape again; avoid whipping the mixture fluffy.
4. **Add eggs and cookies:** Add the eggs one at a time on low speed, mixing only until each disappears. Scrape the bowl and fold in the measured 1 1/2 cups of cookie pieces with a spatula. Do not taste the raw batter. Spread gently over the cooled crust and scatter all the remaining quartered cookies and crumbs over the top.
5. **Bake to a set center:** Bake on the rimmed sheet for about 50–70 minutes, checking at 50 minutes. The edges should be set and the central few inches should tremble together when the pan is nudged, without a liquid wave. Check the filling in the center with an instant-read thermometer, avoiding cookie pieces and the pan base; it must reach at least 160°F / 71°C. Continue in 5-minute intervals if needed, then remove to a rack.
6. **Cool and chill:** After about 10 minutes, carefully run a thin knife between the cake and the pan wall without opening the clasp. Cool on the rack for about 1 hour total, then refrigerate in the pan, loosely covered and with space around it. Refrigerate within 2 hours of leaving the oven, or within 1 hour if the kitchen is above 90°F / 32°C. Once cold, cover well. Chill for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, until cold and firm through the center.
7. **Unmold and slice:** Release the clasp and lift off the ring; leave the cake on its base for support. Cut into sixteen slices with a sharp knife, wiping it clean between cuts. Serve chilled, with coffee or unsweetened tea if desired.

RECIPE: Overnight Oats (overnight-oats.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/overnight-oats/
SOURCE: Adapted from downshiftology.com
SOURCE_URL: https://downshiftology.com/recipes/overnight-oats/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1/2 cup Old-Fashioned Rolled Oats (not instant, not steel-cut)
  - 1/2 cup Milk (any variety)
  - 1/4 cup Plain Greek Yogurt
  - 1 tbsp Chia Seeds
  - 1 tbsp Maple Syrup or Honey
  - 1/2 tsp Vanilla Extract
  - Pinch of Kosher Salt
  - Toppings: fresh fruit, nut butter, granola, toasted coconut, or nuts
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Overnight oats are essentially Bircher muesli, invented by Swiss physician Maximilian Bircher-Benner around 1900. The principle is simple: oats hydrate overnight in liquid, softening into a creamy, pudding-like texture without any heat. Greek yogurt adds protein and tanginess, while chia seeds absorb liquid and create body. The ratio that consistently works is 1:1 oats to liquid plus a quarter-cup of yogurt. Old-fashioned rolled oats are essential -- instant oats turn to mush and steel-cut oats stay crunchy. This is a base recipe; the variations are endless.

## Directions

1.  **Combine:** In a jar or airtight container, stir together oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds, maple syrup, vanilla, and salt. Make sure the chia seeds are distributed throughout -- they clump if left on the surface.
2.  **Refrigerate:** Seal the container and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight (up to 5 days).
3.  **Adjust:** In the morning, stir the oats. If they are too thick, add a splash of milk and stir to loosen. If too thin, add a spoonful of oats and let sit for 10 minutes.
4.  **Top and Serve:** Add your toppings of choice. Serve cold straight from the jar, or microwave for 1-2 minutes if you prefer warm oats.

### Variation Ideas

- **PB&J:** Stir in 1 tbsp peanut butter and top with smashed raspberries.
- **Banana Nut:** Add half a mashed banana to the base mixture and top with walnuts and a drizzle of honey.
- **Berry:** Top with mixed berries and a sprinkle of granola.
- **Carrot Cake:** Stir in 1/4 cup shredded carrot, a handful of raisins, and a pinch of cinnamon. Top with walnuts and a drizzle of maple syrup.
- **Tropical:** Use coconut milk and top with mango, toasted coconut, and macadamia nuts.

RECIPE: Pad See Ew (pad-see-ew-thai-stir-fried-noodles.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pad-see-ew-thai-stir-fried-noodles/
SOURCE: Adapted from recipetineats.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.recipetineats.com/thai-stir-fried-noodles-pad-see-ew/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken ---
  - 750 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced about 1/4 inch thick
  - 1 tbsp regular soy sauce, for the chicken
  - 1 tsp cornstarch
  - 1 tsp neutral oil, for the chicken
  - --- Noodles, vegetables and eggs ---
  - 1000 g fresh wide rice noodles (sen yai); see dried-noodle substitution
  - 500 g Chinese broccoli (gai lan), trimmed; thick stems sliced 1/4 inch thick and leaves cut into 2-inch pieces
  - 4 cloves garlic, finely chopped
  - 3 large eggs, beaten
  - 4 tbsp neutral oil, for cooking, divided
  - 2 tbsp water, for steaming the broccoli, plus small splashes if needed
  - --- Sauce ---
  - 4 tbsp oyster sauce
  - 2 tbsp regular soy sauce
  - 2 tbsp Thai sweet dark soy sauce
  - 1 tsp sugar
  - 2 tbsp water, for the sauce
  - 1/4 tsp ground white pepper
  - --- At the table ---
  - 1 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar, optional, divided among plates to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Soy-seasoned rice noodles, Chinese broccoli, chicken and egg make five portions of pad see ew. Cook the vegetables and eggs first, then finish each portion separately so the noodles have room to brown. Offer a little vinegar at the table so each diner can adjust the sweetness and acidity.

## Directions

1. **Prepare chicken and noodles:** Toss chicken with marinade soy, cornstarch, and its teaspoon of oil; refrigerate during preparation. Gently separate flexible fresh noodles and divide into five 200 g portions. If cold and stiff, warm briefly according to their package before separating. Use the substitution instructions for dried noodles.
2. **Organize sauce and vegetables:** Mix oyster sauce, sauce soy, Thai sweet dark soy, sugar, sauce water, and white pepper until uniform. Cut broccoli, keeping stems and leaves separate. Chop garlic and beat the eggs.
3. **Cook chicken in two batches:** Heat 1 1/2 tsp cooking oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Spread half the chicken in one layer. Leave 1–2 minutes, then turn and stir-fry until several thick slices reach 165°F / 74°C, about 4–6 minutes total. Transfer to a clean bowl. Repeat with another 1 1/2 tsp oil and the rest of the chicken.
4. **Cook vegetables and eggs:** Reduce heat to medium. Add 2 tsp oil and stir garlic for about 30 seconds until fragrant. Add broccoli stems and the steaming water; cover for about 2–3 minutes, until stems are almost tender. Uncover, add leaves and stir-fry 1–2 minutes until wilted and water has evaporated. Transfer to a bowl. Add 1 tsp oil, then beaten eggs; stir gently until fully set with no wet streaks, about 1–2 minutes. Transfer out. Divide chicken, broccoli, egg, and well-stirred sauce into five portions.
5. **Finish one serving:** Heat about one-fifth of the remaining 2 tbsp oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Add one noodle portion and one sauce portion. Lift and fold gently to coat, then spread and leave about 15–20 seconds. Turn and repeat once or twice for a few toasted patches, reducing heat if sauce starts to burn. Add one portion each of chicken, broccoli and egg with their share of any cooking juices. Fold until hot throughout, about 3–4 minutes total for this final batch. Add a small splash of water only if the noodles need loosening.
6. **Taste, plate, and repeat:** Taste the first portion and adjust the remaining sauce if necessary. Plate promptly and repeat step 5 four more times. Offer the measured vinegar at the table in small amounts. Serve plates as they finish, with an optional cool cucumber side; the main already contains its noodles, protein and vegetables.

RECIPE: Pad Thai (pad-thai.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pad-thai/
SOURCE: Adapted from Thaitable.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.thaitable.com/thai/recipe/pad-thai
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Noodles and sauce ---
  - 1/2 package (1 lb) (8 oz) dried wide rice noodles (bánh phở), check the package’s soaking instructions
  - noodle-soaking water, enough to cover the noodles
  - 2 tbsp tamarind paste made from pulp and water, ready to use; not a dry block or undiluted stronger concentrate
  - 2 tbsp palm sugar or granulated sugar, finely chopped if solid palm sugar
  - 4 tsp fish sauce
  - water for finishing the noodles, as needed, added one tablespoon at a time
  - --- Stir-fry and garnish ---
  - 2 tbsp cooking oil
  - 1/3 cup extra-firm tofu, drained, patted dry and julienned
  - 1 shallot, minced
  - 3 garlic cloves, minced
  - 1/2 tsp ground dried chili
  - 1 large egg
  - 1/4 lb shrimp, raw, peeled and deveined; fully thawed if frozen
  - 1 1/3 cups fresh bean sprouts, washed and drained
  - 1 1/2 cups Chinese chives or green onions, cut into short pieces
  - 1/2 cup peanuts, already toasted and crushed
  - 1/2 lime, cut into wedges
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Pad Thai combines tamarind, fish sauce and sugar with chewy rice noodles, shrimp, tofu, lime and peanuts. This version keeps wide noodles and a generous toasted-peanut garnish. Have everything ready before frying so you can judge noodle hydration as you toss. For less heat, omit the dried chili.

## Directions

1. **Soak the noodles:** Use dried wide rice noodles (bánh phở) and noodle-soaking water to soak the dry noodles according to the package’s stir-fry guidance, checking for strands that bend but remain firm rather than fully expanded and soft. Lukewarm or room-temperature soaking is appropriate for Thai rice sticks; wide noodles can take longer. Drain when flexible. Prepare the remaining ingredients during the soak.
2. **Mix the sauce:** Combine tamarind paste made from pulp and water, palm sugar or granulated sugar, and fish sauce, stirring to dissolve the sugar. Have the sauce ready before the wok gets hot.
3. **Fry the tofu:** Have 1/2 of the cooking oil and extra-firm tofu ready. Heat this half of the measured cooking oil in a wok or large skillet and fry the tofu until golden and firm, then remove to a plate. Keep the already toasted peanuts for serving.
4. **Bloom garlic, shallot and chili:** Have 1/2 of the cooking oil, shallot, garlic cloves, and ground dried chili ready. Heat the remaining measured oil in the wok, then add the shallot, garlic and dried chili. Stir about 30 seconds until fragrant, keeping the garlic and chili moving so they do not scorch.
5. **Toss the noodles and sauce:** Add the drained noodles and prepared sauce. Stir-fry over high heat, lifting and turning to coat the noodles. Use water for finishing the noodles only if the strands remain too firm: add a tablespoon at a time, letting each addition absorb, until the noodles are tender and chewy. Use manageable loads if needed and divide all ingredients proportionally; do not force a thick wet mound into one pan.
6. **Set the egg:** Push the noodles aside. Add large egg to the cleared space, scramble until set, then fold into the noodles.
7. **Cook the shrimp:** Add shrimp and all the cooked tofu. Toss, starting to check at about 2 minutes, and continue until every shrimp is firm, pearly and opaque. Pink color and the short time alone are not doneness checks.
8. **Cook the sprouts:** Fold in fresh bean sprouts. Start checking at about 15 seconds, but continue until thoroughly cooked rather than lightly warmed, especially when serving children or other diners vulnerable to foodborne illness.
9. **Finish with chives:** Fold in Chinese chives or green onions and toss briefly, just until they soften. The noodles should be chewy and coated, without a pool of loose sauce.
10. **Serve:** Divide the noodles among the portions and top with all the peanuts and lime. Serve immediately; squeeze the lime over the noodles at the table.

## Sprout variation

For a raw-sprout garnish, reserve half the measured sprouts before frying and cook the other half with the noodles; the reserved half replaces part of the cooked sprouts. Children, older adults, pregnant people and people with weakened immune systems should avoid raw or lightly cooked sprouts; use the fully cooked route for them.

RECIPE: Pad Woon Sen (pad-woon-sen.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pad-woon-sen/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1025396-pad-woon-sen
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6.3 oz Dried Mung Bean Glass Noodles
  - 3 tbsp Oyster Sauce
  - 3 tbsp Fish Sauce
  - 1 tbsp Soy Sauce
  - 1 tsp Granulated Sugar
  - 1/4 Napa Cabbage, sliced
  - 1 Bell Pepper, sliced
  - 1 medium Carrot, grated
  - 1 Yellow Onion, sliced
  - 4 cloves Garlic, thinly sliced
  - 3 large Eggs, whisked
  - 1 Thai Bird Chile, sliced
  - 4 Scallions, sliced
  - Grapeseed Oil
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Pad woon sen is a Thai glass noodle stir-fry that's lighter than pad thai. Mung bean glass noodles should be soaked in hot (not boiling) water for exactly 10 minutes to reach their optimal translucent texture. Sautéing cabbage and peppers over high heat until they develop charred edges before adding noodles creates smoky depth.

## Directions

1.  **Noodles:** Soak mung bean noodles in hot water for 10 minutes. Drain and rinse in cold water.
2.  **The Sauce:** In a small bowl, whisk together oyster sauce, fish sauce, soy sauce, and sugar.
3.  **The Egg:** In a wok, heat a splash of oil. Scramble the eggs with a pinch of salt until just set. Remove and roughly chop.
4.  **The Crunch:** Heat oil until smoking. Sauté cabbage and peppers for 3-4 minutes until charred at the edges but still firm. Transfer to the egg plate.
5.  **Aromatics:** Add fresh oil. Sauté onions and carrots for 2 minutes until soft. Add garlic and sauté for 45 seconds.
6.  **Bind:** Add the drained noodles and the sauce. Toss vigorously over medium-high for 3 minutes until the noodles are glossy and have absorbed the liquid.
7.  **Finish:** Return the eggs and charred veg to the wok. Stir in the Thai chile and scallions for the mandatory **High Note**.
8.  **Serve:** Serve hot or at room temperature for the Kitchen Standard fuel profile.

RECIPE: Pan Fried Noodles with Shrimp (pan-fried-noodles-with-shrimp.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pan-fried-noodles-with-shrimp/
SOURCE: Adapted from thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/seafood-pan-fried-noodles/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Noodle cake and greens ---
  - 8 oz fresh Hong Kong-style egg noodles, check whether the package is raw or already cooked
  - cooking water, enough to cook noodles and blanch greens
  - 2 tbsp vegetable oil for the noodle cake
  - 4 oz yu choy or bok choy, washed; separate thicker stems from tender leaves if needed
  - --- Shrimp and gravy ---
  - 1 lb large shrimp, raw, peeled and deveined; fully thawed if frozen
  - 1/4 tsp baking soda, for the shrimp treatment; rinse it off
  - shrimp-rinsing water, as needed to rinse off the baking soda
  - 1 1/2 cups chicken stock
  - 2 tsp oyster sauce
  - 1 tbsp soy sauce
  - 1/2 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1/4 tsp white pepper
  - 2 tbsp cornstarch for the slurry, prepare the full slurry; add only as much as the gravy needs
  - 2 tbsp water for the slurry
  - 1/2 cup sliced carrots and mushrooms, combined volume; slice carrots thinly
  - vegetable oil for the wok, as needed for a light cooking film
  - 1 tbsp ginger, julienned
  - 2 garlic cloves, minced
  - 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Cantonese-style noodle cake is crisp at the edges and softer beneath its shrimp gravy. Drain the fresh egg noodles well, brown both faces, and pour the glossy gravy over the center just before serving.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the shrimp:** Have large shrimp, baking soda, and shrimp-rinsing water ready. Toss the shrimp with the baking soda and refrigerate for 5 minutes, then rinse thoroughly with the rinsing water and pat dry. Keep nearby food and clean utensils away from splashes; clean the sink and work surface after rinsing. Keep the shrimp refrigerated while preparing the noodles.
2. **Mix the gravy base:** Combine chicken stock, oyster sauce, soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, and white pepper in a bowl and set beside the stove.
3. **Mix the slurry:** Mix cornstarch for the slurry and water for the slurry in a separate bowl. The slurry will settle; stir it again immediately before adding it to the hot gravy.
4. **Prepare the noodles:** Use fresh Hong Kong-style egg noodles and cooking water to prepare the noodles according to their package until just tender. For fresh raw Hong Kong-style noodles, start checking at about 1 minute rather than assuming every product has the same cooking time. Rinse cool, drain thoroughly and shake off surface water. Keep or refresh the boiling water for the greens.
5. **Fry the first side:** Heat vegetable oil for the noodle cake in a nonstick pan over heat permitted by its instructions. Spread the drained noodles into a thin, even cake. Fry undisturbed, checking the underside at about 5 minutes; it should release with a golden, crisp bottom. Use more cakes or pan loads if the measured noodles cannot fit in a thin layer, dividing the measured cake oil proportionally among them.
6. **Crisp the second side:** Loosen and flip the cake, in sections if needed. Crisp the other side in the oil already in the pan until golden, then transfer to a serving platter.
7. **Blanch the greens:** Blanch yu choy or bok choy in the boiling water, starting to check at 30 seconds. Continue until the stems are tender enough to eat; thicker stems may take longer than leaves. Drain and arrange around the noodle cake.
8. **Cook carrots and mushrooms:** Have sliced carrots and mushrooms and vegetable oil for the wok ready. Heat the oil in a wok or skillet, then stir-fry the carrots and mushrooms until the carrots lose their hard raw center and the mushrooms soften. Work in manageable batches if needed; gather all the vegetables for the gravy.
9. **Add the aromatics:** Add ginger and garlic cloves to the vegetables and stir briefly until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Keep the garlic moving so it does not burn.
10. **Sear the shrimp:** Add the prepared shrimp to the hot wok in a manageable layer, moving vegetables aside or cooking shrimp in batches if necessary. Start checking at about 1 minute per side, then add Shaoxing wine. The gravy step completes cooking; continue directly to it.
11. **Finish the gravy:** Pour in the prepared gravy base and bring it to a boil. Stir the slurry again and add it gradually, letting each addition thicken before adding more. Stop when the gravy lightly coats a spoon; the entire prepared slurry may not be needed. Cook until every shrimp is firm, pearly and opaque, and all the carrots are tender. Do not judge doneness from the searing time alone. Discard any unused slurry.
12. **Serve immediately:** Pour all the hot shrimp, vegetables and gravy over the center of the noodle cake, leaving some edges uncovered for crunch. Divide among the portions and serve immediately.

RECIPE: Panang Curry with Chicken (panang-curry-with-chicken.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/panang-curry-with-chicken/
SOURCE: Adapted from Snapguide.com
SOURCE_URL: https://snapguide.com/guides/cook-homemade-panang-curry/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 450 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced about 1/2 inch thick
  - 300 ml full-fat unsweetened coconut milk, divided
  - 3 tbsp panang curry paste, or less for a particularly strong paste
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil, only if needed when frying the paste
  - 2 tbsp unsalted roasted peanuts, finely ground
  - 150 g red bell pepper, thinly sliced
  - 4 makrut lime leaves, central ribs removed and leaves sliced into very fine threads
  - 2 tsp palm sugar or brown sugar, added gradually to taste
  - 1 tbsp fish sauce, added gradually only as needed
  - 2 tbsp water, used only if needed to loosen the sauce
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Ground peanuts give this panang curry body, while makrut lime leaves provide its distinctive aroma. Red pepper adds sweetness and color. Grind the peanuts finely so they blend into the thick sauce; panko is not a substitute for their flavor or texture. Serve with rice prepared separately.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Grind roasted peanuts to a fine meal. Remove the stiff central ribs from lime leaves, stack the leaves and slice into very fine threads. Slice pepper before handling chicken, then slice chicken and clean the work area. Measure the coconut milk and reserve 180 ml, leaving 120 ml for the paste.
2. **Cook the paste:** Simmer the 120 ml coconut milk in a wide skillet over medium heat about 3–5 minutes until thickened, stirring. Add panang paste and stir for about 2 minutes until fragrant. If no oil releases and paste is sticking, add the measured neutral oil. Do not continue cooking a dry paste simply to force visible splitting.
3. **Thicken the sauce:** Add the reserved coconut milk, finely ground peanuts, half the lime-leaf threads and half the sugar. Simmer gently about 3–5 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens enough to leave a brief spatula trail across the pan.
4. **Cook chicken and pepper:** Add chicken and pepper, separating the slices in the sauce. Simmer gently about 6–10 minutes, stirring, until several thick chicken slices reach 165°F / 74°C and the pepper is tender with a little bite. Use the measured water in small splashes only if the sauce becomes too dry before chicken cooks.
5. **Balance and finish:** Taste the fully cooked curry. Start with about 1 tsp fish sauce and add more only if needed; add remaining sugar only if wanted. Fold in the remaining fine lime-leaf threads and warm for about 30 seconds. Serve four modest main portions with separately prepared [plain rice](/mise/recipes/steamed-white-rice).

RECIPE: Parish’s Blueberry Crisp (parishs-blueberry-crisp.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/parishs-blueberry-crisp/
SOURCE: Adapted from Parish
SOURCE_URL: https://www.myajc.com/lifestyles/food--cooking/brown-butter-key-parish-blueberry-crisp/ht0uxKmxnFIptyggBS5fpL/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 cups Fresh Blueberries
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice
  - 1/2 cup Granulated Sugar
  - 2 tsp Cornstarch
  - 1 3/4 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 1 cup Light Brown Sugar, packed
  - 6 tbsp Unsalted Butter (Beurre Noisette)
  - 1 1/4 tsp Sea Salt
  - [Vanilla Bean Ice Cream](/mise/recipes/old-fashioned-vanilla-ice-cream)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A crisp lives or dies by its topping - here, the secret is cooking the butter to brown butter stage (dark milk solids, nutty aroma) before mixing with the dry ingredients, so every crumb tastes like toasted nuts. The blueberry filling is tightened with cornstarch and lemon juice, preventing a soupy cobbler while keeping the fruit's bright acidity front and center.

## Directions

1.  **The Fruit:** In a saucepan, combine blueberries, 1/4 cup water, and lemon juice. Whisk sugar and cornstarch together and stir into the fruit. Cook over medium for 4 minutes until the juices thicken. Pour into a greased 9-inch square dish.
2.  **The Crumble:** In a small pan, melt butter over medium-high. Continue heating for 5 minutes, stirring often, until the milk solids turn dark brown and smell like toasted nuts. Remove from heat immediately.
3.  **The Mix:** In a large bowl, whisk flour, brown sugar, and salt. Drizzle the brown butter over the mix. Stir with a fork until large, crispy clumps form.
4.  **Bake:** Sprinkle the crumble generously over the fruit. Bake at 350°F for 30 minutes until the fruit is bubbling and the topping is a deep mahogany.
5.  **Serve:** Let cool for 10 minutes to allow the syrup to set. Serve warm with a scoop of [Vanilla Ice Cream](/mise/recipes/old-fashioned-vanilla-ice-cream).

## Cooking Notes

Peaches, strawberries or cherries can replace blueberries, with baking time adjusted for their moisture and tenderness. For cherries, almond flour and sliced almonds can be used in the crumble; toasted pecans suit peaches. Sprinkle only as much crumble as desired and save surplus for another bake.

RECIPE: Parmigiano Reggiano Cheesecake (parmigiano-reggiano-cheesecake.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/parmigiano-reggiano-cheesecake/
SOURCE: Adapted from food52.com
SOURCE_URL: https://food52.com/recipes/85524-parmigiano-reggiano-cheesecake/amp
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3/4 cup Finely Ground Parmigiano Reggiano
  - 18 Graham Crackers, crushed
  - 1/2 cup Toasted Sunflower Seeds (Nut-Free option)
  - 1 tsp Lemon Zest
  - 1/2 tsp Cinnamon
  - 4 tbsp Unsalted Butter, melted
  - 40 oz (5 packs) Cream Cheese, room temperature
  - 1 1/3 cups Granulated Sugar
  - 1/2 cup Sour Cream
  - 1 cup Finely Grated Parmigiano Reggiano (Microplaned)
  - 5 large Eggs, room temperature
  - 1 tsp Vanilla Extract
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Savory cheesecake with Parmigiano-Reggiano is a Northern Italian tradition that blurs the line between cheese course and dessert - the aged cheese brings nutty, crystalline depth against the graham cracker crust. The water bath is non-negotiable: it creates gentle, even heat that prevents the edges from overcooking while the center sets. Pull it when the center still jiggles - residual heat finishes the job.

## Directions

1.  **The Crust:** Pulse the cheese, crackers, and seeds in a food processor. Mix with butter and press into a 10-inch springform pan. Bake at 350°F for 15 minutes. Cool.
2.  **The Filling:** Cream the cream cheese and sugar until silky. Add the sour cream, vanilla, and grated Parmigiano.
3.  **Eggs:** Add eggs **one at a time**, mixing on low speed to avoid aerating the batter (bubbles cause cracks!).
4.  **The Seal:** Wrap the bottom of the pan in heavy-duty foil. Place in a large roasting pan.
5.  **The Bath:** Pour the batter into the crust. Pour hot water into the roasting pan until it reaches halfway up the side of the springform pan.
6.  **Bake:** Bake at 325°F for 85-90 minutes until the edges are set but the center still has a slight jiggle.
7.  **The Chill:** Turn off the oven, crack the door, and let it sit for 1 hour. Then refrigerate for at least 6 hours.

RECIPE: Pasta with Abruzzi-Style Lamb Sauce (pasta-with-abruzzi-style-lamb-sauce.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pasta-with-abruzzi-style-lamb-sauce/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/pasta-abruzzi-style-lamb-sauce
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Penne or Rigatoni
  - 1 tbsp Olive Oil
  - Salt and Black Pepper, to taste (plus salt for the pasta water)
  - 3/4 lb Boneless Lamb (Leg or Shoulder), finely diced or ground
  - 2 oz Pancetta, finely chopped
  - 1/4 cup Yellow Onion, diced
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Rosemary, chopped
  - 3/4 cup Dry White Wine
  - 1 (28 oz) can Whole Peeled Tomatoes, crushed by hand
  - 1/3 cup Pecorino Romano, grated, plus extra for optional serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This ragù comes from Abruzzo, the mountainous region in central Italy where sheep farming has been a way of life for centuries. Abruzzese cuisine is rustic and hearty, designed to sustain shepherds in the mountains. Traditional lamb ragù starts with pancetta to render fat and add smokiness, then builds with white wine (not red) and rosemary, which grows wild in the Apennine mountains. Hand-crushing the tomatoes gives a chunkier, more rustic texture than smooth tomato sauce. Pecorino Romano (sheep's milk cheese) is the traditional finishing cheese in this region - it's sharper and saltier than Parmigiano-Reggiano. Dice the lamb yourself rather than buying pre-ground for better texture.

## Directions

1.  **Render:** Heat olive oil in a large skillet. Add the onion and pancetta. Cook until the pancetta fat has melted and the onions are gold (8 mins).
2.  **Sear:** Add the diced lamb and rosemary. Season with salt and pepper. Brown the meat aggressively until it develops a crust.
3.  **Deglaze:** Pour in the white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to release the fond. Simmer until the wine has evaporated by 75%.
4.  **Simmer:** Add the crushed tomatoes and their juices. Reduce heat to low and simmer gently for 30-40 minutes until the sauce is thick, the lamb is tender, and the fat starts to separate. Add a splash of water and simmer longer if diced shoulder is still firm.
5.  **Boil:** While the sauce simmers, cook pasta in salted water until al dente.
6.  **Combine:** Toss the hot pasta directly into the lamb sauce. Add the Pecorino and toss to coat.
7.  **Serve:** Serve with extra cheese and a crack of black pepper.

RECIPE: Pasta with Sausage, Basil & Mustard (pasta-with-sausage-basil-and-mustard.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pasta-with-sausage-basil-and-mustard/
SOURCE: Adapted from Nigel Slater, Food & Wine
SOURCE_URL: https://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/pasta-sausage-basil-and-mustard
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb dry penne or rigatoni
  - 1 1/2 lb raw hot Italian pork sausage, casings removed
  - 3/4 cup dry white wine
  - 3/4 cup heavy cream
  - 3 tbsp whole-grain Dijon mustard
  - 1 cup fresh basil, thinly sliced
  - 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - Red pepper flakes, a pinch or to taste
  - Parmesan, for grating at the table
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  - 1 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Whole-grain mustard and fresh basil give this cream sauce its character. Brown the sausage before reducing the wine, then simmer the cream only long enough to coat the pasta. Fold basil in off heat and taste before adding more salt or cheese.

## Directions

1. **Start water and prepare:** Bring pasta water to a boil. Remove sausage casings, measure sauce ingredients and slice basil. Season water moderately, then time pasta by its package so it finishes near the sauce.
2. **Brown and cook sausage:** Heat olive oil in a broad deep skillet over medium-high. Add sausage and break into small crumbles. Cook about **8–12 minutes**, stirring, until browned in places and representative thicker pieces reach **160°F / 71°C**. Brown in rounds if necessary, sharing the oil between them, then return all cooked meat to the pan.
3. **Reduce wine:** Add wine and scrape up browned bits. Simmer about **5 minutes**, or until the liquid is reduced roughly by half; pan width changes the time.
4. **Make the sauce:** Lower heat, stir in cream, **about two-thirds of the mustard** and the pepper flakes. Simmer gently about **2–3 minutes**, until lightly thickened. Taste and add the remaining mustard if wanted. Meanwhile cook pasta until tender with a little bite and reserve **the listed water amount** before draining.
5. **Toss and serve:** Add pasta to the sauce and fold over low heat just until coated, adding warm pasta water in small amounts if too thick. Remove from heat and fold in basil. Taste before adding salt or pepper. Divide into the intended portions and offer Parmesan for grating at the table.

Adapted from [Nigel Slater’s recipe at Food & Wine](https://www.foodandwine.com/pasta-with-sausage-basil-and-mustard-6415687).

RECIPE: Patatas Bravas (patatas-bravas.md)
CUISINES: Spanish
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/patatas-bravas/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 lbs Yukon Gold Potatoes, peeled and cut into 1.5-inch irregular chunks
  - Neutral Oil, for frying (about 4 cups)
  - Flaky Sea Salt, for finishing
  - 2 tbsp Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 3 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1 small Yellow Onion, finely diced
  - 1 can (14 oz) Crushed Tomatoes
  - 2 tsp Smoked Paprika (pimenton de la Vera, hot or sweet)
  - 1/2 tsp Cayenne Pepper, or to taste
  - 1 tsp Sweet Paprika
  - 1 tbsp Sherry Vinegar
  - 1 tsp Sugar
  - 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1/3 cup Mayonnaise (use vegan mayonnaise for the vegan option; for alioli)
  - 1 clove Garlic, finely grated (for alioli)
  - 1 tbsp Lemon Juice (for alioli)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The double-cook method is what separates bar-standard patatas bravas from unforgettable ones. Parboiling the potatoes first roughens the edges and gelatinizes the starch, creating a shatteringly crisp exterior when they hit the hot oil. Make the bravas sauce in advance -- it benefits from resting as the smokiness from the pimenton rounds out. Cut the potatoes into irregular chunks, not uniform cubes; the jagged edges crisp up better.

## Directions

1.  **Make the Bravas Sauce:** Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 5-6 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds. Stir in the smoked paprika, sweet paprika, and cayenne. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the crushed tomatoes, sugar, and salt. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until thickened. Stir in the sherry vinegar. For a smooth sauce, blend with an immersion blender or pass through a sieve. Set aside.

2.  **Make the Alioli:** Whisk together the mayonnaise, grated garlic, and lemon juice. Season with a pinch of salt. Refrigerate until serving.

3.  **Parboil the Potatoes:** Place the potato chunks in a large pot of generously salted cold water. Bring to a boil and cook for 8-10 minutes until the edges are tender but the centers still have some resistance. Drain well and spread on a sheet pan to steam dry for 10 minutes. This step is crucial for crispiness.

4.  **Fry the Potatoes:** Heat 4 cups of oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven to 375F. Working in batches to avoid crowding, fry the potatoes for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until deeply golden and crispy. Transfer to a wire rack set over a sheet pan. Season immediately with flaky sea salt.

5.  **Serve:** Pile the hot potatoes on a warm serving platter. Drizzle generously with the bravas sauce and dot with the alioli. Serve immediately with toothpicks or small forks -- this is tapas, after all.

RECIPE: Patate al Forno (patate-al-forno.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/patate-al-forno/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Potatoes and seasoning ---
  - 2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, scrubbed and cut into 1-inch chunks; skin may stay on
  - 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 2 fresh rosemary sprigs, leaves stripped and finely chopped; woody stems discarded
  - 1 tsp garlic powder
  - 1 tsp sea salt
  - black pepper, to taste
  - --- Finish ---
  - sea salt, a final pinch, to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

These rosemary-and-garlic Yukon Gold potatoes go straight into a 450°F oven. Dry the cut chunks, coat them evenly and give them room on the sheet so their flat faces can brown. Judge the roast by both color and an easily pierced center; high heat alone does not guarantee a crunchy exterior or a cooked middle.

## Directions

1. **Heat and prepare:** Heat the oven to 450°F. Use a large rimmed metal baking sheet, bare or lined with suitable foil. Use parchment only if its manufacturer rates it for 450°F; keep any lining within its stated instructions. Wash the potatoes under running water before cutting; dry the cut chunks with a clean towel. This method goes directly into the oven without parboiling.
2. **Coat and season:** Toss Yukon Gold potatoes, extra-virgin olive oil, fresh rosemary sprigs, garlic powder, sea salt, and black pepper in a large bowl until the potatoes are evenly coated. Use the chopped rosemary leaves, not the woody stems, and include the black pepper here.
3. **Give the potatoes room:** Spread the coated chunks in a single layer with a little space between them, placing flat cut faces against the pan where possible. Use more sheets or roasting batches if the measured potatoes do not fit; scaling does not enlarge the sheet.
4. **Roast until browned and tender:** Roast for 35–40 minutes, flipping gently with a spatula halfway through. Start checking at 35 minutes: the cut faces should be well browned and a knife should enter the center of a thick chunk easily. Continue if still firm, checking browned areas so they do not blacken. Rotate multiple sheets if browning is uneven; extra sheets can change the timing.
5. **Season and serve:** Taste a potato, then add sea salt if needed. Serve hot, while the browned edges are at their best.

RECIPE: Peach Pie Biscuit Bombs (peach-pie-biscuit-bombs.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/peach-pie-biscuit-bombs/
SOURCE: Adapted from sugardishme.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.sugardishme.com/peach-pie-biscuit-bombs/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 pkg Refrigerated Flaky Biscuits (Grands)
  - 1 cup Fresh Peaches, sliced into 1-inch pieces
  - 4 oz Brie Cheese, rinds removed
  - 2 tbsp Light Brown Sugar
  - 1 tsp Ground Cinnamon
  - 1 tbsp Honey
  - 3 tbsp Unsalted Butter (Beurre Noisette)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

These are a shortcut's triumph - using refrigerated biscuits legitimately, not apologetically. The filling is a lesson in flavor layering: warm peaches, creamy melted brie (unexpected richness), brown butter (nutty depth), and brown sugar with cinnamon (familiar sweetness). Brush with brown butter twice - once before baking and again after - for a flaky exterior and luxurious finish.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 375°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment.
2.  **Split:** Pull each raw biscuit in half horizontally.
3.  **Layer:** Place 3 peach slices and 1 tsp of Brie in the center of the bottom half. Sprinkle with brown sugar and cinnamon. Drizzle with a drop of honey.
4.  **Seal:** Place the top half back on. Pinch the edges firmly and roll gently in your palms to form a uniform "ball." Arrange 2 inches apart on the pan.
5.  **The Sizzle:** In a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter until it crackles and turns nutty brown. Brush each "bomb" generously with the brown butter.
6.  **Bake:** Bake for 12-15 minutes until the tops are deep golden brown and the biscuit has a flaky "Bounce."
7.  **Serve:** Brush once more with the remaining brown butter. Serve warm while the Brie is molten.

RECIPE: Peach Pie Pancakes (peach-pie-pancakes.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/peach-pie-pancakes/
SOURCE: Adapted from amyshealthybaking.com
SOURCE_URL: https://amyshealthybaking.com/blog/2016/06/05/peach-pie-pancakes/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup White Whole Wheat Flour
  - 1/2 cup Plain Greek Yogurt for richness
  - 3/4 cup Nonfat Milk
  - 1/2 cup Fresh Peaches, finely diced
  - 1 1/2 tsp Baking Powder
  - 3/4 tsp Ground Cinnamon
  - 1/4 tsp Sea Salt
  - 2 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - 1 tsp Unsalted Butter, melted
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The secret to peach pie pancakes that aren't heavy is using Greek yogurt as the primary binder, creating a dense, custardy texture that mimics pie filling without excessive oil. Making small, 2-tablespoon "silver dollar" pancakes ensures the diced peaches are distributed evenly and the pancake cooks through before the fruit releases too much moisture. The cinnamon provides essential aromatic warmth.

## Directions

1.  **Dry Mix:** In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt.
2.  **The Emulsion:** In a separate bowl, whisk yogurt, milk, vanilla, and melted butter until perfectly smooth.
3.  **Combine:** Gradually add the dry mix to the wet in 4 parts. Stir with a spatula until **just incorporated**. Small lumps are mandatory for a light texture.
4.  **Fold:** Gently fold in the diced peaches.
5.  **Prep:** Heat a non-stick skillet over **low-medium** heat (crucial for whole wheat). Lightly grease with oil spray.
6.  **Pour:** Drop 2-tbsp portions onto the skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes until bubbles form and the edges look set.
7.  **Flip:** Flip gently and cook for 1-2 more minutes until golden brown.
8.  **Serve:** Serve with warm maple syrup and a few extra fresh peach slices.

RECIPE: Peach Salad with Tomatoes & Beets (peach-salad-with-tomatoes-and-beets.md)
CUISINES: Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/peach-salad-with-tomatoes-and-beets/
SOURCE: Adapted from MyRecipes, Peach Salad with Tomatoes and Beets
SOURCE_URL: http://www.myrecipes.com/recipe/peach-salad-tomatoes-beets
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 medium golden beets, scrubbed, tops trimmed
  - 2 medium ripe tomatoes, cored
  - 3 medium ripe but firm peaches, pitted and sliced
  - 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, divided
  - 1 tbsp honey
  - 1 medium shallot, thinly sliced
  - 2 oz goat cheese, crumbled
  - 3 tbsp fresh mint leaves, torn if large
  - 2 tsp fresh thyme leaves
  - Salt and black pepper, to taste
  - Water, for the covered beet baking dish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Bake the beets until a knife reaches the center easily, then cool them before layering with the peaches and tomatoes. The covered cooking keeps the beets moist; browning is not the goal. Mint, thyme and goat cheese go on at the end. Adapted from [MyRecipes’ Peach Salad with Tomatoes and Beets](https://www.myrecipes.com/recipe/peach-salad-tomatoes-beets).

## Directions

1. **Bake beets:** Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Put scrubbed beets in a small roasting dish with about 1 inch of water. Cover tightly and bake until a thin knife slides easily to the center, checking after about 50 minutes and continuing as needed, often 60–75 minutes. Keep some water in the dish; carefully add hot water if it is drying out.

2. **Cool and slice:** Remove the cover carefully, keeping away from the escaping steam, and lift beets from the water. Cool until comfortable to handle, rub off skins, trim roots and cut into 1/4-inch slices. Spread slices on a plate and let them cool fully before assembling; allow roughly 20–30 minutes total cooling, longer if needed.

3. **Prepare dressing and fruit:** While beets cool, whisk oil, half the measured lemon juice, honey and shallot together. Season to taste. Slice tomatoes into 1/4-inch rounds. Pit and slice peaches and toss gently with the remaining half of the lemon juice.

4. **Assemble:** Layer cool beet and tomato slices on a wide platter and season lightly with salt and pepper. Arrange peach slices over them and spoon over the shallot dressing without stirring the fragile layers.

5. **Finish:** Scatter with goat cheese, mint and thyme. Serve promptly so the herbs remain fresh and the fruit holds its shape.

RECIPE: Peanut Noodles (peanut-noodles.md)
CUISINES: Chinese, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/peanut-noodles/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Noodles (spaghetti, angel hair, or wheat noodles)
  - 1/2 cup Peanut Butter (natural or creamy)
  - 3 tbsp Soy Sauce
  - 2 tbsp Rice Vinegar
  - 1 tbsp Sesame Oil
  - 1 tbsp Honey or Brown Sugar
  - 3 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Ginger, grated
  - 1/4 tsp Red Pepper Flakes (adjust to taste)
  - 1/4 to 1/2 cup Warm Water (to achieve sauce consistency)
  - 2 Green Onions, sliced
  - 1/4 cup Fresh Cilantro, chopped
  - Sesame seeds for garnish
  - Lime Wedges
  - Roasted Peanuts, chopped (optional)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Peanut noodles are Chinese-American comfort food born from the post-WWII boom when peanut butter became accessible in Chinese restaurants. What started as a Chinatown fusion dish is now everywhere - and for good reason. It's simultaneously cold (for summer), warm (for any season), endlessly customizable, and tastes just as good the next day. The sauce comes together in one bowl and clings to whatever noodles you use. Balance is key: the peanut butter needs enough acid (vinegar) and salt (soy) to not taste heavy.

## Directions

1. **Make the Sauce:** In a small bowl, whisk together peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey, minced garlic, ginger, and red pepper flakes. The mixture will be thick. Whisk in warm water a little at a time until you reach the consistency you want - think thickened pasta sauce that clings to noodles, not a soup. Taste and adjust for salt, heat, and acid.

2. **Cook the Noodles:** Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add noodles and cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain well - don't rinse (the starch helps the sauce cling). If making this ahead, toss drained noodles with 1 tsp sesame oil to prevent sticking.

3. **Combine:** In a large bowl, add warm or room-temperature noodles. Pour peanut sauce over the noodles and toss until every strand is coated. If the sauce seems too thick, add a few splashes of warm water.

4. **Finish:** Sprinkle with sliced green onions, fresh cilantro, sesame seeds, and roasted peanuts if using. Serve with lime wedges on the side.

5. **To Serve Cold:** Let the dressed noodles cool to room temperature (or chill for up to 4 hours). The sauce will continue to coat as it cools. If it tightens, add a splash of warm water before serving.

**Warm or Cold:** Eat immediately while warm, or chill and serve cold the next day. Both are completely valid.

**Customization:** Top with shredded carrots, cucumber, steamed edamame, or blanched broccoli. This is a base - build on it.

RECIPE: Pear & Spinach Salad (pear-and-spinach-salad.md)
CUISINES: Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pear-and-spinach-salad/
SOURCE: Adapted from Chowhound, Pear and Spinach Salad
SOURCE_URL: https://www.chowhound.com/recipes/pear-and-spinach-salad-27663
INGREDIENTS:
  - 5 cups baby spinach, washed if needed and dried
  - 1 large ripe but firm Bosc pear, cored and thinly sliced
  - 1/4 red onion, thinly sliced
  - 2 tbsp Dijon mustard
  - 2 tbsp red wine vinegar
  - 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 1 tbsp honey
  - 2 tbsp water, for the dressing
  - Salt and black pepper, to taste
  - Ice water, for soaking onion, discarded afterward
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A strong honey-Dijon dressing needs only a light hand on baby spinach. Soak the onion while preparing everything else, dry it well and slice the pear just before tossing. Taste a bite with fruit before adding more dressing. Adapted from [Chowhound’s Pear and Spinach Salad](https://www.chowhound.com/recipes/pear-and-spinach-salad-27663).

## Directions

1. **Soak onion:** Put thinly sliced onion in ice water for 10 minutes. Meanwhile wash and dry spinach if needed and prepare the dressing. Drain onion and pat thoroughly dry.

2. **Whisk dressing:** Combine Dijon, vinegar, the measured dressing water, olive oil and honey. Whisk until smooth. Add salt and pepper to taste; the mustard already contains salt.

3. **Assemble:** Core and thinly slice pear. Put spinach, pear and dry onion in a wide bowl. Start with about one-third of the mixed dressing and lift gently to coat. Taste a leaf with pear, then add more dressing only as needed; reserve any excess.

4. **Serve:** Adjust black pepper if desired and divide among side plates. Serve immediately while spinach retains its texture.

RECIPE: Peking Duck (peking-duck-an-easy-home-version.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/peking-duck-an-easy-home-version/
SOURCE: Adapted from redhousespice.com
SOURCE_URL: https://redhousespice.com/peking-duck/comment-page-8/#comments
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 Whole Duck (5.5 lbs)
  - 2 tbsp Maltose (or Honey)
  - 1/2 cup Boiling Water
  - 1 tsp Rice Vinegar (The Acid Balance)
  - 2 Scallions, 1 head Garlic
  - 2 Apples, quartered
  - 4 Star Anise, 4 Bay Leaves
  - 2 pieces Cassia Cinnamon
  - 3 tbsp Sweet Bean Sauce (Tian Mian Jiang)
  - 1 tsp Sugar + 1 tsp Duck Fat
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Peking duck from Beijing is famous for its crackling-crisp skin. The secret: pour boiling water over the raw duck to tighten the skin, brush with maltose syrup, then air-dry uncovered in the fridge for 24-48 hours. This separates the skin from the fat layer so it bakes into a glass-like, shatteringly crisp texture. Roast on a wire rack for even air circulation. Serve the skin and meat separately with thin pancakes, scallions, cucumber, and sweet bean sauce.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Pat duck **bone-dry**. Rub 2 tbsp salt over the skin and cavity. Let rest for 1 hour.
2.  **The Blanch:** Pour 6 cups of boiling water slowly over the entire duck skin (both sides). You will see the skin tighten instantly.
3.  **The Lacquer:** Whisk maltose, boiling water, and vinegar. Brush a heavy layer over the duck. Let dry for 1 hour, then brush a second layer.
4.  **The Dehydrate:** Place duck on a wire rack over a tray. **Refrigerate uncovered for 24-48 hours** until the skin feels like parchment paper.
5.  **Thermal Prep:** Bring duck to room temp. Stuff the cavity with aromatics and apples. Seal the opening with skewers.
6.  **Bake:** Preheat convection oven to 390°F (or 425°F conventional). Roast for 15 minutes.
7.  **Roast:** Lower heat to 350°F. Roast for another 60 minutes until the internal temp is 165°F and the skin is dark mahogany. Rest for 15 minutes.
8.  **The Sauce:** Simmer sweet bean sauce, sugar, and a spoonful of rendered duck fat until bubbling.
9.  **Serve:** Slice the skin and meat separately. Serve with thin pancakes, julienned scallions, and cucumber.

## Cooking Notes

If maltose is unavailable, the saved source gives two parts honey mixed with one part hot water as an alternative coating.

RECIPE: Whole-Berry Cranberry Sauce (perfect-cranberry-sauce.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/perfect-cranberry-sauce/
SOURCE: Adapted from damndelicious.net
SOURCE_URL: https://damndelicious.net/2013/11/15/cranberry-orange-sauce/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 340 g fresh or frozen cranberries, divided
  - 150 g granulated sugar
  - 3/4 cup (180 ml) water
  - 1 strip orange peel, about 2 by 1 inches, without white pith
  - 1/16 tsp fine salt
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Whole-berry cranberry sauce brings tart fruit to a rich holiday plate. This version cooks part of the fruit first, then adds the rest briefly so some tender pieces remain. Orange peel adds aroma rather than replacing the cranberries' acidity. Expect a spoonable sauce after chilling, not the firm shape of canned cranberry jelly.

## Directions

1. **Sort and divide:** Rinse and drain fresh cranberries, discarding spoiled berries. Set aside 85 g of the total for the later addition; the other 255 g go in first. Keep frozen berries frozen until each addition. Prepare a thin orange-peel strip with no thick white pith.
2. **Dissolve the sugar:** In a 2-quart saucepan, combine water, sugar, orange peel and salt. Heat over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves and the liquid begins to simmer.
3. **Cook the first berries:** Add the 255 g cranberries, return to a gentle boil and reduce heat to a steady simmer. Cook about eight to ten minutes, stirring occasionally, until most berries have split. Keep clear of hot splashes; do not crush every berry smooth.
4. **Tenderize the remaining berries:** Add the reserved 85 g and simmer another three to five minutes, or until those berries are tender when pressed with a spoon. Some may retain their shape. The hot sauce should still flow; it will thicken as it cools. Remove the orange-peel strip.
5. **Cool and chill:** Put a small spoonful on a cool plate to assess flavor and body once cool enough to taste. Transfer the main batch to a shallow heatproof container and refrigerate promptly, loosely covered while cooling and covered fully once cold. Allow about two and a half hours to chill, or refrigerate overnight. Stir gently before serving two to three tablespoons per person.

## Cranberry-orange variation

Replace the 180 ml water with **120 ml water and 60 ml orange juice**. Omit the peel strip, then stir **one teaspoon finely grated orange zest** into the finished sauce after taking it off heat. Keep the same fruit and sugar quantities. This retains the citrus-forward option in one recipe; two tablespoons of zest are unnecessary for this batch.

## A tarter variation

Use **100 g sugar** instead of 150 g if the meal needs a sharper condiment. Expect a different sweetness and possibly looser body, and judge a chilled spoonful. Do not assume removing sugar leaves identical texture or turns this into a shelf-stable preserve.

RECIPE: Cream Cheese Mashed Potatoes (perfect-mashed-potatoes.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/perfect-mashed-potatoes/
SOURCE: Adapted from Myrecipes.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.myrecipes.com/recipe/perfect-mashed-potatoes
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1360 g peeled Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into even 1-inch pieces
  - 3 L cold water, or enough to cover potatoes by about 1 inch
  - 12 g salt, for the cooking water
  - 75 g unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
  - 115 g cream cheese, cut into small pieces
  - 3/4 cup (180 ml) half-and-half, plus up to 1/4 cup (60 ml) more if needed
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, for finishing, divided
  - 1/2 tsp coarsely ground black pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Cream cheese gives these American-style mashed potatoes a rich, mildly tangy finish. Yukon Golds suit a creamy mash; use a ricer for a fine texture or accept small pieces from a hand masher. Cook the potatoes completely before mashing, then fold in the warm dairy only as much as needed. There is no universally correct number of seconds on an electric mixer.

## Directions

1. **Cut and cover:** Peel and trim enough potatoes to weigh 1360 g, then cut into even one-inch pieces. Briefly rinse, put in a large pot and add about three liters cold water to cover by an inch. Add the twelve grams of cooking-water salt.
2. **Simmer until fully tender:** Bring to a boil, reduce to a steady simmer and cook about eighteen to twenty-two minutes. Test several pieces with a knife and taste a cooled piece; the centers should be fully soft, not just puncturable. While they cook, warm butter, cream cheese and the initial 180 ml half-and-half together over low heat, stirring until the butter melts and the cream cheese softens. Do not boil the dairy.
3. **Drain and dry briefly:** Drain thoroughly. Return the potatoes to the pot over low heat for one to two minutes, shaking or turning gently until the surfaces lose their wet sheen. Remove from heat before they brown or stick.
4. **Mash gently:** Pass hot potatoes through a ricer or use a hand masher until the large pieces are gone. Fold in the warm dairy mixture in two additions with a spatula. Stop when combined. If too stiff, warm and add the optional extra half-and-half a tablespoon at a time until it holds a soft mound.
5. **Taste and serve:** Fold in pepper and half the finishing salt, then taste; add the rest only if needed. The cooking-water salt was largely drained away, while cream cheese contributes its own seasoning. Serve about three-quarters of a cup per person alongside the main.

## A short hold

For up to about thirty minutes, keep the hot mash covered in a heatproof bowl over gently simmering water, with the bowl above the water. Check that the mash stays above 140°F / 60°C. Fold once if needed and adjust with a spoonful of warm milk; avoid repeated stirring or direct burner heat that scorches the base. Longer storage needs cooling and reheating as described above.

RECIPE: Peruvian-Style Beef Empanadas (peruvian-style-beef-empanadas.md)
CUISINES: South American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/peruvian-style-beef-empanadas/
SOURCE: Adapted from a family recipe discussion
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Beef filling ---
  - 2 tsp olive oil
  - 1/2 lb (225 g) 85/15 ground beef
  - 1/2 cup yellow onion, finely chopped
  - 2 tbsp yellow bell pepper, finely diced
  - 1 garlic clove, minced
  - 1/2 tsp ground cumin
  - 1/2 tsp sweet paprika
  - 1/4 tsp dried oregano
  - ground turmeric, a small pinch
  - 1 tsp tomato paste
  - 1–2 tbsp unsalted beef broth
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt
  - 1/8 tsp ground black pepper
  - additional fine salt, to taste, only if needed
  - --- Pastry and optional glaze ---
  - 12 5-inch empanada discs labeled for baking, one 12-count package at the original yield; thawed as directed on the package
  - water for sealing, as needed
  - 1 large egg, optional
  - 1 tsp water for egg wash, optional
  - --- To serve ---
  - 1 lime, cut into wedges
  - 1 tsp powdered sugar, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Empanadas take many forms across Latin America, including Peru's baked savory pastries. This mild family adaptation uses beef, onion and warming spices, without hard-boiled eggs, olives or raisins. Cool the filling before folding so the pastry stays easy to handle and bakes with a crisp base.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Thaw the discs according to their package before starting; keep covered and refrigerated until needed. Finely chop the vegetables so they fit comfortably inside the pastry. Set out a shallow heatproof dish for cooling the filling and line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
2. **Brown the beef:** Set out olive oil and 85/15 ground beef. Heat the oil in a 10- to 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the beef in a thin layer and leave it undisturbed for about 2 minutes, until browned underneath. Break it into small crumbles and cook another 4–6 minutes, stirring, until cooked through to 160°F / 71°C. Spoon off pooled fat, leaving a thin film in the pan. Transfer the cooked beef to a clean bowl.
3. **Soften the vegetables:** Lower the heat to medium and add yellow onion and yellow bell pepper to the same skillet. Cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until fully softened and the onion is translucent with lightly golden edges. Lower the heat if the browned bits start to blacken.
4. **Bloom the spices:** Lower the heat to medium-low. Stir in garlic clove, ground cumin, sweet paprika, dried oregano, and ground turmeric for about 30 seconds, just until fragrant; do not let the garlic or paprika scorch.
5. **Cook the tomato paste:** Stir in tomato paste for about 1 minute, until it darkens slightly and coats the vegetables.
6. **Finish the filling:** Return the beef and add unsalted beef broth, fine salt, and ground black pepper, using the lower end of the broth range first. Scrape up the browned bits and stir over medium heat for 1–2 minutes. Add the remaining broth only if the filling seems dry. Stop when moist crumbles cling together lightly and a spatula drawn across the pan leaves no puddle.
7. **Taste and cool:** Taste the fully cooked filling and add additional fine salt only if needed. Spread it in a thin layer in the shallow dish and refrigerate promptly for about 20–30 minutes, or until cool throughout; stir once to release trapped warmth. Do not wait for a deep bowl to cool on the counter. While it chills, heat the oven to 400°F / 200°C conventional, or the temperature specified by the disc package, with a rack in the middle.
8. **Portion the filling:** Work with 5-inch empanada discs labeled for baking, keeping unused discs covered and cool. Start with 1 1/2 tablespoons of cooled filling per disc, then add a little more up to about 2 tablespoons only if it closes easily. Leave a clean 1/2-inch border. Share the filling across the batch; do not stretch the pastry or force in surplus filling. Refrigerate any extra filling separately.
9. **Seal:** Lightly moisten the clean border with water for sealing. Fold each disc over the filling, gently press out trapped air, then press and crimp firmly with a fork. Set on the lined sheet with about 1 inch between empanadas. If the pastry becomes soft or sticky, refrigerate the assembled tray for 10 minutes before baking.
10. **Glaze if desired:** For the optional glaze, beat large egg (if using) and water for egg wash (if using) together and brush a thin layer over the tops. Omit both for an unglazed finish. Discard leftover wash. Cut one small slit in the top of each empanada to vent steam.
11. **Bake:** Bake for about 20–25 minutes, rotating the tray halfway through, until the pastry is golden on top and underneath and the filling reaches 165°F / 74°C. Follow the disc package if it specifies a different temperature or time; begin checking at its earliest stated time. Use a second sheet if needed rather than crowding; larger batches need additional trays and time, not a higher oven temperature.
12. **Rest and serve:** Rest on a wire rack for 10 minutes before eating; the filling can be very hot. Serve with lime and powdered sugar (if using), squeezing the lime onto each bite and adding only a light dusting of sugar if using. Allow 2–3 empanadas per person with a crisp green salad, or serve individually as a snack.
