RECIPE: Philly Tuna Roll (philly-tuna-roll.md)
CUISINES: Japanese, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/philly-tuna-roll/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 230 g trimmed boneless, skinless yellowfin tuna, weighed after removing tough connective tissue; see raw-service sourcing note
  - 115 g full-fat block cream cheese, cold
  - 100 g English cucumber, weighed after removing the watery seed core
  - 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
  - 320 g (about 2 cups) prepared [Sushi Rice (Shari)](/mise/recipes/master-sushi-rice)
  - 4 full sheets unseasoned roasted nori, about 19 x 20 cm each; trim as directed
  - 120 ml water, for dampening hands and the knife
  - 1 tsp unseasoned rice vinegar, for the hand-dipping water
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This tuna-and-cream-cheese variation keeps its Philly name and its nori-outside wrapping. Cold cheese strips provide a defined creamy center beside cucumber; they should not be spread across the rice. Sesame goes onto the rice before rolling so it stays with the roll instead of falling off dry nori.

## Before buying raw tuna

Tell the supplier it will be eaten raw and confirm species, handling and applicable parasite controls. “Sushi-grade” alone does not establish suitability. Yellowfin has a specific FDA parasite-freezing exemption, but other raw-seafood hazards remain. Do not rely on domestic freezing, vinegar or appearance to establish raw safety. Thaw frozen tuna in the refrigerator as directed, removing vacuum packaging before refrigerator thawing.

FDA advises children, pregnant people, older adults and people with weakened immune systems to avoid raw seafood. Choose a fully cooked preparation for those diners. This roll contains fish, milk and sesame.

## Directions

1. **Prepare rice and the station:** Follow [Sushi Rice (Shari)](/mise/recipes/master-sushi-rice), weigh 320 g for this recipe and refrigerate surplus rice promptly. Let the rolling portion become barely warm during final preparation. Wrap a clean mat in food-safe plastic film. Mix the hand-dipping water and vinegar; it reduces sticking and is not a sanitizer. Do not dip a raw-filling-coated hand or blade into this clean water. Wash hands and clean the blade before returning to it, use a separate damp cloth for wiping the cutting blade, and replace the water if contaminated.
2. **Prepare cheese and cucumber:** During the rice process, cut cold cream cheese into strips about 6 mm thick. Wash the cucumber, remove its watery core and weigh 100 g, then cut into slender matchsticks and pat dry. Divide cheese into four equal portions of about 29 g and cucumber into four 25 g portions. Refrigerate, keeping the cheese firm.
3. **Prepare fish near rolling:** With separate clean equipment, remove tough visible connective tissue, weigh the listed usable amount of tuna and cut across the muscle grain where visible into strips about 6–10 mm thick. Shorter strips can be laid end to end. Divide into four equal portions of about 58 g and refrigerate. Clean the work area and hands before handling the rolling equipment.
4. **Portion rice and nori:** Divide the rice into four 80 g portions. Trim the first nori sheet to about 19 x 15 cm, saving its dry offcut airtight for another use. Keep the other sheets untrimmed until the first closure check. Place one rectangle shiny side down with the 19 cm edge nearest you. Lightly dampen fingers, shake off excess water and spread one rice portion evenly, leaving a 1 cm bare strip at the far edge. Scatter one quarter of the sesame seeds onto the rice.
5. **Fill and roll:** Take out one portion each of tuna, cheese and cucumber. Using clean utensils, arrange them in an even horizontal line about 4 cm from the near edge; keep their ends aligned and avoid a mound in the middle. Lift the mat's near edge and tuck nori and rice over the filling. Pull the mat out of the way while rolling forward so it stays outside. Close on the bare edge, barely moistening it if needed, and press gently through the mat. Check the first roll's closure, then trim the remaining sheets to match and proceed with the other three; no rice ridge is needed.
6. **Cut and serve:** Place seam-side down briefly while preparing the knife. Wipe and lightly dampen a sharp blade. Cut each roll in half, then halve each section twice, producing eight pieces per roll; wipe and dampen the blade as needed between cuts. Serve promptly as 32 pieces, about two main portions or four appetizer portions. Keep unused raw fish and cheese portions refrigerated during the work.

RECIPE: Pho Bo (Beef Pho) (pho-bo-beef-pho.md)
CUISINES: Vietnamese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pho-bo-beef-pho/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 lbs Beef Marrow Bones, cut into 3-inch pieces
  - 2 lbs Beef Brisket, whole piece
  - 2 large Yellow Onions, unpeeled and halved
  - 1 (4-inch) piece Fresh Ginger, halved lengthwise
  - 4 Star Anise, whole
  - 1 Cinnamon Stick (3-inch, Vietnamese preferred)
  - 6 whole Cloves
  - 1 tbsp Coriander Seeds
  - 1 Cardamom Pod
  - 6 quarts Cold Water
  - 3 tbsp Fish Sauce, plus more to taste
  - 1 tbsp Sugar
  - 1 tbsp Kosher Salt
  - 1 lb Dried Rice Noodles (banh pho, medium width)
  - 1/2 lb Eye of Round, sliced paper-thin against the grain
  - Bean Sprouts, for serving
  - Fresh Thai Basil, for serving
  - Fresh Cilantro, for serving
  - Lime Wedges, for serving
  - Thinly Sliced Jalapenos, for serving
  - Hoisin Sauce and Sriracha, for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The soul of great pho bo lives in the charred aromatics and the long, patient simmer. Blackening the onions and ginger under the broiler builds a smoky sweetness that no shortcut can replicate. The most common mistake is boiling the broth too hard, which turns it cloudy and greasy. Keep it at a bare simmer -- you want lazy bubbles, not a rolling boil. Parboiling the bones first and rinsing them clean is the single most important step for a clear, golden broth.

## Directions

1.  **Parboil the Bones:** Place the marrow bones and brisket in a large stockpot. Cover with cold water and bring to a vigorous boil for 10 minutes. Drain, rinse the bones and meat under cold water, and scrub the pot clean. This removes impurities and is essential for a clear broth.

2.  **Char the Aromatics:** While the bones parboil, place the halved onions and ginger cut-side down on a sheet pan. Broil on high for 12-15 minutes until deeply blackened and softened. The char is critical for flavor.

3.  **Toast the Spices:** In a dry skillet over medium heat, toast the star anise, cinnamon stick, cloves, coriander seeds, and cardamom pod for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Place them in a spice sachet or cheesecloth bundle.

4.  **Build the Broth:** Return the cleaned bones and brisket to the scrubbed pot. Add 6 quarts cold water, charred aromatics, and spice bundle. Bring to a boil, then immediately reduce to the gentlest possible simmer. Skim any foam that rises during the first 30 minutes.

5.  **Remove the Brisket:** After 1.5-2 hours, check the brisket with a chopstick. When it slides through with little resistance, transfer the brisket to an ice bath for 10 minutes (this firms the meat for slicing), then refrigerate. Continue simmering the bones for 2 more hours.

6.  **Season the Broth:** After a total of 4 hours, strain the broth through a fine-mesh strainer lined with cheesecloth. Discard solids. Stir in the fish sauce, sugar, and salt. Taste and adjust -- the broth should be deeply savory with a hint of sweetness.

7.  **Prepare the Noodles:** Soak the rice noodles in warm water for 20-25 minutes until pliable. Just before serving, cook in rapidly boiling water for 30-60 seconds until tender. Drain immediately.

8.  **Prepare the Meats:** Slice the chilled brisket across the grain into thin pieces and reheat it in simmering broth to 165°F / 74°C throughout. For the fully cooked eye of round, cook the slices in simmering broth before assembly, checking representative pieces with a suitable thin-tip thermometer for at least 145°F / 63°C, then allow a 3-minute rest before serving. Color change or brief contact with hot broth alone does not establish doneness; if the thin slices cannot be reliably measured, do not assume this endpoint has been verified.

9.  **Assemble:** Divide noodles among deep bowls. Top with the reheated brisket and cooked, rested eye of round. Ladle hot broth over the meat and noodles. Serve immediately with a platter of bean sprouts, Thai basil, cilantro, lime wedges, jalapenos, hoisin, and sriracha.

RECIPE: Quick Refrigerator-Pickled Red Onions (pickled-red-onions.md)
CUISINES: Mexican-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pickled-red-onions/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 200 g red onion, peeled and very thinly sliced into half-moons
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) apple cider or distilled white vinegar, labeled 5% acidity
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) water
  - 1 tbsp (12 g) granulated sugar
  - 1 tsp (6 g) fine or pickling salt
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Thin slicing makes a quick pickle practical: the brine reaches a greater share of each slice in a short time. The result is a tart refrigerated condiment, not a fermented onion or a shelf-stable preserve. Drain the portion you use so its vinegar accents a taco without soaking the bread.

## Directions

1. **Slice and pack:** Peel and rinse the onion, trim its ends and slice about 1/16–1/8 inch thick. Pack into a clean heatproof pint jar, leaving roughly 1/2 inch at the top.
2. **Heat the brine:** Put the measured vinegar, water, sugar and salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer, stirring until dissolved, then remove from heat.
3. **Cover the onion:** Pour hot brine over the onion and gently press it down with a clean spoon. Leave about 1/2 inch headspace. Use a narrower container or additional same-ratio brine if coverage is inadequate; do not add plain water.
4. **Refrigerate and develop:** Cover with a clean lid and refrigerate promptly on a heatproof pad, with space around the jar. After about thirty minutes, taste a drained slice once cool enough. It will still have some raw bite; longer refrigerated time, ideally until the next day, makes the flavor more even.
5. **Use:** Lift out only the needed portion with a clean fork and drain. The full batch yields approximately 1 1/2 cups drained onions; use a tablespoon or two as a condiment, leaving the rest submerged and refrigerated.

RECIPE: Pizza Beans (pizza-beans.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pizza-beans/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cans (15 oz each) Giant White Beans (Butter or Gigante), rinsed
  - 1 tbsp Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 1 Yellow Onion, diced
  - 2 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1 (28 oz) can Crushed Tomatoes
  - 1 bunch Lacinato Kale, chopped
  - 8 oz Mozzarella Cheese, shredded
  - 1/3 cup Grated Parmesan
  - 1 tsp Dried Oregano
  - Salt and Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Tex-Mex inspired skillet dish swaps pizza dough for protein-rich white beans, creating a comfort food that's lighter but equally satisfying. Cooking kale just until wilted preserves a slight bite that contrasts with the creamy beans and melted cheese. Giant butter beans or gigante beans work best for their substantial, meaty texture.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 450°F.
2.  **Base:** Heat oil in an oven-safe heavy skillet (cast iron is best). Sauté the onion until soft (8 mins). Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
3.  **Greens:** Add the kale to the pan and stir until it just turns bright green and collapses.
4.  **Simmer:** Stir in the tomatoes, beans, and oregano. Season with salt and pepper. Let it simmer for 5 minutes to marry the flavors.
5.  **Assemble:** Top with mozzarella and Parmesan.
6.  **Bake:** Transfer the skillet to the oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and has golden brown spots.
7.  **Serve:** Let rest for 5 minutes. Scoop into bowls and serve with crusty bread.

RECIPE: Pizza (pizza.md)
CUISINES: Italian, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pizza/
SOURCE: Family recipe
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Dough and handling ---
  - 600 g prepared, risen pizza dough, at stretching temperature; divide into two equal balls
  - flour, for dusting the work surface and peel, as needed
  - olive oil, for lightly oiling the pans, if using the pan route, optional
  - --- Toppings for both pizzas ---
  - 1 cup thick pizza sauce
  - 12 oz whole-milk low-moisture mozzarella, grated
  - 60 g ready-to-eat pepperoni slices
  - 120 g fresh pineapple, cut into small pieces and blotted dry
  - 40 g baby spinach, washed if needed and dried thoroughly
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Pepperoni, pineapple and spinach bring salty, sweet and fresh contrasts to a generous cheese pizza. Keep the toppings dry and check the underside before serving: a browned rim can hide a soft center. This batch makes two 12-inch pizzas for four portions, served as each pizza comes out of the oven.

## Directions

1. **Choose the baking route:** Start with fully risen dough that is relaxed enough to stretch. Follow its recipe or package for thawing, proofing and warming before this schedule. Heat the oven to 500°F with a middle rack. For the pan route, keep two metal pans with enough flat area for 12-inch pizzas at room temperature; check that they are rated for 500°F. For the stone route, put a suitably rated stone in the cold oven and heat it for 1 hour; have a peel that fits the pizza ready. Neither route uses parchment.
2. **Divide the toppings:** Make two equal sets of toppings before shaping. Each pizza gets 1/2 cup sauce, 6 oz mozzarella, 30 g pepperoni, 60 g pineapple and 20 g spinach. Cut pineapple into approximately 1/4-inch pieces and blot away surface liquid. Keep the second set of perishable toppings refrigerated until needed.
3. **Shape on a cool surface:** Have prepared, risen pizza dough, flour, and olive oil (if using) ready. Divide the dough into two 300 g balls. Cover one while stretching the other to a 12-inch round with a slightly thicker rim. If it springs back, cover and rest 10 minutes. Transfer the bare round to a lightly oiled room-temperature pan, or to a lightly floured peel for the stone route. On a peel, check that it slides freely before topping.
4. **Top one pizza:** Use one half each of thick pizza sauce, whole-milk low-moisture mozzarella, ready-to-eat pepperoni slices, and fresh pineapple on the first pizza. Spread its sauce leaving a 3/4-inch border, then distribute the cheese, pepperoni and pineapple evenly. Reserve the spinach. If using a peel, check that the pizza still moves freely and launch promptly; do not leave a dressed pizza waiting on the peel.
5. **Bake and wilt the spinach:** Reserve one half of baby spinach for this pizza and the other half for the second. Put the pan on the oven rack, or slide the pizza directly from the peel onto the stone. Start checking after 10 minutes; allow roughly 12–15 minutes total. When the rim is nearly browned and the cheese is bubbling, pull the pizza out safely with its pan or peel, scatter on its spinach portion and return it for the final 1–2 minutes. The spinach should wilt and the underside should be browned, with a set center that supports a slice. Check underneath with a spatula or peel; a dark rim alone does not establish doneness. Extend the bake if needed.
6. **Serve and repeat:** Move the first pizza to a rack for 2 minutes, then slice and serve. Keep the oven on; let a stone recover for about 5 minutes between pizzas. Shape and top the second pizza on its own room-temperature pan or prepared peel, using the remaining topping portions, and repeat the bake. Never assemble dough directly on a hot pan or reach over a hot stone.

## Timing and leftovers

With ready-to-stretch dough, allow about 60–70 minutes for the pan route or 1 hour 40 minutes for the stone route. Oven heating overlaps topping preparation; two pizzas still need two baking rounds. Cold or frozen dough needs its own preparation before this schedule.

Refrigerate perishable leftovers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C, at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F / 74°C throughout.

RECIPE: Play-Dough (play-dough.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/play-dough/
SOURCE: Adapted from Gracy Ann
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup All-Purpose Flour
  - 1/2 cup Fine Salt
  - 2 tsp Cream of Tartar
  - 1 cup Water
  - 1 tbsp Vegetable Oil
  - Food Coloring or Liquid Watercolors
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Homemade play-dough is a rainy-day project that's actually food science at work - a cooked dough that stays pliable for months. The cream of tartar is the key: it acts as a preservative and keeps the dough soft, so it won't crack or harden in an airtight container. The oil and salt also help preserve texture.

## Directions

1.  **Combine:** In a medium non-stick saucepan, whisk together the flour, salt, and cream of tartar.
2.  **Emulsify:** Add the water, oil, and food coloring. Whisk until no lumps remain.
3.  **The Cook:** Place over medium heat. Stir constantly with a wooden spoon for 3-5 minutes.
4.  **The Pull:** The mixture will look like a liquid, then suddenly clump together. Continue stirring until the dough pulls away from the sides of the pan and forms a single, non-sticky ball.
5.  **Knead:** Remove from heat and place on a clean surface. Once cool enough to touch, knead for 1 minute until perfectly smooth.
6.  **Store:** Store in an airtight container for up to 6 months to maintain the "Bounce."

RECIPE: Poke Bowl Bar (poke-bowl-bar.md)
CUISINES: Hawaiian-inspired, Japanese-inspired, Korean-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/poke-bowl-bar/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Seafood and dressing ---
  - 680 g total prepared raw seafood: yellowfin tuna, salmon or shucked scallop adductor muscles; choose one or split the total between two, following the sourcing note
  - 3 tbsp soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1 tsp unseasoned rice vinegar
  - 1/2 tsp finely grated fresh ginger
  - 1/2 tsp sriracha, optional
  - 2 tsp fresh lime juice, divided
  - --- Rice and vegetables ---
  - 4 cups prepared [Sushi Rice (Shari)](/mise/recipes/master-sushi-rice), or the same total of plain cooked rice and shari
  - 1 avocado, flesh sliced
  - 1/8 tsp fine salt, for the avocado, only if needed
  - 1/2 recipe [Oi Muchim (Korean Cucumber Salad)](/mise/recipes/korean-pickled-cucumbers), prepared and lifted from excess dressing
  - 150 g frozen unsalted shelled edamame, cooked according to the package and chilled
  - 150 g English cucumber, diced
  - 50 g carrot, shredded
  - 50 g red cabbage, finely shredded
  - 1 jalapeno, thinly sliced, optional
  - --- Garnishes and table condiments ---
  - 1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips
  - 1 tbsp toasted white sesame seeds
  - 1 tbsp toasted black sesame seeds
  - 2 scallions, thinly sliced
  - 2 tbsp chopped cilantro or microgreens, optional
  - 1 tsp furikake, optional; check the label
  - 1 tbsp extra soy sauce, optional for the table
  - 2 tbsp prepared spicy mayonnaise, optional; check the label
  - 1 tsp prepared wasabi, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Poke is seasoned cut seafood from Hawaii; this multi-topping bar is a contemporary bowl format. Choosing two seafoods or rice types changes the variety, not the total portion needed. Cucumber salad, soy and furikake each add seasoning, so offer them separately and start lightly.

## Raw seafood sourcing

Tell the supplier the seafood will be served raw and ask for its species, cold-chain handling and applicable parasite-control information. “Sushi-grade” and “sashimi-grade” labels alone do not establish suitability. For wild salmon, require documented supplier parasite-destruction freezing; fresh wild-caught fish is not automatically preferable for raw service. For farmed salmon, obtain supplier documentation of either parasite-destruction freezing or qualifying raising and feeding conditions; a farmed label alone is insufficient. Yellowfin tuna and scallop products consisting only of the shucked adductor muscle have specific parasite-freezing exemptions, not a general guarantee of raw safety. Do not use a household freezer as an assumed substitute for a documented commercial process.

Freezing does not remove every seafood hazard, and this dressing is not a safety treatment. FDA advises children, pregnant people, older adults and people with weakened immune systems to avoid raw seafood; choose a fully cooked meal for those diners. Follow supplier refrigerator-thawing instructions and remove vacuum packaging before refrigerator thawing.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the rice and cucumber salad:** Make [Sushi Rice (Shari)](/mise/recipes/master-sushi-rice) and measure four cooked cups for the bar, refrigerating any extra promptly. For two rice types, use two cups shari and two cups safely prepared [Plain Short-Grain White Rice](/mise/recipes/steamed-white-rice). During the rice process, make a half batch of [Oi Muchim](/mise/recipes/korean-pickled-cucumbers), starting with 300 g cucumber, then lift the finished half batch from excess dressing for the four bowls.
2. **Prepare edamame and vegetables during rice soaking/cooking:** Cook shelled edamame early in the rice process according to its package, drain and chill promptly in a shallow container. Wash and cut the fresh cucumber, carrot, cabbage, scallions and optional jalapeno and herbs with clean equipment. Slice avocado last and coat with 1 tsp lime juice, adding the measured optional salt only after tasting. Refrigerate vegetables until needed and keep nori dry.
3. **Mix the dressing:** Whisk soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, rice vinegar, ginger and the remaining 1 tsp lime juice. Taste before any seafood touches it. Leave out sriracha for a mild dressing or add it now; for one mild and one spicy seafood bowl, divide the clean dressing in proportion to the seafood weights and add sriracha only to the spicy portion.
4. **Cut and dress seafood while rice cools:** During the final rice cooling period, with separate clean equipment, cut cold tuna or salmon into 1/2-inch cubes, or slice scallop muscles about 1/4 inch thick. Divide the dressing among the chosen seafoods in proportion to their weights and refrigerate for about 5–10 minutes. Keep each type in its own bowl with its own spoon. This short wait seasons the seafood; it does not cook it or establish safety.
5. **Set out and assemble:** Nest small seafood bowls in ice, with meltwater unable to enter them. Check the seafood with a clean food thermometer to confirm 40°F / 4°C or below; clean the probe between seafoods and return portions to the refrigerator if the ice setup cannot keep them cold. Set out the rice barely warm and the prepared vegetables cold, with separate spoons and garnishes alongside. For four bowls, allow about one cup total rice and one quarter of the total seafood per person; a diner choosing two seafoods splits that portion. Lift seafood and cucumber salad from pooled dressing. Add avocado, edamame and fresh vegetables, then sesame, scallion and dry nori. Offer the measured optional garnishes and sauces sparingly. Assemble only when ready to eat and refrigerate unused rice promptly.

## Scaling the bar

Scale the total fish and rice allocation across the choices, then divide dressing in proportion to the fish. Larger rice batches need a suitable pot or separate batches, and more fish needs additional refrigerated space and ice capacity. Allow extra preparation time; keep reserve seafood refrigerated.

RECIPE: Pork and Greens Dumplings (pork-and-greens-dumplings.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pork-and-greens-dumplings/
SOURCE: thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/dumpling-recipe-youll-ever-need/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 lbs green leafy vegetable (like shepherd’s purse, baby bok choy, or napa cabbage)
  - 1 ½ pounds ground pork (can substitute ground chicken or beef, as long as they aren’t too lean)
  - 2/3 cup shaoxing wine (or dry cooking sherry)
  - ½ cup neutral oil (such as canola, vegetable, or avocado oil)
  - 3 tablespoons sesame oil
  - 1 tablespoon salt
  - 3 tablespoons soy sauce
  - ¼ teaspoon white pepper
  - 2/3 cup water (plus more for assembly)
  - 3 packages dumpling wrappers
  - 2 tbsp neutral oil, for pan-frying each batch if choosing that method
  - Water, enough for the chosen cooking method
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Blanch, drain and squeeze the greens before chopping them finely. Stir the filling until cohesive, then cook a small test dumpling completely before tasting for seasoning. Wrapper counts and cooking batches depend on package size.

## Directions

1. **Prepare greens:** Wash and blanch the greens in boiling water: about one minute for delicate leaves or two minutes for cabbage or bok choy. Cool in ice water, drain and squeeze out excess water. Chop finely.

2. **Mix filling:** Combine greens, ground meat, wine, the measured half cup neutral oil, sesame oil, salt, soy sauce, white pepper and the measured two-thirds cup water. Stir vigorously for 6–8 minutes, until cohesive and paste-like.

3. **Test seasoning:** Wrap a small test dumpling and boil it until its filling reaches 160°F / 71°C for pork or beef, or 165°F / 74°C for chicken. Taste only after it is fully cooked, then adjust the remaining filling if necessary.

4. **Shape:** Dampen a wrapper edge with a little water. Add slightly less than one tablespoon filling, fold in half, then pleat and pinch to seal. Keep completed dumplings on a parchment-lined tray without touching; keep filling refrigerated during pauses.

5. **Freeze if desired:** Freeze shaped dumplings in a single layer, then transfer to a sealed freezer bag. Freeze unused wrappers in an airtight bag. This time is additional to the fresh-dumpling total.

6. **Choose a cooking method:** For boiling, bring a large pot of water to a boil, add dumplings and simmer about 6–8 minutes. For pan-frying, heat the separately measured two tablespoons neutral oil over medium-high heat, fry dumplings about two minutes, add a thin layer of water, cover and steam until the water evaporates, then uncover to crisp the bottoms. For steaming, use a lined basket above simmering water for about 8–10 minutes. Frozen dumplings need longer.

7. **Check and serve:** For every cooking method and batch, check a dumpling center for 160°F / 71°C with pork or beef, or 165°F / 74°C with chicken. Floating and browned wrappers alone do not establish doneness. Serve with soy-ginger dipping sauce, chili oil or Chinese black vinegar.

RECIPE: Pressure-Cooker Bolognese (pressure-cooker-bolognase.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pressure-cooker-bolognase/
SOURCE: Adapted from Richard Blais
SOURCE_URL: https://smile.amazon.com/Try-This-Home-Recipes-Plate-ebook/dp/B009JU6UPQ
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Pork or Veal Shoulder, chopped small
  - 1 lb Mild or Spicy Italian Sausage, bulk
  - 1 large Yellow Onion, finely chopped
  - 2 Carrots, finely diced
  - 1 stalk Celery, finely diced
  - 6 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 2 tbsp Tomato Paste
  - 1 cup Dry Red Wine (The Finishing Touch)
  - 1 can (28 oz) San Marzano Tomatoes, hand-crushed
  - 2 tbsp Balsamic Vinegar (The Acid Balance)
  - 20 Fresh Basil Leaves
  - 1 Fresh Bay Leaf
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Ragù alla Bolognese originated in Bologna in the late 18th century as a slow-cooked meat sauce. The official recipe registered with the Bologna Chamber of Commerce in 1982 specifies a soffritto base (onion, celery, carrot), ground beef, pancetta, tomato paste, wine, and milk or cream - simmered for hours until thick and meaty. This pressure cooker version shortcuts the time while maintaining depth by developing a dark fond (browned bits) when searing the meat, then deglazing with red wine to extract those flavors. Use San Marzano tomatoes if possible - they're less acidic and sweeter than regular canned tomatoes. The balsamic vinegar at the end is not traditional but adds complexity.

## Directions

1.  **The Sear:** Set pressure cooker to "Sauté" (High). Brown the pork pieces in olive oil (5 mins); remove. Brown the crumbled sausage; remove.
2.  **The Base:** Add onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft. Add garlic and bay leaf; cook for 30-45 seconds.
3.  **The Bloom:** Stir in the tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes until it turns a deep brick-red.
4.  **Deglaze:** Pour in the wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot vigorously to release the fond. Simmer for 2 minutes.
5.  **Pressure:** Return the meat to the pot. Add the crushed tomatoes. Secure the lid. Set to **High Pressure for 45 minutes**.
6.  **Reduce:** Perform a "Natural Release." Open the lid and set back to "Sauté." Simmer for 15-20 minutes until the sauce is thick and meaty.
7.  **Finish:** Stir in the fresh basil and balsamic vinegar. Taste and adjust with salt and pepper.
8.  **Serve:** Serve over [Fresh Egg Pasta](/mise/recipes/fresh-egg-pasta) with plenty of Parmesan.

RECIPE: Prohibition-Style Gin Lemon Fizz (prohibition-style-gin-lemon-fizz.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/prohibition-style-gin-lemon-fizz/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 oz London dry gin
  - 2 oz unaged mezcal (The Smoky Pulse)
  - 1.75 oz cognac
  - 3 oz Fresh Lemon Juice (The Acid Balance)
  - 0.75 oz Agave Syrup
  - 7 dashes Orange Bitters
  - 12 oz unsweetened sparkling water with lemon juice (to top)
  - Lemon Peel twists
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This cocktail showcases complex aromatic layering. The combination of herbal gin, rich cognac, and a hint of smoky mezcal creates a flavor profile that balances depth with brightness. Unsweetened sparkling water with lemon juice instead of standard soda water provides real fruit acidity that bridges the agave and botanicals. The orange bitters are added twice (in the shaker and on the surface) to ensure the aroma precedes the flavor.

## Directions

1.  **Thermal Prep:** Chill 3 highball glasses in the freezer.
2.  **The Base:** In a cocktail shaker filled with large ice cubes, combine gin, mezcal, cognac, lemon juice, agave, and 4 dashes of the orange bitters.
3.  **Aeration:** Shake vigorously for 15 seconds until the shaker is frosted and the mixture is perfectly cold.
4.  **Strain:** Double strain the mixture into the chilled highball glasses filled with fresh ice.
5.  **Effervescence:** Top each glass with 4 oz of unsweetened sparkling water with lemon juice. Stir once, very gently, to preserve the bubbles.
6.  **The Finishing Touch:** Add 1 final dash of orange bitters to the surface of each drink. Garnish with a lemon peel twist (expressed over the rim).

RECIPE: Puffy Muffin Chicken Salad (puffy-muffin-chicken-salad.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/puffy-muffin-chicken-salad/
SOURCE: Adapted from Puffy Muffin
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups raw chicken tenders (about 1 lb)
  - 1/2 cup Celery, finely diced
  - 2/3 cup Red Grapes, quartered
  - 1/4 cup Red Onion, finely minced (the crunch)
  - 1/2 cup mayonnaise
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice (The Acid Balance)
  - 1/2 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1/4 tsp Black Pepper
  - Water, as needed to cover chicken for poaching
  - Salt, optional, for the poaching water
  - Additional mayonnaise, as needed after mixing
  - Additional salt and black pepper, to taste after mixing
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Puffy Muffin is the credited source name for this pulled-chicken salad. Gently cook the tenders, pull them into bite-sized pieces, then coat with the full mayonnaise dressing. Grapes and celery stay distinct. The onion-and-lemon preparation below keeps those additions; the simpler chicken, celery, grapes and mayonnaise option remains separate. No muffin batter or baking is part of either salad.

## Directions

1. **Poach:** Put enough water to cover the raw tenders in a pot with room for the actual load; use the separate poaching salt allowance if wanted. Bring to a gentle simmer, add all the chicken and maintain that gentle heat. Begin checking around 8–10 minutes, continuing until several thick tenders reach 165°F in their centers. Thickness and the water returning to temperature determine the clock.

2. **Pull and cool:** Drain to a clean plate or shallow tray. As soon as cool enough to handle safely, use clean forks to pull the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Keep the cooked chicken and utensils away from raw chicken equipment. Spread shallowly and refrigerate promptly to cool before combining; a five-minute counter wait does not establish a chilled center.

3. **Mix the dressing:** Whisk all the listed mayonnaise, lemon juice, measured sea salt and black pepper together in a clean bowl. Keep the separate additional seasoning and mayonnaise allowances for any adjustment after mixing.

4. **Combine:** Wash the celery, grapes and onion under running water before preparing them. Add all the finely diced celery, quartered grapes and minced onion to the cooled chicken. Fold in all the dressing with a fork or spoon until evenly coated.

5. **Chill:** Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes after mixing and until cold throughout. Taste cold and use only the separate additional salt, pepper or mayonnaise allowances if wanted.

6. **Serve:** Serve cold as a salad or with separately prepared bread. The original batch is planned for four portions; use the listed portion count when scaling.

## Simpler Pulled-Chicken Variation

Keep the same two-cup raw-tender, half-cup celery, two-thirds-cup grape and half-cup mayonnaise amounts for the original batch, scaling them with the list. Omit the onion and lemon juice. Replace the measured dressing salt and pepper with salt and ground black pepper to taste. Follow the same 165°F poaching, clean pulling, prompt cooling and cold-service steps; stir the mayonnaise into the chicken, celery and grapes with a fork or spoon, then use the separate additional mayonnaise allowance only if needed.

RECIPE: Pulled Pork (pulled-pork.md)
CUISINES: American, Southern
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pulled-pork/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- The Rub ---
  - 3 tbsp dark brown sugar
  - 1 tbsp hickory smoked salt
  - 1 tbsp smoked paprika
  - 1 tsp garlic powder
  - 1 tsp onion powder
  - 1 tsp ground cumin
  - 1/2 tsp black pepper
  - --- The Pot ---
  - 4–5 lb bone-in pork shoulder (Boston butt)
  - 1 yellow onion, chopped
  - 4 cloves garlic, smashed
  - 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar
  - 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This pulled pork uses a bone-in Boston butt, hickory-smoked salt, smoky-sweet rub
and a simple vinegar–Worcestershire pot base. The
clock gets the shoulder close, but the finished meat should meet both a safe
temperature and the fork-pullable texture that makes it ready to shred. Decant
the cooking liquid before returning any of it so the meat stays moist rather
than soupy.

## Directions

1. **Mix and apply the rub:** Start with a fully thawed pork shoulder. Mix the brown sugar, hickory smoked salt, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin and pepper. Rub it over every surface of the pork. For an optional overnight seasoning, put the pork in a covered container and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or colder; this time is not included in the recipe total.
2. **Build the pot base:** Scatter the onion and garlic across the bottom of a 6-quart slow cooker. Pour in the apple cider vinegar and Worcestershire sauce.
3. **Load the shoulder:** Set the rubbed shoulder, fat cap up, on the aromatics. The lid must close fully. Do not add extra liquid; the pork releases juices as it cooks.
4. **Cook until safe and pullable:** Cover and cook on LOW for about 10–11 hours. Check the thickest pork away from the bone with an instant-read thermometer; it must reach at least 145°F / 63°C. It is ready to pull only when a fork turns and separates the meat easily and the bone slides out cleanly. If it is safe but still firm, cover and continue in 30-minute intervals until tender.
5. **Pull the pork:** Transfer the shoulder to a cutting board and rest for at least 3 minutes before pulling. Remove the bone and discard large pieces of fat or gristle. Pull or chop the pork into rough pieces.
6. **Decant, skim and moisten:** Pour the cooking liquid into a heatproof jug and skim off excess fat. Return the pork to the slow cooker. Add the defatted liquid a little at a time, tossing after each addition, until the meat is moist and flavorful rather than submerged.
7. **Serve or store promptly:** Serve with cornbread and coleslaw, or use the pork in tacos, bowls or sandwiches. For later meals, portion and chill it promptly using the storage guidance.

RECIPE: Pumpkin Breakfast Cookies (pumpkin-breakfast-cookies.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pumpkin-breakfast-cookies/
SOURCE: Adapted from Leelalicious.com
SOURCE_URL: http://leelalicious.com/pumpkin-breakfast-cookies/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Wet mixture ---
  - 1/2 cup plain pumpkin puree
  - 1/4 cup coconut oil, melted, warm but not hot when combined with eggs
  - 1/4 cup honey
  - 2 large eggs
  - --- Oats and mix-ins ---
  - 1 cup old-fashioned rolled oats
  - 1 cup quick-cooking oats
  - 1/4 cup ground flaxseed
  - 2/3 cup unsweetened dried cranberries
  - 2/3 cup pumpkin seeds (pepitas)
  - 1 tsp pumpkin pie spice
  - 1/2 tsp sea salt
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Regina’s pumpkin breakfast cookies combine rolled and quick oats with cranberries and pepitas. The mixed oat texture gives a substantial cookie, and the eggs help hold the mixture together. Flatten the scoops before baking: this dough keeps the shape you give it.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Use additional sheets or oven loads when needed; scaled dough should not be crowded onto the original sheet.
2. **Combine oil and honey:** Whisk coconut oil and honey in a small bowl. If necessary, warm them gently together in a suitable microwave-safe bowl or on the stove only until fluid, then let them cool until warm rather than hot before they touch the eggs.
3. **Mix the eggs and pumpkin:** Whisk plain pumpkin puree and large eggs in a separate bowl until combined, then stir in the warm oil-honey mixture.
4. **Mix oats and inclusions:** In a large bowl, stir old-fashioned rolled oats, quick-cooking oats, ground flaxseed, unsweetened dried cranberries, pumpkin seeds (pepitas), pumpkin pie spice, and sea salt together until evenly distributed, including all the salt.
5. **Combine thoroughly:** Add the pumpkin mixture to the oat mixture and stir until all the oats and inclusions are coated and the mixture holds together.
6. **Scoop and flatten:** Scoop about ¼ cup per cookie onto the lined sheet. Flatten each into a roughly ¾-inch-thick disk; these cookies do not spread themselves. The original batch plans twelve cookies; use all the dough and keep similar portion size when scaling.
7. **Bake:** Wait until the oven reaches 350°F. Bake for 15–20 minutes per load, until the edges are lightly browned and the center feels firm. Check again if the center is still loose; sheet loads and cookie thickness can change the time.
8. **Cool:** Let the cookies cool completely on the baking sheet before lifting them or closing them in an airtight container.

## Cooking Notes

### Egg-free and sweetener choices

Maple syrup or agave may replace the full listed honey amount. To make the publisher’s egg-free route, omit both eggs from the original batch and soak the already listed ¼ cup ground flaxseed in ½ cup water until gelled. Keep this flax out of the dry bowl, then add the gel to the pumpkin with the other wet ingredients; do not add a second dose of flaxseed. Scale both the existing flax and added water with the batch. For a vegan route, also replace the honey with maple syrup or agave. Keep all oats, oil, pumpkin, cranberries and pepitas. Gelled-flax cookies can bind and bake differently; check their centers.

Use certified gluten-free oats for a gluten-free preparation and check the other ingredients. A mix of chopped nuts or sunflower seeds and chocolate chips may replace the pepitas at their total listed volume; this changes texture, sweetness and allergen suitability. The main uses the full pepitas.

### Keeping the cookies

Cool fully before closing the container. The publisher’s plain-cookie plan is 3–4 days airtight at room temperature or about a week refrigerated. For longer keeping, freeze cooled cookies in sealed bags and aim to use within four months for quality. Thaw a portion before serving; do not pack warm cookies into a closed container.

RECIPE: Pumpkin Cheesecake Cookies (pumpkin-cheesecake-cookies.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/pumpkin-cheesecake-cookies/
SOURCE: Chelsey White, Chelsweets
SOURCE_URL: https://chelsweets.com/pumpkin-cheesecake-cookies/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Pumpkin cookie dough ---
  - 1 1/2 cups (195 g) all-purpose flour
  - 1/2 tsp baking soda
  - 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
  - 1/4 tsp ground ginger
  - 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt
  - 1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, softened
  - 2/3 cup light brown sugar, packed
  - 1/4 cup granulated sugar
  - 1/3 cup plain pumpkin puree
  - --- Cheesecake filling ---
  - 6 oz (3/4 cup) full-fat block cream cheese, softened
  - 1/4 cup granulated sugar
  - 1 tsp vanilla extract
  - --- Cinnamon-ginger sugar coating ---
  - 1/3 cup granulated sugar
  - 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
  - 1/4 tsp ground ginger
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Soft pumpkin cookies surround a creamy cheesecake filling, with cinnamon-ginger sugar on the outside. Chilling makes the dough easier to wrap, while freezing firms the sweetened cream cheese enough to handle. Divide both mixtures into 12 equal portions so every cookie has the same dough-to-filling ratio.

## Directions

1. **Mix the dry ingredients:** Whisk the dough's all-purpose flour, baking soda, ground cinnamon, ground ginger, ground nutmeg, and fine salt together.
2. **Cream the butter and sugars:** With a stand or hand mixer, beat the dough's unsalted butter, light brown sugar, and granulated sugar until lighter, about 1 minute.
3. **Finish the dough:** Measure the plain pumpkin puree before gently blotting or squeezing away excess moisture with a clean paper towel, then mix it into the butter mixture. Mix in the prepared dry ingredients on low speed only until combined, scraping the bowl as needed.
4. **Chill the dough:** Divide the dough into 12 equal portions on a parchment-lined tray. Refrigerate for about 1 hour, until firm enough to flatten and fill.
5. **Firm the filling:** While the dough chills, beat the filling's full-fat block cream cheese, granulated sugar, and vanilla extract until smooth. Divide into 12 equal dollops on a parchment-lined plate. Freeze for at least 45 minutes, until easy to pick up; they need not become rock-hard.
6. **Prepare to fill:** Heat the oven to 350°F while the dough and filling finish chilling. Line two large baking sheets with parchment. Stir the coating's granulated sugar, ground cinnamon, and ground ginger together in a small bowl.
7. **Wrap and coat:** Flatten each chilled dough portion, place one filling portion in the middle, and wrap the dough around it, pinching the seams closed. If the dough sticks to warm hands, flatten it between two pieces of parchment. Rechill the dough or filling if either becomes too soft to handle. Roll the stuffed portions in the cinnamon-ginger sugar, space them 3 inches apart on the sheets, and flatten slightly. Keep any portions waiting to bake refrigerated.
8. **Bake:** Bake for 16–19 minutes per batch, until the outside and edges have set; do not wait for deep browning. The centers will still feel soft. Allow extra time if your oven requires baking one sheet at a time.
9. **Cool and refrigerate:** Let the cookies firm on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack. After this brief initial cooling, refrigerate the cream-cheese-filled cookies in a single layer to finish cooling; cover once cold. Get them into the refrigerator within 2 hours of baking, or 1 hour if the room is above 90°F. Serve chilled.

## Timing and storage

Allow about 2 hours for mixing, overlapping dough and filling chills, shaping, one oven batch, and initial cooling. Extra oven batches, rechilling during assembly, and cooling completely for cold service take longer.

The filled, baked cookies need refrigeration even though the dough contains no egg. Store covered at 40°F or below and use within 3–4 days, or freeze for longer storage and thaw in the refrigerator. Keep the cream-cheese filling and assembled unbaked cookies chilled whenever you pause; the dough's one-hour handling chill is not a room-temperature storage allowance. Limit the baked cookies' combined cooling and serving time out of refrigeration to 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F.

## Cooking Notes

Chill the dough before wrapping it around the filling. If warm hands make shaping difficult, flatten portions between sheets of parchment. Leave about three inches between cookies and use the surface-texture cue rather than waiting for dark browning.

### Make-ahead routes

The twelve large filled cookies remain one fixed batch. Freeze assembled unbaked cookies airtight for up to one month, thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then bake by the written set-exterior cue. Baked cookies may also be frozen airtight up to one month and thawed in the refrigerator overnight. The two freezer routes are separate; keep all cream-cheese filling and the complete dough and coating in either route.

For cinnamon toast, set aside any clean extra coating before it touches the raw dough. Discard coating that has contacted raw dough; do not put that coating straight on cooked toast.

Longer dough chilling can make flattening and filling harder. Keep the cheese filling chilled and rechill portions if handling warms them; the dough and filling chills do not need to be added together. The full-fat block cream cheese stays in the filling.

RECIPE: Aromatic Purple Rice (purple-rice.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/purple-rice/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1/2 cup whole-grain aromatic purple rice, with a stated stovetop cooking time around 45 minutes; not glutinous black rice or a quick-cooking blend
  - 1 1/8 cups (270 ml) water, for starting the purple rice
  - 1 1/2 cups Japanese-style medium-grain white rice, not brown or parboiled
  - 1 1/8 cups (270 ml) water, for soaking and cooking the white rice
  - 3/4 cup (180 ml) unsalted chicken stock, for soaking and cooking the white rice
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, plus up to 1/4 tsp more after tasting
  - 1 tsp coconut oil or unsalted butter, optional
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) hot water, reserved only for correcting evaporation or firm grains
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

White rice softens the chewy texture and nutty flavor of whole-grain purple rice. Give the purple grain a head start, then let both finish in the same colored cooking liquid. The white grains take on a purple tint while a little chicken stock rounds out the flavor.

## Directions

1. **Rinse separately:** Rinse the purple rice briefly in cool water and drain. Rinse the white rice in several changes of water until much of the loose starch has washed away, then drain well. Purple pigment may continue to tint its rinsing water; it need not run colorless.
2. **Start the purple rice:** Put purple rice and its 270 ml water in the saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover tightly and reduce heat to a very gentle simmer. Set a timer for 20 minutes and continue with the white rice while it cooks.
3. **Soak the white rice:** Combine drained white rice with its 270 ml water, 180 ml chicken stock and the initial 1/4 tsp salt in a bowl. Soak for 20 minutes in this measured liquid. Keep all the liquid for the cooking pot; do not drain it afterward.
4. **Check the head start:** At 20 minutes, check that the purple rice is still moist and taste a grain. Continue gently until the grains are swollen with softened outsides but firmer centers, usually 25–30 minutes total. If still hard throughout, give them another five minutes before adding the white rice. If the pot is drying, add 2 tbsp from the separate hot-water reserve and lower the heat. Re-cover between checks. Retain all the purple cooking liquid.
5. **Combine and reheat:** Add the white rice with all its soaking liquid to the purple rice and stir once to distribute the grains. Bring back to a gentle boil, allowing about five minutes for the pot to reheat. Cover, reduce heat to low and simmer gently for 15–20 minutes, starting that timer only once the combined pot is simmering.
6. **Check both grains and rest:** Taste a white grain and a purple grain. Both should be tender inside, with the purple grain retaining a slight chew, and the cooking liquid should be absorbed. Use the measured correction reserve if the pot is dry and grains are firm. Once ready, turn off heat and rest covered for 10 minutes.
7. **Fluff and season:** Fold gently with a rice paddle or fork, incorporating the optional coconut oil or butter. Taste and add some or all of the reserved salt if wanted. The batch makes approximately 5–6 cups; divide into seven small side portions, roughly 3/4 cup each depending on final yield.

RECIPE: Quadruple Chocolate Brownies (quadruple-chocolate-brownies.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/quadruple-chocolate-brownies/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/quadruple-chocolate-brownies
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Brownies ---
  - 1 1/4 lb (5 sticks) unsalted butter, softened
  - 1 lb unsweetened chocolate, chopped
  - 5 1/2 cups granulated sugar
  - 16 large eggs
  - 2 tbsp pure vanilla extract
  - 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt
  - 3 3/4 cups all-purpose flour
  - 1/2 lb bittersweet chocolate, chopped into approximately 1/2-inch pieces
  - 1/2 lb white chocolate, chopped into approximately 1/2-inch pieces
  - 1/2 lb milk chocolate, chopped into approximately 1/2-inch pieces
  - additional butter, as needed for greasing
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Keep all five sticks of butter in the original batch. Unsweetened chocolate forms the batter, while bittersweet, white and milk chocolate each supply both pieces inside and a separate melted swirl on top. Reserve those shares before folding; complete cooling gives the rich center time to firm for cutting.

## Directions

1. **Prepare pans:** Heat the oven to 300°F. For the original batch, line the bottoms of two 9×13-inch baking pans with parchment and lightly grease the pans with additional butter. Have a mixing bowl large enough for the complete batter.
2. **Melt:** Melt unsalted butter and unsweetened chocolate over low heat in a large saucepan, stirring frequently. Remove from heat and cool for about 10 minutes, until warm rather than hot before combining with eggs.
3. **Mix eggs:** Whisk granulated sugar, large eggs, pure vanilla extract, and kosher salt together until evenly combined. Whisk in all the warm melted chocolate mixture until smooth; stop once evenly combined.
4. **Fold:** Fold in all-purpose flour, 5/8 of the bittersweet chocolate, 5/8 of the white chocolate, and 5/8 of the milk chocolate just until no dry flour remains and the chocolate pieces are dispersed. The three partial chocolate shares belong in the batter; keep their remaining shares separate for the swirl. Divide all the batter evenly among the prepared pans.
5. **Swirl:** Keep 3/8 of the bittersweet chocolate, 3/8 of the white chocolate, and 3/8 of the milk chocolate in three separate microwave-safe bowls. Melt each gently in short intervals, stirring between intervals and stopping once smooth. Divide each melted chocolate over all the pans, then draw a table knife through the batter to marble the tops.
6. **Bake:** Bake for about 35–40 minutes for the original pans, rotating halfway through. Begin checking at 35 minutes: the tops should be shiny and the brownies set at the center, without liquid batter. A toothpick should show moist crumbs rather than a wet batter coating; avoid a chocolate pocket or check a second spot.
7. **Cool:** Set the pans on a wire rack and cool completely before cutting into the listed pieces. Do not use the oven clock as a cooling deadline.

RECIPE: Queso Fundido with Chorizo (queso-fundido-with-chorizo.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/queso-fundido-with-chorizo/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 8 oz fresh raw chorizo, casings removed
  - 1 lb Oaxaca Cheese (or Mozzarella), shredded
  - 4 oz Pepper Jack Cheese, shredded
  - 1/2 medium White Onion, diced
  - 2 poblano peppers, to roast, peel, seed and dice
  - 2 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1/4 cup Fresh Cilantro, chopped
  - Warm Flour Tortillas, for scooping
  - Optional: Pickled Jalapeños for topping
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Mexican-style melted-cheese dip uses Oaxaca for stretchy strands; mozzarella is the listed alternative, with the full pepper Jack alongside it. Roast and peel the poblanos before assembling, and cook the fresh chorizo before it goes back over the cheese. Serve promptly with warm tortillas, because the cheese firms as it cools.

## Directions

1. **Roast peppers:** Wash the poblanos. Roast directly over a suitable gas flame or under the broiler, turning until the skins blacken, starting checks around 8 minutes. Put in a heatproof bowl, cover with a heat-safe cover and rest about 5 minutes, until safe to handle. Peel, remove stems and seeds, and dice.
2. **Cook chorizo:** Preheat the oven to 400°F. Use an oven-safe skillet with room for the entire cheese and vegetable batch; the original batch uses a 10-inch cast-iron skillet, but its depth matters. If necessary use additional oven-safe vessels and divide everything proportionally. Cook all the fresh raw chorizo over medium-high heat, breaking it into small pieces. Begin checks around 5–6 minutes, then continue until cooked through: 160°F / 71°C for pork or beef chorizo, 165°F / 74°C if the product contains poultry. Transfer to a clean plate and leave the rendered fat in the pan. A cured ready-to-eat sausage is a different product from the fresh chorizo called for here.
3. **Soften vegetables:** Add all the onion and garlic to the rendered fat. Sauté until softened, beginning checks around 3 minutes. Add all the prepared poblanos and stir to combine.
4. **Assemble:** Take the skillet off heat. Scatter all the Oaxaca or mozzarella and all the pepper Jack over the vegetables, then return all the cooked chorizo on top. Leave headroom for bubbling.
5. **Bake:** Bake at 400°F, beginning checks around 8–10 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling and the center reaches 165°F / 74°C. Check every vessel if the batch is divided.
6. **Finish and serve:** Top with all the cilantro and the optional pickled jalapeños. Warm the tortillas according to their package instructions and serve immediately, taking care with the hot skillet handle.

## Vegetarian Variation

Omit all the chorizo and its rendered-fat stage. For the original batch, use 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp smoked paprika and 1/2 tsp cumin instead; scale these amounts with the batch. Roast the full pepper supply as above. Heat the oil, sauté all the onion and garlic until softened, then stir in the paprika, cumin and all the diced poblanos. Take off heat and assemble with the full two-cheese supplies; bake and finish as in the main. Choose cheeses suitable for a vegetarian diet if needed.

RECIPE: Caprese Pasta (quick-and-easy-caprese-pasta.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/quick-and-easy-caprese-pasta/
SOURCE: Adapted from Sara Welch, Dinner at the Zoo
SOURCE_URL: https://www.dinneratthezoo.com/caprese-pasta/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 12 oz dry angel-hair pasta
  - 8 oz fresh mozzarella, drained and cut into pieces about 1/2 inch across
  - 6 ripe Roma tomatoes, cored, seeded and chopped
  - 6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 2 cloves garlic, minced
  - 2 tsp dried Italian seasoning
  - 1/2 cup fresh basil, roughly chopped
  - 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, added to taste
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  - 1/2 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Warm the tomatoes just enough to release some juice, then toss with the pasta away from the burner. Let the mixture lose its fiercest heat before adding mozzarella. The aim is soft pieces of fresh cheese, not a melted cheese sauce.

## Directions

1. **Prepare before boiling pasta:** Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Core, seed and chop tomatoes, mince garlic, drain and cut mozzarella, and chop basil. Season water with salt.
2. **Warm tomatoes:** Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low to medium. Stir in garlic and Italian seasoning for **30–60 seconds**, until fragrant without browning. Add tomatoes and a little salt; cook about **2–3 minutes** until warm but still distinct. Remove from heat.
3. **Cook angel hair:** Add pasta to the boiling water and stir gently. Cook according to its package until tender with a little bite, tasting near the end. Reserve **the listed cooking water** before draining without rinsing.
4. **Combine and cool briefly:** Add pasta to the tomato mixture away from heat, transferring to a serving bowl if the skillet is crowded or retains strong heat. Add **half the lemon juice** and lift gently to coat, using a small splash of cooking water only if dry. Let stand about **1–2 minutes**, until no longer steaming fiercely.
5. **Fold and serve:** Fold in mozzarella and basil gently. Taste, then add the remaining lemon juice, salt and pepper only as needed. Serve promptly while the cheese is softened but still in distinct pieces; do not return to the burner to force melting.

Adapted from [Sara Welch’s Caprese Pasta at Dinner at the Zoo](https://www.dinneratthezoo.com/caprese-pasta/).

RECIPE: Drop Biscuits (quick-and-easy-drop-biscuits.md)
CUISINES: Southern
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/quick-and-easy-drop-biscuits/
SOURCE: Adapted from Seriouseats.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.seriouseats.com/recipes/2014/06/quick-easy-drop-biscuits-recipe.html
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 1/2 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 4 oz (1 stick) Unsalted Butter, cold and cubed
  - 3/4 cup Whole Milk (chilled)
  - 2 tsp Baking Powder
  - 1 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1/4 tsp Garlic Powder (Optional)
  - --- For handling and serving ---
  - Butter, for greasing the sheet if not using parchment
  - Salted butter, for serving, optional
  - Honey, for serving, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This rich drop-biscuit dough is scooped rather than rolled. Keep the butter cold, then stir the milk only until the dough holds together. Similar mound sizes and a fully heated oven are more useful than an exact stirring clock.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment, or grease it with the handling butter. Keep the measured dough butter cold.

2. **Dry mix:** Whisk all the flour, baking powder, sea salt and optional garlic powder in a bowl.

3. **Cut in:** Toss in the cold butter cubes, then quickly rub or cut them into the flour with your fingers or a pastry blender until coarse meal and a few pea-sized pieces remain. Alternatively, pulse the dry mixture and butter in a food processor 2–3 times to reach the same coarse state, then transfer to a bowl.

4. **Hydrate:** Pour in all the milk and stir with a fork just until a slightly sticky, shaggy dough comes together. Stop when no dry pockets remain; the dough does not need kneading or an exact stirring duration.

5. **Drop:** Divide into similar mounds, leaving room between them. The original-size main batch plans 12 biscuits; follow the listed scaled count. For the separate smaller option, use a teaspoon or small scoop for about 20 walnut-sized mounds from the original batch. For the larger option, use a ¼ cup scoop for about 8 from the original batch. Scale those approximate counts with the amount of dough while keeping the chosen scoop size.

6. **Bake:** Load only once the oven has reached 400°F. Bake until golden with baked centers, beginning checks around 15 minutes for small biscuits and around 20 minutes for the ¼ cup size. The 12-piece batch may fall between them; use the crumb and color rather than assuming a fixed duration. Bake further trays as needed while keeping waiting dough cold.

7. **Cool and serve:** Let the biscuits cool slightly until they lift intact, then transfer to a rack. Serve warm or at room temperature, with the optional salted butter and honey if desired.

## Salt Variation

Replace the listed sea salt with the same measured volume of kosher salt for the separate kosher-salt version; all other ingredients and steps remain unchanged. Different salt crystal sizes make equal spoon volumes differently salty, so this is a distinct flavor choice, not a universal weight equivalent.

RECIPE: Honey Garlic Shrimp and Broccoli (quick-honey-garlic-shrimp-and-broccoli.md)
CUISINES: American, Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/quick-honey-garlic-shrimp-and-broccoli/
SOURCE: Adapted from Layla Atik, Gimme Delicious
SOURCE_URL: https://gimmedelicious.com/2016/02/11/quick-honey-garlic-shrimp-and-broccoli/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb raw shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails removed
  - 1 cup fresh broccoli florets, cut into bite-size pieces with thin stems
  - 4 tbsp honey
  - 3 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
  - 1 tsp garlic, minced
  - 1/2 tsp fresh ginger, minced
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil, divided between shrimp batches
  - 2 tsp water, for steaming broccoli, plus a little more only if needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This simple version uses oil rather than butter and only a small amount of broccoli. Steam the florets first, keep the clean finishing sauce separate from the shrimp marinade, and use moderate heat so the honey coating does not burn. Adapted from [Layla Atik’s Honey Garlic Shrimp and Broccoli](https://gimmedelicious.com/quick-honey-garlic-shrimp-and-broccoli/).

## Directions

1. **Steam broccoli:** Place florets and measured water in a microwave-safe bowl with a vented cover. Microwave on high for about 2 minutes, then check a stem carefully, keeping your face away from escaping steam. Continue in short bursts if needed until tender with a little bite; add a little water if the bowl dries. Drain.

2. **Mix and divide sauce:** Whisk honey, soy sauce, garlic and ginger together. Put half in a clean bowl for finishing. Toss prepared shrimp with the other half and refrigerate 5 minutes; prepare the broccoli during this rest if not already done.

3. **Drain shrimp:** Lift shrimp from the marinade, letting excess drip off, and blot lightly if very wet. Discard used marinade. Have a clean plate ready for cooked shrimp.

4. **Cook in batches:** Heat half the oil over medium-high and cook half the shrimp in a single layer. Cook about 1–2 minutes per side, adjusting for size, until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to the clean plate and repeat with remaining oil and shrimp. Reduce heat if the honey darkens rapidly; remove burnt residue before the next batch.

5. **Finish sauce:** Lower heat to medium. Add the clean reserved sauce and broccoli; stir gently about 1 minute until bubbling and the broccoli is hot. Return shrimp and plate juices only briefly to coat. A small splash of water can loosen over-reduced sauce. Serve promptly with separately prepared rice and another vegetable side.

RECIPE: Lamb Ragù (quick-lamb-ragu.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/quick-lamb-ragu/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020022-quick-lamb-ragu?smid=ck-recipe-iOS-share
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Ragù ---
  - 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 1 medium yellow onion, finely chopped
  - 4 garlic cloves, minced
  - 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes
  - 2 anchovy fillets
  - 2 tbsp tomato paste
  - 1 lb ground lamb
  - 1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
  - 1/2 cup water
  - salt, to taste for the sauce
  - black pepper, to taste for the sauce
  - 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar
  - fresh oregano or marjoram, for finishing, leaves picked
  - --- Pasta and Serving ---
  - 12 oz dry pasta, penne or shells
  - water, enough to boil the pasta in a suitable pot
  - Parmesan or Pecorino, for grating over the finished dish
  - extra-virgin olive oil, for drizzling at serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Italian-style lamb ragù builds a savory base with onion, garlic, tomato paste and anchovy before the meat and tomatoes simmer together. Keep the lamb’s rendered fat in the sauce and let the tomato paste deepen without burning. The balsamic finish suits the current version; cheese and fresh herbs complete either pasta route.

## Directions

1. **Onion Base:** Heat extra-virgin olive oil and medium yellow onion in a large heavy pot over medium heat, coating the onion with the full measured oil. Cook the onion for 5–8 minutes until softened and golden. Choose enough pot capacity for stirring the full lamb and tomato load without spilling; a larger batch may need separate pots with the formula divided proportionally.
2. **Garlic:** Add garlic cloves and cook for 30–45 seconds until fragrant.
3. **Anchovy and Chile:** Stir in red pepper flakes and anchovy fillets and cook for about 2 minutes until the anchovy breaks down into the oil. Keep the heat low enough that the garlic does not burn.
4. **Tomato Paste:** Stir in tomato paste and cook for about 3 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and smells roasted rather than scorched.
5. **Brown the Lamb:** Add ground lamb. Increase the heat to medium-high and break it up while cooking, about 8 minutes for the original batch, until it browns and sizzles in its fat. Retain all the rendered fat.
6. **Simmer:** Stir in crushed tomatoes, water, salt, and black pepper, scraping up the browned bits. Bring to a boil, reduce to a gentle simmer and cook 25–30 minutes, stirring as needed, until thick and meaty. Check that the ground lamb has reached at least 160°F; browned color alone is not the safety endpoint. Taste the fully cooked sauce before adjusting its seasoning.
7. **Cook the Pasta:** While the sauce simmers, use dry pasta and water and follow the pasta package’s cooking instructions, stopping while it still has a firm center. Drain and keep it ready to finish in the sauce; the listed pasta amount is dry weight.
8. **Finish:** Stir balsamic vinegar and fresh oregano or marjoram into the sauce. Toss with all the hot pasta until it is coated and cooked to the firmness you want.
9. **Serve:** Finish with Parmesan or Pecorino and extra-virgin olive oil: grate the cheese over the portions and drizzle with the extra oil. This oil allowance is separate from the full measured oil already used for the onion base.

RECIPE: Do Chua (Pickled Carrots and Daikon) (quick-pickled-carrots-and-daikon.md)
CUISINES: Vietnamese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/quick-pickled-carrots-and-daikon/
SOURCE: Technique adapted from Andrea Nguyen’s daikon and carrot pickle
SOURCE_URL: https://www.vietworldkitchen.com/blog/2009/05/daikon-and-carrot-pickle-recipe-do-chua.html
INGREDIENTS:
  - 150 g carrots, peeled and trimmed weight
  - 150 g daikon radish, peeled and trimmed weight
  - 1/2 tsp fine sea salt, for the vegetable massage
  - 1 tsp granulated sugar, for the vegetable massage
  - 1/4 cup granulated sugar, for the brine
  - 1/2 cup unseasoned rice vinegar, labeled 4–5% acidity
  - 1/2 cup lukewarm water, plus cold water for rinsing
  - --- Optional extra brine, only if needed for coverage ---
  - 2 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar, labeled 4–5% acidity
  - 2 tbsp lukewarm water
  - 1 tbsp granulated sugar
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Do chua brings sweet-tart crunch to Vietnamese bánh mì, rice plates and noodle bowls. Equal amounts of carrot and daikon keep the bite balanced. A little salt and sugar soften the matchsticks before rinsing; a separate sugar measure sweetens the rice-vinegar brine. Drain the serving portion so it brightens a sandwich or bowl without soaking it.

## Directions

1. **Cut even matchsticks:** Wash and peel the carrots and daikon, trim the ends, then weigh the required amounts. Cut into roughly 2-inch matchsticks, about 2 mm thick for carrot and 2–3 mm for daikon. Put them in a bowl; have a clean jar and colander ready.
2. **Massage briefly:** Toss vegetables with the 1/2 tsp fine salt and the separate 1 tsp sugar. Knead gently for about 3 minutes, until liquid collects and a daikon stick bends without breaking. If the sticks are still rigid, let them stand for a few more minutes rather than crushing them.
3. **Rinse and drain:** Rinse briefly under cold running water in the colander. Drain and press gently to remove excess liquid; do not wring the sticks bone-dry. Pack into the jar without crushing them.
4. **Mix the sweet brine:** Stir the 1/4 cup brine sugar into the measured 1/2 cup lukewarm water until dissolved, then stir in the 1/2 cup rice vinegar. The brine should be cool or lukewarm, not hot. Pour over the vegetables and gently press them below the liquid with a clean spoon. Leave about 1/2 inch space at the top. If coverage is inadequate, use the container or extra same-ratio brine correction above.
5. **Refrigerate and develop:** Cover and refrigerate immediately for at least 1 hour. Taste a drained stick: it should retain a crisp bite with both sweetness and vinegar tang. More refrigerated time, ideally overnight, gives fuller flavor; do not leave the jar on the counter to speed it up.
6. **Drain only what you need:** Lift portions with a clean fork or tongs and let brine drain back into the jar. At the stated quantities, expect approximately 2 cups drained pickles. For four salmon bowls, use about 1/4 of the finished batch—roughly 1/2 cup total, or 2 tbsp per bowl—as a small topping. Keep the rest covered by brine and refrigerated; a larger sandwich or rice-plate portion is a separate allocation.

RECIPE: Quick-Pickled Cucumber Salad (quick-pickled-cucumber-salad.md)
CUISINES: Korean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/quick-pickled-cucumber-salad/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 lbs English Cucumbers (or 4-5 regular cucumbers), thinly sliced
  - 1/4 cup Rice Vinegar
  - 2 tbsp Soy Sauce
  - 1 tbsp Sesame Oil
  - 1 tbsp Sugar
  - 2 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1/2 tsp Gochugaru (Korean red pepper flakes, optional)
  - 2 scallions, thinly sliced
  - Sesame Seeds for garnish
  - 1/4 tsp Kosher Salt, for the cucumber salt rest
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Thin cucumber slices take on the full rice-vinegar, soy and sesame dressing after a short rest. This is a fresh dressed cucumber salad kept refrigerated, without a fermentation or shelf-stable preservation process. Scallions, optional gochugaru and sesame seeds finish it; cucumber variety and slicing affect how much liquid collects.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the cucumbers:** Wash the cucumbers under running water, then slice into thin rounds or half-moons, about 1/8 inch thick. Use the listed cucumber weight; the four-to-five regular-cucumber note describes the original batch only and is not a fixed size-to-weight equivalence. Toss with all the listed kosher salt and rest about 2 minutes as a first check. This short salt rest is not a guarantee against later liquid release.

2. **Mix the dressing:** Whisk all the rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar and minced garlic together until the sugar is dissolved. Keep the full listed oil and sugar; this mixture flavors the salad rather than establishing preservation acidity.

3. **Combine:** Drain only any liquid that has pooled from the salted cucumbers; do not add a rinse or squeeze. Put the cucumber slices in a clean bowl, pour over all the dressing and toss gently.

4. **Rest:** Rest about 5 minutes before immediate service, or cover and refrigerate for up to 2 hours before finishing. The longer cold wait changes texture and liquid release; it does not make a shelf-stable pickle.

5. **Finish:** Wash the scallions before slicing. Fold in all the scallions and, if chosen, the full listed optional gochugaru. Garnish with the sesame-seed allowance and serve promptly.

6. **Store:** Keep covered at 40°F or below. Use within 3 refrigerated days for the short fresh-salad plan; the dressing does not make this a shelf-stable pickle. Refrigerate promptly after service and discard if it has exceeded the usual perishable-food room-temperature limits.

RECIPE: Seasoned Black Beans (quick-seasoned-black-beans.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/quick-seasoned-black-beans/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cans (15 oz / 425 g each) plain cooked black beans, with all their liquid
  - 1 tbsp olive oil
  - 2 cloves garlic, finely minced
  - 1 tsp ground cumin
  - 1 tsp dried oregano
  - 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, added only if needed, plus more to taste
  - 1/8 tsp freshly ground black pepper
  - Water, as needed to loosen
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

These beans keep most of their shape, with a few mashed into the cooking liquid to give it body. Garlic and cumin warm briefly in olive oil before the cans go in. Add lime at the end and taste against the beans' existing salt before seasoning further.

## Directions

1. **Warm the aromatics:** Open the cans without draining. Heat oil in a heavy saucepan over medium-low. Add garlic and stir about 30–45 seconds until fragrant but pale. Stir in cumin for about 15 seconds, then promptly add the beans and all their liquid.
2. **Simmer:** Crush the oregano between your fingers into the pot. Stir and raise heat to medium until gently bubbling, then lower to maintain an uncovered simmer.
3. **Thicken lightly:** Simmer about 8–12 minutes, stirring along the bottom. Mash a few beans against the side of the pot, roughly a tenth of the batch, and stir them back in. Keep most beans whole. Continue until the liquid lightly coats them but they still spoon easily. If too dry, add water a small splash at a time; watery cans may need longer reduction.
4. **Finish:** Turn off heat, stir in lime juice and black pepper, and taste before adding any of the measured salt. Add more salt only if needed. Divide into four generous side portions; final volume depends on the cans and reduction. For a short wait cover off heat; for longer service keep hot at 140°F / 60°C or above, stirring and loosening as needed.

RECIPE: Quick Wonton Soup (quick-wonton-soup.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/quick-wonton-soup/
SOURCE: Adapted from skinnytaste.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.skinnytaste.com/wonton-soup/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 20 mini frozen wontons
  - 6 cups Low-sodium Chicken Broth
  - 1 (1-inch) piece Fresh Ginger, smashed
  - 1 clove Garlic, smashed
  - 4 Baby Bok Choy, halved
  - 1 1/2 cups Shiitake Mushrooms, sliced
  - 1 tbsp Soy Sauce
  - 1 tsp Toasted Sesame Oil
  - Scallions, sliced green parts only
  - White Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Quick wonton soup using store-bought frozen wontons makes a comforting 25-minute meal. The trick to elevating store-bought broth: smash ginger and garlic with the side of a knife (instead of mincing) and simmer them in the broth. This releases their essential oils without adding gritty texture. Add the wontons and bok choy together at the end so the greens stay vibrant and the wonton skins don't get mushy.

## Directions

1.  **Infuse:** In a large pot, bring the chicken broth to a boil. Add the smashed ginger and garlic. Reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
2.  **Add Veg:** Add the halved bok choy and sliced mushrooms. Simmer for 3 minutes until the mushrooms begin to soften.
3.  **Wontons:** Add the frozen wontons. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until they float and are heated through.
4.  **Finish:** Stir in the soy sauce and toasted sesame oil. Add a pinch of white pepper for the mandatory **High Note**.
5.  **Serve:** Divide into bowls, ensuring everyone gets 5 wontons. Garnish with fresh scallions.

RECIPE: Quinoa Pilaf with Toasted Almonds (quinoa-pilaf-with-toasted-almonds.md)
CUISINES: South American, Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/quinoa-pilaf-with-toasted-almonds/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 cups dry quinoa
  - 2.5 cups vegetable or chicken broth, plus hot water as needed if the grains remain firm
  - 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus a pinch for the onion and more to taste
  - 2 tbsp olive oil or butter, divided
  - 1/2 cup raw almonds, roughly chopped
  - 1 small onion, finely diced
  - 2 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1/2 cup dried apricots, chopped, or dried cranberries, optional
  - 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
  - 1 tbsp fresh dill or tarragon, chopped, optional
  - 1/4 tsp black pepper
  - 1 lemon, finely grated zest only
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Onion and garlic cooked in fat make this a savory pilaf rather than a simply dressed grain. Toast the almonds separately and add them back at the end so they retain their bite. Keep the same choice of oil or butter through both stages; the dried fruit and dill or tarragon are optional finishing accents.

## Directions

1. **Rinse and drain:** Rinse the dry quinoa in a fine-mesh strainer, following package preparation guidance, then drain thoroughly.
2. **Toast the almonds:** In a wide heavy saucepan over medium heat, stir the almonds for about 3–4 minutes until fragrant and light golden. Transfer immediately to a plate.
3. **Soften the aromatics:** Add half of the chosen olive oil or butter to the same pan. Add the onion and a pinch of salt; cook about 3–4 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic for about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
4. **Toast the quinoa:** Add the drained quinoa and stir for about 2 minutes, letting surface moisture evaporate and coating the grains in fat. Do not let the garlic scorch.
5. **Simmer and check:** Add the broth and measured salt. Bring to a boil, cover tightly and reduce to a low simmer. Cook about 15 minutes. Check that the quinoa is tender through its center and free liquid is absorbed. If firm and dry, add a little hot water and continue covered; if firm with liquid remaining, continue without adding more.
6. **Rest:** Remove from heat once tender and leave covered for 5 minutes.
7. **Finish:** Fluff gently. Fold in the toasted almonds, remaining chosen oil or butter, parsley, black pepper and lemon zest. Add dried apricots or cranberries and dill or tarragon if using. Taste before adding any finishing salt.
8. **Serve:** Divide into four generous side portions and serve warm alongside a main dish.
