RECIPE: Saffron Cardamom Rice (saffron-cardamom-rice.md)
CUISINES: Indian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/saffron-cardamom-rice/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 1/2 cups (about 300 g) aged white basmati rice, not parboiled or quick-cooking
  - 2 1/2 cups (600 ml) water, for cooking, plus water for rinsing
  - 1/2 tsp saffron threads, loosely measured
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) whole milk
  - 3 tbsp ghee or clarified butter
  - 6 green cardamom pods, lightly cracked but kept together
  - 1 black cardamom pod, optional, lightly cracked
  - 2 cloves, whole
  - 1 small cinnamon stick, about 1 1/2 inches long
  - 1 Indian bay leaf (tej patta)
  - 150 g peeled onion, thinly sliced
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water, reserved only for correcting firm grains
  - 1 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
  - 2 tbsp toasted unsalted sliced almonds or chopped pistachios, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Indian-style rice combines saffron and green cardamom with ghee and golden onion. Steep the saffron while preparing the pot, then add every drop of the infusion so its color and aroma reach the grains. A gentle simmer and a covered rest keep the rice tender without breaking it up.

## Directions

1. **Steep the saffron:** Warm the milk until steaming but not boiling, in a small saucepan or in brief microwave bursts in a heatproof bowl. Lightly crumble the measured saffron threads into it and steep for at least 15 minutes while continuing with the rice and onion. Keep all the threads and liquid.
2. **Rinse and prepare:** Rinse basmati gently in several changes of cool water until much of the loose starch washes away. Drain thoroughly without soaking. Slice the onion thinly and lightly crack the cardamom pods. Measure the remaining spices, water and salt before heating the ghee.
3. **Cook spices and onion:** Heat ghee in the heavy saucepan over medium heat. Add green cardamom, optional black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf; stir 20–30 seconds until fragrant. Add onion and cook for about 10–15 minutes, stirring often, until soft and lightly golden with a few browned edges. Lower the heat if the spices darken rapidly. This is a golden onion base, not a dark caramelized one.
4. **Coat rice and add all liquid:** Fold in drained rice and stir gently for about 1 minute to coat it with ghee. Add the measured cooking water, all the saffron milk and threads, and the salt. Stir once and bring to a gentle boil, allowing about 5 minutes to heat. Cover snugly and lower the heat to maintain a very gentle simmer.
5. **Simmer and check:** Cook for about 15–20 minutes. Near the end, briefly part the rice at the edge and taste a grain: the liquid should be absorbed and the center tender. If firm and dry, use the measured hot-water reserve as described in troubleshooting. If firm with liquid remaining, re-cover and cook a little longer. Do not force the rice dry over high heat.
6. **Rest, fluff and finish:** Once the grains are tender and free liquid is absorbed, turn off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Remove visible cardamom pods, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf; let diners know that small pieces may remain. Lift and fluff gently with a fork or rice paddle, folding in cilantro. Add the optional toasted nuts at serving. Expect roughly 4 1/2–5 cups, enough for four generous rice sides or smaller portions beside dal and potatoes.

RECIPE: Sage Brown Butter Ravioli (sage-brown-butter-sauce-butternut-squash-ravioli.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sage-brown-butter-sauce-butternut-squash-ravioli/
SOURCE: Adapted from Aberdeenskitchen.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.aberdeenskitchen.com/2016/11/sage-brown-butter-sauce-butternut-squash-ravioli/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 16 oz Butternut Squash Ravioli (fresh or frozen)
  - 1/2 cup (1 stick) Unsalted Butter
  - 2 tbsp Fresh Sage, minced
  - 1/2 cup Heavy Cream
  - 1/2 cup Chicken Broth
  - 1/4 cup Freshly Grated Parmesan
  - 1/2 tsp Fresh Lemon Juice (The Acid Balance)
  - Coarse Sea Salt and Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Brown butter and sage is a classic Northern Italian sauce, especially popular with filled pasta like ravioli or tortellini. The French call it beurre noisette ("hazelnut butter") for its nutty aroma. Cook the butter until golden-brown before adding sage - this deepens the flavor dramatically. Adding broth and cream to brown butter prevents it from feeling too rich or greasy. A squeeze of lemon juice at the end brightens the sweet squash filling.

## Directions

1.  **Boil:** Cook ravioli in salted water according to package directions. Drain.
2.  **Brown Butter:** In a large light-colored skillet (mandatory to see color), melt butter over medium. Whisk constantly for 5 minutes until it smells like nuts and golden flecks appear.
3.  **Crisp Sage:** Add the sage. Fry for 1 minute until the leaves are crispy and fragrant.
4.  **Emulsify:** Carefully pour in the broth and cream (it will splatter). Whisk vigorously until a smooth, thick emulsion forms.
5.  **Bind:** Stir in the Parmesan and lemon juice.
6.  **Toss:** Add the cooked ravioli to the pan. Toss for 1 minute until every pillow is coated in the brown butter silk.
7.  **Serve:** Garnish with extra Parmesan and a crack of black pepper.

## Cooking Notes

For an optional crisp garnish, fry a few sage leaves in butter until crisp but not dark. Lift onto a paper towel and season lightly before serving.

RECIPE: Salsa Verde Chicken Casserole (salsa-verde-chicken-casserole.md)

INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups Shredded Rotisserie Chicken
  - 1 cup Sour Cream (for richness)

RECIPE: San Marzano Tomato Sauce (san-marzano-tomato-sauce.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/san-marzano-tomato-sauce/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 can (28 oz) Crushed San Marzano Tomatoes (look for DOP certification; ingredient list should be just tomatoes and salt)
  - 3 tbsp Extra Virgin Olive Oil
  - 3 cloves Garlic (smashed whole for subtle infusion, or sliced for bolder flavor)
  - 1 sprig Fresh Basil (or 1/2 tsp dried oregano)
  - Salt to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This quick Italian-American tomato sauce works with stuffed shells, baked ziti, and eggplant Parmesan. Allow about twenty-five minutes for preparation, warming the pan and tomatoes, and the short simmer. Taste the tomatoes before final seasoning; sweetness and acidity vary by can. The key is restraint: warm the garlic in oil gently without browning it, then let the tomatoes do the work with a short simmer.

## Directions

1. **The Garlic:** Warm olive oil in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the smashed or sliced garlic and let it sizzle gently until fragrant and still pale, about 1–2 minutes; thin slices may finish sooner. Lower the heat if the edges begin to color.
2. **The Tomatoes:** Pour in the crushed San Marzano tomatoes. Add the whole basil sprig or the measured dried oregano. Season with a pinch of salt.
3. **The Simmer:** Let the sauce bubble gently for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally. The sauce will darken slightly and thicken just enough to coat the back of a spoon.
4. **Finish:** Remove the whole basil sprig if used. Remove smashed garlic cloves if you want a subtler sauce; leave sliced garlic and dried oregano in the sauce. Taste and adjust salt. Use immediately, or refrigerate promptly in shallow containers within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C). Keep at 40°F / 4°C or below for 3–4 days, or freeze; when reheating, bring the sauce to a rolling boil while stirring. This is a cooked refrigerator sauce, not a canning formula.

## Variations

**Silk Sauce (for ravioli):** Use the same full listed tomato amount as puree or passata instead of crushed tomatoes. Keep all the main olive oil and whole smashed garlic, and choose the same basil-or-oregano option. Follow the main garlic and simmer stages, then discard the whole garlic and basil if used. Turn off heat and whisk in additional cold unsalted butter: 1 tbsp for the original batch, scaled proportionally with the batch. Keep the same cold handling and rolling-boil reheating instructions. This butter variation contains dairy and is not vegan; serve the main without butter for vegan or dairy-free needs.

RECIPE: Sausage and White Bean Skillet (sausage-and-white-bean-skillet.md)
CUISINES: Italian, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sausage-and-white-bean-skillet/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Italian Sausage (sweet or spicy, either form - links or bulk)
  - 1 Onion, diced
  - 4 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 2 cans Cannellini or Great Northern Beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed
  - 1 cup Chicken Stock
  - 1 tsp Dried Oregano (or 1 tbsp fresh)
  - 1 tsp Dried Thyme
  - 1/4 tsp Red Pepper Flakes
  - 2 tbsp Tomato Paste
  - Juice of 1/2 Lemon
  - 1 tbsp Extra Virgin Olive Oil
  - 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1/4 tsp Black Pepper
  - Fresh Parsley for garnish
  - Grated Parmesan Cheese for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Sausage and white beans is Italian comfort food - sausage brings the fat and seasoning, while white beans add body and earthiness. This is the kind of dish Italian grandmothers have been making for decades with whatever they had on hand. It's equally good warm straight from the pan or cooled and reheated the next day, which makes it perfect for weeknight cooking and lunch prep. The lemon at the end is essential - it cuts the richness of the sausage and brightens the whole dish.

## Directions

1. **Cook the Sausage:** Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. If using sausage links, slice them into 1-inch rounds. Add sausage to the dry pan and let it brown without stirring for 2 minutes. Break it apart if using bulk sausage, or stir links to brown on all sides (about 5 minutes total). Transfer to a plate.

2. **Aromatics:** Reduce heat to medium. In the same pan (don't clean it - those brown bits are flavor), add diced onion. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 30-45 seconds until fragrant.

3. **Tomato Paste:** Add tomato paste, oregano, thyme, and red pepper flakes. Stir constantly for 1 minute. This blooms the spices and tomato and prevents them from being raw and bitter.

4. **Beans and Stock:** Add beans and chicken stock. Stir to combine. Return sausage to the pan.

5. **Simmer:** Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 8-10 minutes until the broth reduces slightly and the flavors meld. The mixture should be thickened but still saucy.

6. **Brighten:** Remove from heat. Taste for salt and pepper. Add lemon juice and stir. The lemon should pop the dish to life - it's no longer heavy, it's bright.

7. **Serve:** Spoon into bowls. Garnish with fresh parsley and grated Parmesan. Serve with crusty bread for soaking up the broth.

**Leftover Magic:** This tastes even better the next day. Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Reheat gently over medium heat, adding a splash of water or stock if it tightens.

RECIPE: Sausage Breakfast Casserole (sausage-breakfast-casserole.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sausage-breakfast-casserole/
SOURCE: Adapted from thepioneerwoman.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.thepioneerwoman.com/food-cooking/recipes/a37215621/sausage-breakfast-casserole-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Breakfast Sausage (Jimmy Dean Standard)
  - 30 oz Frozen Shredded Hash Browns, thawed
  - 10 large Eggs
  - 1 1/4 cups Heavy Cream (for richness)
  - 2 cups Sharp Cheddar, shredded
  - 4 Scallions, chopped (whites and greens divided)
  - 1 Red Bell Pepper, chopped
  - 1 tbsp Dijon Mustard
  - 2 tsp Hot Sauce (The Finishing Touch)
  - Salt and Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This breakfast casserole is ideal for holiday mornings because it feeds a crowd and can be assembled the night before. Baking covered first sets the egg custard without drying it out, then uncovering and increasing heat to 400°F for the final 15 minutes crisps the hash brown crust on top. Whisking Dijon mustard into the cream cuts through the heavy sausage fat, adding tangy brightness that prevents the dish from feeling overly rich.

## Directions

1.  **The Sear:** In a large skillet, brown the sausage over medium-high until no pink remains. Add the bell pepper and scallion whites; sauté for 3 minutes. Let cool slightly.
2.  **The Emulsion:** In a massive bowl, whisk eggs, heavy cream, mustard, hot sauce, salt, and pepper until very frothy.
3.  **Combine:** Fold in the sausage mixture, 1 1/2 cups of the cheese, and the thawed hash browns.
4.  **Assemble:** Pour into a greased 9x13-inch baking dish. Smooth into an even layer.
5.  **Stage 1:** Cover with foil. Bake at 350°F for 50 minutes.
6.  **Stage 2:** Remove foil. Top with the remaining 1/2 cup cheese. **Increase oven to 400°F**. Bake for 10-15 minutes until the top is deep golden and the center is firm.
7.  **Serve:** Let rest for 10 minutes. Garnish with scallion greens and serve.

RECIPE: Sausage, Shrimp & Quinoa Skillet (sausage-shrimp-and-quinoa-skillet.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sausage-shrimp-and-quinoa-skillet/
SOURCE: Adapted from Myrecipes.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.myrecipes.com/recipe/sausage-shrimp-quinoa-skillet
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Recipe ---
  - 1/2 lb medium shrimp, raw, peeled, deveined and thawed if frozen
  - 6 oz spicy chicken sausage, labeled fully cooked, sliced
  - 3 1/2 cups cooked quinoa, frozen prepared according to package, or properly refrigerated leftovers
  - 1 cup onion, pepper and celery blend, chopped
  - 1 tsp Creole seasoning
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil
  - fresh parsley, for garnish, rinsed and chopped
  - salt, a pinch, to taste
  - black pepper, a pinch, to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Onion, pepper and celery provide the trinity base for the Creole seasoning. Heat the cooked quinoa before adding the shrimp so the shrimp can finish without waiting for a frozen block of grain. Use a labeled fully cooked chicken sausage for the sliced main route. The raw, crumbled-sausage variation follows with its own preparation and quantities.

## Directions

1. **Brown sausage and soften vegetables:** Use spicy chicken sausage, onion, pepper and celery blend, and neutral oil for this stage. Heat the oil over medium-high heat in a large skillet. Add the fully cooked sliced sausage and chopped vegetables; cook, stirring, until sausage is browned and vegetables are tender, beginning checks around 5–7 minutes. Lower heat if the pan scorches.
2. **Add seasoning:** Stir in Creole seasoning briefly until fragrant, about 30 seconds, without burning it.
3. **Heat the cooked grain:** Add cooked quinoa, breaking up clumps. Stir until hot throughout; for refrigerated leftovers check 165°F / 74°C in several places. Follow frozen-product heating instructions rather than treating two minutes as sufficient for every frozen load.
4. **Cook shrimp:** Add medium shrimp. Turn through the hot grain mixture until the thickest shrimp is firm, pearly and opaque through its center. Start checking around 2–3 minutes; size, starting temperature and pan load change the time. Keep cooking if centers are translucent.
5. **Finish:** Use fresh parsley, salt, and black pepper for this stage. Taste only after the shrimp are fully cooked. Add the listed salt and pepper allowances if needed, garnish with all the parsley and divide among the listed portions. Serve promptly.

## Raw Chicken-Sausage Variation

For the original four-portion batch of this variation, use 6 ounces raw spicy chicken sausage links with casings removed, one 8-ounce package chopped onion, pepper and celery blend, 1 teaspoon canola oil, the same half-pound shrimp, teaspoon Creole seasoning and 3½ cups frozen cooked quinoa. These replace the primary sliced-sausage, one-cup vegetable and tablespoon-oil choices; do not combine the two shopping amounts. For other quantities, scale each of these source amounts proportionally, keeping the same pan-depth and endpoint constraints. Heat the canola oil over medium heat, add the raw sausage and crumble it. Cook until browned and 165°F / 74°C in the meat, checking beyond the source’s 5–7-minute starting window as needed. Add vegetables and cook until tender, beginning around 3–4 minutes. Add the shrimp and seasoning; begin turning them for about 2–3 minutes. Add the package-prepared cooked quinoa and continue until quinoa is hot throughout and the thickest shrimp is pearly and opaque. Refrigerated leftover quinoa must reach 165°F / 74°C. Package preparation can extend the original source’s short grain-heating interval; do not use a two-minute promise for an arbitrary frozen block. Serve promptly. The primary parsley and salt/pepper finish are optional additions to this separate saved route.

RECIPE: Sauteed Mushrooms with Thyme (sauteed-mushrooms-with-thyme.md)
CUISINES: French, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sauteed-mushrooms-with-thyme/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 lbs Mixed Mushrooms (cremini, shiitake, oyster), cleaned and sliced
  - 3 tbsp Unsalted Butter
  - 1 tbsp Olive Oil
  - 3 cloves Garlic, thinly sliced
  - 4 sprigs Fresh Thyme, leaves stripped
  - 2 tbsp Dry Sherry or White Wine
  - 1 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1/2 tsp Black Pepper
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Parsley, chopped
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A loose single layer gives mushroom surfaces room to brown. Divide the measured oil across the batches, then bring all mushrooms together for the full butter, garlic and thyme finish. Let the pan juices loosen with the sherry or wine rather than treating a thirty-second clock as complete evaporation.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Clean mushrooms, using a brief rinse under running water if needed, then dry their surfaces well. Trim tough shiitake stems and tough oyster bases; slice usable mushrooms into even roughly 1/4-inch pieces. Wash and dry the thyme and parsley.

2. **Brown in batches:** Divide the listed olive oil across the number of batches your skillet needs. Heat a share over medium-high heat until shimmering, not smoking; add a loose single layer of mushrooms. Cook undisturbed about 3–4 minutes until the underside browns, then turn and cook about 2–3 minutes. If released liquid pools, let it evaporate before judging browning. Transfer to a plate and repeat with remaining mushrooms and shares of the same oil; do not spend the full oil amount anew each round.

3. **Butter and aromatics:** Return all mushrooms and their collected juices to the pan; use more vessels if needed for tossing and divide the measured finish among them. Reduce heat to medium. Add all butter, garlic and thyme leaves. Toss about 1–2 minutes until garlic is fragrant and lightly golden; lower heat if butter or garlic darkens quickly.

4. **Deglaze:** Add all the measured sherry or white wine. Stir and scrape loosened browned bits until the sharp wine aroma mellows and no free puddle remains; about 30 seconds is an initial check, not a guarantee of complete evaporation or alcohol removal. Add all measured salt and black pepper.

5. **Finish:** Remove from heat and distribute all parsley over the mushrooms. Serve promptly.

RECIPE: Savory Oatmeal with Egg (savory-oatmeal-with-egg.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/savory-oatmeal-with-egg/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup Old-Fashioned Rolled Oats
  - 2 cups Water or Low-Sodium Chicken Broth
  - 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 2 large Eggs
  - 1 tbsp Unsalted Butter
  - 1 tbsp Olive Oil
  - 2 Scallions, thinly sliced (white and green parts separated)
  - 1 tsp Soy Sauce or Tamari
  - 1/2 tsp Sesame Oil
  - Red Pepper Flakes
  - Freshly Ground Black Pepper
  - Optional: shredded cheddar, crumbled bacon, hot sauce, sliced avocado
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Oatmeal does not have to be sweet. Cooking oats in broth instead of water and topping them with a runny fried egg, scallions, and a drizzle of soy sauce creates a deeply satisfying savory bowl that feels more like congee than breakfast cereal. The oats provide the same comforting starchy base, but the umami from soy sauce and the richness of the egg yolk transform it into something entirely different. A splash of sesame oil at the finish adds a nutty aroma that ties everything together.

## Directions

1.  **Cook the Oats:** In a saucepan, bring water or broth and salt to a boil. Stir in the oats. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the oats are creamy and tender but not mushy.
2.  **Fry the Eggs:** While the oats cook, heat olive oil in a small nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. When the oil shimmers, crack in the eggs. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the whites are fully set and the edges are lacy and crisp, but the yolk is still runny. Season with salt and pepper.
3.  **Finish the Oats:** Remove the oats from heat. Stir in butter, soy sauce, and sesame oil. The butter should melt and make the oats glossy.
4.  **Assemble:** Divide the oats between two bowls. Top each with a fried egg, sliced scallions (both white and green parts), and a pinch of red pepper flakes.
5.  **Serve:** Eat immediately, breaking the yolk so it runs into the oats and creates a rich, silky sauce. Add optional toppings as desired.

RECIPE: Sazerac (sazerac.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sazerac/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 oz rye whiskey (or Cognac for the original recipe)
  - 1/4 oz simple syrup
  - 3 dashes New Orleans-style anise-forward bitters
  - 1-2 dashes aromatic bitters (optional, but traditional)
  - Absinthe or dry anise-flavored spirit for rinsing
  - Lemon peel for garnish
  - Ice
CONTENT:

## Directions

1. **Chill an Old Fashioned:** glass by filling it with ice water or placing it in the freezer.

2. **In a mixing glass,:** combine the rye whiskey, simple syrup, and bitters with ice. Stir well for 20-30 seconds.

3. **Discard the ice water:** from the chilled glass. Add a small amount of absinthe (about 1/4 oz) to the glass and swirl to coat the inside, then discard the excess absinthe.

4. **Strain the stirred whiskey:** mixture into the absinthe-rinsed glass (no ice).

5. **Express a lemon peel:** over the drink by twisting it to release the oils. Discard the peel or rest it on the rim (traditionally, it's discarded).

6. **Serve immediately.:**

## Chef's Note

The Sazerac is one of America's oldest cocktails, created in New Orleans in the 1830s, and it's been the city's official cocktail since 2008. Originally made with Cognac, it switched to rye whiskey when the phylloxera epidemic devastated French vineyards in the 1870s. The drink is named after the Sazerac Coffee House where it was popularized, which itself was named after a brand of Cognac. The absinthe rinse is essential - it provides an aromatic backdrop without overwhelming the whiskey and bitters.

RECIPE: Scallion-Shallot Oil with Crisp Alliums (scallion-shallot-oil.md)
CUISINES: Chinese-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/scallion-shallot-oil/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup (240 ml) neutral oil, such as canola
  - 100 g peeled shallots, sliced evenly about 1–2 mm thick
  - 50 g scallion whites and pale greens, washed, thoroughly dried and thinly sliced
  - 5 g peeled fresh ginger, cut into two thin slices, optional
  - 1/8 tsp fine salt, for the fried solids
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

One small pan yields a cooking oil and a finishing garnish. They need different treatment at the table: use the strained oil where you want an allium aroma, and add solids near serving so they retain their texture. The yield varies with slicing, frying and draining; measure what you actually recover rather than treating the starting oil as the finished amount.

## Directions

1. **Set up before heating:** Slice shallots evenly and dry the washed scallions thoroughly. Place a fine metal sieve over a stable dry heatproof bowl and line a tray with paper towels. Choose a small heavy saucepan with enough headroom for bubbling; ingredients and oil should occupy well under half its depth.
2. **Begin with shallots:** Put oil, shallots and optional ginger in the cold pan. Heat over medium until steady bubbles develop, stirring to separate rings. Reduce to medium-low as needed to maintain a gentle fry without smoking. Cook about 8–12 minutes, until shallots soften and begin to lose their raw white appearance.
3. **Add scallions and watch closely:** Add the dry sliced scallion whites and pale greens carefully. Continue frying about 5–10 minutes, stirring frequently, until shallots are pale golden and scallion pieces begin to color. Lift out any golden pieces early with a dry slotted spoon; do not wait for every piece to turn the same shade. If pieces are still pale and wet, allow more time at controlled heat rather than raising it sharply.
4. **Separate promptly:** Turn off the heat and carefully pour through the metal sieve. Spread the drained solids on the lined tray, discard ginger slices and sprinkle the measured salt over the alliums. Let them cool in one thin layer. Keep the hot oil on a stable surface out of the working area until safe to handle.
5. **Measure and store:** Expect roughly 180–210 ml strained oil and about 1/2 cup loose fried solids, with variation. Once cool enough to package, place oil and solids in separate clean, dry containers, date them and refrigerate promptly. Use within four days or freeze as directed; do not leave the garnish on the counter for several days.

## Using the batch

[Chicken Lo Mein](/mise/recipes/lo-mein) uses **3 tbsp (45 ml) of this strained oil** as its preferred pan oil, with its marinade oil separate. About 180 ml recovered oil supplies four such allocations. Reserve 15 g crisp fried shallots and scallions for the optional lo mein garnish. The all-shallot variation above also works; neutral oil is the lo mein shortcut. Make this condiment ahead, or allow its separate fifty-minute preparation in addition to the dinner time. Start with a teaspoon over a bowl of rice or vegetables and increase to taste. Keep fried solids out of prolonged high-heat searing.

RECIPE: Seafood-Chorizo Tacos (seafood-chorizo-tacos.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/seafood-chorizo-tacos/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/seafood-chorizo-tacos
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Filling and serving ---
  - 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 1/2 lb fresh uncooked chorizo, casings removed and meat crumbled
  - salt, a pinch, for the chorizo
  - black pepper, a pinch, for the chorizo
  - 1 small red onion, minced
  - ground cumin, a pinch
  - 1 garlic clove, minced
  - 1/2 lb raw medium shrimp, shelled, deveined and chopped
  - 1/2 lb cleaned small squid, cut into thin rings
  - 2 tbsp Mexican lager
  - 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
  - salt, to taste
  - black pepper, to taste
  - corn tortillas, for serving
  - avocado, for serving, sliced
  - fresh cilantro, for serving
  - sour cream, for serving
  - lime wedges, for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Fresh Mexican-style chorizo seasons these shrimp-and-squid tacos with its full rendered fat. Cook the sausage before adding the seafood so its endpoint does not force a longer seafood cook. Lager and lime stay in the filling; avocado, cilantro, sour cream and lime wedges complete the tacos.

## Directions

1. **Cook the Chorizo:** Use extra-virgin olive oil, fresh uncooked chorizo, salt, and black pepper at the sausage stage. Heat the oil in a large skillet over moderately high heat, then add the chorizo and its initial salt and pepper. Break up the chorizo as it browns; about 4 minutes is an early check, not guaranteed doneness. Cook fresh pork/beef chorizo to 160°F, or 165°F if its label identifies poultry. Keep the full oil and rendered fat in the pan. Use enough pan area for the actual load, or cook separate proportionate batches with their own full supplies.
2. **Soften the Onion:** Add small red onion and ground cumin and cook about 2 minutes, until onion begins to soften.
3. **Add the Garlic:** Add garlic clove and sauté for 30–45 seconds, until fragrant.
4. **Cook the Seafood:** Add raw medium shrimp, cleaned small squid, and Mexican lager and toss over moderately high heat. Begin checking around 3 minutes; continue as needed for the seafood to reach 145°F. Shrimp should be firm, pearly and opaque, and squid cooked through. Raw size, thin rings and pan loading determine the time; do not stop solely because 3 minutes have passed.
5. **Finish the Filling:** Once sausage and seafood are cooked, stir in fresh lime juice, salt, and black pepper, season to taste and take the skillet off the heat.
6. **Serve:** Use corn tortillas, avocado, fresh cilantro, sour cream, and lime wedges for serving. Warm or char the tortillas in a dry skillet or carefully over a suitable flame, then fill with all the seafood-chorizo mixture and top with the avocado, cilantro and sour cream. Keep the toppings cold until assembly and serve the lime wedges alongside.

## Oil Variation

To make the preparation with half the oil (one tablespoon in the original batch), use half the listed olive oil at the chorizo stage and omit the other half. Keep the full chorizo, seafood and rendered fat, all aromatics, lager and lime, and the same cooking checks and toppings. This is a separate choice; the main preparation uses all the listed oil.

RECIPE: Seared Salmon with Summer Vegetables (seared-salmon-with-summer-vegetables.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/seared-salmon-with-summer-vegetables/
SOURCE: Adapted from Michael Romano, Food & Wine
SOURCE_URL: https://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/seared-salmon-summer-vegetables
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb center-cut salmon fillet, pin bones removed
  - 6 tbsp unsalted butter, cubed and chilled, for finishing the sauce
  - 2 tbsp unsalted butter, for the sauce aromatics
  - 3 tbsp unsalted butter, for mushrooms and corn
  - 1 tbsp unsalted butter, for searing salmon
  - 1 cup red onion, thinly sliced
  - 2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced, for the sauce
  - 1 clove garlic, peeled and left whole, for the spinach
  - 1/4 lb whole shiitake mushrooms, stems reserved and caps quartered
  - 1 medium ripe tomato, coarsely chopped
  - 1 tsp whole black peppercorns
  - 1 bay leaf
  - 1/3 cup balsamic vinegar
  - 1/3 cup water, plus a little only if needed to loosen the sauce
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, for spinach
  - 1 tbsp olive oil, for searing salmon
  - 1 lb fresh spinach, washed and drained
  - 2 cups fresh corn kernels
  - 3 tbsp fresh chives, finely chopped
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Soften the aromatics before reducing the balsamic vinegar, then whisk in cold butter gradually over gentle heat. The sauce should coat the fish without turning oily. Drain the spinach well and cook the salmon last so the vegetables and sauce are ready when the small strips finish.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the components:** Slice the salmon crosswise into similar strips for the intended number of portions. Pat dry and keep cold. Separate the shiitake stems from the quartered caps. Measure each butter and oil allocation, keeping the sauce-finishing butter chilled. Prepare a colander, warm serving plates and a bowl for straining sauce.
2. **Soften and reduce:** Melt **the aromatic butter** in a nonreactive saucepan over medium-low. Add onion, sliced garlic, mushroom stems, tomato, peppercorns and bay leaf. Cook about **10–12 minutes**, stirring, until softened without browning. Add balsamic vinegar and the measured water. Simmer over medium to medium-high about **4–8 minutes**, stirring more often near the end, until syrupy but still moist; do not let it scorch dry.
3. **Finish the sauce:** Turn heat to very low or move off heat if the pan is very hot. Whisk in **the chilled sauce butter** a few cubes at a time, letting each addition blend before adding more. If butter stops softening, briefly return to low heat; do not boil. Strain into the bowl, pressing lightly, and discard solids. Season with salt and pepper. Hold briefly above warm water, with the bowl not touching the water, and stir occasionally while finishing the meal.
4. **Wilt spinach:** Heat **the spinach oil** in a large skillet over medium-high. Add the whole garlic clove and spinach in handfuls, turning with tongs until wilted, about **3–5 minutes**. Remove the garlic, season and transfer spinach to the colander. Let excess liquid drain; keep covered briefly while cooking the next components.
5. **Cook mushrooms and corn:** Carefully wipe the skillet clean. Melt **the vegetable butter** over medium heat. Sauté mushroom caps about **3–4 minutes** until softened, then add corn and cook about **3 minutes** until hot and tender. Season with salt and pepper and transfer to a warm bowl. Do not keep heating solely to force charring.
6. **Sear salmon:** Wipe the skillet if needed and heat **the searing oil and butter** over medium-high, reserving a proportional share of both for each additional batch. Season fish with salt and pepper. When butter foams without scorching, lay in the strips with space between them, in batches if necessary. Cook about **2–3 minutes on the first side**, turn gently, then cook about **2–4 minutes more**, adjusting for thickness. Check representative thick centers from the side for **145°F / 63°C**; lower the heat if the surface browns before the center is ready. Remove each strip as it finishes.
7. **Plate promptly:** Divide drained spinach, corn and mushrooms among the intended portions, add salmon, then spoon over balsamic butter sauce. Sprinkle with chives. Serve immediately; this sauce is intended for a short finish at the stove, not extended warm holding.

Adapted from [Michael Romano’s recipe at Food & Wine](https://www.foodandwine.com/seared-salmon-with-summer-vegetables-12016370).

RECIPE: Seared Scallops with Corn & Avocado Relish (seared-scallops-with-a-corn-bacon-and-avocado-relish.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/seared-scallops-with-a-corn-bacon-and-avocado-relish/
SOURCE: Adapted from foodnetwork.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/seared-scallops-with-a-corn-bacon-and-avocado-relish-3414406
INGREDIENTS:
  - 16 dry sea scallops
  - 4 ears fresh corn, shucked
  - 12 strips bacon, fully cooked and chopped
  - 2 ripe avocados, diced
  - 1 red bell pepper, diced
  - 1 small onion, diced
  - 1 lemon, halved
  - 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, divided
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil, for the corn skillet
  - Neutral oil, as needed to coat the scallop skillet
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste, for the relish
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste, for the scallops
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Dry sea scallops and a dry surface help the pan brown them, but a golden crust does not establish that the centers are cooked. The corn relish uses the full cooked bacon and avocado; sauté the corn and onion in neutral oil, then fold in the bacon and avocado off the heat. Lemon and parsley finish both components.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the Relish:** Use an upside-down small bowl inside a large bowl as a stand to cut corn kernels off the cobs. Add diced onion, bell pepper and half the measured parsley. Have the fully cooked chopped bacon and diced avocado ready. Pat the scallops dry with paper towels and keep them refrigerated until searing.

2. **Sauté:** Heat the measured corn oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the corn mixture for about 5 minutes, stirring, until the onion begins to soften; caramelization is optional, not a stopping requirement. Use more pan space or separate proportional batches if crowded. Take off the heat and let cool for about 2 minutes before folding in the avocado.

3. **Finish the Relish:** Fold all the diced avocado and fully cooked bacon into the warm corn mixture. Season with the relish salt and pepper to taste. Keep the relish and serving utensils away from raw scallops.

4. **Sear the Scallops:** Wipe the skillet and coat with the separate searing oil over medium-high heat. Season scallops with their salt and pepper allowance. Add in a single uncrowded layer; use additional pans or batches as needed. Sear until the underside develops a golden crust, then turn. Check the center of a thick scallop with an instant-read thermometer inserted from the side; cook to 145°F. The flesh should be firm, pearly, and opaque throughout. Lower the heat if the crust darkens before the center is done. Remove each scallop as it finishes; size and pan heat determine the time. Let them stand on a clean plate while you divide the relish.

5. **Assemble:** Divide all the warm corn-avocado-bacon relish among the portions, then add the measured scallops. The original batch plans four scallops per portion; portion sizes depend on actual scallop size.

6. **Finish:** Squeeze the measured lemon over the scallops and garnish with the remaining half of the parsley. Serve promptly.

## Relish Variation

For the original relish preparation, use medium onion in place of the listed small-onion quantity, and use enough neutral oil to coat the corn pan in place of the measured corn oil. Keep the full corn, bacon, avocado, pepper, parsley, lemon and scallop quantities. Use the same separate searing oil, doneness checks and batch guidance.

RECIPE: Seasoned Bean Sprouts (Kongnamul Namul) (seasoned-bean-sprouts.md)
CUISINES: Korean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/seasoned-bean-sprouts/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb soybean sprouts (kongnamul), rinsed and drained
  - 1/2 cup water, for cooking
  - 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1 tsp garlic, minced
  - 1/2 tsp fine sea salt, divided and added to taste
  - 1 green onion, minced
  - 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Kongnamul has larger yellow bean heads than mung bean sprouts. Give those heads time to cook through, then drain before seasoning. This mild version keeps the original sesame oil, garlic and green onion, with salt added gradually after cooking.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Rinse sprouts, discard damaged or spoiled ones and drain. Put them in a medium pot with the measured cooking water and a small pinch taken from the measured salt.
2. **Cook thoroughly:** Cover and heat over medium-high until bubbling and steaming, then maintain steady steam without boiling dry. Allow roughly 10 minutes of covered heating and cooking, continuing until the soybean heads are tender and the sprouts are steaming hot throughout and above 165°F / 74°C. Check the sprouts themselves with a food thermometer and follow any longer package cooking directions; do not deliberately leave the sprouts lightly cooked. Open the lid if needed to check water or doneness, keeping your face away from steam.
3. **Drain:** Drain in a clean colander and let excess steam escape briefly. Use clean utensils for the cooked sprouts.
4. **Season:** Toss with the sesame oil, garlic, green onion and sesame seeds. Add the remaining measured salt gradually to taste; it need not all be used.
5. **Serve or chill:** Serve warm as a small side, or spread in a shallow container and refrigerate promptly for a chilled banchan. People at higher risk of foodborne illness should avoid raw or lightly cooked sprouts.

## Cooking Notes

Allow about 20 minutes for rinsing, heating, roughly 10 minutes covered cooking, draining and mixing. Heat-up and tenderness vary with the pot and batch size; allow longer when needed. Optional chilling is additional.

Cool in a shallow container and refrigerate promptly at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use within 2 days for quality. Avoid leaving out more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C.

## Sources

- [Maangchi — Soybean sprout side dish, covered cooking reference](https://www.maangchi.com/recipe/kongnamul-muchim)

RECIPE: Sesame-Roasted Shelled Edamame (sesame-roasted-edamame.md)
CUISINES: Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sesame-roasted-edamame/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 450 g frozen unsalted shelled edamame, prepared according to the package before roasting
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil
  - 2 tsp light soy sauce
  - 1/4 tsp garlic powder
  - 2 tsp toasted sesame oil, for finishing
  - 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
  - 1/8 tsp fine salt, only if needed
  - 1/8 tsp red pepper flakes, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Shelled edamame and pods have different yields and roasting behavior. This recipe uses edible beans, with a drier surface and some browned spots after roasting. It does not promise the hard crunch or storage life of packaged dry-roasted edamame. Dry the prepared beans well, spread them out, and add toasted sesame oil at the finish for aroma.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the beans:** Heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Read the edamame package. If it requires cooking, cook as directed before roasting; drain afterward. If it is explicitly ready to eat, thaw as directed or overnight in the refrigerator and drain. Do not assume every frozen product has the same preparation status.
2. **Dry and season:** Spread beans on a clean towel, blot thoroughly and let steam escape briefly if hot. Toss with neutral oil, soy sauce and garlic powder. Spread in a single layer on a parchment-lined rimmed half-sheet pan.
3. **Roast and check:** Roast about 30–40 minutes, stirring after 15 minutes and checking regularly thereafter. Stop when the surface is drier with light brown patches and a cooled sample bean has a pleasant firm center. Some edges may crisp; do not keep baking solely to make every bean hard and crunchy.
4. **Finish:** Toss warm beans with toasted sesame oil, toasted sesame seeds and optional pepper flakes. Taste and add the measured salt only if needed. Divide into four side portions and serve soon. Refrigerate leftovers promptly rather than leaving them out as a pantry snack.

RECIPE: Sesame Tomato Salad (sesame-tomato-salad.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sesame-tomato-salad/
SOURCE: Adapted from The New York Times, Sesame Tomato Salad
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024154-sesame-tomato-salad?smid=ck-recipe-iOS-share
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 lb mixed ripe tomatoes, large tomatoes cored and sliced or chopped, small tomatoes halved
  - 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
  - 2 tbsp toasted sesame oil
  - 6 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
  - 2 tbsp distilled white vinegar
  - 1 clove garlic, minced
  - 1 tsp granulated sugar
  - 1/4 cup fresh basil, chopped
  - Flaky salt, only if needed after tasting
  - Black pepper, to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The dressing is deliberately generous, but only part goes on the tomatoes at first. Their juices join the soy and sesame during a short rest; offer the remainder separately and taste before adding flaky salt. Adapted from [The New York Times’ Sesame Tomato Salad](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024154-sesame-tomato-salad).

## Directions

1. **Mix dressing:** Whisk olive oil, toasted sesame oil, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic and sugar until the sugar dissolves and the liquids combine. Set aside; whisk again before using if separated.

2. **Prepare tomatoes:** Wash and dry tomatoes, core large ones and slice or chop them; halve small tomatoes. Arrange on a wide shallow platter without piling them deeply.

3. **Dress and rest:** Spoon about half the dressing over the tomatoes. Let stand about 5 minutes so the tomato juices mingle with it. Keep the rest of the dressing in a separate serving bowl.

4. **Finish:** Scatter with basil and black pepper. Taste a dressed tomato before adding any flaky salt; it may not need more. Serve promptly with the remaining dressing on the side.

RECIPE: Shakshuka (shakshuka.md)
CUISINES: Middle Eastern, Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shakshuka/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 tbsp Olive Oil
  - 1 medium Yellow Onion, diced
  - 1 Red Bell Pepper, diced
  - 4 cloves Garlic, thinly sliced
  - 1 tsp Ground Cumin
  - 1 tsp Smoked Paprika
  - 1/2 tsp Ground Coriander
  - 1/4 tsp Cayenne Pepper (or to taste)
  - 1 (28 oz) can Crushed Tomatoes (San Marzano preferred)
  - 1 tsp Sugar
  - 1 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 6 large Eggs
  - 1/4 cup Fresh Cilantro or Parsley, chopped
  - 2 tbsp Crumbled Feta (optional)
  - Crusty bread for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Shakshuka is a North African dish of eggs poached in spiced tomato sauce that has become a staple across the Middle East, especially in Israeli cuisine. The sauce must be thick enough to cradle the eggs -- if it is too thin, the whites spread and cook unevenly. Building the spice base by blooming cumin, paprika, and coriander in hot oil before adding tomatoes creates a deeper, rounder flavor than simply stirring spices into sauce. The tomato base (without eggs) can be made ahead and refrigerated for up to 3 days, making this an ideal make-ahead weeknight dinner or weekend brunch.

## Directions

1.  **Build the Base:** Heat olive oil in a large (10-12 inch) skillet over medium heat. Add onion and bell pepper. Cook for 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and the onion is translucent.
2.  **Bloom Spices:** Add cumin, paprika, coriander, and cayenne. Stir for 1 minute until very fragrant -- the spices should darken slightly and smell toasty. Add garlic and stir for 30-45 seconds.
3.  **Simmer the Sauce:** Pour in crushed tomatoes. Add sugar and salt. Stir well and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened and reduced slightly. You should be able to drag a spoon through it and see the bottom of the pan for a moment.
4.  **Create Wells:** Using the back of a large spoon, make 6 evenly spaced wells in the sauce. Crack one egg into each well.
5.  **Poach the Eggs:** Cover the skillet with a lid. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook for 5-8 minutes depending on your preference: 5 minutes for very runny yolks, 7-8 minutes for yolks that are jammy and just set. Check at 5 minutes -- the whites should be fully opaque.
6.  **Finish:** Remove from heat. Scatter with cilantro and feta. Serve immediately, straight from the skillet, with crusty bread for scooping.

RECIPE: Shaved Brussels Sprout Salad (shaved-brussels-sprout-salad-with-apples-and-pecorino.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shaved-brussels-sprout-salad-with-apples-and-pecorino/
SOURCE: Adapted from Loveandoliveoil.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.loveandoliveoil.com/2013/04/shaved-brussels-sprout-salad.html
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Brussels Sprouts, shaved paper-thin
  - 1 Granny Smith Apple, matchsticked
  - 1 cup Pecorino Romano, finely grated (about 3 oz)
  - 1/4 cup Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 3 tbsp Apple Cider Vinegar
  - 2 tbsp Honey
  - Salt and Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Shave Brussels sprouts into thin strands so a short dressed rest softens them without losing all their crunch. Set aside a little dressing for the apple before tossing the sprouts, then combine everything gently and add the full measured Pecorino. The cheese supplies salt, so taste before adding extra seasoning.

## Directions

1. **Mix dressing:** Whisk apple cider vinegar and honey in a large bowl, then drizzle in the oil while whisking. Add the listed salt and pepper to taste, remembering that Pecorino will add salt. The dressing can separate during standing; whisk again when needed.

2. **Prepare apple:** Core the apple and cut fine matchsticks. Move a small portion of the prepared dressing into a separate bowl (about 1 tbsp at the original batch) and toss with the apple. Keep this apple bowl aside; its dressing is taken from the measured total.

3. **Shave sprouts:** Trim tough bases and damaged leaves from washed, dried Brussels sprouts. Use a mandoline with its guard or a sharp knife to shave thinly; discard large hard core pieces.

4. **Dress and rest:** Toss sprouts with the dressing remaining in the large bowl until evenly coated. Let stand 15 minutes, or cover and refrigerate for that interval if preparing ahead.

5. **Finish:** Add the apple and all its reserved dressing to the sprouts, then add the full measured finely grated Pecorino. Toss gently to distribute.

6. **Serve:** Taste before adding any extra salt or pepper. Serve now, or keep refrigerated if waiting; serve cool if preferred without treating additional chilling as part of the 30 minute schedule.

RECIPE: Shaved Fennel Citrus Salad (shaved-fennel-citrus-salad.md)
CUISINES: Italian, Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shaved-fennel-citrus-salad/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 large fennel bulbs, stalks removed, tender fronds reserved
  - 2 large navel or Cara Cara oranges
  - 1 small grapefruit, optional
  - 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
  - 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 1 tbsp reserved citrus juice, collected while preparing the oranges or grapefruit
  - 1 tsp honey or agave syrup
  - 1/4 tsp kosher salt, added gradually to taste
  - 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
  - 2 tbsp shaved Parmesan; choose vegetarian-rennet cheese for a vegetarian version, or omit for vegan
  - 1/4 cup pitted Castelvetrano olives, halved, optional
  - Cold water and ice, only if crisping the shaved fennel
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Thin fennel ribbons bring anise flavor and crunch, while citrus adds juice and sweetness. A short ice bath can refresh the shaved fennel, but dry it well afterward. Add dressing gradually and taste with the olives and cheese before using all the salt.

## Directions

1. **Shave fennel:** Wash the bulbs and fronds. Trim stalks and damaged outer layers, halve the bulbs lengthwise and cut out the hard core. Shave thinly with a sharp knife or a guarded mandoline. If the ribbons need crisping, immerse in ice water for **5–10 minutes** while preparing the citrus; drain and spin or pat thoroughly dry.
2. **Segment citrus:** Cut the tops and bottoms off the oranges and optional grapefruit. Set on a flat cut end and slice away peel and white pith. Over a bowl, cut between membranes to release segments. Squeeze the remaining membranes to collect juice, and measure the listed amount for the dressing. Reserve any excess juice for another use, rather than pouring it all over the salad.
3. **Whisk dressing:** Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, **the measured reserved citrus juice**, honey or agave, pepper and **half the salt**. Taste with a fennel ribbon. The dressing should be bright but not harsh; the cheese and optional olives will add more salt.
4. **Assemble and taste:** Spread dried fennel on a broad platter and arrange citrus segments over it. Add optional olives. Drizzle about **half the dressing**, turn gently and taste a complete bite with a little Parmesan if using. Add more dressing and the remaining salt only as needed. Offer unused dressing separately. Finish with the Parmesan and reserved tender fronds and serve promptly.

RECIPE: Roasted Chicken, Broccoli and Cheddar Bake (sheet-pan-chicken-broccoli.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sheet-pan-chicken-broccoli/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken and broccoli ---
  - 680 g (1 1/2 lb) boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
  - 450 g broccoli florets, cut into even 1 1/2-inch pieces, washed and dried
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, divided
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper, divided
  - --- Cheddar sauce ---
  - 2 tbsp (28 g) unsalted butter
  - 2 tbsp (16 g) all-purpose flour
  - 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) low-sodium chicken broth
  - 115 g sharp Cheddar, grated
  - 1/2 tsp garlic powder
  - --- Topping ---
  - 1/2 cup (30 g) panko breadcrumbs
  - 1 tbsp olive oil
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Roasting before adding sauce gives broccoli and chicken some browned flavor. The broth-based roux then thickens the liquid around the cheese, so the finished bake is creamy without relying on condensed soup. This is a casserole with a roasting stage; it needs two trays, a saucepan and a baking dish.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the trays and topping:** Heat oven to 425°F / 220°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Toss chicken on one tray with 1 tbsp oil and half the salt and pepper. Toss dry broccoli on the other tray with the remaining tablespoon oil and salt/pepper. Spread both out. Mix panko with its separate tablespoon oil.
2. **Roast independently:** Roast both trays, swapping rack positions once. Start checking broccoli at 15 minutes and chicken at 18 minutes. Remove broccoli when barely tender with browned tips, usually 15–20 minutes. Chicken may need 18–25 minutes; check thick pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Remove each tray when ready rather than waiting for them to match.
3. **Make sauce during roasting:** Melt butter in a saucepan over medium-low. Whisk in flour and cook 1–2 minutes without darkening. Add broth gradually, whisking smooth after each addition. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 3–4 minutes, stirring, until thickened enough to coat a spoon. Remove from heat, wait for bubbling to subside and stir in Cheddar a handful at a time, then garlic powder.
4. **Assemble:** Put roasted chicken and broccoli in a 3-quart baking dish. Pour over the sauce and fold gently to coat. Scatter the oiled panko evenly over the top. Use a dish deep enough to contain the sauce without packing the food tightly.
5. **Bake and serve:** Return to the 425°F oven for about 10–15 minutes, until panko is golden, edges bubble and the center reaches 165°F / 74°C. If the topping colors early, shield it loosely with foil. Let stand about 5 minutes before portioning into four servings; handle the hot dish carefully.

RECIPE: Sheet Pan Chicken Fajitas (sheet-pan-chicken-fajitas.md)
CUISINES: Mexican, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sheet-pan-chicken-fajitas/
SOURCE: Adapted from Natalie Mortimer at The Modern Proper
SOURCE_URL: https://themodernproper.com/sheet-pan-chicken-fajitas
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 lb (907 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, trimmed
  - 1 red bell pepper, stemmed, seeded and sliced
  - 1 yellow bell pepper, stemmed, seeded and sliced
  - 1 green bell pepper, stemmed, seeded and sliced
  - 1 red onion, peeled and sliced
  - 1 tbsp olive oil, for coating the filling
  - 1 tsp olive oil, for the two pans
  - 2 tbsp fresh lime juice, divided
  - --- Seasoning ---
  - 1 1/2 tsp ground ancho chile, without salt or other seasonings
  - 1 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
  - 1 1/2 tsp ground cumin
  - 1 1/2 tsp onion powder
  - 1 1/2 tsp garlic powder
  - 1 1/2 tsp dried oregano
  - 1 1/2 tsp fine salt
  - 3/4 tsp ground black pepper
  - --- To Serve ---
  - 12 flour tortillas, about 6 inches across
  - Ripe avocado, sliced, optional, for serving
  - Fresh cilantro, chopped, for serving
  - Salsa or hot sauce, optional, for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

These Tex-Mex chicken fajitas use the oven for the peppers, onion and chicken together. Two pans leave room for the filling to roast, though the vegetables will still release some juice. Add half the lime before cooking and the rest afterward; broiling is optional, and the skinless chicken does not need a crisp crust.

## Directions

1. **Heat the oven and prepare toppings:** Heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Lightly coat the two rimmed pans, or their foil liners, with the separate teaspoon of oil, dividing it equally. Chop cilantro and set out the tortillas; keep the avocado whole until near service.
2. **Cut and season:** Slice peppers into 1/4-inch-wide strips and onion into 1/4-inch slices, separating the layers. Pat chicken dry and cut across the grain into strips about 1/2 inch thick and 2–3 inches long; split very thick breast sections horizontally first. Mix all eight seasonings in the large bowl with the filling's tablespoon of oil and half the lime juice. Add chicken, peppers and onion and toss thoroughly. Roast as soon as the oven is ready, or cover and refrigerate briefly while it finishes heating.
3. **Load both pans:** Divide the filling evenly between the pans, keeping chicken strips separate and flat. Spread the vegetables around them in a loose layer rather than a heap. Each pan holds about half the chicken, peppers and onion. Wash the raw-food bowl, utensils and preparation surface before they touch cooked food or toppings.
4. **Roast and check:** Roast for about 20–25 minutes, turning the filling and exchanging the upper and lower pans after about 10 minutes. Begin checking chicken at 15 minutes. Insert a thin-tip thermometer sideways into the thickest part of several substantial strips on each pan; every checked strip must reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue cooking any unfinished pan and recheck. The peppers should be tender but still hold their shape. Transfer done chicken to a clean covered bowl if the vegetables need longer.
5. **Optional browning:** Once the chicken is safely cooked, remove it to the clean bowl if not already there. Leave the vegetables spread on their pans, spooning off a large pool of juice if necessary. Broil one pan at a time about 6–8 inches from the element for roughly 1–3 minutes, watching continuously for browned edges. Keep the other pan and chicken out of the broiler. Skip this step if the vegetables already have enough color. Recombine the hot filling and add the remaining lime juice.
6. **Warm tortillas:** While the finished filling is covered for this brief step, microwave the tortillas in stacks of four between lightly damp paper towels for about 30–45 seconds per stack, adding short bursts until hot and flexible. Follow the package if it gives a different method. Wrap the warm stack in a clean towel. For a skillet, warm one or two tortillas at a time in a dry pan over medium-high, about 10–30 seconds per side; allow several extra minutes for all twelve.
7. **Serve:** Slice the optional avocado. Divide the filling among twelve tortillas and add the cilantro and avocado, serving two fajitas per person. Offer any remaining filling alongside; do not overfill a tortilla until it tears. Offer salsa or hot sauce if desired. Rice, beans and guacamole have their own preparation times in the complete dinner plan.

RECIPE: Balsamic Chicken with Tomatoes and Feta (sheet-pan-feta-chicken.md)
CUISINES: Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sheet-pan-feta-chicken/
SOURCE: Adapted from foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.foodandwine.com/sheet-pan-feta-chicken-8673602
INGREDIENTS:
  - 680 g boneless skinless chicken breasts, divided into 4 portions and evened to about 3/4 inch thick
  - 600 g cherry tomatoes, divided
  - 180 g red onion, cut into 1/2-inch wedges
  - 150 g block feta, drained and cut into 4 slabs
  - 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
  - 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar
  - 1 tbsp honey
  - 2 tsp Dijon mustard
  - 1 tsp dried oregano
  - 1/2 tsp garlic powder
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, for the chicken
  - 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
  - 2 tbsp torn fresh basil
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Two additions of tomatoes create a useful texture contrast, but the later tomatoes will be softer than raw ones, not crispy. Feta softens and may color at its edges; a wet tomato tray is not a reliable way to make a crisp cheese crust. Finish each component by its own cue instead of holding cooked chicken in the oven until the picture looks right.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Cut and weigh the vegetables, drain feta, and even the four chicken portions to about 3/4 inch thick. In a clean bowl, whisk balsamic vinegar, honey, Dijon, oregano, garlic powder and 1 tbsp of the oil. Reserve this mixture away from raw meat.
2. **Arrange:** Use the remaining 1 tbsp oil to coat the chicken, onion and 400 g of the tomatoes on a rimmed half-sheet pan. Season chicken with its measured salt and pepper. Spread everything with gaps, keeping vegetables beside rather than piled over the meat. Wash hands and raw-meat utensils.
3. **First roast, then finish:** Roast for twelve minutes. Add the remaining 200 g tomatoes and the four feta slabs in the spaces. Spoon the reserved clean balsamic mixture across chicken, vegetables and cheese. Do not use a raw-contact marinade as a late drizzle.
4. **Measure:** Return to the oven for roughly 13–18 minutes. Start checking the thickest center of every chicken piece from the side after about twenty minutes total roasting, and remove pieces individually once they reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue as needed. Tomatoes should be juicy with some collapsed and some still holding shape, and onion should be tender. If those need longer, leave them in after removing the chicken.
5. **Rest and serve:** Rest cooked chicken five minutes, then divide it with the vegetables, feta and tomato pan juices among four plates. Scatter the two tablespoons basil. Pair with a starch or a simple green salad as needed; an additional whipped-feta dip duplicates the cheese component.

RECIPE: Sheet Pan Italian Sausage Dinner (sheet-pan-italian-sausage-dinner.md)
CUISINES: Italian, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sheet-pan-italian-sausage-dinner/
INGREDIENTS:
  - For the Sausage:
  - 1.5 lbs Italian Sausage Links (sweet or hot, your preference)
  - For the Potatoes:
  - 1.5 lbs Baby Potatoes (halved)
  - 3 tbsp Olive Oil
  - 1 tsp Garlic Powder
  - 1 tsp Italian Seasoning
  - 1 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1/2 tsp Black Pepper
  - For Serving:
  - Steamed broccoli
  - Store-bought dinner rolls
  - Whole grain mustard or Dijon
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This is the ultimate Tuesday night dinner: everything roasts on one pan, the broccoli steams while you wait, and store-bought rolls round it out. The key is getting the potatoes in the oven first - they need a head start to get crispy while the sausages just need to cook through and brown. Use good Italian sausage from the butcher counter (sweet for kids, hot for adults, or one of each). Halving the potatoes gives you more cut surface to crisp up. Piercing the sausages releases fat that bastes the potatoes.

## Directions

1. **Prep:** Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a large sheet pan with parchment.

2. **Season Potatoes:** Toss halved potatoes with olive oil, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on the sheet pan.

3. **Start Potatoes:** Roast potatoes alone for 15 minutes to get a head start on crisping.

4. **Add Sausage:** Remove pan, push potatoes to one side. Add sausage links, piercing each a few times with a fork. Return to oven.

5. **Roast Together:** Roast for 20 more minutes, flipping sausages halfway, until sausages are browned and cooked through (160°F internal) and potatoes are golden and crispy.

6. **Steam Broccoli:** While everything roasts, steam broccoli (about 5 minutes in a steamer basket or microwave).

7. **Serve:** Slice sausages on the bias. Serve with crispy potatoes, steamed broccoli, warm rolls, and mustard on the side.

## Notes

- **Sweet Italian Sausage:** Mild, fennel-forward, kid-friendly
- **Hot Italian Sausage:** Spicy kick, adult-preferred
- **Chicken Sausage:** Use raw chicken sausage only with a measured 165°F center endpoint; fully cooked products follow their package reheating instructions.
- For extra crispy potatoes, boil them first, smash with a fork, then roast at high heat

RECIPE: Sheet Pan Pancakes (sheet-pan-pancakes.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sheet-pan-pancakes/
SOURCE: bellyfull.net
SOURCE_URL: https://bellyfull.net/sheet-pan-pancakes/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups all-purpose flour
  - 1/4 cup brown sugar
  - 2 tablespoons granulated sugar
  - 1 tablespoon baking powder
  - 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt
  - 2 large eggs
  - 1 1/4 cups whole milk
  - 1/4 cup unsalted butter , melted
  - 1 teaspoon vanilla
  - For the Toppings:
  - 1 1/2 tablespoons seedless strawberry jam , slightly warmed
  - 1/4 cup sliced strawberries
  - 1/4 cup chocolate chips
  - 1/4 cup blueberries
  - 1 1/2 tablespoons unsalted butter , melted
  - 1 tablespoon brown sugar
  - 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
  - maple syrup, butter, or powered sugar , for serving
  - Nonstick spray, for greasing the pan
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A single 9-by-13-inch rimmed pan replaces individual griddle batches. Divide the toppings into four areas and keep the batter depth even so all portions bake together.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat oven to 425 degrees F. Coat a 9×13 rimmed sheet pan with nonstick spray, making sure to get the sides and corners. Set aside.

2. **Mix:** In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, brown sugar, granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt. Whisk in the eggs, milk, butter, and vanilla until combined and smooth.

3. **Continue:** Pour batter onto the prepared pan. Tap the pan on the counter a few times to even out and flatten the batter.

4. **Continue:** Now imagine the batter divided into four equal sections.

5. **Continue:** In one section, dollop teaspoons of the strawberry jam, then swirl into the batter using a toothpick, making a marbled pattern. Top with sliced strawberries.

6. **Continue:** In another section, sprinkle with the blueberries.

7. **Continue:** In another section, sprinkle chocolate chips.

8. **Continue:** For the last section, whisk together the melted butter, brown sugar, and cinnamon. Dollop teaspoons of the mixture, then swirl into the batter using a toothpick, making a marbled pattern.

9. **Cook:** Bake for 15-18 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean and the pancake springs back to the touch.

10. **Finish:** Allow to cool for a minute or so, then slice into portions.

11. **Finish:** Serve with your choice of syrup, butter, powdered sugar, or all three!

RECIPE: Sheet Pan Pesto Chicken Bowls (sheet-pan-pesto-chicken-meal-prep-bowls.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sheet-pan-pesto-chicken-meal-prep-bowls/
SOURCE: Adapted from thegirlonbloor.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thegirlonbloor.com/sheet-pan-pesto-chicken-meal-prep-bowls/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 Chicken Breasts, diced into 1-inch cubes
  - 1 lb Fresh Broccoli, cut into florets
  - 1 small Zucchini, thickly sliced
  - 8 oz Mushrooms, halved
  - 1 pint Cherry Tomatoes
  - 1/2 cup Basil Pesto
  - 1/2 cup Parmesan, freshly grated
  - 3 tbsp Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 2 cloves Garlic, minced
  - Salt and Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Make the pesto mixture before handling raw chicken, and keep its bowl and spoon clean. Only measured portions go onto the roasting food; the rest is a separate clean reserve for another meal. Use enough pan space for the full chicken and vegetable load, and follow the chicken temperature and vegetable tenderness rather than a fixed two-stage clock. Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers at 40°F or below and use within 3–4 days; freeze portions intended for later in the week.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 400°F. Keep raw chicken cold until preparation and thaw frozen chicken in the refrigerator. Prepare all the vegetables as listed. Use rimmed pans and parchment rated for 400°F, with enough space to spread the complete load without piling it up; use additional pans for larger batches.

2. **Make and reserve the clean mixture:** Before handling raw chicken, mix all the listed prepared basil pesto, Parmesan, garlic and 2/3 of the olive oil, with salt and pepper to taste. At the original batch this is 2 tbsp of the 3 tbsp oil. With a clean spoon, measure out the two roasting additions into separate small dishes:2 tbsp of the finished mixture for the first stage and another 2 tbsp for the second stage at the original batch, scaled proportionally. Cover and refrigerate all the remaining clean mixture for another meal. Do not dip a raw-contact spoon back into this reserve.

3. **First roasting stage:** Toss all the diced chicken and mushrooms with the remaining 1/3 of the olive oil and the first measured pesto-mixture addition. At the original batch this is 1 tbsp oil and 2 tbsp finished mixture. Spread over the pans and roast for about 10 minutes; the chicken is not yet assumed cooked.

4. **Add the vegetables:** Add all the broccoli, zucchini and cherry tomatoes, and toss with the second measured finished-mixture addition. At the original batch this is 2 tbsp; it comes from the separate clean dish, not a raw-contact reserve. Spread the complete load out again, using another pan if needed.

5. **Finish roasting:** Start checking after another 10 minutes. Continue until each chicken piece reaches 165°F in its thickest part and the vegetables are tender to your liking. Check several pieces in each pan; wet vegetables and crowding can lengthen cooking. If chicken finishes first, move it with clean utensils to a clean plate and continue the vegetables; any vegetable or liquid that contacted raw chicken must also reach 165°F before serving.

6. **Serve or store:** Divide all the roasted chicken and vegetables among the listed bowls. Pasta or rice is a separate accompaniment. Use refrigerated portions within 3–4 days and reheat to 165°F. Freeze later portions; vegetables may soften after reheating. Refrigerate both the meal and the separate clean pesto reserve within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F, at 40°F or below. Use the reserve within the shorter of its pesto product instructions and 3–4 days, or freeze it; it is not included in the served bowl allocation.

RECIPE: Sheet Pan Pineapple Shrimp Tacos (sheet-pan-pineapple-shrimp-tacos.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sheet-pan-pineapple-shrimp-tacos/
SOURCE: Adapted from delish.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.delish.com/cooking/recipe-ideas/a32173924/sheet-pan-pineapple-shrimp-tacos-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Tacos and slaw ---
  - 1 lb raw shrimp, peeled, deveined and tails removed
  - 2 cups fresh pineapple, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
  - 1 medium red onion, sliced
  - 2 tbsp fresh lime juice, for the shrimp
  - 2 garlic cloves, minced
  - 1 tsp kosher salt, for the shrimp
  - 4 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 1 tbsp water, for the onions
  - 2 tsp chili powder
  - 2 tsp ground cumin
  - 1/2 tsp cayenne
  - 1 1/2 cups green cabbage, thinly sliced
  - 1/2 cup fresh cilantro, for the slaw
  - 1 lime, juiced, for the slaw
  - kosher salt, to taste
  - corn tortillas, as needed to serve the filling
  - avocado, to taste, sliced
  - sour cream, to taste
  - lime wedges, for serving, optional
  - fresh cilantro, for serving, chopped, optional
  - radish, for serving, thinly sliced, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

These Mexican-inspired tacos keep shrimp, pineapple and onion in separate areas of the tray. Check the shrimp before waiting for browned pineapple: finished shrimp can come out while the fruit and onion roast longer. Cold cabbage-cilantro slaw supplies the crisp contrast. For less heat, omit the cayenne or reduce the spicy elements.

## Directions

1. **Marinate:** Use raw shrimp, fresh lime juice, garlic cloves, kosher salt, 1/4 of the extra-virgin olive oil, chili powder, ground cumin, and cayenne for the marinade. Pat the thawed shrimp dry, then whisk the marinade oil, lime juice, garlic, salt and spices together before adding the shrimp and tossing to coat. Marinate in the refrigerator for 15 minutes. Heat the oven to 425°F while you prepare the tray and slaw.
2. **Prepare the Tray:** Use fresh pineapple, medium red onion, 1/2 of the extra-virgin olive oil, and water for the onion and pineapple zones. Divide this pan share of oil equally between them; all the water goes with the onion. Spread the marinated shrimp in a third zone, with all its coating. Use additional rimmed trays if the shrimp or vegetables would overlap; divide the full supplies proportionally rather than adding oil.
3. **Roast:** Bake about 12–15 minutes, checking early. The thickest shrimp should reach 145°F with firm, pearly, opaque flesh throughout. Remove finished shrimp with clean utensils to a clean plate. If the pineapple and onion need longer, return their sections to the oven; do not delay the shrimp for a browning target.
4. **Dress the Slaw:** Toss 1/4 of the extra-virgin olive oil, green cabbage, fresh cilantro, lime, and kosher salt together while the tray roasts, using all the juice from the slaw lime, then refrigerate until serving. Keep this ready-to-eat mixture away from the raw-shrimp bowl and utensils.
5. **Assemble:** Warm corn tortillas, then divide the slaw, shrimp, roasted onion and pineapple among them. The taco count depends on tortilla and shrimp size.
6. **Finish:** Top with avocado, sour cream, lime wedges (if using), fresh cilantro (if using), and radish (if using) and serve.

RECIPE: Sheet Pan Shrimp Fajitas (sheet-pan-shrimp-fajitas.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sheet-pan-shrimp-fajitas/
SOURCE: healthyfitnessmeals.com
SOURCE_URL: https://healthyfitnessmeals.com/sheet-pan-shrimp-fajitas/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 pounds raw jumbo shrimp, peeled and deveined
  - 2 bell peppers, seeded and thinly sliced
  - 1 large red or sweet onion, thinly sliced
  - 2 tablespoons olive oil
  - 1 lime, juiced
  - 12 small corn tortillas
  - Lime wedges, for serving, optional
  - --- Seasoning ---
  - 1/2 tbsp chili powder
  - 1 1/2 tsp ground cumin
  - 1 tsp kosher salt
  - 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
  - 1 tbsp smoked paprika
  - 1/2 tsp garlic powder
  - 1/4 tsp onion powder
  - 1/2 tsp dried oregano
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Peppers and onions take longer than shrimp. Roast the vegetables first, then add the shrimp and cook only until opaque. This staging keeps the vegetables tender without leaving the shrimp in the oven for their whole cook.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Heat oven to 425°F. Line a large rimmed sheet pan with parchment rated for that temperature, or use a suitable bare rimmed pan. Mix all the measured spices in a small bowl. Thaw frozen shrimp in the refrigerator and pat dry; remove tails if preferred for tacos.

2. **Roast the Vegetables:** Toss sliced peppers and onion with half the measured oil and about half the seasoning. Spread in one layer, using additional pans if crowded, and roast about 12–15 minutes, until beginning to soften.

4. **Finish:** Roast about 6–10 minutes more, checking early, until the thickest shrimp reach 145°F with pearly, opaque flesh throughout. Remove as soon as done. Warm the measured tortillas separately and serve with all the shrimp and vegetables and optional lime wedges.

RECIPE: Shoyu Tuna Poke Bowl (shoyu-tuna-poke-bowl.md)
CUISINES: Hawaiian-inspired, Japanese-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shoyu-tuna-poke-bowl/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Tuna and dressing ---
  - 450 g boneless, skinless yellowfin tuna suitable for intended raw service; see sourcing note
  - 3 tbsp Japanese soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1 tsp unseasoned rice vinegar
  - 1/2 tsp finely grated fresh ginger
  - 1/2 tsp granulated sugar
  - 1 scallion, thinly sliced
  - --- Rice ---
  - 4 cups freshly cooked [Plain Short-Grain White Rice](/mise/recipes/steamed-white-rice)
  - 2 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar
  - 1 tbsp granulated sugar
  - 1/2 tsp fine sea salt
  - --- Toppings ---
  - 300 g English cucumber, ends trimmed and thinly sliced
  - 150 g frozen unsalted shelled edamame, cooked according to the package and chilled
  - 1 avocado, flesh diced
  - 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
  - 2 tbsp prepared sriracha mayonnaise, optional; check the label
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Poke is seasoned cut seafood from Hawaii; rice and a full set of bowl toppings are a serving format, not its definition. This mild shoyu bowl uses a little sugar and fresh cucumber, keeping chile mayonnaise optional. The dressing seasons the fish but does not make raw fish safe.

## Before buying raw fish

Tell the supplier you intend to eat the tuna raw and ask about its species, handling and applicable parasite controls. “Sushi-grade” or “sashimi-grade” wording alone does not establish those controls. Yellowfin tuna is among the FDA Food Code's specific tuna exemptions from parasite-destruction freezing; that exemption is not a guarantee against other hazards. Do not assume domestic freezing or the vinegar in this recipe makes fish suitable for raw service.

Raw seafood carries risk even with careful sourcing. FDA advises children, pregnant people, older adults and people with weakened immune systems to avoid it. For those diners, choose a fully cooked seafood meal. Keep the raw version a deliberate choice, not a universally child-friendly dinner.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the rice and edamame:** Follow [Plain Short-Grain White Rice](/mise/recipes/steamed-white-rice); its batch starting with 300 g dry rice should provide approximately the four cooked cups needed here, with any extra reserved separately. During soaking/cooking, prepare shelled edamame according to its package, drain and chill promptly in a shallow container. Thaw-only directions apply only to a product explicitly ready to eat.
2. **Season the rice:** Dissolve the rice vinegar, tablespoon of sugar and fine salt together, warming gently if necessary. Measure four cups hot plain rice and fold in this mixture. Spread gently in a wide bowl and let steam escape until the rice is barely warm, about 10 minutes. This brief cooling is part of final preparation, not an extended room-temperature hold.
3. **Prepare the toppings and sauce during the rice process:** While rice soaks or cooks, slice cucumber and scallion using clean equipment. Dice avocado near assembly, before switching to fish. Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, teaspoon of vinegar, ginger, half teaspoon sugar and scallion in a separate bowl. Taste the clean dressing before it touches fish.
4. **Cut and dress the tuna while rice cools:** During the final rice cooling period, on separate clean equipment, cut the cold tuna into 1/2-inch cubes. Fold into the dressing and refrigerate for about 5–10 minutes while setting out the bowls. Exact minute limits are not a safety control, and texture varies with the fish and dressing.
5. **Assemble and eat promptly:** Divide rice, tuna, cucumber, chilled shelled edamame and avocado among three bowls. Lift the fish from its dressing, adding only a little of its coating to each bowl; keep it away from communal toppings. Scatter sesame seeds and offer the measured optional mayonnaise separately. Add fish to rice only when each diner is ready to eat.

## Prepared sushi-rice option

Use four cups of [Sushi Rice (Shari)](/mise/recipes/master-sushi-rice) instead of the plain rice and all three rice-seasoning ingredients. Measure the cooked amount; a full shari recipe makes extra. Do not make both rice preparations.
