RECIPE: Shrimp & Avocado Summer Rolls (shrimp-and-avocado-summer-rolls.md)
CUISINES: Vietnamese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shrimp-and-avocado-summer-rolls/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/shrimp-and-avocado-summer-rolls
INGREDIENTS:
  - 18 medium raw shrimp, fully thawed, peeled, tails removed and deveined
  - 6 round rice paper wrappers, 8–8.5 inches across, plus spares for tears
  - 2 oz dry rice vermicelli noodles
  - 1 Hass avocado, peeled, pitted and thinly sliced
  - 1/3 cup fresh cilantro leaves
  - 1/3 cup fresh mint leaves
  - 1/3 cup fresh chives, snipped
  - --- Dipping sauce ---
  - 1/4 cup sugar
  - 1/4 cup warm water
  - 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
  - 1 Fresno chile, seeded and minced, or Thai bird chile to taste
  - 1 small garlic clove, minced
  - Salt, to taste, for cooking water and dipping sauce
  - Asian chile-garlic sauce, optional, for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Creamy avocado, shrimp, mint, cilantro and chives fill these fresh rice-paper rolls. Their dipping sauce is sweet with lime, chile and garlic. Let the noodles and shrimp cool and drain before assembly, then wet one wrapper at a time; it should finish softening on the board rather than turn limp in the water.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the noodles:** Cook or soak the rice vermicelli according to its package instructions until tender without a hard center. Drain, rinse under cool running water and drain thoroughly. Snip very long strands into manageable lengths; do not try to dry the noodles until hard.
2. **Cook and cool the shrimp:** Bring a saucepan of water to a boil and season lightly with salt. Add the thawed shrimp and reduce to a gentle simmer. Start checking after about 2 minutes; continue until firm, pearly and opaque throughout, checking 145°F / 63°C in the thickest part with a suitable thin probe. Transfer to a clean ice-water bath just until cold, then drain and pat dry. Halve lengthwise using clean utensils.
3. **Make the sauce:** Stir the sugar into the measured warm water until dissolved. Add lime juice, minced chile and garlic. Season with a small pinch of salt to taste. Serve the optional chile-garlic sauce separately.
4. **Portion the fillings:** Slice the avocado and prepare the herbs. Divide all noodles, avocado, cilantro, mint, chives and shrimp equally among the wrappers. Each roll gets six shrimp halves at any batch size. Keep fillings chilled if you pause before assembly.
5. **Wet a wrapper:** Fill a wide shallow dish with water at the temperature recommended on the wrapper package. Briefly wet both sides of one sheet, then lay it flat on a clean smooth work surface. Let it become pliable and slightly tacky before folding; do not leave it soaking until limp.
6. **Fill and roll:** Arrange one portion of noodles, avocado and herbs in a compact strip across the lower third, leaving space at the sides. Arrange its shrimp halves curved side down near the filling. Fold the bottom over, fold in both sides and roll snugly without stretching. Repeat with all fillings; use a spare wrapper if one tears or the filling will not fit comfortably.
7. **Serve:** Keep rolls separate so they do not stick, and serve with the dipping sauce. The stated batch makes six substantial side rolls; for four diners, cut them in half and share three halves per person.

RECIPE: Shrimp and Corn Chowder (shrimp-and-corn-chowder.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shrimp-and-corn-chowder/
SOURCE: Adapted from foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/shrimp-and-corn-chowder
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Main recipe ---
  - 2 lb raw medium shrimp, shelled and deveined; refrigerator-thawed if frozen
  - 6 garlic cloves, minced
  - 2 scallions, minced
  - 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
  - 1 tsp salt
  - 2 cups fresh or thawed frozen corn kernels
  - 2 cups whole milk
  - 2 tbsp prepared annatto oil or olive oil
  - 1/2 cup red onion, finely chopped
  - 1 red bell pepper, finely chopped
  - 1 tsp ground cumin
  - 3 plum tomatoes, peeled, seeded and finely chopped
  - 6 cups fish or chicken stock, canned low-sodium broth is also an option
  - 1 unripe green plantain, peeled and coarsely grated
  - 2 tbsp cilantro leaves
  - 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper
  - salt, to taste after the shrimp are cooked
  - separately prepared tangy corn salsa, as desired for serving, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Adapted from Maricel Presilla’s coastal Ecuadoran chowder. Grated green plantain thickens the corn-and-milk base. The current partly pureed version keeps some whole kernels; add the refrigerated, marinated shrimp only when the soup base is ready, and use their doneness rather than an exact two-minute promise.

## Directions

1. **Marinate:** In a nonreactive bowl, toss together raw medium shrimp, 2/3 of the garlic cloves, scallions, fresh lime juice, and salt. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour; 1–3 hours is also an option. Keep the remaining garlic separate for the soup. The lime seasons the shrimp; it does not replace cooking.
2. **Corn milk:** Near the end of the shrimp's refrigerated marinade, puree 1/2 of the fresh or thawed frozen corn kernels and whole milk in a food processor. Strain through a coarse sieve, pressing the corn solids to extract the liquid. Keep that corn milk for the soup. Refrigerate it if the soup cooking will not begin promptly.
3. **Base:** Use 1/3 of the garlic cloves, prepared annatto oil or olive oil, red onion, red bell pepper, and ground cumin for this stage. In a pot with room for the measured stock, milk, vegetables and shrimp plus stirring headroom, heat the prepared oil over moderate heat, then add the garlic, onion, pepper and cumin. Cook, stirring, until the vegetables soften slightly, about 5 minutes. Divide all supplies proportionally among enough pots or complete batches if the load will not fit.
4. **Tomatoes:** Stir in plum tomatoes and cook about 2 minutes longer.
5. **Simmer:** Add the corn milk and 1/2 of the fresh or thawed frozen corn kernels, fish or chicken stock, and unripe green plantain. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the grated plantain has softened and the soup has thickened.
6. **Refine:** Blend only a portion of the soup for the chunky texture: about 2 cups in the original batch, adjusted with the batch amount. Use a blender whose manual explicitly permits this liquid at its actual temperature. Follow its hot-liquid fill, venting and speed limits, working in batches. Never put hot soup into a sealed blending cup; if the appliance does not allow it, cool the liquid to its permitted temperature before blending. Return all of this blended portion to the pot and bring the complete soup back to a simmer.
7. **Cook shrimp:** Lift the shrimp out of their refrigerated marinade with a utensil reserved for raw seafood, letting excess marinade drain back into the bowl. Transfer the shrimp to a clean covered bowl and keep them refrigerated. Add all the remaining marinade, including its minced garlic and scallions, to the soup and bring it to a rapid boil. Reduce to a gentle simmer, then add all the shrimp. Start checking after 2–3 minutes and continue until the shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout; check thick centers with a thin probe for 145°F / 63°C. Do not taste before the marinade has boiled and the shrimp have cooked.
8. **Serve:** Use cilantro leaves, cayenne pepper, salt, and separately prepared tangy corn salsa (if using) for this finish. Stir the cilantro and cayenne into the soup, then add finishing salt only to taste. Serve in warmed bowls with the optional salsa separately.

## Variations and preparation

For the fuller pureed version, replace the measured chopped onion with one large red onion in the original batch; scale that onion count with the rest of the recipe. Puree all the measured corn with all the milk, then strain as in step 2; do not reserve whole kernels. Add all the cilantro and cayenne with the stock and plantain in step 5 instead of at the finish. After simmering, coarsely strain the soup, blend all the strained vegetables in permitted batches and return both the puree and every bit of strained broth to the pot. Use the same appliance controls as step 6, then simmer and finish the shrimp as in step 7. All other measured supplies, including the full milk, stock and oil, stay the same.

To prepare annatto oil separately, combine **1 cup corn oil and ¼ cup annatto seeds** for one original preparation batch. Bring to a simmer over low heat, remove from the heat, cover and cool completely, about 30 minutes, then strain into a jar. Measure only the listed chowder oil from this preparation; the remaining strained oil is separate from the soup. Store that remaining oil in a tightly sealed jar in the refrigerator for up to 2 months. The seed and input-oil amounts do not establish a measured finished oil yield. Adjust this preparation batch separately if more prepared oil is needed.

RECIPE: Shrimp and Grits (shrimp-and-grits.md)
CUISINES: Southern
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shrimp-and-grits/
SOURCE: Adapted from Bobby Flay’s Shrimp and Grits at Food Network
SOURCE_URL: https://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/bobby-flay/shrimp-and-grits-recipe-1911862
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup dry regular stone-ground grits, with package instructions matching the ratio and simmer time below
  - 4 cups (950 ml) water, for the grits, with package-specific adjustment if needed
  - 1 cup (240 ml) additional hot water, for loosening the grits as needed
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, for the grits, divided and partly added to taste
  - 3 tbsp (42 g) unsalted butter
  - 2 cups (225 g) sharp cheddar, freshly grated
  - 1 lb (450 g) raw peeled, deveined, tail-off shrimp, weighed after thawing and draining; about 31–40 shrimp in this net quantity
  - 120 g regular-cut smoked bacon, diced
  - 1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper, divided
  - 1 cup (100 g) thinly sliced scallions, white and green parts separated
  - 1 large garlic clove, finely minced
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) water, for the shrimp pan
  - 4 tsp fresh lemon juice, divided and partly added to taste
  - 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Southern bowl combines cheddar grits, bacon and shrimp with scallions and lemon. The bacon provides crunch while the shrimp should stay tender. Stone-ground grits vary substantially by mill and particle size, so finish their hydration before starting the quick shrimp stage.

## Directions

1. **Prepare before cooking:** Check that the grits package matches the stated liquid ratio and simmer time. Heat the four cups grits water in a 3-quart heavy saucepan while grating cheddar, dicing bacon and preparing scallions, garlic, parsley and lemon. Heat the additional cup of water in a kettle or microwave and keep covered for adjusting the grits; rewarm if needed. Keep white and green scallion parts separate. Pat thawed peeled shrimp dry and keep refrigerated. Set aside half the black pepper for grits and half for shrimp.
2. **Cook the grits:** Bring the water to a boil, whisk in grits and half the measured salt, then reduce to a gentle low simmer and cover. Stir thoroughly across the bottom every few minutes to prevent sticking. For grits with the stated package method, begin tasting at twenty minutes and allow about twenty to twenty-five; continue longer if the centers are still firm. If it gets thick before tender, add hot water from the listed additional cup in small amounts. The grains should feel tender in a cooled spoonful, not merely absorb all the water.
3. **Cook bacon and finish the base:** While grits simmer, cook diced bacon in the 12-inch skillet over medium heat for about eight to ten minutes, stirring until browned and crisp. Transfer bacon to a plate; carefully measure one tablespoon of rendered fat into a small heatproof cup and pour off the excess, leaving a thin film in the skillet. Discard or separately save the excess fat. Once grits are tender, take them off heat and fold in butter, cheddar and their half of the pepper. Taste before adding the remaining grits salt. Loosen with a little listed hot water if needed so the grits spread softly rather than stand in a firm mound. Cover and keep gently warm while cooking shrimp.
4. **Cook the first shrimp batch:** Heat the skillet with half the reserved tablespoon bacon fat over medium-high heat; keep the other half aside. Add half the shrimp in one layer and cook about one to two minutes per side. Check the thickest centers as described in the next step, then transfer cooked shrimp to a clean plate. They will return only briefly for coating, not simmer through the sauce preparation.
5. **Cook the second batch and check:** Add the remaining reserved fat and shrimp. Cook and turn as before, until the flesh is firm, pearly and opaque through the center. Check several of the largest shrimp with a thin-tip thermometer inserted into the thickest part for 145°F / 63°C; continue any larger or still-translucent pieces until done. Typical cooking is about three to four minutes per batch, but thickness determines it. Transfer this batch to the clean plate.
6. **Make a brief pan coating:** Reduce heat to medium-low. Add scallion whites to the fat film and stir for about one minute, then add garlic for about thirty seconds without browning it. If the pan looks dry, use a teaspoon from the measured pan water while the scallions soften. Add the rest of the separate quarter-cup pan water and scrape up brown, not black, residue; simmer for thirty to sixty seconds. Turn off heat and stir in three teaspoons lemon juice, most of the scallion greens, parsley and the shrimp's half of the pepper. Return shrimp and any juices just long enough to coat. Taste a shrimp with a little grit and add the remaining teaspoon lemon only if needed. Do not salt the topping automatically; bacon and cheese already contribute seasoning.
7. **Serve promptly:** Divide grits among four bowls, top with shrimp and the light pan juices, then scatter over crisp bacon and the reserved scallion greens. Distribute shrimp evenly, roughly eight to ten per bowl for the stated size. Serve a vegetable alongside; the grits provide the starch for the plate.

RECIPE: Shrimp & Mango Tacos (shrimp-and-mango-tacos.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shrimp-and-mango-tacos/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1013581-shrimp-and-mango-tacos?smid=ck-recipe-iOS-share
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Shrimp and mango filling ---
  - 2 tbsp neutral oil
  - 1 lb small shrimp, raw, peeled, deveined and patted dry
  - salt, to taste for the shrimp
  - 2 garlic cloves, sliced
  - 2 tsp cumin seeds, lightly toasted and ground
  - 2 serrano chilies, minced
  - 1 large ripe mango, peeled, pit removed and finely chopped
  - 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, washed and chopped
  - 5 tbsp fresh lime juice
  - salt, to taste after cooking
  - --- Tortillas ---
  - 8 corn tortillas
  - water, enough for the steamer below the basket, if steaming, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Mango stays in small pieces rather than being cooked down into a smooth glaze. Toasted cumin seasons the shrimp, and the full lime juice goes in after cooking. Warm the tortillas before the filling is ready so the shrimp can be served promptly.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Prepare all the filling ingredients before heating the pan. If the cumin is not already toasted, stir the seeds in a dry pan over moderate heat until fragrant, then cool briefly and grind. Keep the measured cumin total unchanged.
2. **Warm the tortillas:** Warm corn tortillas and water (if using): heat tortillas in a towel in short microwave intervals until flexible, starting around 45–60 seconds for the original batch, or char them briefly on a hot dry skillet, turning as needed. For direct-flame warming: use tongs to turn each tortilla briefly over a gas flame until lightly charred and flexible. Keep wrapped and warm. For steaming, set the wrapped tortillas above about 1 inch of boiling water, cover and steam for 1 minute, then turn off the heat and leave covered for 15 minutes; water must not touch the tortillas. More tortillas may need separate loads.
3. **Start the shrimp:** Use neutral oil, small shrimp, salt, and garlic cloves. Heat the measured oil in a large heavy skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add shrimp and the shrimp-seasoning salt. Stir about 1–2 minutes until they begin to color, adding all the garlic during the last 30–45 seconds so it does not scorch. Use a pan that lets you move the shrimp freely, or divide the whole filling across batches.
4. **Add cumin and chili:** Stir in cumin seeds and serrano chilies and cook about 1 minute until fragrant, reducing heat if the garlic is darkening. Continue cooking shrimp as needed rather than using pink edges as the final test.
5. **Add mango and cilantro:** Fold in large ripe mango and fresh cilantro and cook about 1 minute, until the mango edges soften but pieces remain. Cook until the thickest shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout; FDA guidance is 145°F for seafood when checking with a suitable thermometer. Pink color or a fixed minute count alone does not establish doneness.
6. **Finish and serve:** Off heat, stir in fresh lime juice and salt, adding the finishing salt only as needed after tasting cooked filling. Divide all the filling among all the warm tortillas; the original batch provides eight tortillas for four planning portions. Serve promptly, with separately prepared [Mexican Red Rice](/mise/recipes/mexican-red-rice) if wanted.

RECIPE: Shrimp and Snow Pea Noodles (shrimp-and-snow-pea-stir-fry.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shrimp-and-snow-pea-stir-fry/
SOURCE: Adapted from Delish, Shrimp & Snow Pea Stir-Fry
SOURCE_URL: https://www.delish.com/cooking/recipe-ideas/a35131589/shrimp-and-snow-pea-stir-fry-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 8 oz dry rice linguine noodles
  - 8 oz raw shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails removed
  - 8 oz fresh snow peas, strings removed, sliced diagonally
  - 5 tbsp sweet chili sauce, divided
  - 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
  - 1 clove garlic, minced
  - 2 tbsp neutral oil, divided
  - Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
  - Water, for noodle preparation and a small splash if needed in the pan
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Start the rice noodles before preparing the vegetables and shrimp. Hydrate them according to their package, then finish in the pan with the sweet chili coating. Lift cooked shrimp out while the noodles finish so the two ingredients do not have to share one cooking time. Adapted from [Delish’s Shrimp & Snow Pea Stir-Fry](https://www.delish.com/cooking/recipe-ideas/a35131589/shrimp-and-snow-pea-stir-fry-recipe/).

## Directions

1. **Prepare noodles:** Follow the package instructions for stir-fried rice linguine. For a product calling for a hot-water soak, use a heatproof bowl and expect roughly 25 minutes; separate clumps gently with a fork. Drain when nearly tender, rinsing only if directed, and drain thoroughly.

2. **Marinate and prepare:** While noodles hydrate, pat shrimp dry and season lightly with salt and pepper. Toss with one-fifth of the sweet chili sauce and refrigerate for 15 minutes. Trim and slice peas, grate ginger and mince garlic. Mix the remaining four-fifths of the sweet chili sauce with the measured soy sauce in a clean bowl.

3. **Cook shrimp:** Heat half the oil over medium-high. Lift shrimp from the marinade, letting excess drip away; discard the raw-contact marinade. Cook in a single layer about 1–2 minutes per side, as needed, until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean plate. Lower heat if the sweet coating darkens rapidly.

4. **Cook vegetables:** Add remaining oil, snow peas and ginger. Stir-fry about 2 minutes until the peas brighten and retain a little bite. Add garlic and stir for about 30 seconds without letting it burn.

5. **Finish noodles:** Add drained noodles and the clean chili-soy mixture. Lift and turn gently for about 2–4 minutes until hot and tender; use a small splash of water if they stick or need further softening. Avoid vigorous stirring that tears the strands.

6. **Combine:** Return shrimp and plate juices only long enough to warm through, about 30 seconds. Taste before adding any further salt and pepper. Divide noodles and the actual shrimp count evenly among bowls and serve immediately.

RECIPE: Shrimp & Sweet Potato Noodle Stir-Fry (shrimp-and-sweet-potato-noodle-stir-fry.md)
CUISINES: Korean, Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shrimp-and-sweet-potato-noodle-stir-fry/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Velveted Shrimp ---
  - 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
  - 1 tbsp soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp cornstarch
  - --- Noodles ---
  - 8 oz sweet potato glass noodles (dangmyeon)
  - 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - --- Vegetables ---
  - 6 oz snow peas, strings removed
  - 1 large carrot, julienned thin
  - 3 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
  - 4 green onions, whites and greens separated, sliced
  - --- The Sauce (whisk before cooking) ---
  - 3 tbsp soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
  - 1 tbsp honey
  - 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1 tsp fish sauce
  - --- Finish ---
  - 1 lime, cut into wedges
  - Toasted sesame seeds
  - Gochugaru or red pepper flakes (optional, for heat)
  - 2 tbsp high-smoke-point oil (avocado or grapeseed), divided
  - Water, for cooking noodles according to the package
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This shrimp stir-fry combines Korean sweet potato glass noodles with soy, lime and ginger. The noodles stay chewy when cooked to the package’s endpoint and drained well. Keep their sesame oil separate from the sauce oil, and prepare the sauce and vegetables before the shrimp enter the pan. The cornstarch coating joins the sauce during the final toss; cook the shrimp centers through without waiting for char or a particular curl.

## Directions

1. **Coat and stage:** Pat the prepared raw shrimp dry with paper towels. Toss large shrimp, soy sauce, and cornstarch until evenly coated. Keep chilled during the 10-minute stand while preparing the other ingredients; cook promptly after preparation. Keep coating and sauce soy sauce separate.
2. **Cook noodles:** Have sweet potato glass noodles (dangmyeon), toasted sesame oil, and water ready for the noodles. Boil the noodles following the package for water, timing and any rinse instruction, checking for pliable, springy noodles without a hard center. Drain thoroughly and toss with their measured sesame oil. Start checking around 6–7 minutes only if consistent with the actual package.
3. **Whisk sauce:** Whisk soy sauce, fresh lime juice, honey, toasted sesame oil, and fish sauce until the honey disperses; keep beside the stove.
4. **Start shrimp:** Heat a wok or heavy skillet over medium-high to high heat appropriate to the pan, following its preheating instructions; keep the oil below its smoke point. Add 1/2 of the high-smoke-point oil (avocado or grapeseed), reserving the other half of this oil for aromatics. Spread the coated shrimp into a single layer, using batches and dividing this oil allowance across them if needed. Cook about 1 minute per side as an initial check, until the surface changes color; transfer immediately to a temporary dish for further cooking in step 7. Do not taste partly cooked shrimp.
5. **Cook aromatics:** Add 1/2 of the high-smoke-point oil (avocado or grapeseed), garlic cloves, fresh ginger, the green-onion whites, and gochugaru or red pepper flakes (if using) to the pan. Keep all green-onion greens for finishing. Stir about 30 seconds until fragrant, reducing heat if garlic begins to brown too quickly.
6. **Cook vegetables:** Add large carrot and snow peas, carrots first for about 2 minutes, then snow peas for another 1–2 minutes, stirring until crisp-tender. These are first checks, not fixed endpoints for every cut.
7. **Toss and finish cooking:** Return all noodles, shrimp and collected shrimp juices to the pan. Add all the sauce and lift/toss to distribute it, starting to check after 1–2 minutes. Cook until the thickest shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout; FDA guidance is 145°F for seafood when checking with a suitable thermometer. Pink color or a fixed minute count alone does not establish doneness. The sauce should coat the noodles without dry starch patches. A larger batch needs separate complete pan loads; do not crowd the final toss after batching shrimp.
8. **Finish:** Finish with the green-onion greens, lime, and toasted sesame seeds: fold in all green-onion greens, scatter sesame seeds as wanted, and offer the lime wedges for squeezing to taste. This lime is separate from the measured sauce juice. Transfer to a clean serving dish and serve promptly.

RECIPE: Shrimp Fettuccine Alfredo (shrimp-fettuccine-alfredo.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shrimp-fettuccine-alfredo/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Fettuccine Pasta
  - 1 lb Raw Jumbo Shrimp, peeled and deveined
  - 2 tbsp Olive Oil
  - 1 tsp Garlic Powder
  - Salt and Black Pepper
  - 1 batch Alfredo Sauce (See note)
  - Fresh Parsley, chopped
  - Water, as needed to boil pasta
  - 1/2 cup Pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; one shared supply for sauce and final toss
  - Water, a little as needed when reheating leftovers
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Prepare the full linked Alfredo batch and cook the shrimp just until firm and pearly opaque through their thickest centers. Pasta, shrimp and sauce can overlap, but the scratch sauce needs its own preparation time. The same-skillet route keeps the browned shrimp bits; finish heating the cream base before taking the pan off the heat for the Parmesan.

## Directions

1. For the scratch version, read the complete [Alfredo Sauce](/mise/recipes/real-alfredo-sauce) first and grate its Parmesan. Make one full linked batch for this original four-serving pasta recipe, matching the same scaling factor for both recipes. Use its full butter, cream and Parmesan amounts. Bring pasta water to a boil, using part of the listed salt allowance, and cook fettuccine according to its package. Reserve the listed pasta-water supply before draining.
2. Use raw peeled, deveined shrimp; if frozen, thaw in the refrigerator first and drain. Toss with the garlic powder and some of the remaining salt and black pepper. Keep the raw-shrimp bowl and utensils separate from the cooked-shrimp plate.
3. Heat some of the total olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook shrimp in uncrowded loads, dividing the same total oil across loads. Turn as needed, beginning checks around 2 minutes per side; time depends on size and pan heat. Continue until the thick centers are firm and pearly opaque. Move fully cooked shrimp to a clean plate.
4. For scratch sauce, follow the linked complete butter–cream–garlic stage in the shrimp skillet. Before the offheat Parmesan stage, simmer the cream base as directed and verify it reaches at least 145°F /63°C so liquid in the raw-contact pan is heated as well; then melt the Parmesan gently as the linked recipe directs. Alternatively, prepare that same complete batch in a separate clean saucepan. The sauce recipe can use up to ¼ cup of the original ½-cup shared pasta-water reserve; keep the rest for the final toss. Do not add the sauce allowance on top of the pasta reserve.
5. Toss the hot pasta and fully cooked shrimp with the sauce. Add remaining shared pasta water a little at a time if needed to loosen; not all of it may be necessary. Adjust with the remaining salt and pepper allowance without adding another fixed dose.
6. Top with the chopped parsley and serve immediately.

RECIPE: Shrimp Linguine with Fresh Tomato, White Wine & Basil (shrimp-linguine-with-fresh-tomato-and-basil.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shrimp-linguine-with-fresh-tomato-and-basil/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb raw large shrimp, weighed after peeling and deveining, shells reserved
  - 1 tsp kosher salt, for seasoning shrimp
  - 1/4 tsp baking soda, optional
  - 1 1/2 cups water, for shell stock
  - 1 lb fresh spinach linguine
  - 2 shallots, finely minced
  - 4 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
  - 7 Roma tomatoes, grated, skins discarded
  - 3/4 cup dry white wine, divided
  - 4 oz baby spinach
  - 1/2 to 3/4 tsp crushed red pepper
  - 1 tsp olive oil, for shell stock
  - 1 tbsp olive oil, for cooking shrimp
  - 5 tsp olive oil, for shallots
  - 5 tbsp cold unsalted butter, divided
  - Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
  - 1 lemon, finely zest the whole fruit and juice half
  - 1/3 cup fresh basil, torn, divided
  - Extra-virgin olive oil, optional, for finishing
  - 2 cups reserved pasta cooking water, use only as needed
  - 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs, optional topping
  - 1 clove garlic, grated, for the optional topping
  - 1 tbsp olive oil, for the optional topping
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A quick shell stock gives the tomato sauce a seafood base, while butter rounds out the grated tomatoes and wine. Get the sauce ready before cooking the fresh linguine, then use pasta water sparingly and finish off heat. The optional garlic breadcrumbs add a crisp contrast.

## Directions

1. **Peel and season:** Peel and devein shrimp, reserving shells. Toss peeled meat with the measured shrimp salt and optional baking soda. Refrigerate for 15–30 minutes while preparing the stock and vegetables. Wash raw-contact tools and pat shrimp dry just before cooking.

2. **Make shell stock:** Heat the oil labeled for stock in a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir shells for about 2–3 minutes until pink and aromatic. Add a small splash taken from the measured wine and all the stock water. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 15 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh strainer, pressing shells, then discard shells. Measure the liquid and reduce to half the starting water volume if necessary; add a little water if reduced below that target.

3. **Prepare optional topping:** If using it, warm the topping oil in the skillet over medium-low. Toast panko, stirring, until beginning to turn golden, about 2–3 minutes. Add the grated topping garlic and a little salt and stir about 30–60 seconds more until fragrant and golden. Transfer to a bowl. Meanwhile have tomatoes grated, shallots and garlic prepared and pasta water heating.

4. **Cook shrimp:** Add the oil labeled for shrimp to the skillet over medium-high. Cook shrimp in a single layer about 1–2 minutes per side or as needed until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Use batches if crowded, sharing the oil. Transfer to a clean plate.

5. **Soften aromatics:** Lower heat to medium. Add shallot oil and one-fifth of the butter. Cook shallots about 4–5 minutes until softened, then add sliced garlic and crushed red pepper and stir about 30–45 seconds until fragrant without darkening.

6. **Build tomato sauce:** Add all remaining measured wine and simmer about 2–4 minutes until reduced by roughly half. Add grated tomatoes with their juices and the measured finished stock. Simmer gently about 10–15 minutes until lightly thickened and flowing. Taste before adding salt and pepper.

7. **Cook pasta:** When sauce is ready, stir in baby spinach until wilted. Cook fresh linguine in salted boiling water according to its package, checking early and stopping just short of fully tender. Reserve the listed pasta water before draining. Do not assume every fresh noodle cooks in two minutes.

8. **Finish off heat:** Add pasta to sauce and turn gently, using a small splash of reserved water if needed. When the pasta is tender, remove from heat and add remaining four-fifths of the butter in small pieces, tossing until the coating is smooth. Fold in cooked shrimp and their juices only to warm through.

9. **Season and serve:** Add lemon zest, juice from half the lemon gradually to taste and most of the measured basil. Taste before adding further salt or pepper. Divide into bowls and finish with the remaining basil, optional olive-oil drizzle and optional breadcrumbs. Serve immediately.

RECIPE: Shrimp with Lobster Sauce (shrimp-lobster-sauce.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shrimp-lobster-sauce/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Pan base ---
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil
  - 1/4 lb ground pork
  - 2 garlic cloves, minced
  - 1 tbsp fermented black beans (douchi), quickly rinsed, drained and mashed
  - 1 lb shrimp, raw, peeled and deveined
  - --- Sauce ---
  - 1 cup chicken stock
  - 1 tbsp soy sauce
  - 1 tsp dark soy sauce
  - --- Slurry ---
  - 1 tbsp cornstarch
  - 2 tbsp cold water
  - --- Finish ---
  - 1 large egg, beaten
  - green onions, washed and chopped, as wanted for garnish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This dark, pork-and-douchi version follows a Boston-Chinese style; it contains shrimp, not lobster. Pour beaten egg over gently simmering sauce and give the ribbons time to form before folding. Keep heat available until the pork and egg sauce reach their cooking endpoint.

## Directions

1. **Prepare slurry:** Whisk cornstarch and cold water smooth in a small bowl. Have the prepared beans, garlic, shrimp and beaten egg ready before cooking.
2. **Cook pork:** Cook neutral oil and ground pork: warm the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat, add pork and break it into small crumbles. Cook until browned, beginning to check around 5 minutes; a crisp surface or disappearance of pink is not the final endpoint. Keep cooking promptly through the following steps.
3. **Add aromatics:** Stir in garlic cloves and fermented black beans (douchi) and cook about 1 minute until fragrant, reducing heat before the garlic scorches.
4. **Start shrimp:** Add shrimp and stir-fry about 2 minutes until the outside changes color. The shrimp continue cooking in sauce; pink alone is not the endpoint.
5. **Simmer and thicken:** Pour in chicken stock, soy sauce, and dark soy sauce and bring to a simmer. Re-stir the prepared slurry and stir all of it into the simmering sauce. Simmer about 1 minute, until the starch is cooked and the sauce coats a spoon; continue as needed rather than promising immediate gloss.
6. **Set egg ribbons:** Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer. Pour large egg in a thin stream over the surface; let the ribbons begin to set before folding gently. Continue cooking until the pork and egg sauce reach 160°F / 71°C and the thickest shrimp have firm, pearly, opaque centers. Keep heat on as needed; a 30-second off-heat stand does not certify cooking.
7. **Serve:** Garnish with green onions and serve promptly over separately prepared white rice if wanted.

RECIPE: Shrimp Scampi with Linguini (shrimp-scampi-with-linguini.md)
CUISINES: Italian, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shrimp-scampi-with-linguini/
SOURCE: Adapted from Bon Appétit, Shrimp Scampi
SOURCE_URL: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/shrimp-scampi
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb dried linguine
  - 1 lb raw large shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails removed
  - 1/2 cup unsalted butter, cold and cut into small pieces
  - 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for cooking shrimp
  - 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for shallots and garlic
  - 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for finishing the sauce
  - 4 cloves garlic, minced
  - 2 shallots, finely diced
  - 1/2 cup dry white wine
  - 1 large lemon, juiced, juice added gradually to taste
  - 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes
  - 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
  - Freshly grated Parmesan, for serving
  - Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
  - 1 cup reserved pasta cooking water, use only as needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The sauce is deliberately rich, with butter and olive oil coating a full pound of pasta. Cook the shrimp separately, give the shallots time to soften and use a little pasta water to bring the finish together. Add lemon gradually so its sharpness balances the butter. Adapted from [Bon Appétit’s Shrimp Scampi](https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/shrimp-scampi) into a pasta dish.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and start pasta:** Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it. Prepare garlic, shallots, parsley and lemon; pat the shrimp dry and season lightly with salt and pepper. Cook linguine about 1 minute short of its package al dente time, coordinating it with the sauce below. Reserve the listed cooking water before draining.

2. **Cook shrimp:** Heat the oil labeled for shrimp over medium to medium-high. Add shrimp in a single layer; use batches if crowded, sharing that oil. Cook about 1–2 minutes per side, continuing as needed until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean plate.

3. **Soften aromatics:** Lower heat to medium and add the oil labeled for shallots and garlic. Cook shallots about 4–5 minutes until softened. Add garlic and pepper flakes and stir about 30–45 seconds until fragrant without darkening.

4. **Reduce wine:** Add wine and scrape the pan. Simmer about 2–4 minutes until reduced by roughly half. Add the drained pasta and a small splash of reserved water; toss over low heat until the pasta is tender with a little bite.

5. **Finish off heat:** Remove the pan from heat. Add cold butter a few pieces at a time while tossing, then drizzle in the finishing oil. Add more reserved water in small splashes if needed for a coating that clings. Fold in half the lemon juice, parsley, shrimp and plate juices. Warm very briefly over low heat only if necessary.

6. **Taste and serve:** Taste a strand with sauce before adding remaining lemon juice, salt or pepper. Divide shrimp and pasta evenly among plates and offer Parmesan at the table. Serve promptly rather than holding the pasta over heat.

RECIPE: Shrimp Vodka Pasta (shrimp-vodka-pasta.md)
CUISINES: Italian, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shrimp-vodka-pasta/
SOURCE: Adapted from MyRecipes, Shrimp Vodka Pasta
SOURCE_URL: http://www.myrecipes.com/recipe/shrimp-vodka-pasta
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb dry rigatoni
  - 1 lb raw shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails removed
  - 3 cups prepared marinara sauce
  - 1/2 cup unflavored vodka
  - 1/3 cup heavy cream
  - 1 large broccoli crown, cut into bite-size florets with thin stems
  - 3 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1/2 cup fresh basil, chopped, divided
  - 2 tbsp olive oil, divided into three equal portions
  - 1/2 tsp kosher salt, added to taste, plus salt for pasta water
  - 1/2 tsp black pepper
  - 1 cup reserved pasta cooking water, use only as needed
  - Water, a small splash if needed to finish broccoli
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Cook the broccoli and shrimp separately, then bring them back after the tomato-cream sauce is ready. This gives the broccoli time to soften without overcooking the seafood. Basil goes partly into the sauce and partly over the finished bowls. Adapted from [MyRecipes’ Shrimp Vodka Pasta](https://www.myrecipes.com/recipe/shrimp-vodka-pasta).

## Directions

1. **Prepare and start pasta:** Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it. Cut broccoli, mince garlic, chop basil and dry shrimp. Cook rigatoni about 1 minute short of the package al dente time, coordinating it with the sauce. Reserve the listed pasta water before draining.

2. **Cook broccoli:** Heat one-third of the oil over medium heat. Add broccoli and sauté about 5–7 minutes until stems yield with a little resistance. If needed, add a small splash of water and cover briefly to finish the stems; uncover to evaporate free water. Transfer to a plate.

3. **Cook shrimp:** Add another third of the oil and arrange shrimp in a single layer. Cook about 1–2 minutes per side or as needed until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean plate.

4. **Start sauce:** Lower heat to medium-low. Add remaining oil and garlic and stir about 30 seconds until fragrant. Take the pan away from the burner, add measured vodka carefully, then return to medium-low heat. Simmer gently for about 2–3 minutes, without deliberately igniting it.

5. **Simmer and combine:** Add marinara, cream, half the basil, black pepper and only as much of the measured salt as needed after tasting the prepared sauce. Simmer gently about 5 minutes. Add pasta and broccoli and toss over low heat until pasta is tender with a little bite, using reserved water in small splashes if necessary.

6. **Finish shrimp:** Fold in shrimp and their juices only long enough to warm through. Turn off heat, scatter with remaining basil and serve promptly. Avoid holding the finished pasta over heat.

RECIPE: Shrimp with Black Bean Sauce (shrimp-with-black-bean-sauce.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shrimp-with-black-bean-sauce/
SOURCE: Adapted from thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/shrimp-black-bean-sauce/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Shrimp and pork ---
  - 12 oz shrimp, raw, peeled and deveined, 21/25 size
  - 4 oz ground pork
  - water, enough to cover pork for blanching
  - 2 tbsp vegetable oil
  - 1 garlic clove, minced
  - 1/4 tsp fresh ginger, minced
  - 1 1/2 tbsp fermented black beans (douchi), quickly rinsed, drained and mashed slightly
  - 1/4 cup green bell pepper, finely diced
  - 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
  - --- Stock mixture ---
  - 1 1/2 cups chicken stock, hot
  - 1 tbsp oyster sauce
  - 1 tsp dark soy sauce
  - 1/2 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1/4 tsp sugar
  - 1/8 tsp white pepper
  - --- Slurry ---
  - 2 1/2 tbsp cornstarch
  - 2 tbsp cold water
  - additional water or chicken stock, a little at a time only if needed to loosen sauce, optional
  - --- Egg and scallion ---
  - 1 large egg, beaten
  - 1 scallion, washed and chopped
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Fermented black beans season this dark gravy, which also contains ground pork and egg ribbons. Blanching the pork is a preliminary preparation step; it still cooks in the sauce. Re-stir the measured slurry and add it gradually, then let egg ribbons set before folding gently.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Rinse the black beans and mash slightly. Whisk chicken stock, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, sugar, and white pepper. Have all aromatics chopped and shrimp prepared before pan cooking. In a separate bowl, stir the measured slurry cornstarch and cold water until smooth; keep it separate from the stock mixture.
2. **Blanch pork:** Prepare ground pork and water. Bring enough water to cover the pork to a boil, then add the pork, breaking up clumps, and blanch for about 1 minute. Drain and set aside for immediate further cooking; this blanch is not the final doneness check. Empty and dry the wok before adding oil.
3. **Cook aromatics and start shrimp:** Use shrimp, vegetable oil, garlic clove, fresh ginger, fermented black beans (douchi), green bell pepper, and Shaoxing wine: heat the oil over medium-high heat, then sauté garlic, ginger, peppers, black beans and the blanched pork for about 30 seconds. Add shrimp and Shaoxing wine and stir-fry about 30 seconds. Continue immediately into the sauce stage; these brief stages do not establish doneness.
4. **Heat stock mixture:** Pour in all the stock mixture and bring to a rapid boil, then reduce to a simmer.
5. **Thicken gradually:** Use cornstarch, cold water, and additional water or chicken stock (if using). Re-stir the prepared slurry, then add it gradually while stirring the simmering sauce. Stop when the sauce coats a spoon; you may not need all the slurry. Thin with a little water or stock if needed. Keep unused raw-contact slurry separate from ready-to-eat food and discard it after cooking.
6. **Set egg ribbons:** Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer. Pour large egg across the surface and let the ribbons begin to set before folding gently. Continue cooking until the pork and egg sauce reach 160°F / 71°C and the thickest shrimp have pearly, opaque flesh. Ten seconds alone is not a doneness test.
7. **Serve:** Garnish with scallion and serve immediately over separately prepared steamed jasmine rice if wanted.

RECIPE: Shrimp Wonton Soup (shrimp-wonton-soup.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shrimp-wonton-soup/
SOURCE: Adapted from Chinasichuanfood.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.chinasichuanfood.com/chinese-shrimp-wonton-soup/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 200g Ground Pork
  - 100g Shrimp, minced
  - 1 Egg White (as binder)
  - 1 tsp Toasted Sesame Oil, for the filling
  - Additional Toasted Sesame Oil, a few drops per serving bowl
  - 1 tbsp Light Soy Sauce, for the filling
  - 4 tsp Light Soy Sauce, for the bowls, or less to taste
  - 1 inch Fresh Ginger, grated
  - 3 Scallions, chopped
  - 1 lb prepared Wonton Wrappers; use as many as needed for the filling
  - 4 cups prepared [Cantonese Wonton Broth](/mise/recipes/cantonese-wonton-broth), plus extra to taste
  - Water, for sealing wrappers and boiling wontons
  - 1 sheet Nori, shredded
  - Baby Bok Choy or Spinach, as desired
  - Chopped Fresh Coriander, for garnish
  - 1 tbsp Black Vinegar, for serving, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Cantonese wontons rely on a filling that's sticky and cohesive, achieved by stirring ground pork and shrimp vigorously in one direction until proteins bind into a tacky paste. This traditional technique prevents the filling from crumbling during boiling. The clear broth is finished with sesame oil and shredded nori for an aromatic base.

## Directions

1.  **The Filling:** In a large bowl, combine pork, shrimp, ginger, scallions, egg white, the filling soy sauce, and the filling sesame oil. Stir vigorously in one direction for 3 minutes until sticky.
2.  **Assemble:** Place 1 tsp filling in the center of a prepared wonton wrapper. If making [Fresh Wonton Wrappers](/mise/recipes/fresh-wonton-wrappers), allow their preparation and resting time separately. Dab edges with water, fold into a triangle, and pinch the corners together.
3.  **The Base:** Heat the prepared broth in a saucepan. Divide the nori among four serving bowls and add a few drops of sesame oil to each. Add up to 1 tsp of the bowl soy sauce per bowl, tasting with a little broth first because the broth is already seasoned.
4.  **Boil:** Bring a separate pot of water to a gentle boil. Add the wontons in batches without crowding. Start checking after 3-4 minutes; floating alone does not establish doneness. Check several wontons with a thin-tip thermometer inserted into the center of the filling and continue until they reach 165°F / 74°C. Cook the greens in the hot broth until tender.
5.  **Bind:** Ladle 1 cup of the hot prepared broth into each serving bowl to "wake up" the seasonings.
6.  **Serve:** Transfer the cooked wontons and greens to the bowls. Garnish with fresh coriander and offer the black vinegar at the table. Refrigerate unused wrappers according to their package instructions.

RECIPE: Shruff's End (shruffs-end.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/shruffs-end/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 oz heavily peated 10-year Islay single-malt Scotch
  - 1 oz 100-proof straight apple brandy
  - 0.5 oz French honeyed herbal liqueur (40% ABV)
  - 2 dashes New Orleans-style anise-forward bitters
  - Ice for stirring
  - Orange peel or lemon peel for garnish (optional)
CONTENT:

## Directions

1. **Combine:** Add the Scotch, apple brandy, French honeyed herbal liqueur, and New Orleans-style anise-forward bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.

2. **Stir well for 20-30:** seconds until properly chilled and diluted.

3. **Strain into a chilled:** coupe or rocks glass over a large ice cube (if serving on the rocks).

4. **Express an orange or:** lemon peel over the drink and garnish if desired.

5. **Serve immediately and enjoy:** the complex interplay of smoke, fruit, and herbal notes.

## Chef's Note

Shruff's End comes from the modern craft cocktail movement, representing the bold, spirit-forward style popularized by bars like Death & Co in New York. The name likely references Shruff House from the Harry Potter series, fitting for a drink that combines magic-like alchemy. It's part of a wave of cocktails that pair smoky Islay Scotch with American spirits, creating something uniquely contemporary. The Scotch’s medicinal peat smoke is tamed by the apple sweetness of the brandy, while French honeyed herbal liqueur adds honeyed herbal notes that bridge the two.

RECIPE: Zucchini Soup (silky-zucchini-soup.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/silky-zucchini-soup/
SOURCE: Adapted from Grant Achatz, Food & Wine
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/silky-zucchini-soup
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 1/2 lb zucchini, halved lengthwise and sliced about 1/4 inch thick
  - 1 tbsp unsalted butter
  - 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 1 small yellow onion, finely chopped
  - 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced
  - 2/3 cup chicken or vegetable stock
  - 1 1/2 cups water
  - 1/2 tsp fresh lemon juice
  - Additional raw zucchini, cut into fine matchsticks, for garnish
  - Salt and white pepper, to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Butter and olive oil soften the onion and zucchini before blending; no cream is needed. Cook until the squash crushes easily, then blend to the texture your appliance can achieve. Add the measured lemon at the end and keep raw matchsticks separate for a crisp garnish.

## Directions

1. **Soften onion:** Melt butter with olive oil in a saucepan over medium-low. Add onion and garlic with a little salt and white pepper. Cook about **7–8 minutes**, stirring, until soft without browning.
2. **Cook zucchini:** Add the measured sliced zucchini and cook about **10 minutes**, stirring frequently, until softened. Lower heat if the bottom starts browning.
3. **Simmer:** Add stock and all the measured water. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about **10 minutes**, until zucchini crushes readily with a spoon. While it cooks, wash and finely cut the additional raw garnish zucchini.
4. **Blend:** Remove from heat and let active bubbling stop. Blend with an immersion blender, keeping its guard submerged and stopping before lifting it. Alternatively, cool to your countertop blender’s permitted temperature and blend in as many small batches as its hot-liquid fill limit requires, with the lid and steam vent arranged exactly as its instructions specify. Start low; do not use a sealed personal cup for hot soup.
5. **Finish and serve:** Stir in the measured lemon juice, then taste for salt and white pepper. Warm gently if needed and divide into the intended soup portions. Add raw zucchini matchsticks just before serving.

Adapted from [Grant Achatz’s Silky Zucchini Soup at Food & Wine](https://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/silky-zucchini-soup).

RECIPE: Dry-Brined Roast Turkey with Cider (simple-roast-turkey.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/simple-roast-turkey/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015474-simple-roast-turkey
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 whole turkey, 10–12 lb (4.5–5.4 kg), fully refrigerator-thawed, not kosher, pre-brined or enhanced with a salt solution
  - 25 g salt, weighed regardless of crystal size
  - 2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
  - 1 lemon, finely zested, then cut into wedges
  - 12 garlic cloves, lightly smashed and peeled
  - 1 onion (about 200 g), peeled and cut into wedges
  - 1 bottle (330 ml) dry hard apple cider
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) dry white wine
  - 6 thyme sprigs
  - 2 small rosemary sprigs
  - 6 sage leaves
  - 45 g unsalted butter, melted
  - 1 cup (240 ml) water, plus up to 2 cups (480 ml) hot water for the roasting pan if needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This smaller holiday turkey keeps the original lemon, garlic, herbs and cider, with a measured dry brine instead of a bucket of liquid. Salt seasons and changes how meat proteins retain water; it cannot protect a breast from unlimited cooking. Lemon zest and herbs chiefly perfume the surface and drippings, rather than seasoning every part of the bird to the bone.

Keeping the skin dry helps it brown. The cider is a pan ingredient: manage its evaporation and taste the resulting drippings before using them. It does not make the meat automatically succulent or provide a finished gravy by itself.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the thawed bird:** Remove packaging, neck and giblet bags, checking both cavities. Reserve those parts separately under appropriate refrigerated storage or discard. Pat the turkey dry with disposable towels; do not wash it in the sink. Put breast-side up on a rack over a deep rimmed tray or roasting pan that fits in the refrigerator.
2. **Season twenty-four hours ahead:** Mix the weighed salt with black pepper and the lemon zest. Distribute it evenly over the bird, using some directly over the breast and upper leg meat under gently loosened skin; avoid tearing the skin or depositing the mixture in one pocket. Refrigerate uncovered for twenty-four hours at 40°F / 4°C or below, protected from contact with other foods. Refrigerate the zested lemon separately for the pan. Do not rinse off the seasoning before roasting.
3. **Prepare the oven and pan:** Heat the oven to 325°F / 163°C with space for the turkey on a lower rack. Keep the bird refrigerated while the oven heats. Put garlic, onion, lemon wedges, thyme, rosemary and sage in the roasting pan beneath the rack. Add the cider, wine and initial cup of water. Set the turkey on the rack breast-side up, keep its cavity empty, tuck the wing tips underneath and brush the skin with all the melted butter in a thin coat. Use a clean brush; no repeated basting is needed.
4. **Roast and manage the drippings:** Roast at 325°F / 163°C. Begin checking the pan after about an hour, then periodically; carefully add a little of the listed hot water before the bottom dries out. Keep a shallow layer rather than submerging the bird. If skin colors strongly before the meat is ready, shield that area loosely with foil. Do not repeatedly open the oven just to wet the skin.
5. **Measure every required site:** Begin temperature checks after about 2 1/2 hours; plan roughly 2 3/4–3 1/4 hours total roasting, with additional time possible. A leave-in breast probe helps track progress, but use an instant-read thermometer to check the thickest part of each breast, the innermost part of each thigh and the innermost wing areas, clear of bone. Continue roasting until all reach at least 165°F / 74°C. Check again in a nearby spot if a reading seems implausible. A single thigh reading, clear juices and browned skin are insufficient.
6. **Rest and carve:** Move the bird to a clean carving board and rest thirty minutes, loosely tented if needed. Carve breasts from the bone and slice across the grain, then separate legs and thighs. Divide among about ten diners with sides; this is not a promise of ten identical meat weights or abundant leftovers. Strain the pan liquid, discard spent aromatics and taste before deciding whether to use it in a separate gravy. Do not serve burned or excessively salty pan deposits.

## Choosing between turkey recipes

This dry-brined 10–12 lb bird uses less refrigerator volume than the liquid-brined [Good Eats-inspired turkey](/mise/recipes/good-eats-roast-turkey), whose 14–16 lb bird and aromatic brine have their own schedule. The [roast turkey breast](/mise/recipes/roast-turkey-breast) is a separate smaller-cut option. Choose for actual bird size and available equipment; these are meaningful variations rather than interchangeable serving multipliers.

RECIPE: Korean Spinach Salad (Sigeumchi Namul) (simply-seasoned-korean-spinach-salad.md)
CUISINES: Korean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/simply-seasoned-korean-spinach-salad/
SOURCE: Adapted from Sue Pressey, My Korean Kitchen
SOURCE_URL: https://mykoreankitchen.com/simply-seasoned-korean-spinach-salad-sigeumchi-namul-version-1/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 250 g fresh spinach, roots trimmed and leaves washed
  - 6 cups water, for blanching
  - 1 tsp fine sea salt, for blanching water
  - 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1 tsp scallion, finely chopped
  - 1/2 tsp garlic, minced
  - 1/4 tsp fine sea salt, for seasoning, added to taste
  - 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
  - Cold water, as needed for cooling
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Sigeumchi namul is a simple spinach banchan. Cool the wilted leaves promptly, then remove excess water with a gentle squeeze. Separate the leaves before seasoning so the sesame oil and garlic reach the whole bowl without turning the spinach into a compressed ball.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Bring the measured water and blanching salt to a boil. Set out a colander and cold water for cooling.
2. **Blanch:** Add washed spinach and stir it under the water. Start checking at 30 seconds; remove it when the leaves have wilted and stems are tender, allowing longer for thick stems.
3. **Cool:** Drain and rinse under cold running water or transfer to fresh cold water until cool enough to handle.
4. **Drain gently:** Lift out small handfuls and squeeze gently to remove excess water. Do not wring the leaves bone-dry. Cut long stems and leaves into bite-size lengths; baby leaves can remain whole.
5. **Season:** Mix sesame oil, garlic, scallion and part of the seasoning salt in a bowl. Separate the spinach, add it with the sesame seeds and toss gently. Taste before adding the remaining seasoning salt.
6. **Serve:** Divide into the listed small side portions (four in the original batch), or cover and refrigerate promptly until serving.

## Cooking Notes

About 15 minutes includes washing, heating water, a brief blanch, cooling, draining and seasoning. Larger batches need a larger pot or separate batches.

Refrigerate promptly at 40°F / 4°C or below; use within 2 days for best texture. Limit unrefrigerated time to 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C. Serve cool; freezing gives a softer result.

## Sources

- [Sue Pressey — Simply seasoned Korean spinach salad](https://mykoreankitchen.com/simply-seasoned-korean-spinach-salad-sigeumchi-namul-version-1/)
- [FoodSafety.gov — Four steps to food safety](https://www.foodsafety.gov/keep-food-safe/4-steps-to-food-safety)

RECIPE: Skillet Biscuits with Berries (skillet-biscuits-with-berries.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/skillet-biscuits-with-berries/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/skillet-biscuits-berries
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Biscuit dough ---
  - 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  - 2 tbsp light brown sugar
  - 1 1/2 tsp baking powder
  - 1/2 tsp salt
  - 12 tbsp (1 1/2 sticks) unsalted butter, cold, cut into small cubes
  - 3/8 cup (6 tbsp) half-and-half
  - --- Berries and sauce ---
  - 12 oz raspberries
  - 12 oz blackberries
  - 3/4 cup granulated sugar
  - 1 cup water
  - 1 1/2 tsp finely grated orange zest
  - 1 cinnamon stick
  - --- Topping and serving ---
  - additional granulated sugar, for sprinkling
  - sweetened whipped cream, for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

These butter-rich biscuit mounds steam over berries before a brief broiler finish. Keep the lid on over very low heat until the biscuit centers are cooked, then watch the broiler closely for lightly browned tops against the soft fruit.

## Directions

1. **Mix the dough ingredients:** In a large bowl combine the dough’s all-purpose flour, light brown sugar, baking powder, and salt.
2. **Cut in the butter:** Cut the unsalted butter into the dry mixture with a pastry blender or fingertips until the mixture is coarse with small pieces of butter still visible.
3. **Shape the mounds:** Stir in the half-and-half just until evenly moistened. Scoop one loose mound per listed portion, keeping the mounds approximately the original size; the original batch makes eight. Set them on a parchment-lined tray and keep the dough cool while the berries cook.
4. **Simmer the berries:** Position an oven rack about 6 inches below the broiler and preheat the broiler according to its instructions. In a large, deep skillet approved for broiling, combine the berries’ raspberries, blackberries, granulated sugar, water, finely grated orange zest, and cinnamon stick. Bring to a vigorous boil, then reduce to a moderate simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, for about 10 minutes until the berries are juicy and just broken down.
5. **Steam the biscuits:** Arrange the dough mounds over the bubbling fruit in a single layer with room to expand. The original batch uses eight mounds; for a different quantity use a suitably smaller skillet or additional skillets rather than crowding or increasing mound size. Cover with a fitting lid and simmer over very low heat for about 15 minutes, until the biscuit tops are springy and the centers are cooked through. Check a center biscuit for moist crumb rather than raw dough; if needed, cover and continue simmering before broiling.
6. **Brown the tops:** Remove the lid and sprinkle the biscuits with additional granulated sugar. Broil about 6 inches from the heat for up to 5 minutes, watching continuously and shifting the pan as needed, until lightly browned in spots. Stop sooner if they brown quickly; broiling does not replace cooking the centers.
7. **Cool slightly and serve:** Let the skillet cool slightly, remove and discard the cinnamon stick, then serve biscuits and berries warm with sweetened whipped cream. Handle the hot skillet and handle with oven mitts.

RECIPE: Skinny Broccoli Mac & Cheese (skinny-baked-broccoli-macaroni-and-cheese.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/skinny-baked-broccoli-macaroni-and-cheese/
SOURCE: Adapted from Skinnytaste.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.skinnytaste.com/skinny-baked-broccoli-macaroni-and/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 12 oz High-fiber Elbow Pasta
  - 12 oz Fresh Broccoli Florets
  - 2 cups Low-fat Sharp Cheddar, shredded
  - 2 cups skim milk
  - 1 cup chicken broth
  - 1 1/2 tbsp Unsalted Butter
  - 1/4 cup All-Purpose Flour
  - 1/4 cup Minced Onion
  - 1/4 cup Seasoned Breadcrumbs
  - 2 tbsp Parmesan, grated
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  - Salt, as needed for the pasta water
  - Cooking spray, as needed to coat the baking dish and for the optional source topping finish
  - Additional milk, a splash as needed only to loosen the sauce while reheating
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Thicken the full milk-and-broth sauce before taking it off heat to melt the cheddar. Add broccoli late in the pasta cooking for firmer florets, then drain well so cooking water does not dilute the sauce. Watch the breadcrumb-Parmesan topping closely under the broiler.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 375°F. Wash and trim the broccoli into evenly sized florets. Coat enough baking dishes with cooking spray to hold the full pasta-and-sauce batch with headroom. Any dish placed under the broiler must be broiler-rated; otherwise finish with baking until the topping colors.
2. **Cook pasta and broccoli:** Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add all the pasta. For the late-broccoli route, add all the broccoli about 2 minutes before the pasta is al dente according to the actual package, checking that the florets reach the tenderness you want. Drain both well; they continue cooking in the oven.
3. **Roux:** In a large heavy skillet, melt all the butter over low heat. Add all the onion and sauté until softened, beginning checks around 2 minutes. Whisk in all the flour and cook about 1 minute until evenly combined and lightly golden.
4. **Thicken:** Gradually whisk in all the skim milk and all the chicken broth. Bring to a boil while stirring and scraping, then simmer until smooth and thick, beginning checks around 5 minutes. Season with the salt and pepper to taste.
5. **Combine:** Take off heat. Stir in all the cheddar until melted, then fold in all the drained macaroni and broccoli. Divide the full mixture among the prepared baking dishes.
6. **Top:** Scatter all the breadcrumbs and all the Parmesan over the dishes, divided in proportion to their filling. For a lightly crisped finish, coat the topping with a little of the cooking-spray allowance.
7. **Bake:** Bake at 375°F, beginning checks at 15–20 minutes, until bubbling and 165°F / 74°C in each dish's center. If using broiler-rated dishes, broil briefly to color the topping, watching continuously and beginning checks before 2 minutes. Remove when golden rather than following a fixed broil clock.

RECIPE: Slow Cooker Cheesy Mushroom Quinoa (slow-cooker-cheesy-mushroom-quinoa.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/slow-cooker-cheesy-mushroom-quinoa/
SOURCE: Adapted from Lecremedelacrumb.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.lecremedelacrumb.com/slow-cooker-cheesy-mushroom-quinoa/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups Uncooked Quinoa (rinsed)
  - 8 oz Mushrooms, sliced
  - 4 cups Vegetable or Chicken Broth
  - 4 oz Cream Cheese, cubed
  - 1 cup Italian Blend Cheese, shredded
  - 1/2 Red Bell Pepper, diced
  - 2 Green Onions, chopped
  - 1 tbsp Garlic, minced
  - 1 tsp Italian Seasoning
  - Salt and Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Using a strict 1:2 ratio of quinoa to liquid and cooking on High for a shorter duration (2-3 hours instead of 4-5) ensures each grain maintains its texture and distinct curly tail rather than turning to porridge. Adding cream cheese cubes at the very end creates risotto-like silkiness that standard shredded cheese cannot achieve - the residual heat melts it into a smooth, creamy sauce.

## Directions

1.  **Combine:** Add quinoa, mushrooms, broth, red pepper, garlic, and herbs to the slow cooker. Stir well.
2.  **Cook:** Cover and cook on **High for 2-3 hours** (or Low for 4-5 hours) until the liquid is fully absorbed.
3.  **Emulsify:** Open the lid. Add the cream cheese cubes. Stir vigorously for 1 minute until the cream cheese has melted and emulsified with the grain.
4.  **Bind:** Top with the Italian cheese blend. Cover and cook for another 15 minutes until molten.
5.  **Finish:** Stir once more. Garnish with fresh green onions for the mandatory **High Note**.

## Cooking Notes

The saved recipe serves four as a main or can be portioned as a side. Chicken broth can replace vegetable broth when a vegetarian preparation is not needed.

RECIPE: Slow-Cooker Chicken Noodle Soup (slow-cooker-chicken-noodle-soup.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/slow-cooker-chicken-noodle-soup/
SOURCE: Adapted from damndelicious.net
SOURCE_URL: https://damndelicious.net/2016/10/27/slow-cooker-chicken-noodle-soup/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 680 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed
  - 8 cups (1.9 liters) low-sodium chicken stock
  - 150 g yellow onion, diced
  - 250 g carrots, cut into 1/4-inch pieces
  - 150 g celery, cut into 1/4-inch pieces
  - 4 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1/2 tsp dried thyme
  - 1/2 tsp dried rosemary, crushed
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, added gradually only if needed
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
  - 225 g dried fusilli pasta
  - 2 liters water, for cooking pasta
  - 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, added gradually to taste
  - 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The slow cooker develops a chicken-and-vegetable broth; the pasta needs a short, separate boil. Combining them only in each bowl avoids the large change in texture and liquid level that happens when cooked pasta sits in hot soup. Fusilli holds a little broth in its twists and is easy to portion into six bowls. Lemon and parsley finish the broth, with enough restraint to leave its chicken flavor clear.

## Directions

1. **Load the cooker:** Place onion, small carrot and celery pieces, garlic, thyme, rosemary and pepper in a 6-quart slow cooker. Add thawed chicken and stock. Cover and start cooking immediately; do not use a delayed start with raw chicken.
2. **Cook and check:** Cook on LOW about 5–6 hours, or HIGH about 3–4 hours, until several thick chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C and the carrots are tender. Extend as needed. Keep the lid closed between checks.
3. **Cook pasta near service:** Once the soup is close to ready, bring the pasta water to a boil in a separate pot. Cook fusilli according to its package until just tender, then drain. Cook a proportional amount if serving only part of the soup.
4. **Shred the chicken:** Transfer fully cooked chicken to a clean board, let stand briefly until safe to handle, and shred into bite-sized pieces. Return it to the hot soup and warm through. Avoid leaving it out while doing unrelated preparation.
5. **Balance:** Taste the fully cooked broth. Add measured salt gradually only if needed. Stir in parsley and start with half the lemon juice, adding more to taste.
6. **Assemble bowls:** Divide pasta among six bowls, then add chicken, vegetables and broth. Serve promptly. Keep any remaining pasta separate from the soup for storage.

RECIPE: Slow-Cooker Chicken Ramen with Miso (slow-cooker-chicken-ramen-with-bok-choy-and-miso.md)
CUISINES: Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/slow-cooker-chicken-ramen-with-bok-choy-and-miso/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1019694-slow-cooker-chicken-ramen-with-bok-choy-and-miso
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Broth ---
  - 1.35 kg bone-in skin-on chicken whole legs, fully thawed
  - 2 liters water, plus hot water only to adjust strained broth volume
  - 4 scallions, whites and greens separated
  - 3 cloves garlic, smashed
  - 15 g dried shiitake mushrooms, rinsed briefly to remove grit
  - 2 tbsp mirin
  - 5 g dried kombu
  - 100 g white miso paste, added gradually to taste
  - 2 tbsp tamari or light soy sauce, added gradually only if needed
  - --- Bowls ---
  - 450 g baby bok choy, washed, stems sliced 1/2 inch thick and leaves cut into bite-sized pieces
  - 600 g fresh ramen noodles, seasoning packets discarded if included
  - 5 large eggs, optional
  - 1 sheet toasted nori, cut into 10 pieces, optional
  - 2 tsp toasted sesame seeds, optional
  - 2 liters water, for cooking noodles and eggs as described
  - Ice and cold water, for cooling cooked eggs
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This is a home chicken-miso noodle soup using a slow cooker for the chicken broth. Kombu contributes glutamate and dried shiitake contributes guanylate; combining these savory compounds helps build depth before salt is adjusted. The result is not a promise of restaurant tonkotsu texture. Add miso near serving to preserve its aroma, after the broth volume and vegetable texture are settled.

## Directions

1. **Start the broth:** Put thawed chicken legs, 2 liters broth water, scallion whites, garlic, shiitake and mirin in a 6-quart slow cooker. Cover and start immediately. Keep scallion greens refrigerated for serving.
2. **Cook chicken:** Cook on LOW about 5–6 hours or HIGH about 3–4 hours until each leg reaches 165°F / 74°C away from bone and the meat pulls away readily. Extend if needed. Transfer chicken to a clean tray and mushrooms to a small bowl; let chicken cool only enough to handle.
3. **Strain and infuse:** Strain broth into a 4-quart saucepan and discard spent scallion and garlic. Skim excess surface fat. Aim for about 1.8–2 liters broth, adding a little hot water if needed. While the broth is steaming hot but not boiling, add kombu and leave off heat for about 10 minutes, then remove it. During the infusion, discard chicken skin/bones and shred meat; discard tough mushroom stems and slice the caps.
4. **Prepare optional eggs and noodles:** Bring the noodle/egg water to a boil in a separate pot. If using eggs, lower them in carefully and simmer gently about 11–12 minutes until whites and yolks are firm. Transfer to ice water for 5 minutes, then peel and halve. Return the pot water to a boil and cook ramen according to its package, draining just before assembly. If omitting eggs, simply cook the noodles near serving.
5. **Cook greens and warm meat:** Bring the strained broth back to a gentle simmer. Add bok choy stems and cook about 2–3 minutes; add leaves, chicken and mushrooms and cook until stems are tender, leaves wilted and chicken is heated through to 165°F / 74°C. Turn off heat.
6. **Finish with miso:** Whisk about three-quarters of the miso with a ladleful of hot broth until smooth, then stir it into the pot. Taste and add remaining miso and tamari gradually only as needed. Do not boil the seasoned soup for a long hold.
7. **Assemble:** Divide noodles among five large bowls. Add chicken, mushrooms, bok choy and about 350–400 ml broth per bowl. Finish with sliced scallion greens and the optional egg halves, two nori pieces and a little sesame per bowl. Serve promptly.

RECIPE: Slow-Cooker Cilantro Lime Chicken (slow-cooker-cilantro-lime-chicken.md)
CUISINES: Tex-Mex
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/slow-cooker-cilantro-lime-chicken/
SOURCE: Adapted from damndelicious.net
SOURCE_URL: https://damndelicious.net/2017/07/07/slow-cooker-cilantro-lime-chicken-freezer-meal/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 680 g boneless skinless chicken breasts, fully thawed, left whole
  - 1 can (15 oz / 425 g) black beans, rinsed and drained, about 255 g drained total
  - 1 can (10 oz / 283 g) diced tomatoes with green chiles, with juices
  - 150 g corn kernels, fresh or thawed frozen
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) salsa verde
  - 150 g red onion, cut into 1/4-inch dice
  - 1 jalapeño, seeds removed and finely diced, optional
  - 2 tsp ground cumin
  - 1 tsp mild chili powder blend, not pure hot chile powder
  - 1/2 cup loosely packed chopped fresh cilantro, reserved for finishing
  - 3 tbsp fresh lime juice, added gradually to taste
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, only if needed
  - Water, a small splash only if needed while finishing the onion
  - 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
  - 12 small corn tortillas, about 6 inches across
  - 1 large ripe avocado, about 200 g edible flesh, sliced just before serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Tex-Mex filling combines chicken with beans and corn, so six portions do not require six large servings of meat. Salsa acidity gives flavor, but the breast still needs an internal-temperature check and timely removal. Finish the liquid consistency before stirring in cilantro and lime. Two warm tortillas and a little avocado complete each serving.

## Directions

1. **Load:** Combine drained beans, tomatoes and their juices, corn, salsa verde, finely diced onion, optional jalapeño, cumin, chili blend and pepper in a 4-quart slow cooker. Nestle in fully thawed whole breasts and spoon some sauce over them. Cover and start immediately. Keep cilantro and avocado for serving.
2. **Cook and check:** Cook on LOW about 3–4 hours, beginning checks around 2 1/2 hours, or HIGH about 2–3 hours. Check several thick breast centers for 165°F / 74°C. Remove fully cooked chicken to a clean board even if the onion needs longer; check a piece of onion separately.
3. **Finish the filling base:** If onion is still firm or the base is watery, transfer the bean mixture to a wide saucepan and simmer, stirring gently, about 5–10 minutes or until onion is tender and excess liquid has evaporated. Add a small splash of water only if the onion needs more cooking and the pan is dry. Meanwhile shred the chicken into bite-sized pieces.
4. **Combine and season:** Fold chicken and its juices back into the hot filling and warm briefly through. Turn off heat. Add cilantro and half the lime juice, taste, then add remaining juice and measured salt only as needed.
5. **Warm tortillas:** Heat a dry skillet over medium heat. Warm tortillas in batches, about 20–30 seconds per side or following their package, until pliable and lightly spotted. Wrap in a clean towel as each batch finishes; do not char them until brittle.
6. **Serve:** Slice avocado just before serving. Divide filling among six diners, with two warm tortillas and one-sixth of the avocado each. Spoon excess cooking liquid sparingly so the tortillas stay manageable.

RECIPE: Slow-Cooker General Tso–Style Chicken (slow-cooker-general-tsos-chicken.md)
CUISINES: Chinese-American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/slow-cooker-general-tsos-chicken/
SOURCE: Adapted from lecremedelacrumb.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.lecremedelacrumb.com/slow-cooker-general-tsos-chicken/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 680 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed, left whole
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) hoisin sauce
  - 2 tbsp light soy sauce
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) water, plus a little only if needed to loosen the finished sauce
  - 3 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar, divided
  - 1 tbsp granulated sugar, added gradually to taste
  - 1 tbsp finely grated fresh ginger
  - 2 cloves garlic, finely minced
  - 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes, or less to taste
  - 1 tbsp cornstarch
  - 2 tbsp cold water, for the slurry
  - 2 scallions, thinly sliced
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This is a slow-cooker adaptation of a Chinese-American sweet-sour chicken dish. A wet, covered cook softens a fried coating, so this version uses unbreaded thighs and develops a glossy sauce separately. Ginger, chile and a staged vinegar finish distinguish it from the gentler garlic-led hoisin chicken. Plain rice and a vegetable side complete the plate.

## Directions

1. **Load:** In a 3-quart slow cooker, stir hoisin, soy sauce, 120 ml water, 1 tbsp of the vinegar, ginger, garlic and pepper flakes. Add fully thawed whole thighs and turn to coat. Cover and start immediately.
2. **Cook and check:** Cook on LOW about 3–4 hours or HIGH about 2–3 hours, until several thick pieces reach 165°F / 74°C and are tender. Keep the lid closed between checks. Transfer chicken to a clean plate and cover loosely while finishing the sauce.
3. **Set sauce volume:** Pour cooking liquid into a saucepan, scraping in the garlic and ginger. Skim excess surface fat. Aim for roughly 300–350 ml liquid: simmer briefly if much more remains, or add a little water if very concentrated. Taste only after the chicken has completed cooking; avoid reducing an already salty sauce further.
4. **Thicken:** Mix cornstarch with its 2 tbsp cold water until smooth. Bring sauce to a simmer. Re-stir the slurry and whisk in half, simmering about 1 minute. Add more slurry gradually only if needed, letting each addition thicken. Stop when the sauce lightly coats a spoon and remains pourable.
5. **Balance and return chicken:** Add 1 tbsp of the remaining vinegar and half the sugar. Taste, then add the remaining vinegar and sugar only as needed. Cut or pull chicken into large bite-sized pieces, return it and its plate juices to the sauce, and warm gently through without a long boil.
6. **Serve:** Divide into four main portions and scatter over scallions. Serve with separately prepared plain rice and vegetables. This chicken is tender and saucy; it has no crisp fried coating.
