RECIPE: Slow-Cooker Hoisin Garlic Chicken (slow-cooker-hoisin-garlic-chicken.md)
CUISINES: Chinese-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/slow-cooker-hoisin-garlic-chicken/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1027037-slow-cooker-hoisin-garlic-chicken?smid=ck-recipe-iOS-share
INGREDIENTS:
  - 900 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed, excess surface fat trimmed
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) hoisin sauce
  - 1 tbsp tomato paste
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) water, plus a little only to adjust the finished sauce
  - 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar, divided
  - 6 cloves garlic, finely minced
  - 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes, optional
  - 2 scallions, thinly sliced
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Separate the chicken's cooking endpoint from the sauce's concentration. Remove tender thighs before reducing their juices so the meat does not keep cooking while water evaporates. Hoisin brings sweetness and salt; balsamic adds a fruity acidity to this Chinese-inspired home version. The sauce should lightly coat large strands rather than harden into a sugary shell.

## Directions

1. **Combine:** Stir hoisin, tomato paste, 120 ml water, 2 tsp balsamic vinegar, minced garlic and optional pepper flakes in a 3–4-quart slow cooker. Add thawed whole thighs and turn to coat. Cover and start cooking immediately.
2. **Cook:** Cook on LOW about 4–5 hours or HIGH about 2–3 hours, checking that several thick thighs reach 165°F / 74°C and pull apart readily. Extend if needed for tenderness. Transfer chicken to a clean platter and cover loosely.
3. **Reduce carefully:** Pour liquid and garlic into a wide saucepan and skim excess fat. Bring to a lively simmer, stirring regularly, until it lightly coats a spoon, usually about 8–12 minutes. Roughly 250–300 ml is a useful target, not a reason to oversalt it: taste as it reduces and stop earlier if already concentrated. Add a little water if too sticky or salty.
4. **Pull and coat:** Pull the chicken into large strands, discarding any unwanted gristle. Stir the reserved 1 tsp balsamic into the sauce gradually to taste. Add chicken and plate juices, then fold over low heat just until hot and coated.
5. **Serve:** Divide into six modest main portions with separately prepared rice and broccoli, and finish with the sliced scallions. The recipe does not include an additional batch of rice or lettuce-wrap ingredients.

RECIPE: Slow Cooker Korean Beef (slow-cooker-korean-beef.md)
CUISINES: Korean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/slow-cooker-korean-beef/
SOURCE: Adapted from damndelicious.net
SOURCE_URL: https://damndelicious.net/2015/02/21/slow-cooker-korean-beef/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Beef ---
  - 3 lb boneless beef chuck roast, fully thawed, cut into 1-inch cubes
  - --- Soy-ginger sauce ---
  - 1 cup beef broth
  - 1/2 cup low-sodium soy sauce
  - 1/2 cup light brown sugar, packed
  - 4 garlic cloves, minced
  - 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1 tbsp rice wine vinegar
  - 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
  - 1 tsp Sriracha
  - 1/2 tsp onion powder
  - 1/2 tsp white pepper
  - --- Cornstarch slurry ---
  - 2 tbsp cornstarch
  - 1/4 cup water, cool, for slurry
  - --- Finish and serving ---
  - 2 scallions, thinly sliced
  - 1 tsp sesame seeds, optional
  - cooked jasmine rice, as wanted for serving, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Chuck cubes need long cooking for tenderness. The soy, ginger and brown-sugar sauce thickens with a cool cornstarch slurry near the end; keep its water separate from the broth. The scallions and optional sesame seeds finish the bowl. For a milder portion, reduce or omit Sriracha.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Keep fully thawed beef refrigerated until preparation. Check the actual 6-quart cooker’s load instructions, then cut the chuck into the listed 1-inch cubes. Start promptly after loading; do not use a delayed timer.
2. **Mix the sauce:** Whisk beef broth, low-sodium soy sauce, light brown sugar, garlic cloves, toasted sesame oil, rice wine vinegar, fresh ginger, Sriracha, onion powder, and white pepper in a bowl until the sugar is dispersed. Sriracha enters this sauce, rather than being required again at finishing.
3. **Slow cook:** Put boneless beef chuck roast in the cooker and add all the sauce. Cover and cook on LOW for 7–8 hours or HIGH for 3–4 hours as planning ranges, until the chuck is fork-tender and pulls apart easily. Check beef has reached at least 145°F / 63°C with a three-minute rest before serving; tender chuck commonly needs substantially more cooking than the minimum. Keep covered except for necessary doneness checks.
4. **Thicken at the end:** Whisk cornstarch and water smooth in a small bowl immediately before adding; cornstarch settles while standing. Stir all the slurry into the hot beef and sauce. Cover and cook on HIGH, starting to check around 30 minutes; continue until the sauce is hot and thickened enough to coat the beef, allowing longer if still thin.
5. **Serve:** Use scallions, sesame seeds (if using), and cooked jasmine rice (if using): distribute the scallions over the beef and add the measured sesame seeds if wanted. Serve with the separately prepared rice. Rice cooking time is additional if it is not already ready.

## Cooking Notes

Use a cooker whose instructions permit the actual food load, liquid and meat size. Follow your cooker’s stated minimum and maximum fill limits. A larger recipe needs suitable capacity or separate appropriately filled cookers, with all measured ingredients divided across them. Keep the lid closed except for necessary additions/checks, and do not multiply cooking time with servings or cook on WARM.

Refrigerate promptly in shallow covered containers at 40°F / 4°C or below, within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C). Use within 3–4 days. Reheat on the stove, in the microwave or oven outside the slow cooker, stirring or turning as appropriate for even heating and checking 165°F / 74°C throughout; do not use the slow cooker to reheat cold leftovers. USDA additionally recommends a rolling boil for reheated sauce; stir and keep the boil brief, since prolonged reduction concentrates this thick, sweet-salty sauce. If holding cooked food in the cooker, maintain at least 140°F / 60°C and follow its holding instructions.

RECIPE: Slow-Cooker Chicken Tortellini Soup (slow-cooker-tortellini-soup.md)
CUISINES: Italian-American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/slow-cooker-tortellini-soup/
SOURCE: Adapted from 365daysofcrockpot.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.365daysofcrockpot.com/slow-cooker-tortellini-spinach-soup/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 680 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed, left whole
  - 2 tbsp olive oil
  - 150 g yellow onion, finely diced
  - 3 cloves garlic, minced
  - 2 tsp dried basil
  - 2 tbsp tomato paste
  - 3 tbsp (24 g) all-purpose flour
  - 6 cups (1.44 liters) low-sodium chicken broth, divided
  - 2 cans (14.5 oz / 411 g each) petite diced tomatoes, with juices
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, added gradually only if needed
  - 500 g frozen cheese tortellini
  - 3 liters water, for cooking tortellini
  - 140 g fresh spinach, washed, thick stems removed
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) heavy cream
  - 40 g finely grated Parmesan
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The slow cooker handles the chicken broth while tortellini need a short, controlled boil. Keeping those stages separate protects the pasta seams and prevents a large frozen addition from dictating the soup's finishing time. A small flour base gives body; cream and Parmesan finish the texture and seasoning. The broth should stay spoonable around the pasta.

## Directions

1. **Soften the base:** Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook onion about 5–7 minutes until softened. Add garlic and basil and stir about 30 seconds, then add tomato paste and cook another minute, stirring.
2. **Disperse flour:** Sprinkle flour over the mixture and stir for 1 minute. Gradually stir in 1 cup of the measured broth until the paste is smooth and pourable, scraping the bottom.
3. **Load:** Transfer the base to a 6-quart slow cooker. Add remaining measured broth, tomatoes and juices, pepper and fully thawed thighs. Stir gently, cover and start immediately.
4. **Cook chicken:** Cook on LOW about 4–5 hours or HIGH about 2–3 hours, until several thick thighs reach 165°F / 74°C and shred readily. Remove to a clean board, shred coarsely and return to the hot soup. During the last 20 minutes of the chicken cook, heat the separate pasta water.
5. **Boil tortellini:** Cook frozen tortellini in the boiling pasta water according to their package until seams are tender and centers are hot, meeting any stated filling-temperature requirement. Drain gently. Time this to finish near the soup's final stage.
6. **Finish broth:** With chicken fully cooked and returned, add spinach to the hot broth and stir until wilted, about 2–3 minutes. Turn off heat. Mix cream with a ladleful of broth, then stir it back into the pot with Parmesan. Taste and add salt only if needed. Avoid a prolonged boil after this finish.
7. **Assemble:** Divide tortellini among six large bowls, then ladle over chicken, spinach and broth. Serve promptly. For planned leftovers, cook only the tortellini portions needed and keep any cooked pasta separate from stored broth.

RECIPE: Slow Cooker Vegetable Korma (slow-cooker-vegetable-korma.md)
CUISINES: Indian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/slow-cooker-vegetable-korma/
SOURCE: Adapted from Arman Liew, The Big Man's World
SOURCE_URL: https://thebigmansworld.com/easy-slow-cooker-vegetable-korma/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 900 g cauliflower florets, weighed after removing leaves and the tough core; cut into roughly 1 1/2-inch / 4 cm pieces
  - 300 g carrots, weighed after trimming and peeling; cut into 1/4-inch / 6 mm half-moons
  - 150 g onion, peeled and finely chopped
  - 2 cloves garlic, finely minced
  - 300 ml full-fat unsweetened canned coconut milk, stirred together before measuring
  - 2 tbsp mild, salt-free Indian-style curry powder
  - 1 tsp garam masala
  - 2 tbsp finely ground almond meal or blanched almond flour, not defatted almond powder
  - 1 tsp fine salt
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, reserved for the final seasoning; use only as needed
  - 1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, optional
  - 125 g fresh green beans, weighed after trimming; cut into 1 1/2-inch / 4 cm lengths
  - 1/2 cup (75 g) frozen peas
  - 1/4 cup (60 g) plain whole-milk yogurt, unstrained
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water, reserved only if the sauce begins to catch before the vegetables soften
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This coconut-and-almond vegetable korma is adapted from Arman Liew. Ground almonds give the sauce nutty flavor and a little body; the cauliflower should become soft enough to yield to a fork. Add the green vegetables near the end, then fold in yogurt off the heat for a gentle tang.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the vegetables:** Wash the vegetables, trim and weigh them, then cut as listed. Put the carrots and onion in the bottom of the slow cooker, scatter over the garlic and add the cauliflower. Keep the prepared beans refrigerated. Leave the peas frozen and the yogurt chilled for now.
2. **Coat and start cooking:** Stir the coconut milk thoroughly before measuring 300 ml. Whisk it with the curry powder, garam masala, ground almonds, the first teaspoon of fine salt and optional pepper flakes. Pour over the vegetables and gently turn the cauliflower to coat it, leaving most carrots underneath. Cover and start on **High immediately**. Do not add the reserved water automatically; this is a coated vegetable curry, not a pot of submerged vegetables.
3. **Check and add beans:** After about **3 hours**, check a carrot and a thick cauliflower stem with a small knife. When both are nearly tender, gently fold the green beans into the hot sauce, replace the lid and continue on High. Allow about **45–60 minutes total for the beans**, beginning checks after **30–45 minutes** so the peas can cook during the final part of that window. If the carrots are still distinctly hard at the first check, continue covered and check again in 20–30 minutes before adding the beans. Avoid frequent stirring that breaks up the florets.
4. **Cook the peas and check the whole pot:** When the beans are nearly tender, stir in the frozen peas. Cover and continue on High for about **10–15 minutes**, until the peas are steaming hot throughout and all the vegetables are tender; follow any longer cooking requirement on the pea package. This final pea period overlaps the end of the bean cooking time. Expect roughly **3 3/4–5 hours total on High**, with some cauliflower edges softening into the sauce. Stop when the vegetables are ready rather than keeping a fast batch cooking for five hours.
5. **Hold briefly or finish:** If dinner is running late, keep the fully cooked curry covered on Warm **before adding the yogurt**, checking that it stays at least **140°F / 60°C**. Aim to serve within an hour for better vegetable texture. Warm holds cooked food and does not finish undercooked vegetables. When ready to serve, thicken a loose sauce before adding yogurt, as described in troubleshooting. Turn the cooker off and uncover for about **5 minutes**, until active bubbling stops. Whisk a few spoonfuls of hot sauce into the yogurt in a bowl, then gently fold all of it back into the curry. Taste and add the reserved fine salt a pinch at a time, only as needed. The sauce should coat a spoon and the vegetables, with a little fine almond texture.
6. **Serve:** Divide among six bowls with rice or naan. The batch makes about **7–8 cups**, enough for roughly **1 1/4 cups per person**.

RECIPE: Slow Cooker Lentil Tortilla Soup (slow-cooker-vegetarian-lentil-tortilla-soup.md)

SOURCE: Adapted from Peasandcrayons.com

INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Soup base ---
  - 1 cup onion, diced
  - 1 tsp avocado oil or olive oil
  - 1 bell pepper, diced
  - 1 jalapeño pepper, diced; reduce or omit for a milder soup
  - 2 1/2 cups vegetable broth
  - 1 can (15 oz) tomato sauce or crushed tomatoes
  - 1/2 cup salsa verde or another chosen salsa
  - 1 tbsp tomato paste

  - 1 can (15 oz) pinto beans, fully cooked canned beans, drained and rinsed
  - 1 cup corn kernels, fresh, drained canned, or frozen; follow package preparation

## Chef's Note

Dry red lentils soften and thicken this soup alongside fully cooked canned beans, corn and the onion-and-pepper base. Add optional cream near the end and choose toppings per bowl. Salsa, jalapeño and cayenne control heat. Serve lime alongside or add its juice to taste at the finish.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Check the cooker’s load instructions. Drain and rinse the measured canned black and pinto beans; do not replace them with dried beans in this route. Sort and rinse the dry red lentils and dice the vegetables. Choose salsa/jalapeño heat deliberately; for a milder soup, reduce or omit jalapeño/cayenne. Follow any frozen-corn package preparation directions.
2. **Load the base:** Stir onion, avocado oil or olive oil, bell pepper, jalapeño pepper, vegetable broth, tomato sauce or crushed tomatoes, salsa verde or another chosen salsa, tomato paste, black beans, pinto beans, corn kernels, dry red lentils, chili powder, garlic powder, ground cumin, and cayenne pepper together in the cooker, distributing the tomato paste. Keep dairy, finishing seasoning and toppings separate. The measured oil belongs to this loaded base; no preliminary sauté is required for the slow-cooker route.
3. **Cook the lentils and vegetables:** Cover and cook on HIGH for 4–6 hours or LOW for 7–8 hours as planning ranges. Check that the lentils are soft throughout without a chalky center and the vegetables are tender. Red lentils may break down and thicken the soup; they do not have to vanish completely. Continue covered if still firm, rather than judge only by thickness.

Warm the chosen dairy through and melt cream cheese fully. If loosening, add the extra broth or tomato sauce a little at a time; torn tortillas can thicken the soup. Warm through and taste before adding the finishing salt and pepper. For the existing smoother option, remove from heat and use an immersion blender only if its instructions allow hot soup, keeping the blade submerged to prevent splashing; leave some texture rather than promise a fixed pulse count.
5. **Serve with chosen toppings:** Use fresh lime juice or lime wedges, crushed tortilla chips (if using), shredded cheddar or Mexican-blend cheese (if using), sliced or diced jalapeños (if using), chopped red onion (if using), pico de gallo (if using), diced avocado (if using), fresh cilantro (if using), and sour cream or Greek yogurt (if using). Taste and add lime juice at the finish if wanted, or serve wedges alongside. Divide the soup among the listed small portions, six at the original batch, and let each person choose toppings. For larger meal bowls, plan fewer portions and prepare accompaniments separately. Finished volume and bowl size are unmeasured. Extra jalapeño can stay on the side. Prepare avocado/lime/cilantro with clean utensils.

## Cooking Notes

Use a cooker whose instructions permit the actual food load and liquid. Follow your cooker’s stated minimum and maximum fill limits. A larger recipe needs suitable capacity or separate appropriately filled cookers, with all measured ingredients divided across them. Keep the lid closed except for necessary additions/checks, and do not multiply cooking time with servings or cook on WARM.

Refrigerate promptly in shallow covered containers at 40°F / 4°C or below, within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C). Use within 3–4 days. Reheat on the stove, in the microwave or oven outside the slow cooker, stirring or turning as appropriate for even heating and checking 165°F / 74°C throughout; do not use the slow cooker to reheat cold leftovers. USDA additionally recommends bringing reheated soup to a rolling boil; stir and keep the boil brief, since prolonged boiling can change the texture when dairy is included. If holding cooked food in the cooker, maintain at least 140°F / 60°C and follow its holding instructions.

The tomato option accepts a 14–15 oz can of tomato sauce or crushed tomatoes; the listed main uses 15 oz. Chicken broth is an alternative to the measured vegetable broth, but that version is not vegetarian. Dairy can be omitted. Choose one finishing option: the listed heavy-cream range, or half-and-half or cream cheese added gradually to taste in its place; warm the chosen dairy through and melt cream cheese fully. The sour-cream serving option can be added off heat per bowl using its topping allowance. Extra beans or vegetables are another chunky option; keep within the cooker’s fill limit and adjust seasoning by tasting. For a thicker bowl, stir in crushed tortilla chips at service. The publisher also gives separate stove and pressure-cooker directions; their timings do not replace this slow-cooker route.

RECIPE: Smashed Cucumber Salad (Pai Huang Gua) (smashed-cucumber-salad.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/smashed-cucumber-salad/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 1/3 lbs (600 g) Persian or English cucumber, washed and ends trimmed
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, for draining
  - 1 1/2 tbsp Chinkiang black vinegar
  - 2 tsp light soy sauce
  - 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1 tsp sugar
  - 2 small garlic cloves, finely grated
  - 1 tsp vegan chili crisp, optional; check the label
  - 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
  - 1 scallion, thinly sliced
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Smashing gives cucumber rough surfaces that catch the dressing. The aim is a cracked cucumber with a lively bite, not a flattened pulp. A short salt-and-drain step helps control released water, but the salad will still soften if dressed far in advance. This garlic, vinegar, and sesame version is one interpretation of pai huang gua.

## Directions

1. **Crack and cut:** Set cucumbers on a stable board. If an English cucumber has a loose, watery seed core, halve it and scrape that part away. Cover with a clean towel to contain splashes and tap gently with a rolling pin until cracked. Cut into rough 1-inch pieces.
2. **Salt and drain:** Toss the pieces with the measured salt in a colander over a bowl. Let drain for 15 minutes, preferably chilled. Shake off the released liquid and gently blot the pieces; do not squeeze them into mush.
3. **Mix dressing:** While the cucumber drains, stir vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, garlic, and optional chili crisp together until the sugar dissolves.
4. **Taste and toss:** Taste a drained cucumber piece. If overly salty, rinse briefly and blot well, then begin with only half the dressing. Otherwise add the cucumber to the dressing and toss gently until coated. Taste and adjust the amount of dressing to suit the cucumber.
5. **Finish:** Fold in scallion and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Divide into four side portions and serve soon after dressing. Keep chilled if there will be a short delay.

RECIPE: Spanish Rice and Chickpeas (smoky-spanish-rice-and-chickpeas.md)
CUISINES: Spanish
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/smoky-spanish-rice-and-chickpeas/
SOURCE: Adapted from Thekitchenmagpie.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.thekitchenmagpie.com/smoky-spanish-rice-chickpeas/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup Long-grain White Rice, uncooked
  - 1 can (19 oz) Chickpeas, rinsed and drained
  - 1 tbsp Smoked Paprika
  - 1 tbsp Dried Oregano
  - 3 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1 medium Yellow Onion, finely chopped
  - 1 can (19 oz) Diced Tomatoes
  - 1 1/2 cups Vegetable Broth
  - Shrimp or Fresh Spinach
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Spanish-inspired rice dish draws from paella technique. Frying dry rice in onion-garlic oil for 3 minutes before adding liquid toasts the starch, creating distinct, individual grains rather than sticky clumps - a technique called socarrat in traditional paella. Smoked paprika (pimentón) introduces wood-fired depth that elevates simple canned chickpeas, adding complexity without additional ingredients.

## Directions

1.  **Foundation:** In a large deep skillet, heat 2 tbsp oil. Sauté onion for 7 minutes cook until golden brown and softened. Add garlic, paprika, and oregano; sauté for 30-45 seconds until the spices bloom.
2.  **The Toast:** Add the dry rice. Stir constantly for 3 minutes until the grains are coated in the red oil and smell nutty.
3.  **The Simmer:** Stir in the tomatoes, chickpeas, and broth. Bring to a boil.
4.  **The Finish:** Reduce heat to **low**. Cover tightly. Simmer for 20-22 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
5.  **The Steam Cycle:** Remove from heat. **Do not open the lid.** Let sit for 6 minutes (mandatory for structure).
6.  **Finish:** Fluff with a fork. If adding shrimp, nestle them into the rice during the final 5 minutes of simmering. If adding spinach, stir it in during the steam cycle.

RECIPE: Snickerdoodles (snickerdoodles.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/snickerdoodles/
SOURCE: Adapted from Mimi (Pat Hamilton)
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Snickerdoodle dough ---
  - 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, softened
  - 1 1/2 cups granulated sugar
  - 2 large eggs
  - 2 3/4 cups all-purpose flour
  - 2 tsp cream of tartar
  - 1 tsp baking soda
  - 1/2 tsp kosher salt
  - --- Cinnamon-sugar coating ---
  - 3 tbsp granulated sugar
  - 3 tsp ground cinnamon
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Mimi (Pat Hamilton)’s cinnamon-sugar cookies use cream of tartar alongside baking soda. The coating has its own sugar allocation: mix it separately, then roll the chilled dough in it before baking.

## Directions

1. **Cream:** Beat unsalted butter, granulated sugar, and large eggs until very light and fluffy, scraping the bowl to combine them evenly.
2. **Mix dry ingredients:** Whisk all-purpose flour, cream of tartar, baking soda, and kosher salt in a separate bowl. Stir into the butter mixture just until no dry flour remains.
3. **Chill:** Cover and refrigerate the dough at 40°F / 4°C or below for 30 minutes, until firm enough to roll. If still too soft to handle, allow more chilling rather than adding flour.
4. **Prepare the coating and oven:** Preheat the oven to 400°F while the dough finishes chilling. Mix granulated sugar and ground cinnamon in a shallow bowl; have baking sheets and a cooling rack ready.
5. **Roll and coat:** Shape the chilled dough into evenly sized walnut-sized balls and roll each in the cinnamon-sugar coating. Place them 2 inches apart on baking sheets. Use all the dough; the listed count is approximate and depends on ball size. Scale the coating with the dough and use more sheets or oven loads when needed, keeping ball size and spacing consistent.
6. **Bake:** Wait for the oven to reach 400°F. Bake for 8–10 minutes per load until the edges are set and the centers are soft but no longer wet. Keep remaining dough refrigerated between loads.
7. **Cool:** Leave cookies on the sheets until firm enough to lift, then transfer to a rack and cool completely before packing.

## Cooking Options

### Mimi’s fat and portion options

Mimi’s original formula allows margarine or butter. To use margarine, replace the full listed butter volume with the same volume of margarine; do not add it alongside the butter. The margarine product can change dough handling and spread. For Mimi’s original flour preparation, sift the flour before measuring the full listed volume (2¾ cups in the original batch), then add it with the cream of tartar, soda and salt. Keep the current main flour preparation above when making that version.

Mimi’s original batch was described as making “70 or more,” while the current original-batch planning count is about 36 cookies. The listed volumes are the same, but the flour preparations differ; count also depends on portion size. Smaller portions can finish sooner; start checking at the original 8-minute point, and use set edges and soft, cooked centers to judge them. Do not enlarge dough balls when increasing the batch.

RECIPE: Soba Noodles with Shiitakes & Tofu (soba-noodles-with-shiitakes-broccoli-and-tofu.md)
CUISINES: Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/soba-noodles-with-shiitakes-broccoli-and-tofu/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1016016-soba-noodles-with-shiitakes-broccoli-and-tofu?smid=ck-recipe-iOS-share
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Sauce ---
  - 1/2 cup Chicken or vegetable stock
  - 1 tbsp Soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
  - 1 tbsp Fresh ginger, minced
  - 1 tbsp Garlic, minced
  - 1/2 tsp Sugar
  - Salt, to taste in the sauce
  - --- Noodles and blanching ---
  - 1/2 lb Baby broccoli, florets and stems sliced to cook evenly
  - Boiling water, enough for blanching the broccoli
  - Ice water, for cooling the blanched broccoli, then discarded
  - 8 oz Soba noodles
  - Water, enough to cook the noodles per package instructions
  - 2 tsp Toasted sesame oil
  - --- Pan and finish ---
  - 1/2 lb Extra-firm tofu, drained, patted dry and diced
  - 2 tbsp Neutral oil
  - 1/2 tsp Red pepper flakes
  - 6 oz Fresh shiitake mushrooms, tough stems removed, caps sliced
  - 1 Bunch of scallions, sliced, light and dark-green parts kept separate
  - 1/2 cup Fresh cilantro, chopped
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Cook the noodles to their package’s texture cue, then rinse and drain well before they reach the pan. Soba can contain wheat as well as buckwheat. Keep the tofu and mushrooms in manageable batches; the finishing stock warms and loosens the noodles rather than needing to become a reduced syrup.

## Directions

1. **Mix the sauce:** Whisk Chicken or vegetable stock, Soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, Fresh ginger, Garlic, Sugar, and Salt together. This is the garlic-and-ginger-in-sauce route; set aside.
2. **Blanch the broccoli:** Use Baby broccoli, Boiling water, and Ice water. Add broccoli to boiling water and start checking after about 1 minute; cook until just crisp-tender. Transfer to the ice water, then drain thoroughly and pat dry. Discard the cooling water.
3. **Cook and rinse the soba:** Use Soba noodles, Water, and 1/2 of the Toasted sesame oil. Cook noodles according to their package instructions, checking for a just-tender bite. Drain, rinse under cold running water to remove surface starch, then drain thoroughly. Toss with this step’s sesame-oil allocation.
4. **Cook the tofu:** Use Extra-firm tofu and 1/2 of the Neutral oil. Heat this step’s neutral-oil allocation in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat; it should shimmer without smoking. Add tofu in a manageable single layer and cook, turning, until it begins to color, starting checks after 2 minutes. Transfer to a clean plate.
5. **Finish the stir-fry:** Have 1/2 of the Toasted sesame oil, 1/2 of the Neutral oil, Red pepper flakes, Fresh shiitake mushrooms, Bunch of scallions, and Fresh cilantro ready. Add the remaining neutral-oil allocation and red pepper flakes to the pan, then the mushrooms and light scallion parts; stir-fry until the mushrooms soften, about 2–3 minutes. Add drained broccoli, cooked noodles, tofu and all the prepared sauce. Reduce heat to medium and toss gently until evenly coated and hot, about 1–2 minutes, without requiring a syrupy reduction. Fold in the dark scallion greens, cilantro and remaining sesame oil during the last 30–60 seconds.
6. **Serve:** Serve immediately. Keep scaled pan loads small enough to turn the noodles without crushing them.

RECIPE: Soft Batch Chocolate Chip Cookies (soft-batch-chocolate-chip-cookies.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/soft-batch-chocolate-chip-cookies/
SOURCE: Adapted from joyfoodsunshine.com
SOURCE_URL: https://joyfoodsunshine.com/the-most-amazing-chocolate-chip-cookies/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup (2 sticks) Unsalted Butter, softened
  - 1 cup Granulated Sugar
  - 1 cup Light Brown Sugar, packed
  - 2 large Eggs
  - 2 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - 3 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 1 tsp Baking Soda
  - 1/2 tsp Baking Powder
  - 1 tsp Sea Salt
  - 2 cups (14 oz) Semi-sweet Chocolate Chips
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Use the edge color to judge these soft cookies: remove them when the edges are just starting to brown and the centers have set while staying soft. This dough uses equal cup measures of brown and granulated sugar. A short pan rest helps the cookies become firm enough to move.

## Directions

1. **Prepare and dry mix:** Start preheating the oven to 375°F. Line baking sheets with parchment and set out a cooling rack. Whisk the flour, baking soda, baking powder and sea salt together.

2. **Cream:** Beat the softened butter and both sugars until combined and light, about 2 minutes, scraping the bowl. Beat in the eggs and vanilla until evenly mixed.

3. **Combine:** Add the dry mixture just until no flour pockets remain, then distribute all the chocolate chips through the dough.

4. **Shape:** Roll about 2 tablespoons of dough into each ball and place 2 inches apart on the prepared sheets. Keep waiting dough covered and refrigerated; do not load dough onto a hot sheet.

5. **Bake:** Once the oven reaches 375°F, bake for 8–10 minutes per tray. Remove when the edges are just beginning to brown and the centers have set but remain soft. If the center is still liquid or raw-looking, continue baking and check again.

6. **Cool:** Rest on the sheet for about 2 minutes, then transfer carefully to a rack once the cookies hold together. Allow more pan time if they are too fragile to lift. Cool completely before packing. Repeat with the remaining dough on cooled sheets.

## Cooking Notes

For the same listed butter amount, salted butter is an alternative to unsalted butter; it makes a saltier cookie alongside the listed sea salt. The original batch uses 1 cup of butter and 1 tsp sea salt. Choose one butter type and do not taste the raw dough to decide on seasoning.

For larger cookies, use 2–3 tablespoons of dough per ball, keeping the 2-inch gaps and adding space if portions would touch. Larger portions change the finished count and may need longer baking; follow the edge and center cues.

For make-ahead dough, cover and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below for up to 3 days, then portion and bake in the preheated oven; cold dough may need longer. For freeze-ahead, freeze dough portions separately, then pack them airtight and thaw them in the refrigerator before baking. Check their actual doneness rather than using a fixed frozen-dough bake time.

RECIPE: Soy Ginger Dipping Sauce (soy-ginger-dipping-sauce.md)
CUISINES: Chinese, Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/soy-ginger-dipping-sauce/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1/4 cup Soy Sauce (regular or low-sodium)
  - 2 tbsp Rice Vinegar
  - 1 tbsp Sesame Oil
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Ginger, finely grated
  - 2 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1 Green Onion, thinly sliced
  - 1 tsp Sugar
  - 1/2 tsp Chili Garlic Sauce or Sriracha (optional)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Soy sauce, rice vinegar and sesame oil form a 4:2:1 base by volume. Dissolve the sugar before adding finely grated ginger, garlic and green onion so each small dipping portion carries the same seasoning. Stir before serving because the oil can separate. For a mild version, leave the optional chili sauce out or offer it separately.

## Directions

1. **The Mix:** In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and sugar until sugar dissolves.

2. **The Aromatics:** Stir in grated ginger, minced garlic, and sliced green onion. Add chili sauce if you want heat.

3. **The Rest:** Let rest for 10 minutes to let flavors meld, or refrigerate for a longer wait. Taste and adjust seasoning - add more vinegar for tang or sugar to balance saltiness.

4. **The Serve:** Divide into small individual dipping dishes; keep the unused batch separate from sauce that has been dipped into. Refrigerate the unused sauce promptly at 40°F / 4°C or below and use within 3–4 days. Do not leave it out longer than 2 hours total, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C. Soy sauce and vinegar do not establish a shelf-stable mixture once fresh aromatics are added. Stir before serving; there is no need to warm the whole stored batch to room temperature.

RECIPE: Soy Sauce Butter Pasta with Shrimp and Shiitakes (soy-sauce-butter-pasta-with-shrimp-and-shiitakes.md)
CUISINES: Japanese, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/soy-sauce-butter-pasta-with-shrimp-and-shiitakes/
SOURCE: Adapted from Sarah Leung, The Woks of Life
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/soy-sauce-butter-pasta-shrimp-shiitakes/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 10 oz dry thin spaghetti or angel hair
  - 8 oz raw shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails removed
  - 8 oz fresh shiitake mushrooms, tough stems removed, caps thinly sliced
  - 3 tbsp unsalted butter, divided
  - 3 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
  - 1/3 cup dry white wine
  - 2 shallots, minced
  - 2 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1/4 cup Parmesan, freshly grated
  - 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
  - 1 tbsp olive oil, for cooking shrimp
  - 1/2 cup reserved pasta cooking water, use only as needed
  - Salt, for the pasta water and final seasoning only if needed
  - Black pepper, to taste
  - Water, a small splash if needed for sticking shallots
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Shiitakes supply the earthy flavor while soy sauce and Parmesan season the butter coating. Let the mushrooms lose their excess moisture before finishing the sauce, then add pasta water only if the strands need loosening. Adapted from [Sarah Leung’s Soy Sauce Butter Pasta](https://thewoksoflife.com/soy-sauce-butter-pasta-shrimp-shiitakes/).

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Bring pasta water to a boil. Slice mushrooms, mince shallots and garlic, chop parsley and grate Parmesan. Pat shrimp dry. Salt the pasta water moderately; soy and cheese will season the finished dish.

2. **Cook shrimp:** Heat olive oil over medium-high. Cook shrimp in a single layer, about 1–2 minutes per side or as needed until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean plate.

3. **Cook mushrooms and aromatics:** Reduce heat to medium. Add one-third of the butter and the shallots; cook about 3 minutes until beginning to soften. Add mushrooms and cook about 5–7 minutes, turning, until softened with some brown edges. Add garlic for the last 30–45 seconds. If the pan dries and shallots begin catching, loosen with a small splash of water rather than burning them.

4. **Reduce and cook pasta:** Add wine and simmer about 2–3 minutes until reduced by roughly half. Meanwhile cook pasta about 1 minute short of its package al dente time; for very quick angel hair, start it only when the mushrooms are ready. Reserve the listed pasta water before draining.

5. **Coat:** Add pasta and soy sauce and toss over low heat until the pasta is tender with a little bite, using a small splash of reserved water as needed. Turn off heat. Add the remaining two-thirds of the butter and toss until melted into the sauce, then fold in Parmesan, parsley, shrimp and their juices. Add further water only if the coating is tight.

6. **Serve:** Taste before adding salt; it may need none beyond the soy and cheese. Add black pepper and divide the pasta and shrimp evenly. Serve promptly.

RECIPE: Sun-Dried Tomato Cream Spaghetti (spaghetti-and-spinach-with-sun-dried-tomato-cream-sauce.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/spaghetti-and-spinach-with-sun-dried-tomato-cream-sauce/
SOURCE: Adapted from eatingwell.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/7919563/spaghetti-spinach-with-sun-dried-tomato-cream-sauce/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Ingredients ---
  - 8 oz Dry whole-wheat spaghetti
  - 5 oz Fresh baby spinach, rinsed under running water unless labeled prewashed or ready-to-eat; coarsely chopped and drained
  - 1/2 cup Oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, slivered; reserve jar oil separately
  - 1 tbsp Oil from the sun-dried tomato jar
  - 1/2 cup Sour cream
  - 1 cup Low-sodium chicken broth
  - 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese, grated
  - 1/2 cup Red onion, thinly sliced
  - 3 Garlic cloves, minced
  - 1 tbsp Unsalted butter
  - 1/4 tsp Crushed red pepper
  - 1/4 tsp Salt
  - 1/4 tsp Ground black pepper
  - Water, as needed to boil pasta
  - Salt for pasta water, as desired, separate from measured sauce salt
  - Water for reheating, a little as needed for leftovers
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Use the listed tomato-jar oil and butter in the sauté, then reduce the broth before gently adding sour cream and Parmesan. Put the prepared fresh spinach in a clean heat-safe colander and drain the hot pasta carefully over it. Toss to wilt and drain thoroughly.

## Directions

1. **Cook pasta:** From Dry whole-wheat spaghetti, Water, and Salt for pasta water, season the water with its salt allowance and bring it to a boil; then add the spaghetti and cook according to its package until al dente.
2. **Wilt washed spinach:** Prepare Fresh baby spinach in a clean heat-safe colander with room for the cooked pasta. Set it securely above the sink so food cannot touch sink surfaces. Drain the hot pasta and water carefully over the spinach, keeping hands clear of steam; toss to wilt and drain thoroughly. If some leaves remain crisp, finish wilting them during the final warm toss.
3. **Soften the sauce base:** In the same emptied pasta pot, heat Oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, Oil from the sun-dried tomato jar, Red onion, and Unsalted butter over medium heat, adding onion and tomatoes once the fats are warm. Stir about 3 minutes until onion softens; allow longer as needed.
4. **Season:** Add Garlic cloves, Crushed red pepper, Salt, and Ground black pepper and stir about 45 seconds until fragrant, without scorching garlic.
5. **Reduce broth by observation:** Add Low-sodium chicken broth and simmer, stirring, until roughly half the starting broth remains. Use the change in liquid level as the cue and allow longer as needed. Pot width, heat and batch size change evaporation.
6. **Finish gently:** Reduce heat to low and stir in Sour cream and Parmesan cheese until the cheese melts and the sauce is smooth; take the pot off the heat if it bubbles hard.
7. **Coat pasta and spinach:** Return the drained spaghetti and spinach to the sauce. Toss gently over low heat until hot, the spinach is wilted and sauce clings to the strands. Do not cook until every drop of sauce is absorbed or the bottom dries out.
8. **Serve and reserve leftovers:** Serve hot. The listed Water for reheating is only for reheating leftovers, not an extra dose during this first cooking.

RECIPE: Spaghetti with Tofu Meatballs (spaghetti-and-tofu-meatballs.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/spaghetti-and-tofu-meatballs/
SOURCE: Adapted from Food.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.food.com/recipe/spaghetti-tofu-meatballs-130975
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 lbs Extra-firm Tofu, pressed bone-dry
  - 3/4 cup Walnuts, ground
  - 1 cup Whole-wheat Breadcrumbs
  - 2 large Eggs
  - 1 1/2 tbsp Dijon Mustard (The Finishing Touch)
  - 1 1/2 tbsp Toasted Sesame Oil
  - 3 tbsp Soy Sauce
  - 1 large Carrot, grated
  - 1 large Onion, chopped
  - 1 Green Pepper, chopped
  - 3 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1 1/2 tsp Dried Basil + 3/4 tsp Oregano
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Vegetarian "meatballs" have been made with nuts and grains for centuries, though tofu-based versions became popular in the 1970s and 80s. The key to firm texture is pressing the tofu bone-dry, then binding it with ground walnuts and breadcrumbs. Sauté your vegetables until tender before mixing them into the tofu - this ensures they don't release water during baking. Dijon mustard adds a tangy note that balances the earthy soy and nutty flavors.

## Directions

1.  **Foundation:** In a large skillet, sauté onion, carrot, pepper, and garlic in olive oil for 10 minutes cook until golden brown and softened. Let cool slightly.
2.  **The Base:** In a massive bowl, crumble the pressed tofu with your hands until it looks like ground meat.
3.  **Emulsify:** Add the eggs, breadcrumbs, walnuts, herbs, mustard, sesame oil, and soy sauce to the tofu.
4.  **Combine:** Add the sautéed vegetables. Mix vigorously with your hands until a sticky, uniform dough forms.
5.  **Shape:** Form into 1.5-inch balls. Arrange on an oiled baking sheet.
6.  **Bake:** Bake at 350°F for 20-30 minutes, flipping once, until the exterior is deep brown and "Snappy."
7.  **Serve:** Add the meatballs to your favorite [Roasted Tomato Sauce](/mise/recipes/roasted-tomato-basil-soup) and serve over [Fresh Egg Pasta](/mise/recipes/fresh-egg-pasta).

RECIPE: Spaghetti with Clams & Braised Greens (spaghetti-with-clams-and-braised-greens.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/spaghetti-with-clams-and-braised-greens/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/spaghetti-clams-and-braised-greens
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Main recipe ---
  - 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
  - 8 garlic cloves, crushed
  - 48 live littleneck clams, in their shells, scrubbed and rinsed; 4 dozen in the original batch
  - 2 cups dry white wine
  - 2 jarred roasted red peppers, drained, then pureed with the clam liquid in step 2
  - 1 lb Swiss chard or collard greens, stemmed and chopped
  - 1 tsp red pepper flakes
  - kosher salt, to taste after adding the clam broth
  - black pepper, to taste
  - 1/2 lb spaghetti
  - water, enough to boil the measured pasta
  - salt, to taste in the pasta water
  - 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cubed and chilled
  - 1 lemon, zest and juice all the listed lemons for the current finish
  - 1/2 cup Parmesan, freshly grated
  - Parmesan, as desired for garnish, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Ashley Christensen’s version combines an Italian-style clam pasta with roasted-pepper broth and greens. The current finish keeps the full listed lemon alongside the butter, Parmesan and half-cup oil. Strain the clam liquid before blending, cook greens to tenderness and take the pot off the heat for the butter-and-cheese finish.

## Directions

1. **Clams:** Use live, in-shell clams from a tagged or labeled supplier. Discard cracked shells and clams that remain open after tapping. Scrub and rinse before cooking; keep them cold. Follow the supplier’s purging advice rather than assuming every batch needs a soak. Use 1/2 of the extra-virgin olive oil, 1/2 of the garlic cloves, live littleneck clams, and dry white wine for this stage. In a pot with a lid and room for the measured shells, heat the assigned oil, then add the assigned garlic. Cook the garlic about 30–45 seconds until fragrant; add the clams and wine and bring to a boil. Cover and cook, beginning to check at 5–7 minutes. Transfer clams to a clean dish as they open; discard any that remain unopened during cooking. Keep all the cooking liquid. Divide all supplies proportionally among enough pots or complete batches if the full load cannot fit.
2. **Pepper broth:** Strain all the clam liquid through a sieve, then puree it with jarred roasted red peppers. Use a blender whose manual explicitly permits this liquid at its actual temperature. Follow its hot-liquid fill, venting and speed limits, working in batches. Never put hot soup into a sealed blending cup; if the appliance does not allow it, cool the liquid to its permitted temperature before blending. Keep every batch of the pepper broth for the greens. Wash out the cooking pot to remove grit.
3. **Greens:** Use 1/2 of the extra-virgin olive oil, 1/2 of the garlic cloves, Swiss chard or collard greens, and red pepper flakes for this stage. Heat the assigned oil in the clean pot and add the assigned garlic. Cook the garlic about 30–45 seconds until fragrant, then stir in the flakes and add the greens in batches. Start checking chard at about 3 minutes; cook until the greens are wilted and tender to taste. Collards may take longer. Retain all the oil.
4. **Broth:** Add all the pepper broth to the greens and bring back to a simmer, particularly if it was cooled for blending. Season with kosher salt and black pepper to taste.
5. **Pasta:** Use spaghetti, water, and salt for this stage. Bring the water, salted to taste, to a boil; add the spaghetti and cook until slightly underdone, then drain. Finish it in the pepper broth, checking the pasta rather than relying only on its package clock.
6. **Combine:** Add the drained spaghetti to the greens and pepper broth. Toss over medium heat until the pasta is done to taste, then return all the opened clams and any collected liquid to warm through.
7. **Butter and cheese:** Take the pot off the heat. Add unsalted butter, lemon, and Parmesan, using the full zest and juice of the listed lemon supply. Toss until the butter melts and the cheese is dispersed through the sauce.
8. **Serve:** Serve in shallow bowls with Parmesan (if using) if desired.

## Measured lemon option

For the original recipe’s lemon balance, replace the current whole-lemon finish with **1 tsp grated lemon zest and 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice in the original batch**, scaling both measured supplies with the full recipe. Add them at step 7 with the full butter and Parmesan. Do not also add the main recipe’s whole lemon; all other ingredients and the complete cooking sequence stay the same.

RECIPE: Spaghetti with Clams (spaghetti-with-clams.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/spaghetti-with-clams/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/11952-spaghetti-with-clams
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Main recipe ---
  - 1 lb spaghetti
  - 2 lb live in-shell littleneck clams, scrubbed and rinsed
  - 1/2 cup dry vermouth
  - 4 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 4 garlic cloves, minced
  - 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes
  - 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
  - 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - water, enough to boil the measured pasta
  - salt, to taste in the pasta water
  - salt, to taste after the clams are cooked
  - black pepper, to taste
  - extra-virgin olive oil, as desired for the final drizzle, optional
  - extra-virgin olive oil, a small amount if drained pasta must wait for the clams, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Italian-style spaghetti alle vongole in bianco uses the liquid released by the clams as its sauce. Keep the garlic pale, cook the shells until they open and finish the slightly underdone pasta in that liquid. The current lemon-and-black-pepper finish remains, alongside the vermouth-or-wine small-batch option below.

## Directions

1. **Clams:** Use live, in-shell clams from a tagged or labeled supplier. Discard cracked shells and clams that remain open after tapping. Scrub and rinse before cooking; keep them cold. Follow the supplier’s purging advice rather than assuming every batch needs a soak. If using the current 20-minute cold salted-water soak, keep it refrigerated and use the supplier’s salt concentration and soaking advice, then drain and rinse. The original plain-cold-water soak while the pasta water heats is a separate option; neither soak is a cooking or safety endpoint.
2. **Pasta:** Use spaghetti, water, and salt for this stage. Bring the water, salted to taste, to a boil; add the spaghetti and cook until slightly underdone, about 2 minutes before its package time as a first check. It finishes in the clam liquid.
3. **Garlic oil:** In a wide skillet or saucepan with a lid and room for the measured shells, heat extra-virgin olive oil, garlic cloves, and red pepper flakes over medium-low to medium heat. Cook about 1 minute until fragrant, keeping the garlic pale. Split the full supplies proportionally among enough pans or complete batches if the shells or pasta cannot fit.
4. **Clams:** Add live in-shell littleneck clams and dry vermouth. Cover and bring to a brisk simmer, shaking the pan gently. Start checking at 2–3 minutes; transfer clams to a clean dish as their shells open and continue cooking the remaining clams. Discard any that do not open during cooking. Keep the cooking liquid in the pan.
5. **If pasta finishes first:** Drain the slightly underdone pasta. If it must wait briefly for the clams, toss it with extra-virgin olive oil (if using) to limit sticking.
6. **Finish pasta:** Add the hot drained pasta to the clam liquid. Toss over medium-high heat, starting to check after about 1 minute, until the pasta is done to taste and coated in the sauce. Return all opened clams and their collected liquid to warm through.
7. **Season:** Off the heat, stir in 1/2 of the fresh parsley, fresh lemon juice, salt, and black pepper. Taste before adding salt; clam liquor is already salty.
8. **Serve:** Garnish with 1/2 of the fresh parsley and extra-virgin olive oil (if using) and serve promptly.

## Vermouth-or-wine small batch

For the original single-portion plan, use **¼ lb spaghetti, 8–12 scrubbed small in-shell clams, 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, ½–1 minced garlic clove, ½ dried red chili pepper or ¼ tsp hot red pepper flakes, ⅓ cup Noilly Prat or other vermouth or white wine, and 1–2 tbsp chopped Italian parsley**, with salt as needed for the pasta water. This is a separate full formula; scale all of these supplies together and keep the same live-shell and pan-capacity checks. Its clam count is not an equivalent for the main recipe’s shell-on weight.

Use the plain-cold-water soaking option while bringing the pasta water to a boil. Cook the garlic and chosen chili gently in the full oil, add the wine or vermouth and clams, and collect opened clams as in step 4. If pasta finishes first, drain it slightly underdone and use a small amount of the separate holding oil. Finish the pasta in the clam liquid, covered and gently shaken, starting to check after 1–2 minutes; discard unopened clams. Return the opened clams, add half the parsley and garnish with the remainder. Omit the main recipe’s added lemon and black pepper for this branch. A final drizzle of oil remains an optional current garnish.


======================================================================
RECIPE: Spanish Rice with Chorizo and Chickpeas (spanish-rice-chorizo.md)
CUISINES: Spanish
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/spanish-rice-chorizo/
SOURCE: Adapted from saveur.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.saveur.com/recipes/baked-spanish-chorizo-rice/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Current covered Arborio route ---
  - 1 1/2 cups Arborio rice
  - 1/2 lb Spanish-style chorizo, cured, sliced into rounds; check product label
  - 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained
  - 1 red bell pepper, seeded and diced
  - 1 yellow onion, diced
  - 4 garlic cloves, sliced
  - 1 tbsp tomato paste
  - 1 tsp smoked paprika (pimentón)
  - saffron threads, a pinch, optional
  - 3 cups chicken broth
  - 1/4 cup dry sherry or white wine
  - 1/2 cup raisins
  - hot water, a little only if rice is firm and pan is dry
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Chorizo seasons the vegetables before the rice bakes in broth with chickpeas and raisins. This covered method uses Arborio rice. Bomba and Calasparra absorb differently and need their own liquid and timing adjustments; do not substitute them directly in this version.

## Directions

1. **Render chorizo:** Use Spanish-style chorizo for this stage. Preheat the oven to 400°F. Use a roomy oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven with a tight-fitting lid that holds the rice, full broth, chickpeas and chorizo with room to stir and without a brim-full load. Read the Spanish chorizo label: cured does not always mean ready-to-eat. Prepare any cook-before-eating pork sausage according to its package, checking 160°F / 71°C, before using this rendering route. A raw poultry product needs 165°F / 74°C and is not an assumed equivalent. Render the prepared rounds over medium heat until crisped and their red fat is released; remove to a clean plate. Keep the rendered fat for the current main route.
2. **Soften vegetables:** Add red bell pepper, yellow onion, and garlic cloves to the chorizo fat. Cook about 8–10 minutes until softened, stirring and lowering heat if garlic browns too quickly. Use chorizo that releases enough fat to cook the vegetables without catching. For the olive-oil version, choose the complete uncovered variation below.
3. **Add paste and spices:** Stir in tomato paste, smoked paprika (pimentón), and saffron threads (if using) and cook about 1 minute until fragrant without scorching.
4. **Coat rice:** Add Arborio rice and stir about 2 minutes to coat the grains in the spiced fat.
5. **Add wine:** Add dry sherry or white wine, scrape the bottom and let bubble about 1 minute.
6. **Bring to a boil:** Add chickpeas, chicken broth, and raisins and all the reserved chorizo. Bring to a boil before moving to the oven.
7. **Bake covered:** Use hot water for this stage. Cover tightly and bake at 400°F about 20–25 minutes, then check absorbed liquid and a tender rice center. If the center is firm and the pan is dry, add a little hot water, cover and continue; if wet and firm, keep cooking before adding more liquid. Do not replace Arborio directly with Bomba or Calasparra or use the source variant’s uncovered method here.
8. **Rest and serve:** Rest off heat, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff gently and divide among the listed portions. Allow about 80 minutes overall including 20 minutes preparation, roughly 50 minutes rendering/sautéing/heating/baking and the rest; extra batches or firm rice extend the estimate. Larger quantities need sufficient pan space or separate original-size pans, not proportional oven times.

## Source-Rich Uncovered Variation

This Saveur variation uses 2½ lb chorizo and 5 tablespoons olive oil in its original four-portion batch. Cook it instead of the covered recipe. Scale every ingredient together for other batch sizes, use suitably roomy pans and judge the rice center rather than multiplying oven time.

Use ¼ cup plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil (5 tablespoons total), 2½ lb Spanish-style chorizo sliced ¾ inch thick, 6 thinly sliced garlic cloves, 2 medium yellow onions finely chopped, 1 large red bell pepper seeded and coarsely chopped (the source describes about 1 cup), 1 tablespoon red pepper paste such as choricero, ñora or ají panca OR 1 teaspoon sweet unsmoked paprika, 1 tablespoon tomato paste, ¼ cup dry sherry, 3¼ cups chicken or vegetable stock OR water, a pinch of cinnamon, a large pinch of saffron threads, one 15-ounce can chickpeas drained (the source describes 1½ cups), ½ cup raisins, kosher salt to taste, 1½ cups short- or medium-grain rice such as carnaroli, Arborio or Goya medium-grain, and finely chopped chives for garnish. Use the listed whole pepper and 15-ounce can; their cup descriptions are approximate. This variation uses its own rice, chorizo, oil and spice choices.

Read the chorizo label and complete any required raw-pork cooking to 160°F / 71°C before this browning sequence; package directions apply. Use a large oven-safe Dutch oven, leaving room for stirring the full rice/liquid/meat load. Over medium-high heat, use 1 tablespoon of the total olive oil across uncrowded chorizo batches. Turn until crisped on both sides, beginning checks around 5–7 minutes; move to a clean lined plate. Discard accumulated rendered fat; keep the remaining olive oil for the vegetables.

Set a center oven rack and preheat to 400°F. Add the remaining ¼ cup olive oil, garlic, onions and pepper to the empty pot. Cook over medium heat, stirring, until jammy and browned, beginning checks around 20 minutes. Stir in the chosen red pepper paste OR sweet paprika and tomato paste; cook about 5 minutes, lowering heat if it catches. Add sherry and bring to a boil. Add all the chosen stock OR water, cinnamon, saffron, chickpeas, raisins, reserved chorizo and salt to taste; return to a boil. Add the rice and return to a boil again. Bake uncovered about 20–25 minutes, checking that liquid is absorbed and the rice is al dente. Remove, cover and rest about 10 minutes until just tender; finish with all the chives and serve. Rice and pan differences can require longer cooking.

For the source’s distinct Bomba OR Calasparra choice, use 4½ cups stock instead of 3¼ cups and allow roughly 10 minutes longer cooking, judging the center rather than treating that addition as a guarantee. This applies only to this source-rich uncovered branch; it does not authorize direct substitution in the repaired covered main.

RECIPE: Spatchcocked Roast Chicken (The Best Method) (spatchcocked-roast-chicken.md)
CUISINES: Italian, French, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/spatchcocked-roast-chicken/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- The Chicken ---
  - 1 Whole Chicken (4-5 lbs, not jumbo)
  - --- The Rub ---
  - 2 tbsp Kosher Salt
  - 1 tbsp Black Pepper (fresh-cracked)
  - 2 tbsp Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 4 cloves Garlic (minced or smashed)
  - 2 tbsp Fresh Rosemary or Thyme (or 1 tbsp dried)
  - 1 tsp Smoked Paprika (optional, for color)
  - --- For the Pan ---
  - 1 tbsp Olive Oil (for greasing the pan)
  - 1/2 cup Water or Chicken Stock (for the pan)
  - --- The Finish ---
  - Fresh Lemon (for serving, cut into wedges)
  - Fleur de Sel or Finishing Salt (optional, for the table)
  - Salt and black pepper, to taste for the optional pan sauce
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Removing the backbone and flattening the chicken exposes more skin and can shorten roasting time. Breast and leg meat still differ in thickness, so check each required temperature site rather than assuming they finish together. Use a thermometer and remove the bird once all required sites reach 165°F /74°C. The listed rub is intentionally substantial; kosher salt crystal sizes vary, so retain the chosen brand rather than replacing its volume with the same volume of fine salt.

## Directions

1. **Remove the backbone:** Keep the fully thawed chicken cold until preparation. Place it breast-side down, with the backbone facing up. Cut along both sides of the backbone with sturdy kitchen shears or a suitable knife, and remove it. If saving it for stock, promptly refrigerate in a covered raw-poultry container for use within 1–2 days, or freeze it; stock can also be made without a backbone.

2. **Flatten:** Turn the chicken skin-side up and press firmly on the breastbone to flatten it. Use a board large enough to contain the bird and keep raw juices away from ready-to-eat food. Pat the skin dry with paper towels and discard the towels.

3. **Apply the whole rub:** Mix all the kosher salt, black pepper, garlic, herbs and optional paprika with all the listed rub olive oil. Rub all of this paste over the bird, including under gently loosened breast skin, the legs and the skin surface. The original batch uses 2 tbsp fresh rosemary or thyme, or its distinct 1 tbsp dried option; scale the chosen option proportionally. Keep the full rub quantity.

4. **Optional refrigerated seasoning:** Roast directly after preparation, or refrigerate the seasoned bird on a rimmed tray for 30–60 minutes or up to 8 hours. Leave it uncovered for drying only where it is protected from contamination and cannot drip onto other food. Do not use a counter warm-up as a substitute for refrigerator thawing.

5. **Preheat and prepare the pan:** Preheat the oven to 475°F with the rack in the lower-middle position. Use a rimmed metal pan or roasting pan rated for 475°F. If using an optional baking stone or steel, heat and position it according to its manufacturer’s instructions. Grease the roasting pan with all the 1 tbsp olive oil listed for the pan, and add all the ½ cup water or stock. These are original-batch amounts, scaled with the ingredients; pan geometry is a separate choice.

6. **Roast skin-side up:** Place the flattened bird skin-side up with room around it. Roast at 475°F and start checking after 35–45 minutes; actual birds and ovens can take longer. For larger batches, roast additional original-size 4–5 lb birds in enough rated pans with airflow, checking each separately. Ingredient scaling does not turn a fractional bird or larger bird into the same geometry or multiply the roasting clock.

7. **Check all sites:** Measure the thickest part of each breast and the innermost thighs and wings without touching bone. Every checked site must reach at least 165°F / 74°C before removal. Recheck cooler areas after further roasting; the timer and skin color do not establish doneness. If using the optional convection finish for skin color, follow the oven instructions and watch closely while the bird is still cooking; stop once all required sites reach 165°F rather than adding a mandatory 10–15 minutes after it is done.

8. **Rest and make optional sauce:** Transfer the cooked bird to a clean board with a lip and rest 10 minutes before carving. For the optional pan sauce, put the roasting pan on a burner only if its manufacturer permits stovetop use; otherwise carefully transfer the hot drippings and scraped browned bits into a saucepan. Heat the poultry-contact liquid to 165°F, then simmer, starting with 2–3 minutes, until slightly reduced. Taste with a clean spoon and use the separate optional sauce salt and pepper allowances if needed. Strain if desired.

9. **Carve and serve:** Carve into two leg quarters and two breast portions, or into smaller pieces as preferred. Serve with all the lemon wedges and the optional finishing salt, and spoon over the optional cooked pan sauce. Four portions are a planning yield for the original 4–5 lb bird, with sides; bird size and appetite vary. Refrigerate promptly in shallow covered containers at 40°F or below, within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F). Use within 3–4 days, or freeze portions for later. Reheat hot leftovers to 165°F throughout. For reheated optional pan sauce, USDA also recommends bringing sauces and gravies to a rolling boil. Stir for even heating and avoid prolonged boiling that over-reduces the jus. These handling limits do not promise unchanged texture.

RECIPE: Butternut Squash Purée (spiced-butternut-squash-puree.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/spiced-butternut-squash-puree/
SOURCE: Adapted from Silton Family
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 large butternut squash (about 3-4 pounds), peeled, seeded, and cut into 1-inch cubes
  - 2 tablespoons olive oil (for roasting)
  - 1/2 cup unsalted butter, cut into pieces, room temperature
  - 1/4 cup sugar (adjust gradually to taste)
  - 1/8 cup pure maple syrup
  - 1/2 teaspoon freshly grated nutmeg
  - 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
  - Salt to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

We have evolved this family tradition from boiling to roasting. Boiling the squash dilutes its natural sugars with water; roasting at high heat evaporates moisture and triggers the Maillard reaction, concentrating the squash into a deeper, sweeter version of itself. This is our classic Thanksgiving side.

## Directions

1.  **Roast:** Preheat oven to 400°F. Toss the squash cubes with olive oil and a pinch of salt on a large baking sheet. Spread in a single layer. Roast for 30-40 minutes cook until caramelized and golden brown and starting to caramelize at the edges.
2.  **Purée:** Transfer the hot, roasted squash to a large bowl (or food processor for a silkier texture).
3.  **Mash:** Add the room-temperature butter and mash/process until smooth.
4.  **Season:** Stir in the sugar, maple syrup, nutmeg, and black pepper.
5.  **Finish:** If needed, transfer to a saucepan over low heat to serve piping hot. Taste and adjust salt or sweetness as desired.

RECIPE: Spiced Coconut Chicken & Rice (spiced-coconut-chicken-rice.md)
CUISINES: Indian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/spiced-coconut-chicken-rice/
SOURCE: Adapted from bonappetit.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/spiced-coconut-chicken-rice
INGREDIENTS:
  - 680 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
  - 300 g regular basmati rice, not parboiled or quick-cooking
  - 400 ml full-fat unsweetened coconut milk, stirred smooth
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) water, plus water for soaking and small adjustments
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil
  - 80 g shallot, finely chopped
  - 2 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1 tsp ground turmeric
  - 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper, or less to taste
  - 3/4 tsp fine salt, divided
  - 200 g kale leaves, tough stems removed, cut into thin ribbons
  - 1 lime, cut into wedges
  - 2 tbsp drained sliced pickled red chiles, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This is a full dinner: basmati, chicken, and kale share a coconut-spiced cooking liquid. Soaking starts the rice's hydration before it enters the pot. The measured liquid is a starting point, and the final checks matter more than a fixed timer. Coconut milk contributes both water and fat, so it is not interchangeable with the same volume of concentrated coconut cream.

## Directions

1. **Soak and prepare:** Rinse rice, cover with cool water, and soak for 30 minutes. Meanwhile prepare vegetables and season chicken with half the salt. Drain rice well. Keep raw chicken and its tools away from the lime and optional table garnish.
2. **Start chicken:** Heat oil in a wide heavy 4-quart pot over medium-high heat. Sauté chicken in two batches for about 4–5 minutes per batch, turning for lightly browned patches. Transfer to a plate; it is still partially cooked and must return to the pot immediately after the next step.
3. **Build the liquid:** Lower heat to medium. Cook shallot in the same pot for 3–4 minutes until softened, then stir in garlic, turmeric, and cayenne for about 30 seconds. Stir in coconut milk, measured water, remaining salt, drained rice, and chicken with its juices. Spread the rice evenly around the chicken.
4. **Cook under a lid:** Bring to a gentle simmer, cover tightly, and reduce heat to maintain quiet bubbling. Cook about 15–18 minutes. Avoid repeatedly opening or stirring the pot.
5. **Add kale and verify:** Spread the thin kale ribbons over the top, cover, and cook gently about 5 minutes more. Probe several thick chicken pieces and the rice in several places for 165°F / 74°C. Only after that temperature check, taste a rice grain for a tender center. If rice is hard or chicken is short of temperature, follow troubleshooting and continue cooking before resting.
6. **Rest and finish:** Once chicken and rice meet the checks, remove from heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Fold kale through gently, divide into four bowls, and serve with lime wedges and optional pickled chiles.

RECIPE: Spicy Peach and Avocado Salad (spicy-peach-and-avocado-salad.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/spicy-peach-and-avocado-salad/
SOURCE: Adapted from Country Living, Spicy Peach and Avocado Salad
SOURCE_URL: https://www.countryliving.com/food-drinks/recipes/a43551/spicy-peach-avocado-salad-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 3 ripe but firm peaches, pitted and cut into wedges
  - 2 large ripe avocados, pitted, peeled and cut into wedges just before serving
  - 1 Fresno chile, stem removed and thinly sliced, use less for milder heat
  - 3 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  - 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 2 tsp honey
  - 1 shallot, finely chopped
  - 1/4 cup roasted shelled pistachios, chopped
  - 1/2 cup fresh mint leaves, torn if large
  - Salt and black pepper, to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Let the peach wedges rest gently in the chile-lemon dressing, then fold in avocado and mint just before serving. The peaches keep their shape while their juices join the dressing; pistachios stay crisp when scattered over the top last. Adapted from [Country Living’s Spicy Peach and Avocado Salad](https://www.countryliving.com/food-drinks/recipes/a43551/spicy-peach-avocado-salad-recipe/).

## Directions

1. **Mix dressing:** Whisk lemon juice, oil, honey and shallot in a wide bowl. Add some or all of the sliced chile according to desired heat. Season with salt and pepper.

2. **Rest peaches:** Add peach wedges and lift gently through the dressing. Let stand for 15 minutes while preparing the finishing ingredients; do not toss vigorously or leave the fruit in a warm spot.

3. **Fold in avocado:** Pit, peel and slice avocado near the end of the rest. Add avocado and mint and fold gently just enough to coat.

4. **Serve:** Transfer to a platter, spooning over the peach juices and dressing. Scatter with pistachios and add black pepper only if needed. Serve promptly.

RECIPE: Thai Red Curry Beef (spicy-thai-red-curry-beef.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/spicy-thai-red-curry-beef/
SOURCE: Adapted from MyRecipes, “Spicy Thai Red Curry Beef”
SOURCE_URL: http://www.myrecipes.com/recipe/spicy-thai-red-curry-beef
INGREDIENTS:
  - 12 oz beef tenderloin, cut across the grain into slices about 1/8 inch / 3 mm thick and 2 inches long
  - 1 (13.5 oz) can light unsweetened coconut milk, stirred together
  - 4 tsp Thai red curry paste; use less initially if the paste is particularly hot or salty
  - 2 tsp dark brown sugar
  - 2 tsp fish sauce, divided and added to taste
  - 1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, optional for extra heat
  - 1 1/2 cups red bell pepper, stem and seeds removed, sliced into 1/4-inch / 6 mm strips
  - 1 cup yellow onion, peeled and thinly sliced
  - 1 cup loosely packed fresh basil leaves, washed and dried, large leaves torn
  - 1 tbsp fresh lime juice, added gradually to taste
  - Hot water, only if needed to correct excessive reduction
  - 4 lime wedges, for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Light coconut milk gives this curry a fluid broth rather than a thick cream sauce. Simmer the paste in a small portion of the milk, then cook the vegetables before adding the thin beef. Basil and lime go in off heat so their aroma stays fresh.

## Directions

1. **Prepare everything:** Stir the coconut milk together. Slice pepper and onion, pick and dry the basil, and measure the remaining ingredients. Slice cold tenderloin across the grain into pieces about **1/8 inch / 3 mm thick** and roughly 2 inches long. If it is too soft to slice evenly, firm it in the freezer for about 20–30 minutes first without freezing it solid. Keep sliced beef refrigerated while starting the broth and clean the raw-meat tools.
2. **Simmer the paste:** Put **one-quarter of the measured coconut milk** in the deep skillet with the curry paste. Whisk over medium heat until the paste disperses and the milk begins to bubble. Simmer gently for about **2 minutes**, stirring; do not reduce it to a dry paste or wait for oil to separate. Stir in the remaining milk, brown sugar, **half the fish sauce** and the optional crushed red pepper. Return to a gentle simmer.
3. **Cook the vegetables:** Add pepper and onion. Simmer uncovered over medium-low for about **6–8 minutes**, stirring occasionally, until the onion softens and the pepper is tender with a little bite. Use a little hot water only if the pan becomes too dry; there should still be a fluid broth around the vegetables.
4. **Finish the beef:** Add the cold beef a few slices at a time, separating them in the hot broth. Return to a gentle simmer and cook about **2–3 minutes**, stirring so no folded clumps remain. Check representative thicker slices with a fine-tip thermometer inserted from the edge: **at least 145°F / 63°C** at their centers. Continue briefly if needed; color alone does not establish this endpoint.
5. **Rest and season:** Turn off the heat and allow **at least 3 minutes after the beef reaches temperature before serving**. During this rest, fold in basil and **half the lime juice**. Taste the broth with a slice of beef. Add the remaining fish sauce and lime juice in small amounts only as needed. The broth should remain fluid; add a little hot water only to correct excessive reduction.
6. **Serve promptly:** Divide the beef and vegetables evenly among the serving bowls and ladle over the broth. Serve with separately prepared rice and a vegetable side. Plain [Basmati Rice](/mise/recipes/basmati-rice) lets the curry's seasoning stand out, while [Coconut Jasmine Rice](/mise/recipes/coconut-jasmine-rice) makes a richer accompaniment. Offer the lime wedges at the table.

RECIPE: Spicy Tuna Roll (spicy-tuna-roll.md)
CUISINES: Japanese, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/spicy-tuna-roll/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 230 g trimmed boneless, skinless yellowfin tuna, weighed after removing tough connective tissue; see raw-service sourcing note
  - 1 tbsp Japanese mayonnaise
  - 1 tsp sriracha
  - 1 drop toasted sesame oil
  - 2 scallions, finely sliced
  - 320 g (about 2 cups) prepared [Sushi Rice (Shari)](/mise/recipes/master-sushi-rice)
  - 4 full sheets unseasoned roasted nori, about 19 x 20 cm each; trim as directed
  - 120 ml water, for dampening hands and the knife
  - 1 tsp unseasoned rice vinegar, for the hand-dipping water
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Spicy tuna is a Japanese-American sushi style with many versions. This one keeps the nori outside and uses a small amount of mayonnaise so the chopped fish remains distinct. A larger wrapper accommodates the filling without adding a ridge of rice or squeezing the roll into a dense tube.

## Before buying raw tuna

Ask the supplier about species, handling and intended raw service; “sushi-grade” wording alone is not enough. Yellowfin has a specific FDA parasite-freezing exemption, which does not eliminate other raw-fish hazards. Do not treat trimmings of unknown history, domestic freezing or vinegar as a way to make tuna suitable for eating raw. Thaw frozen fish in the refrigerator as directed, removing vacuum packaging before refrigerator thawing.

Raw seafood remains a risk. FDA advises children, pregnant people, older adults and people with weakened immune systems to avoid it. Choose a fully cooked preparation for those diners.

## Directions

1. **Prepare rice and equipment:** Make [Sushi Rice (Shari)](/mise/recipes/master-sushi-rice). Weigh 320 g for these rolls and refrigerate surplus rice promptly. Let this portion become barely warm during final preparation. Wrap a clean bamboo mat tightly in food-safe plastic film. Mix the water and vinegar in a small bowl; this is to reduce sticking, not to sanitize hands or equipment. Do not dip a raw-filling-coated hand or blade into this clean water. Wash hands and clean the blade before returning to it, use a separate damp cloth for wiping the cutting blade, and replace the water if contaminated.
2. **Prepare the filling:** While the rice cooks, slice scallions and mix mayonnaise, sriracha and sesame oil; taste this clean mixture before it touches fish. Near rolling time, remove tough visible connective tissue, weigh the listed usable amount of cold tuna, then mince into small irregular pieces rather than a paste. Fold in the mayonnaise mixture and scallions. Refrigerate promptly. Wash hands and clean the raw-fish work area.
3. **Portion:** Divide the rice into four 80 g portions with a clean utensil. Divide the tuna mixture into four equal portions, each containing about 58 g tuna plus its seasoning. Keep the filling portions refrigerated and take out one at a time. Trim the first full nori sheet to about 19 x 15 cm; keep its offcut dry and airtight for another use. Leave the other full sheets untrimmed until the first roll closes successfully.
4. **Spread and fill:** Put one rectangle shiny side down on the mat, with its 19 cm edge nearest you. Lightly dampen fingers and shake off excess water. Spread one rice portion evenly, leaving only a 1 cm strip bare along the far edge. Lay one filling portion in a low horizontal line across the rice, about 4 cm from the near edge, using a spoon rather than raw-fish-covered fingers.
5. **Roll:** Lift the near edge of the mat, bring nori and rice over the filling and tuck the leading edge just beyond it. Hold the filling in place gently. Lift the mat away as you continue rolling so it does not become trapped inside. Seal against the bare edge, barely moistening that edge if needed, then give a gentle even squeeze through the mat. Do not build a rice ridge. Check that the first roll closes, then trim the remaining sheets to match and make the remaining three.
6. **Cut and serve:** Set seam-side down while preparing the knife. Wipe and lightly dampen a sharp blade, cut each roll in half, then halve each section twice to make eight pieces per roll. Wipe and dampen between cuts as needed. Serve promptly as 32 pieces: roughly two light main portions or four appetizer portions. Keep unneeded filling cold while working; do not leave all four raw portions on the counter throughout preparation.
