RECIPE: Spinach & Mushroom Quiche (spinach-and-mushroom-quiche.md)
CUISINES: French
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/spinach-and-mushroom-quiche/
SOURCE: Adapted from eatingwell.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/278023/spinach-mushroom-quiche/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 Pie Crust (Homemade or Store-bought)
  - 8 oz Fresh Mixed Mushrooms, sliced
  - 5 oz Fresh Baby Spinach, chopped
  - 6 large Eggs
  - 1/4 cup Whole Milk
  - 1/4 cup Half-and-Half
  - 1 1/2 cups Gruyère Cheese, shredded
  - 1 tbsp Dijon Mustard (The Finishing Touch)
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Thyme
  - 1 1/2 cups Sweet Onion, thinly sliced
  - 1 tbsp Garlic, sliced
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Quiche is a savory French tart from the Lorraine region, traditionally made with eggs, cream, and bacon. Searing mushrooms until browned and dry, sautéing onions until tender, and wilting spinach separately before mixing into the custard prevents excess moisture that would make the quiche watery. Whisking Dijon mustard into the eggs adds subtle tang that bridges earthy mushrooms and rich Gruyère cheese.

## Directions

1.  **Thermal Prep:** Preheat oven to 375°F. Line a 9-inch pie pan with the crust and prick with a fork.
2.  **The Crunch:** In a large skillet, sauté mushrooms in oil until deep golden and all moisture has evaporated (8 mins). Add onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add garlic and cook for 30-45 seconds until fragrant.
3.  **The Wilt:** Add the spinach. Toss for 1 minute until just collapsed. Remove from heat and let cool.
4.  **The Emulsion:** In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, half-and-half, mustard, thyme, salt, and pepper until very frothy.
5.  **Assemble:** Fold the mushroom-spinach mixture and the cheese into the egg base. Pour into the prepared crust.
6.  **Bake:** Bake for 30-35 minutes until the center is set and the top is deep golden brown.
7.  **Set:** Let stand for 10 minutes before slicing - this is mandatory for the structural integrity of the "Bounce."

RECIPE: Grapefruit Gin Fizz (spindrift-gin-fizz.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/spindrift-gin-fizz/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4.5 oz cucumber-and-floral dry gin
  - 12 oz unsweetened sparkling water with grapefruit juice
  - 2 oz Fresh Lime Juice
  - 0.5 oz Agave Syrup
  - 6 dashes Grapefruit Bitters
  - Lime wheels for garnish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This is the ultimate "In the Park" cocktail - refreshing, low-sugar, and aromatic. Cucumber notes in the gin pair with the real-fruit acidity of unsweetened sparkling water made with grapefruit juice. The secret is the **Grapefruit Bitters**: it provides the "High Note" that bridges the gin and the juice.

## Directions

1.  **Shake:** In a cocktail shaker filled with ice, combine the gin, lime juice, and agave. Shake vigorously for 15 seconds until ice-cold.
2.  **Strain:** Strain into three glasses filled with fresh ice.
3.  **Top:** Top each glass with the grapefruit sparkling water.
4.  **Finish:** Add 2 dashes of bitters to each glass. Stir gently once to combine.
5.  **Garnish:** Top with a lime wheel.

RECIPE: Starbucks Egg Bites (starbucks-egg-bites.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/starbucks-egg-bites/
SOURCE: Adapted from eatingonadime.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.eatingonadime.com/starbucks-egg-bites-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6 large Eggs
  - 1 cup Cottage Cheese for richness
  - 1 cup Gruyère Cheese, shredded
  - 4 slices Bacon, cooked and chopped
  - 1/4 tsp Sea Salt + 1/4 tsp Black Pepper
  - Butter or oil spray
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Starbucks popularized sous-vide egg bites with their distinctive velvety texture. Blending eggs with full-fat cottage cheese introduces protein-rich moisture that creates custardy texture standard egg muffins lack. Topping each bite with crispy bacon before baking ensures savory crunch on the surface. Placing a tray of water on the bottom oven rack creates a steam bath that keeps the egg bites moist during baking.

## Directions

1.  **Emulsify:** Preheat oven to 350°F. In a high-speed blender, combine eggs, cottage cheese, salt, and pepper. Blend on high for 30 seconds until completely smooth and frothy.
2.  **Bind:** Pour the mixture into a bowl. Gently fold in the shredded Gruyère cheese.
3.  **Assemble:** Generously grease a 12-cup silicone muffin tin. Fill each cup 2/3 full with the egg mixture.
4.  **The Crunch:** Top each cup with a sprinkle of the chopped bacon. Press down slightly with a spoon to anchor it.
5.  **Bake:** Bake for 20-25 minutes until the centers are set but not brown.
6.  **The Finish:** Let rest in the pan for 10 minutes (mandatory). Gently pop them out with a knife.
7.  **Serve or chill:** Serve promptly. Refrigerate in shallow containers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C, and keep at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use within 3–4 days and reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C.

RECIPE: Bok Choy with Garlic and Oyster Sauce (steamed-bok-choy-with-oyster-sauce.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/steamed-bok-choy-with-oyster-sauce/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 600 g baby bok choy, trimmed, halved lengthwise; quarter wider heads
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil, divided into three teaspoons
  - 4 tbsp water, for steaming, divided, plus up to 2 tbsp more if needed
  - 1 1/2 tbsp oyster sauce
  - 1 tsp reduced-sodium soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp water, for the sauce
  - 2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
  - 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1 tbsp ready-made fried shallots or garlic, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Bok choy has two different textures to manage: tender leaves and firmer, juicy stems. A little covered steam cooks the stems before the final garlic sauce goes in. Oyster sauce already supplies salt and sweetness, so the finish needs only a small measured amount of soy sauce.

## Directions

1. **Wash and prepare:** Trim damaged ends while keeping enough base to hold small heads together. Halve lengthwise; quarter broad heads. Swish in water and rinse carefully between stalks, then lift out and drain well. Divide into two batches.
2. **Mix the sauce:** Stir oyster sauce, soy sauce and the separate tablespoon sauce water together. Set aside with sliced garlic and sesame oil.
3. **Cook the bok choy in two batches:** Heat 1 tsp neutral oil in a lidded skillet over medium-high. Arrange half the bok choy cut-side down and cook about 1 minute. Carefully add 2 tbsp steaming water, cover and cook 2–3 minutes, until a knife enters the thick stem with slight resistance. Add a tablespoon more water and cook longer if the pan dries before the stems soften. Transfer to a plate, draining free water. Repeat with the second teaspoon oil, remaining bok choy and 2 tbsp water.
4. **Make the garlic finish:** Pour away excess pan liquid. Lower heat to medium, add the final teaspoon neutral oil and sliced garlic. Stir 20–30 seconds until fragrant and still pale. Add the mixed sauce and let it bubble briefly.
5. **Coat and serve:** Return drained bok choy and turn gently in the sauce for about 30 seconds. Take off heat and drizzle with sesame oil. Divide into four sides, spooning over only enough sauce to coat lightly. Add optional fried garnish immediately before serving.

RECIPE: Steamed Broccoli with Garlic Oil (steamed-broccoli.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/steamed-broccoli/
SOURCE: Adapted from healthyrecipesblogs.com
SOURCE_URL: https://healthyrecipesblogs.com/steamed-broccoli/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 450 g trimmed broccoli, florets about 1 1/2 inches wide and peeled stems sliced 1/4 inch thick
  - Water, enough to sit just below the steamer basket
  - 1 1/2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - 2 cloves garlic, finely minced
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, added gradually to taste
  - 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Steam cooks the broccoli gently while a separate low-heat pan mellows the minced garlic. Check a thick stem rather than relying on green color or an exact minute count. Let excess water drain before dressing so the oil and seasoning cling. This moist, tender side differs from seared or oven-roasted broccoli.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the steamer:** Add water to a saucepan so it stays below the basket. Bring to a steady boil. Arrange prepared broccoli loosely in the basket; use a larger pot or two batches if tightly packed.
2. **Steam and check:** Cover and steam about 4–6 minutes. Check a thick stem with a small knife: it should yield with slight resistance. Extend briefly if still hard; do not wait for florets to fall apart.
3. **Warm garlic oil:** While broccoli steams, put oil and garlic in a small saucepan over low to medium-low heat. Warm about 1–2 minutes, watching continuously, until gently bubbling and fragrant but still pale. Remove from heat promptly.
4. **Drain and dress:** Lift the basket carefully and let water drain without shaking the delicate florets vigorously. Transfer broccoli to a warm bowl, add garlic oil, pepper and half the salt, then fold gently. Taste and add the remaining salt only if needed.
5. **Serve:** Divide into four small side portions and serve promptly. Keep the broccoli uncovered during a brief wait so trapped steam does not continue softening it.

RECIPE: Edamame with Sea Salt (steamed-edamame.md)
CUISINES: Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/steamed-edamame/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 450 g frozen unsalted edamame in pods
  - 1.5 liters water, or enough for the pods to circulate freely
  - 1 tsp flaky sea salt, added gradually to taste
  - 1/2 tsp toasted sesame oil, optional
  - 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This is the site's simple boiled-pod preparation with salt added after draining. It differs from a strongly salted cooking-water method: much of the finishing salt stays on the pod, so taste as you season. Flaky salt adds texture; fine salt also works in a smaller amount. The bean should be tender with a little bite. Discard the fibrous pod after releasing the beans.

## Directions

1. **Heat water:** Bring the measured water to a rolling boil in a 4-quart saucepan. Read the frozen edamame package so its required cooking time is clear before adding the pods.
2. **Cook the pods:** Add frozen edamame and return to a boil. Cook according to the package, commonly about 4–5 minutes after boiling resumes. Open one pod carefully, let a bean cool enough to taste, and check that it is hot and tender through its center. Continue if still firm inside, and do not shorten a stated minimum cooking requirement just because the pods are green.
3. **Drain thoroughly:** Pour into a colander, shake off water, and let steam escape briefly. Transfer the hot pods to a bowl.
4. **Season gradually:** Toss with optional sesame oil. Add about half the flaky salt, taste, then add more only as needed; the whole teaspoon may not be necessary. Add optional pepper flakes.
5. **Serve:** Divide into four small side bowls and provide a bowl for discarded pods. Release the beans from the pods and eat the beans; do not eat the fibrous pods. If adding edamame to a composed bowl, shell the cooked beans first.

RECIPE: Mussels with Chorizo Broth (steamed-mussels-chorizo.md)
CUISINES: Spanish
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/steamed-mussels-chorizo/
SOURCE: Adapted from Bonappetit.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/steamed-mussels-with-tomato-and-chorizo-broth
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 lbs fresh live mussels, scrubbed and debearded
  - 2 oz dried Spanish chorizo, casing removed, thinly sliced
  - 1 pint cherry tomatoes, halved
  - 3/4 cup dry white wine
  - 3 garlic cloves, crushed
  - 1 tsp fennel seeds, crushed
  - 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the pot
  - 2 tbsp fresh tarragon or parsley, chopped
  - Thick country-style bread, as needed, toasted or charred
  - Extra-virgin olive oil, as needed for generously drizzling the bread
  - Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Spanish-style dish reduces wine and tomato juices before steaming the mussels. The mussels then release their own liquid into the full chorizo-and-olive-oil base, so the finished broth need not resemble the concentrated base. Tarragon or parsley and oiled toast complete the dish.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Scrub and debeard the live mussels just before cooking. Discard shells that are cracked or broken, and open mussels that do not close when tapped. Keep them refrigerated until ready. Use a heavy pot with a tight lid and enough room to turn the mussels; divide the full measured base and mussels proportionally among additional pots or batches if needed.

2. **Render:** Heat the full measured pot oil with the dried Spanish chorizo over medium heat. Stir for about 4 minutes, until it begins to brown and crisp. Add garlic and fennel seeds; cook for 30–45 seconds until fragrant. Keep all the oil and rendered chorizo fat in the pot.

3. **Reduce:** Add all the tomatoes and wine, and season with pepper. Simmer over medium-high for about 6–8 minutes, until the liquid has reduced by about three-quarters and the tomatoes soften. This is the base before mussel juices enter; do not cook it dry or require the finished broth to be a syrup.

4. **Steam:** Add all the mussels and cover tightly. Cook about 6–8 minutes, stirring or shaking the pot occasionally, until shells open during cooking. Check them rather than waiting for every shell to open; discard any that remain closed. Keep finished mussels with their broth.

5. **Serve:** Ladle mussels and all the chorizo broth among deep bowls. Add all the measured tarragon or parsley. Toast or char the bread separately and drizzle it generously with its separate oil allowance; serve alongside. The original four-slice bread option uses one thick slice per listed portion; use the scaled portion count as a planning guide rather than a fixed four slices.

RECIPE: Braised Noodles with Green Beans and Pork (steamed-noodles-with-green-beans.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/steamed-noodles-with-green-beans/
SOURCE: Adapted from thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/green-bean-noodles-bian-dou-men-mian/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Pork coating ---
  - 225 g pork belly, sliced across the grain about 1/4 inch thick
  - 2 tsp light soy sauce
  - 1 tsp cornstarch
  - 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
  - 1/8 tsp ground white pepper
  - --- Noodles and vegetables ---
  - 450 g fresh raw white wheat noodles, medium-thin strands
  - 2 tbsp neutral oil, divided
  - 450 g fresh green beans, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
  - 10 g fresh ginger, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks
  - 1 whole culinary star anise pod
  - 5 cloves garlic, coarsely chopped
  - 2 scallions, sliced, whites and greens separated
  - --- Braising liquid ---
  - 2 tbsp light soy sauce
  - 2 tsp dark soy sauce
  - 1/2 tsp sugar
  - 1 cup (240 ml) water, plus up to 1/2 cup (120 ml) hot water only if needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Bian dou men mian uses a covered pan to finish noodles with green beans and meat. The pork coating seasons the meat first; the separate braising mixture supplies the moisture and seasoning that finish the noodles. Green beans should be cooked tender rather than stopped at the first bright-green color; the finished dish relies on chewy noodles for its firmer texture.

## Directions

1. **Coat and prepare:** Mix pork with the coating's light soy, cornstarch, Shaoxing wine and white pepper. Refrigerate for about 20 minutes while preparing beans and aromatics. Mix the separate braising soy sauces, sugar and 240 ml water.
2. **Steam the noodles:** Bring water below a steamer rack to a steady boil. Use a parchment liner with holes and space around its edges so steam can circulate. Loosely arrange the fresh noodles, toss with 2 tsp of the oil and steam covered for about 10–12 minutes, until flexible. The water must remain below the rack. Check it does not boil dry and handle escaping steam carefully.
3. **Brown pork before delicate aromatics:** Heat the remaining 4 tsp oil in a deep 12-inch pan over medium-high. Add pork and cook 3–4 minutes, turning, until it has some browned patches. Spoon off excessive rendered fat if needed, leaving a thin film for the next step. Lower to medium, add ginger and star anise for 30 seconds, then garlic and scallion whites for another 30 seconds.
4. **Start the beans and braise:** Add green beans and stir for 3 minutes. Pour in the measured braising liquid and scrape the base of the pan. Bring to a simmer, spread the beans evenly, then lay the steamed noodles loosely on top without stirring down into the liquid. Cover tightly and maintain a gentle active simmer over medium-low.
5. **Check both textures:** After 8 minutes, open the lid away from you and taste a cooled noodle and bean. Continue covered cooking, usually another 2–4 minutes, until noodles have no floury core and beans are tender. If the pan is drying while either is firm, add hot water around the edge 2 tbsp at a time before covering again. Do not use disappearance of all liquid as the only stopping rule.
6. **Finish and verify:** Fold the noodles through the pork and beans. Check sliced pork reaches at least 145°F / 63°C; after reaching that temperature, give them at least 3 minutes before serving. The chicken variation must instead reach 165°F / 74°C. Remove and discard the star anise, stir in scallion greens and adjust excess moisture briefly over the heat if needed. Divide among four bowls.

RECIPE: Plain Short-Grain White Rice (Gohan) (steamed-white-rice.md)
CUISINES: Japanese, Korean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/steamed-white-rice/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 300 g Japanese-style short-grain white rice, such as Koshihikari (not glutinous rice)
  - 400 ml water, plus cold water for rinsing
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Short-grain rice should be tender and cohesive, rather than as separate as basmati. The starch within the grain determines much of that texture; rinsing cannot turn one rice type into another. Weighing rice and measuring water removes the ambiguity between kitchen cups and smaller rice-cooker cups. The water quantity here is a starting formula for a covered pot, not a universal rule for every rice, lid, or cooker.

## Directions

1. **Rinse and drain:** Put rice in a bowl, cover with cold water, swish gently, and drain. Repeat a few times until the water is less cloudy; it need not become perfectly clear. Drain well in a fine-mesh strainer.
2. **Soak in measured water:** Transfer rice to a heavy 2-quart saucepan with a tight-fitting lid and add the measured cooking water. Soak for 30 minutes. Keep this water for cooking.
3. **Bring to a boil:** Heat over medium heat with the lid slightly ajar. Once the water is steadily bubbling, close the lid fully and immediately reduce to low.
4. **Cook gently:** Cook 12–15 minutes at the lowest heat that maintains a gentle simmer. Avoid repeated lid lifting. At the end, make one brief check: gently part the rice to see whether free water remains. If so, cover and cook a few minutes longer. If the pot is dry but rice is hard, use the measured-water correction in troubleshooting.
5. **Rest and fluff:** Move off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes. Taste a grain for a tender center, then lift and fold gently with a rice paddle, reaching the bottom without mashing. Serve as four side portions.

## Rice-cooker alternative

Use the cooker's own cup and white-rice fill lines as a matched system, or follow its weight-based instructions for this amount. Choose the appropriate white-rice cycle. If the program includes soaking, do not add a second soak automatically. Follow the appliance's rest guidance and fluff when finished. The stovetop time and water amount are not a guarantee for every cooker.

RECIPE: Steel-Cut Oatmeal (steel-cut-oatmeal.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/steel-cut-oatmeal/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodnetwork.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/alton-brown/steel-cut-oatmeal-recipe-1939448
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Oatmeal ---
  - 1 tbsp unsalted butter
  - 1 cup steel-cut oats
  - 3 cups boiling water
  - sea salt, a pinch
  - 1/2 cup whole milk
  - 9 tbsp low-fat buttermilk, ½ cup plus 1 tbsp in the original batch, divided equally
  - 1 tbsp light brown sugar
  - 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon
  - --- Optional toppings ---
  - fresh berries, as wanted for serving, optional
  - maple syrup, a drizzle as wanted for serving, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Toasting the oats in butter brings out their nutty aroma; it does not seal them against starch release. Keep the water at a gentle simmer, then stir in the dairy over low heat. The buttermilk is divided equally between cooking and finishing, giving the oats richness and a fresh tang at the end.

## Directions

1. **Toast:** Use unsalted butter and steel-cut oats: melt the butter in a heavy saucepan, then add the oats. Stir for about 2–3 minutes, until lightly golden and nutty-smelling; do not scorch the butter.
2. **Simmer gently:** Carefully add boiling water and sea salt. Reduce to very low heat, cover and maintain a gentle simmer for about 25 minutes. Check if it threatens to boil over or catch on the bottom; lower the heat and stir gently if needed rather than let it scorch.
3. **Cook with dairy:** Add whole milk and 1/2 of the low-fat buttermilk. Stir gently over low heat for about 10 minutes, until the grains are tender and chewy without a hard center and the porridge is creamy. Continue as needed for the actual oats and heat.
4. **Finish off heat:** Remove from heat and stir in 1/2 of the low-fat buttermilk, light brown sugar, and ground cinnamon. The buttermilk in this step is the remaining half of its listed total, not an extra amount.
5. **Serve:** Divide among the listed portions and serve hot with fresh berries (if using) and maple syrup (if using).

## Cooking Notes

The original batch contains ½ cup plus 1 tablespoon buttermilk total, or 9 tablespoons. Divide the listed total equally between the dairy cooking step and the off-heat finish.

Use a pan with headroom for the oats to simmer without foaming over. Larger batches may need separate pans and longer heat-up; keep the same gentle simmer and judge grain tenderness rather than multiplying the clock.

About 45–50 min includes preparation, heating and cooking; larger batches and product directions can add time.

Refrigerate promptly in a shallow covered container at 40°F / 4°C or below. Limit time out to 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C. Use within 3–4 days. Reheat to 165°F / 74°C, stirring; the oats thicken as they stand.

RECIPE: Steven’s Margaritas (stevens-margs.md)
CUISINES: Mexican
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/stevens-margs/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 oz reposado tequila
  - 1 oz dry orange liqueur (40% ABV) (The "Silk" Base)
  - 1 oz Fresh Lime Juice (The Acid Balance)
  - 1 squirt Agave Syrup
  - Pinch of Smoked Sea Salt (The complex flavor)
  - Lime wedge for garnish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This modern margarita uses a 1:1:1 ratio of reposado tequila, dry orange liqueur, and fresh lime juice for balanced sweet-tart-boozy proportions. Instead of rimming the glass, a pinch of smoked sea salt added directly to the shaker amplifies the wood-aged notes of the reposado while providing consistent seasoning throughout the drink.

## Directions

1.  **Thermal Prep:** Fill a rocks glass with fresh ice and let it chill while you mix the drink.
2.  **The Base:** In a cocktail shaker filled with large ice cubes, combine the tequila, dry orange liqueur, lime juice, and agave.
3.  **The Pulse:** Add the pinch of smoked sea salt.
4.  **Aeration:** Shake vigorously for 15-20 seconds until the shaker is ice-cold and frosted.
5.  **Strain:** Double strain into the prepared rocks glass over fresh ice.
6.  **Garnish:** Express a lime wedge over the surface and drop it in for the final aromatic **High Note**.

RECIPE: Sticky Miso Salmon Bowls (sticky-miso-salmon-bowl.md)
CUISINES: Japanese, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sticky-miso-salmon-bowl/
SOURCE: Adapted from Andy Baraghani at NYT Cooking
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1025510-sticky-miso-salmon-bowl
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Rice ---
  - 400 g Japanese-style short-grain white rice, rinsed and well drained
  - 535 ml water, plus water for rinsing
  - 2 tbsp hot water, reserved only if rice needs correction
  - 1 tbsp unsalted butter
  - 4 scallions, thinly sliced
  - --- Salmon ---
  - 680 g skinless, boneless salmon, divided into four similar fillets
  - 3 tbsp white miso
  - 2 tbsp honey
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil, for the glaze
  - 1 tsp neutral oil, for the foil
  - 1 tbsp finely grated fresh ginger
  - 2 tsp finely grated grapefruit zest, without white pith
  - 1 tbsp fresh grapefruit juice
  - --- Bowl toppings ---
  - 300 g cucumber, thinly sliced
  - 1 large avocado, sliced just before serving
  - 2 sheets toasted nori, snipped into strips
  - 1/2 cup drained kimchi, optional
  - 2 tsp chile crisp, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Adapted from Andy Baraghani’s NYT Cooking recipe, these bowls combine Japanese miso and short-grain rice with grapefruit, honey and butter. The grapefruit zest supplies a fragrant, slightly bitter edge to the sweet coating, while cool toppings contrast with the warm rice. Watch the glaze closely under the broiler and check the fish's center separately.

## Directions

1. **Start the rice:** Rinse the rice in several changes of cool water until less cloudy, then drain well. Put it in a heavy 3-quart saucepan with the measured cooking water and soak for 30 minutes. Keep this water for cooking.
2. **Prepare the bowl ingredients:** During the soak, slice the scallions and cucumber, snip the nori, and measure the optional toppings. Whisk the miso, honey, measured glaze oil, ginger, grapefruit zest and juice until smooth. Taste before it touches fish; no additional salt is specified because the miso and optional toppings already supply seasoning. Check the salmon for pin bones, pat dry, and refrigerate it until cooking time.
3. **Cook and rest the rice:** Bring the rice and soaking water to a boil over medium heat with the lid slightly ajar. Cover tightly, reduce to low and simmer gently for 12–15 minutes. Briefly check for unabsorbed water; if there is a pool, cover and cook a little longer. Move off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes. A finished grain should be tender all the way through. Fold in the butter and scallions without mashing.
4. **Heat the broiler and coat the fish:** As the rice begins its low simmer, heat the broiler on high and set the rack so the fish will sit 7–9 inches from the element. Line a rimmed metal half-sheet pan with foil and spread the measured foil oil where the fillets will sit. Arrange fish with at least an inch between portions. Divide all the glaze over their tops and sides in an even layer, leaving no thick mounds. Wash tools and hands that touched raw fish; none of this coating is a cold serving sauce.
5. **Broil with attention:** Broil for approximately 10–16 minutes, checking the surface after 4 minutes and frequently thereafter. Rotate the pan if browning is uneven. Brown patches are welcome; a black, smoking crust is not. Check each fillet with a thermometer inserted sideways into its thickest center and remove it when it reaches 145°F / 63°C and flakes under gentle pressure. If the top browns too soon, use the gentler oven finish described above. Let the fish stand briefly while portioning the rice.
6. **Build the bowls:** Slice the avocado. Divide all the buttered scallion rice among four bowls, then add one salmon fillet, a quarter of the cucumber and avocado, and the nori. Offer the measured kimchi and chile crisp at the table so each person can choose the heat and fermented flavor. This is already a complete rice bowl; any edamame side is additional.

RECIPE: Sticky Peking Meatball Rice Bowls (sticky-peking-meatball-rice-bowls.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sticky-peking-meatball-rice-bowls/
SOURCE: Saved Paprika recipe
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Recipe ---
  - 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice, dry; rinse and drain
  - 1 can (13 1/2 oz) coconut milk, shake/stir smooth
  - 1/2 cup water
  - 1 1/2 lb fully cooked frozen meatballs, approximately 24–28 in the original batch; actual piece weight varies
  - 1 tsp oil
  - 1/3 cup hoisin sauce
  - 1/3 cup Peking duck sauce
  - 2 tbsp rice vinegar or apple cider vinegar
  - 3 tbsp water
  - 1 1/2 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
  - 4 garlic cloves, minced
  - 1 bunch of kale, stems removed, roughly chopped
  - 3 carrots, peeled and sliced into coins or ribbons
  - 2 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
  - 1/2 lemon, juiced, or use the separate unmeasured vinegar finish instead
  - black pepper, to taste
  - 1 tsp neutral oil
  - water, a small splash for vegetables if needed
  - water, a splash only if glaze becomes too thick
  - vinegar, a splash instead of lemon juice if chosen, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Hoisin and duck sauce glaze fully cooked meatballs while coconut rice and garlicky greens cook separately. Keep each component’s oil and water separate. The rice-cooker instructions and meatball package determine the working schedule.

## Directions

1. **Start coconut rice:** Use jasmine rice, coconut milk, and water for this stage. Combine the rinsed and drained rice, all the stirred coconut milk and this component’s measured water in a rice cooker that permits the mixture and load. Follow its instructions. If the manual disallows this mixture, use a separately verified coconut-rice method with the full listed rice, coconut milk and water.
2. **Heat meatballs:** Use fully cooked frozen meatballs and oil for this stage. Heat the fully cooked frozen meatballs according to their package until centers reach 165°F / 74°C, checking several of the largest. Brown the heated meatballs in a roomy skillet using their full one-teaspoon oil for the original batch, or the listed scaled amount. Work in batches without assuming 24–28 pieces at every scale.
3. **Add aromatics:** Reduce heat to medium. Add fresh ginger and garlic cloves around the heated meatballs and stir for about 30 seconds, without scorching the garlic.
4. **Glaze:** Use hoisin sauce, Peking duck sauce, rice vinegar or apple cider vinegar, water, and water for this stage. Add the hoisin, duck sauce, vinegar and measured three-tablespoon glaze water for the original batch, following the scaled list for other quantities. Simmer gently about 5 minutes, stirring until glaze clings; use the separate small-water allowance only if the glaze becomes too thick. Keep this water separate from the rice water.
5. **Cook greens and carrots:** Use bunch of kale, carrots, garlic cloves, neutral oil, and water for this stage. In another skillet heat the full vegetable oil. Cook carrots about 2 minutes, then add kale and sliced garlic. Turn through the pan and continue until carrots and greens are tender, beginning checks after 3–5 minutes more. Use the small vegetable-water allowance if needed; lower heat if garlic burns. More pan batches change this time.
6. **Finish the vegetables:** Use lemon, black pepper, and vinegar (if using) for this stage. Season with the black-pepper allowance and all the juice from the listed lemon portion, or the separate vinegar splash instead. Do not add both acid options automatically.
7. **Assemble:** Let the rice finish its permitted cooker cycle and any manual-required rest; check grains are tender. Divide all the rice, glazed meatballs and vegetables among the listed portions rather than fixing five meatballs per person at every scale. Serve promptly; actual total follows rice, meatball package and batches.

## Cooking Notes

Fresh ginger is a prominent part of the glaze. Leftover coconut rice can be used for fried rice; refrigerate it promptly in shallow containers and reheat thoroughly. The written rice liquid is coconut milk and water.

RECIPE: Thai Basil Chicken & Eggplant (stir-fried-chicken-and-eggplant-with-thai-basil.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/stir-fried-chicken-and-eggplant-with-thai-basil/
SOURCE: Adapted from thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/japanese-eggplant-chicken-thai-basil-stir-fry/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken ---
  - 450 g boneless skinless chicken breast, sliced across the grain about 1/4 inch thick
  - 1 tbsp water, for the chicken
  - 1 tsp cornstarch
  - 2 tsp light soy sauce, for the chicken
  - --- Vegetables and cooking ---
  - 450 g Japanese or Chinese eggplant, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
  - 3 tbsp neutral oil, divided
  - 3 tbsp water, for steaming the eggplant, plus small splashes if needed
  - 3 cloves garlic, finely chopped
  - 1 tbsp finely chopped fresh ginger
  - 1 serrano chile, finely chopped, optional
  - 3 scallions, thinly sliced, whites and greens separated
  - 20 g Thai basil leaves
  - --- Sauce ---
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) unsalted chicken stock
  - 1 tbsp fish sauce
  - 1 tsp light soy sauce
  - 1 tsp dark soy sauce
  - 1 tsp sugar
  - 1/8 tsp ground white pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This Thai-inspired home stir-fry combines the site's two overlapping chicken-and-eggplant recipes. Thai basil gives an anise-like aroma; the dish is not pad kra pao, which centers on holy basil. Brown the eggplant in measured oil, then use a little steam to soften it. Its interior should be yielding, not crunchy. A thin starch coating on the chicken gives the sauce a little body without turning it into a thick gravy.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the chicken:** Toss chicken with its tablespoon of water, cornstarch, and 2 tsp light soy sauce. Refrigerate while preparing the other ingredients, about 10–15 minutes.
2. **Organize the finish:** Mix stock, fish sauce, sauce soy, dark soy, sugar, and white pepper. Prepare garlic, ginger, chile, scallion whites and greens, and basil separately. Divide eggplant into two batches.
3. **Brown and soften eggplant:** Heat 1 tbsp oil in a 12-inch lidded skillet over medium-high heat. Add half the eggplant in one layer; cook about 4–5 minutes, turning to brown two cut faces. Lower to medium, carefully add 1 1/2 tbsp water, cover, and cook about 3–5 minutes until the center yields easily. Uncover and let residual water evaporate. Transfer to a bowl. Repeat with the second half, another tablespoon oil, and remaining steaming water. Use small additional splashes only if the pan dries while the center is still firm.
4. **Cook chicken:** Add 2 tsp of the remaining oil over medium-high heat. Spread chicken in one layer, using two batches if needed. Leave about 1–2 minutes, then turn and stir-fry until several thick slices reach 165°F / 74°C, usually about 4–6 minutes total per batch. Transfer to a clean bowl.
5. **Warm aromatics:** Reduce heat to medium and add the final 1 tsp oil. Stir garlic, ginger, optional chile, and scallion whites for about 30–45 seconds until fragrant without darkening. Stir the mixed sauce again and pour it in; bring to a brief simmer.
6. **Glaze and finish:** Return chicken and eggplant. Fold gently for about 1–2 minutes until hot and lightly glazed; add a small splash of water if the coating becomes sticky. Turn off heat, fold in basil and scallion greens, and serve promptly in four portions with separately prepared rice.

RECIPE: Shrimp with Snow Peas and Ginger (stir-fried-shrimp-with-snow-peas-and-ginger.md)
CUISINES: Chinese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/stir-fried-shrimp-with-snow-peas-and-ginger/
SOURCE: Adapted from The New York Times, Stir-Fried Shrimp with Snow Peas and Ginger
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/7036-stir-fried-shrimp-with-snow-peas-and-ginger?smid=ck-recipe-iOS-share
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb raw large shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails removed
  - 2 cups cold water, for the shrimp soak
  - 1 tbsp salt, for the shrimp soak, discarded afterward
  - 6 oz fresh snow peas, strings removed
  - 1/3 cup unsalted chicken broth
  - 2 tsp Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
  - 1 1/2 tsp light soy sauce
  - 1 1/2 tsp cornstarch
  - 3/4 tsp sugar
  - 1/8 tsp ground white pepper
  - 2 tbsp garlic, minced
  - 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
  - 1 scallion, chopped
  - 2 tbsp neutral oil, divided
  - 1/4 tsp salt, for seasoning the peas, added to taste
  - 1/2 tsp toasted sesame oil, optional for a sesame finish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A short saltwater preparation is followed by thorough drying, then quick pan cooking. The ginger and garlic enter after the snow peas have softened, and the slurry is stirred again just before pouring. That keeps the aromatics from scorching while the sauce thickens evenly. Adapted from [The New York Times’ Stir-Fried Shrimp with Snow Peas and Ginger](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/7036-stir-fried-shrimp-with-snow-peas-and-ginger).

## Directions

1. **Prepare shrimp:** Dissolve the soak salt in the measured cold water, add shrimp and refrigerate for 5 minutes. Drain and discard the liquid. Rinse briefly with a gentle flow of cold water to remove surface salt, avoiding splashing, and pat dry. Clean the sink and raw-contact tools.

2. **Prepare sauce and vegetables:** Whisk broth, wine, soy sauce, cornstarch, sugar and white pepper together. Trim peas, mince garlic and ginger and chop scallion. Keep the separate seasoning salt for the vegetables.

3. **Cook shrimp:** Heat half the oil over medium-high in the skillet or wok. Add shrimp in a single layer, using batches if necessary and sharing this oil allocation. Cook about 1–2 minutes per side or as needed until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean plate.

4. **Cook peas and aromatics:** Add remaining oil and snow peas. Stir-fry about 2 minutes until tender with a little bite, adding only as much of the seasoning salt as needed. Add garlic and ginger and stir about 20–30 seconds until fragrant without darkening.

5. **Thicken and finish:** Stir the sauce again to lift settled starch, pour into the pan and bring to a gentle bubbling simmer for about 30–60 seconds, stirring, until lightly thickened. Return shrimp and their juices only long enough to warm through. Turn off heat and stir in scallion and optional sesame oil. Loosen an overthick sauce with a small splash of water and serve promptly with separately prepared rice.

RECIPE: Stovetop Macaroni & Cheese (stovetop-macaroni-and-cheese.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/stovetop-macaroni-and-cheese/
SOURCE: Adapted from Thekitchn.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.thekitchn.com/how-to-make-the-best-macaroni-and-cheese-on-the-stove-82588
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Elbow Macaroni or Shells
  - 1 1/2 cups Whole Milk
  - 2 tbsp All-Purpose Flour
  - 3 cups Sharp Cheddar, shredded
  - 1/2 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1/4 tsp Dry Mustard Powder (The Finishing Touch)
  - 1 tbsp Unsalted Butter
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Whisking flour into cold milk before heating creates a light, stable base that won't separate when cheese is added - an easier technique than making a traditional butter roux. Boiling pasta for exactly 8 minutes (very al dente) ensures it holds its shape against the heavy cheese sauce instead of turning mushy. Mustard powder adds savory depth that enhances the sharp cheddar without tasting overtly mustardy.

## Directions

1.  **Boil:** Cook pasta in salted water for 8 minutes until **very al dente**. Drain and set aside.
2.  **The Base:** In a large saucepan, whisk together one third of the measured milk and the flour until no lumps remain. Stir in the remaining milk.
3.  **Thicken:** Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, for 3-4 minutes until the milk thickens to the consistency of heavy cream.
4.  **Emulsify:** Reduce heat to **low**. Add the cheese one handful at a time, stirring until completely molten and glossy.
5.  **Season:** Stir in the salt, mustard powder, and butter.
6.  **Bind:** Return the hot pasta to the saucepan. Toss vigorously until every noodle is saturated in the cheese silk.
7.  **Serve:** Serve immediately while hot. (Note: if baking, top with breadcrumbs and broil for 2 minutes).

RECIPE: Strawberry Cheesecake Overnight Oats (strawberry-cheesecake-overnight-oatmeal.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/strawberry-cheesecake-overnight-oatmeal/
SOURCE: Adapted from wholefully.com
SOURCE_URL: https://wholefully.com/strawberry-cheesecake-overnight-oats-recipe/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1/2 cup Rolled Oats (Old-fashioned)
  - 1/3 cup Plain Greek Yogurt for richness
  - 2/3 cup Unsweetened Milk of choice
  - 3 tbsp Cream Cheese, softened
  - 1/4 cup Fresh Strawberries, chopped
  - 1 tbsp Chia Seeds
  - 1/2 Lemon, zested and juiced (The Acid Balance)
  - 1/2 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - 1 tbsp Maple Syrup
  - Additional Fresh Strawberry and freshly ground Black Pepper, optional garnish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The key to "cheesecake" oats that aren't a dense brick is whisking the cream cheese and Greek yogurt together before adding the milk and oats. This creates a stable, cheesecake-like base. We use lemon juice and zest to cut through the heavy cream cheese, providing the signature tang of a real cheesecake. Always add the berries just before refrigerating to keep them from bleeding.

## Directions

1.  **The Emulsion:** In a small bowl, whisk softened cream cheese, yogurt, maple syrup, vanilla, and lemon juice until perfectly smooth.
2.  **Combine:** Stir in the milk and chia seeds.
3.  **The Grain:** Add the rolled oats. Stir vigorously until the oats are fully submerged.
4.  **Fold:** Gently stir in the chopped strawberries and lemon zest.
5.  **The Finish:** Transfer to a wide-mouth glass jar. Cover and **refrigerate for at least 4 hours** (overnight is best) to allow the chia and oats to hydrate.
6.  **Serve:** Stir once more. If desired, garnish with the additional strawberry and a little black pepper.

RECIPE: Strawberry Orange Jello Salad (strawberry-congealed-salad.md)
CUISINES: Southern
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/strawberry-congealed-salad/
SOURCE: Adapted from Gwock Family
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 large box Strawberry Jello
  - 20 oz Frozen Strawberries, thawed and drained
  - 1 can (20 oz) Crushed Pineapple, drained
  - 3 large Ripe Bananas, mashed
  - 1 pint Sour Cream (for richness)
  - 1 cup Boiling Water
  - 1/2 cup Pecans, chopped (Optional)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Congealed salads are a Southern tradition - aspic-based dishes that served as both side dish and dessert at mid-century dinners. Despite their reputation, they work because the gelatin provides a light texture that carries fruit and nuts without heaviness. The trick is chilling just until set but not rock-hard, so each spoonful has a slight wobble.

## Directions

1.  **Dissolve:** In a large bowl, whisk the Jello into the boiling water until no crystals remain.
2.  **Combine:** Stir in the thawed strawberries, drained pineapple, and mashed bananas. Fold in the pecans if using.
3.  **Stage 1:** Pour exactly half of the mixture into a 9x13 glass dish. **Refrigerate for 1-2 hours** until firm. Keep the remaining half at room temperature.
4.  **The Emulsion:** Once the first layer is set, spread the sour cream in an even layer over the top.
5.  **Stage 2:** Carefully pour the remaining Jello mixture over the sour cream.
6.  **Set:** Return to the fridge for **at least 2 more hours** (ideally 4) until completely congealed.
7.  **Serve:** Slice into squares and serve cold.

RECIPE: Strawberry Quinoa Breakfast Bars (strawberry-quinoa-breakfast-bars.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/strawberry-quinoa-breakfast-bars/
SOURCE: Adapted from Myfussyeater.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.myfussyeater.com/strawberry-quinoa-breakfast-bars/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Breakfast bars ---
  - 3/4 cup cooked quinoa, chilled; prepared and cooled ahead
  - 1 1/2 cups old-fashioned rolled oats
  - 1 cup fresh strawberries, wash, remove tops and chop before measuring
  - 2 large ripe bananas, peeled and mashed
  - 2 large eggs
  - 1/4 cup raisins or golden raisins
  - 1/2 tsp pure vanilla extract
  - sea salt, a pinch
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Cooked quinoa, oats, bananas and eggs form a moist base around the strawberry pieces. Start with prepared chilled quinoa, distribute the fruit gently and keep the layer thickness similar when changing batch size. Let the bars firm before cutting, then chill them promptly rather than leaving a thick egg-and-grain bake out to finish cooling.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line an 8×8-inch baking dish with parchment for the original batch. Start with cooked, chilled quinoa; boiling and chilling it from dry are additional preparation. Use proportional pan area or additional dishes for scaled batches, keeping similar layer thickness.
2. **Mix bananas and eggs:** Combine large ripe bananas, large eggs, and pure vanilla extract in a bowl, mashing the bananas before stirring the eggs and vanilla through them.
3. **Add grains and raisins:** Stir in cooked quinoa, old-fashioned rolled oats, raisins or golden raisins, and sea salt, including the salt, until evenly distributed.
4. **Fold in strawberries:** Gently stir in fresh strawberries so the pieces are distributed throughout without mashing them.
5. **Fill and bake:** Spread evenly in the prepared dish and level the surface. Wait until the oven reaches 350°F. Bake for 20–25 minutes, until the center is firm to touch and no loose raw mixture remains. Check the center with a thermometer for 160°F / 71°C as well; changed depth or oven loads may take longer.
6. **Set, chill and cut:** Let the bars firm enough to handle, then refrigerate promptly in a shallow dish or shallow containers, within 2 hours of baking or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C. Finish cooling in the refrigerator rather than waiting indefinitely for complete cooling at room temperature. Once cool and firm, cut into portions; the original batch plans nine squares.

## Cooking Notes

### Starting ingredients and keeping

The listed quinoa is cooked and chilled, not dry quinoa. Refrigerate cooked quinoa promptly in shallow containers when preparing it ahead, within 2 hours or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C, at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use it within 3–4 days of cooking, including the time held before the bars are made; rebaking does not reset its storage history.

Keep cooled bars covered at 40°F / 4°C or below and use within 3–4 days of baking, sooner if the starting quinoa is already near its storage limit. They may be served cold. If reheating stored bars, heat their centers to 165°F / 74°C; that leftover endpoint is separate from the initial bake. Raisins or golden raisins are an exclusive choice at their full listed amount.

### Separate ingredient-size option

For the original nine-square batch, another complete version uses 2 ripe bananas of unspecified size, 2 medium eggs, ½ tsp vanilla, 100 g cooked quinoa, 150 g rolled oats, 30 g raisins and 100 g chopped strawberries, without the salt pinch. It uses the same original 8×8-inch dish and 350°F oven, with a 20–25-minute reference; use the main firm-center and 160°F / 71°C checks. Scale this entire ingredient set together rather than combining its weights with the large-egg and large-banana recipe. Different banana and egg sizes can change layer depth and baking time; the weights have not been measured as equivalents for the current ingredient sizes. Keep the same prompt cooling and refrigerated handling.

RECIPE: Strawberry Rhubarb Shortcake (strawberry-rhubarb-shortcake-with-whipped-mascarpone.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/strawberry-rhubarb-shortcake-with-whipped-mascarpone/
SOURCE: Adapted from Bakingthegoods.com
SOURCE_URL: http://bakingthegoods.com/2016/04/06/strawberry-rhubarb-shortcake-with-whipped-mascarpone/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 1 tbsp Baking Powder
  - 3 tbsp Granulated Sugar, for the dough
  - 1 tsp Salt
  - 1 tbsp Coarse Sugar, for the tops
  - 3/4 tsp Pink Peppercorns, ground (The Finishing Touch)
  - 1/2 cup (1 stick) Unsalted Butter, cold and cubed
  - 1 cup Whole Buttermilk
  - 3 cups Fresh Strawberries, sliced
  - 3 stalks Rhubarb, cut into 1-inch pieces
  - 1/4 cup Sugar, for the fruit
  - 2 tbsp Elderflower Liqueur, for the fruit
  - 1/2 Vanilla Bean, seeds scraped
  - 1 cup Mascarpone Cheese (for richness)
  - 3/4 cup Heavy Cream, for the mascarpone topping
  - Additional Heavy Cream, for lightly brushing the shortcakes
  - 1/4 cup Sugar, for the mascarpone topping
  - 3 tbsp Elderflower Liqueur, for the mascarpone topping
  - A few Fresh Thyme Sprigs, for finishing
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This is strawberry-rhubarb shortcake for special occasions. The key is cutting cold butter into the flour until pea-sized to ensure a flaky, vertical rise. We use pink peppercorns for their floral heat, which bridges the gap between the tart rhubarb and the creamy mascarpone. Roast the fruit: baking the strawberries and rhubarb at 350°F concentrates their juices into a thick syrup that won't turn the shortcake soggy.

## Directions

Allow about 90 minutes, including the 30-minute dough chill. Roast the fruit during that chill and make the topping while the shortcakes bake. This is a planning estimate, not a kitchen-timed result.

1.  **The Dough:** Whisk flour, the dough sugar, baking powder, salt, and peppercorns. Cut in cold butter. Stir in buttermilk until a shaggy dough forms.
2.  **Shape:** Knead 3 times. Pat into a 6-by-9-inch rectangle, about 1 inch thick. Cut into six 3-inch squares. **Refrigerate for 30 minutes** (The Gluten Rest).
3.  **The Roast:** While the shortcakes chill, toss strawberries, rhubarb, the fruit liqueur, vanilla seeds, and fruit sugar. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast at 350°F for 20 minutes until syrupy.
4.  **Bake Shortcake:** Brush biscuit tops lightly with the additional cream. Sprinkle with the coarse sugar. Bake at 350°F for 25-30 minutes, until golden on top and browned underneath.
5.  **The Emulsion:** Whip mascarpone and the topping sugar until smooth. Slowly pour in the topping cream and whip until it holds peaks. Mix in the topping liqueur, then refrigerate until assembly.
6.  **Assemble:** Split warm shortcakes. Top with a massive mound of roasted fruit and its syrup.
7.  **Finish:** Add a dollop of mascarpone cream and fresh thyme for the final **High Note**.

RECIPE: Strawberry Rhubarb Yogurt Pops (strawberry-rhubarb-yogurt-pops.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/strawberry-rhubarb-yogurt-pops/
SOURCE: Adapted from Saveur.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.saveur.com/article/recipes/strawberry-rhubarb-yogurt-pops
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Fresh Strawberries, minced
  - 3 stalks Rhubarb, minced
  - 4 oz Plain 2% Greek Yogurt
  - 1/2 cup Orange Blossom Honey
  - 3/4 cup Fresh Orange Juice (The Acid Balance)
  - 1/4 tsp Sea Salt
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The key to successful yogurt pops is simmering the strawberries and rhubarb with the orange juice for 4 minutes. This breaks down the tough rhubarb fibers and creates a thick, pectin-rich syrup that prevents the pops from becoming icy bricks. We use Greek yogurt as the primary base to provide a creamy texture. The orange juice bridges the sweet honey and tart rhubarb.

## Directions

1.  **The Fruit:** In a small saucepan, combine minced strawberries, rhubarb, orange juice, and salt.
2.  **Simmer:** Cook over medium heat for 4 minutes until the fruit collapses and the liquid is syrupy. Let cool.
3.  **Reserve:** Using a slotted spoon, set aside 1/2 cup of the cooked fruit pieces.
4.  **Emulsify:** Transfer the remaining fruit and liquid to a blender. Add the yogurt and honey. Puree until perfectly smooth and vibrant pink.
5.  **Assemble:** Stir the reserved fruit pieces back into the puree (for texture). Divide the mixture among 10 popsicle molds.
6.  **Set:** Freeze for 1 hour. Insert sticks. Freeze for **at least 3 more hours** until rock-solid.
7.  **Serve:** Run molds under warm water for 10 seconds to release. Serve immediately.

RECIPE: Strawberry Summer Cake (strawberry-summer-cake.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/strawberry-summer-cake/
SOURCE: Adapted from smittenkitchen.com
SOURCE_URL: https://smittenkitchen.com/2011/05/strawberry-summer-cake/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Fresh Strawberries, hulled and halved
  - 1 1/2 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 1 1/2 tsp Baking Powder
  - 6 tbsp Unsalted Butter, room temp
  - 1 cup + 2 tbsp Granulated Sugar
  - 1 large Egg
  - 1/2 cup Whole Milk
  - 1 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - 1/2 tsp Sea Salt
  - Unsalted butter, as needed to grease the pan
  - Whipped cream, for serving, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Cream the softened butter and batter sugar until fluffy, then mix only until the flour disappears. Arrange the berries over the batter and add the reserved topping sugar. Lower the oven temperature after ten minutes; test cake crumb between the berries so fruit juice is not mistaken for raw batter.

## Directions

1.  **Cream:** Preheat oven to 350°F. Butter a 9-inch deep-dish pie pan with the extra greasing butter; a standard shallow 9-inch pie pan can overflow. Reserve one-ninth of the measured sugar for the topping. Beat butter and the remaining eight-ninths of the sugar (1 cup at the original batch size) for 3 minutes until pale and fluffy.
2.  **Emulsify:** Add the egg, milk, and vanilla. Mix until just combined.
3.  **Incorporate:** Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt together, then gradually add this dry mixture. Mix until **just smooth** - do not over-mix.
4.  **Layer:** Pour batter into the pan. Arrange strawberries on top, cut-side down, as closely as possible in a single layer; a little overlap is fine.
5.  **The Crunch:** Sprinkle the reserved topping sugar (2 tbsp at the original batch size) over the berries.
6.  **Bake:** Bake for 10 minutes at 350°F, then **reduce heat to 325°F**. Bake for another 50-60 minutes until golden and a tester inserted into cake crumb is free of wet batter; strawberry juice on the tester is expected.
7.  **Serve:** Let cool completely in the pan. Serve with the optional lightly whipped cream.

RECIPE: Strozzapreti with Preserved Lemon & Spinach (strozzapreti-with-spinach-and-preserved-lemon.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/strozzapreti-with-spinach-and-preserved-lemon/
SOURCE: Adapted from Bonappetit.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/strozzapreti-with-spinach-and-preserved-lemon
INGREDIENTS:
  - 12 oz Fresh Strozzapreti (or Cavatappi)
  - 1 stick (8 tbsp) Unsalted Butter
  - 1 tbsp Preserved Lemon Peel, minced
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice (The Acid Balance)
  - 2 bunches Flat-leaf Spinach, trimmed
  - 3/4 cup Panko Breadcrumbs (The Crunch)
  - 1 clove Garlic, crushed
  - 1/2 tsp Red Pepper Flakes
  - 1 tsp Lemon Zest
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Strozzapreti ("priest stranglers") is a hand-rolled pasta shape from Emilia-Romagna and other Italian regions. Browning panko breadcrumbs in garlic butter before starting the pasta gives you a crispy topping that contrasts beautifully with the soft, chewy noodles. Preserved lemon adds a fermented, salty complexity that fresh citrus can't match - it's become popular in modern Italian cooking though it originally comes from North African cuisine. Brown butter ties the earthy spinach and bright lemon together.

## Directions

1.  **The Crunch:** In a large skillet, melt 2 tbsp butter with 2 tbsp olive oil. Sauté garlic and red pepper flakes for 1 minute. Add panko and cook until golden brown and softened mahogany brown (2 mins). Stir in lemon zest. Remove to a plate.
2.  **Boil:** Cook pasta in a massive pot of salted water until **very al dente** (5 mins for fresh). Drain.
3.  **Brown Butter:** In the same skillet, melt remaining 6 tbsp butter. Whisk over medium for 3 minutes until foamy and dark brown.
4.  **The Wilt:** Add half of the spinach to the butter. Toss for 1 minute until collapsed.
5.  **Bind:** Add the hot pasta, lemon juice, and preserved lemon. Toss vigorously. Add the remaining spinach and toss for 30 seconds.
6.  **Serve:** Divide into bowls. Top with a massive pile of the reserved garlic-lemon panko for the final **High Note**.

RECIPE: Spinach & Ricotta Stuffed Shells (stuffed-shells-filled-with-spinach-and-ricotta.md)
CUISINES: Italian, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/stuffed-shells-filled-with-spinach-and-ricotta/
SOURCE: Adapted from NYT Cooking, Stuffed Shells Filled With Spinach and Ricotta
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1013942-stuffed-shells-filled-with-spinach-and-ricotta
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Pasta ---
  - 12 oz jumbo pasta shells
  - 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  - water, enough to boil the shells freely
  - salt, for the pasta water, to taste
  - --- Spinach ---
  - 5 oz fresh baby spinach
  - 1 tbsp olive oil
  - 1 garlic clove, smashed
  - --- Filling and cheese topping ---
  - 15 oz whole-milk ricotta, drain any freely pooling whey
  - 8 oz low-moisture block mozzarella, freshly shredded
  - 2 oz Parmigiano-Reggiano, finely grated
  - 1 lemon, zest only; save the juice for another use
  - 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
  - 2 tbsp fresh chives or basil, minced
  - salt, to taste
  - black pepper, to taste
  - 1 large egg, beaten
  - --- Prepared sauce ---
  - 4 cups prepared marinara or tomato pasta sauce
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Jumbo shells hold a creamy spinach-and-three-cheese filling beneath tomato sauce and a browned mozzarella topping. Squeeze excess liquid from the cooked greens and drain watery ricotta so the filling stays inside the pasta. Divide the cheeses before mixing, and arrange the shells in one layer so they heat evenly.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the oven and ingredients:** Heat the oven to 375°F. Plan on two shallow 2-quart oven-safe dishes, or enough shallow dishes to hold the cooked shells in one layer without stacking. Check that the dishes fit in the oven with space for heat to circulate. Capacity alone does not guarantee enough surface area. Bring a large pot of water toward a boil while preparing the spinach. Divide both grated cheeses into two-thirds for filling and one-third for topping.
2. **Wilt and drain the spinach:** Use fresh baby spinach, olive oil, and garlic clove. Warm the oil in a skillet over medium heat; add the smashed garlic for 30–45 seconds, then the spinach. Cook 2–3 minutes until wilted. Discard the garlic. Let the spinach cool enough to handle, squeeze out excess liquid in a clean towel and chop finely.
3. **Cook the shells short of tender:** Use jumbo pasta shells, extra-virgin olive oil, water, and salt. Salt the boiling water and cook the shells for the package’s baked-pasta time, or about 2–3 minutes short of its fully cooked time. They should be pliable enough to fill but still firm. Drain, spread out carefully and coat lightly with the measured oil. Let cool enough to handle; do not add pasta water to the filling.
4. **Mix and season the filling:** Combine whole-milk ricotta, 2/3 of the low-moisture block mozzarella, 2/3 of the Parmigiano-Reggiano, lemon, ground nutmeg, fresh chives or basil, salt, and black pepper, using only the lemon’s zest, with the prepared spinach. The cheese shares here are two-thirds of each full batch; keep the rest for the topping. Fold by hand until evenly mixed and scoopable, retaining some ricotta texture. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper now, before adding the egg.
5. **Add the egg:** Fold large egg into the seasoned filling. Do not taste the filling after adding the raw egg.
6. **Coat the dishes:** Distribute 1/4 of the prepared marinara or tomato pasta sauce across the bottoms of the baking dishes: 1 cup total for the whole batch. This sauce layer keeps the pasta from sitting against a dry dish.
7. **Fill, sauce and top:** Divide all the filling among the intact cooked shells rather than filling the first ones heavily. Arrange them opening-up in a single layer; use another shallow dish if needed. Distribute 1/3 of the low-moisture block mozzarella, 1/3 of the Parmigiano-Reggiano, and 3/4 of the prepared marinara or tomato pasta sauce over all the dishes: 3 cups sauce total and the reserved one-third of each cheese. Coat exposed pasta edges with sauce. Do not stack shells to force them into one pan.
8. **Bake to the center:** Cover the dishes with foil, tenting it away from the cheese, and bake for about 25 minutes. Uncover and bake another 15–20 minutes until the sauce bubbles and the cheese has golden spots. Check representative filled shells in the center of each dish with a thermometer: the filling and casserole must reach 165°F / 74°C. Extend the time when needed; if the top colors before the center is hot, cover loosely again. Rotate dishes if heating is uneven. Refrigerator-cold assembly takes longer.
9. **Rest and serve:** Let the dishes rest for at least 10 minutes so the filling settles, then divide the full batch into six portions. If serving with garlic bread, the rest can overlap its separate 400°F bake; serve promptly once the bread is ready.

## Make ahead and variations

This six-portion batch takes about 1 hour 30 minutes with prepared sauce: roughly 35 minutes to prepare and fill, 40–45 minutes baking and at least 10 minutes resting. A cold pan or separate oven rounds adds time.

For next-day assembly, cover and refrigerate promptly at 40°F / 4°C or below. Follow the bakeware maker’s instructions for refrigerator-to-oven transitions, allow additional baking time and check the same 165°F / 74°C center endpoint.

For more greens, use 10 oz spinach instead of 5 oz, still wilted and well squeezed; the filling will have more volume. For a vegetarian version, replace the Parmigiano with the same weight of a suitable vegetarian-rennet hard cheese, and check the other cheeses and sauce.

Refrigerate perishable leftovers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C, at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F / 74°C throughout. Divide a large leftover casserole into shallow containers for cooling.

RECIPE: Sugar Cookies (sugar-cookie.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sugar-cookie/
SOURCE: Adapted from preppykitchen.com
SOURCE_URL: https://preppykitchen.com/sugar-cookies/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 cups (480 g) All-Purpose Flour
  - 1 cup (2 sticks) (227 g) Unsalted Butter, softened
  - 1 cup (200 g) Granulated Sugar
  - 2 large Eggs
  - 2 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - 3/4 tsp Baking Powder
  - 3/4 tsp Sea Salt
  - All-purpose flour, as needed for dusting the surface and rolling pin
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Chill this cutout dough until firm, then let it become just pliable enough to roll without cracking. Keep the thickness even and bake similarly sized shapes together. Cool the cookies completely before adding icing.

## Directions

1. **Dry mix:** Sift the measured flour, sea salt and baking powder together into a bowl. Keep any flour for dusting the rolling surface separate from the measured dough flour.

2. **Cream:** With a paddle attachment, beat the softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes. Scrape the bowl, beat in the eggs one at a time, then add the vanilla.

3. **Mix and chill:** Gradually mix in the dry ingredients only until evenly incorporated. Divide the original batch into 2 disks; use additional manageable disks for a larger batch. Wrap tightly and refrigerate for at least 2 hours and up to 2 days.

4. **Prepare to roll:** When ready to bake, start preheating the oven to 375°F and line sheets with parchment. If dough chilled longer than 2 hours is too hard to roll, let it soften slightly at room temperature for 15–30 minutes, just until pliable. Work with one disk while keeping the other covered and refrigerated.

5. **Roll and cut:** Lightly flour the surface and rolling pin using the separate dusting allowance. Roll to 1/4-inch thickness and cut with 2 1/2-inch cutters, or similarly sized shapes. Reroll the scraps gently. Place 1 inch apart on the prepared sheets; bake different sizes in separate loads.

6. **Bake:** Load only after the oven reaches 375°F. Bake one sheet at a time for 10–12 minutes, beginning to check at 8 minutes, until the bottom edges just begin to turn golden brown. Portion size, shape and actual oven determine when they are ready.

7. **Cool and decorate:** Let the cookies firm on the sheet for about 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack and cool completely. Serve plain or decorate the cool cookies with separately prepared [Royal Icing](/mise/recipes/royal-icing). Use the icing recipe’s pasteurized-egg-white route. Allow the sheet to cool before loading more dough.

## Cooking Notes

For other cutter sizes, keep the same 1/4-inch dough thickness and bake similarly sized pieces together. Their finished count and baking time will differ from the original 2 1/2-inch cutter route.

Plain cookies need no icing. Royal icing, melted chocolate, buttercream or powdered-sugar finishes are optional, separately prepared decorations; no amounts are included in this dough. Their ingredients and storage requirements must be planned separately.

RECIPE: Sun-Dried Tomato Chicken Orzo Bake (sun-dried-tomato-chicken-orzo.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sun-dried-tomato-chicken-orzo/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 450 g boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
  - 300 g dry orzo pasta
  - 3 cups (720 ml) low-sodium chicken broth, heated to a simmer
  - 150 g full-fat soft fresh cow’s-milk garlic-and-herb cheese, creamy but crumbly, crumbled
  - 85 g oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, drained and chopped
  - 1 tbsp oil from the tomato jar, or olive oil
  - 140 g frozen chopped spinach, weighed before thawing, then thawed and squeezed dry
  - 1 tsp dried Italian herb seasoning
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
  - 1 tsp finely grated lemon zest
  - 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, added gradually to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The covered dish gives dry orzo time to absorb hot broth while the chicken cooks. Crumbled garlic-herb cheese mixes through more readily than a single cold block in the center. Finish with lemon juice after baking so you can judge the acidity; multiple baked lemon slices can bring more pith bitterness than this sauce needs.

## Directions

1. **Heat and prepare:** Heat oven to 400°F / 200°C. Thaw and squeeze spinach thoroughly. Bring the measured broth to a simmer in a saucepan. Toss chicken with tomato oil, dried herbs, salt, and pepper.
2. **Assemble:** Spread dry orzo in a deep 9-by-13-inch baking dish. Add tomatoes and loosened spinach, then pour in hot broth and stir gently to distribute. Scatter in crumbled garlic-and-herb cheese and arrange chicken evenly through the dish. Keep the orzo beneath the liquid as much as possible.
3. **Cover and bake:** Seal tightly with foil or a suitable lid and bake for 30 minutes.
4. **Check before tasting:** Open carefully away from your face. Stir gently to redistribute the center and edges. Probe several large chicken pieces and the casserole center for 165°F / 74°C. If below temperature, re-cover and continue baking, checking every 5–10 minutes. Only after temperature checks pass, taste orzo for tenderness. Add a little hot water and continue covered if pasta is still firm and the pan is drying.
5. **Finish the sauce:** When chicken and pasta are ready, fold gently to disperse the cheese. Stir in lemon zest and half the lemon juice. Rest 5 minutes, then taste and add the remaining juice only if needed. Divide into four portions; a lightly dressed green salad complements the rich bake.

RECIPE: Sun-Dried Tomato Chicken Pasta (sun-dried-tomato-pasta-with-chicken-and-mozzarella.md)
CUISINES: Italian, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sun-dried-tomato-pasta-with-chicken-and-mozzarella/
SOURCE: Adapted from juliasalbum.com
SOURCE_URL: https://juliasalbum.com/chicken-mozzarella-pasta-with-sun-dried-tomatoes/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 450 g chicken tenderloins, cut crosswise into 1/2-inch-thick pieces
  - 225 g dry penne pasta
  - 1 cup (240 ml) half-and-half
  - 110 g low-moisture mozzarella, freshly grated
  - 85 g oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, drained and chopped
  - 2 tbsp oil from the tomato jar, divided, or olive oil
  - 120 g fresh spinach, washed and roughly chopped
  - 2 tbsp chopped fresh basil
  - 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes, or less to taste
  - 1/4 tsp paprika
  - 3 cloves garlic, minced
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt, for chicken
  - 2 liters water for boiling pasta
  - 1 1/2 tsp fine salt, for pasta water
  - 1 cup (240 ml) pasta cooking water, reserved before draining and added only as needed
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The sauce should coat the pasta, with the gentle stretch of mozzarella. Cook chicken separately to its temperature endpoint, then build the sauce at lower heat. Reserve pasta water so you can loosen the final mixture a little at a time; the whole reserved cup rarely needs to go in at once.

## Directions

1. **Start pasta water:** Bring the measured water and pasta salt to a boil while preparing the other ingredients. Add penne and cook according to the package to al dente, coordinating it with the sauce. Reserve one cup cooking water before draining.
2. **Cook chicken:** Season chicken with its measured salt and paprika. Heat one tablespoon tomato oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Cook chicken in an even layer about 3 minutes on the first side, then turn and cook another 2–3 minutes, checking the thickest pieces for 165°F / 74°C. Work in batches if crowded. Transfer finished chicken to a clean plate.
3. **Cook aromatics gently:** Lower heat to medium-low. Add remaining oil, tomatoes, garlic, and red pepper flakes; stir for about 1 minute until fragrant without scorching.
4. **Build and combine:** Add half-and-half and bring only to a gentle simmer for about 2 minutes. Fold in drained penne, cooked chicken and its juices, and spinach. Cook gently, folding, until spinach wilts, about 1–2 minutes. Add a small splash of reserved pasta water if the mixture is dry.
5. **Melt cheese off heat:** Take the pan off heat and wait for bubbling to stop. Add mozzarella in small handfuls, folding gently as it softens. If necessary, return briefly to very low heat without boiling. Add pasta water a tablespoon or two at a time to reach a creamy coating; you may not use all of it. Fold in basil.
6. **Serve:** Taste before adding any further seasoning, then divide into four portions. Serve promptly while the sauce is loose and the cheese soft.

RECIPE: Super Lemony Olive Oil Cake (super-lemony-olive-oil-cake.md)
CUISINES: Mediterranean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/super-lemony-olive-oil-cake/
SOURCE: Adapted from bonappetit.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/super-lemony-olive-oil-cake?intcid=inline_amp
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Cake batter ---
  - 1 1/2 cups extra-virgin olive oil
  - 2 cups all-purpose flour
  - 1 1/4 cups whole milk
  - 1 1/4 cups granulated sugar
  - 3 large eggs
  - 2 large lemons, wash; use all zest and juice
  - 2 tsp pure vanilla extract
  - 1/2 tsp baking powder
  - 1/2 tsp baking soda
  - 1 tsp sea salt
  - --- Pan oil ---
  - extra-virgin olive oil, enough to lightly oil the pan and parchment
  - --- Sugar topping ---
  - 1 tbsp granulated sugar
  - --- Serving finish ---
  - powdered sugar, a light dusting just before serving
  - lemon zest, a little extra just before serving, if desired, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Mina Stone’s lemon olive-oil cake uses the full oil, whole milk, lemon juice and zest in a whisked batter. Keep the listed surface sugar amount separate from the batter sugar, and the pan oil separate from the batter oil. A golden top and a clean center tester are both needed before the cake cools in its pan.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 350°F. For the original batch use a 9-inch springform pan. Brush the pan lightly with extra-virgin olive oil, line its bottom with a parchment round and lightly oil the parchment. The extra pan oil is separate from the full measured batter oil. When scaling, keep a similar batter depth with proportional pan area or additional pans; do not put extra full batches into this one pan.
2. **Whisk the base:** Whisk extra-virgin olive oil, granulated sugar, and large eggs in a bowl until smooth and combined. This is the batter sugar and full measured batter oil, separate from the pan oil and sugar topping.
3. **Add milk and lemon:** Whisk in whole milk, large lemons, and pure vanilla extract, using the full zest and juice of the listed lemons.
4. **Mix dry ingredients:** In a separate bowl, whisk all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, and sea salt until evenly distributed.
5. **Combine:** Make a well in the dry mixture and gradually whisk in the egg mixture, using circular motions. Stop when mostly smooth with no dry flour pockets; some small lumps are acceptable, but lumps are not required.
6. **Fill and top:** Scrape into the prepared pan and smooth the surface. Sprinkle granulated sugar over the top; this is additional to all the batter sugar.
7. **Bake:** Wait for the oven to reach 350°F. Bake about 50 minutes, until golden on top AND a tester inserted into the center comes out clean. Do not deliberately remove a wet-batter cake to rely on residual heat. Changed pan depths and oven loads need their own checks.
8. **Cool:** Set the pan on a wire rack and let the cake cool completely before unmolding. Cooling time is additional and has no fixed duration here.
9. **Serve:** Just before serving, dust with powdered sugar and lemon zest (if using), adding the extra zest only if desired.

## Cooking Notes

### Salt and make-ahead notes

The listed sea salt is the main version. For the publisher’s original-batch option, use either 1 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt or ½ tsp Morton kosher salt instead of the entire listed sea-salt amount. Multiply the chosen amount with the batch, add it with the dry ingredients and keep every other ingredient and step unchanged. These are the two exact source choices; neither is an established sea-salt equivalence.

The plain cake may be baked three days ahead. Cool before wrapping and store tightly wrapped at room temperature. Add the powdered sugar and optional extra zest shortly before serving. Any separately added perishable topping needs its own storage plan.

RECIPE: Sweet and Spicy Spareribs (sweet-and-spicy-spareribs-with-korean-barbecue-sauce.md)
CUISINES: Korean
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sweet-and-spicy-spareribs-with-korean-barbecue-sauce/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/sweet-and-spicy-spareribs-korean-barbecue-sauce
INGREDIENTS:
  - 8 lbs Pork Spareribs, membranes removed
  - 1 cup Gochujang (Fermented Hot Pepper Paste)
  - 1/2 cup Hoisin Sauce
  - 1/2 cup Honey + 1/2 cup Soy Sauce
  - 1/2 cup Sake (The complex flavor Pulse)
  - 2 tbsp Rice Vinegar (The Acid Balance)
  - 2 tbsp Fresh Ginger, grated
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Garlic, minced
  - 2 tbsp White Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The key to restaurant-quality spareribs is baking the ribs tightly sealed in heavy-duty foil. This allows the meat to steam in the gochujang marinade, breaking down the tough connective tissue into succulent meat without losing any flavor to a pot of water. We finish by grilling the sections at medium-low heat to ensure the sugar-rich sauce sets into a sticky, mahogany glaze without burning.

## Directions

1.  **The Sauce:** In a large bowl, whisk together gochujang, hoisin, honey, soy sauce, sake, vinegar, and all aromatics until smooth.
2.  **Braise:** Preheat oven to 325°F. Layout three double-layers of heavy-duty foil. Place 1 rack of ribs in the center of each.
3.  **Seal:** Brush each rack with 3/4 cup of the sauce. Wrap tightly to ensure no steam escapes. Place on rimmed baking sheets.
4.  **Bake:** Bake for 2 hours until the meat is tender but not quite falling off the bone.
5.  **The Crunch:** Preheat a grill to medium-low. Remove ribs from foil, wipe off excess marinade, and cut into 4-rib sections.
6.  **Glaze:** Brush lightly with remaining sauce. Grill for 3-4 minutes per side until caramelized; watch carefully so the sugar doesn't burn.
7.  **Serve:** Transfer to a platter. Serve with extra lime wedges for the mandatory **Acid Balance**.

RECIPE: Sweet and White Potato Gratin (sweet-and-white-potato-gratin.md)
CUISINES: French
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sweet-and-white-potato-gratin/
SOURCE: Adapted from Kaitlin Gwock
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 lbs Sweet Potatoes, peeled
  - 1.5 lbs White Potatoes (Yukon Gold), peeled
  - 3 cups Heavy Cream
  - 3 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Thyme
  - 1 tbsp Fresh Sage
  - 1 tsp Fresh Rosemary, chopped
  - 2 tsp Salt
  - 1 tsp Black Pepper
  - 1/4 tsp Nutmeg
  - Dash of Cayenne Pepper
  - 2.5 cups Gruyère Cheese, shredded
  - 2 cups Parmesan Reggiano, finely grated
  - Additional fresh thyme, as needed for optional garnish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Kaitlin Gwock’s gratin alternates sweet potatoes and Yukon Golds beneath the full cream and cheese. Keep the slices evenly about 1/8 inch thick. Whisk the seasonings into the cream so every layer gets them; cook until a knife slips through the center layers, and tent the top if it browns first.

## Directions

1. **Mix:** Preheat the oven to 425°F. Whisk all the cream, garlic, thyme, sage, rosemary, nutmeg, cayenne, salt and pepper together.
2. **Slice:** Use a sharp knife or a mandoline with its hand guard to cut the peeled potatoes into even 1/8-inch rounds. Keep the colors separate for layering.
3. **Combine cheese:** Mix all the Gruyère and Parmesan together.
4. **Layer:** For the original batch, use a 9×13-inch oven-safe dish with enough depth for the full potatoes, cream and cheese. If necessary, divide the entire batch among additional dishes before layering, keeping similar depth and headroom. Divide all measured ingredients among the dishes. Pour one-sixth of each dish’s allocated cream over its bottom. Alternate overlapping sweet-potato and white-potato layers, dividing the rest of its cream and cheese through the layers and reserving cheese for its top. Use all the cream; do not leave a fixed-volume remainder behind.
5. **Top:** Arrange the last layer in alternating colors if desired and cover with the reserved cheese.
6. **Start covered:** Cover with foil and bake at 425°F for 15 minutes.
7. **Finish:** Remove the foil and reduce the oven to 400°F. Bake about another 45 minutes, until a knife passes easily through the potato layers in the center of each dish. If the top browns before the potatoes soften, cover loosely with foil and continue checking; thicker slices or deeper layers need longer.
8. **Rest:** Rest for 10 minutes before serving so the layers hold together. Add the optional additional thyme garnish if using it.

## Timing

The original 95-minute estimate includes 25 minutes of preparation, about 60 minutes of baking and the 10-minute rest. Extra loads, thicker slices or deeper dishes can take longer; the center’s tenderness governs.
