RECIPE: Sweet Chili Chicken Sliders (sweet-chili-chicken-sliders.md)
CUISINES: Thai, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sweet-chili-chicken-sliders/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Chicken and marinade ---
  - 2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, raw; fresh or fully thawed
  - 2 tbsp soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp sesame oil
  - 3 garlic cloves, peeled and minced
  - 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
  - --- Clean glaze ---
  - 1/2 cup Thai sweet chili sauce
  - 1 tbsp soy sauce
  - 1 tbsp rice vinegar
  - --- Rolls, slaw and mayo ---
  - 12 Hawaiian rolls, split
  - 1 bag of chopped Asian-style salad kit, cabbage, crisp toppings and sesame dressing; use the complete kit, following its preparation label
  - 1/4 cup mayonnaise
  - 1 tbsp Sriracha
  - 2 tbsp butter, melted
  - sesame seeds, as wanted for topping
  - fresh cilantro, as wanted for topping, washed and chopped, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This slider gets its depth from a quick soy-sesame-garlic marinade that seasons the chicken before it hits the broiler. The sweet chili glaze goes on at the end for that sticky, lacquered finish. Don't skip the sriracha mayo - it bridges the sweet glaze and savory chicken. The store-bought Asian salad kit (cabbage, crispy wontons, sesame dressing) is a legit shortcut that adds crunch, freshness, and another layer of sesame flavor. Toast those Hawaiian rolls - the butter helps them stand up to the juicy chicken.
For kids, serve the heat on the side or reduce/omit the spicy elements.

## Directions

1. **Marinate cold:** Toss all boneless skinless chicken thighs, soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic cloves, and fresh ginger together. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours. Keep the separate glaze, mayo and slaw away from raw chicken and used utensils. Thaw frozen chicken in the refrigerator beforehand.
2. **Mix clean glaze:** Whisk all Thai sweet chili sauce, soy sauce, and rice vinegar in a clean bowl and set aside for the cooked chicken. Keep this whole measured glaze separate from the used marinade.
3. **Mix mayo:** Use mayonnaise and Sriracha for the mayo. For the standard version, mix the full mayonnaise and Sriracha together. For a milder version, keep all the mayonnaise plain and offer the listed Sriracha separately or omit it. Refrigerate until assembly.
4. **Broil chicken:** Use a broiler-safe metal sheet pan and the rack position allowed by the oven, about 6 inches below the element where permitted. Lift thighs from the marinade, shake off excess and discard the used marinade. Arrange in one layer without overlap; use more loads if needed. Start checking at 6–7 minutes per side, turning as the surface browns, and continue until the thickest part of each thigh reaches 165°F / 74°C. Charred spots do not establish the center temperature. Transfer cooked thighs with clean utensils.
5. **Glaze:** Brush all the clean glaze over the fully cooked chicken. Broil about 1–2 minutes, watching closely, until the coating is sticky and lightly caramelized; remove before it burns. Use clean brushing/serving utensils.
6. **Rest and toast rolls:** Rest the chicken for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, use all Hawaiian rolls and butter: brush the roll cut faces with the melted butter, put them cut-side up on a clean broiler-safe metal pan and watch for 1–2 minutes until golden. Remove promptly; toasting can require separate loads.
7. **Finish slaw:** Use the listed bag of chopped Asian-style salad kit for the slaw, following the kit's preparation label. Toss all the cabbage with all the kit dressing and include all its crisp toppings at assembly. Keep ready-to-eat slaw away from raw-chicken surfaces.
8. **Divide and assemble:** Once the chicken has rested, divide all of it into one bun-sized portion for each measured roll. Spread all the mayo across the rolls, add the chicken and complete slaw, then add sesame seeds and fresh cilantro (if using) as wanted. Serve promptly; any Sriracha kept separate goes to the table rather than into a second mayo dose.

RECIPE: Sweet Potato Fries (sweet-potato-fries.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sweet-potato-fries/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1014647-sweet-potato-fries
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 lbs Sweet Potatoes, peeled
  - 2 tbsp Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 1 tsp Garlic Powder
  - 1 tsp Smoked Paprika
  - 1 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1/2 tsp Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The secret to sweet potato fries that aren't limp and oily is proper spacing. Sweet potatoes have more moisture than Russets; you must spread them across two separate baking sheets to ensure every fry has at least 1 inch of space. This allows the hot air to circulate, resulting in caramelized edges rather than steamed softness. We use smoked paprika as the essential savory element - it introduces a wood-fired depth that balances the natural sweetness of the potato.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 400°F. Line two rimmed baking sheets with parchment paper.
2.  **Cut:** Slice sweet potatoes into uniform sticks, about 1/2-inch wide and 3 inches long.
3.  **Toss:** In a large bowl, whisk the oil and all spices. Add the potatoes and toss vigorously until every stick is perfectly coated.
4.  **The Guard:** Spread the fries onto the two pans. Ensure **no fries are touching**.
5.  **Bake:** Roast for 15 minutes. Flip the fries with a metal spatula.
6.  **The Crunch:** Roast for another 10-12 minutes until the edges are dark brown and crispy.
7.  **Serve:** Serve immediately while hot. (Note: do not cover them, or the steam will destroy the snap).

RECIPE: Potato Latkes (sweet-potato-latkes.md)
CUISINES: Jewish
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sweet-potato-latkes/
SOURCE: Adapted from Epicurious.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/sweet-potato-latkes-105919
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb Sweet Potatoes, peeled and coarsely grated
  - 2 large Eggs, beaten
  - 1/3 cup All-Purpose Flour
  - 2 Scallions, finely chopped
  - 1 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1/2 tsp Black Pepper
  - 3/4 cup Neutral Oil (for frying)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Traditional latkes rely on starch; sweet potato latkes rely on proper moisture removal. You must squeeze the grated potatoes in a kitchen towel until they are bone-dry before mixing with the eggs; this ensures the latke sets into a firm texture rather than falling apart in the pan. We fry in 1/2-inch of hot oil to create a deep, lattice-like crunch on the exterior that mimics the best diner-style hash browns. The scallions provide the fresh, savory finish.

## Directions

1.  **The Squeeze:** Grate the potatoes. Wrap in a clean kitchen towel and **squeeze with maximum force** until no more juice drips out. Place in a bowl.
2.  **The Bind:** Stir in the scallions, flour, salt, and pepper. Add the eggs and mix until a tacky, thick batter forms.
3.  **Thermal Prep:** Heat oil in a heavy 12-inch skillet over medium-high until shimmering but not smoking.
4.  **The Crunch:** Spoon 1/8-cup portions into the oil. Use a spatula to flatten them into 3-inch disks.
5.  **Fry:** Cook for 2 minutes per side until the edges are deep golden and the center is set. Do not crowd the pan (4 latkes per batch).
6.  **Drain:** Transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate. Season with a final pinch of salt while hot.
7.  **Serve:** Serve immediately with [Nana Ruth's Applesauce](/mise/recipes/nana-ruths-applesauce).

RECIPE: Sweet Potato Sausage Breakfast Casserole (sweet-potato-sausage-breakfast-casserole.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sweet-potato-sausage-breakfast-casserole/
SOURCE: allthehealthythings.com
SOURCE_URL: https://allthehealthythings.com/sausage-breakfast-casserole/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 pound sweet potatoes, peeled and diced into 1/4 inch chunks
  - 1/2 tablespoon avocado oil
  - 12 large eggs
  - 1/2 cup unsweetened almond milk
  - 1/4 cup thinly sliced green onion
  - 1 tablespoon hot sauce
  - 1 teaspoon salt
  - 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  - 3/4 cup shredded sharp white cheddar cheese
  - 1 pound ground breakfast sausage or ground pork
  - 1 small to medium yellow onion, diced
  - 1 small to medium red bell pepper, diced
  - 1 small to medium green bell pepper, diced
  - 3 cloves garlic, finely minced
  - 5 oz baby spinach, chopped
  - Olive or avocado oil spray, as needed for the baking dish
  - Additional green onion, as needed for optional topping
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Roast the small sweet-potato cubes until tender before the eggs go in. Cook the sausage and wilt the spinach first, retaining their full mixture for the casserole. Spread the filling evenly, then bake until the center is set and reaches 165°F; a browned edge does not measure the middle.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 400°F. Wash the fresh vegetables before preparing them. Lightly grease an oven-safe 9×13-inch casserole dish for the original batch with the separate oil spray. Check its actual depth: when the full filling will not leave headroom, divide every ingredient among additional dishes before roasting or assembling, keeping similar depth.
2. **Roast potatoes:** Toss all the peeled 1/4-inch sweet-potato cubes with the full listed avocado oil in the prepared dish or dishes. Bake for about 15–20 minutes, until a cube in the center is tender when pierced; remove from the oven.
3. **Mix eggs:** While the potatoes roast, whisk all the eggs, almond milk, measured green onion, hot sauce, salt and pepper together. Fold in all the cheddar.
4. **Cook sausage:** Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add all the raw ground breakfast sausage or ground pork, breaking it up as it cooks. Cook ground pork to 160°F /71°C, or poultry sausage to 165°F /74°C; use raw ground sausage and follow its package instructions. Use additional skillet rounds if necessary rather than crowding it.
5. **Cook vegetables:** Add all the yellow onion, red and green bell peppers and garlic to the cooked sausage. Sauté for about 3–5 minutes, until the vegetables begin to soften. Reduce the heat if the garlic darkens before the vegetables soften.
6. **Wilt spinach:** Add all the spinach and stir for about 30 seconds to 1 minute, until wilted. Remove the skillet from the heat. Retain the full cooked sausage, vegetables and pan juices for assembly.
7. **Assemble:** Divide the full cooked skillet mixture among the roasted-potato dishes and toss together. Pour the egg mixture evenly over them, dividing all the eggs and filling among the dishes in the same proportions.
8. **Bake and serve:** Bake at 400°F for about 35–40 minutes, beginning checks at 30 minutes, until the egg center is set and reaches 165°F /74°C in each dish. A deeper load can take longer. Let stand until safe to handle and firm enough to slice, then cut into the listed planning count of slices. Add the separate optional extra green onion if desired.

RECIPE: Spinach Muffins (sweet-spinach-muffins.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/sweet-spinach-muffins/
SOURCE: Adapted from Superhealthykids.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.superhealthykids.com/sweet-spinach-muffins/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 6 oz Fresh Baby Spinach
  - 1 large Ripe Banana
  - 1/2 cup Unsalted Butter, melted
  - 1/2 cup Honey
  - 1 large Egg
  - 1 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - 3/4 cup Whole Milk
  - 2 cups Whole-wheat Flour
  - 1 1/2 tsp Ground Cinnamon
  - 2 tsp Baking Powder + 1/2 tsp Baking Soda
  - 1/4 tsp Sea Salt
  - Butter or baking spray, as needed for muffin cups if not using paper liners
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Puree the spinach, banana and wet ingredients before gently folding them into the whole-wheat dry mixture. Butter, honey and cinnamon give the batter richness and warmth; check a center muffin for doneness and let the muffins mostly cool before serving.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 350°F before mixing. For the original 18-muffin batch, line 18 standard cups across two tins, or grease the cups with the pan allowance. When scaling, prepare enough standard cups for the listed batch. Wash spinach unless labeled prewashed and ready to eat, and drain it. Melt the butter and let it cool slightly before combining it with the egg.

5. **Bake:** Fill the prepared cups no more than ¾ full. Bake for 18–22 minutes, until the tops are firm and a center tester has no wet batter. Bake excess batter separately. If the required tins do not fit with room for air circulation, bake in separate oven batches.

6. **Cool:** Once the muffins can be handled without breaking, transfer them from the pans to a rack. Cool most or all of the way before serving, and fully before sealing for storage.

RECIPE: Chili-Garlic Eggplant and Tofu (szechuan-eggplant-and-tofu.md)
CUISINES: Chinese-inspired
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/szechuan-eggplant-and-tofu/
SOURCE: Adapted from Foodnetwork.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/jeff-mauro/crispy-szechuan-style-eggplant-and-tofu-2352484
INGREDIENTS:
  - 600 g eggplant, ends trimmed, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
  - 400 g drained extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
  - 2 tbsp neutral oil, for roasting eggplant
  - 2 tbsp neutral oil, for pan-frying tofu
  - 1 tsp neutral oil, for aromatics
  - 2 tbsp (16 g) cornstarch, for coating tofu
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) unsalted vegetable broth or water
  - 2 tbsp reduced-sodium soy sauce
  - 2 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar
  - 1 1/2 tbsp (18 g) granulated sugar
  - 1 tsp cornstarch, for the sauce, mixed with the separately measured cold slurry water
  - 2 tsp cold water, for the sauce slurry
  - 1 tbsp finely minced fresh ginger
  - 2 cloves garlic, finely minced
  - 1 Thai bird chili, finely sliced, optional; remove seeds for less heat
  - 2 tsp toasted sesame oil
  - 1 tsp fresh lime juice, optional, only if wanted after tasting
  - 20 g scallions, thinly sliced
  - 1 tbsp chopped cilantro, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Roasting makes eggplant tender while tofu browns in a measured amount of pan oil. A short final toss gives both a sweet-sour garlic coating. The texture contrast is silky eggplant against firmer browned tofu; the sauce will soften the starch crust, so serve soon after coating.

## Directions

1. **Heat and press:** Heat oven to 425°F / 220°C. Drain tofu and press gently between clean towels under a plate for fifteen minutes while you cut eggplant and measure the sauce ingredients. Cut pressed tofu into 3/4-inch cubes and pat dry.
2. **Roast eggplant:** Toss eggplant with its 2 tbsp roasting oil and spread in one layer on a rimmed sheet. Roast 25–35 minutes, turning around halfway, until browned and thoroughly tender. Use a fork to check centers. If it finishes before the tofu, take it out and hold briefly on the tray.
3. **Mix sauce:** Stir broth, soy sauce, rice vinegar and sugar together. Mix the separate sauce cornstarch with its measured cold slurry water. Keep ginger, garlic and optional chili ready beside the stove.
4. **Brown tofu during the roast:** Toss dry tofu with the 2 tbsp coating cornstarch and shake off loose excess. Heat its 2 tbsp frying oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add tofu in one layer and cook about 10–15 minutes total, turning carefully until several faces are golden and no dry coating remains. Transfer to a plate. Use another batch if pieces cannot fit with space.
5. **Make the sauce when both components are ready:** Wipe away loose or burned starch carefully. Lower heat to medium, add the separate teaspoon oil, then ginger and optional chili for 20 seconds. Add garlic and stir another 20 seconds. Pour in the broth mixture and bring to a simmer. Stir the slurry again, add half, and simmer 20–30 seconds. Add more only if needed for a light coating; discard unused slurry.
6. **Combine gently:** Fold in roasted eggplant and browned tofu and heat briefly until coated. If tight, loosen with a tablespoon of hot water. Take off heat and add sesame oil. Taste before optional lime juice.
7. **Serve:** Fold in scallions and optional cilantro, then divide into four portions with plain rice prepared separately. Serve promptly for the best remaining tofu texture.

RECIPE: Weeknight Ground-Turkey Tacos (tacos.md)
CUISINES: Tex-Mex, American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/tacos/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Filling ---
  - 450 g (1 lb) ground turkey, preferably 93% lean
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil
  - 2 tsp mild chili powder blend, not pure hot chile powder
  - 1 tsp ground cumin
  - 1/2 tsp sweet paprika
  - 1/2 tsp garlic powder
  - 1/2 tsp onion powder
  - 1/2 tsp fine salt, divided
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) low-sodium chicken broth
  - --- Shells and toppings, for the whole batch ---
  - 12 small taco shells total: hard shells, 6-inch soft tortillas, or a mixture
  - 80 g sharp Cheddar, grated
  - 1 large avocado, about 150 g edible flesh, sliced just before serving
  - 200 g Roma tomatoes, diced and drained of pooled juice
  - 120 g iceberg lettuce, finely shredded
  - 1/4 cup (60 g) sour cream
  - 1 lime, cut into 8 wedges
  - 2 tsp hot sauce, optional and served separately
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

These are Tex-Mex-style family tacos with a ground-turkey base. Browning develops savory flavor; the small broth addition then loosens the pan residue and coats the crumbles. Bouillon is optional pantry seasoning, not a substance that guarantees juicy meat. Here, measured spices and low-sodium broth make the salt easier to control.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the table components:** Grate Cheddar, dice and drain tomatoes, shred lettuce and cut the lime. Measure sour cream and optional hot sauce. Keep perishable toppings chilled. Set out twelve shells total. If using hard shells, preheat the oven as their package directs.
2. **Brown the turkey:** Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high. Add turkey in several flattened pieces and leave about 2 minutes for the underside to color. Turn and break into coarse crumbles, cooking another 4–5 minutes and adjusting heat to avoid scorching.
3. **Season and finish:** Lower to medium. Stir in all five spices and half the measured salt for about 20 seconds, then add broth and scrape up the brown residue. Simmer 3–5 minutes, stirring and breaking up large pieces, until the coating clings without a watery pool. Check several substantial clumps with a thin-tip thermometer: turkey must reach 165°F / 74°C. Taste and add the remaining salt only if needed. Add a tablespoon of water if the filling dries before reaching its endpoint.
4. **Warm the shells:** Heat hard shells according to their package. For soft tortillas, use a dry skillet over medium-high, usually 10–30 seconds per side until hot and flexible; work in batches and wrap in a clean towel. Alternatively, microwave stacks of four to six between damp paper towels for 30–45 seconds, extending briefly if still cool. Keep filling covered off heat during this short warming step.
5. **Assemble just before eating:** Slice avocado. Divide the filling among twelve small tacos, about one-twelfth per shell, and offer the measured toppings. Serve three per person. Add lime and hot sauce to individual taste rather than soaking every shell in advance.

## Make it a meal

The tacos already include tortillas, protein, avocado and fresh vegetables. A small portion of [Skillet Esquites](/mise/recipes/mexican-street-corn-salad) is one possible side; a complete rice-and-bean spread is a different, longer dinner plan.

RECIPE: Tahini Sauce (tahini-sauce.md)
CUISINES: Middle Eastern
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/tahini-sauce/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1/2 cup (120 g) tahini, thoroughly stirred in its jar
  - 3 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus up to 1 tbsp more to taste
  - 1 small clove garlic, finely grated
  - 1/4 tsp fine salt
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) cool water, plus more a tablespoon at a time as needed
  - 1/8 tsp ground cumin, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Tahini sauce turns concentrated sesame paste into a dressing with lemon, garlic, salt, and water. The first addition of liquid can make it unexpectedly stiff. Keep whisking in water gradually until it reaches the texture you need. Ice water is not a requirement; cool water gives you control without adding more acidity every time the sauce needs thinning.

## Directions

1. **Stir and season:** Stir the tahini jar thoroughly, then measure into a bowl. Add the initial measured lemon juice, garlic, salt, and optional cumin. Whisk together; the mixture may become thick.
2. **Add water gradually:** Whisk in the measured cool water a tablespoon at a time. Continue whisking until smooth. Add more water in small increments if needed for a drizzle, or leave thicker for a dip.
3. **Balance and serve:** Taste on a bite of the food it will accompany. Add some or all of the reserved lemon juice only if needed; adjust salt sparingly. Use immediately or refrigerate. For four shawarma portions, set aside 1/2 cup sauce and refrigerate the rest.

RECIPE: Tamagoyaki (Japanese Rolled Omelet) (tamagoyaki-japanese-rolled-omelet.md)
CUISINES: Japanese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/tamagoyaki-japanese-rolled-omelet/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 8 Large Eggs
  - 3 tbsp Dashi (or chicken stock), cooled slightly
  - 2 tbsp Mirin
  - 1 tbsp Soy Sauce
  - 1 tbsp Sugar
  - 1/4 tsp Salt
  - 1 tbsp Vegetable Oil, plus more for the pan
  - --- Optional ---
  - 1 tbsp Mitsuba (Japanese parsley) or chives, finely chopped
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Tamagoyaki is a Japanese omelet rolled into a compact log and sliced thin - a technique that's been perfected by home cooks for generations and looks more impressive than it is. The egg is whisked with dashi and mirin (sweet rice vinegar), creating something between an omelet and a custard. The rolling happens directly in the pan: you layer thin sheets of cooked egg, rolling from one end to the other, then slice it into rounds. It appears on every bento box, appears at breakfast, and is surprisingly forgiving once you understand the roll. The key is a rectangular tamagoyaki pan, which makes the rolling intuitive - but a regular 8-inch square skillet works fine too.

## Directions

1. **Make the Egg Mixture:** In a small bowl, whisk together eggs, dashi, mirin, soy sauce, sugar, and salt until completely combined and uniform. The mixture should be light yellow and frothy. If using mitsuba, fold it in gently now. Let the mixture rest for 1 minute while you heat the pan.

2. **Heat the Pan:** Use a tamagoyaki pan (rectangular Japanese omelet pan) or a small non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add 1 tbsp vegetable oil and let it coat the pan evenly. Wait 30 seconds until the oil shimmers - do not let it smoke.

3. **First Layer:** Pour about 1/4 of the egg mixture into the hot pan, tilting to distribute it evenly in a thin, even layer. Let it cook for about 1-2 minutes until the bottom is set and the top is still slightly wet. This should happen quickly.

4. **Roll:** Using a wooden spatula or chopsticks, gently roll the cooked egg from one end toward the other, creating a tight log. Push the rolled egg to the far side of the pan.

5. **Repeat Layers:** Lightly oil the empty side of the pan. Pour another 1/4 of the egg mixture into the empty space, tilting so it flows under and around the rolled egg. Let it set for 1-2 minutes until mostly firm but still slightly wet on top.

6. **Continue Rolling:** Roll the entire log (including the new layer) from the far end back toward you, creating a larger roll with multiple layers.

7. **Final Layers:** Repeat the process two more times, oiling lightly and pouring the remaining egg mixture around the roll, cooking until set, then rolling forward. By the final roll, your tamagoyaki should be a compact, multi-layered log about 2 inches wide.

8. **Finish Cooking:** Once all egg is incorporated, let the roll cook for 1-2 more minutes, rotating it gently so all sides are lightly cooked and the exterior is set.

9. **Cool and Slice:** Transfer the tamagoyaki to a cutting board. Let it cool for 2 minutes (cooling helps it hold together while slicing). Using a sharp knife, cut the roll into 1/2-inch thick rounds. The layers will be visible and beautiful.

10. **Serve:** Serve warm or at room temperature, often with a small dish of soy sauce for dipping. Can be packed in bento boxes with rice and pickles.

**Pan Choice:** A tamagoyaki pan is narrow and rectangular (about 3 by 4 inches), which makes rolling intuitive. But a regular 8-inch non-stick skillet works - just make slightly thinner layers and be gentler with the roll.

**Dashi Source:** Quick dashi takes 5 minutes (kombu and bonito flakes steeped in hot water) but instant dashi powder (available at any Asian market) is fine. Regular chicken stock works if you prefer.

**Rolling Confidence:** The first roll feels awkward; by the second, you'll get the rhythm. Don't overthink it - the egg is forgiving and will fuse as it cooks.

**Make-Ahead:** Tamagoyaki tastes equally good warm or at room temperature and keeps well in the fridge for 2-3 days, making it perfect for bento box prep.

RECIPE: Tarragon Potatoes (tarragon-potatoes.md)
CUISINES: French
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/tarragon-potatoes/
SOURCE: Adapted from Craig Plummer
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 lbs Russet Potatoes, cubed (1.5-inch chunks)
  - 2 tbsp Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
  - 2 tbsp Unsalted Butter (Cold)
  - 1 tbsp Dried Tarragon (The "High Note")
  - 1 tsp Sea Salt
  - 1/2 tsp Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The secret to excellent tarragon potatoes is the butter-finish technique. Tarragon has a powerful, anise-like flavor that can become bitter if burned; we toss the potatoes in oil and herbs first, then add cold butter cubes to the pan halfway through roasting. This creates a foaming butter that bastes the potatoes, ensuring a rich interior inside a crispy golden crust. Be precise with the tarragon - its bright flavor defines the dish.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a baking dish with parchment.
2.  **Toss:** Combine potato cubes, olive oil, salt, pepper, and tarragon in a large bowl. Toss vigorously until every chunk is heavily coated.
3.  **Roast:** Arrange in a **single layer** (The Single-Layer Guard). Bake for 25 minutes.
4.  **The Sizzle:** Remove pan. Add the cold butter cubes to the dish and toss the potatoes to coat in the melting fat.
5.  **Finish:** Return to oven. Bake for 20 more minutes, tossing once, until the potatoes are deep golden brown and the edges are crispy.
6.  **Serve:** Serve immediately while the herb aroma is at its peak.

RECIPE: Holy Basil Chicken (Pad Kra Pao) (thai-basil-chicken-pad-kra-pao.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/thai-basil-chicken-pad-kra-pao/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 680 g ground chicken, preferably thigh meat
  - 2 tbsp fish sauce
  - 1 tbsp light soy sauce
  - 2 tsp palm sugar or brown sugar
  - 1/4 cup (60 ml) unsalted chicken stock or water
  - 4 cloves garlic, finely chopped
  - 1 to 4 Thai bird chiles, finely chopped, to suit your heat preference
  - 30 g holy basil leaves, tough stems removed
  - 4 tbsp neutral oil, divided between chicken and eggs
  - 4 large eggs
  - 1 lime, cut into wedges, optional at the table
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Holy basil, garlic and chile give pad kra pao its character. Fish sauce and soy supply savory seasoning, with a little sugar to round it out. Thai basil is a useful substitution with a different aroma. Serve each portion with its fried egg and separately prepared rice. A shallow layer of oil is enough for the egg method here.

## Directions

1. **Prepare everything:** Stir fish sauce, light soy, sugar, and stock until the sugar dissolves. Chop garlic and chiles and pick basil leaves. Keep chicken refrigerated until the pan is ready. Set out a second skillet for the eggs.
2. **Cook chicken in two batches:** Heat 2 tsp oil in a 12-inch skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add half the chicken, spread it out, and leave about 1–2 minutes. Break into small pieces and continue cooking, stirring, until the chicken reaches 165°F / 74°C, usually about 5–7 minutes total. Transfer to a clean bowl. Repeat with another 2 tsp oil and the remaining chicken.
3. **Fry the eggs near serving:** Heat 2 tbsp oil in the second skillet over medium heat. Crack in the eggs, leaving space between them; use two batches if they crowd. Cook until whites set and edges begin to color, then turn carefully and finish until both whites and yolks are firm, about 4–6 minutes depending on heat. Reduce heat if the bottoms darken too quickly. Transfer to plates as the chicken finishes.
4. **Make the glaze:** Meanwhile reduce the chicken skillet to medium, add the remaining 2 tsp oil, and stir garlic and chiles for about 30 seconds until fragrant without blackening. Add the mixed sauce and cooked chicken. Simmer and stir about 2–3 minutes until hot and lightly glazed. Taste the cooked mixture; stop reducing if it is already strongly seasoned.
5. **Finish with basil:** Turn off heat and fold in basil until just wilted. Divide chicken among four plates with separately prepared rice and one fried egg per diner. Offer lime wedges only if wanted at the table.

RECIPE: Thai Basil-Ginger Spritzer (thai-basil-ginger-spritzer.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/thai-basil-ginger-spritzer/
SOURCE: Adapted from Myrecipes.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.myrecipes.com/recipe/thai-basil-ginger-spritzer
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 cup Filtered Water
  - 1/2 cup Granulated Sugar
  - 3 tbsp Fresh Ginger, sliced
  - 2 Thai Basil sprigs
  - 2 Kaffir Lime Leaves (The Finishing Touch)
  - 3 cups Prosecco or Sparkling Wine (chilled)
  - 6 Fresh Thai Basil leaves (for bruising)
  - 6 Lime wedges
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Thai basil (horapha) has a stronger anise note than Italian basil - floral and slightly spicy rather than sweet. Fresh ginger and lime juice make this a refreshing sparkling-wine drink that cuts through heat and richness. Muddle the basil gently so the leaves release their flavor without breaking apart and turning the drink bitter.

## Directions

1.  **The Syrup:** In a small saucepan, boil water and sugar for 1 minute until dissolved. Remove from heat.
2.  **Infuse:** Add the sliced ginger, basil stems, and kaffir lime leaves. Cover and **let stand for 10 minutes**. Strain into a jar and chill.
3.  **thermal Prep:** Chill 6 glasses in the freezer.
4.  **The Bruise:** Place 1 fresh basil leaf in each chilled glass. Use a spoon to gently press (bruise) the leaf against the glass.
5.  **Assemble:** To each glass, add 2 tbsp of the chilled syrup, 1/2 cup Prosecco, and a lime wedge.
6.  **Finish:** Stir once very gently to maintain the Texture of the bubbles. Serve immediately.

RECIPE: Thai Basil Noodles (thai-basil-noodles.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/thai-basil-noodles/
SOURCE: Adapted from thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/thai-basil-noodles/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 8 oz Wide Dried Rice Noodles
  - 1 tbsp Fish Sauce
  - 1 tbsp Soy Sauce (Thai Thin or Light)
  - 1 tsp Dark Soy Sauce (for color)
  - 1 tbsp Oyster Sauce
  - 1 tbsp Brown Sugar
  - 1 lb Ground Pork or Chicken
  - 2 cups Fresh Thai Basil (Holy Basil is ideal)
  - 3 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1-3 Thai Bird’s Eye Chilies, minced
  - 1/2 Bell Pepper, thinly sliced
  - 1 Fresh Lime, cut into wedges
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Pad Kra Pao is Thailand's most popular street food - a fast, pungent stir-fry of holy basil and ground pork that goes from wok to plate in under 10 minutes. The key is very high heat and not stirring too much - let the meat get some color and the basil char slightly before you toss. Serve over rice with a fried egg.

## Directions

1.  **Noodles:** Soak rice noodles in hot water for 15-20 minutes until pliable but still firm (al dente). Drain and set aside.
2.  **Sauce:** Whisk all sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
3.  **Meat:** Heat oil in a wok until smoking. Add the ground meat and spread it flat. Let it sear undisturbed for 2 minutes to get a "crust," then break it up and cook until browned.
4.  **Aromatics:** Add the garlic, chilies, and bell pepper. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
5.  **Toss:** Add the noodles and the sauce. Stir-fry vigorously over high heat, scraping the bottom of the wok, until the noodles absorb the sauce and turn dark brown.
6.  **Wilt:** Add the basil. Toss for 30 seconds until just wilted.
7.  **The Acid Balance:** Turn off the heat. Squeeze half a lime over the noodles and toss.

RECIPE: Thai Red Chicken Curry (thai-chicken-curry.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/thai-chicken-curry/
SOURCE: Adapted from Jordan Silton
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1 lb (450 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced about 1/2 inch thick
  - 1 can (400 ml) full-fat unsweetened coconut milk, divided
  - 3 tbsp Thai red curry paste, or less for a particularly hot or salty paste
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil
  - 150 g red bell pepper, sliced
  - 150 g canned sliced bamboo shoots, drained and rinsed
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) unsalted chicken stock or water
  - 1 tbsp fish sauce, added gradually only as needed
  - 2 tsp palm sugar or brown sugar, added gradually to taste
  - 1/2 cup loosely packed Thai basil leaves
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Red curry paste supplies the chile and aromatic foundation; coconut milk carries it in a rich, fluid sauce. This version fries the paste in measured oil, a practical alternative to first reducing coconut cream. It is not meant to become a thick gravy. Taste before adding fish sauce and sugar because paste brands vary considerably.

## Directions

1. **Fry paste gently:** Heat oil in a wide saucepan over medium-low heat. Add curry paste and stir for about 2 minutes. If it sticks or darkens too quickly, stir in a spoonful of the measured coconut milk rather than letting it scorch.
2. **Make the curry liquid:** Gradually stir in the rest of the coconut milk and the stock or water until paste is dispersed. Bring to a gentle simmer.
3. **Cook chicken and vegetables:** Add chicken and bamboo shoots. Simmer about 6 minutes, then add pepper and continue about 4–6 minutes until pepper is tender-crisp and several of the thickest chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Cook longer if needed.
4. **Balance and finish:** Stir in half the fish sauce and half the sugar. Taste, adding the remainder only as needed. Turn off heat and stir in Thai basil. Serve promptly with plain rice prepared separately.

RECIPE: Thai-Inspired Chicken Meatball Soup (thai-inspired-chicken-meatball-soup.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/thai-inspired-chicken-meatball-soup/
SOURCE: Adapted from cooking.nytimes.com
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020631-thai-inspired-chicken-meatball-soup?smid=ck-recipe-iOS-share
INGREDIENTS:
  - 900 g ground chicken, preferably thigh meat
  - 30 g fresh ginger, finely grated, divided
  - 6 cloves garlic, finely grated, divided
  - 1 jalapeño, finely minced, optional
  - 20 g cilantro, stems finely chopped and leaves roughly chopped separately
  - 3 tbsp fish sauce, divided and partly added to taste
  - 3 tbsp neutral oil, divided
  - 400 ml full-fat unsweetened coconut milk
  - 4 cups (960 ml) unsalted chicken broth
  - 1 tsp brown sugar, optional, added to taste
  - 140 g baby spinach
  - 2 tbsp fresh lime juice, added gradually to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This is a Thai-inspired home soup built around ginger, garlic, cilantro, coconut and fish sauce. It is separate from galangal-led tom kha. Mix the meatballs until cohesive and cook them gently to keep them tender. Small, evenly sized balls are easier to brown and finish consistently. The broth should remain a soup around them, with lime added at the end.

## Directions

1. **Mix:** Keep chicken cold. Combine it with half the grated ginger, half the garlic, optional jalapeño, cilantro stems and 2 tbsp fish sauce. Mix just until the ingredients are evenly distributed and the mixture is slightly tacky; do not beat into a paste.
2. **Shape:** With damp hands, divide into 24 balls of roughly 40 g each, about 1 1/2 inches across. Keep uncooked portions refrigerated while working in batches. Set out broth ingredients before heating the pot.
3. **Brown in three batches:** Heat 2 tsp oil in a wide Dutch oven over medium heat. Add eight meatballs with space between them; brown two or three sides over about 5 minutes, turning gently after the surface releases. Transfer to a tray. Repeat twice with 2 tsp oil per batch. The centers are not yet fully cooked; continue directly to the broth stage.
4. **Build broth:** Remove any blackened residue from the pot, retaining brown fond. Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil and stir the remaining ginger and garlic over medium-low heat for about 30–60 seconds until fragrant. Pour in broth and coconut milk, stirring up the brown residue, and bring to a gentle simmer.
5. **Finish the meatballs:** Return all meatballs and any tray juices. Simmer gently about 10–12 minutes, turning occasionally, until several large meatballs reach 165°F / 74°C at their centers. Extend as needed. Stir in spinach and cook about 1 minute until wilted.
6. **Season and serve:** Turn off heat. Taste the fully cooked broth, adding the remaining fish sauce gradually only if needed, and optional sugar only if it helps the balance. Add half the lime juice, taste, then add more if wanted. Stir in cilantro leaves. Divide into six bowls with four meatballs each and their share of broth and spinach. Serve rice separately if desired.

RECIPE: Thai Green Mango Salad (thai-mango-salad.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/thai-mango-salad/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 medium sour green mangoes, peeled, flesh cut into thin matchsticks
  - 1/2 cup roasted peanuts, roughly chopped
  - 1/4 cup fresh Thai basil leaves, torn if large
  - 1/4 cup fresh mint leaves, torn if large
  - 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, roughly chopped
  - 2 scallions, thinly sliced
  - 1–2 Thai bird’s-eye chilies, thinly sliced, use less for milder heat
  - 3 tbsp fresh lime juice, divided and added to taste
  - 2 tbsp fish sauce, divided and added to taste
  - 1 tbsp honey or agave syrup
  - 1 clove garlic, finely grated
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Taste the mango before adding all the lime: the fruit already brings its own acidity. Fish sauce, honey and chile should season that tart crunch, while herbs and peanuts go in at the last moment. This version is a shredded fruit salad; it is not made with soft dessert mango.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Peel mango, cut flesh away from the pit and slice into thin matchsticks. Taste a small strand for sourness. Slice scallions and chilies, wash and dry herbs and chop the roasted peanuts.

2. **Mix and taste dressing:** Whisk half the lime juice, half the fish sauce, honey or agave and garlic until combined. Add a little chile, then taste a mango strand dipped in the dressing. Add remaining lime, fish sauce and chile gradually as needed; their strength and the fruit’s sourness vary.

3. **Combine:** Toss mango and scallions with enough dressing to coat lightly. Fold in basil, mint and cilantro just before serving, then scatter with peanuts. Reserve excess dressing instead of leaving the mango swimming in it.

4. **Serve:** Divide among side plates and serve promptly. Keep undressed components and dressing refrigerated separately if preparing ahead; add herbs and peanuts when assembling.

RECIPE: Thai Red Curry Shrimp (thai-red-curry-shrimp.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/thai-red-curry-shrimp/
SOURCE: thewoksoflife.com
SOURCE_URL: https://thewoksoflife.com/coconut-curry-shrimp/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 tablespoons neutral oil
  - 1 pound large peeled, deveined shrimp (21/25 size)
  - 2 cloves garlic (minced)
  - 2 slices ginger
  - 1/2–1 can Thai red curry paste (4 ounces/115 g per can; use the lower end of the listed range for less heat)
  - 2 teaspoons brown sugar (or palm sugar)
  - 1 medium onion (cut into small wedges or large diced)
  - ½ red bell pepper (thinly sliced)
  - 13.5 ounces full-fat coconut milk (1 can)
  - cilantro (optional garnish)
  - salt (optional, to taste after the shrimp and sauce finish cooking)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Use the full-fat coconut milk and choose the listed curry-paste amount before cooking. Start the shrimp briefly, then make the sauce and cook the vegetables before returning them to finish. Keep the coconut sauce at a gentle simmer; shrimp centers, not an estimated percentage or a one-minute clock, tell you when to serve.

## Directions

1. **Start shrimp:** Heat a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Add half the listed neutral oil and spread it over the pan. Add the prepared raw shrimp in a single layer and start checking after about 30 seconds on one side and 30 seconds stirring. The surface should begin to change color; no visual percentage proves doneness. Transfer to a temporary bowl for immediate further cooking in step 4. Divide this oil allowance across pan loads if necessary.

2. **Cook curry base:** Over medium heat, add the other half of the listed oil with all the garlic and ginger. Stir about 30 seconds until fragrant without scorching. Add the selected listed curry-paste amount (half to one 4 oz/115 g can at the original batch; scale the amount, not the can size) and fry about 1 minute, stirring. Add all the brown or palm sugar, then the onion and red bell pepper; cook about 2 minutes, stirring.

3. **Simmer sauce:** Stir in all the full-fat coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer. Start checking after about 2 minutes; continue until the onion and pepper are as tender as wanted before returning shrimp. Reduce heat rather than boil vigorously if the sauce starts to separate or turn grainy.

4. **Finish shrimp and serve:** Return all shrimp and collected juices. Simmer, beginning to check after about 1 minute, until the thickest shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout; FDA guidance is 145°F for seafood when checking with a suitable thermometer. Only after the shrimp and raw-contact sauce finish cooking, taste and add the optional salt as needed. The upper end of the listed paste range may supply enough salt; paste composition varies. Use all the optional cilantro you chose to prepare as garnish. Transfer to a clean serving dish and serve promptly, with separately prepared rice if wanted.

RECIPE: Belgian Waffles (the-best-belgian-waffles.md)
CUISINES: Belgian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/the-best-belgian-waffles/
SOURCE: Adapted from Food.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.food.com/recipe/the-best-belgian-waffles-63071
INGREDIENTS:
  - 2 cups All-Purpose Flour
  - 2 large Eggs, separated
  - 2 cups Whole Milk
  - 1/2 cup Vegetable Oil
  - 1/4 cup Granulated Sugar
  - 4 tsp Baking Powder
  - 1 tsp Pure Vanilla Extract
  - 1/2 tsp Sea Salt
  - Vegetable oil for greasing the waffle iron, if its manual recommends it
  - Maple syrup and Perfect Cranberry Sauce for serving (optional)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Whip the separated egg whites to stiff peaks, then fold them into the flour batter just before cooking. The foam adds air, so fold gently and use a fully heated iron. Let each waffle release readily with a golden exterior and a cooked center before lifting it out.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the waffle iron according to its manual. Lightly grease the plates with the separate vegetable-oil allowance if recommended; the measured oil all goes into the batter. Separate the listed eggs, keeping yolks apart from whites. Use a clean, dry bowl and beaters without grease for the whites.
2. **Dry mix:** Sift together the flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt into a large bowl.
3. **Wet mix:** In another bowl, whisk the egg yolks, milk, measured vegetable oil, and vanilla until evenly blended.
4. **Whip the whites:** Beat the whites from the listed eggs until stiff peaks stand upright when the beaters are lifted. Stop before the foam becomes dry and grainy.
5. **Combine:** Add the yolk mixture to the dry ingredients. Stir gently with a whisk just until all flour is moistened, scraping the bowl bottom and sides. Small hydrated lumps may remain.
6. **Fold:** Use a rubber spatula to fold in the whipped whites gently until evenly incorporated, without large pockets of unmixed white. Avoid beating or stirring away the foam, and begin cooking promptly.
7. **Cook the batch:** Fill the hot iron with the amount specified in its manual, leaving expansion room. Cook according to the iron’s settings and readiness guidance; the cycle may be around 5–10 minutes, depending on the iron. Wait until steam has mostly subsided, the waffle releases readily and it is golden with no wet batter in the middle. Repeat with the remaining batter. Keep finished waffles separately on a rack while the next ones cook rather than stacking them.
8. **Serve:** Serve immediately with warm maple syrup and [Perfect Cranberry Sauce](/mise/recipes/perfect-cranberry-sauce) if desired.

## Cooking Notes

The original batch plans six portions, not six waffles of a fixed size. About 40 minutes is a starting allowance for preparation and cooking; a smaller iron or longer cycle can extend the batch. Use the iron’s actual fill amount and cycle count to plan service.

RECIPE: Spinach Lasagna (the-easiest-spinach-lasagna.md)
CUISINES: Italian
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/the-easiest-spinach-lasagna/
SOURCE: Adapted from 100daysofrealfood.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.100daysofrealfood.com/easiest-spinach-lasagna/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 15 oz Ricotta Cheese
  - 8 oz Mozzarella Cheese, grated
  - 1 cup Parmesan Cheese, grated
  - 10 oz Frozen Spinach, thawed and squeezed bone-dry
  - 1 large Egg (The binder)
  - 3 cups (25 oz) High-Quality Marinara Sauce
  - 8 oz Whole-Wheat No-Boil Lasagna Sheets
  - 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt
  - 1/4 tsp Black Pepper
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Lasagna originated in Naples and is one of Italy's oldest pasta dishes, with recipes dating back to the 14th century. The no-boil lasagna sheets are a modern American invention from the 1990s that saves time but requires a saucier sauce to hydrate properly during baking. Squeeze that spinach bone-dry - frozen spinach holds an astonishing amount of water that will make your lasagna watery. This is perfect make-ahead food: assemble up to 24 hours in advance, refrigerate covered, and add 10 minutes to baking time.

## Directions

1.  **The Filling:** In a large bowl, whisk the egg. Mix in the ricotta, mozzarella, 3/4 cup of the Parmesan, the squeezed spinach, salt, and pepper until well combined.
2.  **Layer 1:** Spread 3/4 cup of sauce on the bottom of a 9x13 inch baking dish. This prevents the bottom noodles from sticking.
3.  **Layer 2:** Place a layer of no-boil noodles on top (they shouldn't overlap much). Spread 1/3 of the cheese mixture over the noodles, then top with another 3/4 cup of sauce.
4.  **Repeat:** Repeat the layers (Noodles -> Cheese -> Sauce) until all ingredients are used, ending with a final layer of sauce.
5.  **Finish:** Top with the remaining 1/4 cup Parmesan. Cover tightly with foil.
6.  **Bake:** Bake at 375°F for 30 minutes.
7.  **Crisp:** Remove the foil and bake for another 20-25 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and the noodles are tender.
8.  **Rest:** Let the lasagna rest for 10 minutes before slicing. This is critical for the layers to set.

RECIPE: Chocolate Mug Cake (the-moistest-chocolate-mug-cake.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/the-moistest-chocolate-mug-cake/
SOURCE: Adapted from Tablefortwoblog.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.tablefortwoblog.com/the-moistest-chocolate-mug-cake/
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Mug-cake batter ---
  - 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
  - 2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder
  - 2 tbsp granulated sugar
  - 1/4 tsp baking powder
  - 5 tbsp milk, the original ¼ cup plus 1 tbsp total
  - 2 tbsp vegetable oil
  - 1 tbsp chocolate-hazelnut spread
  - sea salt, a pinch
  - --- Optional extra sweetness and finish ---
  - 1 tbsp additional granulated sugar, only for the sweeter option, optional
  - powdered sugar, a light dusting after cooking, if desired, optional
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

The chocolate-hazelnut spread is dropped onto the center without stirring, while the surrounding flour batter must cook through. The publisher’s 70-second reference is for a 950-watt microwave, and another microwave took 90 seconds. Mug shape and batter volume also matter, so use the reference with the actual appliance instructions and check the cake around the melted center.

## Directions

1. **Mix dry ingredients:** Whisk all-purpose flour, unsweetened cocoa powder, granulated sugar, baking powder, sea salt, and additional granulated sugar (if using) in the microwave-safe mug until evenly combined; include the additional sugar only if choosing the sweeter option. For the original single-cake batch use a microwave-safe mug with about 14 fl oz capacity and enough headspace for rising.
2. **Add milk and oil:** Whisk in milk and vegetable oil with a fork until no flour or cocoa pockets remain, including at the bottom of the mug. The listed milk total is 5 tbsp in the original batch, exactly ¼ cup plus 1 tbsp.
3. **Add the center:** Drop chocolate-hazelnut spread in the center on top of the batter. Do not stir it through or push it down.
4. **Microwave:** Microwave one original-size mug on high for the source reference of 70 seconds at 950 watts. Different power, mug shape or batter volume needs adjustment; this is not a universal finishing clock. If using a paper towel beneath the mug to catch drips, first confirm that the microwave instructions permit it. Check that the cake around the spread has set rather than remaining liquid batter; do not confuse melted spread with uncooked batter. Continue cooking as needed according to the appliance instructions. For multiple cakes, divide into individual original-size mugs and cook separately rather than placing doubled batter in this mug.
5. **Stand:** Remove carefully; the mug can be very hot. Let stand for the listed one minute, then check that the cake is cooked through and cool enough to eat. The standing minute is additional to the heating time. Smaller scaled quantities also change heating behavior; they do not inherit the original mug’s clock.
6. **Serve:** Dust with powdered sugar (if using) if desired. Eat freshly made; further cooling may be needed before serving.

## Cooking Notes

### Center and salt options

Keep the full listed chocolate-hazelnut center for the main version. The same listed amount of mini chocolate chips may replace it, or the center may be omitted; the rest of the full batter stays unchanged. Other spreads are named possibilities without a measured heating plan here.

The sweeter option uses the separate optional sugar amount in the dry mixture. This version uses a pinch of sea salt. The publisher specifies ⅛ tsp kosher salt for its original single-cake batch; scale that measured source alternative proportionally if selected INSTEAD of the sea-salt pinch, not in addition. Do not assume the sea-salt pinch and kosher-salt spoon volume are equal.

The cake is written for microwave cooking. No oven temperature or time is supplied. Self-rising flour is not a recommended replacement for the listed flour and powder. The original bowl-mixing route is also available: whisk all dry ingredients in a bowl, whisk in all milk and oil, pour into the mug, add the center, then use the same microwave checks.

RECIPE: New England Express (the-new-england-express.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/the-new-england-express/
SOURCE: Adapted from Bonappetit.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/the-new-england-express
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1/3 cup Granulated Sugar
  - 8 sprigs Fresh Thyme
  - 2 cups Apple Cider (unfiltered)
  - 1 1/2 cups Dark Rum (The complex flavor)
  - 3/4 cup Fresh Lime Juice (The Acid Balance)
  - 1 tsp aromatic bitters
  - Club Soda (to top)
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This cocktail showcases sophisticated flavor layering. The secret is the herbal syrup: we boil the sugar into a simple syrup but steep the fresh thyme for 10 minutes _after_ removing from heat. This introduces a savory, botanical flavor that bridges the gap between the earthy apple cider and the rich molasses of the dark rum. The fresh lime juice provides the essential brightness that defines the "Express" punch.

## Directions

1.  **The Syrup:** In a small pan, boil sugar and 1/3 cup water until dissolved. Remove from heat. Add thyme sprigs. Cover and **let stand for 10 minutes**. Strain and chill.
2.  **The Base:** In a large pitcher, combine the chilled thyme syrup, apple cider, dark rum, lime juice, and bitters. Stir vigorously.
3.  **Thermal Prep:** Fill 8 rocks glasses with massive ice cubes.
4.  **Assemble:** Pour the cider mixture into each glass, filling 3/4 full.
5.  **Effervescence:** Top each glass with a splash of club soda for the mandatory "Bounce."
6.  **Garnish:** Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig and a lime slice for the final aromatic **High Note**.

RECIPE: Crisp Rice Marshmallow Treats (the-original-rice-krispies-treatstm.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/the-original-rice-krispies-treatstm/
SOURCE: Adapted from ricekrispies.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.ricekrispies.com/en_US/recipes/the-original-treats-recipe.html
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Treats ---
  - 6 cups crisp rice cereal
  - 10 oz (1 package) fresh marshmallows
  - 3 tbsp unsalted butter
  - sea salt, a pinch
  - 1/2 tsp pure vanilla extract
  - --- Pan and utensil preparation ---
  - butter or cooking spray, enough to lightly grease the pan and spatula
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Melt the butter and fresh marshmallows gently over low heat, then remove the pan from heat before adding the salt, vanilla and cereal. Stir until the marshmallows have melted fully; leaving a prescribed fraction unmelted is not needed. Use the full butter and cereal amounts, and press gently instead of packing the mixture firmly.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** For the original batch, lightly grease a 9×13×2-inch pan and spatula with butter or cooking spray. Have wax paper available for pressing. Scaling needs proportional pan area or additional pans to keep a similar layer thickness; do not cram extra full batches into the original pan.
2. **Melt gently:** Use fresh marshmallows and unsalted butter in a large saucepan: melt the butter over low heat, then add the marshmallows and stir until completely melted and smooth. Remove from heat; there is no fixed stovetop melting time.
3. **Flavor off heat:** Stir sea salt and pure vanilla extract into the melted mixture off the heat.
4. **Coat the cereal:** Fold in crisp rice cereal until evenly coated, scraping the bottom and sides. Use the full cereal amount.
5. **Press:** Transfer the full mixture to the prepared pan, or divide across the selected proportional pans. Use the greased spatula or wax paper to press gently into an even layer; avoid compacting it firmly.
6. **Cool:** Let cool at room temperature until set and cool enough to cut. Thirty minutes is the current planning allowance, not a guaranteed finish; thickness and room conditions can change it.
7. **Cut and serve:** Cut into the listed number of planning portions, or smaller squares as desired. The original two-inch-square suggestion is a cutting option, not a claim that a 9×13-inch pan produces twelve exact two-inch squares. Serve the same day for best texture.

## Cooking Notes

### Marshmallow alternatives

Choose ONE marshmallow route. The full listed 10 oz fresh marshmallows is the main version. For the original 6-cup cereal batch, the publisher’s alternatives are 5½ cups miniature marshmallows OR one 7 oz jar of marshmallow crème in place of all the marshmallows. Scale the chosen total with the cereal, keeping jar size fixed while scaling the jar count or crème weight. The miniature volume describes the source product, not a universal weight conversion for every marshmallow. Keep all the current butter, cereal, salt and vanilla amounts in either option. Diet, reduced-calorie and tub margarine are not recommended by the source; the main uses the full unsalted butter.

### Microwave route

Use a microwave-safe bowl with enough room for the butter and marshmallows to expand and for the full cereal to be folded in afterward. For the original batch, microwave the full butter and chosen marshmallow amount on HIGH for the source reference of 3 minutes, stirring after 2 minutes, then stir until smooth. Times vary with the microwave and volume; follow its instructions and the smooth-melt endpoint rather than multiplying the clock when scaling. Stir in the full salt and vanilla off heat, fold in the entire cereal, then press, cool and cut as above. The bowl capacity and microwave wattage are not specified in the source; divide a larger batch or use suitable larger equipment instead of assuming it fits.

RECIPE: Thit Kho (Vietnamese Caramelized Pork) (thit-kho-vietnamese-caramelized-pork.md)
CUISINES: Vietnamese
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/thit-kho-vietnamese-caramelized-pork/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1.5 lb boneless pork shoulder or skinless pork belly, cut into 1-inch cubes
  - 2 medium shallots, halved lengthwise
  - 4 cloves garlic, peeled
  - 2 tsp fish sauce, for the braise
  - 3 tbsp brown sugar, or finely shaved palm sugar
  - 1 cup unsweetened coconut water or water, plus hot water as needed during cooking
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil
  - 2 whole dried chilies, optional
  - 1 tsp black pepper
  - 3 tbsp additional fish sauce, maximum finishing allowance; use only as needed
  - Fresh cilantro and scallions, chopped, for serving
  - Lime wedges, for serving
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Caramel, fish sauce and slow-cooking pork make a concentrated savory-sweet sauce. Keep a little liquid in the pot until the meat is tender, then decide how far to reduce it. Plain rice and a crisp vegetable accompaniment balance the richness; finish with fresh herbs and lime at the table.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Pat the pork cubes dry. Have shallots, garlic, chilies, pepper, the braising portion of fish sauce and coconut water ready beside the stove.
2. **Make the caramel:** Warm the oil in a heavy saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the brown sugar or shaved palm sugar and stir with a silicone spatula until fluid and caramel-scented, about 2–3 minutes. Lower the heat if it smokes; discard and restart if it smells acrid.
3. **Coat the pork:** Carefully add the dry pork with tongs, keeping your hands away from possible splashes. Turn for about 2 minutes to coat in the caramel; a browned crust is not required on every cube.
4. **Add aromatics and liquid:** Add shallots, garlic, optional chilies, pepper and the measured braising fish sauce. Stir, then carefully add the coconut water or water. Scrape up dissolved caramel without scraping any burned material.
5. **Braise to tenderness:** Bring to a gentle simmer, cover with the lid slightly ajar and lower the heat. Stir occasionally and keep a shallow liquid in the pan, adding hot water if it dries before the meat softens. Start testing a cube after about 45 minutes; allow roughly 60–90 minutes, continuing longer if needed. A fork should enter easily. Check a thick cube reaches at least 145°F / 63°C; tenderness usually needs substantially more cooking than this minimum.
6. **Control the sauce:** If the meat is tender but sauce remains thin, lift the pork out and reduce the sauce uncovered, then return the meat. Skim excess surface fat if desired. Taste before adding optional finishing fish sauce, a little at a time; you may need none of the additional allowance. Stop when savory and lightly sweet with enough sauce for the rice.
7. **Rest:** Take off heat and rest for 5 minutes, which also exceeds the 3-minute rest required after the minimum pork temperature.
8. **Serve:** Serve alongside separately cooked rice. Add cilantro, scallions and lime to taste.

RECIPE: Three-Herb Chicken & Mushrooms (three-herb-chicken-and-mushrooms.md)
CUISINES: French
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/three-herb-chicken-and-mushrooms/
SOURCE: Adapted from Bhg.com
SOURCE_URL: http://www.bhg.com/recipe/three-herb-chicken-and-mushrooms/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 8 small bone-in skin-on chicken thighs (about 175 g each)
  - 1 tsp fine salt, divided
  - 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
  - 1 tbsp neutral oil, used only as needed to supplement rendered chicken fat
  - 450 g cremini mushrooms, trimmed and quartered
  - 2 tsp finely chopped fresh rosemary leaves
  - 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves
  - 1 1/2 tbsp all-purpose flour
  - 1/2 cup (120 ml) dry white wine
  - 1 cup (240 ml) unsalted chicken broth, plus a little more to loosen if needed
  - 2 tbsp Dijon mustard
  - 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

This French-inspired roast uses three herbs in two stages. Rosemary and thyme simmer in the mushroom sauce so they do not taste raw or burn against the chicken skin; parsley finishes it with a fresher aroma. Render the skin before roasting and leave room for each thigh. Dijon adds tang and body, while flour provides the main thickening. Spoon sauce around the chicken so the skin stays drier.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C with a rack in the middle. Pat chicken dry. Season with three-quarters of the measured salt and the pepper. Quarter mushrooms and prepare herbs before handling chicken, or clean the board and tools thoroughly between them. Set out a rimmed half-sheet pan.
2. **Render and brown in two batches:** Place four thighs skin-side down in a cool 12-inch skillet, with space between them. Turn heat to medium and cook about 8–12 minutes until skin is golden and some fat has rendered, adjusting heat to prevent scorching. Turn and cook the flesh side about 1 minute. Transfer skin-side up to the sheet pan. Brown the remaining four in the warm skillet over medium heat, about 6–9 minutes skin-side down and 1 minute on the other side. Use a little of the measured neutral oil only if the pan is dry. Proceed directly to roasting after both batches are seared.
3. **Roast and check:** Arrange all thighs skin-side up with space between them and roast about 25–35 minutes. Check each at its thickest meat away from bone: all must reach at least 165°F / 74°C; for more yielding thigh meat, continue toward 175–185°F / 79–85°C. Remove smaller pieces sooner if needed. Rest uncovered about 5 minutes while finishing the sauce.
4. **Brown mushrooms during roasting:** Pour off excess skillet fat into a heatproof container, leaving about 2 tbsp in the pan; supplement with the remaining measured oil only if necessary. Add mushrooms over medium-high heat and cook about 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until their released liquid mostly evaporates and surfaces brown.
5. **Add herbs, flour and wine:** Reduce heat to medium. Stir in rosemary and thyme for about 30 seconds, then sprinkle flour evenly and stir for 1 minute. Add wine gradually, stirring and scraping the brown residue from the pan. Simmer about 2–3 minutes until the wine reduces by roughly half.
6. **Finish the sauce:** Stir in broth gradually and simmer gently about 5–7 minutes, stirring, until lightly thickened. Reduce heat to low and stir in Dijon. Add any juices from the rested chicken and bring back to a brief simmer. Taste, adding the reserved salt only if needed, and loosen with a little broth if thick. Turn off heat and stir in parsley.
7. **Serve:** Divide into four portions of two small thighs. Spoon mushrooms and sauce around or beneath the chicken, leaving the skin exposed. Serve with a separately prepared potato side and a green vegetable if desired.

RECIPE: Tom Kha Gai (Galangal Coconut Chicken Soup) (tom-kha-gai-coconut-chicken-soup.md)
CUISINES: Thai
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/tom-kha-gai-coconut-chicken-soup/
INGREDIENTS:
  - 400 ml full-fat unsweetened coconut milk
  - 2 cups (480 ml) unsalted chicken stock
  - 30 g fresh or frozen galangal, thinly sliced
  - 2 lemongrass stalks, tough outer layers removed, lower halves bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
  - 4 makrut lime leaves, torn into large pieces
  - 2 small dried red chiles, left whole for gentler heat or broken for more heat
  - 450 g boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into 1/4-inch-thick bite-sized slices
  - 225 g oyster mushrooms, torn into bite-sized pieces, or cremini mushrooms, thinly sliced
  - 100 g cherry tomatoes, halved
  - 2 tbsp fish sauce, added gradually to taste
  - 1 tsp palm sugar or brown sugar, plus a little more only if needed
  - 3 tbsp fresh lime juice, added gradually to taste
  - 2 tbsp chopped cilantro
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Galangal gives this coconut chicken soup its distinctive aroma, with mushrooms and a small tomato addition. Ginger makes a different-tasting substitute. Infuse the large aromatics first and remove them before adding the chicken and vegetables. Add lean chicken late and finish with lime off heat for a fragrant, spoonable broth.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the infusion:** Slice galangal, trim and bruise lemongrass, and tear lime leaves. Choose whether to leave dried chiles whole or break them for more heat. Put coconut milk, stock and these aromatics in a 3-quart saucepan.
2. **Infuse and strain:** Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat and cook about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Strain into a heatproof bowl, discarding galangal, lemongrass, lime leaves and dried chiles. Return the fragrant broth to the saucepan. The infused chile heat remains even after straining.
3. **Start the mushrooms:** Bring broth back to a gentle simmer. Add mushrooms and cook about 3 minutes, until beginning to soften. Meanwhile keep the prepared chicken refrigerated until ready to add.
4. **Cook chicken and tomatoes:** Add chicken slices and tomatoes, stirring to separate the chicken. Return to a gentle simmer and cook about 4–6 minutes, until several thick chicken slices reach 165°F / 74°C and mushrooms are tender. Extend as needed, keeping the simmer gentle.
5. **Season off heat:** Turn off heat. Stir in sugar and about half the fish sauce, then about half the lime juice. Taste and add more fish sauce and lime gradually only as needed. The soup should be savory and freshly sour, not cloying. Add a little extra sugar only if the finished balance needs it.
6. **Serve:** Divide meat, vegetables and broth among four modest bowls and finish with cilantro. Serve separately prepared plain rice if wanted. Do not add an unmeasured extra coconut-cream drizzle; the broth already contains its full coconut portion.

RECIPE: Heirloom Tomato & Goat Cheese Tart (tomato-and-goat-cheese-tart.md)
CUISINES: French
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/tomato-and-goat-cheese-tart/
SOURCE: Adapted from foodandwine.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.foodandwine.com/recipes/tomato-and-goat-cheese-tart
INGREDIENTS:
  - --- Tart ingredients ---
  - 2 cups all-purpose flour
  - all-purpose flour, for rolling
  - 3/4 cup (6 oz) cold unsalted butter, cubed
  - 1/2 tsp baking powder
  - 1 tbsp cold apple cider vinegar
  - 3–4 tbsp ice water, add only as needed; unused maximum may remain
  - 3 tsp kosher salt
  - 4 tbsp olive oil
  - 1 tsp black pepper
  - 12 oz goat cheese, crumbled
  - 1 cup whole-milk ricotta
  - 1/2 tsp grated garlic
  - 4 tsp fresh thyme leaves
  - 3 lb heirloom tomatoes, washed and evenly thinly sliced
  - fresh green and purple basil, for garnish
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Roast the tomatoes before layering so their surface moisture has time to evaporate. Goat cheese belongs in both the pastry and the ricotta filling, while the salt, oil, pepper and thyme have separate measured destinations. The baked tart needs its short cooling period before the rim comes off.

## Directions

1. **Make dough:** Use all-purpose flour, cold unsalted butter, baking powder, cold apple cider vinegar, ice water, 1/3 of the kosher salt, 1/3 of the goat cheese, and 1/2 of the fresh thyme leaves for the pastry: pulse flour, baking powder, assigned thyme and assigned salt together. Add all the cold butter and assigned goat cheese and pulse until crumbly. Pulse in all vinegar, then the ice-water supply gradually just until dough gathers; unused water may remain. Form a disk, wrap and refrigerate at least 30 minutes.
2. **Roast tomatoes:** Heat the oven to 425°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Divide 1/3 of the kosher salt, 3/4 of the olive oil, 1/2 of the black pepper, and heirloom tomatoes across two large rimmed sheets for the original batch, spreading the slices without crowded piles and dividing the assigned oil, salt and pepper over every sheet. Roast until slices shrink and their surfaces are dry to the touch, beginning checks around 30 minutes and often taking 30–45 minutes. Rotate sheets between racks halfway through; extra sheets may require more oven rounds. Retain all tomato slices and their oil for the tart.
3. **Shape and freeze shell:** Use all-purpose flour lightly on the work surface. Roll dough to a 12-inch circle about 1/4 inch thick for the original 11-inch removable-bottom tart pan; press into the bottom and sides. Use suitable extra or smaller pans when scaling, with similar pastry thickness and enough room for the full filling. Freeze the shaped shell 20 minutes. Increase oven temperature to 450°F.
4. **Blind-bake:** Put the tart pan on a rimmed baking sheet. Line the frozen shell with foil and pie weights filling to the edge. Bake at 450°F for about 20–25 minutes until set and beginning to turn golden at the edges. Carefully lift out weights and foil and cool about 10 minutes. Reduce the oven to 425°F. Do not replace foil with parchment unless that actual product is rated for 450°F.
5. **Make cheese filling:** Whisk all 2/3 of the goat cheese, whole-milk ricotta, grated garlic, and 1/2 of the fresh thyme leaves until combined. Scrape the entire mixture across the baked shell; this uses every remaining portion of goat cheese and thyme, not another full measured batch.
6. **Add tomatoes and finish seasoning:** Arrange all the roasted tomato slices over the cheese, overlapping slightly as needed. Divide all 1/3 of the kosher salt, 1/4 of the olive oil, and 1/2 of the black pepper over the tomatoes. The earlier roasting oil remains with the tomatoes; this is only the reserved final oil and seasoning.
7. **Finish baking:** Bake at 425°F, starting checks around 20–25 minutes for the original tart, until the tomatoes and pastry are browned and the filling is hot. Shield pastry if its edge colors early; actual pan depth and additional tart rounds alter the clock.
8. **Cool and serve:** Cool 20–30 minutes until just warm before releasing the removable rim and slicing. Finish with fresh green and purple basil. Refrigerate remaining portions promptly.

RECIPE: Tomato Cobbler with Cornmeal-Cheddar Biscuits (tomato-cobbler-with-cornmeal-cheddar-biscuits.md)
CUISINES: Southern
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/tomato-cobbler-with-cornmeal-cheddar-biscuits/
SOURCE: Adapted from thekitchn.com
SOURCE_URL: https://www.thekitchn.com/recipe-tomato-cobbler-with-cornmeal-cheddar-biscuits-206816
INGREDIENTS:
  - 4 lbs Cherry Tomatoes, whole
  - 2 Red Onions, thinly sliced
  - 1/4 cup Red Wine
  - 1/4 cup All-Purpose Flour
  - 4 cloves Garlic, minced
  - 1 1/4 cups All-Purpose Flour + 3/4 cup Cornmeal
  - 6 tbsp Unsalted Butter, cold and cubed
  - 1 1/2 cups Sharp Cheddar, shredded
  - 1 cup Whole Buttermilk
  - 1 tbsp Baking Powder
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

Tomato cobbler is a Southern riff on savory fruit cobblers, where long-caramelized onions create depth and cherry tomatoes collapse into a jammy, bittersweet sauce. The cornmeal-cheddar biscuits are pure Southern technique - cornmeal for texture and corn flavor, shredded cheddar for savory richness, and buttermilk for tang that bridges sweet fruit and cheese.

## Directions

1.  **Reduction:** In a massive skillet, sauté onions in oil for 20 minutes until mahogany brown. Add garlic and wine; simmer until the wine has vanished.
2.  **The Paste:** Stir in 1/4 cup flour until paste-like. Remove from heat. Gently fold in the cherry tomatoes and salt. Pour into a large baking dish.
3.  **The Dough:** In a food processor, pulse flour, cornmeal, baking powder, and cold butter until pea-sized. Transfer to a bowl.
4.  **Emulsify:** Stir in 1 cup of the cheese and the buttermilk until a shaggy, sticky dough forms.
5.  **Drop:** Spoon walnut-sized mounds of dough over the tomatoes - you want gaps for the steam to escape (The Steam Cycle).
6.  **Bake:** Preheat oven to 375°F. Bake for 55-60 minutes until the tomatoes are bubbling and the biscuits are deep golden.
7.  **The Crunch:** During the final 10 minutes, sprinkle the remaining cheese over the biscuits.
8.  **Set:** Let rest for 15 minutes (mandatory) before serving.

RECIPE: Tomato Soup (tomato-soup.md)
CUISINES: American
URL: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/tomato-soup/
SOURCE: Adapted from The New York Times, Tomato Soup
SOURCE_URL: https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1013383-tomato-soup
INGREDIENTS:
  - 1/2 lb unsalted butter
  - 1 lb yellow onions, cut into small dice
  - 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
  - 4 (28 oz) cans diced tomatoes, with their juices
  - 1 1/4 cups chicken broth
  - 1/4 cup granulated sugar
  - 2 tbsp honey
  - 3/4 cup half-and-half
  - 1 tsp celery salt
  - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
CONTENT:

## Chef's Note

A generous butter base and a little flour give this soup its body. Soften onions gently, coat them evenly with flour, then simmer the tomatoes while scraping the pot bottom. Half-and-half and honey finish the soup; blending smooths the softened vegetables into the thickened liquid.

## Directions

1. **Soften onions:** Melt butter in a heavy pot over medium-low. Add diced onions and cook about **20 minutes**, stirring regularly, until soft and translucent without browning.
2. **Cook flour:** Stir in flour until no dry pockets remain. Cook about **3 minutes**, stirring and scraping, until the buttery mixture is pale gold; do not let it darken.
3. **Add liquid gradually:** Stir in broth a little at a time to loosen the flour mixture, then add all listed tomatoes and their juices, sugar, celery salt and black pepper. Raise heat enough to bring to a gentle simmer, stirring so the thick base does not stick.
4. **Simmer:** Reduce heat and simmer gently for about **30 minutes**, scraping across the pot bottom frequently, until the onion and tomatoes are very soft. Avoid a rapid boil.
5. **Blend and finish:** Remove from heat and let active bubbling stop. Blend with an immersion blender, keeping its guard submerged and stopping before lifting it. Alternatively, cool to your countertop blender’s permitted temperature and blend in as many small batches as its hot-liquid fill limit requires, with the lid and steam vent arranged exactly as its instructions specify. Start low; do not use a sealed personal cup for hot soup. Stir in half-and-half and honey. Return to gentle heat just until hot, without a hard boil.
6. **Taste and serve:** Taste before adding salt, since celery salt and broth already season the soup. Divide into the intended soup portions and serve. Bread is a separate accompaniment; refrigerate surplus promptly rather than leaving the large pot out through the meal.

Adapted from [The New York Times’ Tomato Soup](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1013383-tomato-soup).
